stages.name: Orblet
stages.bio: Orblet is a tiny round creature with one enormous violet eye that fills most of its body. Four stubby fins keep it bobbing just off the seafloor while its soft purple skin pulses faintly with each thought. In Coral Bay's shallows it floats between the reef columns, fixing that giant unblinking eye on anything that moves - not to hunt, but out of pure bottomless curiosity. Guardians say Orblet memorizes the shape of every fish it meets, storing them somewhere in the inky depths of its mind.
stages.note: Orblet never blinks - researchers believe it photographs a full scene with each long stare.

stages.name: Sharkmaw
stages.bio: Sharkmaw has grown a streamlined blue-and-purple shark body, long pointed snout, and swept-back purple fins edged in lilac. Its massive single eye now glows with a sharper violet light, and a ridge of psychic energy runs along its dorsal line. It patrols the mid-water columns of Coral Bay with calm precision, reading the intentions of creatures before they even move. Trainers who respect its gaze find it an eerily reliable early-warning partner when Abalont's shadows creep near the reef.
stages.note: Sharkmaw can feel a lie in the water before a single word is spoken - its eye turns deep indigo when it senses deception.

stages.name: Voidtide
stages.bio: Voidtide has transformed into a vast deep-blue manta ray whose wide flat wings are spotted with glowing pale-blue orbs. Trailing luminous tendrils drift behind it like living starlight. Its body measures wider than a rowboat and its passage creates a visible current. It no longer merely watches - it broadcasts its thoughts outward in waves that the reef's fish respond to by clearing a path. Ancient Coral Bay lore says Voidtide's mind-current once guided lost guardian ships home through pitch-black water.
stages.note: Every glowing spot on Voidtide's wings is a memory of a different voice it once heard; the oldest spots shine brightest.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.bio: A walking acorn no taller than a boot, Seedling wears a glossy ribbed cap pulled low over two big eyes, and swings a pair of little pinecone fists it loves to knock together when excited. Two green leaves sprout from its cap - they perk up at a brave new sound and droop when it grows sleepy. It was the first friend the guardians ever made in Verdant Valley, and it stayed among the roots when Akilla fell to Abalont's shadow.
stages.note: A tap-tap-tap through the undergrowth is usually a Seedling drumming its pinecone fists, calling for a friend.

stages.name: Oakmite
stages.bio: Standing upright now, Oakmite's body has hardened into ridged bark, and the leaves on its cap have grown into full sprigs that fan open in sunlight. Its pinecone fists have toughened into knotted knuckles it plants on the ground to brace itself - once set, it holds its place like a young tree in a storm. It patrols the climbing paths where Akilla once roamed.
stages.note: Oakmite refuses to step backward; trainers say you can move a boulder more easily than a planted Oakmite.

stages.name: Giantern
stages.bio: Broad and tree-solid, Giantern carries two great pinecone pods on its shoulders like a warrior's pauldrons, and its acorn-cap crown is thick as oak-heartwood. When it speaks, its voice rolls out as a deep groan of creaking wood, and the roots beneath the valley stir in answer. Patient as the forest itself, it remembers every voice and waits for the lost guardians to come home.
stages.note: The pods on its shoulders drop ripe seeds each autumn; a single one can grow into a new grove of song-trees.

name: Fluttox

stages.name: Fluttox
stages.bio: Fluttox is a plump sky-blue bird fledgling with soft round feathers and a single small iridescent crystal wing-fan sprouting beside its regular wing. Its eyes are wide and brilliantly blue, and it flaps both wings with cheerful uncoordinated enthusiasm. High in Gale Ridge's updraft chimneys, Fluttox tumbles on the wind currents, each tumble teaching it a little more about how air moves. Guardians of the Ridge leave seed perches on the upper platforms, knowing a tumbling Fluttox always finds its way back up.
stages.note: Fluttox somersaults exactly three times before landing - never two, never four, always three.

stages.name: Windox
stages.bio: Windox has grown into a proud blue-and-white bird with layered feathers and large iridescent crystal wings that catch every draft like sails. Its posture is alert and bold, chest forward, tail fanned wide. It rides the constant gales around Gale Ridge without flapping - just tilts a crystal feather and the wind does the rest. Windox scouts ahead of storms, calling back weather-reads to trainers below in a series of precise whistled patterns.
stages.note: Each whistled call from Windox encodes the wind direction, speed, and whether rain is coming - thirty notes, all distinct.

stages.name: Crystalwing
stages.bio: Crystalwing is a magnificent sea-green-and-teal eagle with enormous crystal-shard wings that catch the light like a stained-glass window mid-storm. Its wingspan blots out the sun when it passes overhead, and each crystal primary feather chimes against the others in a continuous moving melody. Its psychic perception now spans the full height of Gale Ridge - it reads thoughts the way a sailor reads clouds. Legends say Crystalwing once guided the guardians through Abalont's blindness-fog by broadcasting a psychic beacon from the tallest spire.
stages.note: When Crystalwing circles three times over the same spot, a storm will arrive within the hour - the Ridge's guardians trust this completely.

blurb: Fluttox got blown away from its flock by a big gust. Help Fluttox fly home!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Jack.
facts: Birds are the only animals with feathers.
Parrots can copy sounds and even words!
question: What covers a bird's body?

stages.name: Aethelchick
stages.bio: Aethelchick is a round grey-white owlet with a single curved pearlescent horn rising from its forehead and wide sapphire eyes ringed with pale blue. Its breast feathers shimmer faintly as if dusted with starlight. In the Psychic Temple's canopy it perches on low branches and tilts its head at new sounds with intense concentration - that horn glows when it understands something for the first time. The temple's guardians say Aethelchick can hold perfectly still for six hours waiting for a single fascinating fact.
stages.note: Aethelchick's horn tip glows blue whenever it hears a sound it has never encountered before.

stages.name: Aethelwing
stages.bio: Aethelwing stands proud as a hawk now, its plumage a deep swirling blue-grey that mirrors the night sky of the Psychic Temple. The single horn has lengthened and curved back like a crescent blade, and its talons are tipped with luminous gold. Its wide-spread wings reveal faint galaxy-like streaks when it lifts off at dusk. It hunts by reading the intentions of its quarry a full heartbeat before they flee - a psychic edge it uses only to protect its temple, never to harm.
stages.note: Aethelwing can read the mood of an entire temple from a single overhead pass; trainers feel unusually calm in its shadow.

stages.name: Aethelion
stages.bio: Aethelion is a blazing golden eagle with wings spread wide in triumph, its entire body radiating warm amber-gold light with violet-purple secondary feathers trailing behind. Water droplets shimmer off its wingtips as it flies through cloud. Its horn has become a full golden crown-spike, and its eyes carry a calm all-knowing warmth. Ancient the Psychic Temple hymns say Aethelion is the temple's living lamp - when Abalont's darkness tries to creep in, Aethelion rises to the highest branch and simply opens its wings.
stages.note: Three wingbeats from Aethelion are enough to clear fog from an entire valley - local farmers time their mornings by its flights.

stages.name: Aethling
stages.bio: Aethling is a small round blue bird with a white belly and a distinctive teal swirl marking on its chest, like a tiny whirlpool. Bright water-drop sparkles float around it constantly. In Poison Marsh's misty channels it hops along floating lily pads, tilting its head at every ripple. Its feathers repel the marsh's toxic vapors like a tiny forcefield. Guardians first noticed Aethling leading safe paths through the marsh by hopping only across patches where the water sparkles blue rather than green.
stages.note: Aethling's swirl marking spins visibly clockwise when fresh air is nearby and counter-clockwise near marsh gas - a perfect compass.

stages.name: Aethawk
stages.bio: Aethawk has grown into a bold blue jay-shaped bird with icy-blue plumage and tail feathers that stream behind it like jets of water. Its chest is pure white and its wings carry teal water-streaks. It sprints low across the marsh surface fast enough to leave a ripple trail in the murky water. In battle it whips its tail feathers to conjure short water-jet gusts that knock toxic spores away from allies. Trainers crossing Poison Marsh trust Aethawk to scout ahead and report back in coded tail-fan patterns.
stages.note: Aethawk can sprint 40 meters across open water without getting its feet wet by riding its own air-cushion jet-wake.

stages.name: Aetherion
stages.bio: Aetherion is a powerful wide-winged raptor draped in deep royal blue, with gold talons and wings spread in a full commanding display. Bands of teal and ice-blue run across its wings, and a crest of swept-back blue feathers crowns its head. When it opens its wings in Poison Marsh, the toxic mist parts for thirty meters in every direction. Ancient marsh-keepers say Aetherion's call is the only sound that reaches across the whole marsh at once - a rolling wave of water and wind combined.
stages.note: One sustained call from Aetherion clears toxic spores from a full marsh sector; the marsh falls silent for a full minute afterward.

stages.name: Alpkit
stages.bio: Alpkit is an adorably round cream-white llama foal with a fluffy woolly coat, large blue eyes, and tiny stumpy legs that make it wobble slightly when it walks. Its wool catches the faint light of Crystal Mines and throws back soft pastel glints. It nuzzles anything that holds still long enough, pressing its forehead against crystals to absorb their stored memories. Young Alpkits born deep in the mines reportedly hum back fragments of ancient guardian songs they learned from the crystal walls.
stages.note: Alpkit absorbs one new memory from any crystal it nuzzles - and will nuzzle every crystal in range before resting.

stages.name: Alpacay
stages.bio: Alpacay has grown into a graceful full-sized llama with a dense white woolly coat and long elegant legs. Its fluffy mane frames an intelligent, knowing face, and subtle iridescent shimmer runs through its coat in sunlight. It navigates the deep tunnels of Crystal Mines by sensing psychic echoes stored in the ore veins - a walking map of everywhere it has ever been. Crystal miners leave small gifts of salt at tunnel crossings, knowing Alpacay will nuzzle the walls nearby and keep the veins calm.
stages.note: Alpacay remembers every tunnel junction it has ever passed through; lost miners follow it out of the dark by watching its ear tilt.

stages.name: Majestiaca
stages.bio: Majestiaca is a breathtaking llama adorned in flowing rainbow-pastel wool that shifts from rose to gold to violet as it moves, hung with ornate golden bells and crystal pendants at its chest and neck. Its mane and tail are braided with light itself. When it walks, its hoofbeats chime softly and the air around it smells of warm quartz. It is said Majestiaca carries the complete memory of every voice ever raised in Crystal Mines - and will share any of them with a child who asks politely.
stages.note: The golden bells on Majestiaca's chest ring a different note for each region of the mines - experienced miners navigate by sound alone.

stages.name: Stonini
stages.bio: Stonini is a chubby grey rhinoceros calf with smooth stone-textured skin and a single small blunt horn on its nose. Its four stubby legs carry it with a trundling shuffle that shakes pebbles loose from the granite paths of Granite Heights. Despite its solid build, Stonini has gentle curious eyes and will stop mid-charge to examine an interesting rock. Young trainers discover quickly that Stonini learns best through touch - press a word into its flank and it will remember it forever.
stages.note: Stonini tests every rock it meets with a light headbutt - the hollow ones it marks with a scratch to find again later.

stages.name: Rhinameth
stages.bio: Rhinameth has grown into a powerful broad-shouldered rhino with dark grey hide and a dramatic crown of purple amethyst crystals erupting from its back like a dorsal ridge. Its horn has lengthened and sharpened to a violet-tinged point. When it lowers its head, those crystal spines hum with psychic energy audible to anything within twenty meters. Rhinameth patrols the boulder fields of Granite Heights, using its crystal ridge to scan for hidden memory-stones buried under rockslides.
stages.note: The crystal ridge on Rhinameth's back hums at a higher pitch the closer it gets to a buried memory-stone.

stages.name: Geomortax
stages.bio: Geomortax is a titanic dark-grey rhino armored head to tail in jutting amethyst crystal formations - great jagged purple shards crown its back and sides like a moving mountain range. Its horn is a massive violet spike and its eyes glow with steady purple psychic light. The ground trembles with each deliberate step. Ancient Granite Heights legend says Geomortax was present when Abalont first cracked the mountain - it absorbed the shockwave into its crystals and has held that memory ever since, waiting to give it back to the guardians.
stages.note: Every amethyst on Geomortax's body stores one memory; the largest spike - between its shoulders - holds the oldest one of all.

stages.name: Amethib
stages.bio: Amethib is a small bright-green lizard with a yellow underbelly and a single large purple amethyst horn jutting from its forehead. Its scales are smooth and vibrant, and its long tail curves behind it with a jaunty flick. In Shadow Caves' dim passages it uses its horn to scratch glowing grooves into the cave walls - these marks are actually directions back to safe ground, a habit it has never stopped. Hatchling Amehibs emerge from the cave rock itself, as if the stone decided to grow legs.
stages.note: The scratch-marks Amethib leaves on cave walls form a complete map of its territory - readable to other Amehibs but not to outsiders.

stages.name: Amethrock
stages.bio: Amethrock has grown dramatically - now a hefty dark green and purple chameleon with a ridged dorsal fin of spiky crystal crests running from neck to tail. Its curling tail is thick and strong, and its wide-set eyes swivel independently. It can shift its color between deep green and murky purple to vanish into the shadow cave walls. The crystal crests secrete a faint toxic residue that smells of wet stone; creatures that touch them directly feel their thoughts scramble briefly.
stages.note: Amethrock can freeze mid-step for up to forty minutes, perfectly mimicking a jagged stalactite - even experienced cave-walkers step past it.

stages.name: Amethyx
stages.bio: Amethyx stands as an imposing upright lizard-beast, its body covered in overlapping armored scales of deep green and dark stone-grey. A towering crown of thick amethyst crystals erupts from its head like a jagged throne, and its broad chest gleams with iridescent gem-shards embedded in the skin. Its heavy clawed hands could crush boulders. Deep in Shadow Caves, Amethyx is the unquestioned keeper of the darkest passages - other cave creatures step aside, and the shadows themselves seem to bow.
stages.note: The crystal crown on Amethyx's head absorbs toxic vapors and converts them into stored energy - it grows larger the deeper in the cave it lives.

stages.name: Amethoad
stages.bio: Amethoad is a squat green toad with a wide flat body, four stubby legs, and several round purple amethyst bumps clustered along its back like a little gem collection. Its large single eye - a startling magenta - dominates its face. In Amber Desert's night-cool sand hollows it hunkers low, using its gem bumps to absorb heat by day and release it slowly at night. Desert travelers find Amehtoad's bumps glow faintly in the dark - a warm, reassuring lighthouse in the dunes.
stages.note: Amethoad's gem bumps glow brightest at the exact temperature where scorpions become sluggish - desert travelers treat this as a safe-sleep signal.

stages.name: Gemsaur
stages.bio: Gemsaur is a broad green toad whose back now carries a dense cluster of large amethyst and purple gem formations that jut out like a cactus spine garden. Its wide body is low and powerful, and its single large eye now has a knowing squint. In Amber Desert it half-buries itself in sand with only its gems visible, luring heat-seeking creatures close - then exhales a toxic vapor puff that smells faintly of hot sand and wet stone. Ancient desert merchants used Gemsaur gem-patterns as natural compass markers.
stages.note: Gemsaur's gem cluster always points the same direction when it buries itself - desert navigators call this the 'poison star'.

stages.name: Amethyrex
stages.bio: Amethyrex has grown into an enormous wide-bodied toad with a full jewel crown of oversized amethyst gems replacing its head-bumps, earning its regal look. Its wide inflated throat-sac glows purple when it calls, and the force of its exhale can push a full grown adult backward three steps. In Amber Desert it sits at the center of oases like an ancient stone idol, and the poison vapors it exhales keep larger predators at a respectful distance. Legend says Amethyrex breathed out a whole valley of clear air when Abalont's shadow first touched the desert.
stages.note: When Amethyrex inflates its gem-ringed throat sac fully, the color tells the whole desert the next day's weather - purple for storm, amber for clear.

stages.name: Amethule
stages.bio: Amethule is a squat dark-purple toadlet armored in bumpy stone-textured skin with a crown of small black crystal spikes sprouting from its head like a tiny jagged halo. Its large amber eye glows with a warm psychic light. In Sand Dunes' windswept hollows it sits perfectly still among the dark stones, indistinguishable from pebbles until it blinks. Young Amethules are said to dream the memories of crystals buried deep in the dunes - waking up knowing paths that haven't been walked in centuries.
stages.note: Amethule can remain motionless for two days; experienced dune-walkers only spot it when its amber eye catches sunlight.

stages.name: Amethump
stages.bio: Amethump has grown into a wide dark-violet toad with a thick stone-grey belly and a substantial crest of purple crystal formations crowning its head and back. Its amber eye has deepened to a knowing gold-orange. When it sits on a dune summit at dusk, the crystal crest picks up fading sunlight and broadcasts it as a faint psychic warmth felt by all creatures within fifty meters - a sensation dune travelers describe as 'remembering somewhere safe'. It hoards knowledge the way other creatures hoard food.
stages.note: Any creature that rests within ten meters of Amethump wakes with at least one new clear memory it didn't have before - origin unknown.

stages.name: Amethyrax
stages.bio: Amethyrax is a massive low-slung dark stone toad armored completely in overlapping obsidian-dark rocky plates, its shoulders hunched wide and powerful. A tremendous crown of long jagged black-and-purple crystal spines erupts from its entire upper body, making it look like a walking boulder caught mid-explosion. Its wide golden eye burns with deep psychic intelligence. In Sand Dunes it sits at the edge of the ancient dune formations and broadcasts psychic memories of the dunes' past to any who approach - including warnings from the time before Abalont's coming.
stages.note: Amethyrax broadcasts a complete memory of the dunes as they existed five hundred years ago - dune cartographers call it 'the living map'.

stages.name: Anchorpup
stages.bio: Anchorpup is a stocky dark-grey crab with a rounded shell etched with anchor symbols and bright orange hair-like frills sprouting from its head and claws like a rocky sea-creature's crown. Two small anchor-engraved shields sit embedded in its shell. It scuttles sideways along the granite coastlines where Granite Heights meets the sea, wedging itself into rock crevices when the tide comes in. Young Anchorpups anchor themselves so firmly that fishermen have been known to mistake them for actual fixed harbor hardware.
stages.note: Anchorpup can lock its legs into a rock crack so tightly that twenty children pulling together cannot move it.

stages.name: Anchoreel
stages.bio: Anchoreel has grown into an imposing dark slate-blue crab with a massive ridged shell and three large decorative anchor-shields embedded across its back and claws. Its orange crest-frills have thickened into dense tufts around its eyes and flanks, giving it a wild salt-spray look. Its claws can grip ocean boulders bare enough to strip barnacles in one pull. In Granite Heights' tidal pools it acts as an anchor for smaller creatures during storms - they cling to its shell as it braces against currents that would sweep them away.
stages.note: In a gale, up to forty smaller creatures have been counted sheltering on a single Anchoreel's shell - it never seems to notice the weight.

stages.name: Colossamchor
stages.bio: Colossamchor is a fortress of a crab - massive dark stone body with a shell as thick as harbor walls, orange coral-frills cascading from its head and flanks, and enormous anchor emblems carved deep into its two front shields. Its claws could redirect a river. It stands at the granite cliffs where the great ocean meets the Heights, and the tide literally rises and falls a few centimeters differently when it shifts position. Ancient mariners built their first harbor walls by tracing the curve of a sleeping Colossamchor.
stages.note: The tidal rhythm at Granite Heights Cove has matched Colossamchor's breathing pattern for three hundred recorded years.

stages.name: Cellara
stages.bio: Cellara is a translucent pale-blue ghostly spider with a round glowing spherical body and six visible legs. Wispy blue flame-tendrils drift off its sides like phantom silk. Its round eyes glow a soft white-blue that casts dim light in Ghost Hollow's eternal murk. It drifts more than walks, hovering just above the hollow floor on barely-visible legs, trailing tiny ghost-light sparks. Children who spend time near Cellara report hearing fragments of words spoken long ago in Ghost Hollow - echoes the little spider has collected.
stages.note: Cellara stores sound fragments in its web - touching one strand of its web plays back a whispered word from Ghost Hollow's past.

stages.name: Spinell
stages.bio: Spinell has grown into a long-legged pale blue spectral spider whose translucent body reveals the faint outline of its internal structure like frosted glass. Electric-blue ghost-flames lick up from its joints, and its web strands carry a visible charge that makes hair stand on end when you brush near one. It hangs at the junctions of Ghost Hollow's oldest trees, weaving complex sound-traps - webs so precise that creatures who walk through them suddenly remember a word they had forgotten.
stages.note: Spinell's completed web contains exactly ninety-six strands - researchers have counted and recounted; it is never more or less.

stages.name: Nexarach
stages.bio: Nexarach is an unnerving skeleton-visible ghost-spider, its pale blue translucent body revealing every bone-like internal structure in eerie detail. Blue ghost-flames blaze at its joints and crown its head, and crackling electric arcs bridge its legs as it moves. Its web spans the full canopy of Ghost Hollow's oldest grove. When it speaks, every voice it has ever collected from the hollow plays back simultaneously as a layered ghostly chorus - the effect is beautiful and deeply unsettling in equal measure.
stages.note: Standing in Nexarach's web at midnight, a trainer hears the last word spoken by every guardian who ever entered Ghost Hollow.

stages.name: Spiderling
stages.bio: Spiderling is a small fuzzy warm-brown spider with eight spindly legs and large round amber eyes that glow with gentle curiosity. Its round abdomen is densely covered in soft earthy hair. In Bug Thicket's leaf-litter it scurries between plant roots, reading vibrations through all eight legs simultaneously. It is the only creature in the thicket that doesn't hide from approaching children - instead it moves deliberately closer, drawn by the psychic warmth of an interested mind.
stages.note: Spiderling reads the emotional state of anyone nearby through ground vibration - it sprints toward happiness and freezes still near fear.

stages.name: Arachex
stages.bio: Arachex is a formidable brown tarantula, dense with coarse hair over its full abdomen and legs. Its two front legs are noticeably longer and more articulate than the rest, used to 'read' surfaces the way a blind creature reads the world. Its multiple eyes carry a faint violet psychic gleam. In Bug Thicket it constructs webs around specific plant clusters it has identified as memory-holders - spots where words were spoken aloud enough times to leave a trace in the bark.
stages.note: Arachex won't eat in a spot where it senses lingering emotional distress - it seems to prefer that certain places stay peaceful.

stages.name: Vexarachne
stages.bio: Vexarachne is a large powerful spider with a dramatic dark purple body and vivid violet psychic energy crackling across its abdomen and between its legs. Its upper body is markedly heavier than its lower, giving it an imposing armored look. Its web construction is almost architectural - complex multi-level traps that serve as both home and library, storing psychic impressions of every creature and word that has ever crossed Bug Thicket's boundary. It is patient, brilliant, and deeply territorial.
stages.note: Vexarachne's web archive holds the psychic echo of every voice raised in Bug Thicket for the past thirty years - it will share them if approached respectfully.

stages.name: Spinkling
stages.bio: Spinkling is a tiny round purple spider with a plush soft body, eight orange-tipped legs, and wide innocent lavender eyes. Its small abdomen glows faintly in Verdant Valley's dappled shade. It spins webs between Akilla's old root paths - not to trap, but to feel every footstep nearby. Something about its soft purple color and wide eyes puts even nervous insects at ease. Local lore says Spinkling only takes up residence near places where kind words were spoken recently.
stages.note: A Spinkling web placed across a path at dusk vibrates at a different frequency for each size of creature that passes - Spinkling learned to read all of them.

stages.name: Spinnex
stages.bio: Spinnex has grown into a large brown-and-black banded tarantula with heavy muscular legs and a dense furry abdomen that catches light in dark bands. Its eyes no longer hold innocence - they hold calculation. In Verdant Valley it occupies the root-space beneath Akilla's old patrol routes, maintaining webs that serve as tripwires, mapping every creature that enters or leaves the valley floor. It has grown more comfortable in shadow than in light, and trainers sense it watching even when they cannot see it.
stages.note: Spinnex keeps a separate web for each creature family it has catalogued in its territory - currently over sixty distinct webs.

stages.name: Vexarantula
stages.bio: Vexarantula is an imposing purple-and-black armored spider with a massive dense body, thick reinforced legs, and a complex pattern of dark orb-markings across its abdomen. Its eyes are cold and intelligent - multiple red pupils watching different directions simultaneously. In Verdant Valley it claims the deepest shadow-root chambers, where it has woven a web-city spanning dozens of old tree hollows. It is not hostile without reason, but its dark instinct means it never fully trusts anything it hasn't studied for at least a season.
stages.note: Vexarantula's web-city maps have been used by cave explorers to chart underground root systems; the webs match geological surveys precisely.

stages.name: Spidlet
stages.bio: Spidlet is a round sandy-tan spider with a broad domed abdomen, eight moderate legs, and three pairs of glowing deep-red eyes arranged across its face. Its earth-toned body blends perfectly with Ghost Hollow's dead-leaf floor. The multiple red eyes give it eerie all-angle vision - trainers say you can never quite catch it looking at you, because it's always already looking. It spins short dense webs low to the ground, using them as tripwire alarms that wake it when anything larger than a moth approaches.
stages.note: Spidlet has six pairs of eyes that never all point the same direction; it has never been successfully startled in recorded history.

stages.name: Arachnode
stages.bio: Arachnode has grown into a wide low-slung brown spider with a large flat abdomen that presses close to the ground for maximum stealth. All six of its red eyes now glow with an active crimson intelligence. It constructs complex layered web networks across Ghost Hollow's root systems - not visible webs, but vibration-reading ones, buried just under the leaf litter. Creatures that walk through Ghost Hollow on Arachnode's route feel as if something is watching from every direction at once, because it is.
stages.note: Arachnode's underground vibration-web can identify a creature by its footstep weight alone - it has never misidentified in documented tests.

stages.name: Toxaranyx
stages.bio: Toxaranyx is a massive dark-stone spider armored in rough rocky-textured chitin plates the color of dried mud and shadow. It carries six sharp crimson eyes and thick blade-tipped legs that leave deep grooves in Ghost Hollow's earth when it walks. Its web is so dense in the deepest hollow that even light bends around it slightly. Ancient Hollow records describe Toxaranyx as 'the hollow's memory' - it has lived so long in the dark that it has become part of it, patient as stone, as difficult to move.
stages.note: Toxaranyx has not moved from its central hollow in an estimated eighty years - everything it needs simply comes to it, eventually.

stages.name: Webling
stages.bio: Webling is a compact black spider with a red hourglass mark on its abdomen and glowing red eyes that flicker like tiny embers. Near Dragon Spire's volcanic vents it lives in crevices where the rock stays warm year-round, using the heat as a hatchery for its eggs. It spins fire-resistant silk around the vent openings, and the silk glows faintly orange in the dark - a little warning lantern that dares other creatures to come close. Despite its intimidating coloring, young Spiderlings are shy and retreat from anything bigger than a pebble.
stages.note: Webling silk resists temperatures that would melt tin - Dragon Spire's forge-workers sometimes use it to reinforce heat-seals.

stages.name: Araneox
stages.bio: Araneox has grown into a sleek black spider with a larger, more prominent red hourglass marking and a web of glowing orange-red fire-silk that it maintains across Dragon Spire's lava-ledge overhangs. Its eyes burn a steady hot red. In a fight it snaps its legs together to generate friction sparks, igniting a quick fire-burst from its spinnerets. Forge-workers at Dragon Spire leave offerings of iron filings near Araneox's web - legend says it blesses the metal of anyone who respects its territory.
stages.note: Araneox fire-silk stays lit for up to three days without fuel - Dragon Spire's forge district uses it as emergency lighting during ash storms.

stages.name: Infernocrawl
stages.bio: Infernocrawl is an enormous black-armored spider wreathed in glowing orange lava-web strands that bridge its legs and spread outward like a living fire-trap. Its abdomen carries a blazing hourglass marking that pulses with heat, and its eyes burn like twin forge-coals. The web it casts across Dragon Spire's summit cracks acts as both territory marker and heat-barrier - lava flows have been recorded deflecting around Infernocrawl's anchor-web points. Ancient Spire lore says Infernocrawl was born the day the first volcano erupted, and will only sleep when the last one goes cold.
stages.note: Infernocrawl's anchor-silk is woven into Dragon Spire's main bridge supports - the bridge has stood without mortar for four hundred years.

stages.name: Sparkid
stages.bio: Sparkid is a round glassy spider with a large pale translucent globe body, six thin legs, and wisps of blue-white electric smoke drifting off its sides. Its wide eyes blink with tiny arc-flashes. In Steel Fortress's circuit-conduit passages it bounces between metal surfaces, building up charge with each contact. It communicates with other Sparkids by sending psychic pulses along the fortress's steel girders - the engineers discovered this when equipment started responding to thoughts rather than controls.
stages.note: Sparkid can transmit a full memory-image through any metal surface it touches - the target receives it as a vivid complete flashback.

stages.name: Voltarachne
stages.bio: Voltarachne is a sleek pale-violet spider with long articulate legs that arc blue electricity between their joints as it walks. Its segmented body carries a soft violet psychic glow. In Steel Fortress it maintains its own private network of conductive threads stretched across the fortress's upper infrastructure, processing and storing the psychic residue of every thought the fortress's inhabitants have ever had. Engineers sometimes leave hard problems near its web junction and find solutions sketched in condensed frost on the steel next morning.
stages.note: Voltarachne has solved seventeen previously unsolvable Steel Fortress engineering problems - always overnight, always without anyone watching.

stages.name: Cerebrawl
stages.bio: Cerebrawl is a magnificent large purple spider wearing what appears to be a glowing crown of pure psychic energy - a luminous ring that hovers just above its head. Its thick body is deep violet with neural-pattern markings, and its eight powerful legs leave faint arc-burns on any metal surface they touch. It sits at Steel Fortress's central control junction, where every conduit in the fortress connects, and processes all of it simultaneously. Visiting scholars describe standing near Cerebrawl as feeling every answer you ever needed suddenly sitting right at the edge of your thoughts.
stages.note: Cerebrawl's psychic crown contains a compressed map of Steel Fortress's entire neural-conduit network - it can reroute any circuit in the fortress from where it sits.

stages.name: Stellaby
stages.bio: Stellaby is a bright blue-and-gold fawn with a spiky electric mane, wide lime-green eyes, and a small five-pointed golden star glowing at the tip of its tail. Tiny lightning sparks dance off its pointed ears as it bounds across Storm Spire's high plateaus. It is relentlessly energetic and cannot stand still - each time it stops it paws the ground twice and immediately starts again. Its sparks leave tiny scorch-trails in the shape of constellations, and on clear nights Storm Spire's highest plateau looks like a star chart drawn in miniature.
stages.note: The scorch-trail constellation patterns Stellaby leaves match twelve actual star formations visible from Storm Spire - researchers debate whether it knows this.

stages.name: Cosmyx
stages.bio: Cosmyx has grown into a powerful deep-blue quadruped with a flowing golden electric mane that crackles with constant voltage. The golden star at its tail has grown larger and brighter, casting light in a wide arc when it runs. Its hooves strike gold sparks from Storm Spire's stone with each stride. It gallops the storm-ridge circuits at speeds fast enough to generate their own updraft, and small stormclouds form briefly in its wake. Trainers who bond with Cosmyx find their own thinking speeds up noticeably - a psychic spillover from its lightning-fast mind.
stages.note: Cosmyx's full-speed run generates a localized electrical field strong enough to power a small lamp for ten minutes afterward.

stages.name: Celesthorn
stages.bio: Celesthorn is a breathtaking gold-and-blue celestial beast with a massive flowing electric mane of lightning-white and gold, a blazing five-pointed star anchored to its tail, and golden horns that fork like lightning bolts from its brow. Its body radiates a warm electrical glow visible from the valley floor on storm nights. Ancient Storm Spire legends name Celesthorn as the creature that called the first lightning down from the sky to teach the guardians the power of words spoken boldly - the thunder was its answer.
stages.note: The lightning above Storm Spire strikes the same four points every storm; those four points mark exactly where Celesthorn stood when it last called down the sky.

stages.name: Chirplet
stages.bio: Chirplet is a small plump golden-yellow fledgling with rounded wing-stubs, a short beak, and wide dark eyes that gleam with intelligence above its oversized round head. Its fluffy yellow breast feathers trap wind and make it bounce slightly even on calm days. In Gale Ridge's lower cliff pockets it sits facing the prevailing wind with its beak open - not eating, but tasting the air, learning each note of the storm's voice. Chirplet's own song is a single pure note, held as long as its small lungs allow.
stages.note: Chirplet holds a single sung note for up to forty-five seconds without breathing - Gale Ridge musicians use it to tune their instruments.

stages.name: Goldwing
stages.bio: Goldwing has grown into a robust upright golden bird with a bright orange-yellow breast, neat compact wings, and a clarion singing voice that carries clear across Gale Ridge's upper platforms. It opens its beak wide when singing, projecting with surprising force for its size. It rides the thermal columns around the Ridge in long lazy spirals, releasing song-phrases that the wind carries and reshapes into new melodies a kilometer away. Gale Ridge guardians used Goldwing song-patterns as long-distance message codes.
stages.note: Goldwing's song changes rhythm depending on wind speed - researchers have mapped twenty distinct patterns, each encoding a different weather condition.

stages.name: Solstryx
stages.bio: Solstryx has expanded into a broad-winged golden raptor with wide spread wings that catch every sun-ray and convert it to lift. Its golden-amber plumage blazes in full light, and its open-winged display shows stripes of deeper bronze beneath. It soars the highest thermal arches above Gale Ridge without a single wingbeat for hours at a time. Its song is no longer a single note but a full harmonic chord - sung on the exhale into the storm's core and heard by creatures fifty kilometers in every direction.
stages.note: Solstryx soars for an average of six hours between wingbeats; the longest recorded continuous glide is eleven hours and forty minutes.

stages.name: Aurkit
stages.bio: Aurkit is a vivid green kitten with bright yellow-green spots scattered across its round body, a plump curved tail, and wide innocent teal eyes. Its soft jungle-green fur smells faintly of fresh leaves after rain. In Shadow Caves it is an unlikely inhabitant - it wanders in from the forest edge and seems genuinely unbothered by the dark, since its spots faintly glow in the absence of light. Young trainers find it irresistible, and Aurkit returns the affection by bumping its head against anyone who crouches down to its level.
stages.note: Aurkit's spots glow brighter when it learns a name it has never heard - a particularly bright flash means it understood something important.

stages.name: Aurfang
stages.bio: Aurfang has grown into a lithe and powerful green-and-gold leopard with large sunflower-pattern spots and bright sharp teal eyes that pierce the cave dark. Its muscles move smoothly under its sleek coat, and its claws click lightly on the cave floor. In Shadow Caves it has found its purpose - patrolling the boundary between the forest and the dark, guiding lost creatures back to the light. It carries the scent of jungle flowers into the deepest shadows, which is strangely comforting to creatures trapped in the dark.
stages.note: Aurfang's scent-trail through Shadow Caves leads outward, never inward - any creature that follows its smell finds the forest edge within ten minutes.

stages.name: Aurmawlix
stages.bio: Aurmawlix is a magnificent large jungle cat with emerald-and-gold spotted fur, powerful wide forequarters, and a dramatic pair of lush green leaf-wings unfurling from its shoulders like a forest canopy taking flight. Its mane is a rich tangle of deep green vines and glowing teal markings trace the lines of its face and sides. In Shadow Caves it stands as a living bridge between darkness and light - its wings carry the scent of the deep forest into places where the forest has never been, and creatures come out of the shadows to follow it home.
stages.note: When Aurmawlix opens its wings fully in Shadow Caves, photosynthesis occurs in the immediate vicinity - moss blooms on cave walls within minutes.

stages.name: Aurylet
stages.bio: Aurylet drifts through the shallows of Coral Bay like a living gem, its orange-and-white body trailing two small fan-shaped tail fins that shimmer with each flick. Large round eyes seem to read the water around it before it moves, as though it already knows where each current will go. Locals say that if Aurylet circles a tide pool three times, a new coral blossom will open there by morning. The guardians once used its shimmering fins as lanterns to find their way through night-dark coves.
stages.note: Aurylet circles a tide pool exactly three times before sleeping, never more, never fewer.

stages.name: Auryx
stages.bio: Auryx has grown a spectacular set of layered fan fins that spread wide like peacock feathers, edged in brilliant orange with blue eye-spots. It moves through the reef with unhurried grace, each fin stroke sending a ripple of visible thought outward - other fish part to let it pass without being touched. Auryx seems to sense the mood of the entire bay at once, surfacing when a storm is three hours out and guiding boats back to harbor with a trail of glowing bubbles.
stages.note: Sailors know a storm is coming when Auryx surfaces and beats its fan fins three times against the water.

stages.name: Auryxian
stages.bio: Auryxian rules the deep channels of Coral Bay, its enormous multi-layered fan fins now blazing orange and deep blue, edged with jewel-bright eye-spots that glow under full moonlight. When it surfaces, the sea goes flat for a hundred meters around it - every fish, crab, and coral creature turns to face it instinctively. Ancient fishers say Auryxian once guided the guardians' fleet through a fog so thick it swallowed the sun, navigating by the pulse of thought alone.
stages.note: When Auryxian spreads all its fins at once, every creature within sight freezes for a full breath before the spell breaks.

name: Aurykit

stages.name: Aurykit
stages.bio: Aurykit is a compact golden rabbit whose fur crackles with static whenever it hops, leaving tiny scorched footprints on the crystal mine floors. Its amber-orange eyes see clearly in the mine's pitch-dark tunnels, lit from within by a faint internal glow. Aurykit thumps its hind legs when it senses an electric charge building in a crystal vein - miners have learned to count its thumps to predict when a crystal will crack and flash. It bounces in tight excited circles every time it learns a new sound.
stages.note: Aurykit thumps exactly once per second when a crystal charge is building - miners count the thumps to stay safe.

stages.name: Aurybolt
stages.bio: Aurybolt has grown long powerful haunches and a sweeping lightning-bolt tail that arcs with visible electricity as it sprints. Its golden fur stands on end when it charges up, giving it a mane-like silhouette that glows warm amber in the mine's dim tunnels. Aurybolt can cover forty meters in a single leap, landing with a crack of static that temporarily illuminates the crystal walls. The guardians say that Aurybolt once raced ahead to warn a lost expedition, lighting the path by skidding along the crystal floor at full speed.
stages.note: Aurybolt's landing spark is bright enough to read by - miners' children use its leaps as lantern-light to find lost tools.

stages.name: Solauryx
stages.bio: Solauryx blazes through the Storm Spire like a living lightning strike, its long golden mane and flowing electric-bolt tail leaving bright afterimages burned into the crystal walls. Where it leaps, light floods the deepest shafts for hours afterward, charging the crystals around its path to a warm amber glow. The mine's guardian texts describe a hare of living sun-light that once drove Abalont's shadow from the deepest crystal chamber by running the full circumference of the mine in a single bound.
stages.note: The crystal walls near Solauryx's resting spots glow for three days after it leaves, preserving its warmth.

blurb: Aurykit hopped far from its burrow family. Help Aurykit find them again!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Riku.
facts: Rabbits have long ears that help them hear danger.
question: What helps rabbits hear danger?

stages.name: Aurkit
stages.bio: Aurkit trots through the Steel Fortress on four quick paws, its cobalt-blue fur threaded with gold-trim markings that light up faintly when it gets excited. Its fluffy yellow-orange tail wags so fast it becomes a blur, and small sparks trail off the tip whenever it wags near anything metal. Aurkit is drawn to the fortress's electrical conduits, pressing its nose against the walls and listening to the current hum inside. The fortress engineers discovered it could detect a failing cable before any instrument could - its ears flatten the moment a circuit wavers.
stages.note: Aurkit's tail sparks visibly the moment a nearby electrical circuit begins to fail - the fortress engineers call it the living fuse.

stages.name: Aurmane
stages.bio: Aurmane has grown a thick ruffled mane of gold-tipped fur that conducts electricity along each strand like a living antenna. Its blue flanks are now streaked with bright gold lightning patterns that flare when it picks up a charge. Aurmane prowls the fortress's outer walls at night, and sentries report seeing its mane light up the ramparts during storms. It discharges once before each thunderclap, as though answering the sky - the fortress soldiers say it never misses the count.
stages.note: Aurmane discharges its mane precisely one second before every nearby lightning strike - the fortress records no exceptions.

stages.name: Auralux
stages.bio: Auralux stands as broad as a steel gate, its magnificent mane of blue-gold fur cresting like a storm cloud permanently charged and ready. When it paces the fortress battlements, every metal surface within ten meters hums. Soldiers say its roar during an electrical storm shakes the fortress foundations and the attackers beyond the walls alike. The guardians' records describe Auralux as the Fortress Heartbeat - as long as it prowls the walls, no shadow of Abalont has ever breached the outer gate.
stages.note: When Auralux roars from the battlements, every weather vane in the fortress spins to face it, as though saluting.

stages.name: Azupling
stages.bio: Azupling is a round, wide-eyed blue chick with fluffy white belly-down and the oversized beak of a bird that fully intends to grow into it someday. Its tiny wing-stubs barely flutter when it tries to leap from one spire ledge to the next, yet it attempts the jump every morning without fail. The Dragon Spire's older creatures watch from above without interfering - they say each fall teaches it something a gentle push never could. Azupling is the first to peep in greeting when a new companion arrives at the spire's gates.
stages.note: Azupling attempts the same impossible ledge jump every dawn; it has never once succeeded and has never once stopped trying.

stages.name: Azuwing
stages.bio: Azuwing has earned its full feathers - crisp white chest and blazing blue wings with a sharp golden beak that knows how to carry the wind. It soars the updrafts of the Dragon Spire with the confidence of a creature that has already conquered every ledge it once dreamed of reaching. Azuwing acts as messenger between the spire's highest roosts and the valley below, arriving so quietly on an updraft that those it visits often only notice it when it speaks. It hovers above struggling travelers as a windbreak, though it never acknowledges doing so.
stages.note: Azuwing arrives so silently on an updraft that its shadow on the ground is the first sign it is there.

stages.name: Azuraptor
stages.bio: Azuraptor is a colossus of feather and gold-armored talon, its massive blue wings spanning the width of a storm. Chest plating the color of hammered brass catches the light as it descends, and its screech clears every cloud within sight. The Dragon Spire records state that Azuraptor once carried the Guardian Council's banner into the sky during Abalont's great assault, its wings generating a gale that turned the shadow tide back for a full day. It lands only on the highest spire point, and lower creatures instinctively hold still when its shadow passes.
stages.note: Azuraptor's wing-strike as it lands creates a downdraft that extinguishes every torch on the spire's upper levels at once.

name: Azukit

stages.name: Azukit
stages.bio: Azukit is a small blue-furred kitten dusted with darker blue spots and carrying a thin water-dripping tail that leaves wet paw-sized puddles wherever it wanders. Its wide eyes hold a distant look - not lost, but listening to something just below hearing. Azukit paws at the tide pools of Coral Bay for hours, not hunting but reading, as though each ripple carries a message. The guardians' diaries describe a small blue kit that sat at the water's edge and whispered the next day's weather to anyone who leaned in close enough.
stages.note: Azukit whispers the next day's wave height into the ears of sleeping tide-pool crabs - the crabs are always right.

stages.name: Azumaul
stages.bio: Azumaul stands taller now, its blue fur patterned with flowing wave-curl markings that shift like liquid in sunlight. Its slender curling tail drips constantly - not with weakness but with surplus - the water it carries seems to refill from somewhere unseen. Azumaul walks the reef's edge at high tide, occasionally pressing a paw to the surface and watching where the ripple travels, charting currents that would take a ship's navigator an hour to calculate. It has a habit of arriving precisely when it is needed and leaving before anyone can thank it.
stages.note: Azumaul's paw-print in wet sand can last through a full tide cycle without washing away - fishers mark it as lucky.

stages.name: Azuravox
stages.bio: Azuravox has grown into a broad-chested deep-blue lion whose entire body is mapped in scale-like wave patterns that ripple as it breathes. Its long flowing water-tail moves with the cadence of a slow ocean current, never still. When it speaks - a sound between a roar and a cresting wave - the sea answers with a swell that rocks every boat in Coral Bay. Ancient records say Azuravox once pushed back a tide that Abalont had drawn away to strand the guardians, holding the sea back with its body for three days until help arrived.
stages.note: Azuravox breathes in time with the tides - twice per day - and the coral reefs bloom visibly at each exhale.

blurb: Azukit got separated from its pack by the tide. Help Azukit get back to them!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Axon.
facts: A cat's whiskers help it feel things around it.
Cats can see well in the dark.
question: What helps a cat feel things?

stages.name: Azuspark
stages.bio: Azuspark dashes along the Steel Fortress's high parapet walls, its cobalt-blue fur trimmed in gold catching every crosswind and generating sparks where the current meets its skin. The orange tail flicks upward the moment a wind shift occurs - a reliable early-warning signal for the fortress's flag-crews. Azuspark is small enough to sprint through the maintenance tunnels beneath the walls, carrying messages faster than any signal drum. It snatches words from the air with visible delight, pausing mid-sprint to repeat a new one loudly before racing onward.
stages.note: Azuspark's tail lifts exactly three seconds before every wind shift - the fortress flag-crew never needs a weather-vane while it is on duty.

stages.name: Azurek
stages.bio: Azurek lopes the fortress ramparts with its thick ruffled gold-and-blue mane streaming behind it like a battle pennant. Every paw-strike on the stone produces a small crackle of static; on gusty nights its whole outline glows with a pale blue-gold corona. The fortress records show Azurek once ran the full perimeter - all three kilometers - in under two minutes during a crisis, its speed creating a visible shock-wave that stripped the banners clean from their poles. Soldiers leave scratch-behind-the-ear tributes on the west tower for good patrols.
stages.note: A single lap of the fortress by Azurek at full sprint creates a shock-wave still detectable on instruments in the inner courtyard.

stages.name: Azuranth
stages.bio: Azuranth stands broad and blazing at the fortress's highest point, its enormous electric mane whipping in the permanent wind that surrounds it. The gold-blue lightning markings on its flanks have deepened to near-white at the center, and its roar combines the crack of lightning with the howl of a gale into a single sound that empties the sky of birds for an hour. The fortress's oldest stones carry claw-marks where Azuranth sharpened its claws; the engineers consider the marks load-bearing.
stages.note: Azuranth's claw-marks on the fortress's eastern tower have never eroded in a thousand years - the stone around them is visibly reinforced.

stages.name: Scaldrak
stages.bio: Scaldrak is a stocky blue-scaled lizard whose back is lined with a vivid row of red and orange spines that glow with internal heat. It scrambles across the Lava Crater's cooled rock shelves with remarkable grip, using its broad claws to anchor against sudden steam vents. The spines puff up double when it is startled, making it look twice as fierce as it is. Scaldrak has a habit of licking the warm stones to taste where the heat is strongest, marking good basking spots with a single claw-scratch so it can find them again.
stages.note: Blazlet scratches a single claw-mark on each new basking stone to remember it - the crater walls are covered in its tiny record-keeping.

stages.name: Blazorn
stages.bio: Blazorn stands upright now, tall and barrel-chested, its blue scales hardened to near-ceramic and the red-orange spines along its back grown into a bold ridge that radiates heat visibly. A pair of forward-curving horn-like spines crown its head and it uses them to push through cooled lava flows that would stop most creatures cold. Blazorn is territorial about the Lava Crater's best thermal vents, and its deep guttural warning call rattles loose rocks from the crater walls. Young ones come to it to be warmed during the crater's rare cold nights.
stages.note: Blazorn's back-ridge radiates enough heat to soft-boil a stone egg in thirty minutes - crater birds use its sleeping body as a nest warmer.

stages.name: Infernazard
stages.bio: Infernazard is a mountain of scaled muscle and fire, its blue-armored body crowned with enormous bat-like wings that turn the air above the crater into a shimmering heat column when spread. The full ridge of blazing red-orange spines along its back glows like an open forge, and its tail sweeps cooled lava into spray with casual swings. Ancient guardians named it the Crater's Lock - as long as Infernazard nests at the Lava Crater's heart, the volcano's pressure holds steady, and Abalont's shadow cannot take root in the magma below.
stages.note: Infernazard's wing-spread over the crater creates a thermal column so strong that ash from the last eruption can still be found in orbit.

stages.name: Sparkit
stages.bio: Sparkit stands on two legs with disproportionately large paws and a crown of spiky amber fur that perpetually looks windswept by a fire that isn't there. It is quick to stand its ground, planting those oversized feet wide and huffing hot breath whenever it feels challenged - which is often. Sparkit patrols the edges of the Lava Crater as though it has been personally assigned to guard it, turning back slower creatures from paths that lead to unstable ground. It can't yet read the crater's danger signs as well as it thinks it can, but its instincts are already sharper than its size suggests.
stages.note: Sparkit plants its feet exactly at the safe boundary of every unstable lava shelf - geologists have verified it has never once been wrong.

stages.name: Inferox
stages.bio: Inferox has thickened into a powerfully-built upright dragon with amber-orange scales and a full ridge of heat-spines cresting its head and running down its neck. Its arms are heavy with muscle and its broad clawed hands can pry apart cooled lava slabs. Inferox roams the Lava Crater's mid-slopes, marking the territory boundaries with deep claw-gouges in the stone. When threatened, it stands fully upright, spreads its arms wide, and roars with enough force to send loose gravel skittering down the crater wall - a sound the guardians have recorded and called 'the crater speaking'.
stages.note: Inferox's claw-gouges in the crater walls mark the exact safe-zone boundary - even experienced crater scouts defer to them.

stages.name: Pyrosauron
stages.bio: Pyrosauron is a towering amber-orange dragon covered in thick overlapping scales like volcanic armour, with a crest of massive heat-spines along head and neck that blaze like a crown of live coals. Its enormous clawed hands could wrap around a stone column and crush it, and its tail leaves a scored channel in cooled lava wherever it drags. The guardians' records name Pyrosauron the Lava Heart - a creature born of the crater's own heat, who answered when the first guardians called for help and drove Abalont's shadow back into the cold places beneath the earth.
stages.note: Pyrosauron has stood at the Lava Crater's edge for longer than any map of it exists - every map uses its silhouette as north.

stages.name: Blazkit
stages.bio: Blazkit is a small blue armadillo with a rounded shell and a tuft of yellow spines along its back that stick out like a crown it hasn't grown into yet. It trundles across the Granite Heights with a rolling gait, tapping the rock with its blunt snout to listen for hollow spaces beneath. When it finds one, it marks the spot with a drool-print - an indispensable skill that the heights' miners quietly rely on. Blazkit rolls into a tight ball when startled but immediately unrolls to check if the danger was interesting enough to deserve a better look.
stages.note: Blazkit's snout-tap can locate a hollow rock cavity down to three meters - the Heights' miners follow its trail before drilling.

stages.name: Blazorm
stages.bio: Blazorm's shell has thickened into a heavy ridged dome the color of polished granite, and its yellow crest-spines have grown broad and flat like shields. It walks with its head low, powerful arms swinging, and can overturn a two-meter boulder without breaking its stride. The Granite Heights' communities know Blazorm by the perfectly smooth bowl-shaped depressions it leaves when it rests - pressed into solid rock. It does not sleep lightly; once it settles, not even a thunderstorm will wake it before it is ready.
stages.note: Blazorm's resting-bowl impressions in granite are smooth as polished marble - climbers use them as handholds on the sheer heights.

stages.name: Terrablazer
stages.bio: Terrablazer has grown so large and heavy that it no longer bothers walking overland - it bulldozes directly through the Granite Heights' stone, tunneling with the slow unstoppable force of a glacier. Its massive shell is now boulder-grey and its wide yellow spines flatten into plates as it plows forward. The Heights' surface is mapped in part by Terrablazer's tunnel network; whole communities have built over its passages without knowing. It surfaces once each season to check the sky, then disappears again, leaving a crater-like depression behind.
stages.note: Terrablazer's seasonal surfacing craters are precise enough that the Granite Heights' farmers use them as irrigation channels.

stages.name: Sproutwit
stages.bio: Sproutwit is the roundest, fluffiest thing in all of Gale Ridge - a ball of warm brown feathers with two alert eyes and a tiny branch-sprig growing from the top of its head like an antenna. It cannot yet manage a proper flight; it hops between the low moss-covered boulders and glides on updrafts for one or two meters before landing with a soft plop. Sproutwit listens with its whole body - turning to every new sound, tilting its twig-antenna in the direction of each unfamiliar sound until it has heard it at least five times and decided whether it likes it.
stages.note: Sproutwit's head-twig tilts toward any new sound it hears - it has been seen tilting back and forth between two arguing spire-keepers for twenty minutes.

stages.name: Thornhoot
stages.bio: Thornhoot has grown from puffball to proper owl - sharp amber eyes under a furrowed brow and a small leafy crown sprouting from its head that fans out in strong winds. It perches on Gale Ridge's exposed rock fingers and rides the storm winds with patient, barely-moving wings, reading every gust the way a seasoned traveler reads a map. Thornhoot hoots twice before each weather change - the spire's bell-keepers ring the storm-warning bell only after they hear it. It collects bright-colored storm debris and arranges it near its roost in order of how interesting each piece is.
stages.note: Thornhoot hoots exactly twice before every wind-direction change at the spire; no instrument has recorded the change faster.

stages.name: Verdanthoot
stages.bio: Verdanthoot spreads wings so wide that their shadow covers the full Gale Ridge lookout platform, the elaborate leaf-vine crown on its head now a full canopy of living growth that blooms in good weather and closes tight before a dangerous storm. Its deep powerful hoot carries across the spire and down to the valley below, shaping the wind it rides as much as riding it. The guardians wrote that Verdanthoot is the Gale Ridge's living weathervane and memory - it has witnessed every storm since the spire's first stone was laid, and remembers them all.
stages.note: Verdanthoot's crown blooms or closes twelve hours before each weather change - more accurate than any forecast the spire's scholars have managed.

stages.name: Budscale
stages.bio: Budscale is a pale cream-and-green lizard with a vivid row of flower-petal-like spines cresting its back in blue, green, and yellow - a startling bloom of color on an otherwise quiet creature. It prowls the cooled lava margins of the crater where green things first push through cracked stone, eating the tender sprouts before they fully open. Budscale is remarkably hard to spot on volcanic rock until it flares its spine-crest in alarm, at which point it becomes impossible to miss. Young ones in a clutch always flare in sequence, creating a traveling wave of color along the whole group.
stages.note: When a group of Budscale flare their crests in sequence, the wave travels at exactly the speed of a walking human - no one knows why.

stages.name: Florasaur
stages.bio: Florasaur has grown upright and angular, its spine-crest now a full ridge of sharp purple and green thorns that extend and vibrate when it roars. The pale scales have deepened to a mottled green-yellow, and it moves with the sudden-start pace of a creature that is very still and then very fast. Florasaur claims a stretch of the Lava Crater's green margin as its territory, enforcing it with a spine-flash and a sharp hiss that most creatures respect without further negotiation. It is fond of rearranging its territory's rocks into rough rings - no one has determined why.
stages.note: Florasaur's rock rings are perfectly round within a centimeter - crater geologists have been quietly measuring them for years.

stages.name: Thorndrake
stages.bio: Thorndrake is a towering dark-scaled dragon whose enormous purple spike-mane rises from head to mid-back like a fortress palisade. The pale colouring is entirely gone - it has become all shadow-green and black with deep purple thorns that flex and clack when it breathes. Thorndrake is the Lava Crater's most unlikely guardian: a creature born of growing things that chose to root itself in fire, covering the green margins against Abalont's shadow by growing too fierce to be approached. It is said that where Thorndrake holds its ground, the first flowers through the lava never stop blooming.
stages.note: The patch of green below Thorndrake's regular resting spot is the most fertile ground in the entire Lava Crater - nothing there has ever died.

stages.name: Pigmote
stages.bio: Pigmote is a round brown boar-pup with a broad flat snout it uses to bulldoze through Sand Dune hillocks like a miniature plow. Rows of flat armored plates have already begun forming across its back, and two small rounded tusks poke out from a perpetually grumpy expression. It is surprisingly fast for its shape, and covers a lot of ground each day in a zigzag pattern as it roots for buried seeds and stone beetles. Pigmote does not share its food and will sit on anything edible it hasn't finished yet to stop others from reaching it.
stages.note: Pigmote sits on its unfinished food to save it for later - the dunes are dotted with its small flat depressions.

stages.name: Tuskling
stages.bio: Tuskling's back is now fully covered in overlapping stone-colored armor plates that clatter faintly as it moves, and its tusks have lengthened into forward-curving weapons that leave clean arcs in the dune sand when it charges. It tests every new piece of ground by stamping once before committing its full weight - a habit that has saved it from hidden sinkhole traps on dozens of occasions. Tuskling does not back down, but it is patient about choosing when to go forward, studying obstacles with small piggy eyes until it has a clear plan.
stages.note: Tuskling stamps once on every new surface before crossing - no Tuskling has ever fallen through a sand sinkhole.

stages.name: Boarthon
stages.bio: Boarthon is a walking stone fortress on four tree-trunk legs, its entire back covered in a fused shell of spiked rock plates and its tusks grown into great sweeping weapons that can carve a channel through a dune in a single pass. The ground shakes in rings when it walks, and approaching sand dunes visibly shift as the compression wave moves ahead of it. Boarthon is the Sand Dunes' unmovable anchor - when Abalont's shadow rolled across the dunes, Boarthon simply stood still in its path and did not move for nine days until the shadow went around it.
stages.note: Boarthon has stood completely still in the same spot for recorded periods of up to nine days - the dune shifts around it, not through it.

stages.name: Boxkit
stages.bio: Boxkit is a young kangaroo with a small pouch and two oversized paws wearing what can only be described as round orange boxing mitts that it was apparently born with. It bounces through Light Grove's open meadows practicing combinations on air, on trees, and on any companion patient enough to hold still. Boxkit has excellent balance - it can bob and weave before its hind legs even decide to commit to a direction. It keeps a small collection of interesting pebbles in its pouch and examines each one after every training session, rating them by feel.
stages.note: Boxkit rates every pebble in its collection after training - the ones it keeps longest are always perfectly round.

stages.name: Boxbound
stages.bio: Boxbound has outgrown the orange mitts - its hands are now powerful bare knuckles with the kind of reach that makes every other creature in Light Grove keep a polite distance. It stands tall and lean, still bouncing from foot to foot in a way that suggests it is always ready and never quite still. Boxbound uses the grove's trees as sparring posts, and the ones it trains on have grown visibly thicker on the impact side. It is a surprisingly patient teacher for younger creatures, demonstrating combinations at half-speed with grave concentration before bounding off to try them at full power.
stages.note: The trees Boxbound trains on have grown measurably thicker on the side it strikes - the grove's oldest trees record its entire training history.

stages.name: Pugalist
stages.bio: Pugalist stands wrapped in combat tape from knuckle to elbow like a veteran who has fought every worthy challenger in Light Grove and earned the right to stop doing the wrapping elegantly. Its massive tail is a rudder and a weapon both; a full swing can redirect a wind gust enough to clear the grove's canopy. The guardians' texts call Pugalist the Grove's First Fist - a creature who understood that the strongest defense of a peaceful place is one fighter who loves peace enough to be very good at fighting. It mentors the next generation by watching silently from above until it is needed.
stages.note: Pugalist has never struck first in any recorded encounter - it always delivers exactly one warning hoot before responding.

stages.name: Brahling
stages.bio: Brahling is a bright green caterpillar whose most striking feature is the glowing blue gem set into its forehead like a third eye that it cannot yet fully control. It blinks with all three eyes at different rates, creating a rhythm that the Crystal Mines' other creatures seem to find oddly calming. Brahling inches along the crystal veins in the mine walls, pressing its forehead gem against each crystal to listen - the gem briefly amplifies the crystal's natural hum to something audible. It is extraordinarily patient and will wait motionless for an hour for the right vibration.
stages.note: Brahling's forehead gem glows brighter near high-grade crystal deposits - miners call it the living dowsing rod.

stages.name: Brahman
stages.bio: Brahman has transformed completely - from crawling green larva to a tall graceful deer whose hide shimmers in green-and-gold crystal patterns and whose antlers are formed entirely of glowing crystal branches. It moves through the Crystal Mines with soundless delicacy, its hooves barely ringing on the stone, and tilts its antlered head to catch the light refracting from the walls. Brahman can broadcast the mines' crystal-hum as a visible light, briefly illuminating entire caverns when it raises its head. The mine workers leave gifts of polished crystals at its trail crossing.
stages.note: Brahman's antlers broadcast the mines' crystal-hum as light when raised - the deepest shafts have never needed lanterns where it walks.

stages.name: Divyahm
stages.bio: Divyahm is a magnificent towering stag whose full crown of golden crystal antlers reaches the ceiling of all but the Crystal Mines' grandest chambers, blazing with a warm amber-gold light that fills every crack and shadow in a hundred-meter radius. Gem-bright markings run from snout to tail in perfect symmetry, and when it breathes out, its breath carries a visible shimmer that settles into the mine walls as an iridescent residue. The guardians' oldest texts speak of Divyahm as the Mines' Memory - a creature who recorded every promise made in the crystal walls so nothing would be forgotten even if Abalont came.
stages.note: The iridescent residue of Divyahm's breath on crystal walls holds a clear impression of every voice raised near it for the past century.

stages.name: Piglet
stages.bio: Piglet is a compact brown boar-pup covered in coarse wiry bristles that stand up along its spine like a tiny hedgehog trying to pass as a boar. It snuffles through the lower slopes of Granite Heights with its flat snout pressed to the stone, listening for hollow cavities and cracking rock. Piglet always runs into obstacles slightly too fast, as though surprised by their continued existence, then huffs, backs up, and runs into them again with increased conviction. The Heights' stone-masons have noticed that places Piglet butts against repeatedly tend to crumble eventually - a slow but reliable demolition service.
stages.note: Piglet has demolished more granite outcrops by repeated insistent headbutting than any tool in the Heights' masonry yard.

stages.name: Briskhog
stages.bio: Briskhog has broadened into a powerful boar with a dramatic crest of long pointed bristle-spines running from crown to rump, giving it a silhouette like a walking mountain ridge. Its tusks are now properly intimidating, and it uses them to lever boulders that would take three people to move. Briskhog is dogged in its habits: it takes the same paths daily and responds to any change in its route with visible displeasure, marking the problem obstacle with a deep tusk-gouge before working out how to deal with it. The Granite Heights' goat-herders follow its worn paths as the safest trails.
stages.note: Briskhog's daily patrol paths have been used as the Granite Heights' official trail maps for longer than any surveyor has been practicing.

stages.name: Ironhusk
stages.bio: Ironhusk is a massively armored boar-titan whose entire body is plated in fused stone-and-hide panels that ring when struck as though cast in iron. The bristle-spines have become rigid stone-ridges, and its tusks are each as long as a young tree. Ironhusk moves across the Granite Heights like a slow landslide - inevitable and patient. The guardians' texts describe it as the Heights' Foundation: a creature who drove itself so deep into the granite that the mountain could not fall while Ironhusk stood within it, holding the heights steady against Abalont's tremors.
stages.note: Ironhusk's footprints in granite measure two centimeters deep - geologists use them as pressure benchmarks for the region's rock surveys.

stages.name: Bristlet
stages.bio: Bristlet is a small dark-brown boar-pup covered in shaggy layered fur that seems perpetually damp from the fog of Ghost Hollow. Its eyes are small, bright, and intensely watchful, missing nothing in the dim undergrowth. Bristlet communicates primarily by listening - it goes utterly still when anything interesting is happening nearby, processing the sounds and scents before deciding whether to approach or melt back into the shadows. It leaves no tracks on Ghost Hollow's soft floor; its passage is known only by the faint scent of damp earth that lingers at shin-height.
stages.note: Bristlet leaves no tracks on soft ground - the only sign it was present is a faint cold-earth scent at ankle height.

stages.name: Bristor
stages.bio: Bristor has grown into something out of a hollow-tale - a long, low, bristle-covered beast with a wide jaw of over-large teeth and a permanent snarl that it wears as a default expression. Its dark spines are thick and stiff, catching on branches and making a distinctive rattle as it moves through Ghost Hollow's thickets, though somehow it is still surprisingly hard to spot until it is very close. Bristor does not chase prey - it positions itself and waits, with the unhurried confidence of something that knows the Hollow better than anything else alive.
stages.note: Bristor waits in the same three ambush positions every night - the Ghost Hollow's sentinels have mapped them and use them as safe-path waypoints.

stages.name: Thorvusk
stages.bio: Thorvusk is the Ghost Hollow's darkest secret - a massive armored beast with a back forested in huge dark spines that creak in the fog like old timber, and enormous interlocking tusks that it clacks together before it charges. It is so perfectly adapted to the Hollow's eternal dim that it casts no visible shadow of its own, and the fog seems to part around it rather than cling. Ancient records describe Thorvusk as the Hollow's Gate: a creature that stands between the living world and whatever lies deeper in the dark, allowing nothing Abalont sent through to pass the other way.
stages.note: Thorvusk casts no visible shadow in Ghost Hollow's fog - the fog simply moves to fill the space it occupies.

stages.name: Bubkin
stages.bio: Bubkin is a round, small, purple creature with stubby fins and a large glowing pink bubble on top of its head that bobs when it moves, as though independently alive. It inhabits the Shadow Caves' quieter pools and tunnels, moving in a gentle slow-drift that belies how quickly it can vanish into the dark when startled. The bubble on its head pulses with a faint psychic light that other shadow-cave creatures find oddly soothing - Bubkin seems to produce it involuntarily as a by-product of thinking hard. It thinks very hard, very often.
stages.note: Bubkin's head-bubble pulses in time with its thoughts - the faster it pulses, the harder it's concentrating on something only it can see.

stages.name: Toadburst
stages.bio: Toadburst has expanded considerably - a wide, bumpy purple toad with several smaller glowing pink bubble-growths covering its back that pop and reform throughout the day. Each pop releases a brief psychic shimmer visible in the dark caves, and a faint sweet-and-wrong smell that is technically toxic but at cave-toad concentrations only produces an unusual sense of déjà vu. Toadburst sits in the same spot for days at a time, watching the cave's drip-patterns with absolute focus. The shadow creatures of the cave have learned to let it be - disturbing it mid-observation produces a triple-pop that leaves everyone confused about what day it is.
stages.note: Disturbing Toadburst mid-observation produces a triple-bubble-pop that causes a brief psychic disorientation lasting roughly one minute.

stages.name: Toxotaur
stages.bio: Toxotaur fills a cave chamber the way a thundercloud fills a sky - its massive broad body covered in large luminous pink bubble-nodules that glow and pulse with a rhythm that seems to sync with the heartbeat of anyone in the room. The psychic shimmer it broadcasts is now strong enough to cast visible shadows behind objects. In Ghost Hollow lore it is called the Dream-Lock: a creature that traps Abalont's shadow-agents in looping visions of words they never learned, keeping them confused and harmless in the deepest cave passages until the guardians can deal with them.
stages.note: Anything that enters Toxotaur's glow-radius without specific intent will spend the next hour convinced it has forgotten a very important word.

stages.name: Bublet
stages.bio: Bublet is an icy-blue pufferfish with a permanently disgruntled expression that it earned the day it was born and has maintained ever since. Its smooth round body is lightly textured like dimpled sea-glass and its small mouth is set in a downward curve of complete skepticism about everything. Bublet inhabits the cold-current channels of Frozen Peaks, where the icy upwellings keep the water clear and brisk. It has a habit of puffing up slightly - not full, just enough to communicate displeasure - whenever anything passes too close to the particular patch of current it has decided is its.
stages.note: Bublet's territory consists of exactly one cold-current patch two meters wide - it has never expanded it or abandoned it.

stages.name: Buboink
