stages.bio: Buboink has grown a proper set of short, sharp spines across its body that it deploys in a ring when threatened, each one carrying a thin coating of ice that freezes anything pressing against it. Its expression has not improved with size - if anything, the larger face provides more surface area for displeasure. Buboink guards the cold-channel entrances of Frozen Peaks with the humorless efficiency of a toll collector who has never once been surprised to find someone trying to sneak past. It inflates to full size at the first sign of any trespass and holds it until the trespasser has been gone for at least five minutes.
stages.note: Buboink remains fully inflated for exactly five minutes after a trespasser leaves its territory - it has been measured repeatedly.

stages.name: Behemoth
stages.bio: Behemoth is an enormous ancient pufferfish whose spines have grown into long crystalline ice-lances covering every surface, and whose fully-inflated form is wide enough to plug a glacial outflow entirely. It is deeply grumpy in the way that only very old things that have watched everything go wrong for a very long time can be. Behemoth holds station in the deepest meltwater trench under Frozen Peaks, and the whole range's temperature stays stable as long as it rests there. The peaks-folk say the day Behemoth leaves its trench the thaw begins - and they are probably right.
stages.note: Behemoth has occupied the same meltwater trench for so long that the lakebed has permanently depressed around it by two meters.

stages.name: Sporoling
stages.bio: Sporoling is a squat purple toad whose head is dominated by a cluster of eye-stalks - each one a different height, peering in a different direction simultaneously, with a single large forward-facing eye at the center that never blinks. This gives it near-complete vision in all directions at once, which makes sneaking up on a Sporoling essentially impossible. It lives in the Bug Thicket's damp floors, where the soil exhales spore-clouds that it seems to navigate by tasting with its wide flat tongue. Other creatures in the thicket avoid crossing its line of sight - not because it is dangerous, but because being stared at from seven angles at once is disconcerting.
stages.note: Sporoling has seven independent eye-stalks each tracking a different quadrant - it has never been documented failing to notice something moving near it.

stages.name: Bulbwart
stages.bio: Bulbwart is heavier and wider now, its purple skin raised in bumps and nodules that each contain a smaller secondary eye peering outward. Combined with its central eye-stalks, it maintains close to three hundred degrees of visual coverage simultaneously, and can process all of it. Bulbwart moves slowly and deliberately through the Bug Thicket, broadcasting a low psychic field that makes insects within ten meters instinctively stop moving - a foraging advantage so efficient it doesn't need to hurry. The thicket's more sensitive creatures say being near a Bulbwart feels like standing very close to an extremely interested audience.
stages.note: The secondary eyes in Bulbwart's skin nodules can each be focused independently - researchers have documented it watching five separate insects simultaneously.

stages.name: Mycodrak
stages.bio: Mycodrak is a low-slung colossus of purple warty hide and clustered eye-growths, its body so wide it fills the Bug Thicket's broadest clearings. Every raised nodule on its back is a functioning eye; its psychic field has grown so strong that insects within thirty meters freeze entirely when it broadcasts, and larger creatures experience a strong involuntary impulse to hold still and consider whether they really needed to walk this way. The guardians' records describe Mycodrak as the Thicket's All-Seer: a creature that has observed every living thing in the Bug Thicket for centuries and holds the knowledge of each in its silent eyes.
stages.note: Mycodrak's psychic still-field has been measured by researchers at up to thirty meters - no instrument has yet located its outer edge.

stages.name: Bullpup
stages.bio: A stocky little pup with iron-grey fur and a chunky flat face, Bullpup wears a red spiked collar that jingles softly as it trots. Its paws are oversized for its body, and it carries its wide head low, sniffing every shadow for hidden dangers. In Ghost Hollow it is said Bullpup was once a guardian spirit's watchdog - it still circles whatever it loves three times before settling, as though guarding an invisible perimeter.
stages.note: Bullpup circles any new friend three times before sitting - an old guard-spirit habit it never outgrew.

stages.name: Bullyx
stages.bio: Bullyx stands wide and low, its grey-plated body now studded with short iron spines along its back. The red collar has grown thick as a chain, and a single spiked ball hangs from its neck like a trophy it earned in the hollow's mist. It walks with a deliberate, heavy-pawed swagger and holds its wrinkled muzzle slightly open, letting fog curl between its teeth. Rivals give it a wide path along Ghost Hollow's stone bridges.
stages.note: The iron spines on Bullyx's back vibrate in response to nearby dark energy - a built-in haunting detector.

stages.name: Ironbull
stages.bio: Ironbull is built like a boulder with legs - wide, low, and covered in thick iron-ridged plating from snout to haunches. Its body bristles with rows of iron spines, and the spiked collar is now forged so deeply into its neck it seems carved from the creature itself. In Ghost Hollow's deepest mists, Ironbull does not growl to warn - it simply appears, eyes red and unblinking, between whatever it guards and whatever threatens it. Guardians say its shadow can hold a ghost in place.
stages.note: Ironbull's footsteps cause the fog of Ghost Hollow to part in two neat walls - it has walked these paths so long the mist knows to move.

stages.name: Sproutoad
stages.bio: Sproutoad is a round little toad the colour of wet soil, with a single white-budded sprout growing from between its eyes like a tiny candle. Its wide eyes blink slowly, and it sits almost perfectly still, watching. The sprout bobs when Sproutoad is excited and folds flat when it senses something creeping in the cave dark. Explorers in Shadow Caves use its flickering bud as a dim lantern, tiptoeing behind it through the blackest passages.
stages.note: The bud on Sproutoad's head glows faintly for about three seconds whenever it hears a name it has never heard it recognises.

stages.name: Thornogre
stages.bio: Thornogre has grown into something half-toad, half-thicket - its warty green hide is draped in rough leaf-layers, and a wild crown of thorned vines spirals from its head. A curling vine-tail trails behind it as it lumbers through the cave undergrowth. Its mouth stretches almost ear-to-ear, and it uses its long tongue not just to catch prey but to taste the air for the bitter scent of dark-energy surges. Shadow Caves explorers call it the gatekeeper of the deep passages.
stages.note: Thornogre never loses its way in the caves - it reads the dark with its tongue the way others read signs with their eyes.

stages.name: Verdewrath
stages.bio: Verdewrath is vast and low-slung, its body half-buried in its own wild moss and dark-vine growth. Glowing green vapour seeps from the dense tangle on its back, and its enormous flat head is nearly obscured by the living canopy it carries. It does not hunt - it simply opens its cavernous mouth and waits, patient as the cave itself, for the dark to bring things to it. Old tales say Verdewrath once swallowed a whole shadow-curse and slept for a century while the caves slowly brightened around it.
stages.note: The green vapour rising from Verdewrath's back is mildly sleep-inducing - visitors often wake up somewhere safer than where they started.

stages.name: Burmite
stages.bio: Burmite is a small, perfectly round green toad with a single leaf-bud antenna bouncing from its head. It has wide shiny eyes and a calm, settled posture - it sits on the warm sand of the dunes like a little green stone with opinions. The antenna flickers up in dry heat, drawing a tiny drop of moisture from the air. Dune travellers say stumbling on a Burmite means there is groundwater close beneath your feet.
stages.note: Burmite's antenna can sense underground moisture up to two metres down - desert guides treat it like a living well-finder.

stages.name: Burmoth
stages.bio: Burmoth has grown wide and solid, its smooth green hide now speckled with sandy earth tones. Three white-tipped antennae crown its head, bobbing in the desert breeze, and its sturdy legs end in broad flat pads that let it walk on loose sand without sinking. It digs shallow burrows each night and fills them with dew collected on its antennae. The blooms it leaves behind mark safe overnight stops for those who travel the Sand Dunes.
stages.note: Each Burmoth fills three small burrows with dew-water overnight - small desert creatures follow it like a moving oasis.

stages.name: Burmatog
stages.bio: Burmatog is a wide, heavy toad whose entire back has become a living garden of green spines and pale bloom-pods that release a faint sweet pollen on the desert wind. Its broad flat body presses close to the earth, and each slow step sends a vibration through the sand that is felt twenty paces away. When it calls at dusk, every plant within earshot unfurls a bloom in answer - as though the desert is responding to a word it has been waiting a very long time to hear.
stages.note: Burmatog calls at dusk every day without fail; botanists have confirmed the sand-bloom cycle follows its cry to the minute.

stages.name: Burrit
stages.bio: Burrit is a soft yellow furred creature with an outsized pointed snout and two enormous flat claws - almost bigger than its body - held out in front like a pair of tiny shovels. Its small round eyes blink owlishly in the light; it spends most of its life underground and finds the open air of Granite Heights startlingly bright. When it stumbles on the surface, it sits back on its haunches, claws spread wide, head tilting left and right as it tries to make sense of the world above.
stages.note: Burrit can excavate a tunnel the length of a classroom in under an hour - and usually forgets which end it started from.

stages.name: Burrixe
stages.bio: Burrixe is a powerful, compact earth-digger with golden-brown fur and claws that have hardened into ridged stone-edged scoops. It hunches low, using those massive forelimbs to pull through granite with surprising ease, leaving perfectly round tunnels behind. Its snout has lengthened and now tapers to a point tipped with a tough keratin tip for probing rock seams. Miners in Granite Heights follow Burrixe tunnel networks - they reliably lead to crystal pockets.
stages.note: Burrixe leaves a faint sulphur-and-stone scent at every tunnel fork that guides other Burrixe out of dead ends.

stages.name: Terravix
stages.bio: Terravix is armoured in overlapping plates of compressed earth and stone, its claws now truly massive - each one longer than a child is tall. It does not simply dig; it reshapes the rock of Granite Heights according to some slow intention, rerouting underground rivers and opening new caverns that no map has ever recorded. Its long snout rests close to the ground as it moves, reading the mountain's heartbeat through vibration. The heights themselves seem to breathe differently when Terravix is near.
stages.note: Every tunnel Terravix makes is perfectly circular - geologists cannot explain how a living creature achieves such geometric precision.

stages.name: Burvil
stages.bio: Burvil is a plump, jewel-purple toad with wide golden eyes and a skin covered in smooth rounded warts that catch the amber desert light. It sits on warm rocks looking both pleased and suspicious. Its slightly toxic skin keeps predators at a respectful distance, and Burvil takes full advantage of this - it moves at whatever pace it chooses and parks itself wherever it likes. Amber Desert wanderers say a Burvil blocking the path means the route beyond is safe; it would not sit somewhere risky.
stages.note: Burvil's purple skin deepens to violet in high heat - desert travellers read its colour like a temperature gauge.

stages.name: Burvox
stages.bio: Burvox is a broad, heavy toad whose purple hide is now dotted with raised golden-yellow warts that secrete a mild amber venom when squeezed. Its golden eyes have grown wide and flat, giving it nearly three hundred degrees of vision, and its four sturdy legs end in wide splayed toes perfect for gripping desert stone. It is slow but utterly unbothered - nothing in the Amber Desert chooses a fight with Burvox twice. It settles into the same sunny rock face each morning like a regular visitor at a favourite café.
stages.note: Burvox returns to the exact same rock to bask every sunrise; researchers have tracked the same individual to the same boulder for eleven consecutive years.

stages.name: Burvexor
stages.bio: Burvexor is a desert titan - wide as a boulder, its purple-and-amber body so studded with raised venom warts that it looks like a living amber mine. The warts have grown large and ridged with dark edges, and a faint amber haze clings to its back in hot midday air. It does not move quickly, but when it settles and presses its wide flat body to the earth, the desert around it goes silent. Amber Desert myths say Burvexor was here before the first sand - it just let the desert grow around it.
stages.note: Burvexor has been recorded sitting completely still for up to six days, motionless enough that rare desert birds build nests in its wart ridges.

stages.name: Calbux
stages.bio: Calbux is a sturdy brown calf with a white-patched face and a gently determined look. Its small horns are just nubs, and white markings on its brow form an almost-cross shape. It trots through the Crystal Mines with surprising confidence for something so young, sniffing at crystal outcroppings and tapping them with one hoof to hear the ring. Miners say Calbux brings good luck to new excavations - it has an uncanny habit of standing precisely above the richest crystal veins.
stages.note: Calbux taps any crystal three times before walking on - the third tap is always the one that rings clearest, and miners mark that spot.

stages.name: Taurox
stages.bio: Taurox is a powerful, deep-chested bull with a wide head, broad sweeping horns, and a dark brown striped hide that has begun to take on the warm shine of polished stone. The white cross-mark on its face has grown bolder. It lowers its head when thinking and raises it sharply when it has decided - a motion the Crystal Mines dwarfs have learned to read as clearly as speech. Once Taurox chooses a direction, no other creature in the mine tries to redirect it.
stages.note: Taurox's horns vibrate at a barely audible frequency near large crystal deposits - cave explorers have learned to hold a hand near each horn to navigate.

stages.name: Minothor
stages.bio: Minothor stands like a living monument - a great bull whose rocky striped hide has fused with the crystal lattice of the mines, and whose enormous cross-marked face radiates a quiet, unshakeable authority. Its horns span wide enough to block a tunnel entrance, and its slow movements cause crystals on the walls to hum sympathetically. Old Crystal Mines legends say Minothor was the first guardian to find the light beneath the stone, and that it still walks the deepest passages, ensuring the mines never go entirely dark.
stages.note: Every crystal within fifteen metres of Minothor brightens noticeably - miners have mapped the whole mine just by following its light-wake.

stages.name: Buzzite
stages.bio: Buzzite is a soft round bee with large violet eyes and small, pale translucent wings that flutter in a constant trembling hover. Its fuzzy yellow-and-black body is patterned neatly, and it holds its two tiny forelegs together as though always about to ask a polite question. It drifts through Bug Thicket in small clusters, leaving faint trails of psychic pollen that makes other creatures feel briefly remembered - like they have just heard their own name called from far away.
stages.note: Buzzite pollen causes a warm sense of recognition in anything it touches - experienced trainers describe it as feeling suddenly homesick for a place they love.

stages.name: Hymenax
stages.bio: Hymenax has lost its soft roundness and sharpened - its body is a sleek yellow-and-black blade in the air, wings now large and angled, and its violet eyes glow with a focused intensity. A psychic halo surrounds its thorax when it is reading the intentions of nearby creatures, which it does constantly and without invitation. In Bug Thicket, Hymenax patrols the mid-canopy, and other insects instinctively clear a corridor for it to pass - not from fear, but from something quieter that they cannot name.
stages.note: Hymenax can detect stress in any creature within ten metres - trainers say it appears beside anxious companions before the trainer has even noticed anything is wrong.

stages.name: Buzzalith
stages.bio: Buzzalith is fearsome and magnificent - a great wasp-titan whose segmented body blazes with deep purple and amber, its long stinger curving like a ceremonial blade and its four wings spread wide enough to cast a shadow over a small clearing. It radiates a psychic field that makes the air itself feel conscious. Bug Thicket's oldest creatures tell stories of Buzzalith settling at the centre of a hive and reciting a lost guardian's whole teaching back - somehow it had collected them, one idea at a time, for years.
stages.note: Buzzalith's wings beat at exactly 6,000 times per minute - researchers cannot explain why this rate creates measurable psychic interference in nearby electronics.

stages.name: Lambkin
stages.bio: Lambkin is a bright golden-yellow lamb with a fluffy round body and small curved horns just beginning to form. Two green-tipped sprigs of leaves grow behind its ears like living earrings, and its eyes are wide and bright. It prances through the Crystal Mines' upper passages where filtered light catches on its wool and sends little gold flickers dancing on the cave walls. Young miners leave Lambkin first to explore a new tunnel - its coat glows brighter where the crystal veins are richest.
stages.note: Lambkin's wool reflects crystal-light brighter than any lamp - miners use its silhouette as a reading light in passages too narrow for lanterns.

stages.name: Caproid
stages.bio: Caproid stands tall and luminous - a golden ram with long curved horns and a broad, confident stance. Green vine-patterns trace its legs like natural armour, and its fleece now holds a steady warm glow rather than just a reflection. It climbs where others hesitate, finding footholds on sheer crystal faces with almost casual precision. In Crystal Mines lore, Caproid marks safe passages through unstable tunnels by pressing its horns to the stone and reading the vibrations - a gift of light showing the living route through darkness.
stages.note: Caproid can stand on a crystal ledge the width of a single hoof without wavering, for as long as needed - climbers have recorded it motionless for over an hour.

stages.name: Aurelion
stages.bio: Aurelion is a being of living gold - its great branching horns spiral upward like the crown of an ancient tree, and green vines wind through its fleece as though the Crystal Mines' plants have chosen it as a trellis. Its body radiates a steady warm light that reaches every shadow in a wide radius. According to the oldest Crystal Mines legends, Aurelion once stood at the entrance to a collapsed tunnel for three days until every living creature inside found the light it cast and walked to safety.
stages.note: The light Aurelion casts promotes crystal growth - geologists have documented formations appearing within days of Aurelion's extended presence in a passage.

stages.name: Capkid
stages.bio: Capkid is a small white goat with a cream-coloured coat and two small nubbin horns still growing in. It picks its way across the Sand Dunes on delicate hooves with total confidence, tilting its head at every new rock formation as though cataloguing them for later. It can balance on a stone no bigger than a fist and seems to regard gravity as a mild suggestion. Dune caravanners say a Capkid sighted above the ridgeline means solid footing lies beneath - it never walks where the sand will shift.
stages.note: Capkid taps the ground three times with a forehoof before stepping onto new terrain - experienced dune guides do the same after watching long enough.

stages.name: Caphorn
stages.bio: Caphorn has grown into a sturdy white-grey mountain goat with long curling horns and a serious amber gaze. Its legs have thickened and its hooves now have a hard mineral edge from years of climbing sandstone. It claims the highest dune ridges and surveys everything below from a favoured perch, utterly untroubled by the wind. Caphorn marks its territory not with scent but by scoring its horns across rock - the scratch-marks are as distinctive as a signature, and no other creature has ever tried to erase one.
stages.note: Caphorn's horn-marks on rock have been found up to forty kilometres apart, suggesting it covers far more dune country in a season than anyone expected.

stages.name: Stonecrown
stages.bio: Stonecrown wears its crown well - its massive layered stone-plated back rises like a ridge of small peaks, and its sweeping multi-branched horns are thick enough to be used as handholds by lost climbers. The rocky plating on its haunches and shoulders is actual compressed desert stone fused into its coat over a lifetime of dune crossings. It stands at the highest points of the Sand Dunes and, when it calls out across the ridgelines, the resonance carries for miles - a signal that has guided lost travellers home since before the oldest maps were drawn.
stages.note: The stone plates on Stonecrown's back develop unique crystal inclusions over decades - no two adults have the same pattern, and elder ones have been read like geological records.

stages.name: Carapyx
stages.bio: Carapyx is a segmented armoured larva - grey-silver plating covering its oval body in neat overlapping sections, with a single glowing purple eye at its front. It moves with a slow, deliberate rolling motion through Dark Forest's leaf litter, pausing often to feel vibrations with its underside. It cannot sting yet but its psychic eye reads surface emotions with unsettling accuracy. Children in the Dark Forest say if Carapyx stops and stares at you, it already knows what you are about to say.
stages.note: Carapyx can predict the exact direction a nearby creature will move in by reading micro-vibrations with its belly-plates - it sidesteps threats before they form.

stages.name: Chrysapyx
stages.bio: Chrysapyx has sealed itself into a upright shell - a smooth rounded carapace of deep grey with a single focused purple eye that never blinks. It does not move from the spot it chose, but the air around it hums. In this sealed state it is absorbing every vibration, sound, and emotion passing through the Dark Forest, cataloguing them in a silence that others find unsettling. Dark Forest creatures give it a wide berth, sensing they are being studied.
stages.note: Chrysapyx in its sealed state has been observed rotating very slowly - always toward the largest nearby psychic disturbance, like a living compass.

stages.name: Vespiarch
stages.bio: Vespiarch has emerged - a sleek, metallic dark wasp with four clear wings, a tapered stinger, and compound purple eyes that glow with an unsettling intelligence. Its black-banded body is elegant and precise, and its wingbeats are almost inaudible, making its approach startlingly sudden. It does not simply sting; it reads exactly what a target fears most and acts on that knowledge with surgical calm. In the Dark Forest, Vespiarch is spoken of as the reason the trees remember where you have been.
stages.note: Vespiarch leaves a faint psychic trace on everything it stings - researchers call it a 'memory tag'; subjects reliably remember the exact moment of contact for years.

stages.name: Carapiny
stages.bio: Carapiny is a small, rounded beetle with a neatly plated green-grey shell and a single short stubby horn on its head. Six legs carry it at a brisk, purposeful trot through Steel Fortress's lower corridors, antennae twitching at every wall seam and rivet. It has a habit of tapping metal surfaces with its front legs, as though testing structural integrity - and in a fortress that has stood for centuries, its checks are not entirely wrong. Workers follow its inspection routes as a loose maintenance schedule.
stages.note: A Carapiny tap-pattern on a wall section has preceded three documented structural repairs at Steel Fortress - the maintenance crew now keeps a log.

stages.name: Caraphor
stages.bio: Caraphor's shell has thickened into heavy segmented steel-green plates, and its single horn has grown wide and swept back. Its six legs end in gripping clamps that let it walk vertically up Steel Fortress walls without slowing down. It grinds its mandibles together in a steady rhythm when patrolling - a sound the fortress residents have learned means the building is being properly maintained. Nothing enters a corridor Caraphor has decided to hold.
stages.note: Caraphor can support five times its own weight on its back - fortress engineers have used sleeping specimens as emergency load-bearing braces in a pinch.

stages.name: Caraphalanx
stages.bio: Caraphalanx is an immense armoured titan - its body a fortress of interlocking steel-hued plates, a massive blunt horn sweeping from its head, and six heavily clawed legs that leave dents in stone floors. It does not patrol so much as occupy; where Caraphalanx stands, no passage is breached. The Steel Fortress's outermost walls show claw-marks at certain heights that historians believe are decades old - evidence that Caraphalanx inspects the same points on the same structure, season after season, never finding anything out of order.
stages.note: The low vibration Caraphalanx produces while stationary is the exact frequency that prevents rust formation in steel - it has been observed standing near weakened sections for days.

stages.name: Carapuff
stages.bio: Carapuff is a tiny segmented pill bug with a pale silver-grey shell and small stubby legs that barely reach the ground. When startled, it curls into a perfect silvery ball and rolls wherever gravity takes it - which is often directly into something else's feet. It lives in Bug Thicket's damp undergrowth, tucked beneath leaves and mossy logs, emerging at twilight to roll methodically over the same patch of ground it considers its territory. Young explorers keep them as companions because a content Carapuff purrs faintly in your pocket.
stages.note: Carapuff rolls into a ball when startled and travels further than expected - one was found 200 metres from its home patch following a particularly loud noise.

stages.name: Carapax
stages.bio: Carapax has grown its segments wide and overlapping, giving its oval body the look of a living shield. Its legs have thickened and its rolling form is now genuinely dangerous - other creatures hear it rolling through the undergrowth and step aside quickly. It has a habit of unrolling in exactly the right spot to block a threat before its trainer has even spotted one. In Bug Thicket, Carapax is considered a reliable first warning of anything wrong on the forest floor.
stages.note: Carapax unrolls with enough momentum to knock over a creature three times its size - trainers have started treating its unrolling as a useful battle signal.

stages.name: Titanshell
stages.bio: Titanshell is a living fortress - its shell so dense and wide that in ball-form it is nearly a metre across, and rolling, it leaves a flat track through undergrowth. Its segmented plates have hardened to something between insect chitin and folded iron, and the ridges on its back are sharp enough to be read like topographic lines. When it unrolls fully, the ring of its plates hitting the ground is heard across Bug Thicket. Old grove-keepers say Titanshell once rolled down a hill and stopped a flood barrier from breaking - the thicket has never flooded since.
stages.note: Titanshell in ball-form is unmoved by anything short of a deliberate explosion - it has been recorded sitting in the path of a mudslide for six hours, unrolling only once it had passed.

stages.name: Shellcrab
stages.bio: Shellcrab is a cheerful orange crab with a large translucent blue bubble-dome for a shell, through which its tiny face peers out with round bright eyes and a permanent grin. Its two front claws are bright orange and held wide in a gesture that could mean hello or challenge - often both at once. It skitters sideways across Coral Bay's tidal shallows, collecting small shiny objects and depositing them in its bubble-shell as though decorating a room. No two Shellcrab shells contain the same collection.
stages.note: Shellcrab collects exactly seven small objects before stopping for the day - if one is taken, it will search until the set is complete again.

stages.name: Ironpinch
stages.bio: Ironpinch is a formidable blue-grey crab with a heavily plated carapace studded with short spines and two large, asymmetric claws - the right distinctly bigger than the left, built for gripping, the left sharper for cutting. It moves quickly across the sea floor with a confident side-step and claims the largest tide pools in Coral Bay through sheer presence. Smaller creatures do not attempt to challenge it; they simply wait until it finishes eating and leave it whatever it did not take.
stages.note: Ironpinch always places its larger claw on the ground first when claiming a tide pool - marine biologists have confirmed it is a deliberate territorial signal, not accident.

stages.name: Titanomaw
stages.bio: Titanomaw is enormous and angular - its steel-blue carapace is plated in massive ridged sections, its claws broad and spiked, and its orange-rimmed eyes hold an intelligence that suggests it has outlasted several generations of everything around it. It moves with deliberate slowness in shallow water but is remarkably fast in the deep; Coral Bay fishers say if Titanomaw is hunting, the safest place is directly behind it. Its claws can cut through stone, but it reserves that capability - it has never been observed using it carelessly.
stages.note: Titanomaw has been documented at the same underwater rock formation every winter for at least forty recorded years - it is believed to be the same individual each time.

stages.name: Pebbluff
stages.bio: Pebbluff is a compact dark-shelled tortoise whose hexagonal shell plates are already bolted-looking, as though assembled rather than grown. Its small legs carry it in a patient, unhurried trudge through the Amber Desert's hot sands. Each plate on its shell catches the desert sun slightly differently, giving its back a mosaic glint. It stops frequently to press its flat face to the ground and feel for the deep vibrations that tell it whether the sand ahead will bear its weight.
stages.note: Pebbluff's shell plates expand slightly in heat and contract at night - the clicking sound at dawn in Amber Desert camps is usually a herd of Pebbluff adjusting.

stages.name: Caramite
stages.bio: Caramite is a solid, heavy tortoise whose dark shell has grown into thick interlocking iron-grey plates with orange-gold studs at each junction. Its head is broad and angular, and it pulls it low when it senses a threat - the shell closing flush to the ground creates a surface nearly impossible to overturn. It navigates the Amber Desert by the faintest tremor in the rock beneath the sand, finding ancient paths that no map captures. Even in sandstorms, Caramite continues without hesitation.
stages.note: Caramite finds buried water sources by detecting the microscopic ground tremor that moving groundwater creates - desert survival guides recommend following one.

stages.name: Caramoth
stages.bio: Caramoth is a moving fortress - its shell is a fortress of dark iron-grey hexagonal plates studded with thick golden spikes at every corner, broad and heavy and ancient. Its legs are pillars. It moves exactly as slowly as it wishes and has never been observed moving faster, even in danger; it has simply never needed to. The Amber Desert's oldest dunes carry faint straight lines that geographers believe are the ancient walking routes of Caramoth, worn so deeply over millennia they became permanent features of the landscape.
stages.note: Caramoth's shell spikes grow throughout its lifetime - the number of golden spikes on an adult can be used to calculate its age within about five years.

stages.name: Tinycara
stages.bio: Tinycara is a small, stocky beetle with a broad grey-green shell and six busy legs that carry it in enthusiastic arcs across the Crystal Mines floor. A small blunt horn nubs from its head - too small yet to be useful, but Tinycara uses it to poke at crystal formations anyway, apparently checking if anything rattles loose. Its eyes are wide and slightly too far apart, giving it a look of permanent mild surprise at everything the mines contain.
stages.note: Tinycara tests every crystal it finds by tapping it once with its horn - if it rings, the beetle marks the spot with a small scratch and returns daily for a week.

stages.name: Thorapyx
stages.bio: Thorapyx has grown a proper horn - swept back and broad, almost as wide as its head, and notched from where it has hammered at mine walls. Its grey-green shell has thickened with ribbed armour segments, and six powerful legs carry it with surprising speed through the mine's lower tunnels. It digs for crystals not by breaking them but by undermining the surrounding stone in precise oval trenches - a method that leaves crystals whole and free. Crystal miners find cleaned specimens where Thorapyx has worked the night before.
stages.note: Thorapyx excavates around crystals without touching them - every specimen recovered from its work sites is unscratched, regardless of crystal fragility.

stages.name: Colossarapyx
stages.bio: Colossarapyx is a hulking, ridge-backed titan whose entire body is a landscape of interlocking steel-green armour plates, glowing green crystal-inlays visible in the deepest plate grooves, and a sweeping multi-ridged horn that has punched through solid granite. It is the unquestioned authority of Crystal Mines' deepest passages - not because it fights, but because nothing has ever found a reason to challenge something so completely, obviously armoured. It keeps the deepest crystal chambers clear of collapse by reinforcing walls with the weight of its own body.
stages.note: The crystal inlays in Colossarapyx's shell grow over its lifetime from the minerals it absorbs tunnelling - no two adults share the same crystal pattern.

stages.name: Carapup
stages.bio: Carapup is a small, determined-looking tortoise with a neat domed grey shell and a slightly pouty expression. Its four solid legs end in blunt-clawed toes perfect for ploughing through sand without sinking. It plods across the Sand Dunes at its chosen pace - which is slow - and regards faster-moving creatures with calm suspicion. Dune children chase Carapup but never catch it; it simply walks in a straight line until the child tires, then turns around and plods past them again.
stages.note: Carapup maintains exactly the same walking pace regardless of terrain - sand, rock, or slope, measured at precisely 0.3 km/h over a full kilometre.

stages.name: Caramax
stages.bio: Caramax is a wide, heavy tortoise whose shell has developed a ridged texture and amber-brown scutes that blend with the dune landscape. Its broad flat head carries a furrowed brow that seems to express permanent mild thought. It has learned to read the sand by the way it shifts around its feet - it never walks into a dune slide and never climbs a slope it cannot descend. Dune caravanners use Caramax route-lines as safe-passage maps; the paths it chooses are still there decades later.
stages.note: Caramax's shell pattern exactly mirrors the dune stripe formations of its home region - researchers believe it actively seeks terrain that matches its own colouration.

stages.name: Caracolossus
stages.bio: Caracolossus is ancient and enormous - its shell is a geography of ridged stone segments, with golden-amber scutes worn smooth by centuries of sand and each leg as thick as a pillar. Its slow, rhythmic footsteps send tremors through the dune in advance of its arrival; the sand shifts to accommodate it. Sand Dunes tradition holds that Caracolossus walked a single great circuit of the region before the first settlement was built, and it has been walking the same route ever since - a living boundary marker for everything the dunes contain.
stages.note: Caracolossus completes its circuit of Sand Dunes in exactly forty-two days regardless of obstacles - researchers have documented it walking into and out of flooded sections without changing pace.

stages.name: Starlamb
stages.bio: Starlamb is a small, fluffy white llama with a shimmering blue star-cloth draped over its back and a single spiralling horn glinting from its forehead. Its wide eyes hold tiny constellations, and when it blinks, they rearrange. It prances through the Psychic Temple leaving faint starlight hoofprints that linger for a few minutes before fading. Young creatures follow those trails the way children follow paths drawn in chalk - knowing something interesting must be at the end.
stages.note: Starlamb's hoofprints glow for exactly ninety seconds and always point toward the nearest source of natural light in the temple.

stages.name: Celestlama
stages.bio: Celestlama stands tall and luminous, its neck long and proud, its mane a flowing river of blue-white star-light. The spiralled horn has grown long and elegant, and when it tilts its head, faint aurora-colour ripples pulse through its coat. It walks the Psychic Temple's outer terraces in slow deliberate arcs, and where it passes, the temple garden orient themselves toward it as they do toward the sun - a reflex so consistent that botanists can map its daily route by the flower-facing angle alone.
stages.note: Every plant within six metres of Celestlama faces it regardless of sun position - the effect lasts for up to an hour after it has moved on.

stages.name: Cosmadeer
stages.bio: Cosmadeer is a being of pure living light wrapped in the form of a great horned llama - its coat a cascade of rainbow aurora, its horn a pillar of spiral crystal that catches and refracts the temple's glow into a permanent halo. Its long graceful neck carries its head high, and from a distance it looks like a moving lighthouse. Temple lore tells that Cosmadeer appeared at the exact moment the guardians first taught a creature to speak - and it has never left, as though it came specifically to witness what language would become.
stages.note: Cosmadeer's presence in a temple courtyard doubles how long young creatures are willing to stay and watch something difficult - no explanation has been found.

stages.name: Cellite
stages.bio: Cellite is a small, translucent jellyfish with a pale blue dome and a single large deep-purple eye at its centre, through which it watches everything at once. Four delicate tentacles trail beneath it as it drifts through Poison Marsh's still waters, pulsing gently. It communicates by changing the bioluminescent patterns in its dome - quick flickers for surprise, slow pulses for contentment. Marsh travellers use Cellite light patterns as a weather guide; three long pulses means the water ahead is safe.
stages.note: Cellite's eye never fully closes - even in deep rest, the pupil continues slow tracking movements, as though watching things the rest of us cannot see.

stages.name: Cellix
stages.bio: Cellix has grown into a fuller, rounder jellyfish with a glowing blue dome and a brilliant purple eye whose iris has widened to nearly fill it. Six tentacles spiral below it, trailing light in lazy curves as it drifts. It radiates a mild psychic warmth that nearby creatures find calming - arguing parties in Poison Marsh will often halt and look around, confused, when a Cellix drifts between them. It feeds on the dark energies dissolved in the marsh water and leaves behind something cleaner.
stages.note: Patches of Poison Marsh within ten metres of a Cellix bloom have measurably lower toxin concentrations - the creature is apparently filtering as it drifts.

stages.name: Cellumarch
stages.bio: Cellumarch is magnificent and strange - a great spreading jellyfish whose luminous dome pulses with deep psychic violet, ringed with pink and blue aurora-frills, and whose many long tentacles trail in spiralling curtains of cold light. Its vast purple eye is the fixed centre of everything around it, and creatures nearby feel gently observed in the way one feels observed by something ancient and patient that has decided you are probably harmless. In Poison Marsh's deepest channels, Cellumarch drifts the old routes where the guardians once taught water-songs, and the marsh itself seems calmer for its presence.
stages.note: Cellumarch's full bioluminescent display has been documented drawing creatures from over a kilometre away, all of which eventually leave again looking inexplicably at peace.

stages.name: Hornlet
stages.bio: Hornlet is a round, solid green rhino calf with a broad flat face, a small knobbed horn just emerging from its nose, and a look of cheerful stubborn determination. Its thick legs plant firmly on Granite Heights' rocky ground, and it has already developed the habit of testing every boulder it encounters by pressing its forehead against it - seemingly checking whether it will move. It does not move boulders yet. But it is absolutely clear it intends to work up to that.
stages.note: Hornlet spends up to twenty minutes a day pressing its forehead against the same specific boulder - researchers believe it is forming a bond with a chosen landmark.

stages.name: Cerathorn
stages.bio: Cerathorn has grown into a formidable creature - its green hide is now armoured with raised stone-ridged scales, and three distinct horns crown its wide face, the largest curving upward in a solid arch. It moves with a heavy-footed confidence that causes small rock slides wherever the path is loose. It charges rarely, but when it does, the vibration is felt before the creature is seen. Granite Heights pathfinders mark their toughest trails by whether Cerathorn uses them regularly - its routes are the most structurally sound.
stages.note: Cerathorn's three-horn configuration provides a reading of rock-seam depth when pressed to stone - miners in Granite Heights call this 'the triple test.'

stages.name: Titanoceros
stages.bio: Titanoceros is the mountain made flesh - its body covered in thick overlapping stone-plate armour, its three horns each large enough to be called a landmark, and its four legs wide as granite pillars. When it walks, small tremors precede it. When it stops, the stillness feels geological. Old Granite Heights legends say Titanoceros was carved by the mountains themselves as their answer to Abalont's shadow - something that could not be moved, could not be turned, and would simply still be there when everything else had changed.
stages.note: The ground within thirty metres of a stationary Titanoceros shows measurably denser stone compression - as though the earth itself is consolidating around it.

stages.name: Cerulip
stages.bio: Cerulip is a round, glossy-blue pill bug no bigger than a fist, with tiny stubby legs tucked beneath a smooth domed shell. Two bright eyes peer out from a gap where the shell opens slightly at the front. It rolls into a perfect ball when startled, and likes to float along Verdant Valley streams tucked up tight. Small children in the valley say finding one downstream means rain is coming within the hour.
stages.note: When Cerulip tucks into a ball, it spins slowly downstream like a tiny blue marble.

stages.name: Cerulex
stages.bio: Cerulex has grown a pronounced horn above its snout and developed a second segmented ring of blue-black plates around its midsection. Its underside bristles with strong gripping legs and it moves in short, deliberate rushes. In Verdant Valley's shallow creeks it wedges itself under stones at dawn, scrubbing algae from the rocks with the stiff bristles under its chin. The guardians once watched it clear a silted singing spring overnight.
stages.note: Cerulex wedges so firmly under stream rocks that the current bends around it rather than moving it.

stages.name: Cerulord
stages.bio: Cerulord is a low, wide armored titan - a mass of overlapping blue-black plates edged in deep cobalt, with three forward-curving horns and a fringe of heavy clawed limbs that grip the riverbed like an anchor. Where it walks, the streambed reshapes itself. Valley lore holds that Cerulord's path carves new singing rivers when the old channels run dry, and it still haunts the deep pools beneath the guardian bridges, waiting for the waters to flow pure again.
stages.note: A Cerulord passage reshapes the streambed; fishers say new pools appear wherever it has rested overnight.

stages.name: Fawnlet
stages.bio: Fawnlet is a delicate, tawny-coated fawn with wide sky-blue eyes and two tiny nubs where antlers will someday grow. Its slender legs end in neat dark hooves, and a small tuft of lighter fur sits between its ears like a soft snowflake. In the Dark Forest it picks its way along ice-edged paths, and its blue gaze flickers when it senses a forgotten word nearby - it tilts its head and stamps once before moving toward it.
stages.note: Fawnlet always stamps its right front hoof exactly once when it discovers something hidden under the snow.

stages.name: Cervain
stages.bio: Cervain carries a full rack of branched antlers dusted with frost and stands tall on strong legs striped with rich brown. Its coat has thickened into layered bands of tan and chestnut, and two pale patches glow faintly on its chest. In the Dark Forest it walks the border paths between shadow and cleared ground, using its antler tines to scratch runes into frozen bark - each rune a word it has guarded through the long winter.
stages.note: Cervain carves one new rune into a frozen tree each full moon; scholars count the marks to read a winter's hidden history.

stages.name: Frostarch
stages.bio: Frostarch is a magnificent beast clad in deep blue-white ice-patterns etched across its flanks like ancient script, its enormous branching antlers trailing crystalline wisps of cold light. Where it stands, frost flowers bloom on the ground in rings, and the air hums with a low psychic resonance that quiets every creature within hearing. It is said to be the memory-keeper of the Dark Forest, holding every voice ever raised in its antlers - frozen, waiting to thaw.
stages.note: A ring of frost flowers 30 paces wide marks any spot where Frostarch has stood still for more than an hour.

stages.name: Cetaby
stages.bio: Cetaby is a plump, snow-white beluga calf with a round melon forehead, tiny pectoral fins, and the most earnest blue eyes in Coral Bay. It bobs at the surface humming to itself, and the vibrations shimmer the water around it in small rings. Young explorers who wade near often say they suddenly remember a word they'd forgotten - Cetaby nudges those memories loose with a gentle pulse from its forehead, then flips away before it can be thanked.
stages.note: Standing knee-deep near a resting Cetaby for five minutes is said to restore one forgotten word to mind.

stages.name: Cetarise
stages.bio: Cetarise has grown into a smooth, powerful beluga with a large rounded melon and a knowing expression. Its ivory skin ripples faintly with a pale interior glow when it echolocates, and its clicks carry so far through Coral Bay that the reef fish school differently in response. It patrols the outer edge of the bay with calm authority, threading clicks between the coral pillars as though checking each one for words that still need to be learned.
stages.note: Cetarise can echolocate a single heartbeat hidden among reef crevices from 200 paces away.

stages.name: Cetamystic
stages.bio: Cetamystic is a luminous, powerfully built whale with fanned tail flukes and iridescent blue-tipped fins that catch the current like slow wings. Its broad melon pulses with soft light when it speaks, and its song carries across the full breadth of Coral Bay in under a minute. It is said the guardians consulted Cetamystic when they needed to remember the original words of the world - its body holds the echo of everything ever spoken near the bay.
stages.note: On calm nights, Cetamystic's song reaches the far shore of Coral Bay and back, bouncing once before fading.

stages.name: Cetyx
stages.bio: Cetyx is a pale, chubby little whale-form with a round swirled marking on its forehead and large expressive eyes that spin with a faint hypnotic shimmer. It floats just below the murky surface of Poison Marsh, blowing small bubbles that pop with a faint lavender flash. Its swirl marking glows gently when it probes the marsh's dark waters for words that have sunk too deep to see - it marks each one with a luminous bubble so it won't be forgotten again.
stages.note: The lavender bubbles Cetyx blows each mark a word it has found sleeping beneath the marsh mud.

stages.name: Narwhyx
stages.bio: Narwhyx has developed a single spiraling tusk that glows at the tip with concentrated purple light, and its body now carries fluid swirling patterns of lavender and white. It slips through the deeper channels of Poison Marsh with unhurried grace, tapping its tusk against submerged roots to stir up words that have dissolved into the dark water. Those who see it by lantern-light say its patterns seem to shift and rearrange just out of clear sight.
stages.note: Narwhyx taps its tusk on roots exactly three times before surfacing - marsh-walkers count the taps to know how deep the water is.

stages.name: Abysryx
stages.bio: Abysryx is a towering, spined sea-beast with icy blue crystalline dorsal spines, a thick spiraled horn, and sweeping tail flukes. Its body glows with inner violet light along every spine ridge, and its gaze holds something ancient and still. In the deepest trench of Poison Marsh it rests beneath the poison-clouded water, dreaming in old words - and the marsh itself grows quieter for a league in every direction whenever it stirs. Guardians say Abysryx remembers the words before words.
stages.note: The water within 50 paces of a resting Abysryx is perfectly still, no matter how fierce the storm above.

stages.name: Shellwee
stages.bio: Shellwee is a tiny, bright-green land turtle with a smooth domed shell patterned in hexagonal tiles and two big round eyes that take up most of its face. Its four legs are stubby and it walks with a determined waddle. Bug Thicket's mossy floor suits it perfectly - it munches leaf-tips and dewdrops all morning, and marks the paths it has already walked by leaving tiny damp footprints. It follows the guardians' old learning-trails without knowing why, as if the paths remember it too.
stages.note: Shellwee's footprints stay damp twice as long as dew on any other creature, making its trail easy to follow in dry thicket.

stages.name: Chelasaur
stages.bio: Chelasaur has grown a stronger, ridged shell of deeper green with golden-edged tiles, and its neck and legs have thickened considerably. It moves with slow confidence through the Bug Thicket underbrush, pausing to press its head flat against the earth and listen for the faint vibrations of root-songs growing below. When it finds one, it will wait patiently beside it until a young trainer passes - it can wait three days without eating if the word is important enough.
stages.note: Chelasaur presses its chin flat to the ground for up to ten minutes at a time, listening for root vibrations no other creature can detect.

stages.name: Coralking
stages.bio: Coralking carries an entire living reef on its back - a crown of branching coral-like growths, orange and gold, that sprout from the edges of its massive shell like a natural fortress wall. Its broad shell is thick as stone, and the coral fringe waves gently even in still air. In the Bug Thicket, water seeps from beneath it wherever it rests, making small pools that other creatures gather around. The guardians believe it is the bridge between sea-songs and land-songs - the creature that carries both at once.
stages.note: A Coralking resting in one spot for a week will cause a small freshwater spring to appear beneath it.

stages.name: Cuplet
stages.bio: Cuplet is a round, jewel-bright insect no bigger than a child's palm - emerald green with orange-swirled wing cases and two bright eyes. Tufts of green light flicker from the top of its head like tiny flames, and its six legs are each tipped with a sticky golden pad. It bounces between the luminous blossoms of the Psychic Temple, depositing tiny seeds of meaning wherever it lands. The temple would grow dull and soundless without Cuplet's constant pollinating hops.
stages.note: Each surface Cuplet lands on gains a faint sticky glow that lingers for exactly one sunrise.

stages.name: Angelim
stages.bio: Angelim stands upright on graceful deer legs, its body a deep emerald-gold with leaf-like scales along its flanks and a crown of antler-tines that glow at the tips. Its tail is leaf-shaped and fans wide when it is calm. In the Psychic Temple it paces the rings of bioluminescent flowers that mark the Abalont boundary - each full circuit it completes causes one flower to bloom brighter, as if it is keeping a tally of sounds learned today.
stages.note: Angelim completes exactly seven circuits of the temple's inner ring each morning before it will stop to interact with anyone.

stages.name: Seraphim
stages.bio: Seraphim is a broad, heavy-antlered guardian of ancient authority - its body is deep forest-green scaled in overlapping leaf-plates, and its enormous rack of antlers blazes with concentrated golden light at every tip. When it lowers its head, the whole temple brightens, and every creature within it becomes briefly calm. It has not left the center of the Psychic Temple since Abalont's shadow fell, standing vigil over the voices the guardians left behind, patient as sunlight itself.
stages.note: The exact center of the Psychic Temple is permanently 4 degrees warmer than its edges - the ground beneath Seraphim's favorite standing-spot.

stages.name: Chitnub
stages.bio: Chitnub is a stubby armored creature with a domed back of ridged brown-tan plates and a round low-slung body that barely clears the amber sand. Two small front claws dig and steer, and its tiny eyes peer forward between heavy brow-plates. It spends the scorching hours of the Amber Desert buried to the neck in warm dune-sand, emerging at dusk to hunt for the old marks pressed into wind-carved stone. It clicks its front claws together twice whenever it finds a old sigil.
stages.note: Chitnub clicks its front claws exactly twice when it finds a old sigil carved in desert stone - never once, never three times.

stages.name: Chithorn
stages.bio: Chithorn is a low-slung, four-clawed predator armored in thick bronze-grey plates with raised ridges along its spine. Its front claws are massive, designed for gripping and prying, and it moves with a surprisingly quick skittering rush when it needs to. By day it lurks in the shadows of Amber Desert's sandstone formations; at night it follows the scent of old ink, tracing the perimeter of buried memory-tablets until it can drag them to the surface.
stages.note: Chithorn can pry open a sandstone memory-tablet that weighs three times its own body weight without breaking the inscriptions inside.

stages.name: Chithyra
stages.bio: Chithyra is a massive, wide-bodied armored beast - its entire back a fortress of overlapping spined bronze plates, its four forward-raking claws carved from something harder than desert stone. When it spreads its stance and hisses, the sand vibrates in a circle thirty paces out. It patrols the deepest dunes of Amber Desert, guarding the buried memory-vaults from those who would take them without first learning their meaning. It will not move aside for anything that cannot answer its challenge-call.
stages.note: No sandstorm has ever buried a memory-vault that Chithyra has chosen to guard - the dunes simply drift around it.

stages.name: Chitling
stages.bio: Chitling is a pale, chubby insect larva - smooth white skin banded in faint rings, a rounded rear, and a dark head with two tiny black eyes and a small hooked beak-jaw. It squirms through Sand Dune tunnels just below the surface, leaving winding channels that explorers call echo-burrows, because the trails it makes seem to form a pattern when viewed from a high dune. It eats nothing but sand grains and the compressed sunlight locked inside them.
stages.note: Chitling's burrow trails, viewed from the top of the nearest high dune, sometimes form a single clear spiral.

stages.name: Chitiderm
stages.bio: Chitiderm is entirely encased in a hard oval shell of burnished bronze-brown chitin, segmented in six horizontal bands. A faint orange glyph glows on its face-plate - the only sign of the creature resting inside. In the Sand Dunes it buries itself at the base of crescent dunes and waits, perfectly still, sometimes for weeks. Old sigils pressed into nearby sand tiles drift closer while it sleeps, as if drawn by the glow of its face-mark.
stages.note: Sand tiles within one body-length of a buried Chitiderm rotate slowly toward it over three days, as if being read.

stages.name: Chitoptera
stages.bio: Chitoptera is a massive upright beetle-warrior: bronze-brown wing-cases folded across a wide thorax, thick raking foreclaws, huge curved horn above its brow, and two powerful hind legs that carry it in bounding rushes across the dune field. Its carapace has hardened over a thousand moults and now deflects wind-whipped sand entirely. It carries every old sigil from its earlier burrows in its memory, and guards the dune boundary as if it were the last memory-keeper between the desert and the dark.
stages.note: Chitoptera can bound twelve body-lengths in one leap - its takeoff leaves a crater that fills with fine ripple-patterns.

stages.name: Shellnip
stages.bio: Shellnip is an endearing little hermit crab hauling a smooth rounded shell on its back, two orange-tipped front claws raised in permanent readiness, and bright round eyes mounted on short stalks. It skitters across the Lava Crater's warm basalt shelves collecting hot pebbles to swap into its shell for heat. When it finds a smoldering memory-stone it grabs it in both claws, holds it up to examine, then tucks it directly into its shell like a tiny archivist. Nothing it picks up is ever truly dropped.
stages.note: Shellnip has never voluntarily set down any object it has picked up - its shell contains 47 stones of various temperatures.

stages.name: Crustatch
stages.bio: Crustatch has outgrown its borrowed shell and now carries a craggy, fire-pitted carapace fused to its back - rough and irregular like solidified lava. Its claws have grown uneven, one heavier than the other, the larger one able to crush basalt. It patrols the crater rim at midday when the heat is fiercest, waving its larger claw in slow circles that the crater's hot updraft catches like a sail. Lava Crater trainers say it is teaching the volcano a name it has never heard each time it does this.
stages.note: Crustatch's claw-wave pattern at noon changes day to day - crater-watchers have mapped 23 distinct gestures over three seasons.

stages.name: Infernoclaw
stages.bio: Infernoclaw is a hulking siege-form crab, its entire back plated in fused volcanic rock, its two massive asymmetrical claws edged in smoldering orange. Embers sift from the joints of its shell when it moves. In the Lava Crater it holds the deepest thermal vents as its territory - even the lava-lizards give it space. It is said to have cracked a old monolith that no other creature could break, and the words inside flew free and taught themselves to every creature nearby.
stages.note: Infernoclaw cracks old monoliths by gripping them with both claws and rotating in opposite directions - the break is always clean.

stages.name: Slityx
stages.bio: Slityx is a small, bright-banded serpent coiled in vivid blue and gold rings, its narrow head lifted with alert curiosity and two amber eyes gleaming. Its tongue flickers constantly, tasting the Dragon Spire air for old voices caught in updrafts. Despite its size it is already venomous - tiny droplets bead on its fangs when it opens its mouth wide to yawn, which it does nine times every sunrise as a kind of ritual counting exercise. The guardians called it the Spire's small interpreter.
stages.note: Slityx yawns exactly nine times at sunrise without fail - trainers say each yawn corresponds to one word it plans to learn that day.

stages.name: Vipraid
stages.bio: Vipraid is a thicker, longer serpent with a flattened wedge-shaped head marked by deep blue and bright gold banding that intensifies near its neck. Its scales have developed a faint metallic sheen, and its hood flares when it rears up to full height. On Dragon Spire's heated ledges it practices strike-precision on carved stone old pillars, chipping one letter at a time with needle-fangs until the whole word is exposed. It has never struck anything it didn't mean to.
stages.note: Vipraid can chip a single letter from a stone pillar without disturbing the letter beside it - verified by three different scholars.

stages.name: Hydracobra
stages.bio: Hydracobra is vast - a great cobra-dragon with a broad flared hood rimmed in blazing gold, a heavily scaled body banded in royal blue and deep amber, and four small draconic wings folded at its shoulders like a battle-cape. When it rises fully upright atop Dragon Spire's highest peak, its hood catches the wind and shimmers. Every creature on the Spire stops moving. It is the oldest voice in these lands, they say - its hiss alone carries more meaning than an hour of talk.
stages.note: When Hydracobra spreads its hood at full height, the wind direction on the Spire changes to blow toward it from every angle at once.

stages.name: Cellume
stages.bio: Cellume is a tiny golden bee nestled in a hexagonal honeycomb cell, with a round amber body, one visible eye glowing purple, and stubby wings folded against its back. It rarely leaves its comb-home for long - it sits in the center of its cell and hums at exactly the frequency needed to warm the honey around it. In the Light Grove its hum is so constant that grove-visitors use it as a tuning pitch when they try to recall an old song. It vibrates harder when it hears a correctly spoken word.
stages.note: Cellume's hum raises exactly half a pitch when it hears a note struck true - apiarists use it as a living tuning fork.

stages.name: Hexazen
stages.bio: Hexazen has emerged from its comb and taken armored form - a stocky upright bee with a golden hex-plated abdomen, purple-glowing compound eye, and a stinger the length of a finger. It still carries a small hexagonal plate on its back as a shield. It patrols the outer flowers of the Light Grove in broad spiraling sweeps, marking each bloom with a drop of warning-venom that repels creatures that can't name the flower correctly. Those who know the word pass unharmed.
stages.note: Hexazen marks each flower it patrols with a single drop of venom that evaporates in sunlight - the grove is re-marked every dawn.

stages.name: Aphelion
stages.bio: Aphelion is a terrifying and beautiful winged wasp-queen - broad translucent wings, a black-and-gold segmented body bristling with purple venom sacs, razor mandibles, and four spread limbs tipped in hooked claws. When it hovers in the Light Grove's canopy, the air below it smells of honeysuckle and danger in equal measure. It is the grove's final guard: only those who can name every flower in the grove correctly may pass beneath it without being marked. It has waited forty years to meet someone who could.
stages.note: Aphelion has not needed to sting anything in forty years - the last trainer to name every flower correctly is still remembered in grove tradition.

stages.name: Acornit
stages.bio: Acornit is an upright acorn-bodied creature with a large ribbed cap, two bright round eyes, and a pair of small leafy fists held at its sides - each fist is a green-leafed pod it shakes when excited. It stands on two stubby legs and toddles along Granite Heights' lower paths at a determined pace, always counter-clockwise, as if memorizing the circuit. Axon the fish-guardian once used these same trails, and Acornit still follows that ancient route, marking the path for any child who wishes to learn it.
stages.note: Acornit always walks Granite Heights' lower circuit counter-clockwise, completing the loop in exactly 22 minutes regardless of obstacles.

stages.name: Conkarl
stages.bio: Conkarl has grown into a stocky upright fighter - its acorn-cap crown is now thick and ridged, its body is broad and banded in warm chestnut, and its fists have become knotted acorn-pod knuckles it can pound together to make a sound that carries the length of Granite Heights' ridge. It still walks the patrol route every morning, but now faster and wider, covering the mid-elevation paths that Axon once climbed. When it finds an old mark carved into the granite it traces it with one knuckle three times before continuing.
stages.note: Conkarl traces any old mark it finds carved in granite exactly three times with its knuckle, as if confirming the shape each pass.

stages.name: Terakhan
stages.bio: Terakhan is immense and ancient - an acorn-cap warrior grown to titan scale, its body wrapped in carved wooden armor and its great round crown cracked with age but unbroken. Its massive fists strike the granite path with such force that fresh sigils appear in the stone face. High in Granite Heights, where Axon the guardian first carved the learning-paths, Terakhan stands at the summit each dawn facing east, waiting with the patience of heartwood for the lost guardians to return and read the stone it has guarded since the shadow fell.
stages.note: Each strike of Terakhan's fist on summit granite leaves a fresh sigil - cartographers have mapped 300 of them attributed to it.

stages.name: Coralite
stages.bio: Coralite is a tiny sea turtle hatchling with a shell patterned in soft teal swirls, four flipper-legs and enormous curious eyes. Its shell markings spiral outward from the center in smooth concentric rings, as if the whole sea is written on its back in one long word. In Coral Bay's shallows it rides the surface current with barely any effort, spinning slowly as the swirl-pattern catches light. When it finds a singing current it spins faster, stirring the water into a bright ring around itself.
stages.note: Coralite spins visibly faster the moment it enters a singing current - bay guides use it to find the strongest tides.

stages.name: Coraleon
stages.bio: Coraleon has grown branching teal antlers from the front edge of its shell - real living coral-antlers that sway with ocean current and catch drifting song-seeds from the bay. Its flippers have grown broader and it moves with powerful strokes. At midtide it rises to float on its back, antlers breaking the surface, letting birds perch on the tines and carry song-seeds to the shore. The guardians of Coral Bay called this the Teaching Float - it still performs it every third day without prompting.
stages.note: Coraleon floats on its back every third day at midtide, holding its coral-antlers above the surface for exactly one hour.

stages.name: Coralarch
stages.bio: Coralarch carries a full living reef upon its back - branching coral-trees in orange and gold draped over a massive golden-green shell, ringed in seaflower garlands that never die. Its four great flippers move with the slow power of tides, and when it surfaces to breathe its exhale creates a warm fog that settles over the bay and triggers blooming in every seagrass bed nearby. Every memory-creature in Coral Bay swam through Coralarch's wake at least once in its life.
stages.note: A bloom of new seagrass follows Coralarch's path within 24 hours of its passage - bay scholars chart its routes by tracking the growth.

stages.name: Corafish
stages.bio: Corafish is a tiny, exquisitely pretty fish - pink-tinged, round-bodied, with an oversized shimmering tail-fin and one enormous deep-blue eye that takes up a third of its face. It swims in slow, wobbling spirals through Poison Marsh's murky channels, trailing a faint bioluminescent wake. The glow is just bright enough to read by for five seconds, and marsh-walkers claim that if they watch carefully they can sometimes see a word written in the light-trail before it fades.
stages.note: Corafish's light-trail persists for precisely five seconds - long enough to follow it to the next reef if you are watching for it.

stages.name: Coralux
stages.bio: Coralux has grown into a graceful mid-sized fish with pearl-pink and lavender scales, a crown of small coral-branches sprouting between its eyes, and a flowing double tail-fin edged in gold. A string of tiny luminous pearls rings its midsection like a belt of lights. In Poison Marsh it navigates the most toxic channels with ease, its pearl-lights never flickering - they only change colour when it has found a word the marsh has tried to dissolve. It guards them by circling them three times before swimming on.
stages.note: Coralux's pearl-lights shift from gold to blue the instant it detects a word dissolving in the marsh toxins.

stages.name: Coralumina
stages.bio: Coralumina is magnificent - a fully bloomed fish-sovereign trailing vast ribbons of flowing finnage in every colour of reef coral, its body iridescent and soft-lit from within, its coral-crown now a full tiara of interlocking branch-antlers. Even in the darkest reach of Poison Marsh, Coralumina carries its own dawn with it, and the water around it turns transparent for a body-length in every direction. The guardians placed it here specifically: a light-keeper for the marsh's hidden words, ensuring they never fully disappear into the dark.
stages.note: The water around Coralumina turns completely clear for one body-length - the only patch of readable water in the entire Poison Marsh.

stages.name: Corayu
stages.bio: Corayu is a small blue sea-sprite with a round body, two wide eyes, and a bundle of bright orange coral-tendrils sprouting from its head like a cheerful crown. A simple anchor emblem is painted or grown on its round belly. In Amber Desert it is a curiosity - a water-creature thriving in the driest region - but it survives by finding the deep underground aquifers below the dunes and surfacing at dusk to bounce on the warm sand. It hums constantly while bouncing, marking each bounce with a different note.
stages.note: Corayu marks each bounce with a different note - researchers have recorded 140 distinct notes from one dusk session.

stages.name: Corlite
stages.bio: Corlite has grown into a broad, powerful sea-beast with a carapace of fused stone-coral, a spiked crown of orange-red coral ridges on its head, and a wide chest bearing a shield-like emblem. It stands on four solid legs and moves with patient deliberateness through the Amber Desert, using its coral-crown to dowse for underground water. When it finds a singing aquifer it marks it by pressing its chest-emblem against the ground, leaving a old seal in the sand that lasts a full moon before it fades.
stages.note: Corlite's chest-seal marks a singing aquifer for exactly one full moon - desert-walkers follow the fading seals like a memory-map.

stages.name: Corlith
stages.bio: Corlith is a fortress of living stone-coral - a broad-bodied warden whose shell and hide are entirely fused coral-rock, its crest a full array of jagged coral spires, and a massive flat shield grown into its chest as natural armour. It carries water inside its coral chambers, enough to sustain itself and three other creatures for a week in full desert heat. In the depths of Amber Desert it stands beside the oldest singing aquifer, patient since before the desert was a desert, waiting for the sea to come back to it.
stages.note: Corlith carries enough internal water to sustain itself for seven days of desert sun without any external source.

stages.name: Cornyx
stages.bio: Cornyx is a compact, upright dino-lizard with vivid green scales edged in yellow-lime and a row of short leaf-shaped spines running from its crown to its tail. Its arms are small but its hind legs are thick and powerful, and it stands with its tiny hands balled at its sides as if ready for anything. In Lava Crater it forages along the cooler grassy ledges above the heat-vents, nibbling at the heat-resistant herb-songs that grow only here. Every herb it eats seems to give it a new sound to practice.
stages.note: Cornyx gains one new vocalization per herb variety it eats - researchers have catalogued 38 distinct sounds from a single well-fed individual.

stages.name: Draken
stages.bio: Draken has thickened into a proper dragon-lizard form - a muscular body in deep forest-green, a spine-crest that runs to a fully raised ridge along its back, a wide jaw showing prominent teeth, and a powerful sweeping tail. It prowls the mid-level ledges of Lava Crater where grass and fire meet, and has begun to breathe a thin greenish vapor when it roars - not quite dragon-fire yet, but it smells of pine and heat together. Song-seeds in the vapor take root faster than normal in lava-rock.
stages.note: Seeds caught in Draken's green vapor breath take root in bare lava-rock within 48 hours - no other creature achieves this.

stages.name: Petalosaurus
stages.bio: Petalosaurus is a magnificent predator-form dragon - low-slung on four massive legs, a back bristling with broad leaf-shaped spines, a wide angular head full of heavy teeth, and a tail as long as its body. Its scales are deep emerald in full battle-light. In Lava Crater it holds the highest grassy outcrop above the caldera rim: one side pure fire, one side living green. The guardians say it breathes both at once - a roar that carries the scent of rain and the heat of magma, ensuring nothing forgets what it fights for.
stages.note: Petalosaurus's roar carries both rain-scent and magma-heat simultaneously - weather-readers use it to predict the crater's next eruption.

stages.name: Corvlet
stages.bio: Corvlet is a very small, extremely round crow-chick, jet-black and fluffy, with stubby wings tucked against its sides and two wide amber eyes that glow slightly in the dark. It has barely any neck - just a ball of dark feathers with a beak sticking out. In Ghost Hollow it perches on fallen memory-stones and stares at them for long stretches, as if reading something adults can no longer see. Every so often it pecks once, lightly, like placing a punctuation mark.
stages.note: Corvlet pecks once on any surface it studies for more than two minutes - ghost-hollow scholars say it is marking a word it has decided to remember.

stages.name: Corvawk
stages.bio: Corvawk has grown into an alert, angular crow with sleek black feathers edged in a deep navy sheen, bright gold-amber eyes, and a crest of four stiff feathers at the back of its head. Its wings are fully developed and it rides the Ghost Hollow's cold wind-columns with minimal effort. It collects objects - buttons, pebbles, bits of old text - and arranges them in patterns outside its roost that, if you squint at the right angle, match the old guardian sigils.
stages.note: Corvawk's ground-arrangements outside its roost have been copied by three scholars; each one matches a different guardian sigil.

stages.name: Corvulture
stages.bio: Corvulture is a massive, imposing dark raptor with a wide wingspan marked by amber lightning-bolt patterns on the underside of each wing. Its feathers are dense black and its neck-ruff is thick as a collar of shadow. At rest it hunches forward with closed wings, looking like a carved gargoyle. When it spreads its wings in Ghost Hollow the hollow wind pauses for a moment - every creature in it freezes - then begins again carrying its voice. It remembers every voice raised in the hollow since the guardians left.
stages.note: When Corvulture spreads its wings, all wind in Ghost Hollow pauses for exactly three seconds before resuming.

stages.name: Corvchick
stages.bio: Corvchick is a small, stubby-winged crow-chick with deep purple-black plumage and amber eyes that hold a curious, old-soul quality for such a small creature. It hatches in the Shadow Caves' upper vaults where thin air-shafts bring in just enough wind to hear, and it practices its call into the dark constantly, listening for which cavern returns the best echo. The echo it receives changes slightly each time it calls - shadow-cave children say it is hearing the answers to questions it hasn't asked yet.
stages.note: The echo that returns to a Corvchick in Shadow Caves always sounds slightly different from the call it sent - no one has explained why.

stages.name: Corvex
stages.bio: Corvex is a lean, sharp-featured crow with a dark purple-grey body, a rough tufted crest, and alert amber eyes. Its wingtips are notched - from years of threading through tight cave passages - and it navigates the Shadow Caves' twisting tunnels without a single wing-touch against the walls, even in absolute darkness. It has memorized every tunnel by its specific air-current signature, and when it finds a new passage it screams a short call into it exactly once to read the echo-map before entering.
stages.note: Corvex reads a new tunnel's layout from a single echoing call before entering - it has never become lost in three years of mapping.

stages.name: Corvexian
stages.bio: Corvexian is a commanding, wide-winged dark raptor whose plumage has deepened to near-black with purple-charcoal highlights and whose eyes burn gold in the lightless caves. Its wingspan is enormous in the cave context - it must tilt to navigate the wider passages - and it navigates by memory alone, moving through pitch-black caverns at full speed without hesitation. In the Shadow Caves' deepest vault it has built a roost from memory-shards: fragments of spoken language petrified in cave calcite, woven together into something that might be a library.
stages.note: Corvexian's roost is built from 400 petrified memory-shards - scholars who have examined it say no word appears twice.

stages.name: Corvit
stages.bio: Corvit is a perfectly round, soft purple bird-chick with one huge golden eye and tiny wing-buds that have not yet spread. It sits on Gale Ridge's lowest ledges gripping the wind-worn rock with both feet and faces directly into the gale, feathers rippling. Its one visible eye never blinks in the wind. It can feel the psychic resonance in the air-currents, and it sorts them by pitch - keeping the voices it recognizes, releasing the ones it doesn't yet understand back into the wind to circle the spire again.
stages.note: Corvit sorts every wind-call it receives: recognized ones are swallowed, unrecognized ones are breathed back out to circle the spire again.

stages.name: Ravolt
stages.bio: Ravolt is a lean, angular purple raven with a narrow head-crest, strong wings that trail slightly longer than its body, and golden eyes that take on a faint metallic sheen during storms.
