It reads emotion as easily as scent, and guides wandering children back toward the temple's lit paths before they realize they were lost. The Psychic Temple feels calmer whenever Aerowhisk is near.
stages.note: Aerowhisk's twin tails always point toward whichever person in the group is the most anxious.

stages.name: Celestyx
stages.bio: Its presence silences noise and fills the air with a warm, buzzing stillness that lets things you had forgotten float back to the surface of your mind. Ancient scrolls from the Psychic Temple call it the Keeper of Spoken Stars - everything ever confided in this place rests somewhere in the shimmer between its tails.
stages.note: When Celestyx lies down to sleep, each of its nine tails wraps a different temple-tree, and the whole forest hums quietly until dawn.

stages.name: Pinklet
stages.bio: Pinklet is a fluffy pink chick with wide eyes and a heart-shaped pattern glowing on its downy chest, and tiny crystal-blue sparkles drift around its body. Its stubby wings flutter constantly, more out of excitement than any aerodynamic purpose, and its rounded beak is already warm to the touch. It hatched in the pink-crystal cavern shafts where light refracts into rosy columns, and it trots toward any glimmer it spots, convinced each one is a friend to meet.
stages.note: Pinklet's tiny beak can heat a single crystal shard until it glows soft pink; miners sometimes carry one as a lantern.

stages.name: Flamara
stages.bio: Flamara stands tall on one elegant leg, its deep pink plumage catching the crystal-mine facets and scattering warm light in all directions. Two shimmering butterfly-like wings of semi-translucent crystal have grown from its back, refracting every torch flame into dozens of tiny rainbows. It wades through shallow underground pools to cool its feet, then fans its wings to dry itself with a burst of heated air. Miners call it the Prism Bird and consider it good luck to spot one perching on a high vein.
stages.note: Flamara fans its crystal wings precisely at noon each day; the rainbow cast on the cave wall tells miners which tunnel runs warmest.

stages.name: Phoenixara
stages.bio: Phoenixara is a towering bird trailing a full mantle of living flame, its plumage ranging from deep rose at the wingtips to blazing gold at its crest, with streams of fire flowing behind every wingbeat. Crystal shards orbit its body in slow rings, warmed to a deep amber glow. It inhabits the deepest crystal-mine chamber where no torch is needed, because Phoenixara itself lights the entire space. When it stretches its wings, the temperature in the surrounding tunnels rises by five degrees, and sleeping crystals wake into new color.
stages.note: Each feather Phoenixara sheds solidifies into a translucent fire-crystal worth a full month of lantern oil.

stages.name: Flumble
stages.bio: Flumble is a dumpy pink fledgling whose stubby body seems too round for its thin legs. Its pale violet-pink down puffs outward in the dry desert breeze, making it look even rounder, and its small beak is already curved in the classic flamingo hook. It wanders the windswept dune-ridges where the psychic thermals lift loose sand into spirals, and it often gets its feet tangled chasing a gust. Despite the stumbling, it never tips over - something invisible seems to cushion it each time.
stages.note: Flumble can sense the direction of the next sandstorm up to ten minutes before any grain of sand begins to move.

stages.name: Psyflara
stages.bio: Psyflara stands with elegant stillness on a single leg even in forty-knot sandstorms, its bright pink wings held half-open to read every shift in the air. Its eyes carry an unusual depth, as though looking slightly past the present moment, and experienced desert travelers follow its gaze to find water. It broadcasts calm intention across the dunes like a slow psychic pulse - panicked animals within earshot will stop mid-bolt and simply blink at the sky.
stages.note: A flock of Psyflara standing in a circle with wings touching creates a windless pocket large enough for a tent camp to shelter inside.

stages.name: Phoenistra
stages.bio: Phoenistra is a magnificent large flamingo whose spread wings span the width of a dune-crest and shimmer with a pearlescent halo of golden light. Jewelled ornaments ring its neck and legs - gifts left by desert travelers over generations - and they chime softly in the wind. Its psychic field now extends across the whole dune sea: creatures near Phoenistra feel an uncanny ability to recall words they thought they'd forgotten, as if the wind itself carries them back. Sand dune settlements mark their maps with a flamingo symbol wherever Phoenistra roosts.
stages.note: Phoenistra's cry, heard in a dream, is said to restore a forgotten name to anyone who has lost one.

stages.name: Emblet
stages.bio: Emblet is a small bright-orange crab wearing what appears to be a tiny golden crown balanced on its shell. Its two round black eyes peer out from beneath the crown with intense seriousness, and it scuttles sideways across the granite ledges with surprising confidence for something so small. Water gathers in the hollow of its shell after rain, and it carries this small reservoir everywhere, sipping from it during the dry granite summers. Guardians say a crab that wears its crown without boasting is worth following into any battle.
stages.note: Emblet polishes its crown-shell with its smaller claws for exactly three minutes every morning before doing anything else.

stages.name: Pyrarex
stages.bio: Pyrarex is a muscular deep-orange crab with thick ridged claws and a broad flat body patterned with swirling orange markings. An anchor symbol is embossed on its chest-plate like a badge of rank. It has traded the simple crown for a full battle-ready posture, walking forward on its claws instead of sideways, which it considers more dignified. It lives in the spray-drenched ledges above the granite heights' hidden waterfalls, and other creatures give way when it raises one claw to signal the water is rising.
stages.note: Pyrarex taps its claws on granite three times before any fight - veterans say it is counting to make sure everyone else is watching.

stages.name: Pyrarchon
stages.bio: Pyrarchon is a massive red-orange crab whose great claws are broad enough to use as shields and whose ridged carapace is scarred from decades of stone-grinding. It carries itself with the total stillness of a creature that has never needed to prove anything, claws resting at its sides. When the granite heights flood, Pyrarchon appears on the highest ledge and signals safe routes with deliberate claw movements that every creature in the range has learned to read. Its shell has become part of the mountain - moss and small stones have lodged in its grooves.
stages.note: A fully grown Pyrarchon's claw-grip can hold a granite boulder the size of a wagon, yet it uses those same claws to lift small creatures out of flood-pools without a scratch.

stages.name: Doekit
stages.bio: Doekit is a tiny spotted fawn with large dark eyes and neat little white-tipped hooves. Its coat is a warm tan with delicate white spots along its back, and its small stub-antlers are barely visible as two tiny bumps. It steps carefully through Verdant Valley's flower-carpeted floor, nose always close to the ground, reading each petal like a page. Children spot it most often at dawn when it grazes on dew-wet clover and blinks sleepily at anyone who approaches too fast.
stages.note: Doekit knows every flowering plant in its home meadow by scent and will stand over a wilting one for hours, breathing warmth into its leaves.

stages.name: Stagbark
stages.bio: Stagbark has grown into a lean, alert stag with a full set of branching antlers and a coat that has deepened to a rich chestnut brown. Its white spots have faded to a pale dapple. It moves through the valley's canopy breaks with measured care, pausing often to read the air with wide nostrils. In the dappled clearing where Akilla once taught the first words, Stagbark still visits each evening, though it cannot say why - it only knows the ground there feels different under its hooves.
stages.note: Stagbark's antler-tips glow faintly gold at sunrise, just long enough for a child to see the direction of the nearest water source.

stages.name: Floracrown
stages.bio: Floracrown is a magnificent great stag whose spreading antlers are wound with living vines and blooming pink flowers that never wilt, even in the dry season. Small tufts of flowering moss grow along its back, and trails of pale petals fall behind each step it takes. The Light seeps through its coat in faint gold veins, and animals throughout Verdant Valley grow still and attentive when it raises its crowned head. Ancient texts say Floracrown carries the memory of every promise made in the valley since the first guardian arrived.
stages.note: The flowers on Floracrown's antlers open for new blossoms only when a child in the valley masters a word they have struggled with for a long time.

stages.name: Floret
stages.bio: Floret is little more than a cheerful yellow body with three wide leaf-wings fanning out on each side, making it look more like a flying flower than an insect. Two short antennae bob as it hovers at low altitude, and its tiny round eyes study every passing leaf with great concentration. It lives in the Bug Thicket's sunlit glades, feeding on pollen dust that drifts between the canopy gaps. Floret moves in tight loops, tasting the air, and always finds its way home even when it wanders far.
stages.note: Floret can hover motionless for up to four minutes while it decides whether a particular flower petal is worth landing on.

stages.name: Florant
stages.bio: Florant has grown a longer armored yellow-gold body and its leaf-wings have narrowed into sharper blades, buzzing at a frequency that makes nearby grass hum sympathetically. It now hunts fast, darting between trunks in the Bug Thicket like a living arrow, tracking the subtle scents left by ripe seed-clusters. Its antennae have extended and curve back along its body, and its mandibles have hardened enough to score bark. Experienced Thicket guides say a grove guarded by Florant never loses a tree to blight.
stages.note: When Florant's wings beat at full speed, the vibration shakes loose exactly the seeds it wants to eat - the rest stay on the stem.

stages.name: Floravant
stages.bio: Floravant is a heavy-bodied gold-green insect with broad overlapping leaf-blade wings and thick segmented armor plating. Its clawed legs grip bark like a vice, and when it spreads its full wingspan, the canopy around it goes still - smaller insects stop flying and leaves flatten. It patrols the Bug Thicket's oldest trees, repairing damaged bark with resin it produces itself, and its buzzing presence drives off anything that would cut or burn the grove. Guardians left a small carving of Floravant at every old tree in the thicket as a marker of protection.
stages.note: Floravant can seal a wound in a tree's bark within two hours using a resin it secretes from glands behind its mandibles.

stages.name: Floxlin
stages.bio: Floxlin is a perfectly round lamb whose cream-white fleece is so thick it seems more cloud than wool. Its small pink face peers out from the fluff with a wide, content expression, and when a breeze passes through the Light Grove, the fleece ripples and sheds tiny motes of brightness that hang in the air for a few seconds before fading. It follows anyone who moves slowly and calmly, nudging their ankles with the top of its woolly head. The guardians kept Floxlin in the grove's clearing as a gentle weather sign - fleece puffing out means a warm wind is coming.
stages.note: Floxlin's fleece grows exactly one centimeter longer on the side the next day's wind will come from.

stages.name: Floxcur
stages.bio: Floxcur has grown stocky and sure-footed, with a pair of curling horns and a dense fleece that stands out from its body in windswept tufts. Its coat has lightened to near-white with a faint luminous sheen, and when it trots across a sunlit clearing the grass bends away from it as though parting in respect. It navigates the Light Grove's shifting air corridors with perfect instinct, and younger creatures follow its path through fog because Floxcur never walks into a dead-end.
stages.note: Floxcur butts its curled horns against grove-stones three times each dawn; locals say the knocking sound tells the grove it is still being watched over.

stages.name: Floxarch
stages.bio: Floxarch is a great broad ram whose massive curled horns sweep wide and whose dense mane-fleece has turned a luminous silver-white. The grove's light threads through its coat permanently now, giving it a gentle halo visible even at midday. When it stamps a hoof, the air ripples outward in a visible pressure wave that bends tall grass for twenty meters. Ancient and deliberate, Floxarch spends long hours standing on the high ridge of the grove, facing the wind, as if reading something written in the air that no one else can see.
stages.note: Floxarch never lies down during a storm; it simply lowers its massive head and holds still, and the wind parts around it like water around a stone.

stages.name: Flurrchick
stages.bio: Flurrchick is a pudgy yellow chick with bright blue eyes and tufts of down that lift in any breeze, making it look perpetually startled. Its small wings already flutter constantly, generating more hot air than lift, and its beak clacks together in time with its excitement. It lives in the warm updraft crevices of Dragon Spire's lower ledges where volcanic heat meets open sky, riding short thermals back and forth between the same two rocks all morning. Anything shiny gets one firm peck before Flurrchick moves on.
stages.note: Flurrchick's down-feathers are always warm to the touch even in the coldest part of the spire's shadow-face.

stages.name: Flurron
stages.bio: Flurron stands tall on the spire's wind-carved outcrops, yellow and orange plumage fanning in the updrafts, wings spread wide to catch the thermals. Its crest of bright feathers rises when it senses a weather change, and it crows loudly into the rising wind whenever the Dragon Spire's fire-vents belch fresh heat. It has mastered the art of riding the spire's updrafts for hours without a single wingbeat, circling the volcanic peak in lazy spirals while spotting visitors from a great distance.
stages.note: Flurron crows exactly twice before every thermal spike that rolls off the spire - miners below use it as a three-minute warning.

stages.name: Inflaryx
stages.bio: Inflaryx is a magnificent great bird whose white, yellow, and orange plumage blazes at the wingtips into living flame, and whose feathered crest stands like a crown of fire-tongues. When it spreads its full wings across the spire's summit, the thermals for a kilometer in every direction respond - ascending columns of heated air mark its flight path like visible roads. Dragon Spire's oldest legends say Inflaryx was circling the peak before the first guardian ever arrived, and that it decided, with great seriousness, to let them stay.
stages.note: Inflaryx has not landed on the same ledge twice in recorded history - it remembers every rock it has touched.

stages.name: Leafkin
stages.bio: Leafkin is a small, upright creature with a round pale body and large green leaf-ears that fan out wider than its head. Three leaf-tufts sprout from its crown, and a broad green leaf-tail sweeps behind it. Its bright green eyes glow softly in the dim light of the Dark Forest, making it easy to spot among the roots - which is how younger creatures find their way back to the path. When wind moves through the canopy, Leafkin's leaf-ears tilt like tiny radar dishes, reading the direction and weight of every gust.
stages.note: Leafkin's three crown-tufts each bend toward a different wind direction; together they show the full wind-rose without a compass.

stages.name: Frondeer
stages.bio: Frondeer is a young stag whose body is armored with overlapping layers of green leaves and whose branching antlers each end in small leaf-clusters that whisper in the breeze. Yellow flower-dots mark its flanks like a second coat, and its eyes carry the focused calm of a creature that has memorized every hiding place in the Dark Forest. It moves through the densest undergrowth without a sound, leaf-antlers threading between branches as naturally as any twig. Travelers lost in the forest recognize Frondeer by the faint leaf-rustle that stays just ahead of them on the path home.
stages.note: Frondeer sheds one leaf from its antler-clusters for every hour it spends in direct sunlight - a useful clock for forest travelers.

stages.name: Verdantler
stages.bio: Verdantler is a great leonine stag whose entire body is wrapped in a living coat of leaves, from the full-mane of layered fronds around its neck to the dense leaf-plating along its back and flanks. Its massive antlers branch high and wide, each tine carrying three or four leaf-clusters that catch even the faintest breeze and amplify it into a soft roar that fills the Dark Forest's canopy. The forest's oldest trees tilt toward it slightly when it passes - as though bowing to a guardian they have known for centuries.
stages.note: When Verdantler shakes its mane, the leaves it sheds drift upward rather than down, rising until they reach the canopy and reattach to whatever branch needs them most.

stages.name: Leafox
stages.bio: Leafox is a small green fox-pup with large golden eyes and a bushy tail that ends in a cluster of rounded leaves. Its ears are lined with delicate leaf-veining, and small leaf-tufts grow along the top of its head. It zips through the Bug Thicket's undergrowth in short bursts, stopping to sniff each new plant with intense concentration before tearing off again. The light filtering through the thicket canopy catches the sheen of its leaf-markings and traces bright lines across the forest floor wherever it runs.
stages.note: Leafox's leaf-tail turns a deeper green whenever rain is less than thirty minutes away, acting as a reliable weather warning for forest travelers.

stages.name: Verdfox
stages.bio: Verdfox has grown into a lean, confident fox with a rich green coat shot through with golden veins that glow when the Bug Thicket's light-beams reach it. Its tail has expanded into a full fan of overlapping green leaves, and it uses this fan to sweep trails clear of debris so younger creatures can follow safely. Gold circlets mark its legs where the light element has crystallized into living ornament. It knows the Bug Thicket's paths by a combination of scent and light-angle, navigating confidently even when fog cuts visibility to a meter.
stages.note: Verdfox marks safe paths through the thicket by pressing its leaf-tail against moss-covered stones, leaving a faint bioluminescent stamp that lasts three days.

stages.name: Sylvamane
stages.bio: Sylvamane is a large, imposing fox with a flowing mane of living leaves that cascades from its head and shoulders like a cloak, glowing softly gold where the light filters through. Multiple leaf-tails stream behind it in a layered fan, and every step it takes leaves brief glowing footprints in the soil that fade after a few seconds. It walks the outer edge of the Bug Thicket each night, checking that every boundary-plant is healthy, and its golden eyes can read the health of a tree from thirty meters away. Guardians called it the Warden of Green Light.
stages.note: Sylvamane sleeps standing up, eyes half-open, and the glow of its mane dims or brightens with the health of the forest around it.

stages.name: Frondlet
stages.bio: Frondlet is a small bright-green creature that sits upright like a vigilant lizard, with a row of pointy green spikes running from its crown down its back. Its large golden eyes and slightly grumpy expression give it the look of a tiny creature taking itself very seriously. Found in the sunny clearings of Verdant Valley where the grass grows tall, it spends most of its time sitting perfectly still among the stems, listening. When it does move, every motion is precise and deliberate - this creature has never taken a careless step.
stages.note: Frondlet's back-spikes each point a different direction when wind shifts, mapping gusts across the valley floor more accurately than any weather vane.

stages.name: Frondarch
stages.bio: Frondarch has grown into a powerfully built four-legged dragon with ridged green-gold plating across its back and a spiral leaf-marking etched into its flank like a natural sigil. Its spines have grown longer and harder, and the deep golden eyes now carry a spark of genuine fire. It walks the outer edges of Verdant Valley where the grass meets the wilder undergrowth, marking territory with scratches on stones. Other grass-creatures give it a respectful distance - not because Frondarch is aggressive, but because it radiates a quiet certainty that takes up space.
stages.note: Frondarch can bite through a vine as thick as a wrist in one snap and immediately weaves the halves back together into a tighter knot than before.

stages.name: Frondyrant
stages.bio: Frondyrant is a massive quadruped dragon covered in thick overlapping plates of dark green armor, each plate edged in gold. Its spine is now a continuous ridge of great curved horns, and the swirling vine-sigil on its flank has expanded to cover most of its side in luminous green spiral patterns. It settles at the heart of Verdant Valley each season-change and the valley's plants seem to grow faster, taller, and greener in a circle around its resting spot. Guardians who knew it as a hatchling still bring it exactly three leaves of sweet clover as a greeting - it accepts them with great solemnity.
stages.note: Every plant within ten meters of a resting Frondyrant grows at twice its normal rate, including weeds, which Frondyrant finds mildly undignified.

stages.name: Sproutbuck
stages.bio: Sproutbuck is a slim fawn with a warm tan coat and two prominent leaf-tipped ears that catch every forest sound. Two small leaves sprout from the top of its head like a living crown, perking up when it hears something interesting and drooping when it grows bored. It picks its way through the Dark Forest's root-tangles on delicate hooves, always stepping exactly where a previous foot fell, never snapping a twig. When it blinks its wide eyes at a stranger, experienced travelers feel an unexpected urge to speak more quietly.
stages.note: Sproutbuck's two head-leaves fold flat against its skull in heavy rain, but extend fully to catch the first drop of post-storm sunlight, acting as a living sundial.

stages.name: Leafdoe
stages.bio: Leafdoe stands upright and alert, antlers now branched and tipped with fresh leaf-clusters that nod in any breeze. Its body has slimmed and elongated, and it moves with an upright, almost contemplative posture - more watching than fleeing. In the Dark Forest, where light arrives at strange angles, Leafdoe serves as an informal landmark: travelers note its white belly-patch visible from a distance and orient themselves to it. It never moves away from an approaching child, only turns its head to keep them in sight.
stages.note: Leafdoe's antler-leaves are always fresh green, even in midwinter - forest researchers have never found a withered one.

stages.name: Verdantarch
stages.bio: Verdantarch is a tall, elegant stag whose antlers branch widely into a full canopy of leaves that shift with every breeze passing through the Dark Forest. Its posture is upright and composed, with a narrow refined face and long legs that carry it silently between the oldest trees. The forest seems to breathe differently when Verdantarch is present - the wind moves in steady, predictable patterns rather than random gusts, as if it is channeling the airflow deliberately. Its antler-canopy has become a shelter for dozens of small forest creatures that nest among its leaf-branches.
stages.note: Verdantarch's antler-spread has never been measured exactly the same way twice; it appears to grow new branches after every storm to replace ones lost.

stages.name: Frondfawn
stages.bio: Frondfawn is a compact green-furred pup with large leaf-shaped ears and a bushy tail that ends in a cluster of round leaves. A yellow sun-disc marking glows on its flank, and the leaf-tufts on its head bounce with every step. It dashes through the Bug Thicket's low undergrowth in excited figure-eights, nose to the ground, following trails of pollen and insect-scent for no reason other than curiosity. Its tiny paws leave leaf-shaped prints in soft soil, as though the forest is stamping itself wherever it goes.
stages.note: Frondfawn digs a small hole at the base of every new tree it meets and deposits one seed inside; it has no memory of doing this.

stages.name: Frondeen
stages.bio: Frondeen has grown into a powerful four-legged creature with a broad chest and a back covered in overlapping leaf-plates that make a soft clatter when it moves at speed. Its legs are strong and its bearing is confident; it marks the Bug Thicket's territories by pressing its leafy flanks against border-stones as it patrols. A yellow sun-mark still glows on its side, brighter now, and when it stands in a sunbeam the whole clearing seems to warm slightly. Thicket guides call Frondeen the Green Sentry because it always faces the direction from which something new will arrive.
stages.note: Frondeen can detect an insect hive hidden inside a hollow tree from twenty meters away and navigate directly to it without circling.

stages.name: Frondstag
stages.bio: Frondstag is a great shaggy beast covered head to tail in thick layers of curling leaf-armor, its back rising in a dramatic mane of spiral green fronds and its broad face framed by long flowing leaf-tendrils. Swirling green-and-gold patterns cover every visible surface of its body. It moves heavily but with absolute sureness through the Bug Thicket, and the breeze it generates just by walking rustles the canopy overhead as it passes. Insects that would otherwise swarm in the thicket move aside in an orderly column when Frondstag approaches, as though following an ancient agreement.
stages.note: Frondstag's spiral mane-fronds slowly rotate counterclockwise on calm days and clockwise before a storm; the direction has never been wrong.

stages.name: Frondcub
stages.bio: Frondcub is a round-bodied little grazer with stubby legs, a broad flat nose, and a cluster of fresh green leaves sprouting from the top of its head like a hat that grew there. Its hide is a warm sandy brown with faint scale-like patterning, and its wide dark eyes blink slowly as it samples every plant it encounters. It lives on the grassy ledges of Granite Heights where thin soil patches between the stone, and it has learned to eat every edible thing it finds immediately, because the next patch may be far away.
stages.note: Frondcub can strip every edible leaf from a granite-ledge plant in under four seconds while leaving the roots and stem completely undamaged.

stages.name: Frondaur
stages.bio: Frondaur is a stocky, low-slung beast with rocky stone-plated armor across its back and a row of leaf-edged spines running from neck to tail. Thick clawed legs grip the granite paths effortlessly, and its broad snout is reinforced with dense cartilage for digging roots from rock crevices. It navigates the heights with slow, methodical confidence - never rushing, never retreating. Climbers say Frondaur's tunnels through dense undergrowth have saved more lives than any trail marker, because they always lead to the next ledge above.
stages.note: Frondaur sheds exactly two stone-plates from its back each autumn; mountain builders collect them for steps because each one is load-bearing flat.

stages.name: Frondbara
stages.bio: Frondbara is a massive, shaggy-maned beast whose back is covered in thick stone-like armor plates interspersed with broad leaf-growths, as though the granite heights themselves have taken on animal form. Its great broad head sweeps low to the ground as it walks, and each footfall leaves a shallow impression in even the hardest ledge-stone. Lichen and small ferns grow from the older plates on its back, turning it into a walking garden that seeds the higher, barren ledges wherever it roams. Granite Heights settlers believe a mountain with a Frondbara on it will never lose its soil.
stages.note: Frondbara has been observed carrying a fallen climber's pack for four hours up a sheer path to where help was waiting, without anyone having asked it to.

stages.name: Frondyte
stages.bio: Frondyte is a small upright lizard-type creature covered in bright green spines from crown to tail tip. Its large golden eyes regard the world with a calm, measuring look far older than its small body suggests. It hatches near the outer cool-stone ring of the Lava Crater where green mosses manage to grow despite the heat, and it spends its days eating those mosses while the crater's warmth radiates up through the rock beneath it. The combination of volcanic mineral-soil and cool green growth gives this hatchling a constitution that surprises everything that tries to outrun it.
stages.note: Frondyte's spines absorb volcanic mineral steam from the crater air; each spine contains trace amounts of obsidian that crystallizes slowly over its lifetime.

stages.name: Frondax
stages.bio: Frondax is a lean, aggressive lizard-dragon whose green spines have grown long and blade-edged, running in multiple rows down its back and flanks. Small tusks curve upward from its lower jaw, and its tail is thick and spiked. It patrols the transition zone of the Lava Crater where basalt stone meets scattered grass, hunting insects that cluster on the warm rock-faces. The heat seems to energize rather than exhaust it, and it can sprint across a scorching rock field that would burn any unarmored foot.
stages.note: Frondax can climb sheer basalt walls using only the edges of its flank-spines as grips, and descends facing forward - a rare combination of agility and nerve.

stages.name: Frondsaur
stages.bio: Frondsaur is a formidable full-grown dragon whose body is a tapestry of long green spines, swept-back horns, and muscled limbs that look carved from the crater's oldest basalt. Its wings are broad and fern-patterned, built as much for gliding the crater's thermal columns as for powered flight. Where it rests at night, a ring of surprisingly lush grass springs up by morning, fed by the mineral-rich residue its scales leave on rock surfaces. Lava Crater settlers speak of Frondsaur with respect: it is the only thing that grows greener the closer it gets to the fire.
stages.note: Frondsaur's shed scales are used by crater-side herbalists as the only planting substrate in which crater-edge herbs will reliably germinate.

stages.name: Frondhoot
stages.bio: Frondhoot starts life as a small, sturdy-looking creature with a boar-like face and a dramatic crown of large green leaves erupting from the top of its head. Its round body and short legs give it a determined, slightly top-heavy appearance as it trots into the Gale Ridge's lower winds. It is fearless about weather in a way that impresses creatures twice its size, pressing its leaf-crown directly into gusts that would send lighter animals skidding. The leaves on its head act as natural sails, and it steers by angling them.
stages.note: Frondhoot navigates by tilting its leaf-crown and letting the wind do the steering - it has never taken a wrong path in a headwind.

stages.name: Frondwise
stages.bio: Frondwise has transformed into a broad-winged owl with a full leaf-ruff framing its disc-face and long green-brown wing feathers that whisper in the storm winds. Its large yellow eyes seem to glow from within, and it can hold completely still on a ledge while a gale howls around it, feathers pressing flat while its leaf-ruff fans wide. Gale Ridge climbers say Frondwise always perches above the safe path and that following the direction its beak points has saved more lives than any guidebook.
stages.note: Frondwise can rotate its head 270 degrees and has been seen scanning three separate storm-fronts simultaneously without moving its body.

stages.name: Frondophage
stages.bio: Frondophage is a great owl whose wingspan spans the width of the Gale Ridge's widest ledge, and whose leaf-patterned feathers have layered into a deep green-brown armor of overlapping fronds. When it opens its wings fully, the wind passing through its feathers produces a chord of tones audible from the valley floor. It hunts in the highest storm-belts, riding turbulence that would destroy any other flier, reading weather patterns the way other creatures read faces. The Gale Ridge's oldest legend says Frondophage was already nesting in the peak when the first storm was born.
stages.note: Frondophage's flight is silent in calm air, but in a storm its wings produce a low harmonic that calms smaller creatures sheltering below.

stages.name: Frondling
stages.bio: Frondling is a small, lively fox-type creature with green-tipped leaf-ears and a bushy tail of layered leaves that holds warmth in the cool desert nights. Its green and tan coat blends into the dry scrub of the Amber Desert perfectly, and its small golden eyes catch firelight well in the pre-dawn hours when it does most of its exploring. It finds the sparse flowering plants of the desert fringes and curls around them to share warmth, keeping them alive through nights cold enough to kill most blooms.
stages.note: Frondling's leaf-tail retains enough heat after a day in the desert sun to keep a small campfire-stone warm for three hours after sunset.

stages.name: Frondance
stages.bio: Frondance is a lean, swift fox-type creature whose layered leaf-mane fans out behind it as it runs the Amber Desert's dune-ridges. The undersides of its leaves have charred slightly golden from seasons of desert heat, giving its mane a warm amber-green color. It is a tireless runner, loping across ten kilometers of sand without breaking stride, and it can find the cool-side of any dune by scent alone. Desert caravans watch for Frondance's path: where it has recently run, the sand is firm enough to carry a loaded cart.
stages.note: Frondance's paw-prints, when arranged in a line, point unerringly toward the nearest living plant with water in its roots.

stages.name: Frondelk
stages.bio: Frondelk is a powerful, broad-shouldered creature with a magnificent mane of large pointed leaves that range from deep green at the roots to warm amber-gold at the tips, as though caught permanently in sunset. Multiple tails of layered leaves fan behind it, and every step it takes on the dune-crest leaves a small ring of green shoots in the compacted sand that - impossibly - survive a full week before the desert heat claims them. The Amber Desert's old traders named its regular route the Green Road, and they navigate by it even when wind erases every other landmark.
stages.note: Wherever Frondelk has slept, the sand underneath reveals a perfectly preserved grass-circle that dune scholars use to map ancient water-tables.

stages.name: Frondcalf
stages.bio: Frondcalf is a round, compact creature that looks like a small antelope puppy with a cluster of fresh green leaves growing from the top of its head and a short tail tipped in leaf. Its warm brown coat has a faint scale-like shimmer, and the leaf-sprout on its crown bobs cheerfully with each step. At Dragon Spire's lower slopes where the warm-air thermals keep a surprising strip of green grass, Frondcalf grazes with the focused attention of something that knows it is in a dangerous neighborhood and means to thrive anyway.
stages.note: Frondcalf's leaf-crown doubles in size between dawn and dusk on days when a dragon-thermal is expected, acting as a natural warning flag.

stages.name: Frondhorn
stages.bio: Frondhorn has grown into a formidable quadruped with a brown-and-green armor hide and multiple rows of stiff leaf-spines running along its back. Its four legs are thick and powerful, built for negotiating Dragon Spire's steep obsidian paths, and its now-prominent shoulder spines make it look wider than it is tall. When dragon-fire sweeps down the slope, Frondhorn simply lowers its head and holds - its leaf-spines absorb the heat and release it as a warm, dry wind from its flanks that actually fertilizes the sparse grass around it.
stages.note: Frondhorn's back-spines store enough heat from a dragon-fire pass to warm a small camp for a full night, if you don't mind the faint smell of scorched leaves.

stages.name: Frondakhan
stages.bio: Frondakhan is an enormous, low-slung armored creature whose back is a fortress of interlocking leaf-armor plates and whose great spiked tail sweeps the path behind it clean of loose stone. Rings of overlapping leaf-spines cover its flanks and neck, and the whole body has deepened to a dark green-brown that makes it nearly invisible against Dragon Spire's vegetation. When a dragon passes overhead, Frondakhan does not flinch - it watches, and the dragon veers aside. This is the creature that taught the Spire's inhabitants that the most powerful thing on a mountain is not always the one that breathes fire.
stages.note: Frondakhan's tail-sweep, performed once a day, clears enough loose stone from the spire-paths to prevent three separate rockfalls that would otherwise occur.

stages.name: Frosicalf
stages.bio: Frosicalf is a small, round-bodied calf with a short single horn of pale blue ice rising from its forehead and a coat that shimmers with frost-patterns in seafoam blue. Its round eyes and stubby legs give it a determined, if wobbly, look as it wades the tidal shallows of Frozen Peaks. The water around its hooves drops a few degrees when it steps in, forming a thin skin of ice that cracks pleasantly as it walks and serves as a fishing platform for the peaks' smaller creatures who hop on before it melts.
stages.note: Frosicalf's ice-horn grows exactly one millimeter per day in winter and retreats the same amount in summer, acting as a precise seasonal calendar.

stages.name: Frostaur
stages.bio: Frostaur is a powerful, shaggy bull whose thick white-blue coat is permanently rimmed with frost crystals and whose two long horns curve outward and up. The water temperature of a mountain tarn drops noticeably within minutes of Frostaur wading in, and the cold-moss along its regular paths has adapted to those sudden chills, growing in a shade of blue found nowhere else in the range. Its massive neck and shoulders carry the frost-coat like armour, and rival creatures give it a wide berth - not out of fear, but because direct contact leaves a ten-second cold-burn.
stages.note: Frostaur's hoofprints in the peak scree fill with clear cold meltwater that stays fresh for two days - a useful water source for small animals in the dry season.

stages.name: Glacihorn
stages.bio: Glacihorn is a titanic ice-encrusted creature whose entire body is now more glacier than animal, with great ice-formations growing along its spine and a crown of crystalline horns that chime in the mountain wind. Its breath comes out as dense blue-white vapour and its footsteps leave ice that lingers on bare rock for days. Frozen Peaks' oldest herders say Glacihorn appears at the start of every cold season and that the range's meltwater follows its path - where it wades, the cold currents arrive, and where the cold currents arrive, everything else follows.
stages.note: A single horn-tip chip shed by Glacihorn keeps a full barrel of water cold for a week without ice - collectors leave offerings at the snowline.

stages.name: Frostail
stages.bio: Frostail is a plump caterpillar-like larva whose body is made up of eight shining blue ice-segments, each one slightly translucent with frozen water visible inside. Two small antennae curl forward over wide blue eyes, and its many tiny legs grip the frost-slick rocks with surprising security even when spray washes over it. It moves with a slow, measured rocking gait and spends much of its time sitting still, letting the spray freeze on its outer shell to build its next layer. Each segment is slightly colder than the one before it, measured from head to tail.
stages.note: Frostail's ice-segments crack and re-seal each night with a sound like distant bells - a sound the peaks-folk recognise as the sign of a hard-frost morning.

stages.name: Glacail
stages.bio: Glacail has sealed itself inside a magnificent ice-crystal cocoon studded with a snowflake pattern and ringed with spines of aquamarine crystal. Inside, the slow work of transformation goes on - the cocoon holds its interior three degrees below the air around it, by a process no researcher has yet explained. Snow-hares and small birds shelter in the cocoon's lee during a thaw, using the pocket of hard cold it keeps as a refuge. The snowflake imprint on its shell is unique to each individual, like a fingerprint.
stages.note: A Glacail cocoon found on the beach marks the precise point where the year's coldest bay-current will arrive, always within two days.

stages.name: Crystalyx
stages.bio: Crystalyx emerges from its cocoon as a stunning ice-wing butterfly whose four wings are patterned with perfect crystalline veining and shimmer with blue-white light. It flies low over the snowfields of Frozen Peaks, the chill of its wing-beats leaving brief frost-trails that catch the morning light. Small ice-crystals trail from its wingtips and settle on the rock, where they melt into mineral-rich water that feeds the cold-moss. Frozen Peaks children traditionally say winter has arrived the moment they spot the first Crystalyx of the season.
stages.note: Crystalyx's wingbeat produces a frequency that keeps cold-moss from dying back within a five-meter radius - field researchers actively chart its flight corridors.

stages.name: Fawnfrost
stages.bio: A dainty fawn no taller than a garden gate, Fawnfrost has pale cream fur dusted silver and two small icy-blue antler buds that catch the light like frozen dewdrops. Its eyes hold a gentle glow - locals say it can sense a child's worry before a sound is spoken. It wanders the outer snowfields of Frozen Peaks at dusk, leaving faint frost prints that shimmer and disappear by morning. The guardians called it the Listening Fawn, for it would always pause and turn its ears toward any voice learning something new.
stages.note: Its antler buds ring softly when a nearby creature feels calm - they go silent when danger approaches.

stages.name: Stagchill
stages.bio: Stagchill stands tall and proud, its warm brown coat flecked with frost patterns that spread across its flanks in winter. Its antlers have grown into full branching racks of pale blue ice, each tine sharp as a shard of frozen glass. When it exhales on cold mornings, its breath crystallizes into tiny floating motes that drift upward instead of down. It patrols the silver birch corridors of Frozen Peaks, and young creatures that follow it safely through the mist often find themselves remembering sounds they had long forgotten.
stages.note: Stagchill always walks the same path through the snowfield every dawn - cartographers have mapped its route as the safest trail through the mist.

stages.name: Glaciarch
stages.bio: Ancient texts say Glaciarch appears only when the Frozen Peaks needs to remember something important, and that staring into its antlers long enough will show you something you have always known but never admitted.
stages.note: A full rack of Glaciarch antlers contains exactly 108 tines - no more, no less, across every individual ever recorded.

stages.name: Chillpod
stages.bio: Chillpod is a pale blue segmented grub, plump and round, with a soft ridged body that always feels cool to the touch like a stone from a mountain stream. Its six tiny legs barely reach the ground as it rolls and wriggles through the undergrowth of Verdant Valley, searching for the coldest, shadiest mossy hollows. Though small and slow, Chillpod leaves a faint icy shimmer on every leaf it crawls across. Explorers in the valley say finding one nestled in your boot means an unusually cold winter is coming.
stages.note: Chillpod only moves when no one is looking - place it on a leaf and look away, and it will have vanished by the time you glance back.

stages.name: Chrysofrost
stages.bio: Chrysofrost has sealed itself inside a smooth teardrop-shaped shell of pale blue crystal, its interior form visible as a shadowy outline through the translucent walls. Faint leaf-vein patterns glow softly inside, pulsing once every few minutes like a slow heartbeat. It hangs from branches in the coldest parts of Verdant Valley, sometimes for weeks at a time. The guardians believed that stories whispered near a Chrysofrost would be absorbed into its forming mind, so they would tell the old tales beside the hanging chrysalises each morning.
stages.note: If you tap a Chrysofrost shell and hold your ear close, you can hear a faint humming of whatever word was last spoken near it.

stages.name: Glacewing
stages.bio: Glacewing emerges a fearsome sight: a sleek pale blue wasp with large multifaceted eyes, four jagged legs tipped with ice hooks, and two pairs of wings printed with perfect snowflake patterns. Its wingspan creates a sharp buzzing hum that drops the air temperature by two degrees wherever it hovers. Each wingbeat scatters tiny ice crystals that drift down like silent snow. It is rarely aggressive, preferring to patrol the high tree canopy of Verdant Valley, but any creature that threatens its territory finds itself flash-frozen mid-motion.
stages.note: A Glacewing's snowflake wing patterns are unique to each individual - no two have ever been found identical.

stages.name: Frostkit
stages.bio: Frostkit is a small fluffy white fox cub with oversized paws and a thick rounded tail that curves up over its back. A single pale blue gem sits on its forehead, glowing faintly when it is thinking hard. Its fur is impossibly soft - visitors at the Frozen Peaks often describe petting it as touching a fresh snowfall. Despite living at the base of the towering spire, Frostkit rarely strays far from the shelter of snow-covered boulders, poking out its round face only when it hears an unfamiliar sound that interests it.
stages.note: Frostkit's forehead gem glows brightest just before it falls asleep - researchers believe it dreams in colors that have no names yet.

stages.name: Frostyne
stages.bio: Frostyne has grown lean and fast, its white fur now edged with pale blue, and two small feathery wings have emerged from its shoulders that are more for balance than flight. Cold wisps trail from its paws and tail as it sprints, leaving ghost-prints in its wake. It has discovered it can read the intentions of nearby creatures - not sounds, but a feeling of what they plan to do next. Frozen Peaks travelers say Frostyne always steps aside exactly one second before a falling icicle strikes where it stood.
stages.note: Frostyne has never been hit by a falling icicle at the spire - locals claim it has never been surprised by anything at all.

stages.name: Glacifox
stages.bio: It no longer merely senses intentions; it can place a thought or a memory directly into a nearby mind with the precision of a needle. The Guardians named it the Voice That Doesn't Speak, and it served as a judge in disputes nobody else could settle.
stages.note: Glacifox's nine tails move completely independently of each other - each tail is said to carry a different memory from the past nine winters.

stages.name: Chillpup
stages.bio: Chillpup looks harmless enough - a soft blue-white pup with wide round eyes and a fluffy tail - but the Crystal Mines have left their mark on it. Its fur carries a faint metallic sheen, and it is far quicker to growl than to wag. It has learned to use the darkness between crystal formations to hide with uncanny skill, its pale coat blending with the frost-rimed walls in a way that makes miners nervous. Small enough to sit in a lap but sharp enough to bite a boot clean through, Chillpup is not a creature to underestimate.
stages.note: Chillpup can vanish between two crystal columns in less than a heartbeat - miners call this vanishing trick the "cold blink."

stages.name: Glacière
stages.bio: Glacière has shed its puppy roundness entirely, replacing it with lean, angular muscle and a bristling mane of sharp ice spikes along its spine that rattle faintly when it moves. Long curved fangs extend below its jaw, and its eyes have sharpened from round innocence to a focused, calculating cold. It hunts through the Crystal Mines by listening for the faint sound of crystal resonance, tracking prey by the vibrations their footsteps make in the stone. Its territory is marked not by scent but by hairline frost cracks left in the walls.
stages.note: Glacière can hear a single drop of water falling from the mine ceiling from over sixty meters away through solid stone.

stages.name: Blizzaroch
stages.bio: Blizzaroch fills the mine corridors like a storm filling a valley. Rows of enormous ice spikes line its back and flanks, and deep scar-lines across its hide tell of ancient battles fought before any current guardian was born. Its massive jaws open to reveal fangs the length of pickaxes. When Blizzaroch howls, frost forms instantly on every nearby crystal, and the temperature in the mines drops so fast that breath freezes before it leaves the mouth. The Crystal Mines belong to Blizzaroch - everything else in them is simply a guest.
stages.note: The ice spikes along Blizzaroch's back never melt, even when carried out of the mines into summer heat - they simply grow colder.

stages.name: Frostyx
stages.bio: Frostyx is a roly-poly pale blue calf with a single short spiraling horn, enormous round eyes, and small solid hooves that clop pleasantly on the stones of Frozen Peaks. It is built compact and sturdy, and always seems mildly puzzled by the world, tilting its wide head at leaves, sounds, and passing creatures with equal fascination. Its small horn pulses with faint psychic warmth when it is happy, which is most of the time. The snowfield's eldest trees seem to lean slightly toward it when it passes, as though they recognize something ancient in its quiet gaze.
stages.note: Frostyx always faces the same direction when it sleeps - toward the oldest tree in whatever snowfield it calls home that night.

stages.name: Bovelace
stages.bio: Bovelace has grown into a muscular and wide-shouldered bull, its horns now curving outward in broad sweeps of pale ice-blue. Its coat is thicker and rougher, flecked with permanent frost that does not melt in summer warmth. Despite its imposing size, Bovelace moves with deliberate patience through Frozen Peaks, never rushing, always pausing to observe before acting. When it lowers its head and stamps one wide hoof, other creatures clear the path - not out of fear, but out of respect. It has earned its place as a steadfast guardian.
stages.note: Bovelace will not break into a run unless something sacred is threatened - but when it does charge, it has been clocked covering a kilometer in under two minutes.

stages.name: Tundravok
stages.bio: Tundravok is a legend given body - a colossal ice bison whose entire frame is encased in thick interlocking plates of living ice that have grown over centuries into true armor. Its vast curved horns reach nearly three meters tip to tip and pulse with pale blue psychic light. The ground shakes with each step. The Frozen Peaks was shaped around the paths Tundravok wore into the earth over thousands of years, and those paths are still the safest routes through the snowfield today. It does not fight - it does not need to. It simply stands, and the world waits.
stages.note: Every crystal formation in the Frozen Peaks aligns toward Tundravok when it stands still - as if the whole snowfield is a compass and Tundravok is north.

stages.name: Sporite
stages.bio: Sporite is a tiny round mushroom creature with a smooth brown cap and big wide eyes that blink slowly and independently of each other. Its two stumpy legs shuffle it along the sand with surprising speed for something so round, and tiny spore puffs drift from its cap whenever it hops. Despite living in the Sand Dunes, Sporite thrives where underground moisture seeps up between the dunes, forming small oasis patches that only it can find. Young Sporites are born in clusters of three, and they spend their first weeks following each other in circles.
stages.note: The spores Sporite releases each morning contain a faint sweet smell that attracts underground beetles - which then aerate the soil and help moisture travel upward.

stages.name: Myconaut
stages.bio: Myconaut stands upright now on two solid legs, its broad flat mushroom cap casting a wide shadow over its compact body. It has short sturdy arms it keeps crossed in front of its chest, giving it an air of permanent skepticism. The cap has widened and flattened, and it releases a visible cloud of spores when startled that can put small creatures to sleep for a few hours - a trick it uses to negotiate rather than fight. Myconaut has been spotted at ancient memory-stone sites throughout the Sand Dunes, seemingly reading the carvings.
stages.note: Myconaut is always found within forty meters of an underground water source, even in the driest dune fields - it has never once been wrong.

stages.name: Fungolith
stages.bio: Fungolith is ancient beyond reckoning - more root system than creature now, with thick twisted root-legs that drive deep into the sand and draw water from aquifers no other being has reached. Its trunk-like body is scored with bark, and its massive mushroom cap shelters an entire ecosystem of smaller creatures beneath it. When it speaks, the vibration travels through the ground as much as through the air, and sand dunes shift slightly in response. The oldest oases in the dunes were not natural - they formed beneath a resting Fungolith.
stages.note: Fungolith has never moved more than ten meters in recorded history - but the sand dunes around it have slowly reshaped over centuries to face it.

stages.name: Sporkit
stages.bio: Sporkit is a tiny round turtle with a smooth mushroom-cap growing from the top of its shell, spotted in warm tan and brown. Its four stubby limbs barely lift it off the ground, and it spends most of its time sitting perfectly still on rocky outcroppings of Granite Heights, absorbing warmth and moisture with equal contentment. It can pull its head and all four legs in at once, leaving only the mushroom cap visible - which makes it look remarkably like an ordinary toadstool until it decides to move.
stages.note: Sporkit's mushroom cap changes color slightly with weather - it darkens before rain, even in the usually-dry heights.

stages.name: Fungrok
stages.bio: Fungrok's mushroom cap shell has grown large enough to shelter its entire body, spotted tan and brown with a frill of pale spores along the edge. It sits upright now with a broad flat face and watchful eyes, moving only when necessary - and never faster than a stroll. The granite outcroppings of the Heights are dotted with resting Fungroks that look indistinguishable from boulders to the untrained eye. When multiple Fungroks gather in the same area, their cap spores combine to create a gentle sleep-haze that settles over the rocks like mist.
stages.note: Fungrok has been recorded sitting motionless in the same spot for eleven consecutive days - it emerged only when the sun finally moved fully off its rock.

stages.name: Fungshell
stages.bio: Fungshell has grown into a massive squat tortoise nearly as wide as it is tall, its mushroom-cap shell expanded into a wide flat canopy that acts as a true roof when it hunkers down. Its skin has thickened into warty plated hide, and a thick ring of root-like tendrils hangs from the cap's edge, anchoring it to the ground when it sleeps. Granite Heights locals have built rest shelters near Fungshell nesting sites because the creature's presence keeps dangerous rockslides from reaching paths below - its weight and roots stabilize the slopes.
stages.note: When a Fungshell sneezes - which happens roughly once a month - the spore cloud it releases can fog an entire mountainside for half a day.

stages.name: Sporkling
stages.bio: Sporkling is a small round tortoise-like creature with a smooth spotted mushroom cap growing from its shell, its underside a warm earthy brown. It moves slowly along the sandy amber flats, leaving faint spore trails that glow faint yellow in sunlight. Though it looks gentle, the spores it releases are mildly toxic to plants - any flower that absorbs them wilts within the hour and regrows as something tougher. The guardians of Amber Desert call Sporkling a hidden test: the plants it visits either die or become stronger.
stages.note: Every plant Sporkling visits either withers completely or grows back twice as hardy within a week - there is no middle result.

stages.name: Mycodon
stages.bio: Mycodon has grown warty and wide, its mushroom-cap shell now bristling with raised nodules that secrete a sticky amber resin. A broad squat face peers out from under the cap with hooded eyes that rarely fully open. When threatened, Mycodon presses its belly flat to the desert floor and puffs its cap, releasing a choking spore cloud that makes intruders stagger and then run. Beneath the amber resin on its cap, amber beetles make their nests - a mutual relationship where the beetles clean the cap and Mycodon protects the beetles from birds.
stages.note: Mycodon can hold its breath for twenty-three minutes, which it uses to outlast the spore clouds it releases when it doesn't want to move.

stages.name: Sporgathor
stages.bio: Sporgathor is a formidable presence in the Amber Desert - a vast flat-capped tortoise whose shell has crusted over with thick yellow-green spore patches that pulse visibly every few minutes. Its four legs are dense as tree stumps, and deep furrows in the amber sand mark its ancient routes between the desert's hidden water seeps. The spore patches on its shell can be seen from a kilometer away, warning other creatures to give it a wide berth. Birds that dare to land on its shell and peck at its spores risk a direct spore-blast and are rarely seen twice.
stages.note: Sporgathor's spore blooms on a 28-day cycle that perfectly matches the lunar calendar - desert communities use its blooms to track the months.

stages.name: Gearling
stages.bio: Gearling is a small mechanical-looking praying mantis with segmented dark metal plating over its thorax and abdomen, two slender antennae that double as signal receivers, and small grasping forelimbs it holds raised and ready at all times. It moves in precise, jerky increments, each movement measured rather than fluid, as if calculating the most efficient path before each step. The Steel Fortress hums at a frequency Gearling can feel in its antenna tips, and it follows the vibrations of machinery the way other insects follow flower scent.
stages.note: Gearling can calculate the RPM of any spinning gear by feel alone - it places one foreleg against the housing and counts without looking.

stages.name: Mechant
stages.bio: Mechant stands tall on four legs with the regal posture of a machine that knows its own precision. Its forearms have lengthened into curved scythe-like blades with serrated gear-notch edges that spin freely when it strikes. Its body segments are now reinforced with interlocking metal plates that click into tighter configurations when it braces for impact. Inside the Steel Fortress, Mechant is treated as a maintenance creature - it instinctively tightens loose bolts with its foreleg notches and will spend hours re-routing a jammed gear track until it runs smoothly.
stages.note: Mechant has never missed a strike in a recorded sparring session - engineers in the fortress have bet wages on it for years.

stages.name: Omnivex
stages.bio: Omnivex is the most sophisticated creature in the Steel Fortress - a towering mantis armored in heavy interlocking gear-plate, with broad gear-disc shoulders, six powerful legs, and twin sickle forearms that can slice through reinforced metal bulkheads. Its multiple compound eyes process information from sixteen directions simultaneously. The fortress's automated defense systems were reportedly designed with Omnivex as the model; it still walks the outer ramparts each night in the same pattern the automated turrets follow. Where Omnivex walks, nothing unauthorized survives.
stages.note: Omnivex never attacks from the front - it has never once been documented initiating a strike from a position an opponent was facing.

stages.name: Gelkin
stages.bio: Gelkin bobs through the murky waters of Poison Marsh like a tiny blue lantern, its round translucent bell lit from within by a soft watery glow. Its short tentacles trail behind it in little loops, too stubby to sting but perfect for feeling texture - it presses them against every surface it encounters as if taking notes. Despite the marsh's toxic reputation, Gelkin is completely immune to the mild poisons dissolved in the water, filtering them through its bell and releasing them as harmless cold vapor. Small marsh fish shelter in the chill beneath it.
stages.note: Gelkin's bell pulses exactly twelve times per minute regardless of temperature - researchers use it as an underwater clock.

stages.name: Frostacle
stages.bio: Frostacle has grown noticeably more beautiful and more dangerous. Its bell now bears elegant snowflake patterns that pulse with blue-white light, and its tentacles have multiplied and lengthened, trailing in intricate spirals beneath it. Any creature that brushes the tentacles feels a deep cold seep into the contact point that lingers for hours. Frostacle has learned to use this not aggressively but protectively - it drapes its tentacles over injured marsh creatures and uses the cold to slow swelling and numb pain. The marsh herbalists call it the Cold Nurse.
stages.note: The snowflake patterns on each Frostacle are different - and they always match the frost patterns found on the nearest reed bed at sunrise.

stages.name: Glacimorph
stages.bio: Glacimorph is an imposing and luminous presence in the deepest channels of Poison Marsh. A crown of jagged ice crystals has formed at the top of its pulsing bell, refracting light into cold rainbow shards. Its long flowing tentacles hang in curtains of pale crystalline threads that freeze the water column around them as they drift. When Glacimorph surfaces, a ring of mist forms around it for twenty meters. It does not travel far from the oldest pools in the marsh - those it has occupied longest are the only places where the marsh water runs clear.
stages.note: The ice-crystal crown on Glacimorph grows one new spike per year - the oldest recorded individual had forty-seven spikes.

stages.name: Gemule
stages.bio: Gemule is a plump round purple slug with a smooth lavender body, two tiny blue-tipped antenna stalks that quiver when it senses nearby thoughts, and a perpetually serene expression. It glides slowly across the warm sands of the Dunes, leaving a faint glittering trail that attracts small sand beetles. Gemule is drawn to places where people have sat quietly and thought hard - it seems to absorb residual psychic impressions from the ground and collect them the way other creatures collect pebbles. Finding one asleep on a meditation stone is considered very good fortune.
stages.note: Gemule always crawls toward the spot where the most words were spoken that day - camp storytellers wake to find it on their pillow.

stages.name: Gemaxon
stages.bio: Gemaxon has undergone a dramatic change - its smooth lavender body is now erupting with jagged crystal spikes of magenta and yellow-gold that have pushed through its hide like emerging teeth. The spikes are hard as quartz and vibrate at a frequency that can be felt rather than heard. Despite its spiny appearance, Gemaxon is not aggressive; the crystals are psychic resonators, not weapons, allowing it to broadcast its thoughts to creatures up to fifty meters away. Wandering traders in the Sand Dunes have learned to follow Gemaxon, as it always knows where the next oasis lies.
stages.note: Gemaxon's crystal spikes hum in perfect harmony with each other - but the frequency changes every full moon, and no one has ever predicted what key it will choose.

stages.name: Crystallux
stages.bio: Crystallux has become nearly more crystal than creature - its body is so densely packed with enormous sharp spines of magenta, yellow, and deep purple quartz that the original slug form beneath is almost invisible. It moves slowly, dragging its weight of crystal with perfect dignity, and when it is still it is genuinely difficult to distinguish from a natural crystal formation. Its psychic field now extends far enough to touch the minds of creatures it cannot see, and it sometimes broadcasts entire memories from centuries of accumulated impressions stored in its crystal body.
stages.note: The crystals on Crystallux's body contain visible internal inclusions - each one is a fragment of a memory it has absorbed and crystallized permanently.

stages.name: Gemlite
stages.bio: Gemlite is a small stocky grey rhinoceros calf with a single short horn and wide blue glowing eyes that see slightly into the infrared spectrum, letting it navigate the Crystal Mines in complete darkness. Its smooth grey hide is just beginning to show the faintest raised nodules where future crystal growth will emerge. Despite its small size it is remarkably dense, and attempting to push it when it doesn't want to move is like trying to push a small boulder. It stamps its forehoof twice when pleased and three times when it wants someone to pay attention - trainers learn this quickly.
stages.note: Gemlite can locate any gem vein in a thirty-meter radius by pressing its horn to the wall and standing silent for exactly thirty seconds.

stages.name: Amethorne
stages.bio: Amethorne has grown into a proper rhinoceros with a significant difference: rows of jagged purple amethyst crystals now erupt from its back and sides, catching the mine lantern light and throwing violet patterns across the walls. Its single horn has lengthened and darkened, and its eyes glow a deeper blue. When it charges through a tunnel, the crystal spikes on its flanks score the walls and leave a trail of sparkling purple scratches that miners follow to find new gem seams. Amethorne charges for the joy of it, selecting the longest straight tunnel it can find.
stages.note: The purple crystals on Amethorne's back are harder than the surrounding mine walls - they have never been scratched despite thousands of narrow tunnel passages.

stages.name: Gemnoceros
stages.bio: Gemnoceros is the apex creature of the Crystal Mines - a massive armored rhinoceros whose entire back, shoulders, and flanks are covered in towering clusters of purple and violet crystal formations that have grown into a full natural armor. Rune-like markings of pale blue are etched into the hide between crystal clusters, each one a psychic sigil that focuses its immense mental power. When Gemnoceros stands in the central mine chamber and focuses, it can draw every loose gem in the caves toward itself with a single exhalation. The mines belong to it the way a meadow belongs to its oldest tree.
stages.note: Gemnoceros has been in the Crystal Mines so long that the largest crystal formations grew outward from its sleeping spots - the mines themselves were shaped by its rest.

stages.name: Gemurp
stages.bio: Gemurp is an endearing round brown bear cub with warm amber fur and a cluster of small teal-green gem crystals sprouting from between its shoulder blades like a natural backpack it forgot was there. Its large round paws dig happily into the rocky soil of Granite Heights, unearthing mineral deposits it licks with great concentration. Though it looks soft, the gem cluster on its back is harder than granite, and nuzzling against it accidentally is genuinely uncomfortable. Gemurp collects shiny pebbles and arranges them in patterns around its sleeping spot each night.
stages.note: Every crystal cluster Gemurp deposits around its sleeping spot has been verified as a different mineral type - it never places the same mineral twice in a row.

stages.name: Gemurite
stages.bio: Gemurite has grown into a powerful adult bear with broad shoulders, and the teal-green crystal cluster on its back has expanded into a full ridge of sharp gem spikes running from its neck to its tail base. It still has the warm brown fur of its youth, but it is now shot through with mineral deposits that make its coat feel like touching fine-grain sandstone. Gemurite stamps out territories in Granite Heights by scoring the rock faces with its crystal ridge, leaving vivid green lines that serve as road markers for other creatures. Miners follow those marks to find the richest veins.
stages.note: The teal crystal spikes on Gemurite's back have been verified as a mineral not found anywhere else in the world - only on Gemurites.

stages.name: Crystallion
stages.bio: Crystallion is enormous and magnificent, its entire dorsal surface now encased in dense overlapping teal-green crystal armor that has fused with its spine and ribs into a permanent geological formation. When it walks, the crystal plates grind and shift with a sound like a small avalanche. Its massive crystal claws can cleave solid granite with three swipes. Crystallion's territory encompasses the highest peaks of Granite Heights, where it sleeps for months at a time in deep winter - during which time, lichens and smaller crystals grow over the exposed portions of its crystal ridge, and the mountains seem to breathe more slowly.
stages.note: When Crystallion wakes from its winter sleep, it shakes, and the sound of the crystal avalanche from its back can be heard in the valley below - residents take it as a sign to begin spring planting.

stages.name: Pebble
stages.bio: Pebble is a compact little tortoise whose shell is made of rough grey stone segments rather than the smooth keratin plates most turtles wear. Small irregular chunks of rock jut from the shell's surface like a geological sample come to life. It is extraordinarily heavy for its size - two strong children cannot lift it when it plants itself. It roams the Amber Desert slowly, feeding on mineral-rich soil it digs with wide flat forelimbs, and during the hottest part of the day it simply stops moving and becomes effectively invisible among the amber rocks.
stages.note: Pebble has never once been successfully moved against its will - even the strongest desert winds cannot budge it when it presses down flat.

stages.name: Stonite
stages.bio: Stonite has grown considerably, and its shell has erupted into a field of upright stone spikes that range from stubby to alarmingly sharp. Its thick neck can swing its head in a full arc, and its broad feet are now equipped with flattened granite-hard claws for traction on steep rock faces. Stonite nests in the ancient petrified wood formations at the desert's edge, where the hard wood and its own spikes create a nearly impenetrable defensive ring. Sandstorm researchers have noted that dunes reform around Stonite resting sites rather than burying them - somehow it always ends up on top.
stages.note: Stonite shells are collected by desert communities after they are shed - each shed shell is hard enough to use as a cutting board indefinitely.

stages.name: Crystallith
stages.bio: Crystallith in the Amber Desert is a different legend than the one of the Crystal Mines - this one is wider, older, and slower. Its shell has become a landscape feature: a vast armored plateau covered in meter-tall stone spikes, with desert lichen colonizing the spaces between. Four legs like stone pillars move it with geological patience across the amber sands. When it finally settles in a spot, it may remain for decades, and the dunes build up around it into new formations. The word for "patience" in the desert tongue is borrowed from the name for Crystallith's walking pace.
stages.note: The largest known Crystallith has been tracked crossing the same desert since before living memory - locals say their great-grandparents mapped its route, and it has not changed.

stages.name: Geodite
stages.bio: Geodite is a small black-shelled turtle covered in raised golden studs that serve as electrical contact points. It moves with quiet confidence through the Steel Fortress, drawn to active machinery by the faint electric fields it detects through its stud-covered shell. Its dark carapace absorbs no light - at night, only the golden studs are visible, giving it the look of a miniature starscape. It has learned to recharge itself by pressing its shell against the fortress's generator housings, and maintenance crews have found that Geodite-rested generators need less servicing.
stages.note: Each golden stud on Geodite's shell is a separate electrical node - they can fire independently, which means it can release charge from any angle simultaneously.

stages.name: Gedonyx
stages.bio: Gedonyx has grown into a formidable dark-armored tortoise with golden spikes now rising from its shell like lightning rods, and a single prominent horn extending forward from its head. When it senses an approaching storm, every golden spike on its body begins to glow with accumulated charge. The Steel Fortress relies on Gedonyx herds in the outer wall corridors as living surge protectors - during lightning strikes, the creatures absorb excess charge and distribute it safely through their contact with the stone floor. They are fed and housed by the Fortress in return.
stages.note: Gedonyx can absorb up to four consecutive lightning strikes without discharging - on the fifth strike, it releases everything at once in a single directed bolt.

stages.name: Gedomancer
stages.bio: Gedomancer is the Steel Fortress's most ancient resident, a creature so laden with stored electrical charge that arc lightning jumps between its shell spikes continuously in dry weather. Its dark armored body is broad as a siege vehicle, its golden spikes now the size of large spears, and the horn on its head has grown long enough to serve as a deliberate lightning rod when it wishes to draw a bolt down from the sky. On the night of the great storm three centuries ago, a Gedomancer stood at the fortress's highest point and absorbed the entire storm, leaving the fortress untouched.
stages.note: Gedomancer has never once been struck by lightning - it has always been what lightning strikes instead.

stages.name: Peblin
stages.bio: Peblin is a tiny round grey pebble creature with large cheerful eyes and a single blue ice-crystal spike growing from the top of its head like a frozen horn. It bounces rather than walks, each hop leaving a tiny frost ring on the stone surface it lands on. Peblin lives on the exposed rock faces of Frozen Peaks where the wind is strongest and temperatures drop below freezing before midnight. It seems to enjoy the cold entirely too much - turning its tiny crystal spike to face into the wind and holding still with what can only be described as bliss.
stages.note: Peblin's crystal spike grows three millimeters for every degree below freezing - at the spire's peak, researchers have recorded spikes forty centimeters long.

stages.name: Geolith
stages.bio: Geolith has transformed entirely - from a round hopping pebble into an upright bipedal warrior with broad stone-plated fists, a chest covered in jagged ice-crystal armor, and a crown of large blue ice spikes jutting from its head and shoulders. It is not graceful, but it is nearly indestructible. Geolith patrols the mid-level ledges of Frozen Peaks, where lightning strikes the stone often enough to melt and refreeze the ice crystals on its body in constant renewal. It braces against the wind with its wide flat feet and never loses its footing.
stages.note: Geolith has been struck by lightning forty-six times in observed history - each strike appears to fuse more crystal onto its body rather than damaging it.

stages.name: Crystallax
stages.bio: Crystallax has transcended its rocky origins - its body is now encased in gleaming golden-bronze armor with a massive crown of enormous blue ice-crystal spires radiating from its shoulders and head like a frozen sun. Each ice crystal in the crown is a different shade of blue, from pale powder to deep glacial, and they catch lightning and scatter it harmlessly into the storm clouds. At the Frozen Peaks' absolute peak, Crystallax stands facing the wind without flinching, arms spread, during the most violent storms - explorers have watched it for hours from the shelter of the lower rocks below.
stages.note: When Crystallax extends its arms fully during a storm, the lightning always strikes the highest crystal spike and travels down through its body into the bedrock below, never entering the spire itself.

stages.name: Geomite
stages.bio: Geomite is a small green turtle with wide curious eyes and a triangular-faceted shell made of purple and blue crystal rather than conventional bone. The crystal shell catches the dappled light of Light Grove and casts tiny prismatic rainbows on the moss below as it walks. When it withdraws into its shell, it can feel vibrations from far-off footsteps through the crystal's resonance, giving it an early warning system much larger creatures envy. The grove's guardian spirits reportedly taught Geomite to arrange small crystal shards in patterns that mark safe paths through the thickest undergrowth.
stages.note: The crystal shell's internal facets form an ancient sigil that no living person has fully unravelled - only Geomite knows what it means.

stages.name: Geoshell
stages.bio: Geoshell has grown considerably, and its purple crystal shell has expanded and sprouted sharp angular spikes that jut outward from each facet. Its green-scaled neck and head are broader now, and it carries itself with unhurried authority through Light Grove's ancient groves. The crystal shell resonates at psychic frequencies that calm agitated creatures within a thirty-meter radius - birds that would normally not land near predators settle on the forest floor near a resting Geoshell. Explorers claim that sleeping near one reliably produces the most vivid and educational dreams they have ever had.
stages.note: Every spike on Geoshell's crystal shell is aligned toward a different star - on clear nights its shell functions as an astronomical navigation tool.

stages.name: Geotyrant
stages.bio: Geotyrant is immense and ancient beyond guessing - a paired double-bodied giant whose two crystal-laden tortoise forms move in perfect synchrony, connected by a shared crystalline ridge that has fused the two shells into a single vast structure. When it moves, the sound of crystal plates grinding against each other is the sound the Light Grove uses to mark the deep hours of the night. The psychic resonance of its double shell is so powerful that it can project full visual memories into the minds of every creature in the grove simultaneously - the guardians called these broadcasts the "All-Lessons."
stages.note: Geotyrant's double body has two heartbeats that alternate - never synchronize, never diverge - a rhythm that Light Grove healers use to calibrate their own pulse when they lose count.

stages.name: Gemling
stages.bio: Gemling is a small round badger kit with soft dark-brown fur and wide eyes that glow faintly pink when it is curious - which is nearly always. A tiny spark of rose-pink psychic light orbits its head when it is thinking hard, appearing and disappearing at random.
