Despite being a creature of the Crystal Mines, Gemling is remarkably social, pressing its whiskered snout against every surface it encounters and sending out gentle psychic pulses that amount to a friendly greeting. Miners have adopted them as unofficial companions, since Gemling always taps twice on a wall before it is going to crack.
stages.note: Gemling taps twice on a mine wall exactly eight seconds before it fractures - miners have relied on this early warning for generations without understanding how it works.

stages.name: Geomaw
stages.bio: Geomaw has grown powerful and compact, with dense rounded shoulders and two long curved tusks that it uses to pry open crystal seams. Its back bristles with erupting pink-magenta crystal spikes that cast rose-colored light through the mine tunnels. Its psychic sensitivity has sharpened to the point that it can taste the composition of a crystal formation by pressing its nose against it. Geomaw marks the richest gem clusters in the Crystal Mines by scratching patterns around them with its tusks - gem prospectors follow these markings to make their biggest finds.
stages.note: No Geomaw marking has ever been found at an empty vein - the strike rate for miners following Geomaw scratch patterns is recorded at one hundred percent.

stages.name: Crystalloth
stages.bio: Crystalloth is a formidable creature to meet in the deep mines - a large powerful badger with enormous tusks, a body armored in dense overlapping pink and magenta crystal formations, and a crown of massive crystal spires radiating from its neck and shoulders. Its psychic field is so powerful that it broadcasts strong impressions to every creature in the mine without effort - trainers call approaching Crystalloth "walking into a thought." The Crystal Mines' oldest gem seams are all located within a kilometer of a Crystalloth sleeping site, as if the creature's presence draws them near over time.
stages.note: Crystalloth is the only creature recorded to have successfully moved a sealed mine wall by applying sustained psychic pressure - it took forty minutes of motionless concentration.

stages.name: Crystelle
stages.bio: Crystelle spends its early life as a closed oyster shell resting at the bottom of Poison Marsh's quieter pools, its two grey-white shells sealed tight around a glowing blue crystal gem it has been growing since before it was born. A ring of faint blue light seeps from the shell's seam when the gem inside pulses. It is perfectly still for days at a time, filtering toxins from the marsh water through its steel-hard shells and locking them away inside its crystalline core. Marsh ecologists believe Crystelle seedlings are responsible for the marsh's clean-water pockets appearing exactly where they are most needed.
stages.note: The blue gem growing inside each Crystelle contains no toxins despite filtering marsh water constantly - it converts them entirely into crystal mass.

stages.name: Shellume
stages.bio: Shellume has cracked open and emerged as a multi-legged crustacean with a pale armored body, six jointed legs tipped with steel-hard points, and a rough domed shell that has absorbed enough metal from the marsh minerals to ring like a bell when struck. A single large blue eye sits above its wide mouth. It walks upside-down on the ceiling of underwater rock formations for days, filtering the water overhead and occasionally dropping crystals that accumulate into formations on the marsh floor below. Researchers mapping the marsh use Shellume crystal deposits as waypoints.
stages.note: Shellume's blue eye can see through murky water as clearly as clean air - marsh explorers claim following one through a fog bank leads to the shortest route every single time.

stages.name: Geomaxon
stages.bio: Geomaxon is massive and ancient, a hulking armored crab-golem whose body segments are thick steel-hard shell plates worn smooth by centuries in the marsh. A single enormous eye glows deep blue from its broad face, and its wide body is ringed with gold-hued detail lines like welded seams on a forged vessel. Its eight legs are powerful enough to walk on the marsh floor during high water, displacing everything nearby with its slow movement. Geomaxon anchors the Poison Marsh's deepest channels - its body is old enough that the entire marsh has reshaped around where it chooses to rest.
stages.note: The gold ring markings on Geomaxon's shell are the only part that is not natural - they were etched by an unknown hand in an age before recorded history, and they have never faded.

stages.name: Shellail
stages.bio: Shellail is the smallest creature of the Poison Marsh - a tiny pale blue snail with a perfectly round smooth shell and a soft round body that retracts instantly at the faintest vibration. It leaves a trail of faintly chilled water behind it as it glides through the shallows, and wherever that trail passes, the marsh water clears and the algae thins. Despite being tiny enough to sit on a large leaf without bending it, Shellail is found in some of the marsh's most dangerous spots, seemingly unbothered by the toxins around it. Marsh children collect empty Shellail shells as good-luck tokens.
stages.note: Shellail's trail clears an exact thirty-centimeter-wide stripe of algae - so uniform that marsh children use Shellail paths to navigate to the safe swimming spots.

stages.name: Frostshell
stages.bio: Frostshell has grown noticeably larger with a more elaborate shell - its smooth spiral now bears a beautiful snowflake pattern in pale blue and white that shimmers when it moves. Its body has taken on a deeper blue, and the trail it leaves is actually cold enough now to feel on bare skin. When threatened, Frostshell withdraws entirely into its shell and releases a ring of freezing water vapor that crystallizes on nearby surfaces in seconds, creating a small frost barrier. Marsh travelers have learned to spot Frostshell's distinctive snowflake-patterned shells from a distance and adjust their routes to use the cleared water it leaves.
stages.note: Frostshell always travels in a perfect spiral - start at any point in its trail and follow it inward and you will find where it spent the night.

stages.name: Crystail
stages.bio: Crystail is a magnificent sight in the grey-green marsh - a large snail with a crystallized spiral shell whose surface has frozen into angular facets, topped by a small crown of ice crystals that has grown from the shell's apex like a tiny glacier. Its body is a rich deep blue, and it moves with slow majestic purpose, never hurrying, never flinching. The marsh's clear-water channels all connect back to paths that Crystail has traveled repeatedly over centuries. It is believed that the Poison Marsh does not poison its own water simply because Crystail has been filtering it since before the marsh was named.
stages.note: The ice crystal crown on Crystail's shell has been photographed from above and below - from directly above, it forms the oldest known sigil, though scholars disagree on what it means.

stages.name: Frostcalf
stages.bio: A small, round-bodied calf coated in pale blue-white fur, Frostcalf has a single short ice-blue horn jutting from its forehead and soft swirl markings across its flank. Its stubby legs barely keep its belly off the ground. Found near the frozen edges of the Poison Marsh where cold mist pools at dawn, it licks mineral-rich ice patches and leaves tiny hoof-prints that never fully melt. The guardians once carved its image into the first frost-stones as a symbol of endurance.
stages.note: Frostcalf's single horn glows faint blue just before temperature drops sharply in the marsh.

stages.name: Tundhorn
stages.bio: Tundhorn stands upright on four sturdy legs, its broad body covered in shaggy pale-blue fur. Two curved horns of solid ice now crown its head, and its wide nostrils breathe out plumes of frozen mist. The swirl markings have darkened into icy ridges along its back. It patrols the outer marshlands, pressing its horns into the boggy soil to freeze narrow paths for smaller creatures to cross safely. Trainers say it always knows where firm ground lies even in the darkest fog.
stages.note: One headbutt from Tundhorn freezes a full metre of bogwater solid in under two seconds.

stages.name: Boralord
stages.bio: Massive and glacier-slow, Boralord is encased from shoulder to hoof in jagged blue ice armour that has grown over its body through years in the cold marsh. Its sweeping curved horns have thickened into enormous blue-white slabs wreathed in perpetual frost vapour, and its eyes glow like frozen amber beneath a heavy ice-brow. When it charges, the ground underneath crystallises in its wake, leaving a glassy trail that lasts for days. Ancient marsh-dwellers call it the Cold Warden - saying it freezes the most toxic bog-pools each winter so they cannot spread.
stages.note: The ice armour on a Boralord's back has been accumulating for decades; no two patterns are ever the same.

stages.name: Glacen
stages.bio: Glacen is a chubby segmented larva made of translucent pale-blue ice-like rings, each segment glowing faintly from within. Two tiny antennae wobble on its head and its wide round eyes give it an endlessly curious expression. It rolls rather than crawls along the tidal rocks of Frozen Peaks, collecting minerals from the spray. At night the glow between its segments pulses in a slow rhythm, and local fishers use it as a lantern to find their moorings in the dark bay.
stages.note: Press a Glacen gently and all its segments chime together with a faint crystalline tinkle.

stages.name: Crystend
stages.bio: In its middle stage Crystend appears as a large faceted blue-and-white crystal - diamond-shaped, floating just above the frost-packed ground in a subtle shimmer. It has shed the larval body entirely and retreated into a pure crystalline form, its internal light refracting through every facet into tiny rainbows across the snow. Creatures approach the glittering stone expecting treasure, but it pulses warmth when touched, startling them away. The guardians of Frozen Peaks believe it is holding something inside the light, waiting for someone patient enough to sit with it.
stages.note: Each facet of Crystend reflects a different colour, and studying which one shines tells attentive trainers the time of day.

stages.name: Prismafly
stages.bio: Prismafly emerges from the crystal with vast iridescent wings - pale lavender and sky-blue - that scatter light into full prismatic fans when they beat. Its small compact body is vivid blue-purple, crowned with two curling antennae, and it floats above the ice shelf in slow graceful arcs. Every wingbeat sends a visible ripple of coloured light washing across the ice. The creatures of Frozen Peaks gather beneath it during the noon sun, basking in its rainbow canopy, and it has never once landed since its first flight.
stages.note: Prismafly's wings beat exactly 4,200 times per minute - researchers verify this is also the frequency of the glacier's daily creep.

stages.name: Frostkitten
stages.bio: Frostkitten is a plump little snow leopard cub with spotted white-and-grey fur, enormous blue eyes, and oversized paws it keeps tripping over. It tumbles through the lower snowfields of Frozen Peaks chasing wind-blown ice crystals as if they were prey. Its spotted coat is too thick for the tumbles it takes, and it bounces right back each time. The guardians say it was the first creature to reach the summit of the Peaks as a bet, and it still holds the record, though no one quite remembers how.
stages.note: Frostkitten sneezes when it senses an incoming storm - never wrong, always inconvenient.

stages.name: Glacepard
stages.bio: Glacepard has grown into a lean, long-bodied snow leopard with pale grey-white spotted fur, glacier-blue eyes, and a thick ringed tail it uses for balance on the icy crags. It moves with effortless silence across ice-slicked rock, leaving no visible prints. Its favourite technique is to lie perfectly still on a white snowfield for so long that ice crystals form along its spine, turning it invisible. Then it pounces on nothing, simply because it enjoys the confusion of nearby creatures.
stages.note: A Glacepard motionless on snow for more than ten minutes begins to grow a fine coat of ice crystals, becoming almost invisible.

stages.name: Crystalion
stages.bio: Crystalion blazes with cold blue-white fire that erupts from its mane and back, framing its powerful snow-leopard body in icy flame. Its coat is brilliant white-blue with faint dark rosettes, its eyes burn arctic-pale, and crystal spines ridge its shoulders and spine. When it roars at the summit of Frozen Peaks the cold blue flames around it flare outward and every storm within a league changes direction. Ancient carvings in the Peaks show Crystalion as the creature that froze Abalont's shadow mid-step and gave the first Guardian time to get clear.
stages.note: Every stone Crystalion treads on develops a delicate ice-crystal flower that lasts exactly one year.

stages.name: Frostpup
stages.bio: Frostpup is a round, fluffy white yeti child with huge blue eyes and a goofy open smile, standing on stubby legs with oversized hands dangling at its sides. Its entire body is a cloud of white fur and it waddles more than walks, often sitting down mid-stride to look at something interesting in the coral sand. Found playing in the tidal pools of Coral Bay, it builds tiny sand-and-ice sculptures and knocks them over with cheerful enthusiasm. The bay's shellfish have learned to hide when they see it coming.
stages.note: Frostpup always builds the same tower - three ice-pebbles, one shell on top - then destroys it immediately, apparently satisfied.

stages.name: Glaciape
stages.bio: Glaciape has grown tall and powerfully muscled beneath its thick white-grey fur, with a broad scowling brow and knuckles that drag along the ground as it walks on all fours. Its blue eyes still hold a keen intelligence. It grips boulders at Coral Bay cliffs with startling ease, tossing stones into the sea to watch the splash - and measuring the distance with great seriousness. Trainers report it will refuse to battle until it has found a rock it considers fair to throw first.
stages.note: Glaciape counts stone-skips on the bay surface and sulks visibly if it scores fewer than five bounces.

stages.name: Crystalbeast
stages.bio: Crystalbeast is enormous - a hulking white yeti whose arms and shoulders have erupted with jagged blue ice-crystal formations, cracking through the fur like armour grown from within. Its fists spark blue when it clenches them, and its eyes burn with fierce cold light. When it pounds the coral-stone floor the vibration is felt half a league out to sea and the tide temporarily reverses. The ocean creatures of Coral Bay swim to shore when they hear it approaching, not out of fear but to watch it break ice formations on the cliff-face for the joy of the sound.
stages.note: The crystal spikes on Crystalbeast's arms regrow overnight - scholars have counted 27 new formations in a single night.

stages.name: Frostling
stages.bio: Frostling is a delicate small deer with a cream-and-tan coat traced with glowing blue swirl patterns, and a single slender ice-blue horn rising from its forehead. Its four thin legs end in tiny hooves that leave frost patterns on soft earth. It browses the lower paths of Frozen Peaks at dusk, and wherever it passes the wildflowers close gently as if bowing. It seems to absorb the snowfield's ambient psychic energy through its horn and radiate it back as cool calm light - young children fall effortlessly asleep within three paces of a resting Frostling.
stages.note: A Frostling's swirl markings shift slowly when it is thinking deeply, tracing new patterns never seen twice.

stages.name: Glacstag
stages.bio: Glacstag has become a tall, elegant stag with an impressive rack of branching ice-blue antlers that shimmer with psychic light. Its long flowing tail of icy vapour drifts behind it as it moves through Frozen Peaks. The swirl markings across its flanks pulse in response to emotion - calm when the snowfield is safe, rapid when it senses Abalont's darkness nearby. It communicates with the snowfield's oldest trees by pressing its antlers to their bark, and they seem to respond, slowly turning their branches toward it.
stages.note: Glacstag's antlers collect dew each morning and freeze it into tiny intricate sculptures by midday.

stages.name: Wyvernox
stages.bio: Wyvernox is a magnificent, blazing creature - a huge ice stag surrounded by cascading cold psychic fire that pours from its massive crystalline antlers and ripples down its spine. Its entire body glows ice-blue and the psychic energy it radiates reshapes the air around it into slowly turning geometric patterns. When it walks through Frozen Peaks the trees part ahead of it of their own accord and close behind like a door. The guardians named it the Dreamer-Stag, believing its presence keeps the waking world from blurring into Abalont's nightmare realm.
stages.note: Standing beneath Wyvernox's antlers for one minute lets a traveller recall something they had long stopped thinking about.

stages.name: Frosthorn
stages.bio: Frosthorn is a compact, stocky little goat with pale blue-grey fur and a cluster of small ice-crystal spines erupting from its back like a frozen mohawk. Its two stubby horns are already hard as granite. It stands on the lowest granite ledges of Granite Heights, head-butting pebbles off the edge and watching them fall with intense fascination. The high-altitude air suits it perfectly - it never slips, never tumbles, and cannot understand why any creature would stand on flat ground when a cliff-edge is available.
stages.note: A Frosthorn can balance on a surface no wider than one centimetre, even asleep.

stages.name: Cryohorn
stages.bio: Cryohorn is a heavily armoured mid-size beast, its entire back and flanks plated with broad overlapping ice-and-rock shields that have fused into solid armour. Its three horns - one central, two flanking - are dense with frozen mineral deposits, making each headbutt land with the force of a falling boulder. It traverses sheer cliff-faces in the upper Granite Heights, carving new paths by simply walking through rock too stubborn to move aside. The guardians use Cryohorn trails as the safest mountain routes - nothing collapses under a path a Cryohorn has approved.
stages.note: Cryohorn's armour plates ring like a struck bell when the temperature drops below freezing - a reliable weather signal.

stages.name: Absolyte
stages.bio: Absolyte is mountainous - an enormous ice-and-rock goat with a body encased entirely in interlocked slabs of glacier-blue stone, and a ridge of jagged frozen peaks rising from its spine like a mountain range in miniature. Its great curling horns are each as long as a grown guardian's arm. When Absolyte digs its hooves into Granite Heights and lowers its head, even the mountain hesitates. Ancient carvers never bothered to depict it moving - they only ever showed it standing still, and said that was enough.
stages.note: The stone beneath each of Absolyte's four hooves has been compressed five centimetres deeper than the surrounding rock.

stages.name: Glaclet
stages.bio: Glaclet is an adorable plump blue narwhal calf with wide friendly eyes and a short spiral horn on its forehead, its belly patterned with soft swirl markings. It floats through the murky surface channels of the Poison Marsh, tapping its horn against submerged branches to test them. The light tapping makes a sound that carries through the water and attracts other Glaclet, so they travel in cheerful bumbling groups. Their presence keeps the marsh water slightly cleaner than it should be - their horns somehow neutralise small amounts of toxin on contact.
stages.note: Glaclet always taps three times before swimming through any new gap - once for depth, once for width, once for luck.

stages.name: Glachorn
stages.bio: Glachorn has grown into a sleek blue narwhal with elongated spiral horn and blue dorsal spines that break the marsh surface like ice-chips. Its body is patterned with pale blue scale-diamonds and it moves with speed and precision through channels too narrow for larger creatures. It uses its horn to break frozen marsh-crust and open feeding pools, then stands guard while smaller creatures drink. Trainers report it can navigate the entire the Poison Marsh blindfolded - it maps channels through vibration.
stages.note: Glachorn's spiralled horn picks up marsh-channel vibrations from over 200 metres away, letting it map its route before swimming it.

stages.name: Frostnarwhal
stages.bio: Frostnarwhal is vast - a deep-blue whale-bodied creature with an enormous spiralling lance of translucent ice extending from its snout, surrounded by crashing frost and wave-spray. Its back bears a crest of ice-crystal formations and its flukes churn the marsh into a river wherever it surges. Ancient marsh legends say it once impaled Abalont's largest shadow-tendril with a single charge, pinning it to the channel floor, and that the ice it left behind still has not melted under the marsh mud.
stages.note: The ice lance on a Frostnarwhal grows one centimetre per decade and has never broken in recorded history.

stages.name: Floecalf
stages.bio: Floecalf is a round, smooth-furred seal pup the colour of pale sky-blue with large dark eyes and swirl markings across its plump belly. It flops cheerfully through the shallower parts of the Poison Marsh, immune to the foul water, slapping the surface with its flippers to make the biggest splash possible. It has no concept of stealth and announces its arrival everywhere. Young guardians who found it near the old canal-banks named it 'Floecalf' for the cold trail it leaves in the water - a brief icy sheen that melts in minutes.
stages.note: A Floecalf's belly-flop splash clears toxin from a one-metre radius of marsh water temporarily.

stages.name: Floetusk
stages.bio: Floetusk has grown enormous - a massive blue-grey walrus with a craggy, wide-muzzled face and two broad white tusks jutting from its lower jaw. Its back has developed rough ice-ridged texture and it moves with surprising speed through deep channels. It uses its tusks to pry open frozen marsh ledges, excavating shelters for smaller creatures caught out in winter freezes. The guardian records show Floetusk once blocked a poisoned runoff channel with its own body for three days until the marsh-folk could redirect the flow.
stages.note: Floetusk's tusks regrow at a rate of one millimetre per week and can never be fully worn down.

stages.name: Crystalord
stages.bio: Crystalord is extraordinary - a colossal sea beast armoured in overlapping crystal-blue ice plates that cover its entire body, two enormous curved tusks of pure glacial ice flanking a vast ridged muzzle. Its small fierce eyes glow ice-blue and its tail sweeps channels clean with each motion. Four stubby armoured legs carry it across the most toxic sections of the Poison Marsh without harm - the crystals on its body seem to absorb and neutralise the marsh's worst poisons. The marsh-wardens call it the Purifier, and say the cleanest water in the region always flows beneath where it rested last.
stages.note: Crystalord sheds one outer ice-plate per year; those plates become the purest ice-crystals found in the marsh, safe to drink.

stages.name: Glacisp
stages.bio: Glacisp is a tiny floating blue teardrop spirit - a round translucent body with a pointed tail that flickers like a candle flame and two wide pale eyes that seem to look in slightly different directions at once. It drifts through the fog-banks of Ghost Hollow barely disturbing the air, leaving a faint trail of cold mist. No one is certain whether it is the spirit of something that was once alive or a piece of the Hollow itself that learned to move. It collects cold air in its body and releases it as brief freezing puffs when startled.
stages.note: Glacisp is always slightly colder than the surrounding air - by exactly 3 degrees, always exactly 3.

stages.name: Glacivor
stages.bio: Glacivor has expanded into a ragged, billowing form - a mass of jagged icy-blue ghost-tendrils radiating from a glowing central core with pale hollow eyes. It moves through solid objects in Ghost Hollow, and the temperature drops sharply wherever it passes. It has no fixed shape for more than a moment, constantly reshaping its frozen vapour tendrils. The hollow's older spirits give it a wide berth, and even Abalont's shadows hesitate at the edges of the freezing aura it projects - cold cuts shadow more cleanly than light.
stages.note: Temperature drops by 6 degrees within one metre of Glacivor - researchers use it as a portable thermometer.

stages.name: Glaciathor
stages.bio: Glaciathor is an immense and terrible frozen phantom - a vast billowing form of jagged ice and ghost-fire filling most of the upper Ghost Hollow, its face a massive pale-glowing snarl of fangs and hollow eyes. Tendrils of frozen energy pour from it in every direction and the hollow's temperatures plunge below anything natural when it fully manifests. Ancient guardian texts describe it as the ghost of the glacier that once covered all the lands before Abalont's first shadow-summer - a memory of cold so deep it refused to end.
stages.note: Glaciathor's oldest ice-tendrils contain air bubbles from before the first words were ever written.

stages.name: Chillpeep
stages.bio: Chillpeep is an impossibly round grey-and-white penguin chick with a tiny beak, one bright blue eye showing, and a belly it rests on more than its feet. It rolled off a ledge on its first day and discovered it preferred rolling to walking, which has not changed. Found on the lower Frozen Peaks ice-shelves, it spends most of its day sliding down the same icy slope and waddling back up, apparently convinced that this is the most important work a creature can do. The guardians of the Peaks keep a count of its runs - the current record is 347 in a day.
stages.note: Chillpeep leaves a different-shaped tummy-slide print each run; no two recorded impressions have ever matched.

stages.name: Frostpenguin
stages.bio: Frostpenguin is a dignified, upright emperor penguin with a sleek black-and-white body and a bold yellow throat-patch. It stands at the edge of the high Frozen Peaks ledges watching the cloud-sea below with calm authority. It no longer rolls. It disapproves of rolling. When the storm-winds begin to build, it is the first to know and it calls out a single measured honk that carries across the entire Peaks - other creatures freeze, then run for shelter, then the storm arrives. It has never been early and it has never been late.
stages.note: Frostpenguin's single storm-warning call is the most reliable weather forecast in the entire region - never off by more than ninety seconds.

stages.name: Glacemperor
stages.bio: Glacemperor is an armoured warrior penguin - a tall, powerful bird with great ice-blue wing-blades fanning out like frozen armour panels, and a striking face marked with bold blue-and-gold patterning above its sharp beak. The ice-wings do not help it fly; instead they catch wind to help it surf storm-fronts at extraordinary speed. When a true gale sweeps Frozen Peaks, Glacemperor runs directly into it, beak-first, and rides the storm's edge clean around the mountain in a matter of minutes. The guardians call it the Gale Marshal.
stages.note: A Glacemperor riding a storm-front has been clocked at 115 km/h - faster than the wind driving it.

stages.name: Glacidot
stages.bio: Glacidot is a fat, cheerful ice-blue caterpillar with segmented translucent rings, a cute wide-eyed face, and a single small ice-spike on its head. It inches through the Dark Forest undergrowth, leaving a faint frost-trail on the bark wherever it grips. It feeds on frozen dew that collects on the underside of leaves in the coldest parts of the forest. Despite being completely defenceless, it has never been eaten - the cold it radiates makes everything within reach of its body just slightly too uncomfortable to approach.
stages.note: Glacidot moves exactly 12 body-lengths per hour; you can set a clock by it.

stages.name: Frostspike
stages.bio: In its next form this creature becomes a six-limbed ice-blue arachnid with sharp crystal spines on its back and elongated forelegs ending in hooked claws. It scuttles through the upper canopy of the Dark Forest at surprising speed, stringing webs of ice-silk between the tallest trees. The webs catch and freeze anything that blunders into them, and the creature inspects each catch with clinical precision, releasing anything too small to bother with. It has developed the habit of working patterns into its ice-silk - the guardians believe these patterns hold old songs of the forest.
stages.note: The ice-silk patterns woven by this creature's webs exactly match marks from an extinct guardian sigil-craft found in forest ruins.

stages.name: Cryolith
stages.bio: Cryolith is a fearsome upright insectoid with long crystal blade-forelegs, a sharp ice-armoured thorax, and glowing eyes beneath an angular crystal helm. Every movement is precise and economical - it never makes an unnecessary motion. The Dark Forest floor around its territory is carpeted with ice-crystal fragments shed from its blades, and walking there sounds like walking on broken glass. When it spreads its blades in warning, the ambient temperature drops five degrees and every creature in the area goes perfectly still.
stages.note: Cryolith sheds one blade-crystal daily; each one is unique and local creatures collect them as talismans.

stages.name: Glacidling
stages.bio: Glacidling is a tiny, round ice-blue spider with a plump body covered in pale blue spots, six thin legs, and enormous wide eyes that make it look permanently astonished. It hangs from a single silk thread in the Bug Thicket undergrowth, swaying in any breeze. When it spots something interesting it drops, spins a tiny web, then immediately forgets what it was spinning it for and wanders away. The thicket is full of its tiny abandoned webs, each perfectly symmetrical, each leading to nothing.
stages.note: Glacidling's abandoned webs are perfectly geometric every time - somehow always a hexagon with exactly twelve radial threads.

stages.name: Glacidian
stages.bio: Glacidian has grown into a proper hunting spider - lean body carried high on sharp jointed legs, its back and head now growing crystal ice-formations that spike upward. It weaves webs in the deeper the Bug Thicket that are genuinely impressive in size and strength, the silk reinforced with ice that hardens on contact with air. It waits at the centre with total patience, feeling the vibrations in every thread. The thicket hunters say it can distinguish between a struggling beetle and a falling leaf from thirty metres of web away.
stages.note: Glacidian's ice-reinforced web strands are stronger than copper wire of the same thickness.

stages.name: Crystalanth
stages.bio: Crystalanth is a commanding ice-crystal spider with a large faceted body bristling with spear-like crystal growths, long armoured legs, and cold glowing eyes. Its web now spans entire clearings in the Bug Thicket, anchored to trees it has partially frozen solid to use as permanent pillars. The web hums in wind and the vibrations carry for hundreds of metres, meaning nothing enters the thicket without Crystalanth knowing. It collects the marks carved into the trees by passing guardians and reproduces them in ice-thread in its web as if preserving a record.
stages.note: Crystalanth's web has been found to contain the full text of a guardian poem - one thread per letter - in a section the scholars lost.

stages.name: Glacicub
stages.bio: Glacicub is a round, grey-furred badger cub sitting upright with a tiny blue gemstone visible on its chest, and chunky forelegs it holds out from its body as if ready to hug something. Its wide dark nose twitches constantly and it has the habit of sitting directly on whatever its trainer is trying to work on. Found near the entrance tunnels of the Steel Fortress, it gets underfoot of every armoured guardian that passes. They have tried to shoo it away many times and it has never once left.
stages.note: Glacicub has sat on 47 separate guardian documents without being asked and ruined exactly none of them - through sheer luck.

stages.name: Glacibear
stages.bio: Glacibear is a muscular, low-slung steel-grey badger with glowing swirl circuit markings across its back that pulse when it senses danger. It no longer sits on things accidentally - it does it deliberately, as a territorial signal. Its forelegs are thick and powerful and it has developed the habit of digging through the Steel Fortress walls to create shortcuts, which the garrison has given up trying to seal. The guardians found it useful once and now it tunnels new routes on request, which it does without being asked far too often.
stages.note: Glacibear's circuit markings glow 30 seconds before any mechanical device in the fortress malfunctions - more reliable than any diagnostic tool.

stages.name: Cryorhino
stages.bio: Cryorhino is an imposing upright-standing rhino-badger hybrid in full articulated metal armour, its chest-plate engraved with the old guardian crest and its armoured forearms crossed as if permanently ready to block an attack. Crackling cold-lightning plays across its shoulder-plates when it is angry - which the Steel Fortress garrison has learned means the entire building goes into lockdown in thirty seconds. It does not charge. It does not need to. Every creature in the fortress moves out of Cryorhino's path from memory.
stages.note: The armour on Cryorhino's chest has never been dented in recorded history; three blows from a guardian siege-hammer left no mark.

stages.name: Glacipp
stages.bio: Glacipp is a plump blue-and-white penguin chick with a single spiralling ice horn on its head, large luminous eyes, and a swirl mark on its belly that pulses faintly with psychic light. It cannot fly, swim, or fight - but it can predict where the next warm sunbeam in Frozen Peaks will fall to the minute, and it sits there waiting. The other snowfield creatures follow it to find warmth and it appears completely unaware of this, wandering from sunbeam to sunbeam without looking back.
stages.note: Glacipp stands in a future sunbeam spot an average of 11 minutes before the light actually arrives there.

stages.name: Glacude
stages.bio: Glacude stands tall and crystal-armoured - a sleek penguin with blade-like ice panels growing from its foreflippers and cold blue eyes that glow with focused psychic awareness. The swirl patterns on its chest have become complex geometric lines. It moves through Frozen Peaks like a scholar on a mission, stopping to press its forehead against trees as if reading them. The snowfield's oldest guardians say it is compiling something - a memory they cannot access. The psychic glow it radiates keeps the snowfield's shadows at bay more effectively than torchlight.
stages.note: Glacude's psychic field erases small anxious thoughts from those who stand near it for more than two minutes.

stages.name: Glaciking
stages.bio: The Guardians believe it sees all futures at once, chooses the one in which the fewest are left behind, and walks toward it every single day.
stages.note: Glaciking has stood on the same stone in Frozen Peaks for three hundred years; the stone has not worn down.

stages.name: Glacix
stages.bio: Glacix is a scrappy, pointy-eared ice-grey wolf pup with a wild mane of spiky fur that sticks up in every direction and keen amber eyes. Small ice-crystal studs dot its scruff and flanks. It prowls the upper tunnels of the Crystal Mines, sniffing out new crystal deposits by following temperature changes in the rock. It has the habit of howling at fresh crystals when it finds one, which makes it easy to find but loud to travel with. The mine-guardians have learned to give it space - every crystal it announces is worth excavating.
stages.note: Glacix can detect a new crystal deposit by smell through 15 centimetres of solid rock.

stages.name: Frostmane
stages.bio: Frostmane has grown into a powerful, athletic wolf with a broad chest, thick spiky silver-blue mane studded with crystal formations, and ice-plate armour growing along its spine. A crystal emblem glows on its sternum. It runs the deep shafts of the Crystal Mines in long fluid strides, checking every tunnel it mapped as a pup. When it finds a collapsed passage it pins the location with a howl pattern that the miners have learned to decode precisely - one long, two short means structural failure; three short means crystal bloom.
stages.note: Frostmane's tunnel-warning calls are so specific that mine engineers have written a formal translation guide based on them.

stages.name: Cryofang
stages.bio: Cryofang is an imposing wolf-like titan - massive, dark blue-grey body armoured in interlocking crystal plates that erupt from every joint and shoulder, its enormous mane a cascade of crystal shards that ring softly with each step. Its eyes blaze with cold crystalline fire and its paws leave faint crystal flowers in the rock wherever it walks. The Crystal Mines themselves seem older where Cryofang has been - as if its presence ages the crystals, deepening their colour and clarity. Ancient mine texts call it the Lord of the Vein.
stages.note: Any crystal that Cryofang has rested against grows 30% larger than surrounding crystals over the following year.

stages.name: Chillkit
stages.bio: Chillkit is an impeccably white kitten with pale blue eyes, delicate ice-crystal ears that catch the marsh light, and a fluffy ringed tail it holds perfectly upright at all times. Small crystal-spike tufts jut from its cheeks. Found in the frost-pockets at the edge of the Poison Marsh, it stalks through the least toxic areas with enormous seriousness, pouncing on frost-pebbles. It refuses to get dirty, which in a marsh is a full-time occupation. The marsh-edge creatures find it inexplicably calming - its presence makes the toxic fog thin slightly.
stages.note: Chillkit refuses to step on any surface that is not at least 60% frozen - it will wait indefinitely for the right path.

stages.name: Frostpurr
stages.bio: Frostpurr is a long, lean ice-cat with crystal-blue cold fire blazing from its shoulders and spine, its white fur now marked with ghostly blue patterns. It moves through the Poison Marsh like a cold current in still water - barely visible until it chooses to be. It freezes small patches of toxic water solid as it crosses, creating stepping-stone paths for marsh creatures. Its cold fire burns only shadow and toxin, which makes it uniquely effective in the marsh where both are plentiful.
stages.note: Frostpurr's cold fire leaves a temporary safe path through the marsh that lasts exactly two hours before the frost melts.

stages.name: Frostlion
stages.bio: Frostlion is a blazing white ice-lion with enormous crystal formations erupting from its mane and spine, cold fire burning steadily from every crystal as if it is made of living ice-flame. Its tail ends in a crystal shard and its paws leave frost-rings on the marsh floor. Unlike most creatures that avoid the most poisonous depths of the marsh, Frostlion walks directly through the centre, its cold fire neutralising the toxins in a slow expanding circle around it. The marsh-folk say it is cleaning the poison one step at a time, and has been at it for a hundred years.
stages.note: Each place Frostlion has stood in the marsh grows water-iris flowers within a season - the only plants that grow there.

stages.name: Frostmite
stages.bio: Frostmite is a small, round-bodied ice-blue spider with enormous soft eyes that take up most of its face and six delicate legs it holds close to its round body. It clings to the undersides of the cool-moisture leaves in Verdant Valley, spinning tiny hexagonal webs between the stems. It collects morning dew, freezes it into tiny ice beads, and arranges them along its web in patterns that nobody has found a reason for except that they catch the light beautifully. The valley's flower-foragers follow Frostmite trails to find the best dew-heavy flower patches.
stages.note: Every ice-bead array Frostmite creates is identical - a hexagon of 18 beads arranged in the exact same pattern each time.

stages.name: Cryamid
stages.bio: Cryamid is an athletic, long-legged ice spider with a broad armoured body covered in blue crystal spines and sharp forward-facing eyes. It has abandoned the small hexagonal webs for elaborate geometric trip-wire structures across the valley floor that are nearly invisible when the morning light is right. It waits at the geometric centre - always perfectly centred - and when something blunders into a wire it is there in a fraction of a second. Verdant Valley's insect population has become extremely careful about where they step.
stages.note: Cryamid's trip-wire webs are consistently built at the exact height of the most common prey passing through the area.

stages.name: Cryoweb
stages.bio: This Cryoweb is the crystal matriarch of the frost-spiders - a large, round-bodied spider with heavy crystal plating on its abdomen and head, long powerful legs, and a constant slow turning motion as it surveys its domain. Its web now covers the entire north-facing slope of Verdant Valley, a permanent frozen silk architecture anchored to rock and tree alike. The valley's ice-creepers and frost-flowers grow densest inside its web perimeter, as if the web itself acts as a cold greenhouse. It has been tending this structure for so long that the valley's summer warmth no longer reaches inside it.
stages.note: The temperature inside Cryoweb's web territory is four degrees colder year-round than the surrounding valley - a reliable natural cold-store.

stages.name: Cubfrost
stages.bio: Cubfrost is a perfectly round polar bear cub, cream-white all over with one bright blue eye visible and a permanently open grin showing tiny teeth. It has arrived in the Sand Dunes from somewhere colder and appears delighted by sand, which it rolls in constantly and in great quantities. Its paw-pads cool whatever sand they touch and tiny frost-flowers appear around its footprints. The dune-skink families have adopted it as a neighbourhood curiosity - it does not eat skinks, it sits on them affectionately, which they tolerate with dignity.
stages.note: Cubfrost's paw-prints leave frost-flowers that survive in the shade of dune crests for up to 72 hours despite the heat.

stages.name: Ursalid
stages.bio: Ursalid is a broad, powerful young polar bear with thick cream-white fur that now carries a fine grit of sand embedded in its outer coat, giving it a rougher texture and faint gold-brown shading. Its gait is steady and unhurried across the dunes. When it lies down on a slope it creates a natural cold-shade that other dune creatures seek out in the hottest hours. The dune-runners have noticed that oases near Ursalid territory stay cooler longer into summer - the cold it brings seems to linger in the sand even after it moves on.
stages.note: The sand in a dune-hollow where Ursalid slept retains its coolness for up to five days after it departs.

stages.name: Glacieroth
stages.bio: Glacieroth is enormous and magnificent - a colossal ice-bear whose body has partly transformed into glacial rock-ice, great crystal spurs erupting from its haunches, shoulders, and crown. Its eyes burn cold blue and its breath turns to ice-fog even in the desert heat. It walks the deepest dune-beds with perfect slow confidence, and wherever it walks an ice-ridge forms in the sand behind it that lasts for weeks. The Sand Dunes caravans navigate by these ridges - they call them the Cold Roads and they have never once misled a traveller.
stages.note: The ice-ridges left by Glacieroth align perfectly with the cardinal directions; navigators say they are more accurate than any compass.

stages.name: Glyphid
stages.bio: Glyphid is a pale purple grub with a glossy segmented body, a round face with simple dot-eyes, and a neat purple orb on its head. It inches through the soil of the Dark Forest floor, eating absorbed shadow-matter that has soaked into the roots. As it feeds, very faint symbol-like marks appear briefly on its back and fade - the guardians who study the forest believe these are fragments of old words that Abalont's darkness has corrupted and buried. Glyphid eats them, and where it passes the soil is slightly lighter.
stages.note: The marks that flicker on Glyphid's back are always legible for exactly one second before fading - never the same symbol twice.

stages.name: Glyphax
stages.bio: Glyphax has sealed itself inside a dark rounded cocoon-shell covered in dense living purple-black runes that shift and rewrite themselves continuously. It is not dormant - it is processing. Inside the cocoon it is decoding every corrupted word it absorbed as a grub, working through them one by one. Touch the cocoon at the wrong moment and the rune under your finger shows you a face you have forgotten - sometimes one you never knew. The Dark Forest grows quieter around a Glyphax, as if the shadows are listening.
stages.note: Glyphax cocoons are always warm to the touch regardless of air temperature - and the warmth is highest where the active runes are.

stages.name: Glypheron
stages.bio: Glypheron emerges as a broad dark beetle with a polished obsidian-black shell covered in glowing purple rune-marks that shift across its back in flowing lines - every voice it ever absorbed as a grub now lives on its carapace in legible form. Its stubby legs hold it close to the ground and its two antennae wave slowly, reading the air for more corrupted language. The Dark Forest scholars discovered that standing near a Glypheron and tracing its markings restores faded guardian carvings - the beetle's shell is a living record of lost names.
stages.note: Glypheron's rune-marks include seventeen words that scholars had declared permanently lost after Abalont's first shadow-wave.

stages.name: Golet
stages.bio: Golet is a small, stocky baby gorilla with charcoal-grey fur and large round eyes that give it a solemn expression it has not yet earned. It sits very still in the lower ash-fields of the Lava Crater and watches the magma channels with intense focus, occasionally reaching out to pat a cooling lava-stone and immediately withdrawing its hand in surprise. It does this every few minutes. It never learns, and it never stops trying. The crater's older creatures find this endearing in a way they would never admit.
stages.note: Golet has patted a cooling lava-stone approximately 900 times in observed records; it is surprised every single time.

stages.name: Gorask
stages.bio: Gorask stands upright on powerfully built legs with thick charcoal-black fur and veins of lava-orange glowing beneath its skin at the wrists and throat. It beats its chest in the Lava Crater more for the echo than for dominance - it seems to enjoy the sound. It wades through shallow lava channels with total indifference, trailing small fires in its wake. The crater guardians have noticed it always moves along the same patrol path each evening, clearing falling ash from the safe crossing-points, though no one asked it to.
stages.note: Gorask's chest-beat creates a resonance in the crater walls that causes volcanic gas to vent harmlessly - unintentionally, but reliably.

stages.name: Goliathyx
stages.bio: Goliathyx is an overwhelming creature - a colossal white-furred gorilla titan wreathed in flame from every surface, lava-orange fire pouring from its mane, knuckles, and shoulders as it stands upright. Its eyes are red with fury and its stone-cracked skin glows like the crater floor. When Goliathyx pounds the Lava Crater walls, volcanic tremors ripple across the entire region and the lava lake stirs. Ancient carvers depicted it as the moment before an eruption - not a disaster, but a question the mountain is asking, and Goliathyx is the voice the question travels on.
stages.note: Seismic records from the Lava Crater show that every major eruption in history has been preceded by Goliathyx's chest-beat by exactly forty minutes.

stages.name: Graxlet
stages.bio: Graxlet is a plump purple gecko no bigger than a fist, with wide golden eyes that catch every flicker of light in the dark tunnels. Its smooth violet body has subtle ridges along the back, and its thick tail curls with nervous energy. It clings to cave walls by tiny adhesive toes and licks the air to taste traces of visitors before they know it is there. In the shadow caves, Graxlet is the first sign that deeper, older things are watching.
stages.note: Graxlet tastes the air with a forked tongue flick every three seconds, even while asleep.

stages.name: Graxorm
stages.bio: Graxorm's body has lengthened and muscled up, with a row of sharp bony spines erupting along its backbone from neck to tail-tip. The purple scales have deepened toward violet-black on its sides, and its golden eyes now carry a shrewd gleam. It moves in slow, deliberate strides, pressing its belly low to the cave floor so its spines scrape the ceiling when it squeezes through narrow passages - a sound explorers learn to dread. Its toxic saliva leaves faint glowing smears on stone.
stages.note: The spine-scrape sound Graxorm makes on cave ceilings is said to echo for a full minute in deep chambers.

stages.name: Graxarch
stages.bio: Graxarch stands fully upright on powerful haunches, its spine-ridge now a crown of long gold-tipped horns that catch the faint light of the shadow caves. Its broad chest gleams with deep purple armored scales, and its thick tail sweeps the ground like a war-club. It exhales slow plumes of poisonous mist with each breath, and the cave walls nearest its lair are permanently stained a sickly violet. Guardians say Graxarch has memorized every voice ever raised in its domain and remembers slights for centuries.
stages.note: Graxarch marks its territory by exhaling a slow mist ring - the ring stays intact for hours in still cave air.

stages.name: Seahippo
stages.bio: Seahippo is a tiny sky-blue seahorse with a plump round belly and a pair of soft lavender fins that flutter like flower petals in still water. Its small snout points upward with a hopeful tilt, and its large violet eyes sparkle with reflected light. In the murky poison marsh, Seahippo floats near the surface where sunlight filters through the reed canopy, trailing wisps of clean shimmering water that push the toxic ooze gently aside. Young guardians say it is the marsh's way of offering a kind hello.
stages.note: Seahippo can produce a tiny bubble of clean fresh water by clicking its snout - it does this to greet strangers.

stages.name: Tidecoral
stages.bio: Tidecoral has grown a beautiful ridged crown along its head, curved like branching coral, and its pastel-blue body is now dusted with soft pink and lavender along the fins. Its large pectoral fins have broadened into graceful sweeping fans, and it moves through water with slow, regal sweeps of its tail coil. It radiates a faint warm glow that purifies small patches of poison marsh wherever it rests, and the purified pools attract rare luminous flowers that bloom only by night. It carries itself with quiet dignity.
stages.note: Pools where Tidecoral has rested for three or more nights glow faintly blue for weeks afterward, even in full darkness.

stages.name: Majesttide
stages.bio: Majesttide blazes with rainbow light - its mane of fins now fans out in full spectral color from coral-red through gold to violet, streaming behind it like a living aurora. Its body is broad and powerful, covered in iridescent scales that shift color with every movement, and its crown ridge has become a tall swept crest of luminous bone. Wherever it swims in the poison marsh, a corridor of brilliant clean water opens before it like a parting of curtains. The guardians call it the Tide-That-Remembers, for it never forgets a kind word.
stages.note: Majesttide's fin-rainbow is visible from the edge of the poison marsh on clear nights, like a second moon rising from the water.

stages.name: Hootix
stages.bio: Hootix is a round puffball of soft cream-brown feathers barely larger than two fists together, with enormous amber eyes that dominate its tiny face. Its stubby wings press tight to its sides and its feet are hidden under the fluff, giving it the look of a feathered ball balanced on nothing at all. It lives in the hollow trunks of Verdant Valley, where the breezes are warm and carry the scent of new leaves. When something startles it, it puffs up twice its size and lets out a squeaky hoot before toppling sideways.
stages.note: Hootix cannot fly yet, but it spins in a full circle when excited - trainers call this the Hootix Wobble.

stages.name: Owlatch
stages.bio: Owlatch has grown into a trim, alert owl with warm brown-and-cream plumage, sharp yellow-orange talons, and keen golden eyes that can track a falling leaf in a gale. Its wings have filled out into proper flight feathers, and it beats them with a quiet precision that barely disturbs the canopy above. It patrols the ridgeline paths of Verdant Valley, counting voices on the wind - trainers swear it remembers everyone who ever passed and marks a stranger with a pointed stare. It perches on the same high branch each dawn.
stages.note: Owlatch chooses one branch as its watching-perch and returns to it every single morning, even after a journey of many days.

stages.name: Vigilarch
stages.bio: Vigilarch spreads its broad brown-and-ivory wings wide enough to shadow a garden plot, and when it launches from a high branch the rush of air bends the grass flat below. Its fierce amber eyes have deepened to a burning gold, and the feather tufts above its brow give it the look of a judge who has heard every excuse. It circles Verdant Valley silently on thermals for hours, and those who learn well beneath the open sky feel a warm updraft brush their shoulders - Vigilarch's silent encouragement. The guardians trusted it with their oldest secrets.
stages.note: Vigilarch's silent wingbeats generate a warm updraft felt up to thirty meters below, used by smaller birds as a free ride.

stages.name: Hornhoot
stages.bio: Hornhoot is a compact grey-and-white owlet with a row of tiny plate-like feathers beginning to harden along its breast, giving it the look of a little knight in training. Its round amber eyes peer out with intense curiosity, and its small hooked beak is already sharp enough to scratch steel. In the lower corridors of the steel fortress, Hornhoot perches on girders and watches the gears turn, memorizing the rhythm of every machine. When asked a question it can not yet answer, it ruffles its breast-plates and looks away with wounded dignity.
stages.note: Hornhoot sharpens its beak on steel beams each morning - maintenance crews can tell the time by the ringing sound.

stages.name: Hornowl
stages.bio: Hornowl's chest is now covered in overlapping grey metallic feather-plates that clatter softly when it adjusts its posture, like coins settling in a purse. Its wings carry flight feathers with hardened silver-grey tips, and its golden eyes cut through forge-smoke without blinking. It has appointed itself guardian of the steel fortress's memory-archives, refusing entry to any visitor who can not correctly answer its three riddles. Its head swivels silently - a full turn in either direction - before it delivers its judgment with a slow deliberate blink.
stages.note: Hornowl's metal feather-plates clatter in a unique rhythm for each individual bird - fortress guards use the sound to identify them.

stages.name: Hornsoar
stages.bio: Hornsoar is armored from crown to talon - full articulated steel-gray plate covers its breast, shoulders, and swept-back wing-edges, and its talons are forged to gleaming points that leave grooves in iron floors. Its great wings, when spread wide, ring with a low metallic hum that silences a room. It keeps watch from the highest spire of the steel fortress, scanning the horizon with golden eyes that never tire. Once, during the time of Abalont's assault, it shielded a class of young learners beneath a single wing for three days without moving.
stages.note: Hornsoar's wing-hum, produced when it spreads both wings fully, can be heard from the fortress's outermost wall half a league away.

stages.name: Tidrop
stages.bio: Tidrop is a small sky-blue sea serpent with a rounded head, tiny budding fins on its cheeks, and a short tail that swishes constantly through the air as though it is already swimming. Twin wisps of water-steam curl from its nostrils, leaving tiny droplets wherever it goes. It was found in a thermal pool at the lava crater's edge - the only creature that thrives where boiling water meets molten stone. Trainers say Tidrop's cheerful nature comes from never knowing a cold moment in its life.
stages.note: Tidrop leaves a tiny trail of water-droplets wherever it travels, even in the hottest chambers of the lava crater.

stages.name: Hydrofen
stages.bio: Hydrofen has grown long and sinuous, with a proud crown-like crest of ice-blue spines along its head and a pair of broad webbed wings folded against its sides. Its coiling blue body gleams with frost patterns despite the surrounding heat, and its tail splits into a fan of fin-rays at the tip. It can swim through lava streams by surrounding itself with a shell of pressurized water, emerging on the other side entirely dry. The guardians of the lava crater valued its calm presence - a cold eye in a world of fire.
stages.note: Hydrofen coils around thermal vents at night and absorbs the heat into pressurized water reserves used in battle.

stages.name: Typhdrake
stages.bio: Typhdrake is a massive coiling water dragon with a full crown of sweeping icy-blue horns, enormous bat-like wings edged in silver-blue, and a deep chest armored in overlapping glacial scales. Its body fills the widest corridors of the lava crater, and its passage creates a wall of cold mist that momentarily snuffs the nearest flames. When it speaks, its voice carries the crash of ocean waves against a cliff face. The ancient lore says Typhdrake weeps cold rain whenever a great word is forgotten, and the crater pools refill overnight.
stages.note: Each of Typhdrake's horn-tips holds a frozen drop of ocean water from the day it was born - they never melt.

stages.name: Hyenip
stages.bio: Hyenip is a compact, stocky dark-furred pup with a black coat patterned in glowing amber spiral markings that pulse faintly in the dark. Its large round eyes burn orange, and it carries its thick tail curled up over its haunches. The amber spirals on its flanks seem to spin slowly when it is excited, leaving faint trails in dim light as though writing invisible words on the air. It lurks at the misty edge of ghost hollow, daring visitors with its amber gaze and retreating with a sharp bark-chirr if they step closer.
stages.note: The spiral markings on Hyenip's flanks rotate clockwise when happy and counter-clockwise when suspicious - never the same direction twice.

stages.name: Hyenox
stages.bio: Hyenox stands taller now, its sandy-brown spotted coat rippling with a mane of dark smoky fur along the neck and spine that drifts like smoke in still air. Its deep-set eyes catch every shadow, and it moves at a loping trot that seems to slide between patches of darkness rather than cross them. In ghost hollow it circles quietly, chuckling in low bursts when it finds something amusing - a sound that sets every hair on end. It knows every hiding place in the hollow and will appear behind you before you have finished looking for it.
stages.note: Hyenox always approaches from exactly the direction you are not looking; trainers say it can read eye movement at twenty paces.

stages.name: Hyenastra
stages.bio: Hyenastra is a lean, powerful beast with a dramatic full mane of dark crackling energy that sparks with pale blue-white arcs along its length. Its spotted coat is shadowy grey-brown, and its massive jaws could crush stone. It paces ghost hollow as its undisputed ruler, and the mist-tendrils part around it as it walks. When it laughs - a deep rolling cackle that carries through the trees - every smaller creature goes still. The guardians left it to guard the hollow's deepest silent tombs, knowing no thief would dare meet its burning gaze twice.
stages.note: Hyenastra's mane-sparks intensify to a continuous blaze when it senses a lie - it has never been successfully deceived.

stages.name: Sparkraven
stages.bio: Sparkraven is a small, sooty charcoal-black bird chick with stubby wings it has not yet learned to use and bright orange feet it shuffles forward on with great determination. Its black plumage absorbs heat from the lava crater vents and radiates it back as a faint warmth that singes finger-tips on contact. Its tiny beak is already sharp, and it pecks at embers along the crater rim to test which words glow hottest. Explorers find it bold for its size - it will hop directly onto a boot to investigate.
stages.note: Sparkraven collects small glowing embers in a pile each evening, counting them before sleeping - always the same number.

stages.name: Inferryx
stages.bio: Inferryx has erupted into a black-feathered bird with broad wings whose trailing edges blaze with living orange flame. Burning embers drift behind it wherever it flies, and its wingspan casts a firelit shadow on the crater walls. It screams as it dives, a sound like tearing metal, and the blast of wind from its wings fans the lava below into spinning fire-spouts. It is fiercely territorial over its updraft columns and will challenge anything larger than itself on principle. Young guardians call it the test of courage - whoever stands still when Inferryx stoops gets its grudging respect.
stages.note: The embers that fall from Inferryx's wing-tips stay lit for three full minutes after landing, even in rain.

stages.name: Phoenixolt
stages.bio: Phoenixolt is a magnificent black bird with enormous wings wreathed entirely in billowing flame - orange and gold fire streams from every primary feather as it spreads wide and catches the thermal columns above the crater. A crown of burning plumes rises from its head, and its talons glow red-hot at the tips. When it lands on the crater's peak, the air itself shudders from the heat it carries. It is said that the ashes from its feathers, collected at the winter solstice, can restore a forgotten word to memory. It has never forgotten a single one.
stages.note: Phoenixolt lands on the same crater peak at sunset every day, and the glow of its wings can be seen from every region on the map.

stages.name: Emblazon
stages.bio: Emblazon is a stocky, dark-coated young beast with crimson and black armored plates beginning to form along its flanks and a single plume of fire rising from its back like a candle. Its eyes glow bright amber-orange, and its short blunt horns point stubbornly forward. It stands with feet planted wide, already practicing the defiant posture it will master later in life. In the shadow caves it trots between the pillars of obsidian, drawn to the faint warmth of volcanic vents deep underground. When challenged, it headbutts the nearest wall and ignites a small fire.
stages.note: Emblazon marks its territory by pressing its horns to the cave wall and scorching a ring of soot - you can tell its age by counting the rings.

stages.name: Pyronyx
stages.bio: Pyronyx has become a broad-shouldered, powerful beast with a deep crimson chest and heavy black obsidian armor plates riveted along its back and shoulders. Two thick curved horns jut forward, glowing faintly orange at the tips, and a steady flame burns at the base of its tail. It charges with head lowered and shakes the cave floor with each impact, sending cracks running through the stone. The shadow cave walls are marked with scorch-rings and impact divots wherever Pyronyx has claimed ground. It does not back down - ever.
stages.note: Pyronyx's horns heat to orange-glow temperature during a full-speed charge and leave melted grooves in cave rock on impact.

stages.name: Infernelope
stages.bio: Infernelope is a colossal beast of dark obsidian plating and blazing fire - its entire back carries a ridge of flame-vents that burn continuously, casting shifting red light across the shadow cave walls. Its massive curved horns are coated in glowing molten rock and its legs leave scorch prints in stone with each step. Fire pours from its nostrils with each breath. It is said that Infernelope was the guardian of the shadow caves' deepest memory-vault, and it has never permitted Abalont's forces to reach it. Its bellow alone collapses tunnels half a league away.
stages.note: Infernelope's flame-vents along its back burn hotter when it hears a lie, rising from orange to pure white in a heartbeat.

stages.name: Smolmite
stages.bio: Smolmite is a round orange-and-red caterpillar with plump segmented rings patterned in dark dots, a cheerful rounded face, and tiny stubby leg-nubs it uses to inch along branches with charming determination. A small orange glow pulses at its tail-segment like a warning lantern. It leaves tiny scorch-marks on the leaves it climbs, and the bug thicket guides warn learners not to sit too long on a log Smolmite has recently passed over. It eats fire-seeds it finds among the thicket's charcoal-core roots, growing plumper with each one.
stages.note: Smolmite can eat fire-seeds that would torch a glove - it hums contentedly as the seeds warm its belly from the inside.

stages.name: Chrysalurn
stages.bio: Chrysalurn is a sealed cocoon of deep amber and bronze, its surface etched with flame-patterns that glow orange at the seams, as though fire is being sculpted into shape within. Flames lick upward from the base of the cocoon in a slow, steady ring. It hangs from the thickest branches of the bug thicket, and the heat it radiates keeps other creatures at a respectful distance. Those who listen closely on quiet nights say they can hear a faint rapid heartbeat inside - or perhaps just the soft roar of something building toward a future it has not yet imagined.
stages.note: The temperature of Chrysalurn's outer shell rises by exactly one degree each day of its transformation, peaking the moment it opens.

stages.name: Infernaflare
stages.bio: Infernaflare bursts from its cocoon as a blazing moth-like creature with four broad wings of living fire - orange, gold, and deep red, edged in black - that leave trails of bright sparks with every beat. Its body is dark and armored, and its compound eyes burn white-hot. It circles the bug thicket in spiraling updrafts of its own making, and every wingbeat scatters glowing motes that drift down like tiny stars. The thicket creatures treat its arrival as a signal - when Infernaflare circles at dusk, a new lesson is about to be learned.
stages.note: Infernaflare's wing-sparks cool into tiny glass beads on the ground - children string them into bracelets for courage.

stages.name: Blazekit
stages.bio: Blazekit is a small orange kitten with dark fire-spot markings scattered across its coat and a thin tail that ends in a tiny wobbling flame. Its wide curious eyes are deep amber, and it pads around the lava crater on soft round paws that leave faint scorch marks on the warm stone. When something catches its interest, the tail-flame brightens to yellow and the spots on its coat seem to shift position. It has an unnerving habit of staring just past your shoulder as though reading something written in the air behind you.
stages.note: Blazekit's tail-flame changes color based on what it is thinking about - yellow for questions, orange for play, red for solutions.

stages.name: Blazmane
stages.bio: Blazmane has grown into a sleek, confident feline with a luxurious mane of living fire flowing back from its neck and down its tail in long bright streamers. Its deep orange coat gleams, and when it walks the mane-flames bend and twist as though processing invisible thoughts. Its psychic ability means it knows what question you are about to ask before you open your mouth, and it has often answered by the time you finish asking. In the lava crater it finds the hottest ridge-paths and walks them with its tail high, rehearsing solutions to problems no one has posed yet.
stages.note: Blazmane answers a question before it is finished being asked - trainers have learned to stop halfway and save time.

stages.name: Infurion
stages.bio: Infurion is a powerful lion-sized feline entirely wreathed in fire - its whole body blazes with orange and gold, its mane a roaring crown of flame, and its eyes burn with white psychic light. The ground at its feet smolders with each step, and the air around it shimmers with distorted heat. It speaks through images pressed directly into the mind - entire lessons delivered in the time it takes to blink. The lava crater guardians called it the Flame That Asks, for it always answered a question with another, sharper question, until the learner found the answer themselves.
stages.note: Infurion cannot be surprised - it perceives every intended action three seconds before it happens, measured precisely by its trainers.

stages.name: Flickfawn
stages.bio: Flickfawn is a small sandy-furred foal with a bright mane of orange-gold flames rising from its neck and a single tail-flame that flickers with every breeze across the sand dunes. Its round amber eyes are warm and eager, and its four legs end in neat hooves that send up tiny puffs of hot sand with each step. When a gust crosses the dunes, its mane-flame stretches and gutters sideways and Flickfawn tilts its head to feel the full warmth of it, pausing whatever it was doing. The sand dunes children say Flickfawn is how fire learned to run.
stages.note: Flickfawn's mane-flame stretches in the exact direction of the next wind gust, moments before it arrives - the best weather-sign in the dunes.

stages.name: Emberfur
stages.bio: Emberfur is a powerful dune lion with a full mane of blazing orange-gold flame-fur that rises and streams behind it as it sprints across the sand dunes at frightening speed. Its tawny coat is burnished gold-brown, and three separate flame-tails stream behind it like burning ribbons when it runs full-out. It hunts in the late afternoon when the dune wind picks up, using the thermal updrafts to leap farther than any creature its size should manage. Its footprints in the sand are small scorch-rings - the dune wanderers follow them like a map toward safety.
stages.note: Emberfur's three flame-tails merge into one at top speed - it has never been caught by anyone counting to three.

stages.name: Pyremanx
stages.bio: Pyremanx is a vast, broad-shouldered lion with a mane of roaring flames that rises taller than its head and casts orange light across the sand dunes for a hundred meters. Four powerful flame-tails stream behind it, each thick as a torch, and when it lifts its head and roars, the hot wind it generates bends the dune crests and scatters burning sand in all directions. The sand dunes creatures stop and face it when it passes - not from fear, but recognition, the way a younger student stops when an ancient teacher enters. It never hurries. It has already arrived.
stages.note: Pyremanx's roar generates a localized hot wind that flips the sand dunes into new shapes - cartographers must redraw their maps the morning after.

stages.name: Jellyx
stages.bio: Jellyx is a tiny cream-white jellyfish with a smooth round bell and a handful of short trailing tentacles that drift behind it like ribbon-ends. At its center, a single deep violet eye regards the world with unreadable calm. It floats through the misty clearings of the light grove as though carried by a current no one else can feel, pausing over flowers and pools to gaze at its own reflection. It does not seem to notice distance or obstacles - walls and branches simply do not interrupt its path. Those who see it say it drifts through light the way dreams drift through sleep.
stages.note: Jellyx passes through solid objects with no apparent effort, leaving behind a faint chill and the faintest violet shimmer on the surface.

stages.name: Medusa
stages.bio: Medusa has grown a wider bell fringed with longer flowing tentacles that trail up to half a meter behind it, each ending in a faint glowing tip. Its single eye has deepened to indigo and now watches with deliberate focus rather than blank calm. When it contracts its bell to pulse upward, a quiet sigh fills the air like breath in a cold room. It gravitates toward the light grove's moonlit pools, where its translucent body makes it nearly invisible, and it has been observed settling gently over sleeping creatures as though keeping watch. It never wakes them.
stages.note: Medusa's glowing tentacle-tips pulse in a rhythm exactly matching the breathing of whoever it is hovering nearest to.

stages.name: Abyssyx
stages.bio: Abyssyx has expanded into an enormous pale-purple jellyfish with a bell as wide as a table and long spectral tentacles that trail meters below it, fading into translucency at their ends. Its single vast eye now pulses with deep violet light, and its whole body glows with a cold dim luminescence in the dark corners of the light grove. When it descends over a place of stillness, time seems to slow - seconds stretch like taffy, and the words on a page grow easier to read. The guardians of the light grove called it the Deep Memory, for it holds every promise ever made beneath its shade.
stages.note: A child who studies directly beneath Abyssyx is said to remember the lesson seven times longer than usual - measured in the grove's own trials.

stages.name: Joeylet
stages.bio: Joeylet in its first stage is a short, earnest brown joey standing upright with oversized round boxing gloves of bright orange that it holds in front of its chest at all times. Its big round eyes are warm and determined, and its long flat feet plant firmly whenever it squares up. It bounces in tight circles when nervous and swings its padded gloves at the air to psych itself up before a challenge. In Verdant Valley it hops between the song-trees practicing rhythm by punching patterns into the bark with satisfying thwacks. Every correct answer gets a little victory bounce.
stages.note: Kangaroo's boxing gloves are permanently attached - trainers have searched for years and cannot find a single lace or buckle.

stages.name: Kangarock
stages.bio: In its second stage Joeylet has grown taller and leaner, its sandy-brown coat now sleek along its shoulders and arms. The boxing gloves are gone - it carries its powerful forepaws at ready, balanced on its thick haunches and long tail. It moves in bounding leaps that carry it six meters at a time, and the wind of its passing stirs the tall grass of Verdant Valley into spiraling waves. It loves to race the valley winds along the ridge-paths, and local children track its jump-distance record with notched stakes. Its current best is eleven meters, achieved on a Thursday morning.
stages.note: Kangaroo's jump-record post is a notched branch near the valley's east ridge - there are forty-seven notches and counting.

stages.name: Roostomper
stages.bio: In its final stage Joeylet is massively built - wide across the shoulders, with arms like bundled rope and a scarred, battle-marked chest it carries with quiet pride. Its thick haunches could drive it through a stone wall, and its tail sweeps the ground with deliberate weight. It stands in the valley as its undisputed defender, watching the paths with calm eyes that miss nothing. When it fights for its learners it does not rage - it measures, waits, and delivers one perfectly placed strike that ends the matter. The guardians say its most devastating blow is a whispered word at the right moment.
stages.note: Kangaroo never throws the same punch twice in the same bout - it has catalogued over two hundred distinct combinations, each named after a place it has been.

stages.name: Leafkit
stages.bio: Leafkit is a small, bright-eyed fox kit with a fresh green coat and a ruff of broad flat leaves around its neck like a flower collar. Two larger leaves sprout from the base of its tail and flutter when it trots. Its paws are quick and dexterous, and it uses them to rearrange fallen leaves into patterns on the forest floor - each pattern slightly different, as though practicing a new pattern. In the bug thicket it follows the sunlight patches, making tiny leaf-fans from fallen fronds to catch the warmth. Its collar-leaves smell of sweet sap after rain.
stages.note: Leafkit rearranges fallen leaves into new patterns each morning - no two patterns are ever the same, and it never seems satisfied.

stages.name: Leafoxen
stages.bio: Leafoxen has grown into a slender, alert fox with a full mantle of layered leaves covering its back and shoulders like a living cloak that rustles with every step. Its tail has become a generous fan of overlapping leaves that it raises when excited like a peacock's display. In the bug thicket it moves fluidly, pressing through undergrowth without disturbing a single stem, and it has learned to communicate over distances by vibrating its leaf-cloak in specific patterns - a private morse code between foxes. Children who learn to read it earn a deep respectful nod.
stages.note: Leafoxen's leaf-cloak sends unique rustling signals depending on the message - locals have transcribed seventeen distinct meanings so far.

stages.name: Verdaxos
stages.bio: Verdaxos is a large, magnificent fox whose entire body is now mantled in rich layered foliage - deep green and gold-brown leaves cover its back, flanks, and long tail like a forest elder's robe. Its face bears old, wise markings, and its amber eyes carry the patience of many seasons. It moves through the bug thicket in near-silence, the leaves parting before it and closing behind. Where it rests overnight, new saplings are found in the morning. The guardians named it the Memory-keeper of the Thicket, for it holds in memory every promise spoken under the canopy's shade.
stages.note: Saplings sprout overnight wherever Verdaxos sleeps - the thicket's oldest trees all trace back to one of its ancient resting places.

stages.name: Rootkit
stages.bio: Rootkit is a round, chubby brown badger-like creature with a single broad leaf sprouting from the top of its head like an oversized hat it has not grown into yet. Its stubby legs and round body give it a rolling, tumbling gait, and it digs compulsively wherever it finds soft soil, piling up tiny earthen mounds in neat rows. In the dark forest's leaf-littered floor it spends its mornings nose-deep in the earth, cataloguing seeds by taste and then carefully replanting each one in a slightly different spot. It insists this is an improvement.
stages.note: Rootkit replants every seed it finds in a new location - foresters claim it has single-handedly moved the dark forest south by several meters.

stages.name: Foliahorn
stages.bio: Foliahorn has grown upright and broad, with a thick collar of layered leaves fanning out around its neck and shoulders like a ruff of forest finery. Its strong clawed forepaws are built for digging, and the dark forest floor is riddled with its tunnel-networks below each patrol route. The leaf-collar seems to grow more leaves after a good day's walk, and Foliahorn has been observed collecting fallen leaves pressed flat between old stones - with great care and ceremony. It treats every piece of knowledge as something to be carefully buried for later.
