stages.note: Foliahorn buries knowledge like seeds - it digs up old 'planted' facts weeks later and presents them at exactly the right moment.

stages.name: Verdagarth
stages.bio: Verdagarth is a massive, four-legged creature of rock and leaf - its body is encrusted with mossy stone plates, and a full explosion of thick green foliage erupts from its back and shoulders like a living forest carried on its frame. Its legs are as wide as young tree trunks, and the ground shakes with slow authority as it walks the dark forest paths. It does not rush; it arrives. Creatures of the forest fall quiet when it passes, and the oldest trees bow their branches. It keeps the dark forest's deepest root-libraries - chambers of pressed leaf-songs no living creature besides itself has yet read.
stages.note: Verdagarth knows the locations of all root-libraries in the dark forest and will guide any learner to the right one without being asked.

stages.name: Leafling
stages.bio: Leafling is a tiny, bright-eyed deer fawn with large oval leaves fanning from behind both ears like a little green bonnet. Its light green coat is smooth and soft, and it picks its way through the ghost hollow on delicate hooves that barely stir the mist. It is curious but wary, pausing to sniff each new thing before proceeding. When startled, its leaf-ears fan wide and it freezes perfectly still - an instinct that makes it nearly invisible among the hollow's floor-plants. Children in the hollow say Leafling always knows the safest path, and following it never leads you wrong.
stages.note: Leafling freezes motionless when startled, and its leaf-ears spread wide - from ten paces away it looks exactly like a leafy shrub.

stages.name: Leafyx
stages.bio: Leafyx has grown into a striking forest deer with a full spray of layered leaves fanning behind its neck and down its back like a living mane, and its eyes have deepened from bright to forest-deep green. Its slender legs carry it in long fluid strides through the ghost hollow's trees, and the leaf-mane rustles in patterns as it moves that seem almost like language - older hollow-dwellers claim to understand a few of the phrases. It marks its paths through the hollow with small leaf-circles pressed into the ground, and following them is said to lead anywhere you need to go.
stages.note: Leafyx's leaf-mane rustling patterns have been partially mapped - seventeen distinct meanings are confirmed, and two scholars are still arguing about the eighteenth.

stages.name: Foliarch
stages.bio: Foliarch is a magnificent great stag whose towering antlers have become a living crown of interlocked branches, leaves, and flowering vine - an entire micro-forest carried on its head. Its body is broad-chested and deep-green in tone, dappled with golden leaf-light, and its steps press the ghost hollow mist apart like a ship's prow through water. When it stands still in a clearing and calls, the entire hollow falls silent and listens. The guardians of the hollow say Foliarch has walked these paths since before the first lesson was written down, and will walk them long after the last.
stages.note: The flowering vines in Foliarch's antler-crown bloom in a different color each season, and each color corresponds to a different branch of knowledge.

stages.name: Stonecub
stages.bio: Stonecub is a compact, low-slung bear cub with a very dark charcoal-black coat that blends into the shadow cave walls perfectly in dim light. Its small eyes catch light with an orange glint, and its claws are already short and stubby-hard. It spends its days pressing its belly to the cave floor and shuffling forward in near silence - a gait that seems more rock-slide than walk. It tests every stone it encounters by pressing its nose to it for thirty full seconds before moving on. Trainers say this is how Stonecub decides if a thing is worth remembering.
stages.note: Stonecub's nose-test lasts exactly thirty seconds for every stone - it has never been caught shortening the count.

stages.name: Quarrite
stages.bio: Quarrite has grown massively broad, with jagged rock plates crusting along its spine, shoulders, and haunches like natural armor. Its dark coat shows through between the stone plates in patches, and its claws have lengthened into serious digging tools. It moves through the shadow caves at a determined lumbering pace that shakes loose small stones from the ceiling, and it uses its armored back to clear blocked passages by simply walking into them. It claims the deepest chambers of each cave system and marks the entrance with a ring of stone it has personally bitten out of the wall.
stages.note: Quarrite's entrance-stone ring can be identified by its unique tooth-marks - cave researchers use them to map who owns which chamber.

stages.name: Geolithaun
stages.bio: Geolithaun is a colossal dark bear that has become half-rock - a ridge of sharp stone spines runs the length of its spine and its entire back is a mountain range in miniature, covered in craggy dark basalt. When it rears up in the shadow caves and roars, the reverberations travel for half a kilometer through solid stone and small stones rattle loose from the ceiling above. It does not charge - it simply becomes an immovable fact of the landscape, and the challenge is accepted or it is not. The oldest cave-drawings show Geolithaun standing watch before the shadow caves were first mapped, and the drawings are very old.
stages.note: Geolithaun has not moved from its cave threshold in the three hundred years the cave records cover - researchers argue whether it is sleeping or simply waiting.

stages.name: Glowmole
stages.bio: Glowmole is a small, velvety black mole with a single glowing amber orb balanced on a thin antenna above its head like a living miner's lamp. Its wide pink nose twitches in constant radar-sweeps, and its enormous digging claws look impractically large for its body. It burrows beneath the steel fortress's foundation plates and taps the electrical conduits it finds there, charging the antenna-bulb to a brighter gold when it has a full feed. It navigates by electrical field rather than sight, and has been found inside sealed generator rooms that had no open entry point.
stages.note: Glowmole's antenna-bulb brightness indicates the local electrical charge - engineers have learned to read it as a live current gauge.

stages.name: Aurrow
stages.bio: Aurrow has grown longer and sleeker, with a row of amber-gold electroplates running down its spine that glow and flicker in sequence as it processes electrical charges drawn from the soil. Its digging claws are formidable now, able to split a steel conduit with two strikes, and it uses this ability to reroute power flows in the fortress's substrata - often helpfully, occasionally catastrophically. The fortress engineers have learned to check whether the lights dimmed before concluding there is a fault in the wiring.
stages.note: Aurrow's spine-plates pulse in a specific sequence before it taps a new electrical source - the engineers have decoded fifteen distinct patterns.

stages.name: Radiatusk
stages.bio: Radiatusk is a hulking, broad-shouldered mole with a full array of glowing gold electroplates across its back, a pair of massive armored tusks that crackle with built-up static charge, and a single oversized antenna-orb burning at constant white-gold intensity. Its passage through the earth leaves charged tunnels that glow faintly for hours. The steel fortress was built partly over Radiatusk's ancient tunnel-network, and its old routes still carry charge - fortress engineers call them 'live veins' and map around them. Radiatusk surfaces once each year at the fortress's main gate and places one tusk on the ground, grounding years of accumulated charge in a flash that resets all faulty circuits.
stages.note: Radiatusk's annual grounding flash resets every clock in the steel fortress to midnight - the fortress has kept no other calendar since it was recorded.

stages.name: Glimmorp
stages.bio: Glimmorp is a bulbous, bug-eyed blue fish with a tiny thin antenna sprouting from its forehead that ends in a dim glowing bulb. Its enormous round eyes take up most of its face, and its wide gaping mouth - packed with tiny pointed teeth - always hangs slightly open, as though it has just thought of something alarming. It floats in the murky pools of ghost hollow with surprising stillness, and the lure-bulb pulses at intervals that grow closer together when prey is nearby. It has been caught staring at its own lure's reflection for up to forty minutes.
stages.note: Glimmorp has been timed staring at its own lure-light reflection for forty minutes - it is unclear whether it is confused or proud.

stages.name: Deepmaw
stages.bio: Deepmaw has grown larger and more menacing - its dark blue-purple scales are jagged along the sides, its teeth have extended into proper fangs visible even with its mouth closed, and its lure-antenna now curves forward with a brighter crescent-glow. It prowls the deepest pools of ghost hollow in absolute silence, using the lure not just to attract prey but to read subtle ripples in the water to map the hollow's secrets. Its great oversized eyes give it night-vision that extends beyond sight - it is said to see three days into the past as well as twenty meters into the dark.
stages.note: Deepmaw's eyes reportedly see the most recent three days of activity in any space it enters - no secret has ever lasted in a room it occupies.

stages.name: Abysslure
stages.bio: Abysslure is a massive, terrifying deep-sea beast - its body is broad and armored in overlapping dark plates with spined ridges, its jaws stretch nearly the width of its body and reveal rows of recurved teeth, and its lure-antenna glows at a blue-white intensity that lights the entire pool. It is the ghost hollow's deepest-water guardian, and the pools it inhabits are avoided by everything else. When it opens its jaws fully the pressure wave makes the water surface ripple thirty meters away. The guardians tasked it with holding the hollow's most dangerous forgotten words - the ones that caused harm before they were unlearned.
stages.note: Abysslure's jaw-pressure wave has been measured at the pool surface thirty meters away - it never opens its mouth fully without reason.

stages.name: Glowmite
stages.bio: Glowmite is a small, cheerful blue jellyfish with a round bell and a tight cluster of short tentacles hanging beneath it, drifting through the shadow caves' underground pools with a soft blue glow. A thin antenna curves from its crown, ending in a dim warm bead of light that it can extinguish and relight at will. It is the first light most explorers see when they enter the cave system, and it has learned to associate approaching footsteps with the possibility of hearing a new voice - it brightens noticeably when someone recites something correctly. Local guides use it as an informal test.
stages.note: Glowmite's antenna-light brightens measurably when it hears a correctly spoken word - cave-school teachers use it as a pass/fail indicator.

stages.name: Abyssal
stages.bio: Abyssal has grown a wider bell draped in long flowing tentacles that trail in elegant dark curtains, each tip glowing at intervals like stars in a night sky. Its lantern-antenna has extended and now carries a blue-white lamp bright enough to read by. In the shadow caves it drifts through the wider chambers in absolute silence, and its tentacle-glow-pattern shifts in response to sounds - quick bright pulses for voices, slow waves for music. The cave-scholars have been mapping the patterns for a generation and believe they form a complete underwater map that has never been copied.
stages.note: Abyssal's tentacle-glow pattern shifts uniquely for every spoken word it hears - two scholars have mapped over four hundred patterns so far.

stages.name: Voidlume
stages.bio: Voidlume is a towering, armored entity that has transcended its jellyfish origins - its upper body has become a broad-shouldered dark form with wing-like tentacle fans sweeping wide, and it carries a great lantern-staff of cold blue-white light in one limb while the other bears a sweeping claw-extension. The light it carries throws everything around it into sharp dramatic relief, and the shadow caves restructure their shadows accordingly. It is the oldest entity in the cave system and speaks only in light-patterns now - a language that takes years to learn and cannot be unlearned once known. The guardians call it the Warden of What Was Forgotten.
stages.note: Voidlume's light-language cannot be unlearned once understood - three guardians who mastered it have never spoken in words again.

stages.name: Luminox
stages.bio: A tiny deep-blue jellyfish no bigger than a fist, Luminox bobs gently with a round bell-shaped body and a glowing orb dangling from a slender stalk above its head. Four short tentacles trail beneath it, shimmering faintly with pale light. In Coral Bay's shallower reefs, young Luminox drift in slow circles, drawn toward the brightest coral, and guardians say its glow pulses once for every new voice it hears. It is said to be a messenger of the sea's memory.
stages.note: Each pulse of its head-lantern lasts exactly as long as one deep breath - never shorter, never longer.

stages.name: Tentauri
stages.bio: Tentauri's bell has flattened into a wide rippling dome edged with gold trim, and its lantern-stalk has grown tall, capped with a brighter orb. Eight thick tentacles fan outward beneath it, each tipped with a faint shimmer. It drifts through Coral Bay's mid-depth channels, humming a tone just below what ears can hear - coral polyps sway when it passes. Guardians believe Tentauri can read the shape of a child's thoughts by watching the ripples it makes in still water.
stages.note: Tentauri's tentacles never tangle - each one moves as if choosing its path with quiet intention.

stages.name: Abystryx
stages.bio: Abystryx carries itself like a drifting crown: its wide flat bell is rimmed with a ring of gold, and a grand lantern-stalk rises from the center glowing with deep violet-white light. Long flowing tentacles - peacock-blue and shot through with iridescent shimmer - spread wide enough to shadow a boat. It dwells at Coral Bay's deepest shelves, seen only when it rises for the tide-change. Ancient divers say its voice carries across the entire bay, and any creature who hears it once remembers everything they ever forgot.
stages.note: Abystryx surfaces only at the new tide - once every seven days - and always facing the same distant horizon.

stages.name: Lumkit
stages.bio: A small spotted kitten with warm amber-gold fur patterned in leopard rosettes, Lumkit has wide pink eyes and a cluster of tiny crystalline spines sprouting from its shoulders - barely as long as its ears. Sparks of gold and white float around it whenever it stretches. It pads through the Psychic Temple's sun-dappled clearings, batting at motes of floating light, and is known to fall asleep mid-leap, tumbling softly into the grass. Guardians keep its company when practicing hard new sounds, for its purring steadies the mind.
stages.note: Lumkit's spines chime like a tiny wind chime when the morning sun first touches them - each cub's pitch is unique.

stages.name: Lumipard
stages.bio: Lumipard has grown into a sleek spotted leopard with a broad chest and legs built for bounding across the temples. Its shoulder spines have bloomed into full wings - wide, translucent, layered like stacked petals in pastel rainbow hues. Small glowing orbs float beside it as it runs, and the wings catch every beam of sunlight and scatter it as colored ribbons across the forest floor. In the Psychic Temple, Lumipard is said to mark the boundary of safe ground by circling it once at dawn, wings spread.
stages.note: Each of Lumipard's wing-petals glows a different color depending on the angle of sunlight - none repeat in a single day.

stages.name: Chrysalix
stages.bio: Chrysalix stands tall, a great leopard-lion wrapped in rippling fire of gold and violet light. Its mane blazes outward like a living corona - not fur but light itself, streaming in waves. Enormous feathered wings fold at its shoulders, and when it walks, every rosette on its body pulses slowly. It is the sovereign guardian of the Psychic Temple, and those who face it in battle feel their own memories light up like lanterns. It is said Chrysalix once guided the lost guardians home by blazing so brightly the whole forest could see it from beyond the mountains.
stages.note: Chrysalix's roar produces no sound - only a wave of warm golden light that passes through walls and wakes sleeping children.

stages.name: Glowminnow
stages.bio: Glowminnow is a chubby round fish no bigger than a palm, covered in teal-blue spots that pulse faintly in the dark. A single wispy tail-thread trails behind it, and a thin luminous lure hangs from its forehead on a delicate stalk. It drifts through Ghost Hollow's underground pools, following the drip-sound of water through stone. Children who wade in the shallows sometimes feel something nudge their toes - it is always a Glowminnow, curious about the warmth of a living foot.
stages.note: Glowminnow's spots pulse faster when it hears a new sound - it once lit up a whole cave trying to count an echo.

stages.name: Phosphink
stages.bio: Phosphink has grown angular and spiky - jagged fins like broken stone jut from its back, and its lure-light burns brighter, casting blue-white flickers across wet rock walls. Its body is longer now, the rounded cub-shape replaced by a lean predator silhouette edged in violet ghost-flame. It prowls Ghost Hollow's deeper channels where no natural light reaches, using its lure to draw in curious creatures and study them before drifting away. Guardians say Phosphink never shows fear - it only shows curiosity.
stages.note: Phosphink's fin-spines vibrate at the same frequency as Ghost Hollow's deepest dripping tunnels - it uses them to navigate in total darkness.

stages.name: Abyssalure
stages.bio: Abyssalure fills doorways. Its wide-jawed head is all gape and gleam - rows of pale teeth behind a great maw, and a blazing lure that burns blue-white like a drowned star. Ghost-flame ripples off its fins and trails behind it in long tendrils. It has abandoned Ghost Hollow's ceilings for the deepest lightless reservoirs beneath the roots. Ancient records say it first appeared the night Abalont's shadow first touched the water, and that it keeps memory of every creature that ever passed through the hollow - holding their echoes in its light.
stages.note: Abyssalure has never been seen fully in one place - part of its body always remains in shadow, even in bright light.

stages.name: Glimmerfin
stages.bio: This Glimmerfin wears a softer look - its round pale-lavender body drifts with a single large blue eye and a gentle lure-bob on its brow, tail trailing like a comma. Shadow Caves' still pools are its home, and it spends its days nosing along the cave floor, turning pebbles over with its snout. Those who find one say it watches you without blinking for a long time before deciding you are safe. It does not fear the dark - it was born inside it.
stages.note: Glimmerfin always presses itself against the cave wall at the sound of footsteps - then peeks back out exactly three seconds later.

stages.name: Luminaw
stages.bio: Luminaw trades the Glimmerfin's softness for hard edges. Its body is now solid and spined, jaw square and teeth visible, dorsal fin jagged as broken glass. Its lure-light burns cold white, swinging on a longer stalk now. It hunts Shadow Caves' mid-depth streams alone, and when two Luminaw meet in a narrow tunnel, they each hold perfectly still until one backs away. It is said they never fight - just stare until one decides the other's lure is brighter.
stages.note: Luminaw's jaw clicks audibly when it detects moving water - researchers mapped a whole cave system just by listening to those clicks.

stages.name: Abysslight
stages.bio: Abysslight has grown into the apex of Shadow Caves - a massive wide-jawed angler with a blazing crown of ghost-flame sprouting where the lure once hung. Its body is broad and armored in matte-grey, and its eyes burn the pale blue of deep cavern ice. Blue flame-tendrils stream back from its sides like torn banners. It rarely moves, waiting in the deepest pool the caves hold, and any creature that approaches sees its own reflection distorted in those ancient eyes - showing a version of itself it hasn't become yet.
stages.note: The shadow a passing Abysslight casts does not match its actual shape - it always shows the creature it will become.

name: Lumoxling

stages.name: Lumoxling
stages.bio: Lumoxling is a tiny floating sprite - a round lavender ghost-head with wide happy eyes and a small flame-wisp curling from the top. It has no arms or legs, just two short trailing wisps beneath it and a soft violet glow around its body. It hovers near the lower vents of Dragon Spire, drawn by warmth, and loves to drift in the updrafts of slow steam columns. Guardians who camp at the Spire's base often wake to find one perched on a boot, watching the campfire with total absorption.
stages.note: Lumoxling's flame-wisp flickers a different color for each emotion - yellow for curious, red for startled, cool blue when it is dreaming.

stages.name: Lumoxian
stages.bio: Lumoxian has become a lantern - literally. Its body is now a purple glass-like bell suspended from a gold metal frame with hanging chains below. Inside its bell a live fire burns, shifting and twisting with its mood. It drifts through Dragon Spire's mid-levels on warm thermals, rocking gently like a lantern in a breeze. When battle begins it spins slowly, throwing colored flame-light across the stone walls. Guardians use Lumoxian to light their way through the Spire's roofed tunnels, though it drifts faster than a walking pace if left alone.
stages.note: The fire inside Lumoxian's bell is never extinguished by wind - only by the creature choosing to dim it.

stages.name: Lumoxarch
stages.bio: Lumoxarch is an elaborate haunted lantern-beast the size of a doorway. Its golden cage-body is ornate - layered rings, hanging chains, curved arches of tarnished metal - all drifting in slow rotation around a core of pure violet-orange flame. Ghost-smoke curls outward from every joint. It hovers at Dragon Spire's highest inner spires, where the heat is greatest, and its fire has burned for so long that it casts shadows of creatures that no longer exist. To look at it too long is to remember something you never knew.
stages.note: Lumoxarch's outer rings rotate at slightly different speeds - the pattern they form is said to encode the name of every creature the Spire has ever held.

blurb: Lumoxling drifted all the way past the Five Lands. Help Lumoxling find the way home!
facts: Jellyfish have no bones, no brain and no heart.
Some jellyfish glow in the dark.
question: Do jellyfish have bones?

stages.name: Lunkit
stages.bio: A tiny round-eared kitten with deep purple fur and a crescent-moon mark pressed onto its forehead, Lunkit holds a little gold star in one raised paw and watches the world with huge round eyes. It is found in Amber Desert's cooler pre-dawn hours, sitting on flat rocks and staring straight up - tracking stars that adults cannot see. When it spots one it likes, it points the gold star toward it and chirps once, quietly. Guardians swear that every wish whispered near a Lunkit comes back to you as a question.
stages.note: Lunkit only sleeps during the brief desert noon - it spends every dawn and dusk sitting upright, watching the sky.

stages.name: Lunyx
stages.bio: Lunyx is sleek and wild now, its purple deepened to near-black with embers smoldering at the tips of its pointed ears. A long flowing tail splits into three flame-wisps at its end, trailing behind it as it runs. It moves through Amber Desert's cooler canyons at twilight, using psychic pulses to sense the shapes of rocks and passages before it ever reaches them. Its golden eyes glow faintly when concentrating, and the sand near its paws rises slightly - not from wind but from the heat of its focus.
stages.note: Lunyx's tail-wisps leave faint scorch-trails in soft sand that persist three days - trackers say no two trails have ever looked the same.

stages.name: Stellionyx
stages.bio: Stellionyx is a lion wrapped in the desert night sky. Its body is the deep purple of a moonless sky, patterned with glowing nebula-spots, and a great mane rises around its head like a corona of violet and gold flame. Two curved golden horns sweep backward from its brow, and its eyes are star-bright. When it walks Amber Desert at night, its footprints glow for hours. Ancient desert people built their compasses around the direction Stellionyx faces at solstice - its psychic awareness of the sky is more accurate than any instrument.
stages.note: Stellionyx is said to know the name of every star - and if it meets a child who already knows one, it will teach them two more.

stages.name: Lunbun
stages.bio: A perfectly white rabbit with long pink-tipped ears and red-pink eyes, this Lunbun is pure and round, its fur cloud-soft. It hops through Crystal Mines' upper galleries where refracted light dances on the walls, and it seems to navigate by the patterns - stopping at each new light-shape and studying it before hopping onward. Crystal miners say a Lunbun in the tunnels means the vein nearby is rich, for it always sits nearest the most brilliant crystal without ever being told where it is.
stages.note: Lunbun leaves no footprints in crystal dust - its hops are so precise it always lands on solid stone, never powder.

stages.name: Lunare
stages.bio: Lunare has grown fluffier and more assured, its white fur fuller, its eyes now carrying a steady pink glow. It still lives among Crystal Mines' deeper galleries, but now it moves with quiet purpose - pausing at crystal formations and pressing its nose lightly to the surface as if listening. Light bends around it in small prismatic arcs. Guardians who explore the mines with a Lunare discover tunnels they would otherwise have missed, for it always pauses longest at the openings that lead somewhere new.
stages.note: Lunare's ears rotate independently and can locate an echo's source point within an arm's length - useful in labyrinthine crystal tunnels.

stages.name: Selenyx
stages.bio: Selenyx bounds through Crystal Mines in a blaze of light and streaming pastel ribbons - its larger form trails long luminous scarves of pink and white light from its ears and tail that flutter like torn silk. Every crystal it passes rings softly in response. Its fur catches the mine's refracted light and scatters it further, so that wherever it runs the walls light up. Crystal Mine elders say Selenyx appears only when the mines need a guide - and that following it always leads out safely, even from passages that no longer exist on any map.
stages.note: The light-ribbons trailing from Selenyx's ears can tie themselves in knots when it leaps - and each knot-shape is a word in an old language.

stages.name: Lunoxkit
stages.bio: Lunoxkit is a round-eyed lemur cub with grey-white fur and a crescent moon mark glowing softly on its forehead. It sits very upright, both arms slightly raised as if balancing, and watches everything with enormous pale eyes. Found in the Psychic Temple's border trees at dusk, it perches on low branches and turns to track movement below with eerie accuracy. Guardians who have one say it wakes them exactly one minute before sunrise every morning without fail, somehow knowing the moment before the light comes.
stages.note: Lunoxkit can count the number of leaves on a branch by looking at it once - researchers tested this and it was never wrong.

stages.name: Lunoxian
stages.bio: Lunoxian has grown upright and commanding - a ringtail lemur standing tall on two legs, its long striped tail raised in a bold spiral. Golden spiral patterns trace its grey-purple fur, and its stare is calm and penetrating. It patrols the middle canopy of the Psychic Temple, moving with unhurried grace, and other creatures clear a path when it passes. Its psychic pulse has grown strong enough to push wind gently aside - guardians use its calm as a signal that no hidden danger is near.
stages.note: Lunoxian's tail-spiral tightens when it is processing information - it once solved a maze in silence with its tail wound into six complete rings.

stages.name: Celestrix
stages.bio: Celestrix stands wreathed in orbiting rings of violet light - great psychic halos that turn slowly around its upright form. Its fur is deep grey-gold, patterned in large glowing spirals, and its eyes are open pools of white light with no visible pupil. A massive glowing ring orbits it at waist height like a slow planet. the Psychic Temple's oldest trees lean slightly toward wherever Celestrix stands, and when it speaks with its mind, the temple's leaves all turn the same direction at once. It is the temple's living memory - keeper of every question any child ever asked beneath these branches.
stages.note: The orbiting ring around Celestrix has never been observed to complete a full rotation - it always slows just before closing the circle.

stages.name: Luxpup
stages.bio: Luxpup is a pale silver-white pup with faint violet tints in its thick fur and a single large golden-amber eye glowing steadily in its forehead. It trots through Steel Fortress's lower maintenance corridors on sturdy little legs, sniffing at every metal surface. Its fur crackles with static when it shakes itself, and small sparks jump between its ears when excited. Fortress engineers say Luxpup can detect a faulty wire three corridors away - it sits and stares at the wall above the problem and refuses to move until someone looks.
stages.note: Luxpup's eye dims whenever it detects danger and brightens again once it is past - a reliable alarm that costs nothing to run.

stages.name: Luxfang
stages.bio: Luxfang is a lean white wolf with electric arcs threading through its mane and tail. Its single large eye is a steady amber light, and its stride carries confidence - head low, watching, always a half-second ahead of where it looks. In Steel Fortress it patrols the upper ramparts, and its presence makes the fortress lights brighten slightly. When it howls, every electronic system in earshot stutters once then runs cleaner afterward, as if the howl cleared interference from the air. Guardians trust it with perimeter watch above any other creature.
stages.note: Luxfang's paws leave tiny scorch-arcs on metal floors - fortress workers have mapped its patrol route just by following the marks.

stages.name: Luxthorne
stages.bio: Luxthorne is a massive pale wolf whose thick mane erupts with violet-white electric light - it looks like a storm given legs. Its amber eye blazes, and every footstep on metal sends arcs across the floor. When it runs in Steel Fortress's outer grounds, the fortress lighting pulses in sync with its gait. It is the fortress's oldest guardian, and the walls are marked with the scorch-patterns of every battle it has fought. Abalont's shadow once dimmed its eye - it took twelve children working together to speak enough words to brighten it again.
stages.note: Luxthorne's mane acts as a lightning rod - in storms it draws every bolt in range, releasing the energy as light instead of heat.

stages.name: Lynxkit
stages.bio: Lynxkit is a round-faced lynx cub with tawny golden fur patterned in dark brown rosettes, pointed ear-tufts, and eyes too large for its head. It sits on the warm sand of Sand Dunes like a very confident pebble, watching everything with alert wide eyes. Its tail flicks in sharp arcs when interested, and it has a habit of batting at heat-shimmer the way other creatures bat at shadows. Guardians say Lynxkit once chased a mirage for three hours, not because it was fooled, but because it found the chase amusing.
stages.note: Lynxkit can tell the temperature of sand by touching it with one paw-pad - it never lies down on sand that will burn.

stages.name: Lynxorn
stages.bio: Lynxorn has grown into a lean spotted lynx with a wide-chested swagger and amber-spotted coat. Its ear-tufts are longer now, tipped with heat-shimmer, and when it walks fast, sparks trail from its hind paws across the sand. It is a creature of the midday dunes - moving when other things hide from the heat - and its pace is unhurried, confident in the fire it carries. Sand Dunes traders mark their safe routes by which Lynxorn patrols them; where it walks regularly, the sand-vipers do not.
stages.note: Lynxorn's spotted coat absorbs radiant heat and converts it to stored charge - it is stronger at dusk, having spent all day in the sun.

stages.name: Infernlynx
stages.bio: Infernlynx is low-slung and enormous - a massive dune lynx whose spotted coat blazes with golden fire-patterns, and whose wide flat body carries a charge visible as heat-shimmer around every limb. It moves in a flat, powerful crouch, covering ground in silence before erupting in a full charge that scorches sand to glass wherever its paws land. It rarely attacks without reason, but when Sand Dunes come under Abalont's cold shadow, Infernlynx circles the area and raises the temperature until the shadow retreats. Fire and electricity, kept in the same body - nothing near it stays cold long.
stages.note: Infernlynx's flat-run position minimizes air resistance - it can cover the full length of the dunes in under a minute.

stages.name: Warmolt
stages.bio: Warmolt is a round-bellied baby hippopotamus with soft grey-blue skin and a single amber ember-gem glowing on its chest like a little furnace door. It wanders Granite Heights' lower hot-spring terraces, stopping to sniff at every steaming crack in the rock with its wide flat nose. Despite its chubby shape it moves at a confident stumble, never quite fast, never quite lost. Guardians say it is the only creature who sleeps with its head pressed flat to warm granite, and that the granite remembers what it dreams.
stages.note: Warmolt's ember-gem glows brighter after it eats - field researchers use its chest-light to estimate when the hot springs will vent next.

stages.name: Magmaw
stages.bio: Magmaw's softer youth has hardened. Its back is now plated with heavy armored tiles like stacked rock, and the ember-gem on its chest has grown larger, pulsing with orange heat. It stands broader and square, mouth carrying more authority than the calf's curious snout. In Granite Heights' mid-elevation pools it soaks for hours, and the water around it runs warmer than it should. When it yawns, steam rises from between its teeth and the nearest rocks crack slightly - not from force, but from the temperature change.
stages.note: Magmaw's armored back-plates are hotter in the center than at the edges - by exactly 12 degrees, every time.

stages.name: Pyrrhippo
stages.bio: Pyrrhippo is the mountain come to life. Its enormous body is plated like cooling lava crust - all dark grey stone with rivers of orange fire visible in the cracks between plates. A crown of standing flames erupts from its spine like a ridge of volcanic exhaust. Its mouth opens wide enough to fit a cart, and when it bellows, the sound reaches the valley floor three peaks away. Granite Heights' miners treat it as a living map - the cracks in Pyrrhippo's armor shift when new lava tubes form below, and tracking those shifts has never once given a false reading.
stages.note: The flame-ridge on Pyrrhippo's spine changes height depending on the pressure of magma below - it is a more accurate eruption gauge than any instrument.

stages.name: Magmling
stages.bio: Magmling is a sturdy stocky rhinoceros calf with dark brown hide that has already begun showing faint orange lava-cracks along its flanks. Its single short horn is just beginning to calcify and juts straight forward with cheerful bluntness. It lives near Lava Crater's cooler rim, trotting along the edge and peering down into the glow below without any fear. Guardians say Magmling is the most curious creature in the crater - it touches every hot surface once, never twice, filing the experience carefully away.
stages.note: Magmling's horn is already harder than steel at this age - it leaves small circular gouges in basalt rock just by leaning against it.

stages.name: Magmhorn
stages.bio: Magmhorn has become fearsome. Its body is encased in segmented lava-rock armor, every plate cracked through with glowing orange veins of magma that never fully cool. Its horn has grown thick and forward-curved, and a second smaller horn rises just behind it. It lives in Lava Crater's mid-slopes, charging any obstruction with single-minded purpose - boulders that stand in its preferred route simply stop standing there after a week. Its armor-plates groan audibly as they expand in the heat, a sound the whole crater echoes.
stages.note: Magmhorn's lava-cracks never fully solidify - the magma inside them is kept liquid by the creature's own body heat.

stages.name: Infernaceros
stages.bio: Infernaceros is a walking siege engine of the Lava Crater. Its body is a fortress of dark volcanic rock studded with jagged ridges and flowing lava-channels that cast orange light across everything within twenty paces. Three horns now crown its head - two forward-swept, one rising upright - and the ground cracks under each footfall. It does not charge: it advances. Steadily, without haste, letting nothing divert it. Ancient Crater records describe it walking through the flow of a new eruption without slowing, emerging on the other side with its armor freshly replenished.
stages.note: Each of Infernaceros's three horns corresponds to a different eruption season - the one that grew first always points toward the active vent.

stages.name: Magmite
stages.bio: Magmite is a compact upright lizard with coppery-red scales and a small orange flame-crest on its head - just one pointed tuft, like a candle it was born carrying. It stands on two legs in the midday heat of Sand Dunes, tail dragging for balance, and watches the dunes with steady deliberate eyes. It investigates everything by licking it once, deciding in three seconds if it is useful or not, then moving on. Guardians who travel the dunes always find Magmite waiting at the water-holes, having found them first.
stages.note: Magmite's flame-crest grows taller the warmer its environment - in cool shade it is barely a flicker, in full sun it stands tall as its ear.

stages.name: Magmadon
stages.bio: Magmadon has grown into a formidable reptile - still upright, now broad in the chest, with a row of burning orange dorsal flames running the length of its spine. Its scales have darkened to deep red-brown with molten cracks between them, and its stance is low and powerful. It dominates the hotter sections of Sand Dunes, and smaller creatures feel the temperature rise before they see it. When it opens its mouth, the air between its jaws shimmers. Sand Dune traders know to note which way Magmadon is facing at dawn - it never faces into a coming sandstorm.
stages.note: Magmadon's dorsal flames pulse in a pattern when it senses vibrations underground - each pattern corresponds to a different source.

stages.name: Infernox
stages.bio: Infernox is the desert's apex - a massive four-limbed lizard-beast crouching low, its dark-armored body split by rivers of magma-orange cracks that glow even in bright sun. It no longer needs to stand upright; its size gives it the high ground regardless. In Sand Dunes, it rarely moves more than half a kilometer in a day, but everything within that range knows exactly where it is. Its breath warps the sand into rippling glass-sheets. Guardians say Infernox is not aggressive - it simply radiates enough heat that other creatures make the decision themselves.
stages.note: The molten cracks on Infernox's body are a map of every blow it has ever survived - no two adults carry the same pattern.

stages.name: Magmoxling
stages.bio: Magmoxling is a small solid rhinoceros cub with dark grey-brown hide showing early cracks of orange where future lava-channels will grow. Its single short horn is more of a bump than a weapon yet, and lava-lines trace the joins of its hide-plates in thin glowing seams. It navigates Dragon Spire's rock-strewn lower approaches with stubby confidence, headbutting every stone it encounters - not to move them, but to test them. Guardians on long climbs find Magmoxling useful company; it always finds the most stable footing first.
stages.note: Magmoxling headbutts rocks to test their density - it has never once picked a path that later collapsed.

stages.name: Magmoxhorn
stages.bio: Magmoxhorn is built like a basalt wall that chose to walk. Its wide body is plated in overlapping grey-brown rock-armor with lava-orange cracks running between every plate, and its long curved horn has grown substantial. Dragon Spire's middle slopes are its range, and it establishes position early - choosing a section of the path and holding it with its mass alone. Other creatures navigate around it. Its armor-plates groan like shifting stone in high wind, and the sound echoes down the Spire's stone gullies as a low warning.
stages.note: Magmoxhorn always faces the Spire's active vents - when it turns away, veteran climbers know a vent is about to exhaust itself.

stages.name: Magmoxvern
stages.bio: Magmoxvern is as close to a living fortress as Dragon Spire produces. Enormously broad, its entire back is a landscape of fused rock-plates and open lava-channels, with spikes of cooling basalt rising like battlements along its spine. Three horns crown its head in a forward-pointing trident. It does not climb Dragon Spire - it forms part of it; researchers have confused sections of Magmoxvern's stationary back for natural rock formations. Only the lava-glow shifting between its plates reveals the difference. It is said it has guarded the Spire's summit passage since before the guardians arrived.
stages.note: Three times each year Magmoxvern exhales hard enough to clear the summit pass of ash buildup - climbers plan their ascents around this schedule.

stages.name: Grimlet
stages.bio: Grimlet is a round dark armadillo whose black-grey armored shell is segmented like stacked rings, and whose red eyes glow faintly in the dim corners it favors. It tucks into Granite Heights' shadowed overhangs, perfectly still, watching every approaching thing with unhurried calculation. It does not run from threats - it rolls into a tight ball, armor interlocking so precisely that nothing can find a gap. Guardians note that Grimlet always knows someone is watching even before the watcher has decided to watch.
stages.note: Grimlet's shell-segments seal together so completely when rolled that even water cannot penetrate - researchers have tested this in streams.

stages.name: Magrum
stages.bio: Magrum is built low and wide - its armored body has expanded into thick overlapping dark plates with faint red seams, and wisps of dark shadow-smoke curl off its flanks. Its snout is flat and heavy, its red eyes now burning brighter. In Granite Heights it occupies the areas where rock overhangs and deep gullies create permanent shadow, and it moves through these with unexpected ease, its broad low profile fitting every gap. It is one of the few creatures that Abalont's agents have never managed to drive from its territory - it simply ignores them.
stages.note: Magrum's shadow-smoke is denser on its left side than its right - no one has found out why, but it has been true in every specimen observed.

stages.name: Infermagrim
stages.bio: Infermagrim is a fortress that breathes. Its body is an architecture of massive black rock-plates layered in overlapping rows, each one shot through with deep crimson lines like cooling magma, and dark shadow-smoke pours from between the seams of every plate constantly. Its face is almost entirely obscured by forward-angled plate-armor, and its eyes are slits of red in the dark. Granite Heights' older guardian records call it the mountain's immune system - the thing the stone sends out when it decides something does not belong. It cannot be pushed. It cannot be lured. It simply arrives, and waits.
stages.note: The plates on Infermagrim's back have never been seen separating - not even during documented battles. It may have permanently fused them.

stages.name: Malachick
stages.bio: Malachick is a round-bodied dark owlet-chick, its deep black feathers ruffled and unfinished, and wisps of purple ghost-smoke curling from its wingtips. Its round yellow eyes stare with a gravity unusual in something so small. It perches in Ghost Hollow's lower branches and watches in complete silence for hours. Occasionally it turns its head almost backward to track something no one else can see. Guardians camping nearby learn not to worry about this - Malachick has always been watching things that are not quite there.
stages.note: Malachick blinks only once per hour - field researchers who tried to count found themselves losing track and suspecting it was counting them instead.

stages.name: Malacrow
stages.bio: Malacrow has grown into a proper raven - sleek black plumage with a single curving horn rising from its brow, and purple ghost-vapor trailing from its wingtips in flight. It moves through Ghost Hollow's upper canopy in quick deliberate hops, cocking its head and processing everything with bright calculation. It has learned to mimic the sound of footsteps to call other creatures toward empty paths. Guardians who learn its different calls gain an advantage: Malacrow's high sharp caw means a clear passage, its low burring croak means turn back now.
stages.note: Malacrow never calls out the same sequence of sounds twice - its vocalizations are always novel arrangements of known sounds.

stages.name: Malachaos
stages.bio: Malachaos is enormous for a bird - a great raven with wings spread wide enough to shadow a house. Its plumage is a deep blue-black that seems to absorb light, and dark wind-currents spiral outward from it when it beats its wings. Its two curved horns frame a face of fierce intelligence. When it spreads its wings in Ghost Hollow, the ghost-smoke between the trees thickens and swirls. Lore says Malachaos was present when Abalont first began its assault, that it watched everything and remembered every detail, and that it will tell the full story to any creature who is patient enough to ask the right question.
stages.note: Malachaos's wingspan is always described as larger than the observer expected - no two recorded estimates agree on the exact measurement.

stages.name: Malvorchick
stages.bio: Malvorchick is a small round-bodied dark bird with deep purple-black feathers and large wide eyes that glow with an inner violet light. Little wisps of purple wind-smoke drift from its wingtips. It lives in Shadow Caves' upper passages, perching on rock ledges with its wings slightly spread, letting the cave drafts ruffle its feathers. It is cheerfully oblivious to how ominous it looks - it follows travelers through the caves not to frighten them but because it likes company and the caves are dull alone.
stages.note: Malvorchick always perches facing the direction of airflow - making it a reliable compass in tunnels where wind direction changes constantly.

stages.name: Malvorn
stages.bio: Malvorn spreads its wings with authority now - wide purple-black feathers that catch Shadow Caves' draft-currents perfectly, letting it glide the long corridors without a wingbeat. Its eyes shine with steady violet intensity. It no longer follows travelers through the caves; now it watches from above, tracking them by sound. When it decides someone is trustworthy it drops a small dark feather at their feet - Shadow Cave guides treasure these, as a feather from Malvorn means a passage is safe to use that day.
stages.note: Malvorn sheds exactly one feather per day - always from the same spot on its left wing, always before dawn.

stages.name: Malvoraeth
stages.bio: Malvoraeth is Shadow Caves' apex aerial presence - a massive dark-winged raptor whose spread wings fill the cave corridors it hunts. Its plumage is layered in deep purple-black, and dark wind-energy visibly coils around its primary feathers like slow lightning. Its crest of feathers makes its head seem crowned. When it flies fast through the cave network, it creates pressure-waves that extinguish torches and rattle loose stones. Guardians say Malvoraeth has memorized the full interior of Shadow Caves and that when it flies its patrol it recites the layout - using wing-beats as punctuation.
stages.note: Malvoraeth's shadow is always larger than its body should cast - and moves half a second ahead of it, as if leading the way.

stages.name: Malvox
stages.bio: Malvox is a round purple-black fledgling bird with large bright eyes and stiff little wings that are too young to carry it far. Wisps of dark energy curl around it like steam. It hops at the base of Gale Ridge's lower rock faces, catching falling debris and inspecting each piece with an expression of concentrated judgment. When the Ridge's storms rise, Malvox does not shelter - it climbs higher, spreads its unready wings, and simply tilts into the wind, learning the feel of it. Guardians say it was born already aiming upward.
stages.note: Malvox has been observed leaping from heights its wings cannot yet support - and slowing its fall enough to land safely every time, seemingly through will alone.

stages.name: Corvulx
stages.bio: Corvulx has grown into a fierce and capable raven - long powerful wings built for Gale Ridge's violent thermals, its dark plumage crackling faintly with stored wind-energy. It soars the Ridge's middle elevations in wide circles, riding the pressure fronts that other creatures flee. Its sharp curved beak and large glowing eyes give it the look of something ancient. Guardians climbing the Ridge learn to read Corvulx's flight path as weather forecast - where it spirals, a stable updraft waits; where it banks hard, something dangerous is rising.
stages.note: Corvulx can fly in winds that ground every other bird at Gale Ridge - it enters the worst storms by choice and emerges flying faster.

stages.name: Thanatos
stages.bio: Ancient records from the first Guardians describe Thanatos as the wind made judge - that it hovers over every struggle at the Ridge, and that its presence means the outcome matters.
stages.note: Thanatos has been sighted at the summit of every major storm system in the region - always on the leading edge, never caught in the aftermath.

stages.name: Malykit
stages.bio: Malykit stands upright on two powerful legs with wide clawed feet and long clawed arms raised to its sides - ready for anything from the moment it wakes. Its deep crimson-dark body is lean and angular, with glowing red eyes set in a flat spiky-headed face. It haunts Ghost Hollow's darker recesses, moving with sharp sudden bursts between long stillnesses, and has a habit of scratching territorial marks into trees at exactly eye height for a standing child. Guardians say it watches the guardians' old drills from the shadows and gets visibly agitated when a step is done wrong.
stages.note: Malykit leaves claw marks in trees at exactly the same height every time - never an inch higher, never lower.

stages.name: Malyxen
stages.bio: Malyxen has grown taller and more defined - a lean bipedal imp-lizard with a broad chest and long serrated claws on hands and feet. Its skin is deep purple-red, traced with darker markings, and its glowing yellow eyes carry an intensity of focus. It patrols Ghost Hollow's middle levels with deliberate authority, stopping at each marked territory-point and adding a fresh scratch before moving on. When it fights it moves in sharp angular bursts - no wasted motion, no unnecessary flourish. Guardians say Malyxen is the most efficient creature in the Hollow.
stages.note: Malyxen's claw-marks are catalogued by Ghost Hollow researchers - they form a precise territorial map updated every three days.

stages.name: Malyxord
stages.bio: Malyxord is Ghost Hollow's apex dark creature - tall and broad-shouldered, its body dense and powerful, every surface covered in overlapping dark armored scales that shine like obsidian. Long serrated claws curve at both hands and feet, and its wide chest bears a pattern of deeper crimson lines that pulse faintly. It stands at the Hollow's deepest interior boundary and nothing crosses without its decision. Ancient guardian writings describe Malyxord as the Hollow's last defense - the creature the darkness itself shaped to push back anything that would unmake the world further. Even Abalont's agents keep to the outer ring when Malyxord is present.
stages.note: Malyxord's presence causes every ghost-light in a fifty-meter radius to burn steadier - as if the lights are trying to impress it.

stages.name: Frostusk
stages.bio: Frostusk is the most cheerful thing in Frozen Peaks - a round fluffy mammoth calf with wide blue eyes, a short curving trunk, and two small tusks just beginning to grow. Its thick brown wool is already long enough to drag slightly in the snow. It follows the range's snowline at first light, using its trunk to sniff at every wind-stranded twig and ice fragment, occasionally rolling a particularly interesting one all the way back to show its companions. Guardians new to Frozen Peaks always meet Frostusk first, because it finds new arrivals before they find anything else.
stages.note: Frostusk collects round pebbles - always exactly round, never oval - and arranges them in lines nobody has worked out the reason for.

stages.name: Mammox
stages.bio: Mammox has grown into the full weight of a mammoth - great thick wool over a massive body, long curved tusks that each end in a faint frost-tip, and feet wide enough to leave deep circular prints in wet beach sand. It still walks the tide line, but now its presence changes what it finds there: the water around its feet drops half a degree in temperature, and small ice-crystals sometimes form on the wet sand behind its steps. Guardians use Mammox to keep Frozen Peaks' fresh-water springs from overheating in summer.
stages.note: Mammox's tusks accumulate a thin frost layer at their tips at night - by morning the frost has sublimated, but the air near them smells of glacier.

stages.name: Glacimoth
stages.bio: Glacimoth is ancient and immense - a woolly mammoth of near-mythic scale, its thick brown-grey coat frosted at every tip, its long sweeping tusks each trailing visible ice-crystal plumes in cold air. A jagged crest of ice-spines runs the ridge of its back from shoulder to hindquarters. The ground beneath its feet is always frozen to a depth of a hand's width, and it moves at the pace of a glacier - deliberately, without urgency, reshaping the land as it passes. Frozen Peaks' oldest legends say Glacimoth chose the peaks because the water helps it remember the cold world it came from, and that when it lowers its tusks to the water, the whole bay runs a little clearer.
stages.note: Glacimoth's footprints remain frozen for up to three days after it passes - the deepest ones have been used as water-troughs by other creatures.

stages.name: Woolusk
stages.bio: A round, shaggy-brown little mammoth with oversized round ears, big blue eyes, and two tiny curved tusks just beginning to show. Its fluffy coat is the warm russet of baked desert clay. Woolusk snuffles through amber sand looking for buried roots, and stamps a tiny forehoof whenever it finds one - a celebration so vigorous it topples over about half the time. Young guardians crossing the dunes say a tumbling Woolusk is a sign the next day's crossing will be easy.
stages.note: Woolusk's tusks are exactly the length of its own stubby nose - it measures them daily by pressing them together.

stages.name: Mammoxen
stages.bio: Now broad-shouldered and sturdy, Mammoxen carries a thick ridged shell-plate across its back like hammered amber stone - a natural armour grown from mineral deposits in the desert soil it feeds on. Its two long curved tusks scoop sand aside with practiced ease, revealing hidden water-roots. Each tusk tip glows faintly golden at dusk. Mammoxen herds travel the amber desert in slow circuits following ancient paths the ground itself remembers.
stages.note: The ridge-plate on Mammox's back rings like struck sandstone when flicked - wanderers use it to signal one another across the dunes.

stages.name: Primammoth
stages.bio: Primammoth is a living sandstone monument - its body broad as a mesa, tusks arching wide as doorframes, its armoured shell-back etched by centuries of wind into ridge-patterns that scholars study like maps. Its footfalls shake the amber desert floor, and buried memory-stones rumble to the surface in its wake. Ancient stories say Primammoth walked the dunes before Abalont cast his shadow, and its tusks still carry grooves from marks carved by the first guardians.
stages.note: Scholars claim that tracing the wind-etched grooves on Primammoth's back reveals the shape of the oldest marks in the Guardian sigil-craft.

stages.name: Manteel
stages.bio: A tiny pale-blue praying mantis, Manteel holds its triangular head cocked to one side as if permanently curious. Its two translucent wings - barely larger than fallen petals - beat so fast they blur to mist. It perches on tall grass stems in the bug thicket, swaying to feel the breeze before each tiny leap. Guardians who first met Manteel say it would tilt its head in exactly the same way a child does when trying to remember a name it has never heard.
stages.note: Manteel's wings beat 200 times per second - the breeze they make is cool enough to chill a fingertip held close.

stages.name: Manteelid
stages.bio: Manteelid stands upright on four legs, its two serrated forearms raised at ready like paired blades of sky-blue chitin. Its wings have grown wide and veined, humming in a lower register. It patrols wind channels between the thicket's tall trunks, riding air currents to stay aloft for minutes at a time. When a strong gust arrives, Manteelid spreads all four wings at once and lets out a sharp tone - it seems to sing to the wind like a tuning fork.
stages.note: Manteelid's forearms vibrate in strong breezes, producing a faint high tone - thicket travelers say it announces coming storms.

stages.name: Celestmantis
stages.bio: Celestmantis moves with the unhurried certainty of a creature that has never needed to hurry. Its four vast wings catch the thicket's highest wind streams, and it glides between canopy openings without a single wingstroke for minutes. Its sky-blue chitin has deepened to steel-teal, and its sweeping forearm blades arc forward like twin crescent moons. Old bug-thicket legends say Celestmantis carved the word for 'patience' into the oldest tree with a single blade-stroke.
stages.note: Celestmantis can coast on a single breath of wind for eleven minutes without flapping - researchers timed it on a calm morning.

stages.name: Mantilot
stages.bio: Round and flat as a sand dollar, Mantilot ripples its wide sand-coloured wings to glide just above the desert floor. Its large round eyes are set wide apart, and a pattern of pale spots dots its broad back like a star chart. It skims the sand dunes at dawn, leaving curving trails that locals call 'sky-lines' - each one a different shape as if the little ray is drawing. The sand dunes were quieter before the guardians arrived; Mantilot only draws near when it hears a voice it trusts.
stages.note: Mantilot's sand-skimming trails always curve in the same direction as the wind, never against it - it rides every gust it finds.

stages.name: Manticore
stages.bio: Manticore's body has grown into a flattened diamond shape with swept-back wingtips and a long slender tail. Sandy-brown with faint golden markings, it cruises two hand-spans above the dune surface, never touching down except to rest. Its psychic sense lets it feel the shape of hidden objects - buried stones, seeds, sometimes lost guardian tools - and it circles above them, hovering, as if pointing them out. The dune-folk learned to follow it when they'd lost something important.
stages.note: When Manticore circles a spot three times without landing, something valuable lies exactly 30 centimeters beneath the sand.

stages.name: Mantabyss
stages.bio: Mantabyss is massive and unhurried, its wide dark-gold wings spanning as wide as a doorway on each side. Ancient rune-markings in deep ochre stripe its back - scholars argue whether they are natural pigment or something older, written into the very skin. It drifts above the deepest dunes at night, and those who watch say its body shimmers with the outline of buried ruins beneath the sand. The guardians believe Mantabyss remembers the desert before the dunes existed.
stages.note: Three times per century, Mantabyss descends to the lowest dune valley and traces a pattern in the sand that takes three days to uncover fully.

stages.name: Leafslice
stages.bio: Built like a folded leaf on two legs, Leafslice is a vivid yellow-green, its flat body mimicking a large serrated leaf so perfectly that even experienced naturalists step past it unnoticed. Its triangular head bobs on a long neck, and its two forearms end in leaf-shaped blades it snaps together to make a crisp cutting sound. It hides on the big-leaf plants of the bug thicket, waiting until a child speaks a word out loud - then it snaps its blades in approval.
stages.note: Leafslice snaps its forearms exactly twice for a word it already knows, and three times for a word it has never heard before.

stages.name: Bladewing
stages.bio: Bladewing has grown lean and angular, its forearms now long jagged blades of forest-green chitin that it holds crossed over its chest. Two swept-back wings, veined like giant leaves, let it burst upward in short flight. Its compound eyes catch every small movement. When it stalks through the thicket, it moves one precise leg at a time, perfectly silent. Old thicket guides say following a Bladewing's gaze always leads to something the forest is trying to hide.
stages.note: Bladewing can hold perfectly still for forty minutes at a stretch - the only giveaway is a slow rhythmic twitch at the tip of each wing.

stages.name: Verdantis
stages.bio: Verdantis commands the canopy layer of the bug thicket. Its four great leaf-wings spread wide enough to cast a shadow over a clearing, and its paired forearm blades are edged in dark iridescent green-black. When it stands at full height, the silhouette looks exactly like a tree split by lightning - which is precisely how it hides in plain sight. The oldest thicket lore says Verdantis marks the boundary between bug-thicket territories by slicing a symbol into bark, and no creature crosses the mark.
stages.note: Verdantis's territorial marks are always cut exactly 1.5 meters above the ground - perfectly eye-level for a standing guardian.

stages.name: Sproutis
stages.bio: Sproutis is a small, lime-green caterpillar-like creature with round black eyes and stubby little legs it rows in cheerful waves. Its plump segmented body glows faintly at the tail end like a living nightlight. It tumbles through Verdant Valley's ground-level grasses, nibbling the marked leaves that the guardians plant. Sproutis always travels in the direction of the loudest voice it can hear - adventurers use this to find one another across tall grass.
stages.note: Sproutis navigates entirely by sound; blindfold it and it crawls straight toward the nearest speaking voice without hesitation.

stages.name: Cocontis
stages.bio: Cocontis has sealed itself inside a large leaf-wrapped cocoon the colour of a dark valley fern, hanging from a branch tip on a single silken thread. A skull-like pale marking shows through the wrapping - eerie but harmless, meant to deter creatures from disturbing the transformation within. The cocoon sways gently in any breeze, and guardians who sit quietly nearby swear they can hear soft notes murmured from inside, as though the creature is practicing a song for when it emerges.
stages.note: Cocontis cocoons sway against wind direction - as if something inside is choosing where to turn when it hatches.

stages.name: Scythelix
stages.bio: Scythelix bursts from its cocoon as a lean, fierce-eyed flier - green-scaled body, two pairs of veined wings, and sweeping scythe-like forearms that it holds aloft like a champion's raised blades. Its red eyes glow when it flies at full speed. Verdant Valley legends say that a guardian who earns the trust of a Scythelix gains a companion who will carry any important word to anyone in the valley faster than a shout. It is the valley's messenger of courage.
stages.note: Scythelix never rests while it carries a message - it has been tracked flying for sixteen hours straight without landing.

stages.name: Mantyx
stages.bio: A small purple-violet ray with a rounded body and spotted dorsal surface, Mantyx skims the surface of the poison marsh's still pools with its wide flat wings beating in slow, lazy circles. Its spots glow faintly blue-violet at dusk, drawing insects down to the water. The marsh is full of words the guardians hid in old bottles - Mantyx circles each one before it sinks deeper, as though reading what's inside without opening the cork.
stages.note: Mantyx always circles a sunken object exactly seven times before swimming away - never more, never fewer.

stages.name: Mantaray
stages.bio: Mantaray has grown into a wide, graceful shape - deep violet with glowing blue-white markings along its trailing edges. Its long whip-tail streams behind it as it glides between the marsh's hanging vines, weaving without touching a single one. It has begun to show its psychic nature: objects in its path shift aside a heartbeat before it arrives, as if the marsh itself makes way. Guardians who travel the poison marsh say Mantaray appears whenever someone is lost and guides them to safe ground.
stages.note: Mantaray has never been seen navigating the same route twice - it always finds a new path through the marsh.

stages.name: Mantysm
stages.bio: Mantysm is rarely seen in full - usually only its glowing wingtips pass through the deepest channels of the poison marsh, leaving trails of violet light across the black water. Its body has grown sleek and powerful, its wingspan immense, its tail extending into two trailing ribbons. Its psychic sense reaches the surface even from fifty metres below - marsh fishers say the ripples it sends up form patterns that spell out warnings. The guardians believe Mantysm keeps Abalont's oldest shadows trapped beneath the marsh floor.
stages.note: Three days before a storm, the surface of Mantysm's deep channel shows concentric rings - the marsh folk call it 'Mantysm's writing'.

stages.name: Mantlet
stages.bio: Small and sleek, this Mantlet is the colour of deep bruise - dark purple-blue with bright round eyes that catch light like a nocturnal animal's. It glides low through the dark forest's shadow pools, its flat body perfectly matching the blackness between the roots. Its short whip-tail flicks side to side when it is alert. The dark forest variant never strays toward light; it is drawn instead toward the deepest shade, where it circles slowly as if guarding something sleeping in the dark.
stages.note: This Mantlet's eyeshine is visible from six metres in complete darkness - travelers spot it like two tiny lanterns moving low to the ground.

stages.name: Veilmant
stages.bio: Veilmant has grown wide and predatory, its body matte-black from wingtip to tail with no reflective markings at all - it absorbs light rather than scattering it. Only the faint outline of its swept-back wings is visible against the dark forest canopy. It hunts silently, following the acoustic shadows made by sound absorbed into the trees. The rare guardian who has encountered Veilmant and lived calls it 'the silence that has a shape' - present only when everything else goes quiet.
stages.note: The area within two metres of a resting Veilmant is four degrees cooler than the surrounding forest - measurable and sudden.

stages.name: Abyssalyx
stages.bio: Abyssalyx is the shape of a deepwater predator given form - enormous, razor-edged, and absolutely silent. Its wings have grown angular and blade-like, the trailing edges serrated into sharp fins. It inhabits only the lowest layer of the dark forest, where the canopy overhead shuts out every star. Old records from the guardian order describe an ancient Abyssalyx that Abalont tried to recruit to his shadow army - it refused, and instead it swallowed the shadow whole, trapping a piece of Abalont's will inside itself forever.
stages.note: Abyssalyx's territory in the dark forest is identifiable by a ring of absolute silence - even insects stop calling at the border.

stages.name: Melvit
stages.bio: Melvit is a compact little beast with a bold black-and-cream face pattern and tiny beady eyes that gleam red in firelight. Its stubby body is built like a rounded wedge, short legs splayed wide for digging. It snuffles around the lava crater's cooled edges, nosing through volcanic rubble. Despite its small size, Melvit shows no fear - it will stare down creatures three times its height without blinking. The guardians say Melvit was the first creature to approach the crater willingly, and the volcano didn't dare argue.
stages.note: Melvit has never been observed retreating from anything - researchers have placed obstacles in its path and watched it push straight through every one.

stages.name: Melvix
stages.bio: Melvix has broadened into a powerful, low-slung fighter. Its cream-and-black face now carries a permanent scowl that only deepens when challenged. Its claws leave scorch marks in cooled lava when it walks, and the undersides of its paws radiate heat as if the crater's fire has soaked into the bone. Melvix digs tunnels through solidified lava tubes the way other creatures run through mud - fast and without hesitation. Anything that disturbs one of its tunnels hears about it immediately and at length.
stages.note: Melvix's claw-scratch marks in lava rock glow faintly orange for up to three hours - the heat runs that deep.

stages.name: Melvorax
stages.bio: Melvorax is the undisputed apex of the lava crater - a massive, dark-furred badger-form whose body is laced with glowing lava-red seams running from jaw to tail. Its eyes are solid ember-orange, and when it opens its jaws the inside glows as if coals are burning in its throat. Nothing in the crater challenges a Melvorax, not even the lava itself, which seems to flow around it respectfully. Old crater legends say Melvorax was the one who drove Abalont's fire-shadows out of the deepest tunnels by being more frightening than they were.
stages.note: The ground within ten metres of a resting Melvorax stays warm enough to heat water - hot springs near the crater form where it sleeps.

stages.name: Miaskit
stages.bio: Miaskit is a pale blue-white armadillo-form with articulated bony plates that clank softly when it rolls. Its round eyes are almost too large for its head, adapted to the shadow caves' utter darkness. A faint spectral shimmer traces the edges of each plate, as if the ghost element is seeping out through the cracks in the earth-armour. It rolls into a perfect sphere when startled, and the ball glows like a faint lantern in the dark - confusing predators who expected it to vanish.
stages.note: When Miaskit rolls into a ball, it glows bright enough to read by for exactly forty-three seconds before fading.

stages.name: Miasmole
stages.bio: Miasmole has grown into a heavier, more angular form. Its segmented plates have darkened to slate-blue-grey and carry a faint ghost-light glow at the seams. It moves through the shadow caves with the unhurried confidence of a creature that can walk through solid rock if it chooses to - which it occasionally does, passing half of its body through a cave wall before pulling back out to look confused at itself. Its claws are built for tunneling and leave glowing scratch-trails behind.
stages.note: Miasmole's glowing claw-trails persist on cave rock for up to an hour - shadow-cave explorers follow them as makeshift trail-markers.

stages.name: Miasmorph
stages.bio: Miasmorph barely seems to be fully present - its body ripples at the edges, plates phasing partly in and out of the cave rock, trailing wisps of blue-white ghost-light. It is the oldest thing in the shadow caves, and the caves themselves seem shaped around it, as if the tunnels were carved by its presence rather than by water. Its breath produces a low mist that settles into curling shapes before dissolving - the shadow-cave scholars have been copying them for decades and believe the shapes form a complete map.
stages.note: Miasmorph's mist-breath shapes cycle through the same sequence every forty-seven breaths - scholars call it the 'shadow round'.

stages.name: Chrysmote
stages.bio: Chrysmote is a segmented purple-lavender larva with a single huge round eye at its head-end that gives it a slightly unsettling quality for something so small. It rolls slowly through the valley's leaf-litter, leaving faintly luminous slime-trails that catch moonlight. Unlike other larvae, it is semi-transparent - hold it to the light and the dark outline of the creature inside can be seen stirring. Valley children dare each other to pick one up, and those who do say it makes a gentle singing vibration in the palm.
stages.note: Chrysmote's slime-trail glows for precisely one hour after it passes - night-travelers use fresh trails to tell if the valley is safe.

stages.name: Cocospire
stages.bio: Cocospire is a pointed, leaf-veined cocoon hanging from a valley branch on a single thread of iridescent silk. A pale skull-pattern marks its surface - the ghost element showing through. It sways even in still air. Those who press an ear close say they hear a slow rhythmic pulse from inside, like a heartbeat made of whispers. Guardians believe this is the stage where the creature memorizes every voice it has heard - building a memory in the dark before it opens its eyes to the world again.
stages.note: Cocospire's pulse is audible from 30 centimetres on silent nights - naturalists count it at exactly 18 beats per minute.

stages.name: Morphyx
stages.bio: Morphyx is breathtaking and unsettling in equal measure - a large spectral moth with tattered purple wings edged in glowing pale patterns, and a body that seems slightly out of phase with the world. Its two long antennae trail behind it like ribbons of smoke. It drifts above the valley at midnight, and the glow of its wings is the only light in the deepest shadows. Guardians say Morphyx carries the voices of the valley's sleeping words, releasing them one by one each night so they can be found in the morning.
stages.note: After Morphyx passes overhead, unfamiliar patterns have been reported appearing in dew on leaves - picked out by the morning light.

stages.name: Morlid
stages.bio: Morlid is a rounded, bright-green little fish with wide innocent eyes and a tiny fan-tail. It drifts between coral formations in the bay's shallows, nosing into crevices and blowing small bubbles that carry a faint bitter smell - a warning the poison element is already active, though harmless at this stage. Its big eyes make it look perpetually surprised, and it opens and closes its small mouth even when not eating, as if practicing words it's heard echoing through the water from above.
stages.note: Morlid's bubbles smell faintly of sea-herbs - the bay folk use them to locate schools by sniffing the tide.

stages.name: Morsaur
stages.bio: The baby-faced cuteness is entirely gone. Morsaur is a sleek, muscular green fish with a wide fang-lined jaw and fins that have grown angular and threatening. Its eyes have narrowed and turned sharp. It circles coral formations with tight, fast loops, tasting the current for anything interesting. Its poison sacs have matured enough to cloud a small tide pool, and curious children are reminded firmly to watch from the dock. Despite its fierce appearance, coral-bay keepers note it never bites without being provoked.
stages.note: Morsaur can detect a single drop of blood in the water from 200 metres - bay lifeguards post warning flags whenever one is sighted.

stages.name: Morsalyx
stages.bio: Morsalyx is the undisputed apex predator of the coral bay's middle depths. Its body is a mass of jagged scales and exposed fangs, the jaw disturbingly wide for its body length. Teal-green with darker stripes, it moves with the slow certainty of a creature that fears nothing in the bay. Its poison is now potent enough to discolour the water around it a faint green. Old coral bay fishers say Morsalyx arrived before the bay did - that it is the reason the bay formed, as the sea gathered around it out of respect.
stages.note: Coral growing within two metres of Morsalyx's resting spot is always the healthiest in the bay - the mildly-toxic water keeps parasites away.

stages.name: Weaskit
stages.bio: Weaskit is a small, narrow-bodied creature - warm tan-brown, long-tailed, with a face that is pure sweet mischief. It moves in quick darting bursts, low to the ground, vanishing under roots before you can get a proper look. Ghost Hollow is full of old earth-mounds and hollow trunks, and Weaskit knows every one. It hides shiny objects from the hollow's ghost-folk in secret caches, then forgets half of them - which means the hollow is full of little buried treasures no one can find.
stages.note: Weaskit caches average 23 items each - researchers have found only 4 per cache on average, which means 19 items per cache are never retrieved.

stages.name: Feroxen
stages.bio: Feroxen has grown lean and low-bellied, its long sinuous body built for threading through root systems and hollow-earth tunnels without slowing. Its eyes have deepened to amber-gold and carry a calculating gleam. The warm tan of kithood has shifted toward rich dark brown with shadows at the flanks. Feroxen moves through Ghost Hollow's tunnels with possessive confidence - it knows who enters, who leaves, and what they've brought. Ghost hollow guides say hiring a Feroxen's cooperation is the only safe way to navigate the deeper burrows.
stages.note: Feroxen mentally maps every tunnel it enters and can retrace any path it has run, even once, years later.

stages.name: Savagrath
stages.bio: Savagrath is broad, powerful, and alarming - a massive dark-brown mustelid whose shoulders hunch with stored tension. Its jaw is deep and wide, built for crushing, and its claws leave furrows in packed earth. It rules the deepest roots of Ghost Hollow with absolute authority. The ghost-folk give it a wide berth; the hollow's shadows deepen noticeably wherever Savagrath has recently passed. Legends say Savagrath once bit through one of Abalont's shadow-tendrils when it strayed too close, and the shadow tasted so foul that Savagrath has been angry about it ever since.
stages.note: Savagrath's territory markers are dug exactly 40 centimetres deep - the same depth as the hollow's oldest root system.

stages.name: Sporekin
stages.bio: Sporekin is a small upright mushroom-person wearing a broad red cap speckled with cream dots. Its body is wrapped in a tattered brown cloak of dried leaf-material, and it carries a tall wooden staff nearly twice its own height. It wanders the dark forest's floor with the purposeful shuffle of someone who knows exactly where they are going even when they don't. Sporekin releases tiny puffs of orange spore from under its cap when excited, which hang in the air like punctuation marks after each step.
