stages.note: Sporekin's spore-puffs are mildly luminescent - a trail of them in the dark forest glows faint orange for up to six minutes.

stages.name: Fungroot
stages.bio: Fungroot has grown taller and more weathered, its red cap widening and curling at the edges like an ancient hat. The leafy cloak now trails behind it, and smaller mushroom growths have begun to sprout from its shoulders and staff. Its staff has grown gnarled and branched, as if it is slowly becoming a tree. Fungroot moves slowly and deliberately through the dark forest, and everywhere it rests for more than an hour, new mushrooms ring the spot in a perfect circle overnight.
stages.note: Fungroot's resting circles average exactly 47 centimetres in diameter, regardless of terrain - forest scholars measure them religiously.

stages.name: Myconarch
stages.bio: Myconarch is the patriarch of the dark forest's fungal network - a towering mushroom elder draped in layered garments of moss and bark, crowned with a vast spotted cap from which smaller mushrooms grow like attendants. Its staff has become a living branch, putting out leaves and smaller caps. The mycelium network running beneath the entire dark forest connects to Myconarch directly; it knows where every creature in the forest stands at all times, and the forest floor trembles faintly wherever it walks. Old records say Myconarch was already ancient when the dark forest was young.
stages.note: The mycelium web directly under Myconarch's footsteps is twenty times denser than anywhere else in the forest - researchers call it the 'nerve highway'.

stages.name: Sporbin
stages.bio: Sporbin is an adorably round mushroom-cap creature with a pale brown cap and a single glowing blue eye. A soft haze of ghost-energy wisps around its base, faint as morning mist. It bounces through the bug thicket with endearing energy, its cap bobbing with each hop. The ghost element means it occasionally passes partway through a leaf or twig without noticing, then looks startled when it catches what happened. Thicket children follow Sporbin trails because the ghost-haze marks a path through dense undergrowth better than any lantern.
stages.note: Sporbin's ghost-wisps turn green when it is happy and blue-white when it is frightened - a reliable mood-indicator every thicket traveler learns.

stages.name: Fungling
stages.bio: Fungling has grown into a stooped, root-heavy form - broad dark cap, a gnarled woody body with root-like legs dug into the soil, and purple ghost-mist rising steadily from around its trunk. Smaller mushroom growths dot its shoulders. It moves slowly but with deep purpose, and when it stops, the roots extend into the soil and connect directly to the thicket's mycelium network for hours. Fungling seems to hold conversations with the thicket floor, and the purple mist thickens when it is listening to something old.
stages.note: When Fungling's ghost-mist turns deep violet, old thicket explorers start moving quickly in the other direction - they say something ancient is speaking.

stages.name: Arborveil
stages.bio: Arborveil is part fungus, part tree, and part ghost - its massive mushroom cap has grown to shade a full clearing, and its root-trunk body has merged with the soil so completely that it is impossible to say where Arborveil ends and the thicket begins. Ghost-light streams upward through every gap in its cap. It is one of the oldest living things in the bug thicket, and it remembers the guardian order from before Abalont's shadow fell. Arborveil does not move; it grows - imperceptibly, relentlessly, through the dark seasons.
stages.note: Arborveil's cap grows exactly one centimetre in diameter each year - scholars can date the bug thicket's history by measuring its cap rings.

stages.name: Sporeling
stages.bio: Sporeling is a stumpy little mushroom-cap creature with a shiny brown cap, a wide smile, and round stubby feet it pats against the marsh floor in a kind of perpetual happy shuffle. Its ghost element is gentle at this stage, just a faint shimmer at the cap's edge when light catches it. It explores the edges of the poison marsh's pools with cheerful recklessness, tasting the water with a tiny extended tendril and then making a face. Despite tasting everything, nothing in the marsh has ever made a Sporeling sick.
stages.note: Sporeling has been observed tasting 37 different marsh-pool water samples in a single day - apparently for fun.

stages.name: Fungstem
stages.bio: This Fungstem has grown into a stooped, vine-wrapped figure, its cap broader and more muted, its body trailing dark tendrils that probe the marsh soil. Its face carries a tired, knowing expression. Ghost energy leaks from the base of its cap as faint wisps that drift downwind. It stands at the edges of the deepest poison pools for hours, as if listening to something the water is saying. Marsh-keepers say Fungstem marks the boundary between safe marsh and truly dangerous marsh by simply refusing to cross it.
stages.note: No Fungstem has ever been found on the other side of a genuinely toxic pool - their refusal to cross is a reliable safety marker.

stages.name: Spectralmush
stages.bio: Spectralmush towers over the poison marsh's reed-beds, its immense glowing cap lit from within by ghost-energy in cold green-white light. Its body has become partly translucent - the outline of internal root-structures visible through its trunk. Vines and marsh-growth drape it like a king's cloak. When Spectralmush exhales, ghost-light spores drift across the marsh surface, marking the safe paths through. Old marsh guides say Spectralmush appeared right after Abalont's shadow tried to poison the marsh permanently - and that its ghost-light has kept the water from going fully dark ever since.
stages.note: Spectralmush's glowing spore-paths are visible from three metres altitude on dark nights - marsh travellers navigate by them like stars.

stages.name: Sporepuff
stages.bio: This Sporepuff wears a vivid pink-and-cream speckled cap with glowing blue eyes set wide in a little stem-face. Two curling leaf-sprouts grow from its sides like raised hands. It bounces energetically through the ghost hollow's shadows, and its pale cap catches the hollow's ambient glow and reflects it, making the area around it just a little bit brighter. Where other creatures are cautious in the ghost hollow, Sporepuff is delighted - it treats every shadow like a new discovery.
stages.note: Sporepuff's cap brightens by 30% when someone nearby speaks a word it has never heard - its excitement is literally illuminating.

stages.name: Funghost
stages.bio: Funghost has grown taller, its pink cap fading toward rose-white with a crescent moon pattern that glows soft gold. Its stem now ends in four tendrils it uses to anchor itself - half foot, half root, always touching the hollow earth. The light element has strengthened: its glow illuminates a small circle around it, and ghost-hollow creatures gather in that circle at night. Funghost doesn't appear to know it has become everyone's night-light; it just stands quietly, glowing, radiating contentment.
stages.note: The hollow animals that sleep within Funghost's glow-circle wake up calmer than those who sleep outside it - the light element is soothing them.

stages.name: Myconyx
stages.bio: Myconyx is magnificent - a wide glowing pink-and-gold mushroom crown ringed by curling luminous vine-tendrils that reach outward like open arms. Crescent-moon markings glow along the cap edge, and the entire body pulses with gentle light-energy in slow, rhythmic waves. Its tendrils have grown long enough to touch six trees at once, transmitting the light element through the ghost hollow's mycelium until the hollow floor itself glows at night. Those who enter the hollow after dark say it looks like walking inside a living lantern.
stages.note: At full glow, Myconyx's light-pulse is visible from the ridge overlooking the ghost hollow - a soft pink heartbeat in the valley dark.

stages.name: Sportle
stages.bio: Sportle is the most endearing creature in the crystal mines - a small round turtle with a mushroom cap growing from the top of its shell instead of the usual dome. The cap is pale green-brown and perfectly smooth, and the turtle beneath is big-eyed and wide-footed, ambling through the mine tunnels with patient good humour. The mushroom cap absorbs trace minerals from the cave air and channels them into the shell below, slowly hardening it from the inside. Sportle is the only creature that actually grows stronger the longer it stays underground.
stages.note: Sportle's shell is 12% denser for every year spent in the crystal mines - the oldest ones ring like struck stone.

stages.name: Fungurtle
stages.bio: Fungurtle has grown into a heavy, deliberate plodder. Its shell is now distinctly ridged and mineral-dark, and the mushroom cap on top has broadened and begun to develop secondary cap growths around its edge. Crystal dust clings to the cap's gills and catches the mine's light. Fungurtle moves through the narrowest mine passages without hurry, occasionally stopping to press its cap against a crystal vein for several minutes - absorbing something, researchers believe, though what it takes from the crystal has never been identified.
stages.note: Fungurtle sections absorb trace crystal resonance so precisely that placing a Fungurtle near a cracked crystal vein causes the crack to slowly anneal over weeks.

stages.name: Mycolemoth
stages.bio: Mycolemoth is an ancient, ponderous form - a great tortoise body whose shell has partially merged with the stone floor of the mines, ringed by a cluster of mushroom caps that have hardened to the texture of limestone. It moves so rarely that crystals have begun to grow directly on its shell, and the mushroom cluster on its back is large enough for small creatures to shelter under. The crystal mines were dug around Mycolemoth, not before it - it was there when the first pickaxe struck, and it was not impressed, but it allowed the miners to stay.
stages.note: The crystal specimens growing on Mycolemoth's back are 40% more pure than any found in the walls - the mycelium filters the mineral as it grows.

stages.name: Hornpod
stages.bio: A round, soft blue-grey narwhal pup with an oversized horn barely longer than a finger and huge guileless eyes. It floats in the light grove's still pools on its round belly, spiraling its tiny horn slowly as if tuning into something. The light grove's reflection pools are said to show the future to those patient enough to wait, and Hornpod drifts toward the brightest reflections without hesitation. Young guardians find it by following the ripples it leaves behind - always in perfect spiral patterns.
stages.note: Hornpod's horn spirals create perfectly-spaced ripples of exactly 3 centimetres apart - naturalists have never found an exception.

stages.name: Narwhisk
stages.bio: Narwhisk has grown into a graceful, spotted blue-grey cetacean form with a long spiraling horn that glows softly at the tip. It skims the light grove's reflection pools just below the surface, its horn breaking the water in front of it and casting prismatic light across the pool-bed. It has developed its psychic reading of the water's surface - ripples carry information to it about events upstream and down, both in water and in time. Guardians who seek Narwhisk in the grove say it always knows they are coming before they arrive.
stages.note: Narwhisk surfaces in the exact spot where the next guardian will approach the pool - it has never been recorded swimming to the wrong side.

stages.name: Spiralux
stages.bio: Spiralux is magnificent - a large blue-grey narwhal form with swirling lore-patterns etched in its skin like carved ivory. Its great spiral horn catches the light grove's light and refracts it into complex patterns that move across the grove floor. Ancient. Slow. Infinitely patient. The light grove was built around the pools it inhabits, and the pools were dug by its own passage. When Spiralux sings - a rare event - the light grove becomes briefly visible from every other region at once, as a distant shimmer on the horizon.
stages.note: Spiralux's song is audible once per decade, for exactly eleven minutes - grove scholars have kept records for 200 years, and it has never been twelve.

stages.name: Tinwhyx
stages.bio: Tinwhyx is a pale lavender-white narwhal pup with a single gold-spiraling horn and glowing swirl markings on its round body. Its large eyes carry a faint violet glow. It drifts in the coral bay's shallows, horn-first, using its psychic sense to taste the emotions of the coral formations - happy coral, stressed coral, growing coral. It produces small rings of light around its horn when it finds something that pleases it. Bay-keepers follow Tinwhyx to find the healthiest coral gardens.
stages.note: Tinwhyx's light-rings appear only above coral that is actively growing - it is a more accurate reef-health indicator than any instrument.

stages.name: Spirwhyx
stages.bio: Spirwhyx has grown sleek and graceful, its lavender-blue body now adorned with deeper violet spiral markings that pulse when it uses its psychic abilities. Its horn is longer and catches tides of emotional energy from the coral bay's entire reef system. It drifts at moderate depth, occasionally surfacing to release a spray of luminous droplets that hang in the air before dissolving. The droplets spell different shapes each time - local legend holds each shape corresponds to a current in an ancient ocean map.
stages.note: Spirwhyx's spray-patterns have been documented for 60 years; scholars have identified 214 distinct spray-shapes so far.

stages.name: Maelwyx
stages.bio: Maelwyx is a creature of genuine grandeur - enormous, white and violet, its body half-submerged in a permanent swirling current it creates simply by existing. Its long horn crackles with psychic energy visible as violet light, and ice-crystal formations ring the horn's base where psychic and water energy collide. It can read the entire coral bay at once - every creature, every current, every reef crack. Old records say Maelwyx was the coral bay's original guardian, appointed before Abalont's age, and that it has been keeping the reef growing through every dark season since.
stages.note: Whenever Maelwyx surfaces fully, the coral bay's water temperature drops by 2 degrees and the fish count in the adjacent grid squares doubles within the hour.

stages.name: Necryx
stages.bio: Necryx is a small, bleached-bone armadillo whose plated body is the colour of dry old ivory. Its joints are slightly translucent where ghost energy seeps through. It shuffles through the valley's root-layer with its nose to the ground, sniffing for something that may not be physical - the dark element draws it toward hidden secrets. Despite its unnerving pallor, Necryx is shy. It curls into a tight ring when startled, and the ghost energy at its joints briefly illuminates the inside of the curl - so a frightened Necryx looks like a tiny lantern.
stages.note: Necryx curls faster than any other armadillo-form creature measured - complete curl from open posture in 0.4 seconds, every time.

stages.name: Ossyx
stages.bio: Ossyx has grown into a disturbing and strangely beautiful form - elongated, low-bellied, with armour plates that have darkened to deep purple-grey and begun to crack at the edges where ghost energy leaks out as faint smoke. The exposed skeleton-visible sections at its joints glow purple. It moves through the valley's shadow zones at dusk, leaving slight frost-marks where it steps. Verdant Valley's older guardians say Ossyx marks the places where old dark memories have been buried in the valley's soil - it can't help being drawn there.
stages.note: Ossyx's footprint frost-marks always appear on soil that was a battle site within the last 300 years - the dark element reads history in the ground.

stages.name: Plaguarch
stages.bio: Plaguarch is the most unsettling creature in Verdant Valley - a massive, plate-armored dark armadillo whose body is half bone, half ghost-energy, with visible skeleton structures glowing purple at every seam. Dark smoke rises steadily from its back. Its jaw is wide and lined with bone-plates. Where Plaguarch walks, the valley's chime-flowers wilt for a day and then regrow stronger - as if its dark presence reminds the valley what it could lose. Guardians believe Plaguarch was created by Abalont's first shadow as a warning, but it chose to stay in the valley rather than serve him.
stages.note: The chime-flowers around Plaguarch's resting spots always bloom twice as densely the week after it moves on - as if the valley is celebrating its departure.

stages.name: Cloudmite
stages.bio: Cloudmite looks exactly like a tiny white cloud that decided to grow a face - two bright eyes and a gentle smile peek out from its fluffy body, with wispy tendrils trailing behind it like tiny legs it never quite uses to walk. It drifts through the lower gales of Storm Spire, humming softly and absorbing the mist rising from lightning-heated rain. Guardians who first climbed the Spire thought these floating puffs were simple weather formations, until one of them winked back.
stages.note: A Cloudmite can hold exactly 40 mL of rainwater inside its body before it must sneeze it all out.

stages.name: Stormjelai
stages.bio: Stormjelai has shed its cloudlike shape and grown into a true jellyfish form - a pale blue translucent bell with long trailing tentacles that crackle with stored lightning. Its gentle smile has sharpened into something more focused, and the eyes now glow when a storm front rolls in. It rides the mid-altitude winds of the Spire like a living kite, letting its tentacles act as lightning rods that feed it. Touch one of those threads and you'll feel why it earned its name.
stages.note: Stormjelai recharges itself by dangling its tentacles into active lightning bolts - it takes exactly three strikes to fill up.

stages.name: Tempestus
stages.bio: Tempestus fills the upper storm layers of Storm Spire like a living storm cell - its broad dark-blue bell crackles with continuous lightning and its long tentacles hang down through the clouds below, invisible until they brush the mountain's highest crags. Its eyes, now heavy-lidded and ancient, watch the valley far beneath with the patience of weather itself. The old guardians believed Tempestus was responsible for every storm that swept the Spire, and they were not entirely wrong.
stages.note: When Tempestus drifts east, locals say to bring in the laundry - the storm it carries is never more than ten minutes behind it.

stages.name: Noctidlet
stages.bio: Noctidlet is a small purple crab with a luminous crescent moon symbol on its back and wide, curious eyes that pick up the faintest traces of ghost energy drifting through Ghost Hollow. It scuttles sideways in the leaf-fall, pinching at shadows to test whether they are real or just illusions left behind by the Hollow's restless spirits. Its little claws are more curious than fierce - it pinches once to say hello and twice to say goodbye.
stages.note: Noctidlet can tell a real shadow from a ghost-shadow by pinching it - real shadows do not pinch back.

stages.name: Noctidus
stages.bio: Noctidus has grown a broad dark shell spangled with glowing star-spots, and its horns have curved into twin crescents that frame its face like a crown. Its large star-patterned claws now carry real psychic weight - objects near Noctidus sometimes drift an inch off the ground when it concentrates. It prowls the central paths of Ghost Hollow at dusk, arranging fallen bones and trinkets into patterns that nobody has fully decoded yet.
stages.note: The star-spots on Noctidus's shell rearrange themselves each night - no two mornings show the same pattern.

stages.name: Noctidemon
stages.bio: Noctidemon is encased in a massive star-flecked shell bristling with jagged golden spines, and its claws are enormous, crackling with psychic energy that bends the air around them. Its eyes - now a fierce glowing yellow - have seen every ghost that ever wandered Ghost Hollow, and it has spoken to all of them. It does not hunt; it simply sits at the Hollow's heart, holding the boundary between the living world and whatever lies beyond, as patient and immovable as the oldest grave.
stages.note: Touching a Noctidemon's spine causes vivid flashbacks of memories you have never personally lived.

stages.name: Noctix
stages.bio: Noctix is a small round-bodied purple bat with wide glowing eyes and stubby wings it flaps with great determination. A faint violet glow hovers at its chest - the first hint of the heroic energy that runs through its lineage. It roosts in the highest towers of Steel Fortress, dangling upside down from iron beams, and launches itself at any noise in the dark with fearless curiosity. New recruits sometimes mistake it for a piece of equipment until it squeaks and falls on their heads.
stages.note: Noctix always launches itself headfirst toward the loudest noise it can hear, landing on it before looking first.

stages.name: Noctilix
stages.bio: Noctilix stands upright now on powerful clawed legs, its wings spread wide with crackling purple lightning tracing their veins. The glow at its chest has become a constant crackling light, and its eyes carry a focused intensity that makes smaller creatures step aside. It patrols the Steel Fortress ramparts at night, and the guardians learned long ago to leave lanterns unlit when it is on watch - Noctilix reads the dark better than any torch.
stages.note: Noctilix can detect a single unlit candle from 200 metres away purely by the heat it would have made.

stages.name: Noctivex
stages.bio: Noctivex is a great broad-winged bat with two blazing purple rings of heroic energy framing its chest - the sigil that marks it as one of the Steel Fortress's ancient guardians. Its wings, now fully spread, blot out the moon when it circles the Fortress walls on patrol. Those rings pulse with a light that wards off both shadow-threats and doubt. The youngest recruits are told: when you see those twin purple moons moving overhead, the Fortress is safe.
stages.note: The two glowing rings Noctivex carries are said to be promises it made to the first guardian - and it has kept both.

stages.name: Hootlet
stages.bio: Hootlet is a small plump purple owl with enormous violet eyes and a crescent moon marking on its chest - it blinks very slowly, as if every thought takes longer than the one before it. A faint curl of lilac smoke trails from its wingtip when it tilts its head, which it does constantly. It nests on Dragon Spire's lowest stone ledges, and trainers say it is practicing: every slow blink is an attempt to read the mind of whatever it is staring at, with limited success.
stages.note: Hootlet blinks once per question it thinks of - on a quiet day it has been seen blinking seventy times a minute.

stages.name: Prowlure
stages.bio: Prowlure has grown tall and sleek, its purple plumage darkened to near-violet at the wingtips and tendrils of lavender smoke now curling continuously from its head feathers. Its eyes have narrowed into a focused, knowing stare that unsettles even the dragon-kind that nest above it on the Spire. It no longer simply tries to read minds - it succeeds, sorting through nearby thoughts the way a scholar sorts letters, filing each one before hooting softly and moving on.
stages.note: Prowlure will always hoot once at the exact moment you think of something you were trying not to think about.

stages.name: Starprowl
stages.bio: Starprowl unfurls wings so wide they catch the highest Dragon Spire thermals with ease, and the star-swept feathers along its face and crown mark it as a creature old enough to remember when the Spire had no dragons yet. Its eyes now glow with a soft, continuous light that can be seen from the valley floor on clear nights - the locals call it the third moon. It flies in slow spirals above the clouds, watching everything below with perfect recall and absolute calm.
stages.note: Starprowl never forgets a face - it has recognized returning travellers after absences of more than thirty years.

stages.name: Nocturnyx
stages.bio: Nocturnyx is a small deep-purple kitten with pointed star-flecked ears, a curled tail, and glowing orange eyes that spark faintly when it is startled. Golden stars speckle its coat like scattered embers, and it crouches low to the ground as it prowls the rocky ledges of Storm Spire, attracted to any humming electrical conduit or lightning rod it can find. It bats at sparks with tiny paws that absorb the shock and store it, then look smug about it.
stages.note: Nocturnyx can charge itself from a single loose spark to full static in under three seconds - it then refuses to be touched for an hour.

stages.name: Nocturnox
stages.bio: Nocturnox has grown into a sleek, powerful feline with a dark-violet body and a sweeping tail arcing with gold. The star-spots on its coat now pulse faintly in rhythm with nearby storm activity, and its eyes carry a constant electric glow. It stalks the mid-sections of Storm Spire with supreme confidence, using the static in its fur to sense incoming weather a full hour before it arrives. The guardians nicknamed it the living barometer - it is never wrong.
stages.note: Nocturnox's tail rises to exactly ninety degrees twenty minutes before a lightning strike lands nearby.

stages.name: Nocturnarch
stages.bio: Nocturnarch is a massive armored feline with a gold-spiked mane and a body ridged with dark violet plating that sheds sparks with every step. Its roar channels the full voltage stored in its enormous frame, and when it opens its jaws on the upper Spire, the sound rolls out ahead of a visible shockwave of dark electricity. It has claimed a peak no dragon dares dispute, and it greets each storm that rolls through not as a threat but as kin.
stages.note: Nocturnarch's roar has been recorded echoing back off the valley walls for a full three minutes after it falls silent.

stages.name: Lunscorp
stages.bio: Lunscorp is a dark purple crab with several glowing yellow eyes arranged across its carapace and two large front claws it holds raised like it is permanently ready to fight something it has not located yet. Its shell is the color of deep space, and those yellow eyes watch every direction at once - a useful ability in the haunted maintenance tunnels of Steel Fortress where it first appeared. Nobody is sure if it wandered in from outside or materialized from the ghost-energy that seeps through the old iron walls.
stages.note: Lunscorp always raises both claws before it sees what startled it - its claws know before its eyes do.

stages.name: Voidcrab
stages.bio: Voidcrab is rounder and heavier now, its shell a deep starless purple dotted with ghost-glow spots and a curl of eerie vapor rising from its back. Its many eyes have grown larger and now pulse with a slow electric rhythm. It moves through Steel Fortress's shadow corridors by phasing partly through solid iron - never fully, just enough to pass through the thinnest walls, leaving a trace of cold and the smell of ozone behind it. Engineers patch the holes it leaves, but they always come back.
stages.note: Voidcrab passes through exactly three centimetres of iron before it needs to rest - no walls in the Fortress are that thin.

stages.name: Cosmoscorp
stages.bio: Cosmoscorp fills the Fortress's highest vaulted chamber like a thunderhead that learned to walk - its massive star-speckled shell blazes with electric corona light, and its enormous claws crackle with arcing violet lightning. The dozens of eyes on its carapace have merged their glow into a single eerie pulse that matches the rhythm of the Fortress's old power core. The engineers believe Cosmoscorp feeds on the Fortress's residual ghost-electricity and in return keeps its walls from falling apart.
stages.note: When Cosmoscorp pulses its shell-light three times in a row, a power failure somewhere in the Fortress is less than an hour away.

stages.name: Owlite
stages.bio: Owlite is a round, fluffy purple owl with a glowing golden star on its forehead and wide bright eyes that track movement with unnerving precision for something so small. It sits atop rocky outcroppings near Dragon Spire's base, ruffling its feathers in the updrafts and occasionally emitting a single soft hoot as if answering a question nobody else heard. Trainers who camp on the Spire overnight say Owlite watches them sleep and seems to take careful notes.
stages.note: Owlite's star-mark brightens whenever it hears a word it has not learned yet - it brightens a lot.

stages.name: Twilight
stages.bio: Twilight has grown a sharp horn-like crest and feathers that shimmer between purple and blue. Its wingbeats are near-silent even in calm air - a useful quality near Dragon Spire's listening walls, where sound carries in strange directions. It hunts by reading the intent of prey before they move, and it is almost never surprised. The guardians who trained near the Spire used to ask Twilight for advice in difficult decisions, and it would answer with one deliberate blink: yes, or two: no.
stages.note: Twilight's horn-crest crackles faintly every time it detects a conscious mind focusing intensely on something.

stages.name: Celestowl
stages.bio: Celestowl carries a crown of blue-white ice crystals that never melts, even in Dragon Spire's volcanic updrafts - a sign of how completely its psychic energy has crystallized inward. Its great wings spread wide in silver-blue, and the wind it commands is cold with purpose. It circles the highest peaks in absolute silence, and the dragons nest only where Celestowl permits them to. The old stories say it arrived before the Spire had its name and that it decided what the mountain was for.
stages.note: Celestowl's crown of ice was formed in a single night - no one who watched it form could remember it afterward.

stages.name: Owlmist
stages.bio: Owlmist is a small, warm-brown owl fledgling with soft rounded wings and a glowing crescent moon symbol on its chest. Faint blue wisps trail from its wing feathers when it flies, giving it the look of a tiny candle moving through dark air. It perches near Ghost-hollow pathways that cut across Dragon Spire's lower slopes, and travellers who see its soft glow through the fog instinctively feel less afraid - which is exactly what it intends.
stages.note: Owlmist always faces the direction from which the coldest draft is coming - it says it can smell when ghosts are near.

stages.name: Spectowl
stages.bio: Spectowl stands tall now, its warm brown plumage faded to tawny grey and its eyes burning ice-blue with ghost energy. A flowing tail of translucent mist trails from its body like a second set of feathers, drifting in the opposite direction from the wind. It guards the misty switchback paths of Dragon Spire's middle heights, and travellers who lose their way in fog often find themselves gently turned around by a large winged shape they could not quite see clearly.
stages.note: Spectowl's ghost-tail always points toward the nearest recently-departed spirit, no matter the distance.

stages.name: Noctyrax
stages.bio: Noctyrax has shed its owlish roundness entirely and become a sleek dark raptor wreathed in blue ghost-fire that streams behind it in flight like a comet's tail. Its skull-pale face and hollow blue eyes are the last things visible in the fog before it passes through - because it passes through walls, trees, and storm clouds without slowing. It haunts Dragon Spire's highest passes with total possession, and the dragons that nest there give its flight path a respectful and wide berth.
stages.note: Noctyrax flies through solid stone rather than around it - cartographers who map the Spire find tunnels with its precise wingspan that no one dug.

stages.name: Noctylet
stages.bio: Noctylet is a small pale blue-white owl wreathed in electric blue ghost-flame that flickers whenever a gust passes through Gale Ridge's upper ledges. Its eyes glow a steady cool blue, and it carries itself with the slightly confused dignity of a creature that knows it is important but is still figuring out why. It perches on the highest antennae of the Ridge's old lightning conductors and calls into the storm, learning each thunderhead's name one at a time.
stages.note: Noctylet's ghost-flame doubles in size in the thirty seconds before a lightning strike it cannot yet see.

stages.name: Noctavis
stages.bio: Noctavis has grown powerful wings edged in crackling blue energy, and the ghost-flame around its body has intensified into a constant corona that dims all other light within arm's reach. A bold thunderbolt symbol now blazes on its chest - earned, the Ridge's oldest records say, when Noctavis flew into the eye of the Ridge's greatest recorded storm and came out changed but calm. It rides storm thermals at speeds that make it look like a streak of blue lightning from below.
stages.note: Noctavis can predict the exact second a lightning bolt will land - it positions itself one wingspan away, every time.

stages.name: Noctyryx
stages.bio: Noctyryx is a great blue raptor ringed in fierce electric fire, wings spread wide enough to shadow an entire market square from above. Its tail fans out in brilliant blue feathers that crackle with continuous psychic lightning, and when it screams, the sound arrives before the visual - it travels at the speed of thought. Gale Ridge's legends say Noctyryx appeared the first time Abalont's shadow reached the heights, and it has kept watch there ever since, too proud of its sky to share it with darkness.
stages.note: Noctyryx's scream has been measured arriving 0.8 seconds before the creature itself does - something physics professors quietly file away.

stages.name: Noctlet
stages.bio: Noctlet is a small, plain purple bat that trots low to the ground with its wings half-open, ears pricked for every sound the Dark Forest makes. It is wide-eyed and alert in a way that says it is still cataloguing its world - each new sound gets a careful triangulation before the little bat decides whether it is a friend or a branch. When children entering the Forest speak their words bravely aloud, Noctlet perks up and hovers closer to listen.
stages.note: Noctlet memorises the sound of every creature within a 100-metre radius within its first ten minutes in a new location.

stages.name: Noctyre
stages.bio: Noctyre stands upright now on clawed feet, its wings broad and dark with a faint violet sheen. Its eyes have shifted from wide to narrow and knowing - it reads fear the way others read weather, and has learned to echo it back at intruders or soothe it away from those with honest hearts. Deep in the Dark Forest, Noctyre's cry bounces off the trees in strange angles, confusing those who mean harm and guiding those who answer back with steady words.
stages.note: Noctyre's echo bounces at slightly different angles depending on whether the listener is feeling brave or afraid.

stages.name: Noctyrex
stages.bio: Noctyrex is a massive dark bat with a wide horned face and enormous wings that swallow the light around them when fully spread. It moves through the Dark Forest like a living piece of night - not flying so much as relocating the darkness itself. Those who speak fear aloud near it hear their own words returned in a deeper voice from the treetops, the Forest's own warning. But those who answer Noctyrex with courage find the shadows part and the path ahead becomes visible. The guardians believe it remembers every voice ever raised beneath its wings.
stages.note: Noctyrex repeats the last word spoken within its hearing range, once, before it decides whether to let you pass.

stages.name: Noctkit
stages.bio: Noctkit is a compact dark bat that walks on its wing-knuckles with surprising confidence for its size. Its coat is a near-black grey with a faint purple sheen, and its eyes glow a stubborn bright violet. It was born somewhere in Steel Fortress's lower armory levels and has spent its short life jumping off increasingly tall ledges to test its wings - currently at about the third rung of the ammunition rack. The fortress engineers have quietly started placing cushions.
stages.note: Noctkit has attempted 47 solo flights and landed cleanly on the 48th - it keeps precise count with scratches in the iron pillar it sleeps on.

stages.name: Noctwing
stages.bio: Noctwing has grown broad-shouldered, its wings now wide enough to generate a real downdraft when it hovers, and its eyes carry a serious, guarding energy that unsettles intruders. Its knuckle-walking has given way to confident upright stances, and it patrols the ramparts of Steel Fortress at dusk with the focus of a sentry who has never taken a break. When something unauthorised enters its patrol range, its wings snap open instantly - the sound alone has sent grown adults scrambling back through the gate.
stages.note: Noctwing has memorised every gap, crack, and shadow in its patrol route and can fly it in total darkness without slowing.

stages.name: Noctyvern
stages.bio: Noctyvern (Steel) is a colossal dark bat wreathed in twin blazing purple rings of heroic power - the mark that separates it from all lesser dark-flyers. Its enormous wings carry a weight of centuries, and when it opens them fully inside the Fortress's great hall, every torch gutters as the displaced air rolls through. It does not prowl the walls at night - it IS the night inside those walls, a guardian so old it predates the mortar between most of the stones. The fortress was built around it, not the other way.
stages.note: The twin rings Noctyvern carries have never dimmed - not in 300 years of recorded Fortress logs.

stages.name: Nullit
stages.bio: Nullit looks like a small dark ragdoll - a round blank-faced head with hollow eye-sockets, a tiny ragged body, and limp limbs that trail as it drifts through Shadow Caves' lower passages. One faint ember of blue ghost-light glows in its left eye, the only warm thing about it. It does not walk so much as float an inch off the ground, and it gravitates toward the quietest corners of the caves, where the darkness is most complete. Children who find it by torchlight sometimes try to carry it, and it always turns up somewhere it shouldn't be.
stages.note: Nullit can pass through locked doors, but only doors - it seems to have a strong opinion about walls.

stages.name: Nullox
stages.bio: Nullox has solidified into something more physically imposing - a hulking dark figure with a featureless face dominated by two glowing red eyes and fists that look heavy enough to leave dents in stone. Yet it walks with perfect silence. It roams the mid-depths of Shadow Caves drawing psychic energy from the residual despair left behind by Abalont's old influence, and it neutralises it - not by fighting it, but by absorbing it entirely and becoming heavier and calmer with each passing year.
stages.note: Nullox weighs more at the end of a long night than the beginning - it literally gets heavier as it absorbs the cave's sorrow.

stages.name: Nullvortex
stages.bio: Nullvortex has shed all pretense of solid form - it is now a towering mass of trailing dark tendrils and swirling psychic void, with only two pinprick eyes remaining as landmarks in its churning body. It moves through Shadow Caves like a drain in the middle of the air, and anything within five metres of it begins to feel its thoughts loosen and drift. The caves' oldest writings describe it as the Abalont-Eater - the creature that fed on the shadow and grew to contain it, binding the worst of the dark so the rest of the caves could breathe.
stages.note: Nullvortex contains more than eight hundred years of absorbed Shadow Cave darkness - researchers estimate it is nearly full.

stages.name: Acornbit
stages.bio: Acornbit is a plump, honey-colored squirrel with a perfectly round acorn cap balanced on its head and wide bright eyes full of absolute conviction about where the next nut is buried. It bounds across the sandstone shelves of Amber Desert carrying treasures twice its head size, and buries them in precise locations it then forgets completely before it gets ten steps away. Despite this, it is one of the happiest creatures in the desert - every buried nut is a future surprise.
stages.note: Acornbit buries approximately 60 nuts per day and remembers the location of exactly zero of them.

stages.name: Squirrelion
stages.bio: Squirrelion stands upright now on muscled legs, its coat a richer amber and its fluffy tail dramatically large for its body. It clutches a stone nut in one fist like a trophy and holds its ground on the desert's rocky escarpments with the energy of something that has finally decided it is in charge of this particular boulder. Its cheeks can expand to store three large stones at once, which it uses as projectiles at ranges that surprise everyone who assumed it was just looking for a snack.
stages.note: Squirrelion's throw accuracy is perfect at 12 metres - it trains daily by bouncing stones off the same canyon wall.

stages.name: Crystalnut
stages.bio: Crystalnut stands tall with a crown of ice-blue crystals sprouting from its head and a puffed-up chest radiating a quiet authority that has cowed dust storms. Its enormous amber tail sweeps behind it like a living dune, and its fists are now solid knuckle-stone hardened by decades of desert wind. The guardians who cross Amber Desert leave offerings of smooth river stones at the ancient feeding rock Crystalnut has claimed - it has sat on the same boulder for forty years and has no intention of moving.
stages.note: Crystalnut's crystal crown grows a new facet for each decade it lives - currently at four, and counting.

stages.name: Nymphid
stages.bio: Nymphid is a bright green caterpillar-like larva with a row of pink feathery gills fanning from its sides and enormous green eyes that take up most of its face. It crawls through the Crystal Mines' lower galleries, pausing to press its face against glowing crystal faces and absorb whatever light seeps through. The gills flutter rapidly when it is excited, which is most of the time - Crystal Mines offers more colors of light than anything it has encountered, and it is cataloguing each one.
stages.note: Nymphid's gills change color depending on which wavelength of crystal-light it absorbed most recently.

stages.name: Nymphant
stages.bio: Nymphant is caught mid-transformation - it clings to a glowing crystal stem with one set of clawed forearms while the golden chitinous shell of its chrysalis still clings to its lower body. The transformation is nearly complete, and light bleeds from every crack in the old casing. It has been in this state for eleven days by the miners' count, and the glow is intensifying. Crystal Mines veterans say the brighter the emergence light, the more powerful the wings that follow it.
stages.note: Nymphant's chrysalis cracks release a brief pulse of light bright enough to read by - researchers call it the reading moment.

stages.name: Nymphara
stages.bio: Nymphara is a fully emerged dragonfly of extraordinary size, its four wings catching every color of the Crystal Mines spectrum and refracting them in arcs that decorate the cave walls when it passes. Its body is iridescent blue-gold and its eyes reflect the whole mine in a thousand facets. When it hovers in a cave entrance at full wing-span, the light it splits can be seen from the mine's lowest levels. The guardians use its appearance as a signal: where Nymphara rests, new crystals will form within the season.
stages.note: Nymphara's wing-beat creates a light diffraction pattern on nearby cave walls that predicts which crystal clusters will grow next.

stages.name: Ocelyx
stages.bio: Ocelyx is a round-faced golden ocelot kit with warm amber spots and vivid green eyes that study Granite Heights' lava-warmed boulders with enormous curiosity. Its paws radiate a faint heat it has not yet learned to control, leaving small scorch-paw-prints on soft stone wherever it walks. It stalks the lower sun-baked shelves of the Heights, mostly practicing pounces on rocks to see which ones explode and which ones just hurt its toes. Results are instructive.
stages.note: Ocelyx's paw-prints on soft volcanic rock harden within an hour and stay forever - there are trails of them through the lower Heights going back decades.

stages.name: Leonyx
stages.bio: Leonyx has grown into a powerful spotted feline with rocky stone ridges erupting along its spine and shoulders, and fire flickering at the tips of its ears when it is alert. Its golden coat carries a permanent ember-glow, and its tail swings in lazy arcs that leave faint heat-haze in the air. It climbs the mid-level crags of Granite Heights with comfortable authority, and no other creature disputes which sun-warmed boulder belongs to it - partly out of respect and partly because the rock is hot.
stages.note: Leonyx's spinal ridges grow one centimetre per year - measuring them is a reliable way to age an individual without disturbing it.

stages.name: Blazocat
stages.bio: Blazocat is a massive fire-scarred feline with a mane of actual flame framing its snarling face and armored stone plates fused to its shoulders and flanks. It leaves scorch marks on the granite it walks across, and its roar sends loose shale sliding down the Heights for thirty seconds after it falls silent. It keeps to the upper volcanic ridges where no grass grows and the air shimmers year-round. Granite Heights' old name, before the guardians arrived, was Blazocat's Shelf - and some old maps still use it.
stages.note: Blazocat's flame-mane burns hotter during arguments - researchers discovered this accidentally and have not repeated the experiment.

stages.name: Octryke
stages.bio: Octryke is a small pale octopus with a single enormous glowing eye in the center of its head and a short purple horn that crackles faintly with psychic energy. It bobs in the shallower pools of Poison Marsh, extending one tentacle at a time to probe the murky water for thoughts - because it cannot fully tell the difference between objects and minds yet, and touches both with the same wondering curiosity. Its single eye narrows into a suspicious squint at anything that doesn't give it information fast enough.
stages.note: Octryke touches every new object with exactly three tentacle-tips before deciding if it is interesting - anything that requires a fourth is very interesting indeed.

stages.name: Octrapus
stages.bio: Octrapus has grown substantially, its eight tentacles trailing long through the marsh water and its pale body now marked with purple ghost-energy patterns that pulse in rhythm with its thoughts. Its twin horns have sharpened, and it has gained the ability to become partially translucent - not quite invisible, but hard to focus on, like a word that keeps slipping out of memory. It lurks beneath Poison Marsh's floating weed-mats and occasionally surfaces to stare at travellers with unsettling comprehension.
stages.note: Octrapus goes semi-transparent precisely when it is thinking most intensely - the more invisible, the deeper the thought.

stages.name: Octyrax
stages.bio: Octyrax is a vast purple octopus that barely fits in any single pool of Poison Marsh, its tentacles reaching the far banks while its body rests somewhere in the center, glowing with deep ghost-purple light. The single eye has multiplied into an eye cluster that sees on multiple psychic planes simultaneously. Old marsh-walkers say it is the Marsh's memory - every creature that has lived and died there exists as a pattern in Octyrax's enormous, still mind. It does not act unless the balance is threatened; when it does, the whole marsh knows.
stages.note: Octyrax has one tentacle permanently extended into each of the marsh's seven deepest pools at all times - all simultaneously.

stages.name: Spinlet
stages.bio: Spinlet is a compact round-bodied spider striped boldly in orange and blue, with eight legs that tap-tap against the Dark Forest floor as it bounces along on springy steps. Its body is plump and glossy, its eyes multiple and bright. It spins small trial webs - getting better each time, but still prone to spinning them across walking paths at face-height and then being very surprised when something walks through. It is learning. The Forest's older spiders are patient teachers.
stages.note: Spinlet reuses every strand of silk it accidentally ruins - nothing is wasted, everything becomes the next attempt.

stages.name: Webarch
stages.bio: Webarch is a stocky mid-sized spider with a vivid orange and blue-banded body and thick legs designed for precision work. It weaves webs of remarkable geometric complexity in the Dark Forest's mid-canopy - patterns so intricate and regular that researchers argue about whether they are functional or decorative, and Webarch does not clarify. It positions itself at the exact center of each web and remains perfectly still until something touches a single strand, at which point it moves at a speed that seems to break the rule about how large things move.
stages.note: Webarch's webs use exactly 47 anchor points every time - different shapes, always exactly 47.

stages.name: Arachnova
stages.bio: Arachnova is a massive spider with an abdomen the size of a lantern, bold orange and blue plates across its body, and legs that span a full arm's length in each direction. Its webs now span significant sections of the Dark Forest canopy, and it maintains all of them simultaneously through psychic extension - it does not need to touch a strand to feel what lands on it. The guardians who first mapped the Forest found Arachnova's web described in the very oldest records, already vast even then. It has been weaving the same pattern for two hundred years.
stages.note: Arachnova's master web contains one deliberately incomplete spiral - left open to remind itself that no web is ever truly finished.

stages.name: Bonepup
stages.bio: Bonepup is a small puppy-shaped skeleton with cream-yellow bones and wide hollow eye-sockets that somehow still manage to look endearingly bright. It patters across Amber Desert on bony paws that click lightly on the sandstone, wagging a tail of connected vertebrae that rattles cheerfully behind it. It is inexplicably friendly for something with no soft tissue, and it has discovered that sand makes a perfectly acceptable bed if you dig deep enough not to feel the heat. It checks on its digs frequently, having repeatedly forgotten where it left them.
stages.note: Bonepup wags its tail in exactly eight vertebral segments - it once dislocated the ninth and has never quite forgiven itself.

stages.name: Skelewolf
stages.bio: Skelewolf is a lean skeleton wolf that lopes across Amber Desert with the efficient ease of something that never gets tired, hungry, or hot. Its ribs cast bar-shadows on the sand at midday and it stalks the desert routes at dusk, following travellers at a safe distance with what veterans have come to recognise as protective intent - it keeps other things away, not people. Its hollow eye-sockets catch the last of the sunset light and glow amber for a few minutes each evening.
stages.note: Skelewolf always positions itself exactly fifteen paces behind any traveller it has chosen to follow - it measures this with impressive consistency.

stages.name: Deathmaw
stages.bio: Deathmaw is a massive armored skeletal beast with broad dorsal bone-plates, enormous jaws, and four stocky legs built to hold against desert storms. Its skeleton is dense and ancient, the bones stained amber from centuries of desert sand, and its jaw hangs open in a permanent grin that is less menacing once you realize it cannot close. It patrols the deep desert where no living creature goes willingly, marking the boundaries of Abalont's old influence and ensuring nothing crosses back out. Whatever Deathmaw chases turns around.
stages.note: Deathmaw's jaw has been open for 200 years - historians believe it swallowed something it is still digesting.

stages.name: Bonelet
stages.bio: Bonelet is a small spider with a round skull-white carapace above a small pale body, six visible legs, and hollow dark eye-sockets that give it the look of a tiny lost ghost wearing spider shoes. It picks its way through Bug Thicket's leaf litter with careful steps, pausing frequently as if it just forgot where it was going. It is not lost - it is simply processing an enormous amount of ghost-echo information from the soil beneath it, which contains centuries of Bug Thicket's layered spirit-history.
stages.note: Bonelet can tell how old a patch of leaf litter is purely by standing on it - it gives a small tremor when the layer beneath is very old.

stages.name: Skelspine
stages.bio: Skelspine is a larger pale arachnid with a spined carapace studded with bony protrusions and a rounder, heavier frame than its predecessor. Its hollow eye-sockets now carry a faint ghost glow, and it has learned to use the spines on its back to anchor itself in the undergrowth and become completely still - practically invisible in the thicket's dappled shadows. It eats ghost-energy that gathers in old insect husks, and is thus very useful to have around anywhere the Thicket's restless past tends to accumulate.
stages.note: Skelspine can hold perfectly motionless for six hours at a time - the record, logged in the Thicket research register, is nine hours and forty minutes.

stages.name: Necrcrawl
stages.bio: Necrcrawl is an enormous pale-white spider with a massive pocked carapace like weathered bone and eight heavy legs that barely make sound as it crosses the Thicket floor. Its body is scarred and ancient, dotted with hollow pits that emit faint ghost-light from whatever it has absorbed over its long centuries in Bug Thicket. It does not spin webs anymore - it simply exists, and the Thicket organizes itself around it with the deference of a forest for its oldest tree. Smaller creatures move out of its path in absolute silence.
stages.note: Necrcrawl has crossed Bug Thicket in the same direction on the same night every year for as long as the oldest records reach - no one has determined where it is going.

stages.name: Padsprout
stages.bio: Padsprout is a tiny teal toad with enormous shining blue eyes and a pair of small leaf-wings that flutter from its back when it hops - not quite enough to fly, but enough to make every jump twice as far as its legs alone could manage. It bounces through the lily-padded pools of Verdant Valley, landing on every floating leaf with a small plop and a satisfied blink. It is the first creature many children meet in the Valley, and it greets them with the same generous enthusiasm it gives to everything, including puddles.
stages.note: Padsprout's leaf-wings fold flat when rain is coming and open wide when sun is expected - valley farmers rely on them as weather indicators.

stages.name: Padoctor
stages.bio: Padoctor is a large, calm toad with a broad flat back on which a collar of green leaves has grown, circling its neck like a living ruff. It sits in the central pools of Verdant Valley with unhurried patience, and smaller creatures come to perch on its back and dry their feet. It produces a mild healing nectar from glands in its feet that seeps into the water around it, keeping the pool's other residents healthy. The guardians kept records of Padoctor's presence going back three hundred years - apparently the same spot, possibly the same toad.
stages.note: Padoctor's leaf-collar adds one new leaf each spring - a twenty-leaf collar indicates a very long and quiet life.

stages.name: Padbloom
stages.bio: Padbloom is a great broad toad crowned with twin pink lotus blossoms that have rooted into its back and grown with it for so long that it is impossible to say where the toad ends and the flowers begin. It sits in Verdant Valley's deepest central pool with the stillness of something that has decided its purpose is to be exactly where it is. The lotus flowers open at dawn and close at dusk in perfect reliability, and the valley's people use Padbloom's blooms to set their morning routines. When Abalont's shadow reached the Valley, Padbloom did not move - and the shadow did not come that way.
stages.note: Padbloom's lotus blooms are never the same shade of pink two days in a row - the full color cycle takes exactly 365 days.

stages.name: Pavkit
stages.bio: Pavkit struts on two turquoise legs, its round teal-and-blue body capped with a single slender crystal horn on its head. A compact fan of iridescent tail feathers already sport luminous eye-spots that glitter in the crystal mines' refracted light. It tilts its head whenever a gem shard catches a sunbeam, transfixed for minutes at a time. The mine's guardian elders say a Pavkit once led explorers out of a tunnel collapse simply by following its glowing horn, which pulses faintly when it senses hidden crystal veins.
stages.note: A Pavkit's horn glows three times brighter just before a new crystal vein is about to crack open.

stages.name: Pavinox
stages.bio: Pavinox stands tall and proud, its deep teal plumage electric against the mine walls. Its horn has lengthened and now splits into a short glowing fork, and branching lavender antler-like projections sprout from either side of its head. The tail fan has fully unfurled into a wide spread of eye-spotted feathers, each tip catching light like a polished lens. It paces crystal corridors in slow circles, its antler-prongs casting prismatic shadows. Miners who work near a Pavinox report that their lanterns last twice as long.
stages.note: Pavinox fans its tail precisely at noon each day - the reflected light serves as a crystal-mine sundial.

stages.name: Pavenaxis
stages.bio: Pavenaxis has shed its physical feathers for a swirling mantle of violet and white light energy that flows like a living aurora. Its body glows with an inner luminescence, and its once-crystal horn has become a radiant spike of pure psychic energy. Four curling light-tails spiral outward behind it, each tipped with a blazing eye of pale gold. Where it walks, refracted rainbows paint the mine walls. Ancient records claim that Pavenaxis can read a word's meaning directly from a child's thoughts and reflect it back as a beam of colored light.
stages.note: Each of Pavenaxis's four spiraling light-tails corresponds to one of the four compass directions of the crystal mines.

stages.name: Pebblet
stages.bio: Pebblet is a compact upright tortoise whose rounded body is covered in rough grey-brown rock-textured skin. A single small green sprout pokes up from the top of its shell like a tiny flag. Its wide eyes and stubby arms give it an endearing look, but the shell already feels like solid granite to the touch. Young Pebblets collect small stones in the crevices of their shells and tumble them around like marbles during play. They are found near the lower trails of the Granite Heights, where the first memory-stones are carved into boulders.
stages.note: Pebblet polishes its single sprout every morning by rolling in the dew-wet grass at the cliff's base.

stages.name: Stonox
stages.bio: Stonox walks on four thick boulder-like legs, its back now a broad plate of segmented rock tiles overgrown with moss and a small leafy plant sprouting from the center. The shell's edges are cracked and layered like a geology sample, each layer a different shade of brown and grey. It moves slowly but with total certainty across the steep granite paths, pausing to press its nose against carved memory-stones and study them. Stonox is so heavy that its footprints become permanent indentations in softer stone - younger creatures follow these prints as trail markers.
stages.note: Every place Stonox has rested for more than a week, a new ring of grass grows in a perfect circle around its shell.

stages.name: Terravian
stages.bio: Terravian is a walking mountain fortress. Its shell has become an enormous segmented dome of stacked granite slabs, each slab carved naturally with mineral veins. A full tree - trunk, branches, and rustling leaves - grows from the shell's crown, sheltering smaller creatures in its canopy. Its four legs are as thick as pillars, and each step sends a faint tremor through the stone beneath. Terravian has stood at the summit of Granite Heights longer than any map remembers, and the guardians say it holds the roots of the whole mountain in place with its stillness.
stages.note: The tree growing from Terravian's shell has never once lost a leaf, even through the fiercest mountain winters.

stages.name: Petkit
stages.bio: Petkit is a small woolly four-legged creature with a round pale tan body and a single small nub of a horn on its forehead. Its fleece is fluffy and cream-colored, and its wide brown eyes are full of bright curiosity. It bounces from rock to rock in the amber desert, testing each stone with a quick headbutt before deciding whether to trust it. Young trainers in the region first meet a Petkit when it steals a memory-tablet off a low boulder and carries it proudly back to its herd. The nub-horn glows faintly orange when it finds a stone worth remembering.
stages.note: Petkit headbutts the same boulder each morning - researchers have counted up to forty-three consecutive taps before it gives up.

stages.name: Petrocorn
stages.bio: Petrocorn stands proud on four sturdy hooved legs, its woolly brown coat now thick and rough-textured. The single horn has grown into a sweeping curved ram's horn, broad and ridged like a spiral of layered sandstone. Its dark eyes are calm and appraising, and it moves across the amber desert with a confident swagger that makes younger creatures step aside. When charging, it lowers its head so that only the horn hits - it has shattered boulders twice its own size without flinching. The crack of its impact echoes off the amber cliffs and signals to its herd that a new path is clear.
stages.note: A Petrocorn can identify the age of any desert boulder by licking it once - a trait no geologist has been able to explain.

stages.name: Stonarch
stages.bio: Stonarch is a massive four-legged beast whose grey-brown hide has petrified to the texture of weathered desert stone. Three thick curved horns fan out from its broad head - the central one enormous and cracked at the tip from a lifetime of headbutts, the two flanking ones coiled with deep spiral ridges. Its barrel-round body is covered in natural rock patches that look like natural desert outcroppings. Stonarch moves so rarely that amber desert maps mark its preferred resting spots as landmarks. The guardians say that where Stonarch stands at sunrise, the desert will hold firm against Abalont's creeping dark for another season.
stages.note: The three horns of a Stonarch form a natural compass: the tallest always points toward the nearest underground water source.

stages.name: Flarcub
stages.bio: Flarcub stands on four clawed legs with an armored red-and-black body plated in overlapping scales like a knight's armor. A tuft of bright orange fire blazes at the tip of its tail, and its eyes are wide and golden. Even at this young stage its scale plates are fully formed, giving it the look of a miniature warrior. It runs along sand dune crests at dusk, leaving tiny claw marks and scorch spots where its flame-tail sweeps too close. Explorers who camp near the sand dunes often wake to find a Flarcub has singed the edges of their tents while inspecting the campfire.
stages.note: Flarcub can hold a single ember in its closed claws for up to six hours without burning itself.

stages.name: Pyrdrake
stages.bio: Pyrdrake has grown into a fierce four-legged drake with a heavily armored red-black body and a broad, flat-skulled head crowned with spiky frills. The flame at its tail has expanded into a roaring blaze. Its claws are wider and sharper, and the scale plates on its chest and shoulders have fused into a nearly impenetrable breastplate. It hunts alone across the sand dunes, using the shimmer of heat above the sand to hide its silhouette. When it stops moving, it looks exactly like a red-streaked dune rock - only the steady flicker of its tail flame gives it away.
stages.note: Pyrdrake buries itself in hot sand up to its neck each midday to supercharge its flame, then erupts out in a shower of sparks.

stages.name: Infernolith
stages.bio: Infernolith looms over the sand dunes on four pillar-like legs, its body a fortress of black-edged crimson scale-armor. The flame crown blazes from the nape of its neck, and its broad head is flanked by swept-back horns and a chest so wide it blocks out the horizon when it turns broadside. Three separate flame plumes burn from its back like living torches. Its footsteps melt a thin glass layer into the sand. The desert clans say Infernolith was born from the first volcanic vent that burst through the sand dunes and has burned without rest ever since, guarding the dunes from those who would put out every last fire.
stages.note: The glass prints Infernolith leaves in the sand contain tiny trapped air bubbles - each one is shaped like a mark from the ancient fire-sigils.

stages.name: Pinqulet
stages.bio: Pinqulet is a tiny pink-bodied sea creature that curves and bounces through Coral Bay's shallows like a living toy. Its round belly and upturned snout are a soft bubblegum pink, and its cheerful blue eyes are huge and round. A small dorsal fin and a pair of side fins are all it needs to zip around the coral gardens. It has already discovered that staring at the coral polyps causes them to briefly glow pink - an accidental psychic pulse it triggers whenever it blinks at a new creature. Young reef-tenders keep Pinqulets as companions because they alert the bay when storm-waters are coming by spinning in circles.
stages.note: Pinqulet spins left-clockwise when rain is an hour away, and right-clockwise when it's ten minutes away.

stages.name: Pinquale
stages.bio: Pinquale has grown into a sleek, confident swimmer - its body still blush pink but now streamlined, with a longer snout and a confident tail fluke. The side fins have broadened to help it cruise at speed through the bay's deeper channels. Its wide eyes see through murky coral-bay waters as clearly as glass, a psychic sharpening that lets it notice things other creatures miss entirely. It leaps from the water in low arcs at dawn, the spray catching the morning light and scattering it in brief rainbows that the bay's guardian markers track. Pinquale is said to remember every voice raised in its presence, even those whispered under the water.
stages.note: Pinquale's wake always curves in the shape of the last word it heard spoken above the water's surface.

stages.name: Pinquarch
stages.bio: Pinquarch is a magnificent full-grown sea creature whose pink body is now adorned with a glowing golden halo that hovers above its head. Pink feather-like fins trail from its back and flanks, shimmering with iridescent patterns as it glides. Its golden tail-fluke sweeps water into gentle spirals that glow faintly where they touch the coral. The bay's oldest records describe Pinquarch as a living tide-reader - it knows when Abalont's shadow touches the water before any storm appears, and its halo dims as warning. Children who touch its flank claim they briefly understand every language spoken by the sea.
stages.note: When Pinquarch's golden halo turns copper-orange at sunset, the bay clams all close their shells simultaneously.

stages.name: Piranule
stages.bio: Piranule is a small, chubby round-bodied fish with a bright green body and a single enormous eye that dominates its face. Its tiny mouth curves upward in what looks like an innocent smile, but a faint row of teeth hint at what's coming. It floats in the murky still pools beneath Ghost Hollow's twisted trees, and bubbles drift up around it constantly. When frightened, it puffs up to nearly twice its size like a tiny balloon and drifts to the bottom. Ghost Hollow travelers always warn each other: if you see a small green fish smiling at you from the dark water, keep your fingers up.
stages.note: Piranule's single large eye can see in complete darkness, and it watches its trainer even while appearing to look the other way.

stages.name: Piranash
stages.bio: Piranash has lost any pretense of innocence. Its teal-green body is now angular and powerful, with a wide gaping mouth of triangular teeth that it rarely fully closes. Three sharp dorsal spines jut from its back, and water-bubble clusters appear around it as a threat display. Its large eye has gained a cold menacing quality, taking in everything around it without betraying any reaction. It circles the hollow's deeper pools in slow hungry loops, occasionally thrashing the water's surface with its tail to make prey flinch. Ghost Hollow fishers say that Piranash never bites the same spot twice - it tests patience before it strikes.
stages.note: Piranash always surfaces exactly three times before attacking - watchers who count to three and step back are always safe.

stages.name: Pirannox
stages.bio: Pirannox is a terrifying sight - a massive teal-green fish armored with jagged ice-blue crystal spines along its back and a gaping maw of interlocking serrated teeth as wide as a child is tall. Its body is thick and muscular, and the cold dark water of Ghost Hollow steams faintly where it moves. The crystal spines conduct dark energy that radiates outward like cold fog. Ancient maps of Ghost Hollow mark one pool simply as 'Pirannox - do not fish.' The guardians say a Pirannox once held its territory unchanged for three hundred years, and that marks carved into its territory-stones stay sharp forever, preserved by its chill.
stages.note: The temperature of Ghost Hollow's water drops exactly two degrees every time a Pirannox bares its teeth fully.

stages.name: Plumling
stages.bio: Plumling is a tiny round fluffball of soft pink feathers with two enormous round eyes that take up most of its face. A small yellow beak peeks out from the fluff, and its stubby wings are barely visible under all the downy plumage. It lives in the lowest spire crannies of the Dragon Spire, puffed up against the wind. When the spire's updrafts kick in at dawn, Plumling tucks its wings in and lets itself tumble upward like a pink dandelion seed - shrieking happily the whole way. Dragon Spire climbers carry Plumlings in their pockets because the little owlets sneeze out a burst of warm air that rekindles frost-bitten fingers.
stages.note: A Plumling sneezes precisely twelve times every hour - and the thirteenth sneeze always smells faintly of lightning.

stages.name: Plumwing
stages.bio: Plumwing stands upright on two taloned feet, its pink-and-gold feathers now arranged in neat layered tufts. Ear-tufts have grown from the top of its head like small horns, and its amber-gold eyes are sharp and focused. The wings have filled out into broad, capable fans edged with flight feathers. It perches on the Dragon Spire's mid-level ledges and watches the skies for hours, rotating its head nearly all the way around when something catches its interest. When Plumwing opens its wings fully and catches a spire updraft, it can sail upward for half a minute without a single wingbeat, eyes fixed on some distant point only it can see.
stages.note: Plumwing can identify any word spoken in the wind from half a mile away, rotating one ear-tuft toward the sound like an antenna.

stages.name: Plumarch
stages.bio: Plumarch is a magnificent wing-spread owl creature whose pink-and-gold plumage blazes with bioluminescent patterns in full flight. Its wings are enormous, each primary feather edged with a warm golden glow that illuminates the spire's fog. The ear-tufts have grown long and swept back, giving it a crowned look, and its golden eyes see through both dark and storm. It is the Dragon Spire's living lantern - explorers lost in the high crags need only look for the moving glow of a Plumarch's wings to find their way back to the paths. The guardians say Plumarch is the only creature that has ever sat on the spire's highest point and looked across all four regions at once.
stages.note: The glow of Plumarch's wing-edges brightens whenever a name it has never heard is spoken in the spire's ancient guardian language.

stages.name: Plumchick
stages.bio: This Plumchick is a round, downy green-and-yellow chick with a small orange beak and bright curious eyes. Its plumage is the color of fresh spring leaves, soft and ruffled in every direction. It clings to the Gale Ridge's sheltered ledge-nests with oversized yellow feet, letting the gale winds ruffle its feathers without ever losing its grip. It chatters constantly - a rapid quiet clicking - and stuffs seeds and leaf fragments into cracks in the rock wall, rarely finding them again later. The Gale Ridge's howling winds seem to carry its tiny voice for remarkable distances.
stages.note: Plumchick stores at least thirty seeds a day but retrieves fewer than five - the rest sprout into small cliff-plants that line the spire paths.

stages.name: Plumawk
stages.bio: Plumawk has the look of a confident young raptor - its green-and-yellow body now lean and strong, with long tail feathers and a proud crest of spiky head feathers. Its hooked beak is sharp and its talons are built for gripping storm-tossed branches. It glides the Gale Ridge's wind columns effortlessly, reading the gusts the way a river fish reads currents. It is notorious for snatching star-charts from trainers and carrying them to the top of tall trees, then screaming down at the trainers as if it's helping them learn. Despite this, its navigational instincts make it invaluable to spire explorers.
stages.note: Plumawk always glides in the exact direction of the next safe landing point - even in zero-visibility storms, its course is flawless.

stages.name: Aeroplume
stages.bio: The Guardians say that Aeroplume once turned Abalont's shadow-storm away from the Ridge by flying directly into it and screaming until the storm broke.
stages.note: The trailing crest feathers of an Aeroplume drop one feather per decade - each feather, planted in soil, grows into a storm-tree.

stages.name: Fluffyx
stages.bio: Fluffyx is a perfectly round purple fluffball with two tiny wide eyes peering out and stubby little orange feet. Its entire body looks like a pom-pom that rolled through a lavender bush. Despite its impractical shape, it rides the Psychic Temple's gentle updrafts by fluffing itself even larger, turning its whole body into a living balloon. It drifts from tree to tree, landing with a soft bounce. Fluffyx has an odd habit of staring at a chosen spot in the temple for minutes on end, eyes going distant - the light-temple keepers say it is watching the psychic currents that run like invisible rivers through the trees.
stages.note: Fluffyx's feathers rise and fall in sync with the Psychic Temple's ambient psychic current - it's used as a living barometer by temple-keepers.

stages.name: Plumox
stages.bio: Plumox stands tall and sharp, its purple-and-brown plumage now fully aerodynamic. A fierce hooked beak and bold yellow eyes give it the look of a veteran aerial hunter. Its chest is broad and its talons are curved and ready. It perches on the highest the Psychic Temple canopy branches and watches everything below with an eerie stillness - only its eyes move. When it decides to take flight, the launch is instantaneous: a single powerful stroke and it is already gone into the tree-tops. Plumox uses its psychic sensitivity to track the exact trajectory of prey or enemies before they move, always arriving a half-second before they expect.
stages.note: Plumox can predict where a falling leaf will land three seconds before it hits the ground, then sit exactly on that spot.

stages.name: Aetherclaw
stages.bio: Its eyes glow with a deep amber psychic light, and when it opens them fully, loose pages on nearby tablets lift and hang in the air like slow snow. Ancient temple-keepers say Aetherclaw was the first creature ever to carry a message to the Guardians, and that it has never once lost one.
stages.note: When Aetherclaw spreads both wings fully, loose pages on nearby stone tablets settle themselves into a neat stack.

stages.name: Pluvling
stages.bio: Pluvling is an endearing small axolotl with a round white-lavender body and a frill of purple-blue feathery gill-fans spread wide around its head. Four tiny legs and a flat tail help it waddle along the poison marsh's shallower edges. Its large eyes are pale and attentive, taking in everything. The gill-fans pulse gently with a faint psychic glow when it concentrates, which it does often - usually while staring at reflections in the water. Despite living in the poison marsh, its own body stays pristine because a thin psychic field filters out all marsh toxins before they reach its skin. The marsh's other creatures leave it alone, recognizing that aura.
stages.note: Pluvling's gill-fans change from purple to blue whenever it detects a lie being told within five meters of the water.

stages.name: Pluvian
stages.bio: Pluvian's body has grown longer and more graceful, its pale lavender-white sides patterned with subtle blue-purple striping. The feathery gill-fans are now wider and more elaborate, flowing back along its neck in sweeping fronds. Four stronger legs let it move easily between water and damp marsh-earth. It moves with an unhurried patience through the poison marsh, using its psychic senses to map the currents flowing under the surface. Pluvian leaves faint glowing trails in the marsh water behind it - marsh-keepers say these trails last six hours and mark safe passage routes through the toxic waterways.
stages.note: The glowing trail a Pluvian leaves in marsh water can be followed safely for exactly six hours before fading - not a minute more.

stages.name: Pluvarch
stages.bio: Pluvarch is a beautiful and alien presence in the poison marsh - its long axolotl body is covered in intricate purple-and-white feather-fin fronds that fan out all along its back and sides, each tipped with a soft glow. Its four legs are elegant and sure-footed on both land and shallow water. Pale psychic light radiates from its entire body, pushing the marsh's toxic haze back in a gentle sphere around it. It rarely speaks, but when it does, its voice carries across the whole marsh as a clear crystalline vibration that resolves into meaning rather than sound. The guardians of the poison marsh believe Pluvarch knows the true name of everything in the marsh, and that saying those names aloud could purify the entire region.
stages.note: A Pluvarch that has lived thirty years will have turned every toxic plant within a ten-meter radius into a medicine herb.

stages.name: Posskit
stages.bio: Posskit is a small round-bodied opossum-like creature with soft grey-white fur, a pointed snout, and a thin pink tail that curls at the tip. Its big round ears frame a face full of alert curiosity. It clutches a small golden orb in its front paws - a psychic focus-stone it found in a hollow log and has never let go of since. In Verdant Valley, Posskit is found in the song-trees, hanging by its tail from low branches and listening to the leaves talk. Its gold orb glows faintly when it hears a word it has never heard before, which in its first weeks happens almost every hour.
stages.note: Posskit's golden orb pulses once for every new voice it hears in a day - trainers count the pulses to track how far it has wandered.

stages.name: Possurge
stages.bio: Possurge has grown edgy and clever, its grey-brown fur now rougher and its posture upright and ready.
