The golden orb still hangs at its chest, but now it orbits in a slow arc around its body like a moon on a leash. Its long rat-like tail is fully prehensile, and it uses it to snatch objects from trainers mid-conversation. It sprints through the valley with low scuttling bursts followed by explosive leaps, zigzagging in ways that seem impossible until you realize it is reading the valley's wind currents with its psychic sense two seconds ahead of their arrival. Possurge never falls.
stages.note: Possurge has never once stumbled or dropped a held object in its life - researchers believe it psychically calculates each footfall in advance.

stages.name: Possemancy
stages.bio: Possemancy stands upright like a seasoned champion, its dark grey fur wild and electric, and multiple golden orbs now orbit its body in slow intersecting circles that crackle with psychic energy. Its long tail coils and uncoils with a life of its own, and its sharp eyes hold the amused patience of a creature that has seen everything twice. It can pluck words from the air - literally: Verdant Valley children report that after Possemancy passes, the word they were about to say appears visible in the air in glowing letters for three seconds before fading. The guardians call it the Memory-Keeper: it holds Akilla's last spoken word hidden somewhere in one of its circling orbs.
stages.note: The golden orbs orbiting Possemancy all stop moving simultaneously for exactly three seconds when it recalls a memory more than a century old.

stages.name: Primling
stages.bio: Primling is a compact little brown monkey with a tuft of fur that sticks straight up on its head and big round eyes full of mischief. It sits on its haunches and picks at the bug thicket's bark and leaf litter, finding hidden beetles and carrying them around for no clear reason. Its small hands are surprisingly dexterous and it uses them constantly - braiding grass, piling pebbles, sketching shapes in the dirt. Primling is drawn to old carvings on thicket trees and traces them with a careful finger before scampering away, as if storing the shape somewhere private.
stages.note: Primling traces every old carving it finds with one finger before moving on - and never traces the same carving twice.

stages.name: Simarch
stages.bio: Simarch has grown into a lean, knuckle-walking ape with an angular face and permanent scowl. Its brown fur is wild and unkempt, and it moves through the bug thicket with aggressive confidence, knocking aside roots and branches with its forearms. It communicates by hitting things rhythmically - two fast knocks means danger, three slow knocks means food. When challenged, it stands fully upright and beats its chest, which produces a surprisingly deep booming sound from such a lean frame. Bug thicket travelers who hear that sound know to move sideways, not back, because Simarch always charges straight.
stages.note: Simarch beats its chest exactly seven times before any serious charge - never six, never eight.

stages.name: Junglord
stages.bio: Junglord is an enormous shaggy primate wearing a heavy mantle of woven leaves and jungle vines draped across its broad shoulders like a living cloak. Its wide flat face is framed by a massive pale mane, and its knuckles are calloused into near-stone hardness. It sits at the center of the bug thicket and lets the forest reorganize itself around its position - vines thicken where it rests, roots rise to form a natural throne. It does not seek out battles but wins them instantly. The thicket's bug-creatures bring it tribute: the most interesting old carvings from the deepest trees, which Junglord studies one by one and never forgets.
stages.note: Junglord's vine-mantle grows exactly one new vine for every new friend it makes - the oldest vines at its collar are over forty years long.

stages.name: Primlet
stages.bio: Primlet is an orange-furred infant hanging from a vine with both small arms, big round eyes taking in the Psychic Temple below with wide-eyed wonder. Its arms are already disproportionately long compared to its small body, perfectly built for swinging. It makes soft cooing sounds when curious and clings to anything it can reach - trainers' sleeves, vine loops, the edges of star-charts. The light temple's psychic currents make its fur stand on end whenever it passes a particularly powerful light-tree, which it interprets as exciting rather than alarming. Primlet is the most trusting creature in the temple.
stages.note: Primlet will swing toward any glowing light-tree without hesitation - no fear, only curiosity, which the temple-keepers say is its greatest gift.

stages.name: Primorph
stages.bio: Primorph is a fully grown orangutan-build ape with a broad face, long red-brown arms, and powerful shoulders. It moves on all fours with a deliberate calm, and its orange-red fur is thick and textured. It no longer swings freely; instead it moves steadily through the temple, stopping to press its large flat hands against light-trees and closing its eyes. The psychic connection it makes in those moments leaves a faint warm handprint glow on the bark that lasts for hours. Primorph is patient with young creatures but firm - it will gently move aside any creature blocking a light-tree so that it can read it properly.
stages.note: Every handprint a Primorph leaves on a light-tree bark glows for exactly as many hours as the creature's age in years.

stages.name: Primachon
stages.bio: Primachon speaks rarely. When it does, temple-keepers write down what it said, because nothing Primachon has told anyone has ever turned out to be wrong.
stages.note: The orb atop Primachon's staff glows brightest when a child tries something difficult for the very first time.

stages.name: Prisect
stages.bio: Prisect is a tiny bright-green mantis with outsized triangular eyes and a small shining blue crystal gem embedded in its chest like a jewel. Its six legs are slender and precise, and its two forearms are held in the classic folded-prayer mantis pose at all times. Small translucent wings lie flat along its back. The crystal in its chest pulses with a slow psychic light when it focuses, which it does frequently while standing completely motionless, watching a single point in the bug thicket for minutes. Young trainers say that Prisect is either thinking very deeply or has simply forgotten what it was doing - the effect is identical.
stages.note: The crystal on Prisect's chest glows brightest when it is looking at something invisible to everyone else in the thicket.

stages.name: Vitralis
stages.bio: Vitralis has grown into a tall, angular green mantis with two pairs of transparent wings spread in a permanent display stance. Its forelegs are now long serrated blades that it holds at chest height, and the crystal gem has grown to cover a larger patch of its thorax. It moves with extreme deliberation - each step tested, each pose held - yet when it decides to strike, the movement is invisible to the naked eye. It occupies the middle canopy of the bug thicket, and smaller creatures instinctively give it wide berth. Vitralis uses its psychic senses to replay lessons it has observed and shares them with the thicket's young insects by projecting them as crystal-clear mental images.
stages.note: Vitralis can project a full three-minute psychic lesson-replay into any creature that makes direct eye contact with it.

stages.name: Iridoptera
stages.bio: Iridoptera is a striking and alien-looking mantis of crystalline blue-green, its body now largely translucent with glowing internal light visible through its carapace. Four enormous iridescent wings fan out behind it, each layered with hundreds of prismatic cells that scatter light into color clouds. Its blade-forearms are longer and more precise than ever, held in a permanent ready stance. It stands still for hours at the thicket's highest reaches, then vanishes between wingbeats. The bug thicket's oral history says that Iridoptera was the first creature to decode the psychic language of the guardian song-trees, and that its wing-patterns are actually a written record of every voice ever raised in the thicket.
stages.note: If you photograph Iridoptera's wing pattern and enlarge it, each cell contains a different word from the ancient guardian language.

stages.name: Prisma
stages.bio: Prisma is a chunky iridescent grub with a segmented body that shimmers with soft rainbow colors - purple, blue, pink - as it inches along. Its face is dominated by a single enormous round eye that reflects the whole world in its surface. It moves with a slow rolling undulation across leaves and bark, leaving a faintly shimmering trail. When it finds a spot it likes, it curls into a tight loop and pulses gently, broadcasting a soft psychic contentment that makes nearby creatures feel briefly peaceful. Verdant Valley children consider finding a Prisma grub in their garden to be a sign that good things are coming.
stages.note: Wherever a Prisma rests for more than one night, the surrounding grass grows into a perfect circle of richer, brighter green.

stages.name: Prismoll
stages.bio: Prismoll has encased itself in a floating crystalline shell that hovers a few centimeters above any surface. The chrysalis is shaped like a rounded diamond, its faceted surface reflecting light into brief spectrum flashes. It has no visible eyes, legs, or mouth in this stage, and seems barely alive - yet it is wildly active internally. Psychic observers report that the interior of a Prismoll chrysalis is filled with thousands of luminous sound-fragments from everything Prisma ever absorbed, being rearranged and woven into something new. Verdant Valley explorers are told never to shake, tap, or shout near a Prismoll: it may be dormant, but it is listening to everything.
stages.note: Prismoll's crystal shell plays back the last sound it heard in the valley whenever the valley goes completely silent.

stages.name: Prismagnis
stages.bio: Prismagnis has emerged from its chrysalis as something extraordinary - a sleek, angular insect with a smooth pale body and four enormous prismatic wings that scatter light into color storms wherever it flies. Its dark eyes are multifaceted and seeing, its six legs light and sure. It moves through Verdant Valley in low buzzing circuits, and where its wing-shadow passes over the hand-carved stones, the letters briefly lift and float in colored light before settling again. Children chasing its light-reflections often find they have followed it to the exact memory-stone they most needed to study. The guardians say Prismagnis remembers every voice ever raised in the valley and can return them to whoever lost them.
stages.note: Prismagnis always lands on the memory-stone containing the word the closest child has been struggling most to learn.

stages.name: Prismite
stages.bio: Prismite is a tiny pale round-bodied moth-butterfly with oversized white wings marked by a single round eyespot on each. Its two long antennae curve outward like question marks, always quivering. It drifts through the crystal mines' lower chambers on barely-there wingbeats, drawn toward any facet of quartz that refracts light. When a crystal catches the mine-light and splits it into colors, Prismite freezes mid-air, antennae spread wide, absorbing the spectrum. Mine-workers who see a Prismite hovering in a dark passage say there is always a hidden gem-vein behind the wall at that exact point.
stages.note: Prismite hovers motionless for exactly as many seconds as the number of gem-facets in the crystal it is studying.

stages.name: Luminyx
stages.bio: Luminyx has taken on a more otherworldly form - its body now a luminous blue-white orb hovering within a halo of diaphanous wings that blur with motion. Two long curved horns sweep back from its head, and trailing light-tendrils drift behind it wherever it moves. It barely touches the mine floor, preferring to hover at head height and study the faces of creatures it meets. When it focuses its large dark eyes on you, there is a sensation of being read - every memory you carry floating to the surface of your mind like bubbles. Luminyx is the living map of Crystal Mines' deepest echo chambers.
stages.note: Looking into Luminyx's eyes for ten seconds causes any forgotten word to surface in your memory, clear and complete.

stages.name: Chromalith
stages.bio: Chromalith is breathtaking - a massive butterfly with wings that contain every color simultaneously, each cell a living prism that refracts light into shifting spectra. Its purple-and-gold body is jeweled with crystal nodules, and its long trailing hindwings sweep the ground like a ceremonial robe. In flight, it leaves a corridor of prismatic light that lasts for hours. The crystal mines go quiet when Chromalith enters: every gem, every facet, every crystal vein begins to pulse in sync with its wingbeat. The guardians say Chromalith is the mines' memory-keeper - that each color in its wings represents a different kind of knowing, and that it has never once forgotten a single thing since it hatched.
stages.note: Every color shift in Chromalith's wings corresponds to a different mood of the mines - scholars have counted forty-seven distinct hues.

stages.name: Prismule
stages.bio: Prismule is a compact, fluffy white foal with a short purple-tipped horn spiraling from its forehead and a full purple mane and tail that are already longer than its legs. Its large blue eyes are wide with the unfiltered wonder of a creature that has just discovered the world. It trots through the crystal mine's upper galleries on small sure hooves, knocking its horn gently against gem-veins and giggling - a psychic chime sound - when they ring. The mine-keepers say Prismule's touch never dulls a crystal but always brightens it, as if the foal is returning something the stone forgot it had.
stages.note: Every crystal Prismule touches with its horn glows ten percent brighter for the rest of its life.

stages.name: Prismalin
stages.bio: Prismalin stands gracefully in the crystal mines, a full-grown unicorn with a long flowing purple mane and tail, and a spiraling horn of pale crystal that casts rainbow light on the cave walls. Its white coat is luminous, lit from within. It moves with measured elegance, choosing its path deliberately through the narrow mine passages, its hooves ringing on the stone floor like struck bells. When it lowers its horn to a child's eye level, the light it casts temporarily illuminates words on any scroll or tablet nearby in their original intended meaning - clearer than any printed page. Mine-keepers say it visits the deepest memory-vaults once a month and reads everything inside.
stages.note: Prismalin's horn illuminates words in the exact color corresponding to their emotional meaning - warmth words glow gold, difficult truths shine blue.

stages.name: Prismarcy
stages.bio: Prismarcy is a vision of pure radiance - a magnificent unicorn whose coat has deepened to brilliant white-gold, its mane and tail now flowing in every color of the spectrum simultaneously: red, gold, green, blue, violet, all shifting and blending as it moves. The horn is long, faceted like a cut diamond, and blazes with psychic light bright enough to read by a mile away. Its hooves leave glowing prints on the mine floor that fade after one hour, but while they remain, they mark the safest path through every crystal passage. Ancient mine-records describe Prismarcy as the guardian who first taught the crystal mines' creatures to speak, by shining its horn on the walls and turning gem-veins into letters.
stages.note: The prints Prismarcy leaves in the mine dust spell out, letter by letter, the most important word any reader nearby needs that day.

stages.name: Pryxling
stages.bio: Pryxling is a chunky, angular violet-grey insect with a compact rounded body plated in thick stone-textured shell segments. Its four limbs end in strong gripping claws, and its small compound eyes are deep violet. It scuttles along the light grove's stone borders, wedging itself into rock crevices and blending in almost perfectly with the grey-purple lichen. When something approaches, it freezes solid - not just still, but truly rigid, like a rock. Grove visitors have sat down on a Pryxling thinking it was a comfortable boulder, only to have it suddenly skitter away. This extreme stillness is a genuine psychic trick: its nervous system actually pauses to avoid detection.
stages.note: Pryxling can hold perfect stone-still for up to four hours - grove-keepers mark known Pryxling 'rest spots' with chalk so visitors don't sit on them.

stages.name: Praxion
stages.bio: Praxion stands tall and bipedal, its purple-grey carapace now sharp-edged and crystal-faceted. A wide flat head and enormous compound eyes give it a commanding presence, and its two bladed forearms are edged with natural stone-crystal that can chip granite. It carries a large kite-shield of solid stone as its left arm-guard. Praxion patrols the light grove's stone outcroppings with methodical sweeps, leaving parallel scratch marks in the rock as territory signs. It is a dutiful creature: if it adopts a trainer, it will stand between them and any threat without hesitation, shield raised, and refuse to move until the danger is gone.
stages.note: Praxion's stone shield has never been successfully broken - researchers estimate it has blocked over three hundred strikes without a crack.

stages.name: Pryrarch
stages.bio: Pryrarch is an imposing bipedal insect-warrior whose entire body has crystallized into angular purple-violet stone plates. Four swept-back wing-blades extend from its back like frozen lightning-strikes, purely decorative now but razor-edged. Its head is a broad armored plate with deep-set glowing violet eyes, and its limbs end in heavy crushing claws. It stands at the stone gates of the light grove like a living wall, motionless for weeks at a time, then moves with sudden frightening speed when needed. The guardians say Pryrarch was the first creature to defend the light grove against Abalont's initial advance, and that the deep gouges in the grove's stone gate-posts are its claw-marks from that battle.
stages.note: The claw-gouges Pryrarch carved into the grove's stone gate-posts have not eroded at all in the centuries since the first battle.

stages.name: Psibab
stages.bio: Psibab is a small psychic monkey wreathed in drifting violet wisps that brighten whenever it hears something it has never heard before, briefly holding a shape in the air before dissolving. The temple-keepers say every Psibab is born already certain of exactly one thing - and never the same thing twice.
stages.note: Every Psibab arrives already certain of one thing - no two have ever been born certain of the same one.

stages.name: Psihowl
stages.bio: Psihowl is a powerfully built orange-red gorilla that moves through the light temple on its knuckles with confident weight. Its broad muscular body is plated with natural purple psychic-energy tattoo-like markings that glow when it concentrates. It pauses often, pressing both fists into the earth and closing its eyes - a meditation posture that lets it read the light temple's psychic root-network from below. It communicates with other creatures through projected feelings rather than sound, though when it does vocalize, the sound is felt in the chest. Psihowl has memorized every light-tree in the temple by the texture of the root it grows from.
stages.note: Psihowl identifies every light-tree in the temple by feel alone - blindfolded, it can navigate to any specific tree by tracing its root through the soil.

stages.name: Psikanth
stages.bio: Psikanth sits in the deepest heart of the light temple with its back straight and its powerful fists resting on its knees, surrounded by swirling rings of violet psychic fire. Its white-silver fur radiates an electric calm, and purple flame burns steadily in each clenched fist without consuming them. It meditates constantly, but its eyes are open - it watches the temple even while its mind traverses its root-network. When it stands, the air pressure in the temple changes measurably. It is one of the few creatures that Abalont's shadow has never been able to approach: the psychic field emanating from Psikanth's meditation is a ward that has held without interruption since the guardians first fell.
stages.note: The psychic fire in Psikanth's fists burns precisely as bright as the collective unspoken knowledge of every creature currently in the temple.

stages.name: Pteryx
stages.bio: Pteryx is a small tan-gold bat creature with a round compact body, wide leathery wings folded against its sides, and enormous round eyes that catch every flicker of lava-light. Two small pointed ears sit at the top of its round head, and its toothy little grin is both unsettling and charming. It lives in the lava crater's high cliff-niches, hanging upside-down in groups and chattering. When startled, it launches into the air with a surprised squeak and circles back immediately to reinvestigate the source of the fright. Lava crater climbers say Pteryx will follow a warm lantern for hours, mistaking it for a particularly interesting volcanic vent.
stages.note: Pteryx always lands back on the same exact rock niche it launched from, within two centimeters, no matter how far it flew.

stages.name: Pterygon
stages.bio: Pterygon has grown into a lean, two-legged wyvern with long membranous wings, a long neck, and a narrow flat-skulled head full of sharp teeth. Its gold-tan scales have a subtle metallic sheen, and its hind legs are strong enough to launch it vertically from a standing start. It glides the lava crater's thermal columns for hours without landing, banking on outstretched wings with confident elegance. Its dark eyes see equally well in full sun and crater-dark. Pterygon is possessive of its thermal columns and will chase any other flying creature out of its territory with sharp snapping dives, pulling away at the last possible moment every time.
stages.note: Pterygon memorizes the shape of every thermal column in its territory and adjusts its glide by a single degree whenever one changes.

stages.name: Drakopteryx
stages.bio: Drakopteryx is a full dragon of the lava crater - broad-shouldered, four-limbed with massive leathery wings, and a head crowned with swept-back crests and fang-flanked jaws. Its gold-brass scales are heavy and layered, and the darker patches on its flanks and wing-membranes absorb volcanic heat and radiate it back as shimmering waves. When it beats its wings on takeoff, loose rock pellets are thrown hundreds of meters. The lava crater's oldest record describes Drakopteryx as the dragon that sealed Abalont's first passage through the crater by breathing a column of superheated air into the vent and collapsing it. The vent is still sealed. The record notes it never needed to do it again.
stages.note: Drakopteryx has sealed every unstable volcanic vent in its crater territory with a single breath - geological surveys confirm none have reopened.

stages.name: Puppoxling
stages.bio: A tiny carved wooden puppet no bigger than a lantern, Puppoxling dangles from two red strings that rise into the shadow-cave darkness - nobody has ever seen what holds them. Its round beaked face blinks with wide curious eyes, and it knocks its stubby wood-block limbs together when startled, making a hollow tock-tock sound that echoes through the tunnels. The guardians once believed these strings were the vines of a sleeping cave plant reaching down, weaving its first shape from root and shadow.
stages.note: Puppoxling's strings always point toward the deepest part of any cave, no matter how it turns.

stages.name: Puppoxid
stages.bio: Puppoxid's body has grown into a fully articulated humanoid marionette - jointed elbows, knees, and a neck that swivels silently. Its strings now number four and vanish upward into the cave ceiling like black roots in reverse. It moves with an unnerving smoothness, each limb swinging just a half-beat after the rest, as though something above is learning how to walk. In the shadow caves it patrols root-choked passages, drawn to the sound of spoken words, tilting its beaked head to listen.
stages.note: Puppoxid can stand perfectly still for six hours; trainers only notice it has moved when its shadow is in a different place.

stages.name: Marionox
stages.bio: Marionox is encased in burnished gold armor etched with vine-knot patterns, and a spired golden crown rises from its angular head. A sweeping purple cape hangs from its broad shoulders, catching the cave drafts like a sail. Its strings - now thick as rope - fan out in seven directions and hum a low note when it walks, as though the cave itself is the instrument. Ancient texts in the shadow caves call it the Hollow Sovereign, a puppet that grew large enough to pull its own strings.
stages.note: When Marionox spreads its cape fully, the shadows in the room rearrange themselves into shapes only children can see.

stages.name: Pymlox
stages.bio: A compact four-legged pup cloaked in deep darkness, Pymlox wears a wild crest of orange-red flame that flares around its face like a burning halo. Its paws leave faint scorch marks on hollow ground, and it moves fast - always darting between the ghost-hollow wisps as though chasing something only it can see. The guardians say it was born from an ember that fell into a ghost-flame candle and would not go out, stubborn and bright against the hollow's cold grey.
stages.note: Pymlox's fire-crest doubles in size whenever it hears a name it has never heard, then slowly settles back down as it thinks.

stages.name: Pyrmlox
stages.bio: Pyrmlox has grown into a powerful wolf-form with black armored plating along its back and shoulders. Its fire mane now blazes continuously, throwing orange light across the grey trees of ghost hollow. It walks with its head low and eyes fixed, and when it stops it becomes nearly invisible - the black armor blends into shadows while the fire mane flickers like a hollow lantern. It hunts the hollow for ancient lost words that have drifted away from their owners, carrying them back in its mouth like embers.
stages.note: Pyrmlox's pawprints always point toward wherever something has been forgotten, even if that thing was forgotten years ago.

stages.name: Pyrmloxar
stages.bio: Pyrmloxar is immense - a wolf of living fire and shadow with a blazing mane so vast it lights the entire hollow orange, turning even the ghostly mist warm for a moment. Its black-armored flanks bear the scorch-marks of every battle it has survived, and its eyes burn with ancient patience. The hollow's wandering spirits give it a wide path. It is said that when Abalont's darkness pressed heaviest against the guardians, an Pyrmloxar stood at the hollow's edge for forty nights without sleep, its fire-mane burning until dawn.
stages.note: Pyrmloxar's mane burns coolest in the exact spot where a forgotten name is spoken aloud for the first time again.

stages.name: Sparakeel
stages.bio: Sparakeel is a scrappy little biped with vivid orange plumage spiking from its head like a tiny flame-crest, and clawed feet it stamps in the sand with great confidence. Though no bigger than a boot, it puffs its chest and tilts its head side to side whenever it encounters something new, sizing up the world with bright round eyes. Sand dune travelers say you can find a Sparakeel by following tiny three-toed prints in the morning dunes - it circles whatever new thing it found overnight, studying it from every angle.
stages.note: Sparakeel practices its crest-spike display at sunrise each day, spreading each feather individually until satisfied.

stages.name: Blazekeel
stages.bio: Blazekeel stands upright like a warrior and runs in short explosive bursts across the dune faces, kicking up plumes of scorched sand. Its flame-crest has grown into a dramatic ridge of five bright spines, and its clawed hands glow orange at the knuckle when it is ready to fight. It patrols the heat-shimmer zones between dune ridges where mirages dance, and the guardians say it can tell the difference between a real word and a trick-sound at fifty paces just by the heat it throws.
stages.note: Blazekeel always runs in zigzag bursts - it says straight-line running is for creatures with no imagination.

stages.name: Infernakeel
stages.bio: Infernakeel is a towering bipedal dragon-beast, broad-shouldered and thick with orange-gold scales, its flame-crest now a blazing crown of seven great spines that glow like molten metal in the desert sun. Each step shakes the sand flat for a meter in every direction, and it roars with a sound that rivals the dune-wind. It has guarded the sand dunes since the age when the guardians first mapped the desert, and every young Sparakeel in the region knows its silhouette as the shape of courage.
stages.note: The seven crest-spines of Infernakeel each glow a different temperature, ranging from deep red at the base to white-gold at the tip.

stages.name: Scorpling
stages.bio: Scorpling is a small sandy-tan scorpion with eight nimble legs and a curved tail tipped with a single glowing ember-spark. It scurries between sun-warmed rocks in the amber desert, clicking its pincers together when curious. Despite its fierce posture it is shy; it buries itself up to its eyes in warm sand when frightened, with only the glowing tail-tip visible - which, unhelpfully, makes it easier to find. The guardians prize these little creatures because they always signal the direction of water with a tail-point.
stages.note: Scorpling taps out a rhythm with its front two legs before speaking, like a tiny drum-roll introduction.

stages.name: Pyrosting
stages.bio: Pyrosting has shed its sandy coloring entirely for a deep orange-red shell that radiates heat you can feel from two steps away. Flames lick along its tail and cascade over its pincers like living gauntlets. In the amber desert's scorching afternoons it is almost invisible against the hot rock faces, only betrayed by the shimmer above its shell. It communicates in patterns of flame-pulses from its tail - three quick pulses mean danger, one slow pulse means food - a language the desert hawks have learned to read.
stages.note: Pyrosting can extinguish its flame completely in under a second when threatened, dropping into total stillness and appearing as plain rock.

stages.name: Pyraclaw
stages.bio: Pyraclaw is enormous by any desert measure - a scorpion the size of a boulder wreathed in orange flame from claw-tip to tail-stinger, leaving a trail of glass-fused sand wherever it treads. Its pincers glow white at the grip point, and the flame-aura around its tail can be seen from the far dune ridges on clear nights. Ancient desert guides mark its territory on their maps with a simple sun-spiral symbol, meaning: show respect and speak clearly. Pyraclaw has never harmed a creature that answered its riddle correctly.
stages.note: Every ten years Pyraclaw sheds its shell in the deepest amber-crater; the old shell becomes a hollow that small desert creatures nest in.

stages.name: Emberspire
stages.bio: Emberspire is a small brown cobra coiled on warm rock, its wide hood fanned out and its round eyes gleaming with new-fire curiosity. It cannot yet breathe flame but its scales are warm to the touch and radiate gentle heat. In the lava crater's outer rock fields it rides warm updrafts coiled around boulders, swaying its upper body to sense vibrations from deep below. The guardians say Emberspire hatches already knowing three words - the names of the three crater vents - and repeats them softly to itself while it grows.
stages.note: Emberspire chooses exactly the same warm boulder to sleep on each night; if moved, it returns within the hour.

stages.name: Infernal
stages.bio: Infernal rears up tall, its hood now bearing two small dragon-like horns curved back from its skull, and a tongue of pure fire flickers at its mouth. Its golden scales pulse orange-warm, and when it spreads its hood the heat can be felt across the crater platform. It guards the lava crater's mid-ring - the zone where the rock is solid but the ground is always warm underfoot - coiling around hot-spring vents and hissing long slow warnings at anything that approaches uninvited. Skilled trainers say its fire-tongue can taste the temperature of words.
stages.note: Infernal always flicks its fire-tongue exactly seven times before striking, which experienced trainers use to their advantage.

stages.name: Blazehydra
stages.bio: Blazehydra is a colossus - a fire-crowned cobra whose flame-mane blazes in a great sunburst ring around its raised head, visible from every lookout point in the lava crater. When it lifts its head fully from the crater floor the fire-halo scorches the rock ceiling, and lava pools ripple in response to its breathing. It is the oldest creature in the crater, older even than the guardians' first maps, and the lava itself is said to rise a full handspan whenever Blazehydra speaks aloud.
stages.note: Once every season Blazehydra dips its flame-mane into the main lava flow for exactly one minute; no one knows why it does not sink.

stages.name: Pyraxling
stages.bio: Pyraxling is a round, soft-looking purple dragon hatchling with big expressive eyes, stubby wings it flaps too fast to ever lift off, and a tail it curls around itself when nervous. Its small horns have barely sprouted from its forehead, and it squeaks when surprised. Found on the lower ledges of storm spire where the wind is gentlest, it hatches during thunderstorms and is so drawn to the sound of rushing air that it will walk directly into a gust with its wings open, delighted, no matter how many times the wind knocks it over.
stages.note: Pyraxling can predict storms twenty minutes early; its wingtips tremble slightly and it starts spinning in small circles.

stages.name: Pyraxon
stages.bio: Pyraxon's wings are now broad enough to catch real storm-currents, and it launches from spire ledges in long gliding sweeps, reading the updrafts with its pointed snout. Its purple scales have deepened to a violet-blue and its horns sweep elegantly back from its head. It can hover in place against a strong headwind without once flapping, adjusting only the tip angle of each wing. The storm spire's wind-channels are its training ground, and experienced Pyraxon can fly an entire circuit of the spire backwards to show off.
stages.note: Pyraxon lands on precisely the same perch every evening; it has worn a dragon-shaped groove into the stone over the years.

stages.name: Impedrax
stages.bio: Impedrax is a massive violet dragon that rides the uppermost spire thermals where no bird flies, its great bat-wings holding it still as a flag in a gale. When it dives, the resulting windshear flattens anything within thirty meters. Its deep-purple scales bear silver-grey wind-scars from centuries of flying through storm cores, and its eyes have turned pale silver from looking into lightning. The guardians gave it a name that means Ruler of High Winds, and every storm that passes over the spire is said to wait for Impedrax's permission.
stages.note: Impedrax's wingspan is exactly as wide as the widest gap in storm spire's upper arches, which is not a coincidence.

stages.name: Pyrrit
stages.bio: Pyrrit is a round, fluff-covered red bird that spreads its small wings wide and leans into the dune-wind as though daring it to move. A tiny red crest pokes from its forehead, and its whole body is the warm amber-red of a coal just cooling. It cannot fly yet but it runs across sand dunes at surprising speed, wings out for balance, making one quick screechy call every time it crests a dune - as though announcing its own arrival at the top. Sand dune travelers watch for them as signs of an upcoming afternoon wind.
stages.note: Pyrrit always positions itself at the very highest point of any dune, even if it has to run up and down three times to find it.

stages.name: Scorchawk
stages.bio: Scorchawk has grown into a proper hawk-form with wide feathered wings of deep orange-red and a sharp curved beak that glows at its tip. It rides the thermal columns that rise off the hot sand in the afternoons, barely flapping, circling in wide lazy spirals while scanning the dune faces below. Its feathers shed embers in a line when it banks hard, leaving a brief dotted trail across the sky. The dune-traders say if a Scorchawk circles your camp three times you will find water the next day.
stages.note: Scorchawk's flight feathers are heat-stiffened; they make a faint hissing sound when it folds its wings after landing.

stages.name: Infernix
stages.bio: Infernix spreads wings of pure fire-and-feather that span the width of a market stall, each primary flight-feather tipped with living flame that leaves orange ribbons in the sky on each wingbeat. It soars above the sand dunes on the hottest days when mirages ripple across the desert floor, and the shadow it casts is warm rather than cool. Ancient sand-dune lore says Infernix taught the first desert children how to read direction by watching where the fire-feathers bend in the wind, a lesson the guardians still pass on.
stages.note: When Infernix lands, the sand beneath its talons fuses into a tiny glass disc; it never lands in the same spot twice.

stages.name: Flickowl
stages.bio: Flickowl is a small teal-green owlet with one very large round eye set in a pale disc face, and soft feathers that graduate from teal-blue at the shoulders to warm orange at the wing-tips. It perches on the lower dragon spire ledges and swivels its head a full half-turn whenever a wind gust passes, tracking the sound with silent precision. At night it sits very still and blinks slowly, each blink sending a tiny ember-flicker from the orange feather-tips - local children call it the night-lantern owl and use it to light their way through the spire paths.
stages.note: Flickowl blinks exactly once per minute at rest; if it blinks twice in quick succession, something is watching from above.

stages.name: Embrawing
stages.bio: Embrawing has grown larger and fiercer, its teal-blue body now studded with feathers that have orange flame-tips that glow visibly in daylight. Its face is stern and its beak sharp, and it hunts the wind-channels of the spire with absolute silence - no wingbeat, no breath, nothing until the sudden snap of its talons. It nests in the hollows just below the spire's flame-vents, where the updraft is constant, and it can hover motionless in that updraft for hours. The dragon spire guides say it is the best teacher of patience of any creature in the region.
stages.note: Embrawing never blinks while in flight; its eyes stay wide and fixed on a point three seconds ahead of where it is.

stages.name: Infernowl
stages.bio: Infernowl is a great teal-fire owl whose wingspan fills the full width of the spire's upper arches when it spreads fully. Each wing-feather tip blazes with a permanent orange flame that never goes out, and when it rises on the spire thermals the feathers create a ring of moving fire that ancient maps mark as a navigation beacon. Its call carries across the entire dragon spire region on a still night. The guardians believe it was the creature that first taught the spire-dragons to use wind rather than fire alone, and the dragons have never forgotten.
stages.note: Infernowl's call always echoes back in a different pitch than it left, as though the spire is answering it.

stages.name: Embroot
stages.bio: Embroot is a round orange-red bulb sitting on a ring of dark volcanic rocks, with a crown of flaming orange petals-and-tendrils erupting from its top like a sunburst. It cannot move its body but it can rotate its flame-petal crown in a slow full circle, which it does whenever it senses something interesting approaching. The lava crater's youngest guides learn direction from Embroot clusters - the flame-petals always lean slightly toward the nearest active vent, no matter which way the surface wind blows.
stages.note: Embroot petals always point toward the nearest underground lava flow, even through fifty meters of solid rock.

stages.name: Lavamaw
stages.bio: Lavamaw has unfurled into a taller volcanic creature, its orange-red body now mounted on a rocky base and sprouting several long lava-tendril arms that wave and reach independently of each other. Each tendril glows at its tip and can probe the rock for heat or cracks. In the crater's mid-zone, Lavamaw tendrils sometimes grow up through rock fissures and surprise travelers who step on what looks like solid ground. The guardians use Lavamaw's fissure-sense to map the safest walking routes through the crater's unstable surface.
stages.note: Lavamaw extends its longest tendril in the direction of structural weakness, so miners follow its reach before striking with a pick.

stages.name: Infernoflora
stages.bio: Infernoflora has become a broad volcanic cone-creature sitting on a wide platform of hardened lava rocks, its multiple tendril-arms extended outward like the roots of a great fire-tree, each one thick as a beam. Its interior glows visibly through cracks in its rocky outer shell, and when it contracts its arms the lava inside pulses brighter. In the lava crater it is the anchor - the one creature that never moves, never needs to. The crater's entire ecology orbits it; even the youngest Embroot clusters lean toward it before they lean toward the vents.
stages.note: Infernoflora produces a low sub-frequency hum once every twelve hours; every living thing in a hundred-meter radius pauses for exactly three seconds.

stages.name: Embole
stages.bio: Embole is a compact round creature covered in overlapping lava-rock plates, dark brown with vivid orange cracks between every scale where inner heat glows. It hugs the ground at all times, stubby legs barely visible beneath its heavy shell, and rolls slowly across the granite heights with a sound like a bag of warm rocks. Despite looking completely armored, it is shy and tucks its head into its shell at any sudden noise. The granite heights' miners consider Embole a good-luck sign - finding one near a dig site means the rock face is warm and stable.
stages.note: Embole's shell-plates shift slightly every dawn, expanding as it warms, producing a faint tick-tick sound granite-heights children call the morning clock.

stages.name: Magmole
stages.bio: Magmole has grown into a proper pangolin-lizard with a spine-ridge of upright armor plates running from neck to tail-tip, and its lava-crack glow has intensified to a near-continuous orange shimmer across its sides. Four sturdy clawed legs carry it with surprising speed along the granite ridges, and it can dig through rock faces that would blunt a pickaxe in a single hour. The guardians discovered that Magmole tunnels always run true-north without any instrument - the creature uses the granite heights' geothermal gradient as a compass.
stages.note: Magmole's claws glow brightest just before it strikes rock, as though calling heat forward to soften the stone ahead.

stages.name: Infernole
stages.bio: Infernole is a massive low-slung armored beast, broad as a boulder and covered in thick volcanic plating that blazes with orange-lava cracks from head to tail. Its weight alone cracks the granite underfoot, and each step leaves a warm impression in the rock. When it lowers its head and charges the resulting tremor registers in the granite heights' crystal-monitors half a mountain away. Ancient tunnels in the heights were made by Infernole ancestors, and the current generation uses those same tunnels, slowly widening them year by year.
stages.note: Infernole's underside is cooler than its top; the stone it rests on stays warm for three days after it moves on.

name: Pyrcub

stages.name: Pyrcub
stages.bio: Pyrcub is a small lion cub with a tiny tuft of genuine flame where its mane should be, and an orange-tan coat that blends into the sun-baked dunes so well that only the flame-tuft gives it away. It bounds rather than walks, clearing small sand ridges in two easy leaps, and its tail-tip flickers with a tiny flame when it is pleased. In the sand dunes it follows older trainers at a respectful distance, watching everything they do before trying it - then attempting it with considerable confidence the next morning before breakfast.
stages.note: Pyrcub's flame-tuft produces exactly no smoke regardless of wind speed, which young naturalists have tested repeatedly.

stages.name: Pyrflare
stages.bio: Pyrflare has grown into a lean, fast lion with a proper fire mane blazing in orange and gold, and its movements carry the confident flow of a creature that has decided it owns the dunes it walks across. It runs against the wind whenever possible, mane streaming backwards in a ribbon of flame. Its growl can be heard across three dune ridges, and smaller creatures in the sand-dune region follow it to water with remarkable faith. The guardians say Pyrflare learned direction by watching stars - it is never lost.
stages.note: Pyrflare's mane burns brighter when it faces the wind and lower when it turns away; no one has figured out if this is deliberate.

stages.name: Pyrsovran
stages.bio: Pyrsovran is the great maned fire-lion of the sand dunes - a creature so regal it seems to make the desert quieter by entering it. Its blaze-mane is enormous, a full ring of living fire around its proud head that throws gold light across fifty meters of sand. It walks slowly because it has nowhere to be in a hurry, and every smaller creature in the dunes adjusts its own path to give it room. The guardians gave it a name meaning Sovereign of the Open Sand, and when the first children of the dunes were taught courage, they were told to think of Pyrsovran walking toward the sun.
stages.note: Pyrsovran's mane-fire casts no shadow; everything near it is simply bathed in uniform warm gold light.

blurb: Pyrcub wandered away from its family in the warm dunes. Help Pyrcub find the way back!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Hunter.
facts: Lions live in big families called prides.
A lion roar can be heard from far away.
question: What is a family of lions called?

stages.name: Emberspike
stages.bio: Emberspike is a dark reddish-brown creature with a back covered in short pointed quill-spines and bright clawed paws it uses to scramble confidently across granite faces. Its face is earnest and it holds its head slightly to one side, ears pricked, always listening. When threatened it puffs its spine-quills outward and stamps both front feet simultaneously - a behavior that looks more indignant than frightening but has deterred more than a few larger creatures. Granite-heights children keep Emberspike as a companion because it always shows up at mealtimes with impressive punctuality.
stages.note: Emberspike counts its own spines each morning by arching its back and feeling each tip with its nose; it has never miscount.

stages.name: Ignishard
stages.bio: Ignishard has lengthened into a four-legged stalker with a dramatic ridge of long quill-spines running from its shoulders to its haunches, orange-flame tipped at each point. Its orange-red coat is wiry and tough, and it moves low and fast across the granite ridges with its spine-ridge fanned. When it shakes its body all the spines rattle together, producing a sound that carries far in the mountains - a sound the guardians learned to recognize as a location signal when caught in granite-heights fog. It has perfected the art of looking irritated even when happy.
stages.note: Ignishard's spines are always cooler at the base and hotter at the tip; touching the base is safe, touching the tip is memorable.

stages.name: Magmafang
stages.bio: Magmafang is dark-orange and enormous - a wide, powerful creature with a back bristling with long heavy spines that glow ember-orange from their cores. Its open-mouthed roar shows a row of heat-glowing teeth, and the spines along its back shed small ember-sparks when it shakes. It is the guardian of the granite heights' upper pass, and has held that position for so long that the rock beneath its favored lookout has been polished smooth by its paws. Everything in the heights knows its sound; even the mountain winds seem to go quieter when Magmafang speaks.
stages.note: Magmafang has thirty-seven spines on its back; every one of them grew in during its first winter, one each night during the coldest storm.

stages.name: Embrowl
stages.bio: Embrowl is a tiny fluffy white-grey owlet so round it looks more like a snowball with eyes than a bird. Its large glowing orange eyes dominate its face, and small ember-sparks drift from its downy feathers at random - it cannot fully control the embers yet, which means it sets fire to small things near it when startled. Found on the low sheltered ledges of storm spire, it presses itself against warm rock and watches the world with unblinking orange intensity. Children at the spire say Embrowl is easy to find at night because it looks like a floating pair of orange lamp-eyes.
stages.note: Embrowl's ember-sparks are harmless at stage one, but they trace tiny shapes in the air that fade before anyone can make them out.

stages.name: Flamstryx
stages.bio: Flamstryx has shed its white down for vivid orange-gold feathers, and a crown of flame now burns permanently from the crest of its head. Its body is lean and powerful - more hawk than owl now - and its wings beat with a sharp crackle audible at twenty meters. It hunts the storm spire's wind-corridors where prey is scarce and skill is everything, learning to time its strikes between gust-pulses. The spire guides say Flamstryx can ride a vertical air column standing completely still, simply watching, for six hours without landing.
stages.note: Flamstryx's fire-crest changes color in different winds: orange in warm drafts, deep red in cold ones, white in storm-core gusts.

stages.name: Infernus
stages.bio: Infernus is a great golden-red bird of the highest spire peaks, wreathed in orange flame that streams from every primary feather as a living fire-trail when it flies. When it spreads its wings the thermal column beneath it heats fast enough to be felt on the ground far below. Its roar crosses the full spire valley. Ancient storm-spire maps show Infernus in the same position at the summit - wings spread, fire blazing - suggesting it has occupied the peak for longer than records exist. The storm that gave the spire its name was, by some accounts, Infernus deciding to stretch.
stages.note: Infernus leaves exactly seven ember trails in the sky during any single flight; never six, never eight.

stages.name: Smolsnek
stages.bio: Smolsnek is a small, round-headed orange-brown serpent with a tiny flame flickering at the end of its tail, which it curls protectively inward when resting. Its eyes are large and bright, and it sways in a slow S-curve when alert - a habit that desert traders find either charming or unsettling depending on their experience with fire serpents. It lives in the warm pockets between amber desert rock formations, coiling into tight spirals to sleep. Children who encounter one are surprised by how soft its scales feel, which is not a feature it appreciates being commented on.
stages.note: Smolsnek's flame tail never flickers in wind but always flickers when it is being watched, as though showing off.

stages.name: Inferno
stages.bio: Inferno is a substantial orange-yellow serpent with a row of fire-spines and pointed frills erupting along the ridge of its body. It moves in long smooth waves that cross the desert floor faster than they appear, and the fire-frills glow brighter when it accelerates. In the amber desert it follows the subterranean heat channels beneath the surface, surfacing at points where the sand is hottest. Ancient maps mark these surfacing spots as landmarks - an Inferno will always appear at the same spot within two days of a desert sandstorm.
stages.note: Inferno's spine-frills each heat to a different temperature, and the total pattern of hot and cool frills is unique to every individual.

stages.name: Infernoviper
stages.category: Dragon Serpent of the Amber Waste
stages.bio: Infernoviper is a legendary desert serpent so large its full body can circle a small oasis when it coils. Dramatic fire-wings of living flame fan from its mid-section, and its tail blazes with a permanent torch-flame that serves as a beacon for lost desert travelers. When it rises above the dune horizon the surrounding sand vitrifies into amber glass in a ring beneath it. The guardians of the amber desert believe Infernoviper is the desert's own memory - that it has witnessed every sandstorm, every voice raised in the waste, since the desert was formed.
stages.note: Infernoviper's flame-wings never flap but they change orientation to indicate wind direction; desert pilots have used them as an instrument for generations.

stages.name: Sparkitail
stages.bio: Sparkitail is a small dark-red fox kit with one fluffy tail tipped in shadow-black and a coat the color of deep ember-red. It moves in short dashes, always close to the cave wall, pausing to sniff the dark carefully before darting to the next shadow. Its tail-tip doesn't glow - it absorbs light, making the space around it fractionally darker, which Sparkitail uses to hide in plain sight on dark cave floors. The guardians of the shadow caves leave small lights at their path junctions specifically because Sparkitail keeps snuffing them out to practice hiding.
stages.note: Sparkitail's tail-tip shadow-spot is exactly five centimeters across; experienced shadow-cave guides call it 'one tail-step' in the dark.

stages.name: Infernatail
stages.bio: Infernatail has grown into a lean dark-red wolf-fox with multiple spiked dark tails that radiate shadow around it, making it look larger than it is. Embers flicker in its fur when it runs, trailing brief sparks that extinguish immediately in the cave air. It hunts the shadow caves' mid-passages with unsettling expertise, vanishing into darkness between one step and the next and reappearing from a completely different shadow. The guardians say it never sleeps in the same shadow twice, cataloguing every dark corner of the caves in a memory that appears to be perfect.
stages.note: Infernatail can find every entrance and exit of any cave it has entered once, without fail, even years later.

stages.name: Novatail
stages.bio: Novatail is a massive dark-red multi-tailed beast with a dramatic ruff of dark-spiked fur around its neck and multiple great tails spread like a dark fan, each one tipped with living shadow. Ember-light pulses through its coat continuously, making it look like a creature built from cooling magma draped in night. In the shadow caves it is the apex presence - even the cave's own darkness seems to organize itself around Novatail, shadows pooling in its wake. The guardians call it the Keeper of What Is Hidden, believing it guards the secret language of the caves from those who would misuse it.
stages.note: Novatail's tails never all move at once; they rotate in a slow wave-pattern, each shadow momentarily lighting the next before going dark again.

stages.name: Pyrule
stages.bio: Pyrule is a small purple lizard hatchling with a row of orange flame-spines along its back and a thick tail it swings for balance. Its round amber eyes look slightly too large for its face, giving it a perpetually surprised expression it does not feel. It lives in the lava crater's outer cooling-stone zone, hopping between warm boulders and testing each new surface with its tongue before stepping on it. The guardians say Pyrule always picks the next word to learn by touching it with its snout - an instinct no one has fully explained.
stages.note: Pyrule's flame-spines each grow exactly one millimeter per week; its age can be measured by counting the spine-rows precisely.

stages.name: Pyrusaur
stages.bio: Pyrusaur stands bipedal now, its heavy purple body balanced on thick haunches and a long flame-tipped tail. Its flame-spines have grown dramatically, blazing orange from the nape of its neck to its tail-ridge, and its clawed hands glow warm. In the lava crater it runs along the inner lava-lip with surprising grace, using its tail as a counterbalance when it leans to look at the molten surface below. The guardians use Pyrusaur's spine-glow as a temperature gauge - the brighter the spines, the closer the underlying magma.
stages.note: Pyrusaur never puts both feet on the same rock at once; it always keeps one foot ready to push off in a new direction.

stages.name: Pyrusaurex
stages.bio: Pyrusaurex is a dark-purple bipedal dragon of tremendous build, its back blazing with a full ridge of towering flame-spines that form a crown of fire visible from the crater rim. Its tail is as long as its body and burns continuously at the tip, and each footfall shakes the cooled lava crust. The crater's most dangerous inner approaches are its territory - places where the rock surface is thin and no one else dares walk. It was the guardians' companion during the first crossing of the crater's center, and the path it walked is the only safe route still used today.
stages.note: Pyrusaurex's flame-spine crown changes from orange to deep white just before any volcanic event, giving thirty minutes of warning.

stages.name: Pyxlite
stages.bio: Pyxlite is a tiny round purple jellyfish drifting silently above the poison marsh's still surfaces, trailing four short tentacles and bearing a glowing lavender orb on its crown. It produces no sound and barely stirs the air it moves through. The marshland's toxic vapors pass right through it - ghost and fire both render the poison harmless to Pyxlite. Children of the poison marsh region are told to follow a Pyxlite through fog, as it always drifts toward clean air. Its crown-orb glows brighter near words spoken with kindness, dimmer near harsh ones.
stages.note: Pyxlite's tentacles never touch the marsh water; they hover exactly one centimeter above the surface at all times.

stages.name: Pyxaura
stages.bio: Pyxaura has grown into a larger jellyfish with a clearly visible flame burning inside its translucent dome body - a warm orange-gold fire that illuminates the bell from within like a paper lantern. Its tentacles have multiplied and lengthened, trailing through the marsh air. The inner flame casts a moving glow across the murky water below and the poison-ivy walls of the marsh. Marsh-travelers say Pyxaura's flame goes out if it passes over a place where a lie was told, and comes back brighter when it drifts over where a truth was spoken.
stages.note: Pyxaura's inner flame burns at exactly the same intensity day and night; the marsh appears brighter during the day only because Pyxaura is easier to see against dark sky.

stages.name: Pyxalith
stages.bio: Pyxalith has transformed into a breathtaking form - a golden-framed lantern encasing a brilliant fire, mounted within a spectral dome and ringed by heavy purple-gold tentacle-arms as thick as rope. Its golden frame bears inscribed symbols the guardians cannot fully translate, suggesting it predates the known history of the poison marsh. It drifts through the deepest marsh channels where no solid ground exists, and the flame at its center burns with a color that cannot be named - somewhere between orange and gold and something purely its own. The marsh itself grows quieter in its presence.
stages.note: The symbols on Pyxalith's golden frame change arrangement once per lunar cycle; scholars have been recording the sequence for ninety years without finding a repeat.

stages.name: Pyxling
stages.bio: Pyxling is a small blue lizard with yellow-gold dorsal spines running from its forehead to its tail-tip and a plump, round body it carries with casual dignity. Its four sturdy legs are all the same length, giving it a steady low-slung stance, and it regards everything with the calm interest of a creature that has decided it is in charge. In the sand dunes it digs shallow bowls in the warm sand and rests in them throughout the afternoon, spines catching the sunlight. The guardians gave it the family name that means first fire, and it carries this with obvious awareness.
stages.note: Pyxling's dorsal spines rattle gently in wind; each spine is tuned to a different frequency, making it a living wind chime.

stages.name: Pyxard
stages.bio: Pyxard has grown stocky and powerful with enlarged gold-tipped spines standing upright in a proud ridge along its back. Its blue scales are rougher now, scaled for desert abrasion, and its clawed feet leave deep imprints in hard sand. It is comfortable in both the scorching midday heat and the cold desert nights, and has been observed sleeping through sandstorms without moving, trusting its spine-ridge to deflect the sand. The dune-traders who cross the sand dunes regularly consider Pyxard a neutral figure in desert politics - one who watches everything and takes nobody's side.
stages.note: Pyxard never walks in a straight line; it always takes the path with the most shade, even if that path is three times longer.

stages.name: Pyxarion
stages.bio: Pyxarion is a magnificent blue dragon with gold-fire wing-spines that fan from its shoulders like a crown of radiating blades. Its broad-muscled body carries the marks of every desert crossing it has survived, and its amber eyes have seen the dune formations shift and re-form over centuries. When it spreads its golden wings the sand around it swirls in a corona, and the sound of its deep call crosses the entire dune basin. The guardians believe Pyxarion has memorized every voice ever raised in the sand dunes, which is why it is never surprised.
stages.note: Pyxarion's golden wing-spines are hollow; when wind passes through them at the correct angle they produce a note in perfect harmonic with the desert's own frequency.

stages.name: Pyxlet
stages.bio: Pyxlet is a compact dark-grey dragon hatchling with a stubby muzzle and yellow-gold spines emerging from its head and back like oversized thorns. Its body is sturdy and it plants itself on the ground with the confidence of a creature that already knows it will be large. Found at the upper mid-levels of dragon spire where the wind is strong and the light dim, it shelters in rock crevices and watches the upper storm with gold-tinted eyes. The guardians say Pyxlet hisses once per second when frightened and stops the instant the threat is gone - a useful clock in an emergency.
stages.note: Pyxlet's gold spines produce a faint sparkling shimmer in moonlight; spire children say finding one after dark is three times as hard as finding one in daylight.

stages.name: Pyxorn
stages.bio: Pyxorn is fully upright now, a dark-armored dragon with prominent gold-yellow spines and claws and a heavy tail. Its scales have deepened to near-black with a faint iridescent quality in strong light. It hunts the dragon spire's wind-exposed upper faces with unhurried patience - circling, watching, deciding. When it decides to move it moves very fast. The guardians say Pyxorn learned the spire's language of echoes before it learned to use its voice, meaning it could navigate the spire blindfolded by sound alone before any of the other spire dragons reached that skill.
stages.note: Pyxorn can hold its breath for nine minutes, a habit it developed stalking in the spire's low-oxygen upper caves.

stages.name: Pyxarchon
stages.bio: Pyxarchon is a great dark-black dragon of imposing presence, its gold-yellow spines blazing against its shadow-black scales and its wings spread to full width at the spire's summit. The contrast of gold-fire spine and black armor makes it look like a creature built from both night and sunlight simultaneously. Its roar sends reverberations through the spire's rock columns for minutes after it falls silent. The guardians say it is the keeper of the spire's oldest draconic carving - a set of thirty marks etched into the summit rock that only Pyxarchon understands fully, and that it sings to itself each sunrise.
stages.note: Pyxarchon's shadow is always larger than its actual body, regardless of the light source or angle; scholars have measured this repeatedly.

stages.name: Quilkin
stages.bio: Quilkin is a small green-brown pangolin-lizard whose overlapping scales have a mossy texture that blends perfectly with the crystal mine walls. Its large purple eyes stand out vividly against the earthy tones, giving it a look of perpetual alertness. It moves slowly, scale by scale, feeling the mine walls for vibration before committing to each step. The crystal mines' deep tunnels are its home, and it memorizes every crack and crystal cluster in its territory - explorers say if you follow a Quilkin rather than your map, you will never get lost in the mines.
stages.note: Quilkin's scales are slightly magnetic; small crystal fragments cling to its sides and it collects them deliberately, then drops them in specific spots.

stages.name: Quillvern
stages.bio: Quillvern has grown longer and heavier with enlarged crystal-studded scale armor that catches and refracts the mine lanterns into moving rainbow patches on the tunnel walls. Its purple eyes are keener now, able to see mineral veins in rock that experienced miners miss. When threatened it rolls into a tight scale-ball that no mine tool can dent and waits, perfectly patient, until the threat passes - which has taken as long as four days by some accounts. The crystal mines' deepest-level workers consider Quillvern a colleague rather than a creature, and it seems to agree.
stages.note: Quillvern taps the mine wall exactly three times before turning a corner - a habit the miners adopted and now use universally as a safe-passage signal.

stages.name: Quilarch
stages.bio: Quilarch is vast and low-slung - a pangolin the size of a small cart, armored in enormous overlapping crystal-rock plates that fracture light into prismatic fans across the mine ceilings. Its purple eyes glow with a faint inner light in the deepest tunnels where no lantern reaches. It walks the oldest mine passages at its own slow pace, and when it rolls into a ball every crystal in the surrounding area rings softly. The guardians believe Quilarch is the living memory of the crystal mines - that each scale it has grown carries the mineral signature of the exact tunnel it was formed in, mapping its entire life as a geological record.
stages.note: Quilarch's eldest scales are as hard as the mine's own crystal - researchers have been unable to mark them with any tool available in the region.

stages.name: Pricklet
stages.bio: Pricklet is a tiny, round-bodied hedgehog wrapped in a coat of cream-colored fur with stubby steel-tipped quills just beginning to push through its back. Its wide black eyes sparkle with curiosity and its small snout twitches constantly, smelling out the tiniest scraps of iron ore. In the Steel Fortress it scurries between wall-joints, collecting flakes of rust that it somehow works into its growing quills. Guardians say Pricklet once led young explorers to a hidden ore-seam by following its nose alone.
stages.note: Its tiny quills are still soft enough to bend - press one and it springs back like a spring wire.

stages.name: Shardine
stages.bio: Shardine's back is now bristling with long, sharp steel-grey quills that clatter softly when it walks. Its body has broadened and its legs are stout and sure-footed on rough stone. It patrols the lower ramparts of the Steel Fortress with a slow deliberate tread, pressing its broad snout against the walls to sense vibrations. When threatened it curls its head low and fans its quills outward in a rattling display. Engineers in the fortress have learned to follow Shardine when they hear its quills chime - it always finds the stressed beams first.
stages.note: When Shardine fans its quills, they hum a faint chord together - each quill tuned to a different pitch.

stages.name: Ironspike
stages.bio: Ironspike is a hulking armored beast whose back sprouts enormous bladed spines of dark metal, each one edged bright with ice-blue light at the tips. Its four legs are thick as gate-posts, and its glowing red eyes scan the fortress walls with cold authority. The ground trembles faintly when it stamps. Abalont's forces never broke through a wall that Ironspike guarded; its spines can splinter stone if swung with full force. The guardians carved its shape above every forge in the region as a promise: some things are built to last.
stages.note: Each of Ironspike's spines rings like a struck blade in cold air - the deeper the tone, the older the spine.

stages.name: Quilkit
stages.bio: Quilkit is a small, round hedgehog-like creature with tawny-brown fur and a back covered in short, stubby quills still capped with earthy grey tips. Its face is round and soft with tiny dark eyes and a button nose always dusted with grit. It roots through rubble piles in the Steel Fortress, pushing stones aside with surprising strength for its size. Guardians often find the tidiest rubble corners cleared overnight - Quilkit has organized them by weight, because it can tell the difference just by touch.
stages.note: Quilkit sorts stones by weight using only its paws, stacking lighter ones on top with near-perfect accuracy every time.

stages.name: Quillyx
stages.bio: Quillyx has grown stout and low-slung, its body now covered in long, densely packed grey-brown quills that overlap like roof slates. It moves with a quiet, rolling confidence, belly close to the ground. In the Steel Fortress it follows the scent of molten ore through ventilation shafts too narrow for larger guards. When it shakes itself, the quills click together in a rhythmic pattern that other Quillyxes recognize from great distances inside the fortress's echoing corridors. Even enemies hesitate before striking something that rattles like a bag of nails.
stages.note: Quillyx's quill-rattle changes tempo by mood - a slow beat means calm, a fast staccato means run.

stages.name: Ironquill
stages.bio: Ironquill is broad and low, its back a forest of heavy dark-steel quills with bright glowing tips that pulse red in low light. Its four legs are armored with layered plates, and its red eyes never blink. It patrols the deepest chambers of the Steel Fortress where memory-vaults are sealed, pressing its side against the doors to feel for vibrations. Nothing enters without its knowledge. Abalont once sent a dozen shadows at once to breach the vault; Ironquill spun in a circle so fast the quills became a spinning barrier of blades and held the line until dawn.
stages.note: When Ironquill spins its quills at full speed, the air between them screams like metal under a grinding wheel.

stages.name: Quilox
stages.bio: Quilox is a chubby little porcupine-shaped creature blanketed in lush green fur with clusters of leafy quills rising from its back, each tipped in a warm orange-red like a tiny ember. Its round face carries a cheerful fierce expression, dark eyes glinting above a tuft of green around its cheeks. In the Dark Forest it burrows under leaf piles and waits quietly until words drift close enough to chase. The guardians first noticed this line when the forest glowed faintly amber at night - little Quiloxes sleeping with their warm quills lit up like lanterns.
stages.note: On cold nights Quilox glows amber through leaf piles; forest travelers use the warm patches as impromptu campfire spots.

stages.name: Spinoquill
stages.bio: Spinoquill has grown thick and low, its body covered in overlapping green-tinged leaf-quills edged in blazing orange-red. It lumbers through the Dark Forest pushing through undergrowth with its broad snout, leaving a trail of gently scorched ferns. Its temperament is feisty - it stamps one forefoot when annoyed and fans its quills wide, releasing a warm waft of smoke. Travelers say the forest actually smells better where Spinoquill roams, because the small controlled singeing keeps the undergrowth from going too wild and lets unfamiliar names take root in cleared soil.
stages.note: Spinoquill leaves a trail of half-scorched leaves; forest children follow the path to find new clearings where rare plants grow fastest.

stages.name: Pyrequill
stages.bio: Pyrequill is massive and low-slung, its back erupting in a great crown of long leafy quills that burn continuously at their tips, casting shifting orange light across the forest floor. Its head is broad, its jaw powerful, and its body ripples with overlapping bark-tough hide. It moves slowly but never stops. In the Dark Forest it is said that Abalont once tried to freeze the region with endless shadow - Pyrequill walked a slow circuit through the deepest grove, and wherever its burning quills passed, the shadow thinned. It is the fire that lives inside the forest's green heart.
stages.note: Pyrequill's quill-flames never set the living forest alight - they burn only what is already dead or turned to shadow.

stages.name: Rambyx
stages.bio: Rambyx is a fluffy golden lamb with a single small curved horn just beginning to coil from its forehead. A bright green star-shaped mark glows on its brow, and its thick mane is the color of summer grass. It bounces through the Bug Thicket on four sturdy legs, nosing at every flower it passes and sneezing when insects tickle its muzzle. The thicket's giant beetles avoid it - somehow Rambyx always knows which leaf hides the most dangerous ones and steers its friends safely around. Even the wind seems to shift direction to keep pollen out of its face.
stages.note: The green star on Rambyx's brow brightens just before a gust arrives - local children use it as a three-second wind warning.

stages.name: Oviking
stages.bio: Oviking stands taller now, its golden mane flowing behind it in a permanent invisible wind even on still days. Two full curved horns spiral from its head, etched with faint green vein-lines. It has grown alert and purposeful, patrolling the tall-grass corridors of the Bug Thicket with its nose high and ears swiveling. When it runs, its hoofbeats are almost silent - the wind beneath its mane cushions each step. Travelers who get lost in the thicket's tangled maze say a flash of gold between the stems and a rush of warm air usually means Oviking has already found the way out.
stages.note: Oviking's hoofbeats are nearly silent at full gallop - the first sign it is near is the scent of cut grass on the air.

stages.name: Arcuron
stages.bio: Arcuron is a magnificent golden ram whose twin horns spiral into great arching loops wreathed in green light and woven with flowering vines. Its thick mane ripples with living grass, and emerald leaf-armor covers its flanks. When it walks, a gentle wind lifts from its hooves and stirs the canopy overhead. In the Bug Thicket it is both guardian and compass - creatures orient themselves by the direction of Arcuron's wind, and the thicket's ancient song-trees grow tallest in the ring where it rests. Abalont's shadows cannot enter a space where Arcuron breathes.
stages.note: The flowers woven into Arcuron's horns are never the same two days running - it chooses fresh ones every dawn without pulling a single stem.

stages.name: Ramkin
stages.bio: Ramkin is a plump, woolly cream-colored calf with a tiny grey nub of a horn pushing from its forehead. It wobbles across the granite ledges of the heights, planting each hoof with exaggerated care, always looking down at the rock before committing. A small grey cap-like stone formation seems to have grown into the fur between its ears, giving it a permanently studious look. Guardians of the heights say Ramkin is the only creature that never slips - it tests every stone with one hoof before trusting it, a habit the mountain seems to reward.
stages.note: Ramkin taps every stone three times before stepping on it - it has never once chosen a stone that crumbled.

stages.name: Ramnite
stages.bio: Ramnite has grown lean and sure-footed, its tawny hide darkening toward brown along the spine, and its two curved horns now fully formed - spiraling backwards from its brow with a satisfying weight. It navigates the crumbling cliff-paths of the Granite Heights with easy confidence, using its horns to probe crevices for handholds that bipeds cannot find. The wind up here is fierce, but Ramnite lowers its horns and pushes through with steady muscular strides. Travelers who earn its trust find it will stand broadside on the narrowest ledge, blocking the gust so they can pass.
stages.note: Ramnite will stand completely still for up to an hour as a windbreak for smaller creatures on exposed ledges.

stages.name: Titanhorn
stages.bio: Titanhorn is enormous, a barrel-chested ram clad in layered stone-grey armored plates that have grown from within its hide over decades. Its great sweeping horns are thick as a child's waist, trimmed with golden plate at the base, and it wears the scars of a hundred cliffside battles as proudly as a crown. It stands at the highest point of the Granite Heights each morning, and when it calls, the sound rolls down every valley below, so every creature in the region hears it wake. The guardians say that as long as Titanhorn's call echoes, the heights are safe.
stages.note: Titanhorn's morning call travels so far down the mountain that villages at the base use it as their wake-up bell.

stages.name: Rayvling
stages.bio: Rayvling is a small, round-bodied raven chick with deep violet-purple plumage, oversized blue eyes that glow faintly, and a beak already sharper than its size suggests. Its wings are still too short for proper flight - it hops and flutters between the hollow roots of Ghost Hollow, collecting shiny fragments it buries under bark. It is not yet afraid of anything and will walk right up to a shadow-wraith, tilt its head, and stare it down. The guardians say the hollow became a little less frightening the day the first Rayvling hatched, because something unafraid finally lived there.
stages.note: Rayvling hides one shiny object a day and will lead a patient friend directly to its entire buried collection if it likes them.

stages.name: Ravyx
stages.bio: Ravyx has grown into a proper raven, sleek and dark-purple with a tuft of ruffled feathers crowning its head and deep-set glowing blue eyes. Its wings are broad enough to carry it in long gliding arcs between the hollow's pale trees. It watches everything from high perches - tilting its head at the precise angle that means it is memorizing, not merely looking. In Ghost Hollow it acts as a messenger between the scattered guardians, carrying words it has heard and repeating them in context, perfectly, days later. It never forgets a word it has been given.
stages.note: Ravyx can repeat any word it has heard in the exact voice that first spoke it - travelers say hearing their own voice from the treetops is deeply unsettling.

stages.name: Nyxraven
stages.bio: Nyxraven is a great dark raptor with a wingspan that seems to fold shadow around itself. Its feathers are layered in deep purples and blacks, and its six wings spread wide like a living eclipse when it lands. The feathers along its wing-edges trail like tattered storm-clouds. In Ghost Hollow it perches at the oldest tree and has not moved from it in decades - creatures come to it, never the reverse. It knows every secret ever whispered in the hollow since Abalont first cast his darkness, and it is said to answer a sincere question with the exact truth the asker needed most.
stages.note: Nyxraven is the only creature whose call can be heard inside a dream - children sometimes wake with a name it has never heard they cannot explain.

stages.name: Crowkin
