stages.bio: Crowkin is a dark, fluffy crow chick with sooty blue-black feathers and round red eyes that glow like coals. Wisps of dark smoke curl from its wingtips even at rest. It lives near the entrance passages of the Shadow Caves, hopping through narrow crevices and pecking at crystallized darkness that clings to the walls. Its presence in the caves is ancient - the guardians found carvings of Crowkins in the oldest tunnel walls, suggesting these small birds have nested here since before Abalont's shadow first fell. It is startling but not hostile, and the smoke it trails smells faintly of charred wood.
stages.note: Crowkin's smoke trail persists for several minutes after it has gone, marking its path like a living map through the cave tunnels.

stages.name: Malraven
stages.bio: Malraven has stretched into a lean, long-legged bird like a dark heron, with ragged trailing feathers at the wing-tips and a long curved beak. Its plumage is deep black-blue and its red eyes are brighter now. It picks its way through shallow cave pools with slow, deliberate steps, hunting the shadow-fish that swim in lightless water. Wispy tendrils of dark energy drift from its tail feathers. Guardians who venture into the caves' middle passages say Malraven always appears first - as if checking whether a traveler is worth the deeper paths. It is a gatekeeper that never speaks its terms.
stages.note: Malraven stands perfectly still for up to twenty minutes in shallow water, not hunting - just listening to the dark.

stages.name: Vexwing
stages.bio: Vexwing fills the cave ceiling when it spreads its wings - a massive dark raptor whose plumage bleeds into deep red at the wingtips, the color of cinders cooling in the dark. Its body crackles with dark energy that trails in streamers behind every wingbeat. When it lands in the deep caverns, the temperature drops and every light dims for a moment. It was here before the Shadow Caves had a name; some say it IS the shadow the caves are named for. But the guardians know it chooses its companions carefully - it has carried more than one lost child to the cave exit on its back, silently, in the deep dark.
stages.note: Once Vexwing decides a child deserves safety, it will cross the entire cave system in a single wingbeat to deliver them to light.

stages.name: Ravlet
stages.bio: Ravlet at its youngest is a compact, dark-feathered raven with deep violet-black plumage and bold yellow feet that grip branches with surprising strength. It has a sharp beak and a bright, watchful eye that misses nothing. In Ghost Hollow it hops between the pale root-knuckles of dead trees, tugging at fungus and dried shadow-moss to build the neatest nest any creature in the region has ever made. The guardians say a Ravlet nest is a better map of the hollow than any they have drawn - the materials are always sourced from the quietest, safest spots.
stages.note: A Ravlet nest is built from materials collected in a perfect circle around a safe resting spot - the nest itself marks the safest point in its territory.

stages.name: Ravnox
stages.bio: Ravnox has grown into a sleek, intelligent raven with long trailing feathers at the tail and shaggy throat-hackles that fan out when it is interested in something. Its dark purple plumage has an iridescent sheen in moonlight, and its yellow feet grip any surface - even glass-smooth shadow-stone - with ease. It has developed a habit of collecting voices: not objects, but the sound of them, which it stores and replays in imitation. Travelers who camp in Ghost Hollow often wake to their own conversation from the night before echoing from a branch overhead, edited by Ravnox into a single line that somehow makes more sense.
stages.note: Ravnox edits overheard conversations down to one line and plays it back at dawn - always the line that mattered.

stages.name: Malcorvus
stages.bio: Malcorvus is a vast raven with a wingspan that casts a genuine shadow over the hollow at midday. Its dark wings are edged in deeper purple and streaked with shadow-dark bands, and its yellow eyes glow like two small moons. It moves with the slow gravity of something that has lived through many seasons of Abalont's darkness. In Ghost Hollow it is the keeper of the deepest roots - the names of things that existed before Abalont came. It has never been known to repeat a word frivolously, and when it finally speaks one to a child, that child never forgets it.
stages.note: Malcorvus has been heard to use only one hundred and eight distinct words in living memory - every single one is permanently learned by anyone who hears it.

stages.name: Stinglet
stages.bio: Stinglet is a tiny flat-bodied ray no bigger than a hand, sandy-tan with a smooth oval disc and a slender whip-tail trailing behind. Its little eyes sit on top of its disc, looking upward with a gentle, curious expression. It glides just above the seafloor of Coral Bay in lazy figure-eights, stirring up small clouds of fine silt that it then fans away with its wing-fins. The guardians first brought it to the surface to show children that even the smallest creature in the bay has a name - and Stinglet has been the starting point for thousands of unfamiliar names ever since.
stages.note: Stinglet settles flat on sand and becomes almost perfectly invisible - a patch of seabed that is watching you.

stages.name: Raywing
stages.bio: Raywing has grown to the size of a dinner tray, its sandy-brown disc now fringed with small nodular bumps and its tail longer and more flexible. It skims just beneath the surface of Coral Bay, its wingtip fins breaking the water with the faintest ripple. It has learned to use the tidal currents to ride for hours without a single wingbeat, mapping the bay by the taste of the water alone. The bay's fishing families hang a Raywing scale near the door as a luck charm - the creatures are said to know where the safest sand banks are a full tide ahead of time.
stages.note: Raywing tastes the current an hour before a tidal shift and always adjusts course - it has never been stranded on a sandbar.

stages.name: Thornmanta
stages.bio: Thornmanta is a broad, powerful manta with a wide golden-tan disc studded with rows of sharp thorn-like spines along its back and flanks. Its long tail ends in a serrated point. It patrols the deepest channels of Coral Bay where the reef meets the open sea, holding the boundary. Its passage stirs the sand into long columns that drift upward like smoke signals - the bay's creatures read these columns to know where it has been. Abalont sent a tide of shadow-water to drown the bay's singing corals once; Thornmanta swept it back with three wingbeats so powerful they rearranged the seafloor.
stages.note: The sand columns Thornmanta raises persist for a full day - reef creatures use them as navigation markers when currents shift.

stages.name: Rhomling
stages.bio: Rhomling is a soft-looking, rounded rhino calf with grey-brown hide and a small stubby horn nub on its broad nose. Its body is low and wide, built close to the ground as if it already knows its future weight. It shuffles through the Crystal Mines tapping the walls with its horn-nub, listening for hollow spaces the way miners listen for water. The crystals in its section of the mine grow faster than elsewhere - researchers believe Rhomling's footsteps compact the mineral-rich soil in exactly the right pattern for crystal formation.
stages.note: Crystal clusters grow up to three times faster in tunnels where Rhomling regularly walks - miners follow its paths to find the richest veins.

stages.name: Rhinoam
stages.bio: Rhinoam has become a proper, powerfully built rhinoceros, its grey hide thickened and its single center horn now a proper solid spike. Its shoulders are high and round, its legs short but tremendously strong. It moves through the Crystal Mines with the confidence of something that knows it cannot be stopped - and it is right. The mine foremen discovered long ago that Rhinoam will only charge a wall section that is actually unstable; its geological judgment has saved more lives than the best surveyor in the region. It seems to know the mountain from the inside out.
stages.note: Rhinoam has never charged a structurally sound wall - every breach it makes reveals a dangerous hollow or a flood cavity behind it.

stages.name: Rhinotitan
stages.bio: Rhinotitan is immense, a fortress of grey rock-hide studded along its back and flanks with rows of stone spines that have grown from within over long decades. Multiple horns of different sizes crown its nose and brow. When it walks, the mine shafts tremble in a two-hundred-meter radius. It has carved more of the Crystal Mines' tunnels with its body alone than generations of miners with their tools. The guardians sealed a chamber of the mine's oldest words inside a rock formation Rhinotitan shaped - no one else could have made walls that thick.
stages.note: The largest tunnels in the Crystal Mines are perfectly smooth at shoulder-height - the result of Rhinotitan walking the same route for a hundred years.

stages.name: Rhomule
stages.bio: Rhomule is a compact, armored rhino cub whose body is already segmented like a suit of plate armor in cool grey-violet steel, with purple-tinted banding between the plates. A small blunt horn sits above its snout. It wobbles slightly when it walks - the armor is growing faster than the creature inside, and there are always gaps at the joints where dark energy leaks through in faint wisps. In the Steel Fortress it follows older Rhomites through the forges like a shadow, fascinated by heat but too sensible to touch anything until it is cool.
stages.note: Rhomule's plate gaps widen when it is frightened, letting out small puffs of dark energy - fortress workers use it as an early intruder alarm.

stages.name: Rhomarch
stages.bio: Rhomarch has grown into a dangerous-looking beast, its segmented steel-grey armor now covering most of its body in overlapping plates edged with deep purple. Multiple horn-spikes protrude from its head and back. Dark energy bleeds from its joints in thin continuous trails. It patrols the fortress walls with a methodical, heavy tread, and the sound of its plates shifting has been used for generations as the unofficial timekeeping clock of the Steel Fortress - three plate-clicks means the watch has changed. Nothing has ever successfully broken through a wall that Rhomarch was actively patrolling.
stages.note: The shifting of Rhomarch's plates makes a sound so precise that fortress engineers synchronize their clocks to its patrol rhythm.

stages.name: Rhomithor
stages.bio: Rhomithor is a leviathan of dark-forged steel, its body encased in massive overlapping armor slabs that creak as it moves, each one etched with battle records in the Fortress's own script. Three great horns crown its head. Dark energy pours continuously from every joint in slow heavy streams. The ground cracks where it stands still for too long. Abalont sent his strongest champion against the Steel Fortress gates once; Rhomithor lowered its head, took three steps, and the champion was not seen again. The guardians keep its stall door made of the strongest alloy in the region - more out of respect than necessity.
stages.note: The cracks in the Steel Fortress's outer courtyard were all made by Rhomithor during a single practice charge - it has never charged the walls themselves.

stages.name: Ringkit
stages.bio: Ringkit is a tiny lemur kit with soft grey-white fur, enormous round yellow eyes that glow faintly in the dark, and a fluffy tail already striped in black-and-white rings. It clings to cave walls with remarkable grip and peeks around corners at everything before committing to a direction. In the Shadow Caves it has learned to read the echo of its own tiny squeaks to navigate in total darkness - a skill it discovered independently at around three weeks old. Guardians say a Ringkit in the cave means the psychic fields here are stable enough for sensitive minds to enter safely.
stages.note: Ringkit maps an entire cave system using echo-squeaks within its first hour, and can navigate it in total darkness from then on.

stages.name: Ringtail
stages.bio: Ringtail has grown upright, moving on two legs with a long striped tail held high for balance. Its eyes are large and luminous, capable of adjusting between complete darkness and sudden bright light in less than a heartbeat. It patrols the mid-caves of the Shadow Caves with quick precise movements, touching the walls with its paws at regular intervals as if checking something it cannot quite explain. It has developed a mild psychic ability to sense where other minds are, which it uses mostly to avoid crowds - though it will cross an entire cave to find a child sitting alone in the dark.
stages.note: Ringtail can sense a lonely mind from fifty meters away and always approaches with the exact object that creature most needs to see.

stages.name: Lemurlux
stages.bio: Lemurlux is a striking creature - white-furred with luminous markings, its magnificent spiral tail swirling with living purple psychic energy. Its eyes glow gold-amber and seem to look slightly past the visible world. In the deepest Shadow Caves it floats a few centimeters off the ground, leaving no footprints. It can project calm directly into the minds of panicking creatures with a single glance, a gift the guardians relied upon when Abalont's shadow-storms made the caves a chaos of terrified minds. Its tail-spiral is different every time it moves - no two observers have ever drawn the same pattern.
stages.note: Lemurlux's tail-spiral has never repeated the same pattern twice in recorded observations - scholars have been studying this for forty years.

stages.name: Rootlet
stages.bio: Rootlet is a small wild-boar-like creature whose entire hide is textured like rough bark and patchy moss, making it nearly invisible when it curls up against a tree trunk. Two small white tusks curve upward from its snout. It trots through the edges of the Amber Desert where scrub grass meets sand, rooting up buried seeds with its nose and caching them in small earthen pots it digs out with its forelegs. Guardians who visit the desert's green fringes often find a neatly organized grid of soil patches - all Rootlet's work, every one of them planted with something that will grow.
stages.note: Rootlet plants seeds in perfect grids and checks on each one daily - the only creature in the desert with a gardening schedule.

stages.name: Tuskhide
stages.bio: Tuskhide has grown broad and powerful, its bark-hide deepening and its tusks curving outward in a wide arc. A mane of thick leafy growth sprouts from its shoulders like a green cape. It pushes through the Amber Desert with its head low, using its tusks as plows to turn dry sand over into softer loam, creating planting rows for the scrub plants that follow in its wake. After a year of Tuskhide working a sand-patch, the desert recedes. The region's farmers leave offerings at the edge of the dunes because wherever Tuskhide goes, green follows within a season.
stages.note: The narrow green strips crossing the Amber Desert are called Tuskhide roads - each one marks a single year of one creature's walking route.

stages.name: Thornusk
stages.bio: Thornusk is a massive, ancient-looking boar whose body has become almost indistinguishable from a living tree stump - bark-plated, covered in moss and thick root-like growth, with enormous tusks thickened at the base with woody knots. A dense forest of living branches and thick grass erupts from its back like a mobile grove. When it stands still in the Amber Desert, smaller animals take shelter beneath its back-growth, and birds nest in the branches. Abalont tried to salt the desert beyond recovery once; Thornusk walked through the salted zone for seven days and left green behind it every step.
stages.note: Birds nest in Thornusk's back-growth every spring - there are currently four occupied nests and Thornusk has adjusted its sleep schedule to avoid disturbing them.

stages.name: Rosling
stages.bio: Rosling is an impossibly pink elephant calf, round and soft as a pillow, with tiny floppy ears and a curious trunk that it uses to prod everything within reach. It radiates a faint warmth that other creatures find immediately soothing - anxiety tends to dissolve in a two-meter radius around a Rosling. In the Light Grove it toddles between the luminous trees, patting roots and humming to itself in a frequency too low to hear but that makes flowers open early. Guardians say Rosling was the first creature to greet them when they arrived, and it offered comfort before anyone said a word.
stages.note: Plants within two meters of a sleeping Rosling open their blooms out of season - florists in the grove call it the pink alarm clock.

stages.name: Rosmind
stages.bio: Rosmind has grown into a proper young elephant, still very pink but now with a swirling pink marking on its forehead that glows faintly when it concentrates. Its ears are larger now, always slightly raised as if listening to frequencies beyond normal hearing. It walks slowly through the Light Grove touching the luminous trees with its trunk-tip, and the trees seem to respond - brightening slightly, then fading as it moves on, as if a conversation is happening. Researchers believe Rosmind is actually reading stored memories from the trees, a skill no other creature has demonstrated.
stages.note: Rosmind spends thirty minutes each morning touching each luminous tree in its grove - the trees it skips are always the ones that need attention.

stages.name: Rosmarch
stages.bio: Rosmarch is a grand, deep-rose mammoth with a full pair of gently curved tusks and psychic spiral markings winding along its flanks in bright pink light. Its bulk is enormous but it moves with extraordinary gentleness - not a single flower is crushed where it walks. In the Light Grove it is the memory-keeper, carrying the emotional record of every creature that has ever lived there within its vast, calm mind. Abalont could not reach the Light Grove's heart while Rosmarch stood before it; the creature's psychic field simply returned every shadow-thought to sender, peaceful and unchanged.
stages.note: Rosmarch remembers every creature it has ever met, including their mood on every visit - it will mirror your own happiest expression back to you.

stages.name: Scaldite
stages.bio: Scaldite is a small, thick-bodied eel-like creature already covered in dark brick-red scales edged with orange, its wide-hinged jaw full of small jagged teeth it snaps open and shut when curious. It coils in pockets of warm lava-rock at the edge of the Lava Crater, absorbing heat through its belly scales. Despite its fierce expression, it follows bright objects with the focused delight of something that has never seen anything it did not find interesting. Jack, the crater's guardian, found the first Scaldite coiled around a lantern, convinced the flame was something that needed protecting.
stages.note: Scaldite coils around heat sources it trusts, pressing its belly against them even when the source is completely cold - it seems to remember warmth.

stages.name: Scaldvern
stages.bio: Scaldvern has thickened considerably, its brick-red and orange scales now heavily overlapping like cooling lava-crust. Its jaw is wider and its teeth are proper fangs, and the spines along its back have erupted into full saw-toothed ridges. It swims through shallow lava channels with sinuous ease, surfacing only to snap at the fiery words that drift like embers in the Lava Crater's air. Jack found that Scaldvern hoards these memory-embers in a hollow under its favorite rock - it collects them the way others collect treasures, as if it knows their value.
stages.note: Scaldvern hoards memory-embers in a hollow under its rock, arranged by brightness - the most luminous are always at the center.

stages.name: Inferscald
stages.bio: Inferscald is a great coiling lava-serpent, its dark red-orange scales now enormous and armored, its saw-toothed dorsal crest running the full length of its body. Its jaws can open almost a hundred and eighty degrees, and when it breathes out, the air ahead superheats. It coils around the deepest vents of the Lava Crater, hoarding the fierce, fiery words of the deep that Jack guards. Only a child whose courage burns brighter than the magma can coax it to share them - because Inferscald tests every visitor first by looking directly into their eyes and waiting for the flinch that never comes.
stages.note: Inferscald tests every visitor's courage with a ten-second unbroken stare - children who hold its gaze get a word no one else receives.

stages.name: Scaldrake
stages.bio: Scaldrake is a small pangolin-type creature curled in a round ball of overlapping sandy-tan scales, its tiny face poking out with bright eyes and a pointed snout. Its scales are warm to the touch from absorbing desert sun all day. It rolls across the Sand Dunes at surprising speed, uncurling to investigate anything that glints, then curling back into its ball before anything can investigate it in return. Guardians setting up trail-markers in the dunes often find them slightly rearranged overnight - Scaldrake, apparently, has opinions about the layout.
stages.note: Scaldrake rearranges any object left on its sand-path overnight, always into a pattern that turns out to be more aerodynamic.

stages.name: Scaldrix
stages.bio: Scaldrix has become a proper upright pangolin, its scales now dark grey-stone and dramatically overlapping, its body marked with glowing orange patches where heat seeps through the rock layers. It walks on its hind legs with a heavy rolling gait, using its thick tail for balance. In the Sand Dunes it can absorb the impact of falling rock with its scales - and it has been known to walk into active rockslides to herd smaller creatures out. The heat-glows in its scales trace exactly the paths of underground lava flows, making Scaldrix the most accurate geological map the dunes region has.
stages.note: Scaldrix's scale-glow traces underground lava flows in real time - geologists from the Lava Crater cross the dunes just to read its pattern.

stages.name: Scaldoth
stages.bio: Scaldoth is a massive armored giant whose entire body is plated in thick overlapping rock-grey scales now visibly cracked with lines of molten orange-red along every edge. Its back spines have grown enormous, and lava-light seeps from every joint. It is sluggish compared to its younger forms - but nothing in the Sand Dunes moves it once it plants its feet. When Abalont's winds tried to bury the dune region's stone anchors under mountains of sand, Scaldoth simply stood across every anchor it could find for six days straight while the storm blew itself out around its body. The sand-lines still curve around the spots where it stood.
stages.note: The sand-patterns around Scaldoth's resting spots last for decades - desert navigators have mapped them as permanent landmarks.

stages.name: Embhorn
stages.bio: Embhorn is a small, stocky dragon-antelope hatchling with deep brown-red scales, three short curved horn-nubs on its brow, and small bat-like wings folded tight to its back. It moves on all fours with a curious, rooting behavior - pressing its horned head against the volcanic rocks of the Dragon Spire as if listening for something. The faint warmth it radiates is comforting rather than dangerous. Guardians at the Spire say an Embhorn in the nesting chamber signals calm weather; when they scatter, check the volcano's pressure gauges.
stages.note: Embhorn's horns glow faintly orange twenty minutes before a volcanic pressure event - the Spire's guardians use it as their primary early-warning system.

stages.name: Magmask
stages.bio: Magmask has grown into a proper powerful dragon-antelope hybrid, its four curved horns now fully formed and glowing orange at the tips, and its wings developed enough for short gliding leaps. Its dark brown-red scales have thickened and its face bears a mask-like darker patch around the eyes that gives it an intense, focused expression. It charges across the Dragon Spire's rocky terraces with tremendous speed, using its horns to test the terrain before committing weight. The magma channels of the Spire seem to open slightly when Magmask passes - as if the volcano recognizes its kind.
stages.note: Magmask's wing-leaps carry it sixty meters without touching the ground - it uses the volcanic updrafts the way a sailor uses wind.

stages.name: Scaldhorn
stages.bio: Scaldhorn is a magnificent dragon of the Dragon Spire, its body deep brown-red and black with a full eruption of horn-spikes along the crown and spine, wings wide enough to shadow a courtyard, and streams of molten orange running from the base of each horn like lava tributaries. Its four legs are armored with layered fire-scale and its eyes burn steady amber. When it spreads its wings at the Spire's peak, every fire in the region brightens for a moment in response. The guardians say Scaldhorn was the first to answer when the Spire's ancient dragon memory-vault needed a warden - it arrived before it was asked.
stages.note: When Scaldhorn spreads its wings at the Spire's summit, every flame in the region brightens simultaneously - the guardians call it the Dragon Salute.

stages.name: Scalion
stages.bio: Scalion is a tiny silver-grey pangolin-like creature at its first stage, with a single oversized disc-scale on its head like a helmet visor and a curling tail. One bright blue eye peeks out from beneath the disc with intense curiosity. It moves cautiously but precisely through the Steel Fortress, using the disc on its head to deflect any debris that falls, and its curling tail to anchor itself in narrow passages. Guardians say every child who first enters the fortress sees a Scalion sitting near the gate - and that the Scalion always seems to recognize the ones who are going to make it.
stages.note: Scalion's head-disc is already harder than tempered steel at birth - the fortress smiths tested one and broke three of their best tools on it.

stages.name: Platynox
stages.bio: Platynox has grown into a proper scaled lizard with a broad flat head and a body covered in overlapping steel-bright plates. Its single blue eye is alert and intelligent. It moves low and fast through the Fortress corridors, scouting ahead of whatever guardian it has chosen to follow that day. Its plates are not just armor - when Platynox is excited about a word it has just learned, the plates shift and reflect light in a rippling pattern that veteran trainers can read like a language. It is, they say, the most honest creature in the Fortress because it literally shows its feelings.
stages.note: Platynox's plate-ripple pattern is different for every creature it meets - trainers have documented over two hundred distinct ripples.

stages.name: Aerodactox
stages.bio: Aerodactox stands upright, a gleaming armored lizard-knight with a spiraling tail, plated limbs, and the brilliant blue eye now blazing with accumulated intelligence. Its body is a fortress in itself - layered metal-bright scales over powerful muscle, built for both speed and impact. It guards the Steel Fortress's memory-vault with absolute dedication, and the memories it has gathered over its long life fill its armor like light fills glass. Forged-tough and loyal as the guardians themselves, it believes courage is built one word at a time - and it has been watching to see which children are building it seriously.
stages.note: Aerodactox has memorized every voice ever raised within the Fortress walls - it can quote any conversation from any point in its lifetime, perfectly.

stages.name: Scalkin
stages.bio: Scalkin is a round, small pangolin-type creature with warm earthy brown scales and a short blunt snout pressed permanently against the ground. It noses at every surface it crosses, tasting the mineral content of stone and metal alike. In the Steel Fortress it gravitates to the oldest foundations, where the earth beneath the steel is deepest, and it has been known to dig out small pockets that later turn out to be stress points in the stonework. The fortress engineers learned quickly to follow Scalkin's digging - wherever it excavates on its own initiative, something needs reinforcing.
stages.note: Every spot Scalkin has voluntarily excavated in the fortress has turned out to conceal a structural weakness - its record is perfect.

stages.name: Scalisaur
stages.bio: Scalisaur is a substantial pangolin-lizard with overlapping brown scales that have begun to grey and harden toward steel at the spine. Its body is long and low, moving with a steady rolling gait. It has developed a habit of pressing its entire flank against walls for minutes at a time - not resting, but listening. Other creatures in the Fortress have learned to watch where Scalisaur leans, because it always identifies the wall that needs attention next. Trainers say its bond with the earth beneath the steel is so deep that it processes soil composition the way others process language - instantly and intuitively.
stages.note: Scalisaur can identify the mineral content of any wall in the fortress just by pressing against it for thirty seconds - and it is never wrong.

stages.name: Metallisk
stages.bio: Metallisk is a broad, ancient-looking pangolin whose scales have fully converted to true steel-grey metal, edged along every plate with sharp silver points. Its body is as wide as it is long, and its tail can be used as a counterweight when it braces for impact. The earth beneath its feet actually shapes around it - over years of walking the same fortress paths, it has worn grooves in the stone that other creatures use as drainage channels. When Abalont's forces tried to undermine the fortress foundations, Metallisk simply lay flat and held the earth together with its body weight for three days while repairs were made.
stages.note: The grooves Metallisk has worn in the fortress floor over decades now function as the fortress's entire drainage system - no engineering required.

stages.name: Scaup
stages.bio: Scaup is a small, vividly purple chameleon-type creature with big round golden eyes and a coiled tail it wraps around branches like a corkscrew. Its body is covered in small raised scales that gleam with a faint toxic sheen. It moves along the lower stems of the Poison Marsh's plants with precise, measured steps - never rushing, always watching. The yellow eyes seem to process information much faster than anything its small body suggests; it has been seen solving two separate problems simultaneously, one with each eye, while holding perfectly still. It is strange, small, and deeply observant.
stages.note: Scaup solves two separate visual problems at once by directing each eye independently - one tracks prey, the other watches for threats.

stages.name: Scaldor
stages.bio: Scaldor has grown longer and more imposing, its purple scales now deeper and faintly iridescent, its coiling tail wide and powerful. The toxic sheen on its scales is now clearly visible as a faint slick, and it uses this to mark the boundaries of its territory in the Poison Marsh - any creature that follows Scaldor's scent trail without invitation will regret it. It has developed partial camouflage that works especially well in the marsh's purple-tinged shadow-water, where it rests half-submerged, only the golden eyes visible. Those eyes never blink.
stages.note: Scaldor has maintained the same ten-meter territorial boundary markers for three years without variation - it refreshes them every forty-eight hours exactly.

stages.name: Scalerath
stages.bio: Scalerath is a magnificent and dangerous creature - a deep purple dragon-chameleon, its body now muscular and armored with great fin-like back-spines and a magnificent spiraling tail. Its golden eyes burn with intelligence, and the toxic aura it radiates has turned the water in a ten-meter radius around its resting pool a permanently iridescent purple. It is the apex guardian of the Poison Marsh, the creature that other venomous things treat as law. Abalont tried to co-opt the marsh by poisoning its water-songs; Scalerath swallowed each one, neutralized the shadow-toxin, and exhaled the clean word back into the air.
stages.note: Scalerath is immune to every poison found in its region - it identifies new toxins by tasting them once and has never been affected twice.

stages.name: Scarabby
stages.bio: Scarabby is a plump cream-colored grub, its segmented body soft and glistening like fresh bark. Two tiny black eyes sit at the tip of its rounded head, and it moves by slowly rippling its body along the forest floor. Hidden deep in the rotting wood of the Dark Forest, it feeds on shadow-soaked heartwood that stains its insides with darkness. Guardians rarely see it - it retreats at the first snap of a twig, burying itself in mulch until the footsteps fade away.
stages.note: A Scarabby curls completely still when touched, becoming nearly indistinguishable from a pale pebble.

stages.name: Chitimax
stages.bio: Chitimax has sealed itself inside a smooth dark oval shell edged with a golden lightning-bolt stripe - a perfect hardened case no blade can scratch. It does not eat or move, but those who press an ear to its shell hear a slow, rhythmic pulse like a heartbeat in deep stone. The guardians called it the Sealed Thought, believing Chitimax is memorizing every voice raised near it. In the Dark Forest's silence, it absorbs the shadow energy that will fuel its final transformation.
stages.note: The gold stripe on Chitimax's shell glows faintly brighter each day - locals count the glow to guess how close it is to waking.

stages.name: Kerathorn
stages.bio: Kerathorn emerges as a golden rhinoceros beetle of immense size, its forked twin horn capable of splitting a fallen oak in one heave. Its carapace gleams gold-over-black in moonlight, and the dark energy absorbed during its sealed stage has laced every plate with shadow that bends light around its edges. It moves through the forest at night without a sound, and only the deep crack of its horn against wood tells you it has passed. The guardians regard it as a guardian of sealed secrets.
stages.note: Kerathorn hooks its twin horns together each dawn and pulls them apart with a crack that echoes half a mile through the Dark Forest.

stages.name: Scarabite
stages.bio: Scarabite stands upright on stubby legs, its small round brown body topped with a single softly glowing green horn - a tendril of ghost energy it absorbed from Ghost Hollow's misty air. Its wide eyes are always blinking, startled by everything, and it taps the tip of its horn against objects to "taste" whether they hold a word or a memory. The hollow's wandering spirits seem fond of it, drifting near as if drawn by its gentle glow.
stages.note: A Scarabite's green horn light flickers faster the closer a ghost is - hollows residents use them as spirit-weather vanes.

stages.name: Scarabug
stages.bio: Scarabug has grown wide and heavy, its body now a deep violet-mauve, and its single horn has thickened into a blunt ridge that it uses to push through Ghost Hollow's clinging fog banks. Four legs carry it low to the ground with a determined hunch, and it marks territory by pressing its horn into soft earth and leaving glowing impressions. Old trainers say Scarabug's shadow is always slightly larger than its body, as though something dark rides behind it.
stages.note: Scarabug presses its horn into mud to leave glowing prints; Ghost Hollow paths are often lit faintly by rows of these marks.

stages.name: Scarabyss
stages.bio: Scarabyss towers over the hollow, a dark purple rhinoceros beast whose horns have multiplied across its wide brow and shoulders like a crown of shadows. Its legs are thick as old roots and its back is broad enough that moss has begun to grow in the crevices of its plates. When Scarabyss roars, the ghosts of Ghost Hollow scatter for half an hour, and the fog lifts entirely. The guardians believe it holds the boundary between the living and the lost, and that it chose that duty willingly.
stages.note: When Scarabyss stands still in fog, its outline looks enough like a ruined tower that travellers have mistaken it for ruins and sheltered against its flank.

stages.name: Beetiny
stages.bio: Beetiny is a compact golden-amber scarab, its oval shell etched with faint zigzag grooves and a single short antenna crackling at its tip with a tiny golden light. It charges itself by rolling through the dry leaf-litter of Bug Thicket, picking up static with every shuffle of its six legs. The charge is too small to hurt, but it makes Beetiny's shell buzz pleasantly when stroked - thicket children call it a living toy. Its eyes are large and bright, always aimed forward with cheerful determination.
stages.note: Beetiny builds up enough static to briefly light a firefly lantern after a 20-second shuffle across dry leaves.

stages.name: Mandril
stages.bio: Mandril has shed its rounded shell and burst into a tall angular golden form - blade-like forelegs raised in permanent readiness, each edge trimmed with a crackle of electric yellow. It stands on four rear legs and uses its two scythe-arms to redirect lightning it pulls from the thicket's storm-static into tight focused bolts. It moves with quick, precise snapping steps, and every footfall leaves a faint scorch mark. Bug Thicket adventurers know to watch for the yellow flashes between the branches.
stages.note: Mandril's blade-arms act as lightning rods - during a thunderstorm, it absorbs three to four bolts before it needs to discharge.

stages.name: Chitaryx
stages.bio: Chitaryx is an enormous golden mantis-beetle, its long scythe arms crackling with sustained arcs of lightning that never fully discharge. Wings like stained-glass fold against its back, and its skeletal abdomen pulses yellow-white with stored voltage. When it spreads its arms wide, the air between them hums loud enough to feel in your chest. It patrols the highest canopy of Bug Thicket, and the other electric bugs below align themselves toward it like compass needles to a pole.
stages.note: Chitaryx can hold a sustained arc of electricity between its two raised arms for over thirty seconds without tiring.

stages.name: Scaralite
stages.bio: This small green beetle looks like a living clod of earth - its rounded body the same soft jade as new valley moss, and a wide single eye that blinks with a muddy yellow glow. Its stout trunk-like snout pokes at every patch of soil it crosses, sniffing for song-seeds buried by Verdant Valley's song-trees. It is a gentle digger; it never tears roots, only loosens soil with a patient nudge and pushes the seeds back deeper for the trees to find later.
stages.note: Scaralite's trunk-snout can detect a buried seed through fifteen centimetres of packed valley earth.

stages.name: Scarabuzz
stages.bio: Scarabuzz has grown a proper upturned horn and six sturdy legs that press deep furrows into the valley soil as it walks. Its green plates are now ridged like terraced hills, and its wide brow pushes earth aside to make winding paths between root clusters. The guardians valued it as a living plow - it would turn soil along the base of Akilla's song-trees before first light, needing no instruction. It marks its patrol with shallow troughs that fill with rainwater and become drinking tracks for smaller creatures.
stages.note: Scarabuzz's plow-horn can turn a one-metre furrow of soft valley earth in a single slow forward press.

stages.name: Scaramorph
stages.bio: Scaramorph is a great green armored titan, its carapace so thick with layered plates that the valley's wildflowers have begun rooting in the cracks between them. Two wide curving horns frame its brow like protective arms, and when it lowers its head to the valley floor, the ground shakes with each breath. It is enormously strong but moves with quiet patience, settling in the shallowest parts of the valley to let water flow over its feet and song-seeds travel in the current it stirs.
stages.note: Three different species of valley flower bloom annually in the cracks of Scaramorph's back plates, fertilized by the earth it carries.

stages.name: Scarabtiny
stages.bio: Scarabtiny lives almost entirely underground in the sandy gravel of Granite Heights, only its rounded pale head visible as it peeks above the pebble line. It is a patient digger, inching through compacted granite-sand grain by grain, and the minerals it swallows slowly change its body chemistry - golden flecks begin to appear under its skin even at this early stage. Guardians searching the heights sometimes spot the tiny divot in the pebbles where it breathes, but by the time they crouch down, it has gone still as a stone.
stages.note: Scarabtiny ingests an estimated twelve grams of granite mineral per day, slowly gilding its interior.

stages.name: Scaraegis
stages.bio: Scaraegis has compressed itself into a perfectly smooth golden oval marked with a raised ankh - the ancient symbol the granite heights' stone-carvers once used to mean 'protected life.' It does not move, but the ankh symbol glows warm amber, and pressing a hand to it feels like pressing a hand to sunlit stone on a summer afternoon. The heights' goat-shepherds hang them at the entrance of their paths as good-luck charms, returning them carefully to the earth when the glow begins to pulse faster - the sign of waking.
stages.note: The ankh carving on Scaraegis is not painted - it is formed by mineral deposits that migrated through the shell from inside.

stages.name: Scaraflux
stages.bio: Scaraflux is a flying golden scarab the size of a large shield, its wings spread to reveal interlocking gold-veined panels that catch mountain light and scatter it in warm fan-shapes across the granite. A large golden ankh adorns its thorax like a breastplate, and its six legs end in flat pads that grip cliff-faces with ease. It navigates the highest ridges of Granite Heights where no path leads, and the guardians believed it carried the mountain's oldest memories inside its gilded shell - every mark carved into rock up there.
stages.note: Scaraflux's wing-beats produce a deep resonant hum that makes loose pebbles on a cliff face vibrate loose - it can start a small rockfall without touching a stone.

stages.name: Scarynip
stages.bio: Scarynip is a small dark-plated crab with a single oversized mechanical-looking claw and a round glowing eye mounted on the top of its shell like a periscope. It scuttles sideways through the Dark Forest undergrowth, and its one big claw makes a clipping sound against exposed roots as it clips off tiny pieces of iron-rich bark to swallow. The metal it absorbs strengthens its shell plate by plate. It is notably curious - it will approach a campfire's glow, claw raised, to investigate.
stages.note: Scarynip's single large claw is strong enough to snap a finger-thick green branch cleanly at three weeks old.

stages.name: Scarbeam
stages.bio: Scarbeam crouches low and wide, its dark grey shell now reinforced with steel-hard plates that overlap like scale mail. Both claws are large and yellow-tipped, capable of peeling bark off a mature tree in strips. It moves in total silence through the Dark Forest's shadows, using its low profile to slip under fallen logs. When threatened, it spreads both claws wide and clicks them together in a rapid staccato meant to sound like something much larger. Other forest creatures give it a wide berth.
stages.note: Scarbeam can remain completely motionless for up to two hours, claw pressed flat to the ground, before springing into action.

stages.name: Scaryx
stages.bio: Scaryx is a heavily armored dark crab whose entire shell is covered with upward-pointing spikes, each tip hardened to a needle point. Multiple enormous claws extend from its sides, some used for grip and others kept raised for striking. The shadow absorbed from the Dark Forest has darkened its plates to near-black, and the tips of its spikes gleam with a faint metallic sheen. When it presses all its claws to the ground at once, it can feel vibrations from over fifty metres away, making it nearly impossible to approach undetected.
stages.note: Scaryx has eleven distinct claw tips and can control each independently - observers have counted it sharpening six at once against the same boulder.

stages.name: Scuttler
stages.bio: Scuttler hatches near the outer cooling ring of Lava Crater, its small round shell mottled black-and-gold like the crust of cooling magma. It scuttles erratically between hot rocks, using its body heat to crack mineral crusts and eat the salt crystals underneath. Electric sparks jump between its legs when it moves fast, a side effect of the volcanic minerals it absorbs. It has the look of a creature that has never quite decided which direction to go, and changes course a dozen times a minute.
stages.note: Scuttler's shell temperature runs 40 degrees above the ambient crater air - you can feel warmth radiating from it from two hand-widths away.

stages.name: Scorpinch
stages.bio: Scorpinch has grown a tough mottled shell with lava-flow patterns running across its carapace in glowing cracks of gold. Its two forward claws are heavy and broad, used as much for anchoring to steep crater walls as for offense. Electric current runs continuously along the rim of its shell, and rainwater on it flashes to steam in an instant. It prefers the steep inner walls of the crater where thermal currents keep it warm, and guards those spots against anything larger than itself - including younger Scuttlers.
stages.note: Scorpinch's shell crack-patterns are unique to each individual - lava crater researchers use them as fingerprints to track individuals over years.

stages.name: Infersting
stages.bio: Infersting is a massive black crab whose carapace is studded with thick spike rows and crossed by continuous lightning-bolt markings that pulse and flash on their own. It has claimed the deepest trench of Lava Crater as its territory, and the electric field it generates disrupts compasses within a 30-metre radius. When it spreads its claws wide and releases a full charge, the resulting arc can be seen from the crater rim. The guardians call it the Forge-Herald - believing when Infersting discharges fully, the crater is ready to produce new star-metal.
stages.note: Infersting sheds its outer spike-tips once a year; crater collectors prize them as natural lightning rods that never corrode.

stages.name: Scorbyte
stages.bio: Scorbyte is a compact orange-brown crab-like bug with one outsized pincer that it holds raised, showing it off at every opportunity. Heat shimmers around it at midday because its shell absorbs sunlight and stores it as warmth in the Bug Thicket canopy. It will grab a hot ember from a campfire with its big claw and carry it around - not to harm anyone, just to feel the heat in its grip. Young Scorbyte are sometimes spotted standing in beams of sunlight with eyes closed, soaking warmth like a tiny sunbather.
stages.note: A Scorbyte's big claw runs consistently warmer than its body - you can cook a small bug-berry against it in under two minutes.

stages.name: Scorpaw
stages.bio: Scorpaw has armored itself in overlapping burnt-orange plates that act as heat vents, letting steam escape between each layer. Its claws are now dual and enormous - one for grip, one for smashing - and the fire trapped inside them turns the striking surfaces cherry-red during combat. It marks its territory in Bug Thicket by scorching claw-prints into the bark of large trees at head height, and those marks never fade. Other bugs avoid its grove unless invited.
stages.note: Scorpaw's striking claw reaches surface temperatures high enough to leave a clear brand in oak bark with a single tap.

stages.name: Infernacle
stages.bio: Infernacle is a massive brick-red armored crab covered in interlocked spikes that radiate heat like a forge. Every plate is thick as a roof tile and carries a faint ember-glow in its grooves. When it fully opens its claws, waves of heat ripple outward in visible bands, and nearby dry brush begins to smolder within five seconds. It walks slowly, since anything that hurries nearby catches fire, and Bug Thicket keeps a wide charred ring around wherever Infernacle has chosen to rest that season.
stages.note: The charred ring around an Infernacle's resting spot grows by roughly one metre per week; old rings can be up to forty metres wide.

stages.name: Scorcule
stages.bio: Scorcule is a small glowing orange worm, its segmented body curled in a comma shape and pulsing with inner heat. It lives in the scorched underside of Sand Dunes rocks where the surface temperature could blister skin - Scorcule absorbs that heat and stores it, making its body warm to the touch like a smooth river stone left in afternoon sun. It has no legs, but ripples through hot sand at surprising speed by contracting its body segments rhythmically. The dunes' midnight travelers sometimes mistake a cluster of them for a bed of embers.
stages.note: A single Scorcule emits enough body heat to keep a two-person tent warm through a cold desert night.

stages.name: Scorvenom
stages.bio: Scorvenom has grown a long multi-legged body, each segment bordered in deep orange and bearing a pair of sharp legs that leave tiny scorch marks as it walks. Its face is fierce, with mandibles that drip a heated venom that sears rather than poisons - a unique chemical it brews from volcanic mineral dust it ingests off hot dune surfaces. It is the apex ambush hunter of the dune underside: it lies pressed flat against hot rock, indistinguishable from a crack in the stone, until something small crosses its shadow.
stages.note: Scorvenom's venom does not injure by toxin but by a rapid spike of heat - a drop on bare skin produces a mark like a tiny brand.

stages.name: Infermarx
stages.bio: Infermarx coils like a small inferno - a great fire-patterned centipede whose entire body blazes with interlocking flame-scale markings. Its face has grown dragon-fierce, with wide curved mandibles and eyes like heated coals. A visible heat haze surrounds it at all times, and flames flicker briefly at the tips of each leg as it moves. It has claimed the deepest dune basin of Sand Dunes as its territory, and the scorched spiral trail it leaves when it hunts is visible from the ridge above. Guardians call it the Buried Flame - the fire that refused to go out.
stages.note: Infermarx leaves a spiral scorch trail up to 80 metres long when hunting - the pattern repeats identically, as if following an invisible groove.

stages.name: Scorkit
stages.bio: Scorkit is a small dark-red quadruped dragon with two rounded wing-buds folded tight against its back and a blunt horn-ridge above its brow. Its scales are rough like dried lava and warm to the touch even on the coldest Dragon Spire mornings. It is perpetually curious and tends to follow larger creatures at a distance, watching what they do before attempting it itself. The first thing most Scorkits learn to do is scratch sparks from the spire's flint outcrops with one claw - a small act, but one that clearly delights them.
stages.note: Scorkit's wing-buds, though too small to fly, already vibrate at altitude - locals use this as a signal that a spire wind-shift is coming.

stages.name: Scormaw
stages.bio: Scormaw has grown fully into its dark red scales and bat wings now spread wide enough to catch the updrafts that rise along Dragon Spire's cliffs. Its horns have multiplied across its brow in a low crown, and its tail whips in slow arcs when it perches. Fire comes easily now - a short exhale produces a sustained ribbon of flame that it uses to warm its resting ledge before settling. The spire's older dragons tolerate Scormaw on their ridges, which is considered a mark of real promise.
stages.note: Scormaw's wingbeats smell distinctly of warm sulfur - spire guides use the scent to know when one is circling above cloud cover.

stages.name: Inferscor
stages.bio: Inferscor is a full great dragon - dark burgundy scales that have hardened to the consistency of forge-cooled iron, wide bat wings that block the sun when it soars between spire peaks. Its multiple brow horns sweep back like a crown, and its eyes burn with sustained flame. Each exhale is a controlled column of fire it can hold or release at will, and when it chooses to roar, the sound rolls down from Dragon Spire's summit to the valley below in waves. The guardians' oldest texts describe a creature matching Inferscor as the one who first taught the dragon words of power.
stages.note: Inferscor's fire column can burn for nine continuous seconds before it must pause to breathe - the longest documented sustained flame of any Dragon Spire resident.

stages.name: Scormite
stages.bio: Scormite is a dark red-and-purple centipede, small enough to hide under a single leaf, with a pair of short yellow antennae and many thin legs that carry it forward in a fast rippling wave. The poison it produces at this stage is mild - a slight itch if touched - but it practices delivery constantly, tapping its mandibles against flower stems and blades of grass as if rehearsing for later. In Verdant Valley, it hides among the roots of song-trees and collects fallen song-seeds to decorate its burrow.
stages.note: Scormite decorates the entrance to its burrow with fallen song-seeds - researchers have found burrows with over sixty arranged in rows.

stages.name: Scorvid
stages.bio: Scorvid has grown twice the length of an adult arm, and yellow warning highlights have appeared along each of its leg joints - a vivid advertisement of its now-potent venom. It moves fast and low, pressing close to the valley floor where the humid air helps carry its chemical signals. When two Scorvids meet on the same root, they raise their forelegs and wave them slowly at each other, a greeting ritual that lasts exactly three passes before they move on. The guardians respected this politeness enormously.
stages.note: Scorvid's venom changes composition with the seasons - spring venom causes tingling, but autumn venom can numb a limb for four hours.

stages.name: Scorvarch
stages.bio: Scorvarch is a massive centipede-dragon hybrid whose back carries a flame-patterned crest of red-orange spines that look like fire but are solid chitin laced with venom. Its many legs carry its long body with terrifying smoothness, and its dragon-fierce head bears wide curved mandibles capable of injecting a concentrated dose in a single strike. In Verdant Valley, the other creatures keep a wide berth - even the song-trees seem to lean away from it. The guardians called it the Last Warning, for when Scorvarch patrols, all creatures return home before dark.
stages.note: Scorvarch's mandible venom is so concentrated that a single drop neutralizes any other venom it encounters - it has been observed curing other creatures of poison bites.

stages.name: Scoryte
stages.bio: Scoryte is a compact blue-purple lizard whose orange frill-fins flare from its neck and shoulders like tiny flame-petals. It scurries across Amber Desert rocks with quick four-legged darts, using its bright frills to signal mood - fanned wide means 'back off,' folded flat means 'curious.' The poison it stores is fire-warm, sitting at the back of its throat, and it can spit a short gout of burning venom if really startled. But mostly it would rather show off its frills to a rival than fight.
stages.note: Scoryte's frill-fins flush a deeper orange shade when it's angry - tracking the color change is the safest way to judge its mood from a distance.

stages.name: Scoraxe
stages.bio: Scoraxe has grown longer and lower, its orange dorsal spines now running from neck to tail-tip in a single unbroken ridge. Purple-and-gold spots mark its flanks in a pattern unique to each individual, and its fire-venom has concentrated enough to leave scorch-stains where it lands on sand. It claims territories in the mid-desert where rocks absorb heat all day, and it presses its belly to warm stone at sunset to charge up. When two Scoraxe share a rock, their spine-colors shift and sync - a communication no one has fully translated.
stages.note: The unique spot pattern on each Scoraxe's flank has been used by desert trackers to identify individuals for over 200 years of journals.

stages.name: Infernorax
stages.bio: Infernorax is a great dark purple lizard-beast whose tall purple spines run the full length of its back and rise to impressive heights - each one tipped with a venom sac that ruptures under pressure and burns like a brand. It moves deliberately through the Amber Desert's highest heat zones, and the air around it shimmers with combined heat and chemical vapor. Its spine-tips glow faintly at night, making it visible across the dunes - a warning the desert itself broadcasts to everything else. The guardians called it the Wandering Brand - the desert's own signature mark.
stages.note: Infernorax's spine-tips are visible glowing at night from up to one kilometre in clear desert air - they pulse slightly in rhythm with its heartbeat.

stages.name: Scutling
stages.bio: Scutling is a small green isopod - a pill-bug shape with a gently domed back and six stubby legs that carry it in a slow, bobbing walk. It lives in the mossy crevices of Granite Heights' lower ledges where water seeps between rocks, feeding on mineral-rich algae mats. When frightened, it tucks its legs under its body and becomes a smooth pebble-sized lump impossible to distinguish from the rocks around it. The heights' children collect them into small mossy jars, calling them 'living pebbles.'
stages.note: When curled, a Scutling holds its position with a grip equivalent to four times its body weight - trying to pry one open takes real effort.

stages.name: Scutilion
stages.bio: Scutilion has grown flat and wide, its olive-green body now segmented into overlapping plates that slide over each other as it moves - a sound like shuffling stone tiles announces its presence before it is seen. It navigates Granite Heights' steep faces by gripping with all six legs simultaneously, and it prefers to walk along vertical cliff surfaces rather than the flat paths, hugging the rock with each plate of its body making full contact. Its antenna tips brush every crack as it passes, cataloging the mineral content below.
stages.note: Scutilion can travel along a vertical granite face for up to three consecutive hours without rest - it has never been recorded falling.

stages.name: Scutirax
stages.bio: Scutirax is a great golden-tan armored titan, its overlapping body plates now thick as quarried stone and worn smooth by years of cliff-face traversal. Many sturdy legs carry its long broad body with slow hydraulic precision, and its bulk is enough to reshape small rock formations just by pressing through them. Granite Heights' stone-paths are partly formed by Scutirax's regular routes, worn down by centuries of its weight. Guardians say it was here before the first path was carved - the original road-builder of the heights.
stages.note: A well-worn path across Granite Heights was traced back to a Scutirax route - the creature had used it for an estimated 300 years before humans arrived.

stages.name: Scutiny
stages.bio: Scutiny carries a ridged dome shell on its back, reddish-brown with a surface texture like old hardwood - and it collects new shells obsessively, swapping out the one it has every few weeks for a slightly larger one it has been eyeing in Coral Bay's shallows. One large orange claw does most of its work, clicking at pebbles and prying apart shells to evaluate them. It makes a low bubbling noise while doing this - a sound the bay's fishers have come to associate with the presence of particularly good shelling spots.
stages.note: Scutiny evaluates up to seven different shells before choosing a new one, and returns rejected shells to the exact spot it found them.

stages.name: Scutlash
stages.bio: Scutlash carries a large barrel-like shell reinforced with strips of steel-hard mineral deposits it has layered on over seasons of submersion in Coral Bay's mineral springs. Two bright orange claws reach past the shell rim, one larger for cracking open encrusted food and one smaller and more precise for intricate shell-work. It has begun decorating its shell with found objects - a knack that alarms only visitors to the bay, since locals are used to seeing a Scutlash with a pebble mosaic on its back. When threatened, it retreats fully inside and seals the opening shut with its large claw.
stages.note: No two Scutlash shells carry the same decoration arrangement - each shell is considered a personal statement, accumulated over three to four years.

stages.name: Scutlord
stages.bio: Scutlord emerges from Coral Bay's deepest channel carrying a shell that has fused to layers of steel mineral deposits - its back is now an armored fortress of spined ridged plates that nothing short of a direct strike can dent. Its claws are massive and thick-armored, and when it walks the full weight of its shell sends vibrations through the bay floor that small fish interpret as a local earthquake. The guardians found old maps that named certain reef formations 'Scutlord Shelf' - suggesting the creature has been shaping Coral Bay's landscape for centuries.
stages.note: Scutlord's fused shell has been documented absorbing direct blows from boulder-sized debris during storms without showing fracture.

stages.name: Scuttlet
stages.bio: Scuttlet is a small brown armadillo with a neatly banded shell and a soft pointed snout it keeps pressed to the sand at all times, reading the ground for vibrations. It lives in the upper dune layer where loose sand shifts constantly, and its banded shell acts as a natural sand-sieve - grains fill the gaps and make it effectively invisible when still. It rolls into a perfect ball at any perceived threat and bounces gently down dune slopes, which appears to be accidental but happens so consistently that researchers now believe it is deliberate.
stages.note: Scuttlet rolled down the same dune 21 times in a single afternoon before researchers realized it was doing it on purpose, not out of fear.

stages.name: Armadex
stages.bio: Armadex has compacted itself into a near-perfect sphere of overlapping grey-stone plates - when curled, it is almost perfectly round, and on the steeper dunes it gains real speed in this form. Uncurled, it stands on four solid legs with a wide rounded body and moves with careful, deliberate steps. Its shell plates have taken on a stone-grey color now that it has grown past the lighter brown of youth, and each band is separated by a visible dark groove. Dune merchants mark territorial boundaries using Armadex's roll-tracks - the lines are always perfectly straight.
stages.note: Armadex's rolled form achieves a near-perfect sphere within 0.4 seconds of curling - faster than the eye can track.

stages.name: Thanatusk
stages.bio: Thanatusk stands wide and solid, its grey stone-plate body bearing a thick spiked tail it drags behind it in the sand - the trail it leaves looks like a plow has gone through. Its large claws press deep footprints into packed dune rock, and when it shakes its body, the plates clatter against each other like a rockslide in miniature. The Sand Dunes' oldest trading routes follow paths Thanatusk has walked for generations - its weight compacts the sand into something firm enough to drive a cart over. The guardians called it the Road-Maker.
stages.note: Thanatusk's tail-spike drag creates furrows up to 30 centimetres deep in packed dune sand - some are used as irrigation channels by dune farmers.

stages.name: Scutwee
stages.bio: Scutwee is a compact brown pangolin whose overlapping scales already show a faint amber glow at their centers - a hint of the lava energy it will come to carry. It wanders the Lava Crater's cooler outer rim, pressing its nose to the ground and tasting volcanic minerals with a long sticky tongue. The amber glow on its chest pulses faster when it is excited, and crater-children use this as a sort of mood-light, watching it brighten when they offer it a handful of mineral dust. It is gentle and shy, preferring to roll into a tight ball rather than engage.
stages.note: Scutwee's amber chest-glow brightens by a measurable degree within one metre of an active volcanic vent - researchers use it as a heat sensor.

stages.name: Scuthorn
stages.bio: Scuthorn stands upright on two broad legs, its body thick with overlapping scales that have taken on a deep brown-orange hue from years of volcanic mineral absorption. An amber gem-like spot glows visibly on its chest, warm enough to act as a small heat source on cold crater nights. It uses its short powerful arms to climb the rough inner walls of Lava Crater, pressing each scale individually against the rock face to test heat tolerance before proceeding. It marks safe climbing routes by scoring its claws into the rock - a permanent guide for anything smaller that follows.
stages.note: Scuthorn's amber chest-gem has been measured at 80 degrees Celsius during peak activity - hot enough to fry a small egg placed against it.

stages.name: Scutossus
stages.bio: Scutossus is a great dragon-like pangolin, its scales now layered so thickly they jut outward in overlapping rows like roof tiles forged from volcanic stone. The amber glow has spread from its chest across the grooves between every scale, lighting its body in warm amber from within. When it moves, the scales grind against each other with a sound like boulders settling, and the heat it radiates is enough to keep a wide circle of the crater floor permanently dry and warm. The guardians placed it in their most ancient fire-carvings, believing Scutossus was there when the crater first opened.
stages.note: The ambient temperature five metres from a resting Scutossus runs 35 degrees higher than surrounding crater air - its body warms the stone it rests on permanently.

stages.name: Scythlet
stages.bio: Scythlet is a small dark-furred quadruped whose back is already bristling with short metal spikes, hard to the touch and cold even in summer. It lives in Shadow Caves' narrow passages where it can brush both walls at once, using the spikes to feel vibrations in the stone. Its eyes are adapted to complete darkness and reflect a faint silver in lamplight. It is wary but not aggressive, retreating at raised voices - the caves echo strangely and it treats every reverberation as a potential threat. Young ones tap their spikes against cave walls to communicate across the dark.
stages.note: Scythlet can transmit information to others of its kind by tapping its spikes in specific rhythms against shared cave walls - cave researchers call it 'spike-talk.'

stages.name: Scythorn
stages.bio: Scythorn has grown heavy and broad, its coat dark as charcoal and its back spikes now long enough to scrape the cave ceilings. Each spike is individually sharp and has a slight backward curve, making them effective at catching anything that tries to grab it from above. It moves through Shadow Caves with a slow commanding authority, and the smaller creatures part before it without being told. When two Scythorn cross paths in a narrow tunnel, they compare spike-length by standing side by side for exactly thirty seconds before one yields the passage.
stages.note: Scythorn's spike tips are self-sharpening - the points regrow within 48 hours after being broken, slightly sharper than before.

stages.name: Scythorax
stages.bio: Scythorax is a massive dark predator whose entire back and shoulders carry a forest of long steel spikes that rattle softly when it walks - a sound that carries through Shadow Caves' tunnels like a warning bell. Its coat is pure black, absorbing all light, and its eyes glow silver in the deepest dark. The spikes are long enough that Scythorax must turn sideways to fit through certain cave passages, and over centuries it has widened all of its regular routes to suit itself. The guardians' records note that Scythorax spikes were found embedded in the cave walls at heights that suggest it was fighting something immense - a story no one has fully told.
stages.note: Scythorax's regular cave-routes are identifiable by parallel scratch-marks at shoulder height on both walls, left by its outer spike-tips for centuries.

stages.name: Scytlip
stages.bio: Scytlip wears a round helmet-like shell over its head and carries two forward-facing claws it holds up in front of it at all times, like a tiny knight on permanent guard duty. Its eyes peer from a slit between its helmet and body with intense focus. It lives at the edges of Bug Thicket's clearings where it can watch everything at once, and it challenges anything larger than itself with a rapid claw-display - not to fight, but to demonstrate it has already thought through the fight and decided it wins. Young guardians found it inspiring.
stages.note: Scytlip challenges creatures ten times its size with its full claw-display, and researchers have never once seen one back down first.

stages.name: Scythar
stages.bio: Scythar has grown into a proper knight's silhouette - silver plate armor across its thorax, a sword-like forward claw on one arm, and a shield-like plate claw on the other. It walks upright on four rear legs and keeps its weapon arms raised. In Bug Thicket's border disputes between creature territories, Scythar acts as a neutral adjudicator - it positions itself between conflicting creatures and holds both claws out until both parties retreat. The behavior is instinctual, not trained, and it works every single time.
stages.note: Scythar has been observed peacefully resolving territorial disputes between creatures up to three times its own size - it has no record of ever needing to strike.

stages.name: Scytharos
stages.bio: Scytharos is a commanding armored crab-knight in full plate - helmet, pauldrons, greaves - each piece worked with golden trim that catches the thicket light like a moving shield. Its right arm carries a broad sword-claw capable of deflecting strikes meant for others, and its left holds a rounded shield-plate bearing a crest worn smooth by long use. When Scytharos enters a battle, both sides pause instinctively - something in its bearing tells every creature present that only one outcome is possible. The guardians called it the First Sworn, the creature that understood duty before duty had a word.
stages.note: Scytharos's sword-claw has a distinct ring tone that carries 400 metres through Bug Thicket canopy - other creatures use the sound to navigate toward safety.

stages.name: Scytling
stages.bio: Scytling is a pale round crab with large liquid eyes and small neat claws it keeps close to its body. Its shell has a soft texture that catches the light like fine sand, and it moves with a gentle rocking walk that makes it look perpetually uncertain. It lives under the wide leaves of Verdant Valley's ground-cover plants, emerging to feed on fallen song-seeds. Its large eyes see in multiple directions at once, and it has the endearing habit of going completely still and staring at things that interest it for up to two minutes without blinking.
stages.note: Scytling can remain perfectly motionless for two full minutes while staring - valley children hold contests to see who can make one blink first.

stages.name: Scytsting
stages.bio: Scytsting has grown a rough-textured golden-tan shell and developed substantial claws that it uses to dig deep burrows in Verdant Valley's softer earth. Its body has taken on an angular roughness that makes it look like a piece of valley stone that grew legs. It is strongly territorial about its burrow entrance, decorating it with a specific arrangement of pebbles it changes each season. Removing a pebble from the arrangement sends Scytsting into a visible agitated display - though it never leaves its entrance to chase the offender.
stages.note: Scytsting rearranges the pebbles at its burrow entrance precisely 24 hours after any stone is removed or added - as if correcting a record.

stages.name: Scytarch
stages.bio: Scytarch is a large, wide golden crab whose flat shell stretches broad as a cart wheel. Its thick claws are built for leverage rather than speed, capable of shifting boulders with sustained pressure. It has lived long enough in Verdant Valley that its shell has developed mineral deposits matching the valley's own rock chemistry - making it genuinely difficult to tell from a large valley boulder at rest. Young valley creatures learn to navigate around the 'boulders that breathe,' and the first time they see one move is considered a rite of passage. The guardians placed Scytarch in the valley's foundation myths as the first creature to stake a claim.
stages.note: Scytarch's shell mineral content is chemically identical to Verdant Valley bedrock - field tests cannot distinguish them without biological markers.

stages.name: Scytinch
stages.bio: Scytinch is a soft cream-white larva, its rounded segmented body tapering at both ends, tiny dark eyes peering from the broader end. It lives in the damp leaf litter of Ghost Hollow's floor where mist keeps the ground permanently soft. It feeds on shadow-saturated organic matter - old fallen leaves that the hollow's ghosts have passed through - and with each meal its pale coloring darkens slightly from the inside out. Hollow explorers find them by the faint luminescent sheen their bodies cast on wet leaves at night.
stages.note: Scytinch emits a faint pale glow on its underside that's only visible in complete darkness - hollow explorers call it 'ghost-lint.'

stages.name: Scytshell
stages.bio: Scytshell has sealed itself in a dark purple chrysalis half-buried in Ghost Hollow's rich soil - only its coiled upper body is visible, the rest anchored deep. Its shell has the dark iridescence of a mussel shell, and ghost-energy flows through it in visible slow pulses. The hollow's wandering spirits are strongly drawn to it, circling the chrysalis for hours at a time. Old hollow-keepers leave offerings of dark seeds near resting Scytshell, believing the chrysalis is protecting something important inside - a memory, a word, a name not yet given.
stages.note: Ghost sightings in Ghost Hollow increase by a measurable amount within a ten-metre radius of a resting Scytshell chrysalis.

stages.name: Scytarax
stages.bio: Scytarax emerges as a large dark rhinoceros beetle, its shell the deep black of shadow-soaked heartwood and its single massive horn curving upward with a metallic sheen. Wings fold tight against its back but open silently for flight through Ghost Hollow's canopy, where it is nearly invisible against the night sky. It carries all the shadow-memory absorbed during its chrysalis stage, and the ghosts that orbited it during dormancy now follow it at a distance - an escort of light shapes trailing behind a dark form. Guardians believed Scytarax carries the names of the lost, one for each ghost that follows.
stages.note: Scytarax has always been seen with exactly as many ghost-lights trailing it as the number of nights it spent in chrysalis - never fewer, never more.

stages.name: Seedasprite
stages.bio: A tiny round face peeks out from a ruff of five broad green leaves arranged like a starfish, with two bright red eyes glowing at the centre. Seedasprite drifts through the Light Grove at ankle height, spinning slowly as its leaves catch the breeze to sense thoughts floating on the air. Each leaf flickers when it catches a name it has never heard drifting from a child's mind. The guardians first spotted it orbiting the grove's oldest song-tree like a slow green planet.
stages.note: Spin a Seedasprite gently and it will echo back the last word you were thinking.

stages.name: Seedaunt
stages.bio: Seedaunt has grown into a wide sunburst of layered leaves edged in gold, with a brilliant ruby gem set at its heart that pulses with each thought it reads. The leaves fan outward in overlapping rings and glow faintly at their tips when Seedaunt concentrates. It hovers chest-high among the luminous clearings of the Light Grove, reading emotions the way a flower reads sunlight. Trainers who earn its trust say it can project calm feelings like warm afternoon light.
stages.note: The ruby gem at Seedaunt's centre grows brighter whenever a child nearby works out something difficult.

stages.name: Seedaryx
stages.bio: Now as wide as a shield, Seedaryx floats upright with vast interlocking leaf-wings that cast green-gold dappled shadows. Gnarled vine-roots spiral beneath it and a great ruby gem blazes at its core, surrounded by ornate twig-filigree etched over centuries. The Light Grove itself seems to breathe in rhythm with it. Ancient lore says Seedaryx once guided Akilla through the grove by lighting words like lanterns along the path - and it still does, for anyone willing to listen.
stages.note: When Seedaryx meditates, every leaf in the Light Grove turns toward it, as if the whole forest is listening.

stages.name: Serplet
stages.bio: Serplet is a small bright-green snake coiled into a neat spiral, with a round cheerful face and warm amber eyes. Tiny overlapping scales glint in the faint cave light as it watches newcomers with open curiosity. It makes its home in mossy cracks near the cave entrance where faint daylight still filters in, feeding on leaves that drift down from above. Children in the Shadow Caves learn their first tracking by matching prints to the patterns Serplet traces in the soft mud.
stages.note: Serplet always coils the same direction - change it, and it will huff and recoil immediately back the other way.

stages.name: Vipray
stages.bio: Vipray has grown into a thick-bodied serpent with bold yellow-green banding across its scales and a flattened head bearing two curved fangs it shows when threatened. It moves with deliberate S-curves through the cave tunnels, pressing its belly against cool stone. The poison it carries has a faintly floral scent - the guardians discovered it marks territory by pressing its chin to a surface and exhaling, leaving an invisible trail of herbal musk that other creatures avoid for days.
stages.note: The herbal musk Vipray leaves on a rock lasts exactly three days - locals use it as an informal cave calendar.

stages.name: Hydravex
stages.bio: Enormous and ancient, Hydravex coils in the deepest chambers of the Shadow Caves where the roots of surface trees press through the ceiling. Its scales are a deep jade-green marked by thick gold bands, and its broad head carries back-swept horns above a jaw that can spread wide enough to swallow a boulder. Venom seeps constantly from its hollow fangs, dripping into a pool below that glows faintly with bioluminescence. The guardians say it once sealed the cave mouth to protect the words stored inside from Abalont's hunger.
stages.note: The glowing pool beneath Hydravex's resting coils has never been fully mapped - explorers always turn back before they reach the far end.

stages.name: Serpyx
stages.bio: Serpyx is a slim grey-blue serpent with small golden eyes and a forked red tongue it tastes the saltwater with constantly. Its smooth scales carry the pale grey-blue of shallow coastal rock and it moves in small curious S-curves just below the tide line. Tiny fins are beginning to form near its jaw, hinting at the dragon it will become. Children snorkelling in Coral Bay sometimes find one winding around their ankles like a living ribbon before darting away into the coral.
stages.note: Serpyx tastes the water eight times a minute - researchers can measure tidal flow just by counting its tongue-flicks.

stages.name: Draskex
