stages.bio: Draskex is now an upright-rearing serpent, its pale blue scales growing into distinct ridged plates along its spine, jaws set in a permanent determined expression. It surges through Coral Bay with powerful lateral sweeps, disturbing sand clouds that billow like undersea thunderheads. A crest of small spines has appeared behind its head that fans open when it senses danger. The guardians recorded it circling a sunken memory-stone for three days without stopping, as though memorizing what was carved there.
stages.note: Draskex circles any unfamiliar object in the water exactly seven times before deciding whether it is safe.

stages.name: Hydrodrake
stages.bio: Hydrodrake is a full sea dragon - four legs, a long ridged tail, and swept-back horns above a fierce fanged jaw. Its blue-white scales carry the sheen of deep ocean where sunlight barely reaches. When it surfaces at Coral Bay a visible wake spreads to both shores, and the reef creatures go quiet. Ancient maps drawn by the guardians mark the routes it patrols as sacred channels where young learners travel safely. A sound like a breaking wave precedes every word it speaks.
stages.note: The wake Hydrodrake leaves on the surface takes nearly twenty minutes to fully settle - fishing boats use it to gauge wind direction.

stages.name: Kitsuval
stages.bio: Kitsuval is a small grey kitten with round dark eyes and a short wispy ghost-ribbon tail that drifts behind it like smoke. Its paws are soft and silent and it moves without disturbing a single leaf on the floor of Ghost Hollow. It watches travellers from behind mossy stones, flicking its transparent tail whenever it is curious. The guardians found the first one sleeping on Akilla's abandoned cloak, and they say it still guards small things that have been forgotten or left behind.
stages.note: Kitsuval never leaves a footprint - the only sign it passed through is a faint chill where it sat.

stages.name: Panthex
stages.bio: Panthex is a sleek black panther that walks upright on powerful hind legs, its glossy dark-steel coat absorbing the little light that filters through Ghost Hollow's canopy. Its forepaws are tipped with silver claws that ring faintly against stone - the only sound it makes when choosing to be heard. It patrols the hollow's border paths in long unhurried strides, and travellers who see it pass feel a sudden impulse to whisper. It has no patience for loud boasting, but respects a quiet kind of bravery.
stages.note: Panthex walks its patrol route in exactly the same order every night - local children use it as a living clock.

stages.name: Abyssrath
stages.bio: Abyssrath is massive - a broad-shouldered four-legged beast whose entire body is plated in overlapping dark-steel armour, studded with rivets that glint like cold stars. Heavy chains loop around its neck and chest, forged from shadow-iron, and its red eyes burn with ancient authority. It does not patrol; it simply stands, and the Ghost Hollow rearranges itself around it. The guardians' oldest texts name it the Gatekeeper of Forgetting - anything Abalont's shadow tried to erase, Abyssrath refused to release.
stages.note: The chains around Abyssrath's neck were never placed there by anyone - they grew from its own body as it aged.

stages.name: Shardlet
stages.bio: Shardlet is a compact dark-grey armadillo with rows of raised stone-plate scales across its back and small round eyes that peer out from a triangular wedge head. Its four sturdy legs splay wide for balance on the Crystal Mines' uneven floor. When frightened it tucks its legs and rolls into a smooth stone ball. Children working the upper tunnels use Shardlets as living test weights - if one will sleep in a corner, the rock there is stable enough to dig.
stages.note: A curled Shardlet is indistinguishable from a loose stone - miners have accidentally put them in their pockets.

stages.name: Shardbeast
stages.bio: Shardbeast has grown into a broad-chested quadruped with a broad blunt head and thick stone-plate armour covering its shoulders and haunches. Crystal fragments jut from its back like rough-cut gems and its horn has lengthened into a single forward spike it uses to wedge apart seams in the rock face. It moves with slow deliberate purpose through the Crystal Mines, its footsteps leaving shallow pits in the stone. The guardians valued it as a natural excavator - every path Shardbeast opens reveals words the old rocks have been holding.
stages.note: Every slab Shardbeast moves exposes mineral writing from the ancient earth - geologists argue whether it's pattern or language.

stages.name: Shardking
stages.bio: Shardking fills a tunnel from wall to wall, its body entirely encased in fused crystal-and-stone plate that has grown over centuries of the Crystal Mines pressing around it. Its massive horned head hangs low and forward, and its tail sweeps slowly, grinding sparks from the floor. The mines themselves seem to have adopted it - new crystal formations appear wherever Shardking rests, as though the earth is building a throne. Ancient lore says Shardking can feel the weight of every mark carved into stone throughout the entire region.
stages.note: When Shardking exhales, a fine quartz dust settles on every surface nearby - miners call it the king's blessing.

stages.name: Sharpup
stages.bio: Sharpup is a chubby little shark with navy-blue and yellow colouring and an oversized grinning jaw it can barely close. Its pectoral fins stick out like stubby wings and its eyes are wide and bright with mischief. It bobs near the surface of Coral Bay stealing shiny pebbles and bits of coral from other creatures' hoards. Trainers describe it as the reef's least-threatening scoundrel - it wants to look fierce but mostly ends up looking pleased with itself.
stages.note: Sharpup cannot resist a shiny object - it will abandon a battle mid-fight if something glints on the seafloor.

stages.name: Sharkaw
stages.bio: Sharkaw is now a full-sized powerful shark with a navy-and-gold body and a jaw lined with rows of sharp teeth it displays freely. Dorsal and pectoral fins cut the water cleanly and its dark eyes carry a calculating gleam. It circles the deeper reef channels of Coral Bay, tolerating no trespassing in its claimed territory. The guardians noted it memorizes the location of every reef creature it encounters - it returns to check on the same spot at the same hour each day, as if keeping attendance.
stages.note: Sharkaw patrols exactly the same route at the same time daily - local divers set their watches by its passing.

stages.name: Abyssjaw
stages.bio: Abyssjaw has grown beyond shark into something closer to a dragon of the deep - massive legs have pushed through its flanks, its jaw has widened to an enormous rend of gold-and-dark teeth, and its yellow eyes burn with predatory intelligence. It moves along the bottom of Coral Bay in a slow prowl, stirring up columns of sand that rise like towers. Ancient charts drawn by the guardians show the entire bay shaped around where Abyssjaw chooses to rest, as though the reef grew to accommodate it.
stages.note: The sand towers Abyssjaw raises as it walks sink back down in exactly the shape of letters - researchers are still decoding them.

stages.name: Sharkil
stages.bio: Sharkil is a stocky slate-blue shark that navigates the flooded lower tunnels of the Shadow Caves, its wide blunt snout pressing into crevices in search of the small phosphorescent creatures that live there. Its eyes are proportionally large for reading in near-darkness and its dorsal fin is slightly flattened to let it move through low passages. Children who visit the cave pools find Sharkil circling their lantern light with great interest, drawn by the brightness it almost never sees.
stages.note: Sharkil is the only cave-dwelling shark that actively seeks out light rather than avoiding it.

stages.name: Sharclaw
stages.bio: Sharclaw has developed hind legs tipped with curved claws it uses to anchor itself against the cave-tunnel currents. Its blue body is now dark as deep water and its jaw has widened, rows of teeth visible even when its mouth is closed. It rules the larger underground pools of the Shadow Caves, and the bioluminescent fish give it a wide berth. The guardians recorded it caching small objects - bone fragments, polished stones, lost tools - near the cave's oldest old carvings, as if protecting them.
stages.note: Every cache Sharclaw keeps contains exactly one polished stone among the rest - no one knows how it picks which stone.

stages.name: Megashark
stages.bio: Megashark fills the main underground river of the Shadow Caves from bank to bank, its enormous body a deep blue-black so dark it looks like a section of the cave itself has come alive. Its jaw opens to a width that could swallow a doorway and its small eyes carry the cold patience of something that has outlasted every light source this cave has ever held. When Abalont's shadow swept through the region, Megashark submerged so deep even the darkness could not find it - and the words it was guarding with it.
stages.note: The current in the Shadow Caves' main river changes direction each time Megashark turns around - it is large enough to redirect the flow.

stages.name: Sharkyte
stages.bio: Sharkyte is a small upright-standing shark with dark steel-blue scales, stubby arms that end in clawed fins, and big determined red eyes. Its small dorsal fin is rigid as sheet metal. It waddles across the shallows of Coral Bay on its tail-base with surprising confidence, inspecting anything metallic it finds on the seafloor and collecting it into small piles near its favourite rocks. Trainers say it is deeply sincere - if Sharkyte decides you are its friend, nothing in the bay will bother you.
stages.note: Sharkyte's metallic fin rings like a tuning fork when struck - reef musicians tune to it.

stages.name: Sharkonyx
stages.bio: Sharkonyx has grown into a broad-chested shark-quadruped with thick plated legs and a reinforced snout that it uses to batter through coral formations like a battering ram. Its dark blue scales have hardened into steel-edged plates that shed water in sheets. Sharkonyx patrols the deep coral channels of Coral Bay with methodical precision, cataloguing the reef in sections the way a careful scholar catalogues words. The guardians valued it as a reef engineer - passages it cleared are still used as the safest routes today.
stages.note: The passages Sharkonyx clears through coral grow back around the edges in perfect arches - local divers call them steel gates.

stages.name: Gigashark
stages.bio: The final form is colossal - Gigashark sprawls wide with an enormous plated body, four massive armoured limbs, and a head the size of a small boat, studded with protruding steel spines along the jaw ridge. Its dark blue steel-plated hide has fused into a single continuous armour. When it moves through the deep water of Coral Bay, the surface above shows its wake like a moving island. It is the bay's oldest guardian and the reef has slowly grown around it - coral polyps colonise its back fins as though they are just another kind of reef.
stages.note: Coral has grown so thick on Gigashark's dorsal fins that small fish nest there without realising what the rock they live on is.

stages.name: Finlet
stages.bio: Finlet in the Poison Marsh is a dark blue compact shark that has adapted to the murky shallow waters, its eyes narrowed against the stinging mist. It skims low through the surface film of the marsh, eating the toxic water-skaters that other creatures avoid. Its stubby legs let it haul out onto mud banks where it rests with its mouth open, letting the warm marsh air dry its teeth. Children who know the marsh paths say a Finlet following you means you are on the safe route - it avoids the patches where the ground is not solid.
stages.note: Finlet always avoids the soft mud patches - locals follow its tracks to find the safest marsh paths.

stages.name: Sharyx
stages.bio: Sharyx is a lean powerful shark-form with a low flat profile that lets it slide through the marsh reeds without disturbing them. Its blue scales carry a faint iridescent sheen from the toxic minerals it has absorbed over years in the Poison Marsh. It moves in long gliding bursts, almost never breaking the surface, and arrives at a location before you realise it was tracking you. The guardians marked the channel Sharyx uses as a reliable clean-water indicator - it always keeps to the least-contaminated flow.
stages.note: The channel Sharyx swims stays cleaner than the surrounding marsh - its passage seems to filter the water behind it.

stages.name: Megalodon
stages.bio: Megalodon rises from the deepest fens of the Poison Marsh like a continent of dark fin and jaw. Its enormous blue-dark body has evolved fins as wide as sails and a tail that fans out into sharp trailing points. It moves through the marsh mostly submerged, leaving only a dark ridge of dorsal fin visible above the toxic mist. The poison of the marsh runs through it now - it no longer tolerates any water that is not laced with the same compounds it grew up in. Ancient stories say it once swept the entire marsh clean by swimming a single lap.
stages.note: Megalodon's single lap of the Poison Marsh takes three days - plants grow back differently every time it passes.

stages.name: Shellite
stages.bio: Shellite is a tiny hermit crab carrying a smooth purple-and-white spiral shell that is nearly as large as its whole body. Two large round eyes sit atop short stalks that swivel independently, and small orange claws reach out to test every surface before it steps. It lives in the damp lower passages of the Shadow Caves, collecting shells discarded by other creatures and examining each one with serious attention before choosing a new home. Children who find one say it always has a shell that is slightly too large - it is saving room to grow.
stages.note: Shellite always selects a shell one size too large - it says, in its way, that it already knows what it will become.

stages.name: Shelkrab
stages.bio: Shelkrab has outgrown its first shell and replaced it with a larger ridged spiral shell studded with rough spines. Its orange legs have lengthened and it now walks with a broad-legged confident stance, claws raised. It has begun secreting a mild venom from the tips of its claws that it uses to mark territories on the cave walls in patterns the guardians identified as crude maps of local water channels. Those who learn to read the markings can navigate the Shadow Caves without a lantern.
stages.note: Shelkrab's claw-markings on cave walls form a working map of underground water - older ones show routes no longer accessible.

stages.name: Shelkiath
stages.bio: Shelkiath carries a massive ridged purple shell larger than a wheelbarrow, covered in twisted spines and old cave-calcite deposits from decades underground. Its six powerful legs grip the cave floor with such force it leaves claw-marks in solid stone. The venom from its claws has concentrated over the years into a potent compound - even a small drop permanently marks any surface it touches with a glowing pattern. The Shadow Caves' deepest chambers are covered floor to ceiling in Shelkiath's accumulated scratchings, a record of everything it has ever seen.
stages.note: The glow from Shelkiath's venom markings in the deepest caves is bright enough to read by, even without any other light source.

stages.name: Shellox
stages.bio: Shellox is a round dome-shaped beetle the colour of baked desert sand, with a single large amber eye on its face and six stubby legs it uses to trundle purposefully across the dunes. Its shell has a smooth mounded surface that lets desert wind slide over it without catching. It buries itself to the neck during the hottest midday hours, leaving only the top of its dome visible - which looks exactly like a small sandy rock, fooling most passers-by. Desert children collect the neat round holes Shellox leaves when it emerges each dawn as trail markers.
stages.note: The emergence-hole Shellox leaves in the sand is a perfectly round cylinder - desert travellers use a fresh one to estimate the morning hour.

stages.name: Carapox
stages.bio: Carapox has hardened its shell into segmented stone-plate armour with ridged edges that catch the wind and produce a low harmonic hum on breezy days. Its single eye has grown larger and gained a richer amber tone, and its legs are now thick and purposeful. It can roll itself into a complete sphere and tumble down dunes at remarkable speed to escape danger or to reach a cool valley faster. The guardians used the hum of its shell as a weather signal - a rising pitch meant a desert storm within the hour.
stages.note: The pitch of Carapox's shell-hum rises noticeably before a sandstorm - desert villages listen for it before securing their shutters.

stages.name: Titanox
stages.bio: Titanox is enormous - its shell now covers the entire back of a creature the size of a small cart, with complex armour plates that have fused with actual mineral deposits from the Amber Desert floor. A ring of raised stone spines circles its shell rim and its single eye glows deep amber in the desert night. When it walks, its legs press into the sand deep enough to strike the cooler damp layer beneath, and small desert plants sprout in the footsteps it leaves behind. The guardians called it the Desert's Slow Memory - patient enough to outlast any sandstorm.
stages.note: Plants grow in Titanox's footsteps within a week - desert communities plant seeds in its trail after it passes through.

stages.name: Skelplet
stages.bio: Skelplet is the skeleton of a small upright theropod dinosaur with large round amber-glowing eye sockets and tiny forearms that clutch at the air. Its exposed ribs are narrow and its small tail-bones flick nervously. Despite being entirely skeletal, it moves with surprising energy - hopping between the warm volcanic stones of the Dragon Spire and letting heat radiate up through its bones like a radiator. Children encounter it first as a small clattering sound in the dark, followed by those two amber eyes peering around a rock.
stages.note: Skelplet seeks out the warmest spot in any room and sits there for exactly an hour before moving on to the next warmest.

stages.name: Skelptor
stages.bio: Skelptor stands upright on powerful hind legs with the full ribcage and spine of a mid-sized theropod, eye sockets burning with deep amber fire. Its forearms are small but its jaws are substantial, lined with individual bone-teeth that clack impressively when it opens wide. It climbs the Dragon Spire's lava-rock shelves at night, apparently drawn to stored heat, pressing its entire skeleton against warm surfaces like it is recharging. The guardians found old etchings showing Skelptor guarding the Spire's flame-carved memory-stones after Akilla's fall.
stages.note: Skelptor's jaw produces a specific clacking rhythm when it is content - locals transcribed it and found it matches an ancient drum-prayer.

stages.name: Skelphadon
stages.bio: Skelphadon is a magnificent terror - a full-sized skeletal theropod with a sweeping thick tail, a huge armoured skull, and fire burning in both eye sockets that casts orange light across the entire Dragon Spire. Its ribcage has broadened and new bone-plates have grown over the joints, giving it a plated war-armour look. When it opens its jaws, a gust of hot air carries ash from somewhere inside the chest cavity. The guardians say it was already ancient when the Spire was first settled - it has watched every guardian pass through and waited for each one to return.
stages.note: The heat from Skelphadon's eye-fire can be felt three body-lengths away - Dragon Spire nights are always slightly warmer wherever it walks.

stages.name: Skyveep
stages.bio: Skyveep is a fluffy round blue chick with stubby wings it flaps with enormous enthusiasm and a tiny open beak it cheeps through constantly. Its round body is sky-blue and its small wing-tips are just beginning to show the white-edged feathers that will come later. It lives in the upper reaches of the Gale Ridge where the wind is almost always blowing, and it leans into gusts with clear delight, letting them ruffle every feather before snapping them flat again. Trainers say it is the noisiest small creature in the entire region.
stages.note: Skyveep cheeps exactly once for every metre of altitude it gains - climbers use it to measure how high they have come.

stages.name: Skywing
stages.bio: Skywing is a proud hawk-form with white-and-blue plumage, broad fanning wings it holds spread to catch every thermal, and keen golden eyes that track movement two cliff-faces away. It rides the updrafts of the Gale Ridge in long slow circles, occasionally diving to inspect something below with a sharp scream. Its feathers have developed a water-resistant oil that lets it fly straight through rain clouds without losing any altitude. The guardians relied on its flight paths to predict which routes through the Ridge would be safe on storm days.
stages.note: Skywing always turns into the wind before calling out - its cry travels three times further downwind than any other call in the Ridge.

stages.name: Skyverath
stages.bio: Skyverath is a magnificent eagle of storm and current, its broad white-and-blue wings spanning wide enough to block the sun from the Ridge's summit. Its golden eyes carry a calm authority and its talons are hooked and powerful. When it spreads its wings fully, the wind changes direction around it - a localized weather phenomenon that guardians mapped and named after it. It is said to know every sound carved on the Ridge's stone pillars simply from reading them at full speed during its daily circuits of the summit.
stages.note: When Skyverath spreads its wings at the summit, the wind on all four sides of the Ridge shifts in sequence - like the turning of a page.

stages.name: Slowth
stages.bio: Slowth is a small round-faced sloth with light green fur patched in darker moss green, and a perpetually contented drowsy expression. Its long curved claws hold it to the bark of any surface it reaches and it seems perfectly happy wherever it ends up. It moves at a pace that makes watching grass grow feel urgent, but once it settles on a branch or a friendly shoulder it radiates a calm that the whole Bug Thicket seems to absorb. Children who spend time near Slowth consistently score better at recalling long words - nobody is certain why.
stages.note: Slowth blinks exactly once every forty seconds - researchers use it as a reliable timer when their instruments are wet.

stages.name: Boughling
stages.bio: Boughling hangs from a branch with all four long limbs, its green-and-brown fur now thick with actual living moss that has colonised its back. Small leaf-sprigs poke from between its shoulders and its rounded face wears an expression of serene focus. It spends most of its time suspended upside-down high in the Bug Thicket canopy, slowly turning to face whichever direction the light is coming from. Trainers who travel with it report that their sleep improves significantly - something in the rhythmic slow breathing seems to quiet everything around it.
stages.note: Boughling's breathing rate - one breath per two minutes - has been used by doctors in the Bug Thicket to calibrate calm.

stages.name: Canopyth
stages.bio: Canopyth stands on four vast earth-brown limbs, its entire body covered in a dense living canopy of moss, mushrooms, flowering vines, and small trees that have grown through its fur over centuries. Antler-like branches crown its broad head and blossoms bloom across its shoulders in season. It moves so rarely that the Bug Thicket's map treats its resting position as a fixed landmark. When it does move, the entire forest canopy shifts with it. The guardians believed it was the Bug Thicket itself given form - a creature that had simply decided to remember everything.
stages.note: Three different species of bird nest exclusively in Canopyth's antlers and are never found anywhere else in the entire Bug Thicket.

stages.name: Slugmaw
stages.bio: Slugmaw is a plump pale slug with purple-and-white stripes running lengthwise along its soft body and two gentle eyestalks that bob as it moves. It glides on a silver foot-trail across the mossy floors of the Light Grove, leaving a faint shimmering path that catches the morning light. Its trail has mild psychic residue in it - small creatures that follow a Slugmaw path often arrive feeling unexpectedly cheerful. It is drawn to the sound of unfamiliar names being spoken, gathering silently under the trees where children practise their lessons.
stages.note: The trail Slugmaw leaves glows faintly for one hour - children in the Light Grove use fresh trails as reading lamps for dawn lessons.

stages.name: Gastroplex
stages.bio: Gastroplex has grown a small ridged spiral shell on its back that it cannot retreat into but uses as an amplifier for the psychic pulses it now emits deliberately. The purple stripes on its body have deepened and tiny frilled edges have appeared along its sides that it fans to slow itself on downhill slopes. It moves through the Light Grove with gentle authority, its trail now broad enough to walk along comfortably. The grove's song-trees lean slightly toward any path it has recently crossed, as though the soil carries an afterglow.
stages.note: Song-trees in the Light Grove lean measurably toward Gastroplex's old trail-paths - grove-keepers reroute them to shape the trees.

stages.name: Gastromorph
stages.bio: Gastromorph has transformed into something extraordinary - a large upright form trailing sweeping frilled tentacles that billow around it like a living skirt of purple and white. Its eyestalks have lengthened dramatically and carry a deep violet glow. The frills pulse with psychic light and the air around Gastromorph shimmers at the edges, bending light slightly the way heat does over hot sand. In the Light Grove it is regarded as a philosopher-creature - it moves to wherever an argument is being had and sits quietly until the participants reach agreement on their own.
stages.note: Arguments near Gastromorph rarely last more than twelve minutes - the purple light seems to make sharp edges go soft.

stages.name: Solkit
stages.bio: Solkit is a bright golden-yellow rabbit with long upright ears that catch the storm-spire wind and large vivid red eyes that hold the steady warmth of a carried sun. It holds its forepaws together in a ready posture and watches everything with focused attention. At high altitude its golden coat shines noticeably brighter, and travellers on the Storm Spire claim seeing it in the distance helps them find their direction even in cloud. It races the high winds Jack the raven once watched from above, carrying a little sun into every storm it enters.
stages.note: Solkit's ears glow faintly in thick cloud - mountain rescuers in the Storm Spire follow those two amber lights when visibility fails.

stages.name: Solhare
stages.bio: Solhare stands upright on strong hind legs with a muscular build and golden-amber fur that catches the light like polished metal. Its long ears are tipped in bright gold and its red eyes have deepened to a determined gleam. The claws on its forepaws have sharpened and it holds them in a ready fighting stance. It trains in the highest wind-lashed platforms of the Storm Spire, using the resistance of the gale to strengthen its strikes. The guardians wrote that Solhare arrives whenever someone faces something too large for them alone.
stages.note: Solhare always arrives from the upwind direction - storm navigators say you can predict its approach by the way the clouds suddenly part.

stages.name: Solarch
stages.bio: Solarch is a blazing figure - a tall upright golden-armoured hare with a full brilliant mane of golden light trailing behind its ears like a comet tail, one arm raised in a strike pose that burns bright enough to cast shadows behind you. Its entire body radiates steady warm light that cannot be put out. On the Storm Spire summit, Solarch's glow is visible from the valley below as a fixed golden star on the peak - the one light that Abalont's shadow never managed to reach. It carries the memory of every brave word spoken by every child who climbed up after the guardians.
stages.note: The light from Solarch at the summit is listed on storm-spire navigation charts as a permanent landmark - it has not gone out in recorded history.

stages.name: Solarix
stages.bio: Solarix is a compact golden-blue fawn with upright pointed ears, a swept-back mane of electric-yellow fur, and large bright eyes that carry a small star-spark in each one. Its coat crackles faintly with static when it trots across the high stone paths of the Storm Spire. It picks up speed quickly and turns sharply, using the wind to assist rather than resist its movement. The guardians' young scouts used to race Solarix across the spire's flat-top platforms - it always ran directly into the prevailing wind, leaning forward with complete commitment.
stages.note: Solarix's mane stands fully upright exactly four seconds before a lightning strike - storm-spire children use it as a warning bell.

stages.name: Asteron
stages.bio: Asteron has grown into a proud and powerful stag with a full mane of deep blue-gold electric fur and a single lightning-bolt shaped growth at the tip of its tail. Its eyes hold steady twin star-sparks and its coat now discharges small visible sparks during rapid acceleration. It gallops the Storm Spire ridgelines at full speed, mane streaming, and the air behind it carries the sharp clean smell of ozone for minutes after. The guardians timed Asteron's ridge runs and found it always travels faster on days when a name it has never heard is spoken for the first time in the region.
stages.note: The ozone trail Asteron leaves on a ridge run lasts forty minutes - early-rising travellers use it to tell which routes were safe at dawn.

stages.name: Heliarch
stages.bio: Heliarch stands at the Storm Spire summit in a permanent corona of blue-gold electric light, its magnificent full mane billowing with contained lightning. A large golden star-gem blazes at its chest and four great electric feather-wings of storm-light fan from its shoulders. Its eyes are twin suns. When it rears up and cries out, the storm above the Spire responds - clouds rotate, lightning follows the arcs of its movement. The guardians called it the Voice of the Spire - whatever Heliarch announces to the sky, the sky confirms.
stages.note: When Heliarch rears and calls at the summit, a visible lightning arc follows the exact arc of its raised foreleg - every time, without exception.

stages.name: Specklet
stages.bio: Specklet is a small compact bird in deep blue-purple feathers with a short tail and a single glowing ember floating above its head on a wisp of blue flame. Its small wings are held half-open and its round eyes carry a distant, slightly dreaming quality. It hops through the Psychic Temple's lower paths, pausing to stare at empty spaces where it is clearly seeing something no one else can. Children who follow Specklet claim it always stops at spots where something interesting is about to happen - nobody has disproved this.
stages.note: Specklet stops and stares at a spot for exactly three seconds before something unusual happens there - temple-keepers have learned to pay attention.

stages.name: Spectreel
stages.bio: Spectreel has grown a magnificent fanned tail of deep blue-violet with silver-eye markings that seem to shift and turn of their own accord. When it spreads the tail fully, the eye-spots all focus simultaneously in the same direction - and whatever they are looking at becomes slightly visible through solid objects for a moment. It walks the Psychic Temple with graceful unhurried authority, tail sweeping. The guardians wrote that looking into Spectreel's fanned tail too long was inadvisable - not dangerous, just deeply distracting for several hours afterward.
stages.note: Staring into Spectreel's fan for more than ten seconds causes vivid memory replays for up to two hours - never unpleasant, always educational.

stages.name: Plumelux
stages.bio: Ancient texts name it the Keeper of the Unsaid - everything thought but never spoken aloud, held safe in the eyes of its tail.
stages.note: The eye-patterns in Plumelux's tail rearrange themselves slightly each day - no two mornings are identical, and long-term watchers claim the pattern means something.

stages.name: Spectril
stages.bio: Spectril is an adorable pale-lavender manta ray that drifts through the Ghost Hollow as though swimming in invisible water, its flat body gently undulating and a long slender tail curling behind it. Its large round eyes are set close together giving it a permanently friendly expression and it approaches newcomers directly, apparently unafraid. It passes through solid branches without disturbing them. Children in the Ghost Hollow keep one as a companion by sitting very still - Spectril will drift down and settle on a shoulder like a sleeping wish.
stages.note: Spectril will drift right through a solid object if it decides the shortest path goes there - it simply does not register walls as obstacles.

stages.name: Spectraith
stages.bio: Spectraith has grown into a full manta-ray wraith with two prominent horns curving above its face and a mischievous expression that masks sharp intelligence. Its lavender body is now edged in darker violet along the fins and it flies higher through Ghost Hollow's canopy, occasionally diving to investigate things it senses from above. When it hovers it rotates slowly, horns tilting, as though reading the air. The guardians' field notes describe it appearing at the edge of any situation where someone was about to make an important decision - as if it wanted to observe the outcome.
stages.note: Spectraith appears at decision points without fail - guardians began using its arrival as a prompt to think more carefully before choosing.

stages.name: Spectralyx
stages.bio: Spectralyx is vast and otherworldly - a great winged manta-form in deep purple with a mane of drifting tentacles behind its head and a jewelled diamond gem blazing at its chest. Its body ripples at the edges as though the boundary between it and the air is not fully decided. It circles the highest points of Ghost Hollow in silence so complete that every other sound in the hollow pauses when it passes. The guardians called it the Mirror of What Was - a creature that reflected back to each viewer a memory of something they once knew but had let go of.
stages.note: Looking directly at Spectralyx for more than a moment causes immediate recall of one forgotten memory - always a useful one.

stages.name: Shadolt
stages.bio: Shadolt is a compact black foal with a short dark-purple mane and tail that lift and drift like smoke when the Lava Crater's heat rises beneath it. Its red eyes glow steadily in the volcanic dark. It trots across the cooled lava flats with surprising nimbleness, occasionally stopping to paw at the ground where heat vents hiss beneath the surface. Children who encounter it say it watches them steadily without blinking for longer than is comfortable, then suddenly trots off - and the direction it goes is always toward the safest path through the crater.
stages.note: Shadolt always trots away toward the safest exit from the Lava Crater - lava-zone guides follow it without question.

stages.name: Nightmane
stages.bio: Nightmane is a powerful black stallion with a full purple-smoke mane that streams fire-edged behind it at full gallop. Its red eyes have deepened to a burning intensity and hooves strike the lava rock with enough force to leave scorched prints. It circles the active crater rim at night, and the violet fire in its mane lights the outer edges of the Lava Crater in a slow purple glow. The guardians recorded that Nightmane's presence near a flame vent increases its output - as if the dark fire in its blood calls to the fire below.
stages.note: Flame vents near Nightmane's patrol path run 30% hotter than equivalent vents elsewhere in the Lava Crater.

stages.name: Phantorvex
stages.bio: Phantorvex is a magnificent terror of the Lava Crater - a great black stallion wreathed entirely in violet-purple flames that pour from its mane, tail, and hooves in long cascading streams. Its eyes blaze with ancient fire and its nostrils trail dark smoke. When it runs the full crater rim, the trail of purple fire it leaves lingers for hours, visible from the valley below as a ring of violet light. The guardians say Phantorvex was present at Abalont's first shadow-fall - it watched from the crater edge, then turned and set every fire-marker in the region burning to warn the others.
stages.note: The fire-ring Phantorvex leaves running the full crater rim lasts six hours - Lava Crater communities use it as a nightly clock.

stages.name: Spectulp
stages.bio: A tiny lavender jellyfish no wider than a hand, Spectulp drifts through the shadow caves with a single wide eye dominating its pale bell. Four wispy translucent tentacles trail beneath it like pale ribbons, and a faint spiral pattern swirls along its cap. It is nearly weightless, carried wherever cave drafts wish. The guardians called it a wandering thought - something that had not yet decided what it wanted to become. It lingers near glowing crystal walls, staring at its own reflection for hours.
stages.note: Spectulp will follow any light source for up to thirty minutes before drifting off again.

stages.name: Wispulse
stages.bio: Growing to roughly knee height, Wispulse has a rounded purple-tinged bell etched with swirling markings and eight long tentacles that fan outward and downward. Its single large eye has deepened from pale to violet, and a faint bioluminescent glow pulses along each tentacle tip. It moves with surprising deliberateness - choosing its path rather than drifting - and has been seen pressing a tentacle tip against cave walls as though reading something written there long ago.
stages.note: Each tentacle tip glows a different shade when Wispulse is concentrating; explorers use the colour to guess its mood.

stages.name: Thanatopus
stages.bio: Thanatopus has shed the jellyfish grace of its youth and expanded into a looming skull-faced form: a broad grey-blue domed head carved with hollow eye sockets, a wide grimacing mouth, and eight thick muscular tentacles that writhe and grip cave stone with ease. Its appearance is solemn rather than threatening - old explorers say it guards the deepest shadow cave passages where Abalont's whispers still echo, and that it lets only those who know a name it has never heard pass unimpeded.
stages.note: The shadow caves fall completely silent when Thanatopus extends all eight tentacles flat - a warning the deep passage is sealed.

stages.name: Phantkit
stages.bio: A tiny white-furred kit with alert blue eyes and two neat upright ears, Phantkit trots the poison marsh edges with surprising confidence for something so small. Its fur is almost luminous against the dark reeds, and a small bushy white tail flicks behind it. Newly hatched in the murk of the poison marsh, it does not yet understand the dangers around it - instead it pounces on reflections in the dark water, convinced something lives just beneath the surface.
stages.note: Phantkit's paw-prints glow faintly blue-white for several minutes after it walks on damp mud.

stages.name: Spectryx
stages.bio: Spectryx has grown into a lean, long-legged fox with silver-grey fur and a thick, sweeping tail that carries a faint purple sheen at its tips. Its eyes are still vivid blue but now hold a calm, calculating look. It moves between the rotting trees of the poison marsh without stirring a single dead leaf, and other creatures part the water to let it pass. Older marsh folk say Spectryx carries small riddles in its mind and will share one if you sit still long enough.
stages.note: Spectryx can hold perfectly still for up to two hours, so motionless that marsh birds sometimes land on its back.

stages.name: Phantomyx
stages.bio: Phantomyx stands as tall as a doorway, its brilliant white fur now threaded through with crackling purple-dark energy that forms a wild mane and blazing tail plume. Several trailing tails sweep behind it like slow flames, each tipped in deep violet. It strides the poison marsh as though the toxins are merely damp grass, and its gaze alone can still the chittering of marsh insects for a hundred metres. Those who have looked into its eyes speak of seeing a map of everywhere they have ever been.
stages.note: Phantomyx sheds one glowing fur every full moon; marsh villagers frame these in birchwood for good fortune.

stages.name: Shadowpup
stages.bio: A chunky charcoal-grey pup with a stocky body, two red glowing eyes, and a little spiked ruff of fur that stands up when it is excited, Shadowpup pads through the dark forest like a small storm cloud. Its red eyes see perfectly in zero light, and it spends most nights chasing shadows it mistakes for playmates. The guardians once called these pups the forest's laughter - small, boisterous, and utterly unafraid of the dark that frightens everyone else.
stages.note: Shadowpup can extinguish a candle flame just by staring at it from two paces away.

stages.name: Specwolf
stages.bio: Specwolf has grown lean and angular, its dark fur now split with a wild spiky mane along its spine and a swept-back crest above its glowing red eyes. Four sturdy legs carry it through the dark forest at silent speed - its paws make no sound even on dry leaves. A faint violet aura pulses around its mane when it is alert. It patrols a fixed territory of roughly fifty trees, and any creature that breaks a promise it has made will find Specwolf sitting in its path.
stages.note: Specwolf's fur absorbs moonlight and releases it slowly over the next day as a faint violet glow.

stages.name: Phantomaw
stages.bio: Phantomaw is all dark mass and controlled fury: a huge wolf with charcoal-black fur, an enormous spined mane, and twin wings of deep violet-blue ghost-flame that unfurl when it howls. Its red eyes are set deep beneath a heavy brow, and two curved tusks jut from its lower jaw. The ground does not quite hold its weight the way it should - it steps as if gravity is a suggestion. In the darkest groves of the dark forest, the guardians placed Phantomaw to hold the boundary Abalont cannot cross.
stages.note: When Phantomaw howls at midnight, every leaf in a hundred-metre circle falls silently to the ground at once.

stages.name: Spiklet
stages.bio: Spiklet is a tight ball of ice-blue crystalline spines radiating in every direction, with two small glinting eyes peeking out from the dense cluster. It rolls along the frost-shattered scree where cold air pools against sun-warmed stone, and every spine is razor-edged and faintly luminous. It cannot move fast, but nothing in the peaks wants to nudge it either. The Guardians of Frozen Peaks once used these little balls as lanterns through the longest winter nights.
stages.note: Spiklet can retract all its spines at once and drop into a snow hollow in under a second when it senses danger.

stages.name: Spiconid
stages.bio: Spiconid has flattened into a wide low body plated in dark grey-blue armour, its spines now longer and arranged in dense overlapping rows along its flanks and back. It moves slowly across the high scree, ploughing a clear furrow through the frost. The spines at its front are slightly longer and angled forward, used to wedge apart stones to reach the frost-algae it eats. Young snow-hares use it as a moving shelter, darting between its spines while Spiconid remains entirely unbothered.
stages.note: A single Spiconid spine, once broken off, regrows to full length in exactly eleven days.

stages.name: Crystallurk
stages.bio: Crystallurk barely fits through most cave mouths in Frozen Peaks: a massive low-slung armoured body bristling with enormous ice-blue spines grown thick as stalactites, packed so densely that its body is almost invisible beneath them. Its eyes are slitted and cold, scanning the ice shelf with patient intelligence. When Abalont's influence tried to freeze the whole range solid, Crystallurk was already there - holding the cold in one place so the rest of the range stayed liveable.
stages.note: Crystallurk's outer spine layer is hollow; on calm nights you can hear the mountain wind whistle through it.

stages.name: Spikpup
stages.bio: A stocky tan-and-dark pup with a wide spiky mane of coarse fur that sticks up like desert scrub, Spikpup has the heavy shoulders and low stance of something that will one day be much harder to knock over. Its golden-brown eyes are wary and quick. It digs shallow dens in sand dune slopes at dawn, marking each one with a scratch pattern, then forgets which one it used. The other creatures of the sand dunes give it a wide berth - even at this size, its jaw pressure is startling.
stages.note: Spikpup can bite through sandstone pebbles; trainers sometimes find small quarried rocks stacked near its sleeping spot.

stages.name: Spikfang
stages.bio: Spikfang has grown into a sleek, long-legged predator with dark tawny fur, a thick spiky mane spreading from neck to mid-back, and a sweeping tail. Its fangs are now prominent, slightly longer than its lip, and faintly darker than its teeth. It hunts at dusk when the sand dunes cast the longest shadows, using the crests of dunes to stay low and invisible until the last moment. It carries a pebble in each cheek when at rest - no one has ever figured out why.
stages.note: Spikfang always approaches downwind and will circle a target three times before deciding to move closer.

stages.name: Spikmaul
stages.bio: Spikmaul stands at shoulder height to a tall adult, its enormous spiky mane now fanned wide and bristling with dark-tipped guard hairs that catch desert light like iron filings. Three heavy tails sweep behind it, and its deep-set golden eyes evaluate everything with the patience of someone who has never once lost. The sand dunes record its passing in a chain of deep prints - its weight sinks a paw-width into packed sand. The dune guardians say Spikmaul's roar settles the shifting sands when storms move them.
stages.note: Spikmaul's footprints fill with rainwater that stays fresh for three days longer than any other puddle.

stages.name: Frostquill
stages.bio: A small round porcupine-shaped creature with a pale grey-blue body and a full coat of short ice-tipped quills that rattle when it walks, Frostquill huddles on the lower ridges of storm spire where the cold winds begin. Its tiny face peers out between front quills with dark round eyes. When frightened, all its quills fan outward at once with a sound like a handful of icicles dropped on stone. It finds warmth by burrowing under the frost-moss that clings to spire rocks.
stages.note: On cold mornings Frostquill's quill tips grow tiny ice crystals that it shakes off before breakfast like frost off a window.

stages.name: Spiklix
stages.bio: Spiklix has grown taller and denser, its body now a thick barrel shape packed with long blue-white quills that have hardened to near-stone density at their bases. It stands its ground against storm spire winds without moving - quills angled backward to cut drag. When it rolls into a ball, the outer quill layer locks together like slate tiles, making it nearly impossible to unroll by force. It is said that the strongest storm spire gusts have never once pushed a curled Spiklix off a ledge.
stages.note: Spiklix can fire three quills with enough force to embed them a thumb-width deep in granite.

stages.name: Glacispine
stages.bio: Glacispine fills a doorway. Its body has broadened into a wide low mass of interlocking ice-stone quills so dense and long that its legs are barely visible beneath them, and its face - a narrow pair of cold eyes and a flat stone-grey nose - is almost completely hidden in the quill forest. The quills have fused at their bases into ridge-like plates. Older storm spire folk say that when Glacispine stamps once, every loose ice shard on the spire face falls at once - clearing the path for those who dare to climb.
stages.note: Each of Glacispine's outer quills has a different ice crystal pattern at its tip - no two have ever been found identical.

stages.name: Spikkit
stages.bio: A small cream-and-tan feline-shaped creature with a bright blue electric-charged crest of spines fanning above its head like a crown, Spikkit scrambles along the low granite ledges of granite heights with quick nimble paws. Its blue eyes crackle slightly when it blinks. When two Spikkits meet and press crests together, the resulting static pop can stun a fly at two paces. They sleep coiled in shallow granite bowls worn smooth by centuries of their ancestors before them.
stages.note: Spikkit's crest discharges with a visible blue flash every time it sneezes, which happens often in dusty granite tunnels.

stages.name: Spikard
stages.bio: Spikard has stretched into a lean spotted lynx with broad paws and a long electric-spined mane that now runs from head to mid-back and crackles with visible blue arcs when it moves quickly. Its body shows dark leopard spots on tawny fur. It hunts by driving prey toward granite cliff edges, then arcing a charge between its extended front paws to stun rather than harm - it seems to prefer live catches. The granite heights carry its static signature days after it passes a particular ledge.
stages.note: Metal tools left on rock near a resting Spikard will slowly drift toward it over several hours - pulled by residual static.

stages.name: Spikarch
stages.bio: Spikarch is a towering armoured beast on four massive legs, its body covered in layered stone-grey scales shot through with blue-electric veins, a vast ridge of electric spines running its full length from crown to tail. Its deep gold eyes sit behind a heavy stone brow and watch the granite heights with absolute ownership. When it exhales, small sparks drop from its jaw. The guardians of granite heights built their signal towers in the shape of Spikarch's crest, knowing lightning would follow the same lines.
stages.note: The granite directly beneath Spikarch's favourite resting boulder has been fused to glass - smoothed by years of slow discharge.

stages.name: Lionfin
stages.bio: Lionfin is a vivid little lionfish - brilliant red and white vertical stripes across a compact body, with a fan of long venomous spines spreading above and around it like a tiny crown. Its large purple eye watches everything with bright suspicion. It drifts near coral bay's shallower reef heads, barely moving unless something comes too close, at which point the spine fan snaps wide. Reef fish twice its size give it a lane of clear water. The guardians say Lionfin's colour warns: 'I have something to teach, and it may sting.'
stages.note: Lionfin can hold perfectly still for over an hour and is frequently mistaken for a piece of stinging coral by passing fish.

stages.name: Spinfin
stages.bio: Spinfin has grown into a bold, full-bodied lionfish with an extravagant fan of white-edged pectoral fins spreading wide on both sides and a full dorsal spine array. Its red-and-white stripes deepen toward crimson, and its large eye holds a steady purple glow. It moves through coral bay mid-water with slow wing-like fin sweeps, ruling a patch of reef with complete confidence. Smaller creatures never challenge it directly - they simply reroute. In the bay's old tales it represents a word once forgotten that returns with twice the force.
stages.note: Spinfin's venom changes flavour with the season - bitter in winter, sharp in summer - and reef researchers taste-test it with extreme caution.

stages.name: Spinaryx
stages.bio: Spinaryx wears a crown of long ornate spines that trail like royal ribbons, its body now a deep crimson-violet with purple-tipped fan fins that spread wider than a child's arm-span on each side. A faint toxic shimmer surrounds it in the water. It moves rarely and only with purpose, and when it does the entire reef falls still. In coral bay legend, Spinaryx holds the memories of every creature that ever learned something and passed it on - each spine tip carries a word the reef will not let be forgotten.
stages.note: The water within an arm's length of Spinaryx glows faintly purple at night - enough to read by if you hold a page very still.

stages.name: Spinule
stages.bio: Spinule is a plump little orange-gold fish with a trio of purple-tipped psychic spines jutting from its head like a tiny antennae array. Its single wide purple eye catches Light Grove's canopy glow and reflects it back doubled. It lives in the shallow stream-pools beneath the light grove's glowing trees, and its spines pulse whenever it hears a name it has never heard spoken nearby. The grove's light seems to flow into it - it is slightly brighter on sunny days than on cloudy ones.
stages.note: Spinule's spines vibrate at a frequency only young children can hear; they often find it before adults do.

stages.name: Spinara
stages.bio: Spinara has broadened into a proper lionfish silhouette but dressed in green-gold with sweeping fan fins that catch dappled Light Grove sunlight filtering through the canopy. Its body stripes are vivid against bright fins, and its pectoral fans spread horizontally wide. A gentle psychic resonance follows it through the water - Light Grove creatures seem to grow calmer when it swims nearby, and children who splash in the streams where it lives tend to remember unfamiliar names more easily.
stages.note: Spinara memorises the surface patterns of every leaf that falls into its pool - over time it knows if the grove above is healthy.

stages.name: Spinamorph
stages.bio: Spinamorph is spectacular: a large deep-bodied fish surrounded by a full corona of long trailing spines and fins in magenta, purple, and gold, its broad pectoral fins sweeping like a flowing robe. Its eye carries a deep violet glow, and the water around it shimmers faintly as though light is bending. It rises from Light Grove's deepest spring pool only when the grove is in need - and every time it surfaces, the trees nearest the water grow an inch that same day.
stages.note: The pool Spinamorph lives in is twelve degrees warmer than all surrounding water - warmed, the grove folk believe, by concentrated thoughts.

stages.name: Spiramite
stages.bio: A small purple chameleon with a thick coiled tail curled against its body, Spiramite watches the bug thicket through wide amber-gold eyes that move independently. Its round spotted body has a spiral marking on its flank that glows faintly when it is thinking hard - which appears to be always. It changes its skin between two shades of purple rather than a full colour range, which makes it easy to spot for those who know where to look. It eats only the brightly coloured bugs it has seen at least twice before.
stages.note: Spiramite counts to three before doing anything - blink, step, or eat - as though checking something no one else can see.

stages.name: Spiramor
stages.bio: Spiramor has broadened into a stocky, low-bellied form closer to a toad than a chameleon, its four splayed legs gripping bug thicket bark with wide padded toes. Its body is deep purple-grey, densely spotted, and its belly sits close to branches. The spiral marking has grown into a full pattern across its back. A long sticky tongue capable of crossing two arm-spans snaps out when it detects psychic resonance from the insects it hunts. It never misses - not because of speed, but because it anticipated the movement seconds before it happened.
stages.note: Spiramor positions itself in the exact same spot each morning and afternoon, as if reading a schedule only it can see.

stages.name: Spiramarch
stages.bio: Spiramarch is a broad, heavy creature with a wide flat skull, four powerful stubby legs, and a body covered in deep spiral whorls of purple-violet that seem to rotate slowly when you watch too long. Its amber eyes have grown enormous. It moves rarely, spending most of its time anchored to a large bug thicket branch with all four feet gripping, reading the psychic noise of the forest around it. When Abalont tried to poison the thicket's words, Spiramarch sat still at the forest's heart and filtered every bad thought until the thicket grew quiet.
stages.note: The spiral patterns on Spiramarch's skin shift position by three degrees each full moon - mappers who sketch it carefully can track the seasons by them.

stages.name: Spirpup
stages.bio: A tan-and-brown wolf pup with a round spiral marking on its chest and bright amber eyes, Spirpup has the alert, chest-forward posture of a creature that has decided it is in charge of something but hasn't worked out what yet. Its fur is soft but already shows the layered mane that will grow larger with age. It was born in the ghost hollow at a crossing where dark and light balance - the guardians say it is proof that shadow and courage come from the same place.
stages.note: Spirpup sits with its back to every wall it finds - it refuses to ever have something approach from behind.

stages.name: Spirwolf
stages.bio: Spirwolf stands strong and broad-chested, its tawny-brown fur now featuring a full layered mane and haunches marked with deep spiral rune patterns that faintly glow amber when it uses its hero spirit. Its amber eyes are steady - it does not look for threats, it simply already knows where they are. Spirwolf has been seen leading younger hollow creatures out of the darkest ghost hollow paths, not by fighting what lurks there but by walking without hesitation and letting the darkness decide to step aside.
stages.note: Spirwolf's paw-prints briefly glow amber for ten seconds after it passes - enough light to follow safely in total darkness.

stages.name: Spirion
stages.bio: Spirion is massive and patient, a full-maned wolf with a layered golden-brown coat swept back from a broad face, tail and mane fanning out like a living banner. Deep spiral runes glow steadily across its flanks, and its amber eyes carry the calm of a creature that has faced everything the ghost hollow had to offer and found it manageable. It holds the hollow's boundary between shadow and light - not by force but by being the most unmovable thing in it.
stages.note: Every creature that passes through the ghost hollow in Spirion's company arrives at their destination ten minutes faster than expected.

stages.name: Coilbug
stages.bio: Coilbug is a small golden-shelled creature, round as a bun with a spiral shell marking on its back and six stubby legs tucked underneath. Its shell catches every scrap of verdant valley sunlight and sends it back as a warm glow. It moves with slow, rolling determination - always in a straight line until it bumps something, then picks a new direction without any visible frustration. The guardians of verdant valley called it the valley's coin - something small, bright, and worth finding.
stages.note: Coilbug's shell produces a faint golden light at night, just enough to show what's directly beneath it.

stages.name: Hornbeetle
stages.bio: Hornbeetle has grown into a proper large beetle with a gleaming gold-amber carapace, six strong legs, and a single curved horn rising from its head. The spiral on its shell has been integrated into the carapace plating as a raised ridge. It walks with a low centre of gravity and a swinging, sure-footed gait. It carries dung-ball sized objects for other verdant valley creatures when asked - nobody quite knows why, but it seems to find the work satisfying. Its horn catches morning light and throws a small sunrise onto the grass each dawn.
stages.note: Hornbeetle pushes a perfect sphere of golden leaf-pollen wherever it walks, growing larger until it decides to bury it.

stages.name: Spirolith
stages.bio: Spirolith is enormous - a towering golden armoured beetle standing upright on four thick legs with two powerful forelimbs held forward. Its carapace is engraved with deep spiral runic patterns that pulse with warm light when it takes a slow breath. A massive curved horn crowns its head. It anchors itself at the centre of verdant valley during solstices, and every creature in the valley instinctively gathers near it - not out of fear but because its golden light makes unfamiliar names feel possible.
stages.note: When Spirolith beats its wings - once a year, at midsummer - the entire valley hears a single deep resonant chime that lasts thirty seconds.

stages.name: Spirlet
stages.bio: Spirlet is a round-bellied small monkey with warm brown fur, big blue eyes full of wonder, and a thick coiled tail with a golden glow at its tip that spins slowly like a living spiral. It clings to the lower steel fortress walls, curious about every bolt and rivet. Small blue electric sparks flick from its fur when it gets excited - which is often. It was one of the first creatures drawn to the steel fortress not by the cold metal but by the warm hum of electricity in the walls.
stages.note: Spirlet taps metal surfaces with its knuckle three times before touching them with its palm - always checking the charge first.

stages.name: Spirax
stages.bio: Spirax has grown lean and tall for a monkey, with long arms and hard-knuckled fists that crackle with blue electric charge. Its brown fur is shot through with lightning-pale highlights, and blue arcs jump between its hands when it holds them close. It trains alone in the steel fortress courtyards, throwing punch combinations at nothing - its knuckles strike invisible targets with enough static to singe scorchmarks into the metal walls. Other fortress creatures know to clear the yard when Spirax starts its morning routine.
stages.note: The steel fortress floor near Spirax's training spot has permanent scorch rings from ten thousand static punches.

stages.name: Spirarch
stages.bio: Spirarch is built like a fortress itself: a massive broad-shouldered ape with thick gold-armoured arms ringed in deep electric coils, a wide chest, and two enormous gold-banded fists perpetually wreathed in arcing lightning. Its amber eyes carry absolute focus. It stands at the steel fortress's highest rampart in all weather - lightning rods in the towers were placed there because the builders noticed that storms always centred on Spirarch first. When it roars, the steel fortress rings like a bell.
stages.note: Spirarch can charge a drained power cell to full just by wrapping both hands around it for thirty seconds.

stages.name: Spirling
stages.bio: Spirling is a plump purple caterpillar with spiral markings along its entire body, each segment ringed in a swirling circle that pulses faintly with psychic light. It moves in a slow, deliberate S-curve rather than a straight line, as though writing something with its path. Every leaf it passes on the verdant valley floor is turned face-up by a gentle unseen force. It is so calm and slow that other creatures often step over it without noticing, which suits Spirling perfectly - it is in no hurry.
stages.note: Spirling leaves a faint invisible psychic trail that keeps the precise shape of its path for up to six hours.

stages.name: Cocolix
stages.bio: Cocolix is a large purple egg-shaped cocoon decorated with deep spiral swirls that faintly rotate in one direction when observed. It rests perfectly still in the verdant valley, balanced on nothing visible. Inside, something is reorganising - the spirals on its shell slowly shift position over days, and children who sit near it and speak find their thoughts come out clearer. The guardians say Cocolix is the moment between knowing a word and truly understanding it.
stages.note: No one has ever seen a Cocolix fall over - even in high wind, even placed on a steep slope, it simply stays put.

stages.name: Spiralyx
stages.bio: Spiralyx emerges as a wide-winged purple butterfly with broad wings printed in deep spiral eye-patterns and soft curved edges. Its large vivid eyes hold a calm psychic glow. It drifts through verdant valley on slow wingbeats, and wherever it passes, the air shimmers faintly with an after-image of its wing pattern. Children in the valley say if you watch Spiralyx long enough and then close your eyes, you will remember the hardest word you ever learned - perfectly.
stages.note: Spiralyx's wingbeats produce a low psychic frequency that is below hearing but causes nearby flowers to open slightly wider.

stages.name: Spirulot
stages.bio: Spirulot is a small spiral-shelled snail with a pale body and a single curling green vine tendril rising from the top of its shell like an antenna. Its round sleepy eyes observe the dark forest floor from very close up, since it never climbs higher than ground level. The vine tendril moves independently, reaching toward light sources and occasionally tapping objects that interest Spirulot. When it retreats into its shell, the vine keeps swaying outside as though it hasn't noticed.
stages.note: Spirulot's vine tendril grows exactly one centimetre per week, regardless of how much sunlight it receives.

stages.name: Spirulax
stages.bio: Spirulax has grown a much larger spiral shell - green and teal-striped, with a wide opening from which a tangle of pink tentacle-roots and vine tendrils flow. It moves on these tendrils rather than a single foot, advancing in a slow wave-like motion through the dark forest undergrowth. Small flowers bloom briefly on each tendril tip when it is content. It has been found sharing meals with dark forest fungi, apparently communicating through chemical signals too subtle for anyone else to parse.
stages.note: The tentacle roots of Spirulax tap out a regular slow rhythm on the forest floor - researchers have counted and it repeats exactly every 47 beats.

stages.name: Spirocrust
stages.bio: Spirocrust is a vast creature: a mossy boulder-sized spiral shell bristling with flowering growths, from which a mass of thick vine-tentacles and pink root-arms extend in all directions, gripping the dark forest floor at multiple anchor points. Three large luminous eyes are set into the shell face between flowing tentacle clusters. It barely moves - it simply grows. The dark forest's oldest trees have roots that interlock with Spirocrust's vines, and the two share water and old words across a network no one else can read.
stages.note: Spirocrust produces a new ring on its shell every year; the current oldest known Spirocrust has 112 rings.

stages.name: Spotmew
stages.bio: Spotmew is a small spotted green-and-tan kitten with round luminous eyes, a compact body, and a short tail. Its spots are olive-dark on a bright grass-green coat, and two tiny raised scale ridges run along its back - just the beginning of something armoured. It was born on the cooler outer slopes of the lava crater, where the heat from below makes the grass grow tall and unusually tough. It plays in the grass verges, pouncing on lava beetles and carrying them three steps before letting them go.
stages.note: Spotmew's spots are slightly warm to the touch - warmer on the left side than the right, for reasons no one has confirmed.

stages.name: Spottyx
stages.bio: Spottyx is a stocky, powerful ocelot with dark olive spots on a vivid grass-green coat and a full row of raised scale ridges running from neck to tail-base. Its amber eyes are fixed and confident. The scale ridges are hard enough to deflect small lava-rock chips when the crater vents suddenly. It claims territory on the middle crater slopes where grass and rock meet, patrolling a loop of about 200 paces every morning and evening without variation. Lava crater creatures that threaten the grass slopes quickly learn to avoid its ridge.
stages.note: Spottyx sharpens its ridge scales on cooled lava rock each morning; the grooves it carves have been measured growing half a centimetre deeper per year.

stages.name: Spottyrax
stages.bio: Spottyrax is a large, long-bodied champion with a heavy ridge of overlapping dark-gold scales running its full length, a broad chest, and four powerful legs. Its deep olive-green coat is patterned in bold spots that seem to absorb rather than reflect lava glow. The scale ridge can spread slightly when it is challenged, flaring like a defensive crest. It stands at the point where the lava crater's fire meets the surrounding grassland - and the grass on its side has never burned, not once, in living memory.
stages.note: Spottyrax has not changed its territory boundary by a single metre in over twenty years - the exact line is known to every lava crater creature.

stages.name: Sproutling
stages.bio: Sproutling is a small bright-eyed deer fawn with grass-green coat and a pair of leaf-shaped antler nubs that have just pushed through its forehead. Small fresh leaves sprout directly from the antler tips. It stands on slender legs at the edge of the sand dunes where desert meets the last line of grass - an unlikely place for a fawn, but Sproutling has found that the sand stays warm at its hooves long after the air cools. When it dips its head, the leaf antlers sweep the sand gently, and seeds fall from them.
stages.note: Sproutling has never been seen eating - it absorbs sunlight through its leaf antlers at dawn for two minutes and seems satisfied.

stages.name: Bramlock
stages.bio: Bramlock stands at adult height with a full spreading rack of antlers thick with living leaves and a few small flowers. Its body has deepened to a rich tawny-green, with the legs patterned in climbing vine shapes. It walks the sand dune ridges at dawn, and where it steps, short grass pushes through the sand within the hour. It has been observed touching its antler tines to dune crests, and those dunes shift more slowly - as though roots have found them.
stages.note: Bramlock's hoof-marks are found far inside the deepest sand dunes - places where no grass grows and no trail leads in.

stages.name: Verdanthos
stages.bio: Verdanthos is vast and unhurried - a great stag with a full crown of branching antlers so heavy with leaves, vines, and small blossom clusters that birds nest in the upper tines. Its powerful body is dark earth-brown, and its hooves sink deep even in packed sand, leaving prints filled immediately by green shoots. It moves rarely through the sand dunes, but each time it crosses the same ground, the dune that was there before is gone and a flat green plateau takes its place. The desert remembers where it has been.
stages.note: A single fallen leaf from Verdanthos's antlers, pressed between two stones at sunrise, will root and grow in the driest sand.

stages.name: Spynlet
stages.bio: Spynlet is a tiny purple sea slug moving through shadow caves on a slow muscular foot, its soft rounded body dotted with small pale spots and topped with two short sensory antennae-horns. Its colour glows faintly with toxic warning - nothing in the shadow caves eats it, which suits it perfectly. It leaves a thin luminescent trail of psychic slime that persists for hours, and small shadow insects have been observed following these trails to navigate the darkest passages.
stages.note: Spynlet's trail glows strongest at the exact spot where it paused longest - always where the air is warmest.

stages.name: Spynose
stages.bio: Spynose has grown to the length of a forearm and developed a dramatic ridge of sharp golden-tipped spines running down its back in alternating rows. Its body is vivid purple with pale yellow spots scattered across the softer flanks. The spines carry a mild contact venom, but Spynose only raises them when crowded - otherwise they lie flat. It navigates shadow caves with remarkable accuracy despite the dark, reading the psychic imprints left in cave walls by everything that has ever touched them.
stages.note: Spynose has been observed pressing its antennae to cave walls for up to twenty minutes - researchers believe it is reading old impressions.

stages.name: Spynarch
stages.bio: Spynarch is a wide, heavy-bodied sea slug filling the shadow cave floor from wall to wall when it fully extends. Its back is a forest of long, stiff violet-purple spines that spread sideways and catch the faint cave glow. The spots on its flanks have grown into iridescent eyes-patterns that seem to follow you. It moves at the pace of a slowly turning page, but covers ground steadily. The shadow caves' most venomous passages are also Spynarch's territory - other creatures navigate around its route, not through it.
stages.note: Spynarch has mapped every shadow cave passage in living memory - it corrects its own path by a fraction of a degree to explore a new section every single year.

stages.name: Spykling
stages.bio: Spykling is a small, dark-crimson dragon-bat with a wide head, two large red eyes, a stocky body, and stubby wings it cannot yet use for sustained flight. Its feet are large and clawed for clinging to the lava crater's vertical walls, which it does for most of the day, watching everything below with unblinking red eyes. In short glides it launches itself from ledge to ledge, and each landing is precise. The other crater creatures do not push it off its ledge - it seems too certain for something so small.
stages.note: Spykling licks the cooling lava rim each morning - researchers believe it is reading the temperature to decide when to move.

stages.name: Spyxon
stages.bio: Spyxon has grown bipedal and humanoid in outline - a lean, tall dark-crimson drake standing upright on two muscular legs with two broad arms ending in claws, and wide leathery wings folded at its back. Its red eyes glow in the lava crater's thermal haze. It can launch itself from the crater rim and circle the entire crater in a single thermal, riding the heat without a wingbeat. It does not chase things. It waits and glides, and arrives exactly when expected.
stages.note: Spyxon's shadow is consistently thirty centimetres longer than its body size should produce - no one has found an explanation.

stages.name: Spyxalor
stages.bio: Spyxalor is a fully grown dragon with the proportions of a warlord - massive chest, broad wings that shadow a ten-metre circle when spread, a long heavy tail, and enormous clawed forelimbs that grip the lava crater rim with casual ease. Its deep crimson scales have darkened toward black at the wing joints, and its red eyes hold a low burning glow. It is old enough to remember when the lava crater was formed, and the guardians placed it there not as a threat but as a recorder - its body heat has mapped every eruption for a century.
stages.note: Spyxalor exhales a smoke ring once each hour, on the hour - no one has ever observed it miss.

stages.name: Starmite
stages.bio: Starmite is a small, wide-eyed crab-like creature with a round orange-red carapace, two large blue eyes above a simple grin, and two claws held forward and upward, each tipped with a cheerful pom-pom of purple-pink anemone blooms. It scuttles sideways across bug thicket floor, waving its bloom-claws when it meets something new. Despite the soft flowers on its claws, it can pinch with surprising firmness - the guardians say the blooms are its way of asking a question before deciding whether to close.
stages.note: Starmite regrows a bloom-pom within one day of losing it; the replacement is always a slightly different shade of purple.

stages.name: Arcanid
stages.bio: Arcanid has grown a wider, harder carapace and its bloom-claws have expanded into full open anemone crowns - large, vivid, purple-pink, and faintly glowing at the frond tips. Its blue eyes are larger and now carry a steady psychic glow. It walks with a slow, deliberate sideways pace through the bug thicket and other insects move out of its path with unusual courtesy. When it opens its bloom claws fully, the psychic light at the frond tips illuminates a circle of ground three metres wide.
stages.note: The bloom fronds on Arcanid's claws are sensitive enough to feel changes in air pressure - it knows a storm is coming two hours before anyone else.

stages.name: Cosmarch
stages.bio: Cosmarch is a formidable elder crab - wide as an armchair, with a deep red-orange carapace etched in faint star patterns, and two enormous bloom claws each carrying a full crown of glowing purple anemone fronds large enough to shelter under. Its wide blue eyes are calm and ancient. In the bug thicket it sits at the oldest clearing - the one the thicket's original trees ring - and the psychic light from its bloom claws is the only light source that never flickers, not even during the deepest shadow storms.
stages.note: Cosmarch's bloom fronds record every creature that has passed within ten metres - researchers have spent years cataloguing the psychic impressions in the oldest fronds.

stages.name: Starlet
stages.bio: A plump, glossy pink star no wider than a child's hand, Starlet beams a permanent happy smile and carries two small round bumps on its topmost arms like tiny rosy cheeks. It drifts through the Crystal Mines' glittering shafts of light, absorbing their glow until it pulses like a lantern. Miners say a Starlet hovering near your lamp means good luck is buried nearby. It flickers its arms in a slow wave whenever it hears a name it has never heard spoken aloud.
stages.note: A Starlet's glow brightens noticeably the moment someone nearby learns something new.

stages.name: Stellix
stages.bio: Rounder and rosier now, Stellix sports a wide face at its center and five sturdy arms dimpled with glowing bumps. It rolls slowly through the mine's crystal corridors like a ball of soft light, leaving faint pink trails on the quartz walls. Local children believe each glowing bump on its arms holds a memory - and Stellix does seem to pulse whenever it passes a spot it has visited before. It guards the mid-level tunnels where the lightstones grow.
stages.note: Stellix retraces the exact same patrol loop through its tunnel every single night without fail.

stages.name: Cosmara
stages.bio: Cosmara no longer rolls - it floats, its thick arms writhing slowly like the limbs of something between a star and a creature far older than either. Its face has deepened into a stern gaze beneath a brilliant luminous core, and its curled arm-tips trail glowing wisps the color of distant starlight. Every crystal in the deepest mines resonates when Cosmara hums. Those who have seen it say its light doesn't illuminate the dark - it simply makes the dark feel less important.
stages.note: The deepest crystal veins in the mines grow fastest along paths Cosmara drifts through on its night rounds.

stages.name: Stellite
stages.bio: No bigger than a fist, Stellite is a tiny pale-blue creature with a faceted crystal dome on its back and two small antennae poking up from its rounded head. It skitters sideways across wet frost-rock, its shell catching the light and scattering tiny rainbows. When startled, it tucks its antennae flat and becomes almost indistinguishable from a chip of blue ice. Young Stellites sometimes wash into the meltpools of Frozen Peaks and stay for months, polishing their shells on the grit-rough stones.
stages.note: Each Stellite's shell facets are unique - no two scatter light in the same pattern.

stages.name: Stellox
stages.bio: Stellox has grown a broad rounded shell covered in sparkling ice-crystal facets that catch every angle of light. Its body is pale blue-white and it moves with a slow, deliberate grace along the frozen shallows. The shell is not merely decoration - it holds enough cold meltwater inside to keep its temperature stable for days away from the ice. Stellox leaves faint frost trails on sun-warmed rock, and herders use those glittering marks to read a cold front before the storms arrive.
