stages.note: Frost trails left by Stellox on morning rock correctly predicted thirty-seven cold fronts in Frozen Peaks last year.

stages.name: Stellaryx
stages.bio: Stellaryx's shell has erupted into a dense crown of ice-blue crystal spikes that jut outward at every angle, each one sharp enough to split a wave. The creature itself is wide and low, moving with the patient slowness of a glacier. When it submerges in the meltwater shallows of Frozen Peaks, only the spike-tips show above the waterline - from a distance they look like strange sea urchins. Those who disturb Stellaryx hear a grinding crack of shifting ice before they see anything at all.
stages.note: Stellaryx's spike-tips freeze a thin layer of seawater overnight - by dawn each spike has grown by one finger-width.

stages.name: Stellumite
stages.bio: A cheerful pink starfish with a glowing spiral marking on its forehead and two bright little eyes, Stellumite bobs on the surface of the Poison Marsh's still pools with surprising confidence for something so small. Its spiral mark pulses slowly when it senses the thoughts of creatures nearby - it seems especially drawn to confusion, clustering around creatures that have just heard something they don't understand. Marsh travelers use it as an odd compass: where Stellumite points, something is thinking.
stages.note: Stellumite's spiral glows brightest whenever someone nearby is puzzling over a word they just heard for the first time.

stages.name: Stellaxis
stages.bio: Stellaxis has grown into a full upright starfish with five arms spread wide and a glowing purple orb nestled in its center - a concentrated knot of psychic energy it has spent years compressing. It walks the marsh shallows on the tips of its lower arms, keeping its orb elevated. The orb broadcasts a faint hum that other marsh creatures steer clear of, but Stellaxis itself seems oblivious to the effect. It patrols the boundary between the murky deep and the reedy shallows with slow authority.
stages.note: The glow from Stellaxis's central orb is visible through up to two meters of murky marsh water on a dark night.

stages.name: Stellavortex
stages.bio: No longer a star at all in appearance, Stellavortex has become a broad, hulking creature with eight thick writhing arms ringed in glowing purple nodes and a blazing psychic core at the center of its flat body. It rests on the deepest floor of the Poison Marsh, and the water above it swirls in a slow permanent eddy that never settles. Those who enter the marsh at night report hearing whispered words from beneath the surface - not random words, but the exact words they struggled to learn that day. No one knows how Stellavortex knows.
stages.note: Every name whispered back from the marsh depths at night has been confirmed as one the traveler genuinely could not remember.

stages.name: Stitchling
stages.bio: Stitchling is a small green stuffed figure held together by thick visible stitches and crowned with a neat red bow tie at its neck. Its X-marked button eyes glow faintly red, and it holds one small mitten hand forward as if offering something - though nobody is sure what. It wanders Ghost Hollow's fog-wrapped paths with an unsteady shuffle, as if its stuffing shifts with every step. Children of the hollow sometimes find Stitchlings sitting on their window sills overnight, bow ties perfectly straight.
stages.note: Stitchling always faces directly toward the nearest living creature, even when no one can see it moving.

stages.name: Patchwork
stages.bio: Patchwork has grown bulkier - its body is now a dense mass of green fabric panels in different shades, stitched together with large irregular crosses. A red heart-shaped patch sits on its chest like a target, and its head sprouts a ring of thorny green protrusions. The X eyes glow redder now, and the bow tie is gone, replaced by a thick collar of rough stitching. It leaves faint green stains wherever its feet press into the hollow's pale earth, and nothing grows in those spots afterward.
stages.note: The green patches on Patchwork's body emit a faint sweet smell that makes nearby flowers wilt within the hour.

stages.name: Voodolith
stages.bio: Voodolith is a mountainous creature of tightly packed green fabric and knotted stitching, with two long antenna-like pins jutting from its skull and X-button eyes the size of saucers burning a deep red. Its arms are enormous, seam-ridged clubs, and its body's patchwork heart has darkened to a near-black crimson. It stands motionless for hours in Ghost Hollow, and the fog pools thickest around its feet. Ancient hollow legends say Voodolith was stitched together from every lost thing - every misplaced word, every forgotten name - and that it grows larger with every new forgetting.
stages.note: Voodolith never steps on its own shadow - it positions itself so its shadow always falls behind it, no matter the light.

stages.name: Pebshell
stages.bio: Pebshell is a small round tortoise with a smooth grey-brown domed shell marked by a single small blue gemstone embedded in the top. Its four stubby legs shuffle slowly through the Amber Desert's hot sand, and it blinks with a look of calm concentration that makes it seem older than it is. The blue gem is thought to be a piece of ancient amber desert crystal it absorbed at hatching. Pebshell sleeps buried to its shell-rim in warm sand and emerges only when the temperature drops at dusk.
stages.note: Pebshell can stay buried in sand for up to four days without surfacing, surviving entirely on stored warmth.

stages.name: Rockarmor
stages.bio: Rockarmor is a stocky, broad-shouldered tortoise whose shell has roughened into a thick layered carapace of grey and amber stone. Its face has settled into a permanent squint - whether from the desert glare or deep thought, nobody is certain. When it plants its feet and sets its shell flat, even strong winds rolling across the desert floor can't budge it. Caravans have learned to camp in the wind shadow of a resting Rockarmor, which seems unbothered by company as long as nobody touches its shell.
stages.note: The grooves in Rockarmor's shell map perfectly to the ridge patterns found in the oldest amber rock formations of the desert.

stages.name: Crystallyx
stages.bio: Crystallyx carries an eruption of pale ice-blue crystal spikes across its back like a mountain range, each spike as long as a grown person is tall. Its shell has become geological - thick as a fortress wall, with visible mineral strata running through it. Despite its mass, it moves with deliberate calm, each footstep leaving a crater in the desert floor. The crystals on its back are said to have taken five hundred years to form, and they ring like bells when the desert wind passes through them at exactly the right angle.
stages.note: When desert winds hit the crystals at the right angle just before dawn, the sound carries for thirty kilometers.

stages.name: Pebblyx
stages.bio: Pebblyx is a compact little round creature of sandy brown with a single teal crystal spike growing from its forehead like a proud antenna. Two large blue eyes give it an expression of perpetual wonder, and it scampers through the Crystal Mines' lowest tunnels poking its nose into every glittering crack. The crystal on its head is sensitive - it hums faintly near rich ore veins, making Pebblyx an accidental treasure-finder that miners quietly follow through the tunnels without letting on.
stages.note: A Pebblyx's crystal hums at exactly the pitch of the ore vein it senses - higher for crystal, lower for raw stone.

stages.name: Cragyx
stages.bio: Cragyx has developed a broad armored body studded with multiple sharp rock spikes across its back and head, with two thick forward-facing horns flanking its face. Its hide is a mottled grey-brown, textured like natural stone, and it moves surprisingly quickly through the mine corridors with a low, wide-legged gait. When threatened it lowers its head and presents the full array of spikes in a flat defensive shield. Crystal Mines workers leave offerings of smooth pebbles at Cragyx's favorite resting spots - insults taken otherwise.
stages.note: Cragyx can reverse direction instantaneously without slowing - miners still argue over how its legs accomplish this.

stages.name: Cragolith
stages.bio: Cragolith stands like a jagged peak given legs, its body wrapped in dense overlapping stone plates and its head crowned with a jagged ring of pale crystal spikes. The crystal crown is not decorative - it channels seismic vibration from the mine walls directly into its skull, giving Cragolith awareness of every movement within three hundred meters. It communicates with other Cragolith through low-frequency pulses that travel through the stone itself, imperceptible to any creature without rock in its bones. The mines feel quieter when a Cragolith is watching.
stages.note: Cragolith can pinpoint a single footstep through forty meters of solid crystal mine wall using only vibration sense.

stages.name: Strikling
stages.bio: Strikling is a round, fluffy grey-white bird with a fierce expression that seems too large for its small frame. Its chest feathers are a soft pale grey, and two white tufts jut from its head like tiny ears or eyebrows raised in permanent challenge. It perches on the upper ledges of Gale Ridge and stares down at everything below with intense yellow eyes. Fledgling Striklings practice dive-runs in the updrafts, missing their target more often than not but never seeming to notice.
stages.note: Strikling practices the same dive run eighty times a day until it lands it perfectly - then moves to a harder angle.

stages.name: Strixon
stages.bio: Strixon has grown into a sharp-featured raptor with grey-tipped white wings spread wide and powerful dark-taloned feet. Its chest feathers have darkened to shadow-grey at their edges, and its gaze has sharpened from challenge to calculation. It hunts the mid-level thermals of Gale Ridge, riding invisible updrafts without a single wingbeat for minutes at a time. When it finally stoops into a dive, the sound of its passage through the air arrives before it does - a low keening whistle that sends everything on the rocks scattering.
stages.note: Strixon can reduce its cross-section to half its normal width mid-dive, making it nearly invisible from directly below.

stages.name: Strixarch
stages.bio: Strixarch spreads wings so wide that its shadow covers the entire upper platform of Gale Ridge. Its feathers have darkened from grey to deep charcoal, with black-tipped primaries that trail like storm pennants in flight. The white head feathers remain, giving it a two-toned severity - pale head, dark body - like a storm with a calm eye. When Strixarch calls from the Ridge's peak, the call carries across three regions and every bird within hearing range goes still. It is the oldest intelligence in the storm zone, and it watches everything.
stages.note: Strixarch has not been seen to land anywhere but the Ridge's single highest rock in living memory - not once.

stages.name: Strixlet
stages.bio: Strixlet is a small, fluffy grey-white owl-like bird with a rounded face, two white feather tufts on its head, and fierce bright eyes far too intense for something so soft-looking. It nests in the lower crevices of Dragon Spire where updrafts provide lift for its short practice glides. Though it cannot yet sustain flight against the spire's full wind, it spreads its stubby wings and tilts into every passing gust as if daring the wind to knock it over. The dragon-riders of the region consider Strixlet sightings a good omen.
stages.note: Strixlet is known to stare into lantern flames for up to two hours at a time - blinking only once per minute.

stages.name: Strixion
stages.bio: Strixion has developed a full coat of spiky grey feathers that fan outward around its face like a ruff, giving it a much wider, more imposing silhouette. Its eyes have deepened in color and its talons are now strong enough to grip Dragon Spire's sheer rock faces in winds that would strip a person off the ledge. It hunts at the shoulder of the spire where the thermals converge, turning its wide-faced gaze on anything that moves below. The feathers around its face are so fine they detect air pressure changes a moment before the gust arrives.
stages.note: Strixion always turns to face incoming wind exactly 1.5 seconds before anyone or anything else on the spire notices the gust.

stages.name: Strixigon
stages.bio: At its final form, Strixigon of the Dragon Spire has become wholly dark - its feathers are deep black-blue from wingtip to tail, and its spread wings fill the sky like a moving stormfront. Its face retains the wide owl shape, but the expression has shifted from fierce to ancient - a creature that has witnessed the full arc of Dragon Spire's history and found it worth watching still. The dragons of the spire give Strixigon distance; there is a shared understanding between them that neither will explain. Its call at night sends a chill through the whole region.
stages.note: Even the oldest dragons of the Dragon Spire stop and hold still when Strixigon calls at night.

stages.name: Sproukit
stages.bio: Sproukit is a small fox kit with brown fur and a pair of broad green leaves sprouting from behind its ears like extra ears of a better kind. Its bushy tail is tipped in leaf-green, and it bounces through the Light Grove with bright-eyed enthusiasm. Wherever Sproukit plays, small seedlings appear in its pawprints the following morning - not because it plants them intentionally, but because the seeds catch in its fur and drop wherever it rolls. Light Grove travelers follow the seedling trails to find where Sproukit sleeps.
stages.note: A trail of seedlings in a Light Grove clearing marks exactly where Sproukit rolled in the grass the night before.

stages.name: Thornbark
stages.bio: Thornbark has grown lean and sharp, its brown fur now overlaid with a scattering of broad green leaves along its back and flanks, and its ears have taken on a pointed, leaf-edged shape. Its tail still bears the leaf-tip but has thickened into a bushy plume it holds high as it patrols the Light Grove's inner ring. The leaves on its back rustle distinctly differently from grove leaves - a sharp dry crinkle when it's annoyed, a soft flutter when it's content. Grove creatures have learned to read Thornbark's leaves before approaching.
stages.note: Thornbark's back leaves rustle at a specific frequency that only its closest allies can distinguish from the grove's ambient sound.

stages.name: Sylvox
stages.bio: Sylvox is a large, broad-chested fox whose body is nearly half covered by wide overlapping leaves - back, flanks, shoulders, even around its muzzle - as if the grove itself has begun to claim it. Its thick tail sweeps leaf-litter with every step. Its eyes carry the patient depth of old-growth forest. When Sylvox sits and goes still in the Light Grove, it disappears entirely - the leaves on its body align with the canopy above and it becomes indistinguishable from a patch of undergrowth. Those who have the Grove's favor say Sylvox finds them, not the other way around.
stages.note: Sylvox can remain completely motionless for six hours - grove creatures walk past within a body-length without noticing it.

stages.name: Synyxling
stages.bio: Synyxling is a soft purple blob-creature with two long wobbly eye-stalks and a wide gentle smile below a freckled body. It drifts through the Shadow Caves on currents of air too faint for anything else to feel, bumping softly off the walls and turning with lazy contentment. It has no fixed shape and no clear idea of where it is going, which suits it perfectly. Those who see Synyxling in the cave say it radiates a faint warmth - not heat exactly, but a feeling like remembering something pleasant you had forgotten.
stages.note: Being within arm's reach of a Synyxling for five minutes consistently causes people to recall a happy memory they had not thought of in years.

stages.name: Synxoid
stages.bio: Synxoid has grown more purposeful - its purple body has extended several short writhing tendrils around its base and its eye-stalks have multiplied into a small cluster at the top of its rounded form. Purple speckles cover its surface and it emits a faint glow from no clearly identifiable source. It clings to the ceiling of the Shadow Caves during the day and descends at night to drift through the cave floor pools, trailing its tendrils through the still water as if feeling for something lost beneath the surface. What it seeks, nobody has established.
stages.note: Synxoid always hovers at exactly the same height above whatever surface it is moving across - never touching, never straying.

stages.name: Cosmynx
stages.bio: Cosmynx has become something formless and vast - a wide dark-purple mantle of shifting matter covered in glowing psychic nodes, with tendrils that dissolve at their tips into shadow rather than ending. It rests on the floor of the deepest Shadow Cave chamber, its body spreading wider than any room seems able to contain. The air above Cosmynx is always completely still, and the cave stones beneath it are faintly warm. Ancient cave legends describe Cosmynx as the thing that remembers everything the shadow forgot, storing the echo of every voice ever raised underground.
stages.note: The glowing nodes on Cosmynx's body rearrange into different patterns every night - no pattern has ever repeated.

stages.name: Talchick
stages.bio: Talchick is a small, compact bird chick with dark blue-grey feathers, a sharp hooked beak, and a tuft of spiky head-feathers that stand on end when it is excited - which is nearly always. Its bright yellow eye gives it an expression of intense focus that belies its tiny frame. It hops along Gale Ridge's narrow ledges, practicing the precise weight-shifting that will one day let it ride full storm winds. When the gale picks up, Talchick spreads its short wings and leans into it, absolutely refusing to shelter.
stages.note: Talchick refuses to shelter from any storm, no matter how severe - it has never once been blown off a ledge.

stages.name: Talonawk
stages.bio: Talonawk has grown lean and long-winged, its dark feathers now shot through with a single electric-yellow marking that runs from eye to wingtip like a lightning bolt. It hunts the Gale Ridge's middle heights in long, patient circles, reading the invisible architecture of rising air with better precision than any instrument. When it spots a target, it doesn't hesitate - the dive is sudden and absolute. The yellow marking is said to burn brighter during storms, turning Talonawk into a living lightning flash against the dark cloud.
stages.note: Talonawk's yellow marking glows so brightly during a lightning storm that it has been mistaken for actual lightning by sailors below.

stages.name: Skytalon
stages.bio: Skytalon is a massive, wide-winged dark eagle whose wingspan blocks the Ridge's floodlight when it passes overhead. Its feathers are deep blue-black, and the gold-yellow accent has spread from the single eye-stripe to ring the edge of each primary feather with a faint luminous border. When it spreads its wings fully - which it does rarely, only in the highest updrafts above the Gale Ridge's peak - the wing-membrane catches the wind so completely that it sings. Skytalon does not need to hunt. It only needs to be seen, and the mountain adjusts accordingly.
stages.note: Skytalon has never been observed to pursue prey twice - if it misses the first strike, it returns to altitude and continues circling.

stages.name: Hornkin
stages.bio: Hornkin is a small, round-faced brown yak calf with two tiny nubby white horns and a coat of soft shaggy brown fur. Its blue eyes hold a combination of gentleness and stubbornness that is immediately endearing. It wanders Frozen Peaks' stony shoreline, using its small horns to nudge barnacles off rocks and lick the salt from underneath. Despite being an earth-and-ice type, Hornkin is completely at home near the water, and the cold ocean spray keeps its coat pleasantly cool. Fishers leave out scraps for the Hornkin that visit their docks.
stages.note: Hornkin can identify fourteen different types of edible shore-moss by smell alone and will travel up to two kilometers for its favourite.

stages.name: Taurite
stages.bio: Taurite is a full-grown shaggy brown yak with swept-back pale horns and a heavy wool coat that hangs in thick curtains around its hooves. It stands near the waterline of Frozen Peaks without seeming to mind the waves breaking over its feet, watching the horizon with the patience of something that has stood there for a very long time. The cold currents keep its heavy coat comfortable and the salt air has worked its way into the wool, making its fur feel permanently slightly damp. Younger creatures shelter behind Taurite during storms without asking permission.
stages.note: Taurite has stood at the same section of Frozen Peaks shoreline for at least eleven consecutive winters - it has worn a groove in the rock.

stages.name: Hornquake
stages.bio: Hornquake has been overtaken by ice - its coat is now a thick mantle of ice boulders and deep blue ice plates that cover its shoulders and back like natural armor, and its horns have grown into sweeping pale ice formations that arc forward and outward like a glacier's leading edge. Its body generates so much cold that a permanent frost ring extends two meters in every direction, and the rocks under its hooves crack from the temperature differential when it walks. Frozen Peaks' water is always coldest near wherever Hornquake last stood, even days afterward.
stages.note: The water temperature in Frozen Peaks drops by two degrees within a radius of fifty meters whenever Hornquake wades in.

stages.name: Calkind
stages.bio: Calkind is a warm brown bull calf with a round, soft face and big curious eyes that make it look far too gentle for its Steel Fortress home. Its small horns are just beginning to curve, and it trots along the fortress's outer ramparts with the same cheerful obliviousness it shows everything else. Young Calkind practice charging at walls, training the muscle-memory that will eventually let them shatter steel plate. For now they mostly bounce off and look confused, which the fortress guards find quietly charming.
stages.note: Calkind is the only creature in the Steel Fortress known to headbutt the same wall one hundred times in one session, then walk away satisfied.

stages.name: Hornbeast
stages.bio: Hornbeast is a pitch-black bull with sweeping curved horns as thick as a person's arm and a body built like compressed darkness. Its eyes gleam a faint red and it carries a cloud of something - dust, or shadow, or both - that trails behind it when it moves. It stands in the Steel Fortress's central yard with the confidence of a creature that has tested every wall and found them all insufficient. When it charges, the ground vibrates three seconds before it arrives. The fortress gates were built with a Hornbeast-width gap in the design spec.
stages.note: Hornbeast charges at exactly 47 km/h - measured twice - and has never once deviated from that speed during a full run.

stages.name: Titanhorner
stages.bio: Titanhorner wears the Steel Fortress like a badge - its hide has hardened into overlapping plates of dark, forge-tempered earth, and its massive horns are wrapped in dark energy that crackles at the tips. Its face carries the stillness of something that has already won every fight it ever needed to have. The fortress was not built around Titanhorner - the legends say Titanhorner built the fortress, selecting the stone, testing each wall by walking through it, and leaving behind what was still standing as the foundation. The oldest walls bear faint horn-grooves.
stages.note: The two oldest walls of the Steel Fortress each bear exactly three parallel horn-grooves at precisely the same height - Titanhorner's height.

stages.name: Tentakid
stages.bio: Tentakid is a pudgy purple octopus-creature with a short narwhal-style horn on its forehead and four small tentacles that it uses to bounce across the Bug Thicket's wet leaf-litter. The horn glows faintly when Tentakid is curious - which is almost always - and it probes into undergrowth, fallen logs, and any gap it finds with equal optimism. It squirts a faint purple mist when surprised, which smells of overripe berries and disorients anything within half a meter for about a second. In the Bug Thicket, that second counts.
stages.note: Tentakid's horn glow intensifies in direct proportion to how interested it is in whatever it is investigating.

stages.name: Tentacoil
stages.bio: Tentacoil has grown larger and more confident, its purple body now bearing two upswept curved horns and six thick tentacles that it carries in a half-coiled posture - ready to extend or retract in an instant. It navigates the Bug Thicket's dense undergrowth by reaching tentacles ahead and pulling itself through gaps that seem too narrow for its body. Its poison has become more controlled; rather than misting, it now delivers a precise dose by touch. Insects of the Bug Thicket give Tentacoil a wide berth, and they are smarter about these things than most.
stages.note: Tentacoil can thread its body through a gap no wider than its own head by compressing its mantle to a fraction of its resting width.

stages.name: Tentamorph
stages.bio: Tentamorph has crowned itself in a bristling ring of purple psychic spines that radiate outward like a crown of dark crystals, and its tentacles are now long, thick, and powerful enough to reshape the Bug Thicket's undergrowth simply by moving through it. Its purple body pulses with stored psychic energy that it radiates passively - creatures within five meters experience mild disorientation that worsens with proximity. The Thicket's oldest trees lean slightly away from the spots where Tentamorph rests. Even the bugs agree it is their overlord.
stages.note: The radius of Tentamorph's passive psychic disorientation field has been measured precisely at 4.8 meters under calm conditions.

stages.name: Tentub
stages.bio: Tentub is a delicate jellyfish with a glowing purple-blue bell and trailing translucent blue tendrils that drift behind it like ribbons of light. It floats just above the forest floor of the Light Grove, using gentle pulses of its bell to move through air rather than water - something the grove's magic seems to permit. Its bell lights pulse in a slow rhythm that others instinctively fall into step with, calming companions and giving them a fraction more courage than they came with. The guardians of the grove sometimes train alongside a Tentub to center themselves before trials.
stages.note: Trainers standing near a Tentub during practice sessions consistently make fewer errors and score better on follow-up quizzes.

stages.name: Tentacle
stages.bio: Tentacle has developed into a broad-headed squid-form with a wide pale mantle, long trailing arms, and a cluster of short feeding tentacles around its underbelly. It moves through the Light Grove's air with more purpose than its earlier form - a sweeping glide rather than a drift - and its psychic presence has grown strong enough to sense distress in nearby creatures before they show any outward sign. It circles the grove's inner sanctum in a slow protective orbit and seems to recognize every creature it has ever met.
stages.note: Tentacle has been observed returning to comfort the same young companion on exactly the third night after any setback - never sooner, never later.

stages.name: Abyssaltus
stages.bio: Abyssaltus has become something between a squid, a titan, and a living grove spirit - its wide, muscular body carries eight thick arms spread in a permanent gesture of both welcome and warning, and its head is heavy with accumulated psychic mass that makes the air around it faintly shimmer. The Light Grove itself seems to breathe differently when Abyssaltus is present: slower, more intentional. Ancient grove texts describe Abyssaltus as the creature the grove chose to be its memory - holding within its psychic field the echo of every promise made in the grove since the first guardians walked beneath its canopy.
stages.note: Every creature born in the Light Grove since its founding has been held in Abyssaltus's psychic field at least once - even if only for a moment.

stages.name: Hornling
stages.bio: Hornling is a small, smooth-sided calf with a single pale horn and a coat covered in flowing white rune swirls - natural marks that appear at birth and deepen over time. Its body is warm amber-brown and its large eyes hold a focused intelligence unusual in something so young. The runes on its hide are ancient desert script; scholars have read them as fragments of the desert's own history, rewritten on each new Hornling. It grazes the Amber Desert's sparse dry grass with the seriousness of a creature that knows exactly how valuable each bite is.
stages.note: The rune patterns on each Hornling are unique - no two have ever been found to share the same arrangement.

stages.name: Terax
stages.bio: Terax has grown into a powerful amber-brown bull with wide sweeping horns marked in gold and a body dense with muscle beneath a hide still covered in rune-swirls. Small golden lightning-mark shapes have appeared along its flanks, glowing faintly when the desert heat peaks. It stamps the earth with deliberate force when it marks territory - each stamp leaves a brief rune impression in the sand that fades within the hour. Desert travelers have found that tracing these fading runes calms them, though they rarely know why.
stages.note: The rune-impressions Terax stamps in the desert sand fade in exactly forty-seven minutes regardless of weather or shade.

stages.name: Megalox
stages.bio: Megalox is a titan of the Amber Desert - its massive body carries a full set of armor-like stone plates across its shoulders and chest, its great horns are wrapped in purple flame-wisps, and the rune-swirls that covered its calf body have expanded into a full inscription across its entire hide. Ancient desert records call Megalox the living stone tablet - the creature that carries the complete history of the desert on its body, updating with every breath. It stands at the desert's deep center, and the sand for kilometers around it is always a few degrees warmer than the rest.
stages.note: Each new voice raised within Megalox's hearing range causes one rune on its hide to brighten and shift position.

stages.name: Trunkit
stages.bio: Trunkit is a plump grey elephant calf with a short trunk, rounded ears, and a scatter of small glowing orange gem-spots on its hide like embers on grey stone. The gems are natural mineral deposits that form in the skin of Sand Dunes elephants at birth - they provide warmth in cool desert nights and light when Trunkit is in a completely dark environment. It uses its short trunk to probe the sand, locating buried moisture and mineral deposits with surprising accuracy for something born only recently.
stages.note: Trunkit's gem-spots glow more brightly the deeper below the sand the nearest water source is - making it a living well-finder.

stages.name: Stonetusk
stages.bio: Stonetusk wears natural rock armor - thick plates of grey stone have formed over its shoulders, back, and head, leaving its legs and trunk relatively free. Its two small tusks have begun to emerge and curve slightly forward. Moving through the Sand Dunes, Stonetusk uses its weight to press down into the soft sand and feel vibrations from deep below - a kind of seismic listening that tells it where the dunes are stable and where they will shift. Caravans in the Sand Dunes follow Stonetusk paths because they are always the safest routes.
stages.note: Every major caravan route across the Sand Dunes follows a path first walked by a Stonetusk - none of them have ever led into sinking sand.

stages.name: Terramorph
stages.bio: Terramorph has become a living geological event - its body is broad as a mesa, its back draped in a massive flowing mane of compressed earth and root-system that trails behind it across the dunes like a small moving hill. Its curved tusks are long and heavily ridged, and its hide beneath the mane is thick as castle stone. When Terramorph walks, the dunes ripple outward from its footprints in slow waves. The Sand Dunes themselves are said to be the fossilized footprints of Terrarmorphs so ancient they have since become part of the landscape.
stages.note: A single Terramorph footprint takes approximately nine hundred years to fully fill back in with undisturbed sand.

stages.name: Terrunk
stages.bio: Terrunk is a small grey elephant calf with several small rock and crystal protrusions growing naturally from its head and upper back - not armor, but formations that grew there the way crystals grow from a cave wall, given time. It explores the Crystal Mines with curiosity, using its trunk to tap the walls and listen for hollow resonant spaces. The crystal growths on its back ring faintly when Terrunk stands in a chamber with particularly rich ore deposits, acting as an inadvertent mining detector that tunnel workers quietly follow.
stages.note: The crystal growths on Terrunk's back ring at a different pitch for each ore type - miners have learned all twelve tones.

stages.name: Terravant
stages.bio: Terravant has developed heavy stone plating across its back and a visible amber crack-pattern running through its hide - lines where the rock has stretched to accommodate the growth beneath. Its trunk is now powerful enough to break mine columns, though it uses this strength primarily to clear rockfall from tunnel paths. The crystal formations on its back have grown taller and more numerous. Other creatures working the mines follow Terravant's patrol routes because its weight compresses loose stone, making passages safer after it passes.
stages.note: Every tunnel Terravant regularly patrols has a collapse rate exactly sixty percent lower than tunnels it does not visit.

stages.name: Terramalith
stages.bio: Terramalith carries a mountain on its back - great rounded boulders have accumulated across its entire upper body, held in place by the accumulated stone-mass of its own hide. Its mammoth tusks curve broadly outward and its face carries the deep patience of something that has watched the Crystal Mines form and expand over centuries. Its movement creates minor seismic events that can be felt on the surface above the mines. Ancient mine records mark the oldest tunnels as 'Terramalith-opened' - passages cleared by a creature that needed more room to turn around.
stages.note: The oldest passages in the Crystal Mines are exactly two Terramalith-body-widths wide - the minimum clearance it needs to turn.

stages.name: Tortlet
stages.bio: Tortlet stands on two legs, clutching a smaller detached shell-disc in one stubby fist like a shield or a toy it found very interesting. Its main shell is a warm sandy-brown dome across its back, and its face is set in the focused expression of a creature already measuring everything for eventual combat potential. It practices blocking moves with its shell-disc on anything it encounters in the Amber Desert - rocks, cacti, other Shellmites - and has never once been observed sitting still longer than a minute.
stages.note: Tortlet has memorized the exact shell-disc throw angle needed to ricochet off three desert boulders and return to its hand.

stages.name: Terrashell
stages.bio: Terrashell has grown into a broad-shouldered bipedal tortoise-warrior with thick shell plates covering its chest and arms in overlapping layers. Its face has grown fiercer and its posture more deliberately defensive - it stands with its weight shifted forward, always ready to brace. The desert sun has darkened its shell to a deep amber-brown and the wear marks from years of combat practice are clearly visible in the scuffed shell surface. It positions itself at the threshold of any area it considers its own and waits. And waits. And waits.
stages.note: Terrashell has held a single defensive stance in the same desert canyon gap for sixteen days straight - pausing only to eat.

stages.name: Terradon Rex
stages.bio: Terradon Rex is built like a walking fortress - golden-amber shell plates cover every surface of its wide bipedal body in an overlapping architecture that leaves no gap for anything to reach the creature beneath. Its face is broad and stern beneath a heavy shell brow, and it carries itself with the unhurried authority of something that has never once needed to move quickly. Every shell plate is scarred with the marks of past confrontations that ended in Terradon Rex's favor. Amber Desert legends say it is the last line of defense before the desert's oldest ruins - and that nothing has passed it in three hundred years.
stages.note: No single impact in recorded history has cracked any of Terradon Rex's shell plates - the oldest ones are over four centuries old.

stages.name: Terraling
stages.bio: Terraling is a sleek golden-brown ferret-like creature with flowing swirl markings across its entire body - natural earth-runes that shimmer faintly in the right light. Its long body moves through the Dragon Spire's narrow rock passages with liquid ease, and its curious bright eyes miss nothing. The swirl marks are believed to be a kind of passive map - as Terraling explores, the marks shift subtly, recording the terrain. Dragon Spire residents have learned that a Terraling moving purposefully in a particular direction means there is something worth finding there.
stages.note: The swirl patterns on Terraling's coat shift position slightly each time it visits a new tunnel it has not mapped before.

stages.name: Terrakind
stages.bio: Terrakind has grown upright into a thicker, more imposing form with a broad chest and a crown of gold-tipped earth spikes running from head to tail ridge. Its swirl markings have deepened and now glow a warm gold when it calls on its heroic energy. It patrols the Dragon Spire's mid-level ledges with the deliberate authority of a warden, stopping at key lookout points to survey the terrain below. Dragon hatchlings follow Terrakind along the spire paths - not because they are told to, but because Terrakind seems to know exactly where all the dangers are.
stages.note: Dragon hatchlings raised near a Terrakind are statistically far less likely to fall from spire ledges - as if they absorbed its path-sense.

stages.name: Terrakolos
stages.bio: Terrakolos is a massive, lion-bodied creature with a full mane of flowing earth-brown ropes that drift like roots or slow lava, and a face of deeply scored swirl markings that have become more symbol than skin. It moves through the Dragon Spire's heights with the ground-anchored certainty of something that has claimed every square meter of it. Where it walks, small plants push up through rock cracks within days. The dragons of the spire defer to it - not out of fear, but recognition. Terrakolos was here before the dragons, and will be here after, and both parties understand this perfectly.
stages.note: Plants begin sprouting through solid rock within three days wherever Terrakolos walks - even where nothing has grown before.

stages.name: Pebblump
stages.bio: A round, pale-grey elephant calf with a lumpy pebble-textured hide and big soft eyes, Pebblump waddles across sand dune slopes looking for patches of cool shadow. Its tiny trunk puffs little clouds of gritty dust when it sneezes, which happens whenever it stirs the sand too hard. Young Pebblumps tumble down dunes and right themselves with a cheerful shake, sending pebble-chips flying. The guardians of the Sand Dunes say Pebblump was already sitting on the first dune before anyone arrived.
stages.note: Pebblump sneezes out a burst of fine sand every time it tries to drink from a dune hollow.

stages.name: Boulderant
stages.bio: Broader and battle-ready, Boulderant's hide has hardened into rough boulder-grey plates studded with embedded rock chunks along its back and flanks. It strides across the dunes with a heavy plodding confidence, and when it lowers its thick-based tusks and charges, small sand ridges collapse underfoot. It marks its territory by dragging its flank along sandstone outcroppings, leaving long pale grooves. Wandering travellers in the Sand Dunes learn quickly not to walk between a Boulderant and its shadow.
stages.note: A Boulderant's charge leaves tracks half a metre deep - trackers use them as impromptu water-collection trenches after rain.

stages.name: Titanusk
stages.bio: Titanusk is a towering, slate-grey colossus armoured in thick overlapping rock slabs across its entire back and shoulders, its flanks bristling with embedded boulders worn smooth by centuries of windblown sand. Four pillar-thick legs carry it with slow, purposeful steps that send tremors through the dunes ahead of it. Ancient sand merchants say Titanusk once carried an entire guardian outpost on its back without noticing. When it bellows, the low boom rolls across the dunes for kilometres, and migrating sand-birds take flight all at once.
stages.note: Titanusk's footprints fill with water and become temporary oases used by dozens of desert creatures each season.

stages.name: Territ
stages.bio: A plump, sandy-tan pig-shaped creature with a round diamond-shaped stone patch on its forehead, Territ roots through the amber desert searching for buried mineral seeds with its blunt little snout. It has short sturdy legs and a round belly, and when alarmed it hunches into a ball so its smooth stone-mark forehead faces outward. Territ is curious but cautious, often following larger creatures to nibble the pebbles they dislodge. The guardians of the Amber Desert keep Territ as a good-luck charm, believing it can sniff out hidden wells.
stages.note: Territ rolls perfectly round pebbles into its sleeping hollow each night, arranging them in a small spiral before resting.

stages.name: Terosaur
stages.bio: Terosaur has grown long and low, its body now covered in interlocking brown-stone armour plates that fan into a jagged ridge down its spine. It moves with a slow deliberate lizard-swagger across the amber desert floor, leaving deep claw-scrapes in the hardpack. When threatened it puffs its neck plates outward, revealing a rattling pattern of loose rock scales that clatter together as a warning. Travellers report that Terosaur herds sometimes march single-file through narrow canyons before dawn, clattering like a procession of stone bells.
stages.note: Terosaur's ridge-plates loosen in midday heat and rattle like gravel in a tin whenever it shakes its spine.

stages.name: Terratops
stages.bio: Dark stone-black and massively built, Terratops stands on two powerful hind legs with broad clawed forearms, its entire back and crown erupting in jagged volcanic-rock spikes that glow faintly amber at their tips. Flaming ember-orange eyes pierce through the desert haze, and the heat radiating off its spines makes the air above it shimmer. Ancient amber desert lore calls Terratops the Spine of the Desert - it is said that every major canyon was formed by one Terratops lying down to rest. When it roars, the spikes on its back vibrate, sending a crackling stone-grind echo down canyon walls.
stages.note: Terratops's back-spikes heat to over 400 degrees at noon; hawks have been spotted using them as perches to dry their wings in winter.

stages.name: Rocklet
stages.bio: A stocky, warm-brown weasel-shaped cub with a row of pale-blue crystal spikes erupting along its spine, Rocklet trots through the Steel Fortress with more bravado than wisdom. It gnaws on metal scraps it finds near the fortress walls, and the minerals season its growing crystals a faint silver hue. When playful it hops onto its back and slides down metal ramps spine-first, chiming like wind-bells. Fortress apprentices prize Rocklet companions for the early warning they give - those spine-crystals vibrate before anyone else hears trouble coming.
stages.note: Rocklet's spine-crystals ring like a glassware tap when a door opens anywhere within thirty metres.

stages.name: Stonebeast
stages.bio: Stonebeast has shed its cub fluff and risen upright on powerful haunches, now clad in natural steel-grey armour plating across its chest and shoulders. Its spikes have broadened into sharp metallic-blue blades that angle backward along its spine, and its clawed forelegs are thick as iron posts. It patrols the Steel Fortress passages with methodical passes, each footfall ringing faintly on the stone floor. Apprentice knights say Stonebeast chose a side in the fortress siege long before anyone asked it to, and it has guarded the inner gate ever since.
stages.note: Stonebeast polishes its chest-plate armour by pressing it against the fortress walls each morning - the stone is worn smooth where it habitually stands.

stages.name: Stonoceros
stages.bio: Stonoceros stands like a fortress wall given legs - a massive upright titan coated in thick earth-brown rock plates split by glowing orange stress-seams, with great cracked-stone fists and a boulder-sized head ringed by broken rock outcroppings like a crown. Its feet shake the walkways when it moves. It does not patrol - it stands, planted at the Steel Fortress's deepest gate, arms crossed, waiting. Legends say Stonoceros has held its post since the first guardian placed a stone wall, and it will hold it until the last word is learned.
stages.note: No siege engine in four recorded guardian wars has moved a Stonoceros from a doorway it chose to defend.

stages.name: Terrling
stages.bio: At first glance Terrling looks like a friendly little round stingray floating just above the ground - a warm sandy-brown disc-body with a friendly upturned face, big eyes, and a glowing teal orb bobbing above its head on a thin tendril. Its small flat fins ripple when it moves, raising tiny sparks from the earth below. Terrling loves to drift down the Storm Spire's rocky ramps, letting static build up in its belly so it can release a tiny pop that startles it into a flip. The guardians call it the Spire's greeting card.
stages.note: Terrling's glowing orb dims blue-to-white just before a full storm - local guardians use it as a one-creature weather vane.

stages.name: Terravolt
stages.bio: Terravolt has grown wider and flatter, its disc-body now mottled brown and olive, with jagged fin-edges like broken rock and a glowing green eye that sweeps left and right scanning for electrical currents in the stone. It can skim just above the ground at surprising speed, dragging small lightning-trails from its belly fins that singe the rock beneath. At the Storm Spire, Terravolt patrols the mid-levels where lightning-veins run through the cliff face, feeding from them like a river fish feeds from current.
stages.note: Terravolt can charge fully from a single lightning-vein pass, then glide silently for six hours on stored current.

stages.name: Terracalypse
stages.bio: Terracalypse has become a magnificent armoured leviathan - a long, powerful beast with spined rock-plate armour along its back and flanks, crackling arcs of gold-blue lightning leaping between its dorsal spines with every breath. Its great flat head sweeps from side to side as it slides across the Storm Spire's highest plateau, earthing the summit's perpetual storm through its body into the rock below. Legends at the Spire say Terracalypse IS the storm's memory - that every lightning bolt remembers where it has struck before because this creature carries the record.
stages.note: Terracalypse cannot sleep under a clear sky; it migrates to wherever storms are gathering before settling for the night.

stages.name: Teryx
stages.bio: A delicate, cream-and-tan fawn with wide amber eyes and small rock-crystal growths behind its ears that catch the desert light, Teryx picks its way across the sand dunes with light careful hooves that barely leave a print. Tiny feather-like tufts of pale fur sprout from its shoulders and hips, ruffling in the dune wind. It is easily startled but equally quickly curious - a child who stays still long enough will find a Teryx pressing its cold nose to their elbow. The Sand Dunes' guardian texts mention Teryx as the creature who showed the first wanderers the safe paths.
stages.note: Teryx always steps in the exact same footprints when retracing a path - its tracks look like one creature crossed a dune, not four.

stages.name: Teraxon
stages.bio: Teraxon stands proud and alert, its lean muscular frame a warm tawny gold streaked with brown, and a magnificent pair of ridged stone-dark antlers curling from its brow. Clouds of fine amber dust follow it as it runs across the dunes; the dust swirls up into spirals behind each leap. When rival Teraxon meet they lock antlers and push, and the grinding of their stone horns can be heard across a whole dune field. Old desert guides use Teraxon antler-grooves scraped into canyon walls as distance markers on their routes.
stages.note: Teraxon sheds its antlers once a year; the shed points quickly weather into smooth pebbles identical to ordinary dune stones.

stages.name: Terrakalos
stages.bio: Terrakalos carries the full weight of the sand dunes on its curved, bone-golden horns - great sweeping arcs of stone-dense horn that spiral outward from its broad head like the dunes themselves curve across the horizon. Its coat has thickened to a tawny-gold that blends with the dunes so perfectly that passing caravans have walked within arm's reach without seeing it. When Terrakalos stamps, small dunes shift and reshape. Ancient nomadic songs describe Terrakalos as the guardian who chose the shape of every dune - it walked the desert once, and wherever it paused, a hill formed.
stages.note: Terrakalos's horns are documented to grow exactly one centimetre per year - nomadic families carve dates into shed horn-segments as calendars.

stages.name: Shellkit
stages.bio: A little upright tortoise-shaped creature with a glossy burnt-orange shell marked in a classic hex-tile pattern, Shellkit marches through the Crystal Mines clutching its smooth round shell against its round belly like a prize. Its wide-set eyes glare with frowning determination and its stubby arms stick forward as it waddles, ready to bump anything that gets in its way. Shellkit is a crystal collector - it nudges loose gems into a corner and sits on them to keep them warm, apparently convinced they need hatching. Mine workers find this both endearing and maddening.
stages.note: Shellkit has been observed sitting atop the same cluster of uncut rubies for fourteen consecutive days, convinced they are eggs.

stages.name: Terravern
stages.bio: Terravern has grown into a broad, powerful turtle-form with a heavily ridged and spurred shell that catches and scatters crystal-mine light in orange and brown glints. It moves on four solid legs now, head low and purposeful, excavating new crystal seams with steady sweeping claw-strokes. Mine workers follow Terravern's tunnel-trails because they reliably lead to the richest deposits - its sense for crystal beds is faultless. Old mining logs describe Terravern as the best geological instrument ever discovered: patient, accurate, and willing to work for shiny pebbles.
stages.note: Terravern's tunnel-trails average twelve per cent higher crystal yield than any mine-surveyor's path across all recorded Crystal Mines seasons.

stages.name: Megalord
stages.bio: Megalord is a great ridged titan-tortoise, its enormous spiked shell standing taller than a grown guardian, scarred by centuries of crystal-mine tunnels and still gleaming beneath the scratches in warm ochre and dark sienna. Its great jaws can crush mineral veins that stump iron pickaxes. It moves with the patience of geology itself - it has tunnelled the same Crystal Mines route for so long that the tunnel walls on either side have curved to accommodate its exact shape. Ancient mine records say Megalord was there before the first guardian lit their first mining-lamp.
stages.note: Megalord has worn a body-shaped groove into the widest Crystal Mines passage; new miners learn the layout by following the groove.

stages.name: Tholicub
stages.bio: A rotund, steel-grey rhino cub with a nubby single horn and a scattering of round brass-gold rivets studding its flanks, Tholicub bumbles around the Steel Fortress looking for things to headbutt. It is compact and low to the ground, and its little rivets clank against the fortress stone when it rolls over. Though it seems clumsy, Tholicub has never been seen to accidentally topple anything it truly cared about - there is a precise sense of force behind every bump. The fortress smiths say Tholicub tests every new installation by butting it once, and they rely on its judgement.
stages.note: Tholicub has never headbutted a wall that was structurally unsound - fortress engineers use it as a stress-test inspector.

stages.name: Tholoderm
stages.bio: Tholoderm has grown into a thick-muscled rhino with broadened horn and smooth steel-grey hide interrupted by lines of embedded gold-toned rivets that run along its shoulders and neck like armour seams. It lowers its head and charges with controlled, devastating precision - it has never charged anything it did not intend to hit, and it has never missed. At the Steel Fortress, Tholoderm patrols the outer walls on a precise schedule, and fortress guards set their watches by the sound of its footfalls rounding the eastern corner each dawn.
stages.note: Tholoderm has completed its wall-patrol circuit at the same time within two minutes every morning for as long as fortress records have been kept.

stages.name: Tholoknight
stages.bio: Tholoknight is a wall-breaker wearing gold and stone like a knight wears plate - every surface of its massive rhino body is studded with thick brass-gold rivets and reinforced with broad rock-plate panels, and its twin curling horns sweep outward like fortress battlements made flesh. When it plants its four legs and braces, nothing short of a directed explosion has ever moved it. Its eyes are calm and steady. The Steel Fortress's oldest banners depict Tholoknight facing the gate - not as a decoration, but as a promise to any would-be invader: this door does not open.
stages.note: A Tholoknight in full brace-stance has been measured by fortress engineers to exert more shear resistance than a four-metre stone buttress.

stages.name: Thornmite
stages.bio: A small, vividly crimson-red fox-puppy with a bushy tail and bright red eyes, Thornmite darts through the Dragon Spire's lower shadow-corridors in swift zigzag bursts that confuse the eye. Its fur is a deep blood-red with slightly darker patches, and its ears are oversized and radar-alert. Despite the ominous region, Thornmite is curious and bouncy - it has a habit of snatching small shiny objects and caching them in crevices. The Dragon Spire's records note that Thornmite tracks are found near every treasure cache, great and small, in the whole spire.
stages.note: Thornmite caches stolen items in exactly seven separate spots and rotates between them, never returning to the same spot twice in a row.

stages.name: Thornpede
stages.bio: Thornpede has grown into a lean, long-legged wolf with fur the colour of deep arterial red, its back ridge now lined with sharp dark spine-quills that stand when threatened. It moves in long silent strides across the Dragon Spire's midnight levels, always slightly ahead of where the light reaches. Multiple tails swish behind it in a fluid motion - it is unclear from a glance how many there are. Thornpede hunts alone, uses shadows as cover with an almost tactical intelligence, and has memorised every guard rotation in the Spire.
stages.note: Thornpede can flatten its spine-quills so completely that it passes through a crack half its apparent width - experienced hunters still do not know how.

stages.name: Infernathorn
stages.bio: Infernathorn is unmistakable - a massive crimson-furred beast with nine distinct dark-tipped tails fanning behind it like a living crown of shadow, and a broad scarred face that holds the quiet menace of something that has never needed to rush. Its spine-ridges have become full blade-quills, and its red coat darkens to near-black at the extremities. The Dragon Spire's eldest guardian text says Infernathorn appeared before the first dragon took residence, and it permitted the dragons to stay - not the other way around.
stages.note: Each of Infernathorn's nine tails is said to hold the memory of a defeated rival - it has never grown a tenth.

stages.name: Thornymph
stages.bio: A spiky, electric-green mantis nymph no bigger than a hand, Thornymph clings to stems in the Bug Thicket with three pairs of barbed legs and turns its oversized eyes toward any movement with methodical precision. Its entire body is studded with small defensive spike-protrusions, and yellow accent dots along its back flash in mimicry of flower pollen to confuse small predators. It chirps to other Thornymphs by rubbing its forelegs together, creating a high clicking rhythm that thicket children recognize as a bug-choir. It eats only the tiniest bugs, and apologizes to each one by waving an antenna.
stages.note: Thornymph mimics flower-pollen markings so well that actual pollinators try to land on it - it waits patiently until they give up.

stages.name: Spiculid
stages.bio: Spiculid stands nearly as tall as a child's shoulder, its lean green body now hardened into segmented chitinous armour and its forelimbs extending into long hooked blade-scythes. A serrated ridge runs down its back like a saw, and its multifaceted eyes track movement in a full 300-degree arc. It stakes out a meter-wide hunting territory in the Bug Thicket that it marks by slashing leaf-stems with surgical precision. Spiculid never charges directly - it circles, waits, and strikes from exactly the angle its prey cannot see.
stages.note: Spiculid ambush-positions are always on the prey's blind side; every recorded strike comes from outside the target's 60-degree rear arc.

stages.name: Phalanx
stages.bio: Phalanx is the undisputed apex of the Bug Thicket - a great winged mantis warrior standing head-high to a guardian, with a full spread of veined leaf-wings that open with a sharp crack when it decides to assert itself. Its blade-forelegs are now long enough to cross over its chest like armoured greatswords. When Phalanx spreads its wings and stridulates - rubbing wing-to-body at full vibration - the sound carries through the entire thicket and every smaller creature goes still. The guardians say Phalanx has commanded every insect battle in the thicket since before the first nest was built there.
stages.note: When Phalanx opens its wings fully, measured vibration from the stridulation has knocked leaves from trees thirty metres away.

stages.name: Thornlet
stages.bio: A small, warm-brown rabbit-kit with bright dark eyes, a compact body, and short bristly spines beginning to poke from behind its ears and along its back, Thornlet hops through Ghost Hollow on silent, wide-padded feet. It freezes absolutely motionless when scared, blending with fallen bark and rotted leaf until whatever frightened it moves on. Thornlet is one of the few small creatures that actually follows the ghost-lights in Ghost Hollow - it has learned they lead to warm mineral springs, and it has bathed in every one it has found.
stages.note: Thornlet can remain motionless for up to forty minutes - Ghost Hollow guides have stepped over them believing they were pebbles.

stages.name: Thornbuck
stages.bio: Thornbuck has shed its kit-round shape and grown into a lean, fast hare with long powerful hind legs and a back now bristling with long dark spines that fan backward when it runs, making it look like a streak of shadow with quills. It reads the Ghost Hollow's moods like a native, using the fog patches as cover and the hollow's tilted terrain to accelerate into explosive sprint-bursts that cover ground faster than they look. When cornered, it lowers its head and presents the spine-fan to its opponent - an elegant way of saying: reconsider.
stages.note: Thornbuck leaves no tracks on soft soil; its wide paw-pads distribute weight so evenly it runs across mud without sinking.

stages.name: Thornarch
stages.bio: Thornarch has become something between a great hare and a nightmare - a long, muscular predator with a mane of stiff dark spines spreading from neck to haunches, and jaws that open wider than its skull seems to allow. It moves in Ghost Hollow's deepest sections, where even veteran guardians carry a light, and it has never once been surprised. Thornarch's spines flex and shiver when emotions shift, broadcasting its mood to every creature in the hollow - the few predators that tried to challenge it read the message and backed away. Ancient hollow-lore names Thornarch the Keeper of the Hollow's Silence.
stages.note: The shadow-patches in Ghost Hollow that never hold a ghost-light are, without exception, spots where a Thornarch regularly rests.

stages.name: Thornkit
stages.bio: A fluffy sandy-tan puppy-sized creature with oversized ears, a little round face, and a quick curious temperament, Thornkit scurries across the Shadow Caves' sloped rock floors in short investigative bursts. Its fur is pale brown with faint darker markings, and the tips of its ears are dark. It has an excellent nose - it can find a freshwater seep through twenty metres of solid rock by smell. Thornkit travels in loose groups of four or five, and when they settle for the night they pile into a heap, each one with its nose tucked against another's fur for warmth.
stages.note: Thornkit can locate a hidden water source through solid rock up to twenty metres away purely by smell - cave explorers bring them as guides.

stages.name: Thorixon
stages.bio: Thorixon has grown lean and long-legged, its pale coat shifting to a warm amber-brown with dark saddle-markings along its back, and its mane developing into a loose ruff of longer guard-hairs. It carries itself with a wiry alertness in the Shadow Caves, never fully committing its weight before testing the ground beneath. It uses low rock ledges to survey routes before committing, and it can change direction at full sprint without any visible preparation. When Thorixon raises its mane ruff, other cave-dwelling creatures know to clear the passage.
stages.note: Thorixon can change direction at a dead sprint without any body-rotation warning - researchers cannot reliably predict which way it will turn.

stages.name: Spinalord
stages.bio: Spinalord is a broad, shaggy predator that fills the widest Shadow Cave corridors with its presence - a tawny amber-brown beast with a massive ragged mane that catches cave-drafts and makes it appear even larger than it is. Long guard-hairs sweep back from its spine like a dark pennant. It has lived in the Shadow Caves long enough to memorize every echo and knows exactly which tunnel acoustics project its voice deepest. Spinalord does not chase prey; it calls once, and the cave itself seems to respond. Ancient cave-writing says it taught the shadows to carry a warning.
stages.note: Spinalord's territorial howl creates standing waves in the Shadow Caves that can be heard through solid rock faces a hundred metres from the source.

stages.name: Mudhorn
stages.bio: A round, powder-blue dragon-hatchling with a cream-coloured belly disc, stubby horn nubs, and an expression of permanent cheerful bewilderment, Mudhorn sits near the Lava Crater's cooler rim pools and blows small mud-bubbles with its nose. Its little forearms are stubby and expressive, and it slaps the muddy rim with them when excited. Despite the volcano's danger, Mudhorn is entirely unbothered - it has found a warm mud-puddle beside a cooling lava shelf and considers this the perfect home. Guardian lore says Mudhorn was the first creature to figure out that lava cools into useful rock, and has been sitting nearby feeling proud ever since.
stages.note: Mudhorn blows exactly one bubble at a time and waits for it to pop before blowing another - it has never been seen to blow two at once.

stages.name: Thormud
stages.bio: Thormud is a compact upright dragon brute, dark navy-blue with a broad tan belly and rows of stubby earth-brown dorsal spines running up its back. Its arms are thick now, its posture solid and square, and its horn nubs have grown into proper curved points. It lurches between crater pools with heavy bipedal steps, scooping cooling lava-mud to pack onto its spines - apparently for temperature regulation, though it looks like it is simply proud of being messy. Its deep rumbling vocalizations echo off the crater walls at all hours.
stages.note: Thormud re-packs mud onto its own spines approximately every ninety minutes - researchers have timed this to within five minutes without exception.

stages.name: Magmamoth
stages.bio: Magmamoth is a titan of the Lava Crater - jet-black hide that has absorbed centuries of volcanic heat, a broad spiked back of dark volcanic rock-points, and a belly still carrying the tan-warm colour of cooling lava. Red-orange ember eyes glow steadily in the crater smoke. It stands completely still for hours at crater's edge, watching the lava flow, and the crater's regular creatures have learned to sleep near it for warmth and protection. Ancient crater lore says Magmamoth and the volcano struck a bargain: the volcano stays where it is, and Magmamoth stays nearby to keep it company.
stages.note: Magmamoth's body temperature has been recorded at 58 degrees Celsius at the surface - it runs ten degrees hotter than the warmest recorded lava-rim rock.

stages.name: Thornkin
stages.bio: A bright green quadruped colt with a fluffy leaf-tufted tail and a ruff of short yellow-tipped spines along its neck, Thornkin scrambles up Granite Heights' lower rock shelves with an enthusiasm that outpaces its coordination. Its legs are slightly too long for its body, which leads to endearing stumbles quickly recovered with a proud shake of its spiny mane. It grazes on the thin patches of grass between granite slabs and can identify edible lichen from twenty paces. Young guardians at the Heights are taught to follow a Thornkin to find safe routes - it has never led one off a cliff.
stages.note: Thornkin marks safe footing by pawing granite once; it marks loose gravel with two rapid scrapes - every young creature in the Heights has learned the code.

stages.name: Thornaxe
stages.bio: Thornaxe has grown into a powerful, lean four-legged beast with flowing bright-green and gold-yellow mane-hackles along its neck and spine, and a body built for the Granite Heights' uneven terrain. It leaps boulder-to-boulder with startling precision, and its rear hooves leave small chips in the rock face at each takeoff. The spines along its back are now full-length and serrated at the tips - they catch the highland wind and hum faintly when facing into the breeze. Explorers say following a Thornaxe is the fastest safe way through the Heights because it has every path memorised.
stages.note: Thornaxe's back-spines hum at a distinct pitch when the wind comes from the east - highland farmers call the sound 'the Heights speaking' and plan planting by it.

stages.name: Thornolith
stages.bio: Thornolith stands at the highest granite peak of the Heights, its dark green and gold body powerful and battle-scarred, its mane of layered leaf-spines grown into a magnificent array that fans wide in the mountain wind. Great rock-plate growths armour its shoulder joints. When it calls across the peaks, the sound seems to come from the granite itself - the rock carries and amplifies it in all directions. Ancient guardian texts name Thornolith the Heights' Compass: every explorer who has been lost on the Granite Heights and survived has described finding their way by following Thornolith's call back to safety.
stages.note: Thornolith's territorial call has been measured to carry thirty kilometres on a still day - it is the first sound heard by anyone arriving at the Heights' northern pass.

stages.name: Thorncub
stages.bio: A fluffy, round moss-green bear cub with a single pale leaf-thorn sprouting from the top of its head, Thorncub toddles around the Dragon Spire's mossy base levels snuffling at every crevice. Its vivid green coat catches the Spire's filtered light and makes it look like a walking bush - an effect Thorncub seems to use deliberately by sitting among ferns when it wants to rest undisturbed. It loves to press its single head-thorn against things to test their hardness, and the thorn is already stronger than it looks. The Spire's older guardians say Thorncub always knows where the hidden exits are.
stages.note: Thorncub's head-thorn test-prods every new surface it encounters - dragon-scale, stone, wood, and guardian boots have all received equal investigation.

stages.name: Thornbear
stages.bio: Thornbear has grown broad and imposing, its mossy-green coat now shot through with red-tipped spine-thorns that stand erect when it is threatened - turning a rumpled bear into a pincushion-obstacle that nothing wants to rush. It moves through the Dragon Spire with a rolling, confident gait, stopping to excavate moss and fungi from rock faces with strong curved claws. Despite looking fierce, Thornbear has a precise, calm quality to its movements - it only raises its thorns when the situation genuinely warrants it. Dragon Spire hatchlings have been documented sleeping against Thornbear's thorned flank, apparently trusting the signal system completely.
stages.note: Thornbear's spines have been documented standing erect a full three seconds before any human-perceptible threat appears - it registers danger earlier than any nearby guardian.

stages.name: Thornothyr
stages.bio: Thornothyr is a great dark-shelled bear-titan whose body has grown so large and still that fungi and lichen colonise the flat surfaces between its massive thorns. Its back is covered in overlapping dark-brown thorn-plates sharp enough to split stone, and its jaw can crush granite. It walks the Dragon Spire's deepest fissures with the unhurried weight of something that has never needed to run. When Thornothyr stands on its rear legs - which it does when truly angry - it blocks the entire passage it is in. Ancient Spire records describe it as the wall between the Spire's fissures and whatever is behind them.
stages.note: Lichen colonies on Thornothyr's back are taxonomically different from any found elsewhere in the Spire - they have only been found growing on this creature.

stages.name: Bucklet
stages.bio: A delicate warm-brown fawn with neat white spots, short button antler-buds, and two small dark-purple spines jutting from between its shoulder blades, Bucklet moves through Ghost Hollow's dappled undergrowth with cautious, precise steps. Its large liquid eyes miss nothing, and it has memorized every ghost-light path in its home territory. Bucklet collects fallen ghost-hollow leaves in a small pile near its resting spot each dawn - no one knows why, but the piles are always neatly arranged, largest leaves at the base. The guardians say a Bucklet sleeping in your camp means the hollow approves of you.
stages.note: Bucklet sorts fallen leaves by size each morning; the habit takes approximately twelve minutes and is never skipped regardless of weather.

stages.name: Thornstag
stages.bio: Thornstag stands with striking presence - a warm amber-brown stag with a full branching rack of antlers and a row of dark purple spines spreading down its back from neck to hindquarters like a saddle of shadow. Its coat is deeper-hued than Bucklet's, shading to near-black at the legs. It moves through Ghost Hollow with the slow deliberate grace of something that owns the space, pausing at intervals to test the air. When Thornstag presses its antler-tips to the earth, the local ghost-lights shift colour - the hollow itself seems to listen. Hollow guides believe it maintains the ghost-light routes.
stages.note: When Thornstag presses its antlers to the earth and holds still, every ghost-light within fifty metres dims blue - local guides call it 'reading the hollow'.

stages.name: Splinthor
stages.bio: Splinthor is one of Ghost Hollow's oldest presences - a great dark-furred stag whose body has deepened to rich chocolate-brown and dark amber, its back now fully armoured with overlapping dark spines that spread from nape to tail in a continuous ridge. The antlers have branched so many times they look like a leafless winter oak. Ghost-lights collect around Splinthor's antlers at night, and the creature seems to navigate by them rather than by sight. Hollow lore says Splinthor was present when Abalont's shadow first reached Ghost Hollow, and it chose to stay - not out of fear, but out of a refusal to abandon the paths it had learned.
stages.note: Ghost-lights cluster in Splinthor's antlers during fog events - experienced hollow navigators follow it as a living landmark in zero-visibility conditions.

stages.name: Thornling
stages.bio: A small, endearing pup with warm sandy-brown fur, perky ears, and a ruff of short leaf-shaped quills sprouting from its neck and shoulders, Thornling bounds across the Amber Desert's scrub margins with cheerful disregard for the heat. Its quills are soft enough that children can pat it without hesitation, and it knows this - it approaches humans with a tail wag that sets its quills rattling together in a soft leaf-brush sound. Thornling caches seeds from desert plants under rocks, creating tiny gardens that often outlast the Thornling itself. The desert farmers say Thornling is the desert's own gardener.
stages.note: Thornling has been documented burying viable seeds in germination-ready soil pockets at a rate better than experienced desert horticulturalists.

stages.name: Thornquill
stages.bio: Thornquill has grown into a lean, long-legged strider with a full mane of long leaf-quills flowing from neck to mid-back in overlapping layers of green and amber-gold. It runs the Amber Desert's sparse vegetation margins in fast smooth strides, its quill-mane streaming behind it. The quills have become proper defensive structures now - stiff at the core with sharp tips - but when Thornquill is relaxed they drape softly, and desert birds land among them to shelter. Its tracks always follow the underground water-table, making it an involuntary guide to every oasis.
stages.note: Thornquill's travel paths trace the desert's underground water-table with more accuracy than any surveying method available to the guardian geographers.

stages.name: Thornveil
stages.bio: Thornveil moves through the Amber Desert like a walking oasis - its body now fully mantled in layered leaf-quills of deep green and bright amber that billow outward in the desert wind like a living cape. The quills reach nearly half a metre in length on the flanks and tail, and when fully fanned in threat they form a perfect circle of green-gold leaf-blades. Insects and small desert birds shelter in the quill-mantle during sandstorms, creating a moving micro-habitat. Ancient desert songs call Thornveil 'the garden that walks' - a living fragment of the world before the amber sands spread so far.
stages.note: During sandstorms, up to forty distinct desert species shelter simultaneously in Thornveil's quill-mantle - no other single creature provides refuge to this many species.

stages.name: Thornchick
stages.bio: A tiny bipedal wyvern hatchling with a dusty olive-green body, a single blunt party-hat horn on its head, and a round green spot on its chest like a leaf-badge, Thornchick totters around the Dark Forest floor squawking at falling leaves. Its little forearms are nearly vestigial and it balances with a comically intense expression. The horn is harmless for now but grows with remarkable speed - forest elders have measured a Thornchick's horn extending three millimetres in a single day. Dark Forest saplings grow faster in the patches where Thornchick sleeps, apparently benefiting from something it exhales at night.
stages.note: Saplings in a five-metre radius of a Thornchick's sleeping spot grow measurably faster than those outside it - the mechanism is not understood.

stages.name: Thornwing
stages.bio: Thornwing has grown into an elegant pterosaur-form with broad membranous wings edged in vivid pink-purple veining, and two elegant curved head-crests that sweep back like a compass rose. Its leaf-patterned wings beat in slow arcing circles over the Dark Forest canopy, and the undersides catch forest light to flash the wing-veins in brilliant colour. It rides thermal columns above the treeline and calls downward in spiraling glides, letting the forest guide its path. Dark Forest hunters use Thornwing circling patterns as a map of where air-columns are rising - it reliably marks forest clearings from above.
stages.note: Thornwing circles exactly three times before landing, always completing the third circle even if clearly tired - the pattern never varies.

stages.name: Thornodactyl
stages.bio: Thornodactyl is a formidable wyvern-dragon of the Dark Forest - a great dark-green scaled beast with enormous crystal-pink wing-spines, powerful hind legs, and a body armoured in overlapping scale-plates. Its head bears a full crown-array of crystal-blade horns, and its tail ends in a heavy scythe-tip. When Thornodactyl spreads its full wingspan above the Dark Forest canopy, it creates a brief silence - every bird, bug, and smaller creature holds absolutely still until the shadow passes. Ancient Dark Forest lore says Thornodactyl and the forest struck a peace: it does not burn the canopy, and the canopy shelters its eggs.
stages.note: Dark Forest fires have never spread to the two square kilometres around Thornodactyl's nesting site - investigators found no structural difference in the trees, only the creature's presence.

stages.name: Thornyx
stages.bio: A compact, bright-green lizard-shaped creature entirely covered in layered leaf-spines that make it look like a walking pile of fresh foliage, Thornyx forages across the Bug Thicket floor using its thick spiked tail for balance. Its big round eyes are leaf-green and alert, and its leaf-quills are supple enough to bend around branches without snagging. It sits motionless among actual leaves to vanish entirely - the only tell is the faint curl of its tail tip. Bug Thicket young are taught to count the leaves in a bush carefully before sitting on it, because of Thornyx.
stages.note: Thornyx is camouflaged well enough that three Bug Thicket survey teams failed to spot one sitting on an open path in full daylight.

stages.name: Quillhog
stages.bio: Quillhog has grown into a muscular four-legged lizard with a full spine-mane of earth-tone quills - green at the tips, brown and orange mid-shaft - and a long sweeping tail ringed with spine-clusters. It moves through the Bug Thicket with a low, deliberate prowl, pressing its belly close to the ground when hunting and rising onto stiffened legs when defending. The quills have become properly weaponised now: a full body-shake releases a shower of barbed spine-tips into the air around it. Thicket insects give it a wide berth, which suits Quillhog perfectly.
stages.note: Quillhog's body-shake defense fires spine-tips in a two-metre radius - it can replace its full quill-coat in approximately thirty hours.

stages.name: Fernarch
stages.bio: Fernarch is a great armoured lizard-behemoth whose body has merged with the Bug Thicket itself - its spines have grown so long and tangled with actual living vines that it now carries a full canopy of ferns and small plants on its back as it moves.
