Its four legs are pillar-thick, and its tread opens furrows in the thicket floor that quickly become waterways. Fernarch moves slowly, eats constantly, and has remodelled more of the Bug Thicket's terrain than any other creature. Ancient thicket records call Fernarch the Gardener-Who-Walks - every major fern-grove in the thicket began as a spine-plant dropped from Fernarch's back.
stages.note: Every major fern-grove in the Bug Thicket has been traced to a location where Fernarch rested; the spines it sheds take root and grow.

stages.name: Sproutnyx
stages.bio: A small, lush-green kitten with oversized tufted ears and a single bright green leaf sprouting straight up from between them, Sproutnyx pads through the Shadow Caves on silent paws, investigating every fungal bloom with its nose. The leaf on its head is mildly toxic to touch but Sproutnyx seems unaware of this, pressing it cheerfully against things for emphasis. It is clever enough to open sealed containers by working at the seams with its paws, and cave foragers have learned not to leave food low to the ground. The Shadow Caves' elder texts describe Sproutnyx as the creature that discovered which cave fungi are edible by eating all of them and surviving.
stages.note: Sproutnyx has consumed seventeen cave fungal species toxic to other creatures without apparent ill effect - researchers are still cataloguing its internal adaptations.

stages.name: Thornlynx
stages.bio: Thornlynx has grown into a long-bodied, muscular lynx with a full coat of overlapping green-and-brown leaf-scales, sweeping leaf-plume tail, and vivid orange-green eyes that glow slightly in the Shadow Caves' darkness. Thin toxic vine-tendrils grow from its spine and trail behind it as it moves, leaving faint chemical trails that other Shadow Cave creatures learn to avoid. It hunts by ambush, pressing its leaf-pattern coat against the cave walls until it is invisible, then striking with extraordinary speed. It has been in the Shadow Caves long enough to have memorised the scent-signature of every creature that shares its territory.
stages.note: Thornlynx's vine-trails remain chemically active on cave rock for up to six hours after it has passed - it effectively keeps a dynamic chemical map of its territory.

stages.name: Venomarch
stages.bio: Venomarch is a terrifying apex presence in the Shadow Caves - a massive red-scaled predator bristling from nose to tail with toxic blade-horns, its back a ridge of venomous spines, its jaw a wide-set weapon capable of crushing stone. The vivid red colouration is not camouflage: it is a warning the Shadow Caves eventually taught everything else to obey. Venomarch secretes a territory-marking toxin from its spine-tips that lingers for days; nothing enters its range without that signal. Ancient Shadow Caves lore says Venomarch was created by Abalont's shadow as a guardian of the deepest passages - and it accepted the role.
stages.note: Venomarch's spine-toxin has been detected in Shadow Cave water samples six hundred metres from any known Venomarch sighting - it marks territory more deeply than any visible boundary.

stages.name: Tigrkit
stages.bio: A golden-yellow kitten with bright green eyes and a coat patterned in warm amber spots, Tigrkit pounces across the Storm Spire's rocky ledges with reckless joy. It is small enough to shelter in rock crevices between storm-bouts and has learned exactly which crevices have the best airflow. Its spots are faintly warm to the touch - early signs of the electrical charge it will carry as an adult. Tigrkit loves to swat at the small static discharges that crackle off the Spire's metal fixtures, and the sparks make its fur stand on end in a spectacular ruffle it appears proud of.
stages.note: Tigrkit's spot-markings warm measurably when a lightning storm is within five kilometres - Storm Spire apprentices keep them as personal weather stations.

stages.name: Tigrawn
stages.bio: Tigrawn has grown into a lean, striking tiger-form - golden amber stripes on a tawny coat, with a dramatic crest of stone-grey back-spines that stand erect when it is charged. Its green eyes now hold a steady focused intensity, and its paws leave faint scorch-marks on the Storm Spire's stonework. It hunts through vertical terrain with startling comfort - its claws have small electrical grippers that let it cling to rock faces at angles that should send it sliding. Storm apprentices at the Spire track Tigrawn's preferred hunting routes because they reliably follow the most electrically active fault lines.
stages.note: Tigrawn's preferred patrol routes trace the Storm Spire's most electrically active fault lines with consistent accuracy - it is used as a live geological sensor.

stages.name: Tigracron
stages.bio: Tigracron is a magnificent, powerful tiger-sovereign with a full mane of crackling stone-spine ridges across its shoulders and back, its golden coat now streaked with permanent electric-burn scars that glow faintly in low light. Its tail sweeps in a controlled arc that leaves a trailing arc of static in the air. When Tigracron roars at the Storm Spire's summit, the lightning rods mounted there discharge simultaneously - the engineers learned to budget for replacements. Ancient Spire texts describe Tigracron as the reason the Spire was built where it was: it had already chosen the site as the highest natural electrical ground for a hundred kilometres.
stages.note: Tigracron's roar has been measured to cause simultaneous discharge from all eight of the Storm Spire's summit lightning rods - engineers replaced them quarterly before learning to work around its schedule.

stages.name: Toxadpole
stages.bio: A round, bright-green toadlet barely bigger than a fist, Toxadpole has wide yellow eyes and two small purple orbs dangling from its sides like toxic baubles. Its belly is a sickly yellow-green, and its stubby limbs end in round, sticky toes. Restless and curious, it hops in tight circles when it senses a name it has never heard - tapping its baubles together to produce a soft, venomous chime. In the Light Grove's glowing clearings, it pokes its nose into every glowing flower, sniffing for the sweeter poisons.
stages.note: Its purple side-orbs glow faintly at dusk, luring night insects straight into its waiting mouth.

stages.name: Toxarump
stages.bio: Standing upright now, Toxarump is a stocky green toad with a muscular chest, scarred knuckles, and a purple-trimmed sash tied around its waist bearing a small skull emblem. Its yellow eyes have grown more slanted and fierce, and thick poison pores line its back and shoulders. It has learned to punch first and ask questions later - the sash catches any venom that drips from its fists. It holds the shadowed edges of the Light Grove like a bouncer who never forgets a face.
stages.note: Trainers who try to sneak past a Toxarump find its fist in the way every single time - it never sleeps on its feet.

stages.name: Toxazaur
stages.bio: Toxazaur is a hulking, war-scarred toad covered in dark blotches and thick ridge-like poison glands along its spine. Its giant fists drip with a violet venom that pools on the ground wherever it stands. The skull emblem on its sash has grown into full spiked shoulder-armor, and its eyes burn yellow with ancient menace. In the Light Grove, it is the shadow beneath the brightest trees - something the guardians noticed only after it had already been watching them for years.
stages.note: A single drop of Toxazaur's dripped venom can keep a patch of ground toxic for seven days straight.

stages.name: Toxkit
stages.bio: Toxkit is a tiny orange kitten with large dark spots and a short tail that curls upward. Wisps of purplish-grey smoke drift off its fur as if it is perpetually smouldering. Its eyes are wide and golden, and it pads through the Shadow Caves with a kitten's clueless boldness, leaving tiny scorched paw-prints on stone. It licks its spots when nervous - which releases a brief burst of fragrant but mildly toxic smoke. The guardians first spotted one rolling in a warm volcanic vent, purring.
stages.note: Its spots are hotter to the touch than the surrounding fur - tiny venom-fire glands just waiting to be fully lit.

stages.name: Toxfeline
stages.bio: Toxfeline is a lean, confident leopard with bold orange and brown spots, a long twitching tail, and smoke constantly seeping from the base of its neck and haunches. Its paws carry a faint purple tint from built-up venom beneath the claws. It prowls the cave corridors in a low, fluid crouch, breathing out thin jets of fire-tinged toxic mist when startled. Cave fungi wilt for hours wherever Toxfeline has marked its territory - a reliable sign to watch your step.
stages.note: Toxfeline marks trails with tiny jets of hot poisonous breath - follow them in the wrong direction and you'll walk in circles for an hour.

stages.name: Miasmaul
stages.bio: Miasmaul is a massive, low-slung leopard radiating intense heat from dozens of glowing spots - each one a charged venom-fire chamber. A single purple orb of toxic flame hangs above its head, drawn by the creature's own magnetic poison field. Its mane-like neck fur stands spiked with heat, and when it opens its jaws wide in challenge, a column of purple-tinged fire roars out. In the Shadow Caves it is the apex presence - even the stones seem to lean away when it walks past.
stages.note: The glowing orb above Miasmaul's head grows brighter the angrier it gets - experienced trainers count it like a thermometer.

stages.name: Toxling
stages.bio: Toxling is a cheerful little purple-and-green snake, no longer than a boot, with bright round eyes and a wide, friendly smile. Its short body curves in a loose S-shape, and two small green stripes run down its sides like racing marks. Despite its gentle look, the tiny venom sacs behind its jaw are already developing, and it drools a faint purple mist when overexcited. It slithers through the Poison Marsh's flooded reeds, tasting the water for unfamiliar names to learn.
stages.note: Toxling always smiles, even in battle - the grin is inherited; the venom sacs beneath it are entirely real.

stages.name: Venomcoil
stages.bio: Venomcoil rears up tall, its hood flared wide and bristling with sharp purple spines along the rim. Its green-and-purple scales have deepened to a richer, more dangerous pattern, and its eyes have narrowed to fierce amber slits. It can hold a hooded threat display for ten minutes without wavering, daring anything nearby to make a wrong move. In the Poison Marsh it controls the deep channels, rearing up from murky water with hood spread to steer creatures away from its den.
stages.note: Venomcoil's hood-spread is so precise it can direct its venom spray to hit a target the size of a coin at three metres.

stages.name: Hydratox
stages.bio: Hydratox rises from the Poison Marsh as five cobra heads on thick, writhing necks - each head independent, each wearing its own hooded frill and bearing its own set of deadly fangs. Its coiled lower body is enormously thick, keeping it anchored in the deepest marsh mud. All five mouths can spray venom in different directions simultaneously, filling the air with a toxic purple fog. Ancient Abalont lore warns that any word spoken carelessly near a sleeping Hydratox is stolen by one of its five hungry minds.
stages.note: Each of Hydratox's five heads hisses in a different pitch - together they form a dissonant chord that can freeze prey mid-step.

stages.name: Jellotox
stages.bio: Jellotox is a tiny, round-capped jellyfish in purple and pink, bobbing gently with four thin, trailing tentacles that drip a faintly luminous venom. Its face - two wide eyes and a tiny open mouth - gives it a permanently startled expression, as if surprised by its own existence. It drifts through the Ghost Hollow, pulled by breezes no living creature can feel, and its tentacles leave short glowing streaks in the air. It seems to be looking for something it lost long ago.
stages.note: Jellotox produces one tiny venom droplet per hour - if you bottle it, the liquid glows soft purple all night long.

stages.name: Toxjelly
stages.bio: Toxjelly has grown into a wide-capped jellyfish with prominent yellow-green spots across its dome and long, sinuous tentacles hanging below. Its body has a half-real quality - light passes through it at certain angles - and it moves through solid stone walls as readily as through open air. The spots pulse in sequence when it senses danger, broadcasting a warning that other Ghost Hollow spirits heed immediately. Where it drifts, the air tastes metallic and faintly sweet.
stages.note: The yellow-green spots on Toxjelly's cap pulse in a pattern unique to each individual - experienced hollow-guides can tell them apart at a glance.

stages.name: Venomjel
stages.bio: Venomjel spans wide - its domed cap now as broad as a child is tall - and its many long tentacles spiral outward like the arms of a dark galaxy. Purple and deep green swirl across its surface in slow, hypnotic patterns that mimic the night sky above Ghost Hollow. Anything brushing a tentacle feels a profound chill before numbness sets in. Venomjel does not hunt; it simply drifts, and those who linger too near drift along with it, forgetting where they were going.
stages.note: Venomjel has been observed drifting the exact same route through Ghost Hollow for three years - no one knows what it is circling.

stages.name: Toxynlet
stages.bio: Toxynlet is a gentle-looking purple-and-green snake with round eyes and an open, curious mouth - it raises its head high and sways left to right when something catches its attention. Two thin green stripes mark its body from head to tail, and its scales shimmer softly in the volcanic light of Dragon Spire. Though small, it has already developed a mild venom, and it practices its strike on fallen leaves, rehearsing the motion the way a young scholar rehearses unfamiliar names.
stages.note: Toxynlet raises exactly one-third of its body off the ground to survey its surroundings - no more, no less, every single time.

stages.name: Venomyx
stages.bio: Venomyx rears up with a full hooded frill ringed by sharp purple spines, each one a secondary venom delivery point. Its scales have deepened to a rich teal-and-purple gradient, and its eyes have gone narrow and calculating. It patrols the Dragon Spire's basalt ledges with the patience of a sentry that has memorized every shadow. When it detects an intruder, it inflates its hood slowly - a display that takes a full ten seconds and is meant to give the intruder time to leave.
stages.note: Venomyx always inflates its hood three times before striking - researchers say it is giving itself permission.

stages.name: Dracotoxus
stages.bio: Dracotoxus is a great coiled serpent draped in overlapping jade and violet scales, its immense body ringed by thick armour-like ridges. Its full hood bristles with long blade-like spines, and when fully spread it blots out the light behind it. Green-tinged venom seeps from the tips of its fangs constantly, pooling in the volcanic rock below. At Dragon Spire it is one of the oldest living presences - the guardians believe it was here before the Spire had a name, and it will be here long after.
stages.note: The largest recorded Dracotoxus was measured at exactly the same length three separate times, five years apart - it had simply stopped growing.

stages.name: Tusklet
stages.bio: Tusklet is a plump, sandy-beige elephant calf with oversized ears, a stumpy trunk it hasn't quite learned to control yet, and small nubs of tusks beginning to push through its lower jaw. Rocky ridges have started to form across its back like a natural saddle - the first signs that this creature is built for something heavier than just wobbling around Sand Dunes. It uses its trunk to flick sand into the air and watch it fall, a habit that drives dust into everything nearby but delights Tusklet endlessly.
stages.note: Tusklet's trunk can't reach its own forehead yet, so it scratches its head on whatever rock happens to be the right height.

stages.name: Tuskmaw
stages.bio: Tuskmaw is a solid, four-legged elephant now fully armoured across its back with rows of stone-like plates that have fused with its hide. Its tusks have grown long and curved, streaked with mineral deposits from the sand it constantly roots through. A calm, methodical creature, it paces the same dune ridge every morning - the vibration of its footsteps tells it which dunes are hollow and which are solid. Where it walks, the ground compacts into a reliable path other creatures follow.
stages.note: Tuskmaw tests every dune before stepping on it - it has not fallen through a hollow dune in its entire adult life.

stages.name: Mammolith
stages.bio: Mammolith is immense - a walking ridge of stone and ancient bone, armoured head-to-tail in thick rocky plates that have grown too massive to remove. Its tusks are long, broad, and scarred by hundreds of battles, curving outward like the gates of a fortress. Every step leaves a deep impression in the desert that fills with sand over the years, forming ridges cartographers have mistaken for natural features. In Sand Dunes, Mammolith is the bedrock given legs - the guardians say it predates the dunes themselves.
stages.note: Mammolith leaves footprints two hands deep in packed sand - surveyors have mapped its favourite route by following the indentations alone.

stages.name: Tuskbit
stages.bio: Tuskbun's first form is a round, fluffy, light-brown creature - part mole, part digging machine - with two oversized crystalline diamond-blue tusks erupting from its snout that are already bigger than the creature's head. Its tiny round eyes peer out above the tusks with determined calm, and it holds its stubby forelimbs close to its chest. In the Steel Fortress, young Tusklets bore exploratory shafts through walls, leaving perfectly circular tunnels the diameter of their tusks - which architects quietly use as ventilation.
stages.note: A Tuskbit's crystal tusks are harder than most drilling tools used in the Steel Fortress - the garrison tests new chisels against shed tusk-fragments.

stages.name: Tuskburrow
stages.bio: Tuskburrow has grown stocky and low-slung, its fur thicker and brindled, with three massive crystal-blade tusks that jut forward and slightly outward - a drill-head configuration. Its powerful forelimbs end in broad, shovel-shaped paws perfect for clearing debris behind its tusk-cuts. It can chew through packed earth and softstone at a walking pace. The Steel Fortress tunnels it excavates are so geometrically precise that construction crews sometimes request a Tuskburrow before laying water pipes.
stages.note: Tuskburrow always circles a tunnel entrance once counterclockwise before entering - construction teams call this "the twist" and consider it good luck.

stages.name: Burrowtitan
stages.bio: Burrowtitan is a low, wide-bodied hulk whose multiple enormous crystal-blade tusks and back-spines form a complete drilling and breaking array. Its fur has given way to thick, interlocked hide plates that look almost manufactured. The creature moves slowly but with total commitment - no material it has faced has stopped it. In the Steel Fortress it is both worker and warden, digging the deep foundations that keep the great walls standing. It barely notices battles; it simply puts its tusks to the obstacle and pushes.
stages.note: Burrowtitan's largest tusk has survived every recorded impact without cracking - metallurgists believe it has a microstructure no forge can replicate.

stages.name: Pigmite
stages.bio: Pigmite is a round-bodied pink piglet with a fine spray of pale blue crystal shards erupting from its back like a sparkling crown. Its face is dusted with stone-flecks and a flat snout, and it trots briskly through the lower passes of Granite Heights, sniffing at rocks to read the words Axon once scratched there. It is entirely unbothered by cold and sleeps nose-down against a granite slab, absorbing the stone's memory through the night.
stages.note: Pigmite sneezes crystal shards when startled - Granite Heights miners keep a respectful distance and collect the shards afterward for good luck.

stages.name: Tuskite
stages.bio: Tuskite is a stocky boar with a thick neck, iron-gray hide, and a pair of upward-curving stone-grey tusks that look capable of splitting a boulder - which they can, given the motivation. A ridge of grey stone-spines runs down its back, and small rocks orbit its ankles when it stamps the earth hard. It holds the high passes of Granite Heights with stubborn resolve, letting through those who speak carefully and planting its feet for those who do not. A lowered head is the only warning it gives.
stages.note: Tuskite's tusks grow exactly one millimeter per correct word spoken in its presence - the longest tusk ever recorded was seventeen centimeters.

stages.name: Stonusk
stages.bio: Stonusk is a great stone-armored mammoth-boar: thick iron-grey armor plates cover its shoulders and flanks, and two enormous curved tusks bracket a face as impassive as the granite peaks above it. Its legs are as thick as young trees, and each step leaves a circular crater in the stone. It guards the highest pass where Axon once climbed toward the sky, remembering every traveler who ever came through - and every word they said on the way. To a child who speaks with respect, it lowers its massive head and clears the road.
stages.note: Stonusk's footstep craters fill with rainwater within an hour and become known local water sources - Granite Heights villagers plan their routes by them.

stages.name: Tusknub
stages.bio: Tuskle's first form is a chunky little brown boar with a wide snout, small sharp eyes, and a ridge of bristly spines running from head to tail. Its two forward tusks are already prominent, curving slightly outward and catching amber light beautifully. It charges everything it finds interesting - which is everything. The sandy floor of the Amber Desert suits it perfectly; it roots through it constantly, flinging pebbles and crumbling sandstone chunks in enthusiastic fountains.
stages.note: A Tusknub boar charges at a full run, stops precisely one body-length from its target, then sniffs it as if nothing unusual happened.

stages.name: Bristusk
stages.bio: Bristusk is a powerful, low-to-the-ground boar with a wide armoured forehead, heavy curving tusks streaked with mineral deposits, and a dense ridge of thorn-like spines along its spine that have hardened into rock-solid keratin. When challenged it drops its head and digs its hooves in - a warning it gives once. Amber Desert traders mark the locations of Bristusk dens on their maps; not out of fear, but because a Bristusk den always sits above a stable rock shelf - ideal for a safe campsite.
stages.note: Bristusk marks its territory by dragging its tusks through sandstone - the gouges it leaves are perfectly level, as if measured.

stages.name: Terrausk
stages.bio: Terrausk is a massive, squat-bodied boar whose entire dorsal surface is covered in thick interlocking stone plates that have fused with its spine. Its great tusks are as long as a child's arm and as hard as granite. It moves at a slow, deliberate walk - but when it charges, nothing short of a solid wall stops it. The Amber Desert's western canyon was partly widened by centuries of Terrausk herds pushing through it each dry season. The guardians revere it as a creature that reshapes the land by simply going where it needs to go.
stages.note: Terrausk's stone back-plates absorb so much desert heat that small lizards bask on sleeping individuals, undisturbed, all afternoon.

stages.name: Hoglet
stages.bio: Tuskol's piglet form is a warm-brown wild boar with two stubby forward-pointing tusks already gleaming faintly with a metallic sheen. Its body is compact and its eyes small but bright. A scatter of diamond-blue crystal fragments dot its back where its future armour plates are budding. It trots through the Steel Fortress's lower courtyards with the absolute confidence of a creature that has never been told no - knocking over supply crates and eating whatever rolls out.
stages.note: The crystal specks on a Hoglet's back make a faint ringing sound in cold weather - fortress guards call it 'the bell pig.'

stages.name: Tuskthorn
stages.bio: Tuskthorn is a grey-brown boar now armoured across its back with a row of thick stone-metal plates, each one fused to the spine and edged with sharp ridges. Its tusks have grown heavy and slightly curved, scored with the marks of past impacts against steel walls. A no-nonsense creature, it rams intruders rather than warns them. Fortress engineers discovered that a Tuskthorn ramming a wall at full speed can locate hairline cracks in the masonry before any inspector does - they accept this as a service.
stages.note: Tuskthorn's back-plates are always slightly warmer than its body - the fortress smiths say it runs an internal forge.

stages.name: Ironwrath
stages.bio: Ironwrath is fully encased in thick, overlapping steel-fused stone armour from snout to flank, with a massive steel-banded skull and two enormous tusks that could peel a fortress gate off its hinges. Its eyes glow faintly in the sockets of its armoured face-plate. The creature does not charge out of anger; it charges out of principle - it has decided something is in the wrong place and is correcting it. The Steel Fortress's eastern gatehouse was rebuilt twice; both times the architects found old Ironwrath tusk-gouges in the original foundations.
stages.note: Ironwrath's tusks leave marks in forged steel - the garrison files them under 'structural inspections' and considers the creature essential maintenance.

stages.name: Burrowlet
stages.bio: Tuskora's first form is a small, dark-purple mole with two gleaming silver crystal-blade tusks proportionally enormous for its body, tiny star-shaped pink ears that rotate independently, and a round velvet snout. Its small forelimbs are already broad-pawed and built for digging. In the Light Grove it burrows up into glowing clearings at dusk, squinting at the brightness before deciding it is worth it, and then diving back down at the slightest loud noise.
stages.note: Burrowlet moles use their star-shaped ears like radar - one full rotation in each direction before they surface anywhere new.

stages.name: Tuskora
stages.bio: Tuskora has grown wide and low, its dark body now thick with muscle and its crystal tusks gleaming silver-blue in any light. Its paws have widened into formidable digging tools edged with hardened steel-like nails. Small red star-shaped markings sit behind its shoulders - possibly sensory organs, possibly ornamental. It spends most of its time just below the surface of the Light Grove, creating a dense network of tunnels that routes moisture to the grove's oldest trees - a fact the trees seem to appreciate.
stages.note: Tuskora digs its tunnel network to within a hand-width of every major tree root in its territory - never breaking through, just staying close.

stages.name: Tuskquake
stages.bio: The Light Grove's Tuskquake form is a wide-bodied, ridge-backed mole-titan whose entire dorsal surface is covered in overlapping armour plates that look forged rather than grown. Its multiple massive crystal-steel tusks radiate outward like a crown of blades. It moves underground mostly, but when it surfaces - which happens only for significant threats - the ground bulges and cracks before it emerges. The grove's oldest guardian trees are said to have grown up around the routes this creature carved, their roots tracing every tunnel like a map.
stages.note: When Tuskquake surfaces in the Light Grove, the surrounding trees lean slightly toward it for three minutes afterward - as if greeting an old friend.

stages.name: Hippusk
stages.bio: Tuskos's first form is a squat, grey-brown creature with the broad face and wide nostrils of a hippo, stumpy legs, and a beginning set of small forward-facing tusks just emerging. Its hide is already thick and slightly rough to the touch. It sits exactly where it is placed and looks at everything with an expression of extreme patience that seems implausible for something this small. In the Crystal Mines it waddles into crystal-lit caverns and simply sits, which other creatures interpret as wisdom - it is mostly just comfortable.
stages.note: Young Tuskos calves can sit perfectly still for two hours - researchers initially mistook them for unusually convincing stone carvings.

stages.name: Tuskodon
stages.bio: Tuskodon is enormously wide and low, its thick grey hide now studded with rock-crystal protrusions that catch light from every direction. Its two large forward tusks have become thick and blunt-edged, excellent for prying up crystal formations from the mine floor - which it does regularly and seemingly at random. It moves through narrow mine passages by simply expanding them, and the Crystal Mines maintenance crews have learned to re-route paths around Tuskodon's preferred corridors rather than fight it.
stages.note: Tuskodon always yawns before it moves - the yawn functions as a ten-second warning system, which the mine crews genuinely rely on.

stages.name: Megatus
stages.bio: Megatus is a colossal, open-mouthed behemoth - all wide jaw and mountainous stone-hide - whose body has gradually fused with the crystal and rock of the mines over decades. Crystal formations now grow directly from its spine and shoulders, glowing with the same light as the deepest Crystal Mine veins. Its roar can shatter loose crystal formations fifty metres away. Megatus does not guard the mines - it simply is the mines, as much as any tunnel or vein, and has been here longer than the first miners' torches.
stages.note: Crystal formations grow on Megatus's back at a measurable rate - geologists use them to date the creature's age to at least two hundred years.

stages.name: Pigmole
stages.bio: Pigmole is a round, golden-brown creature blending pig and mole: a wide snout, small forward eyes, and two tiny crystal-blue tusks flanking its nose. Its stubby body barely clears the ground, and its feet are wide-pawed for digging. In the Granite Heights it burrows into the thin soil between rocks, surfacing to sniff the cold mountain air and immediately going back down. It communicates with other Pigmoles by tapping its tusks against buried stones - a surprisingly complex language made entirely of knocks.
stages.note: Each Pigmole has a personal tusk-tap rhythm - other Pigmoles recognise individuals by the beat alone, even through ten feet of granite.

stages.name: Groundtusk
stages.bio: Groundtusk has emerged as a powerful digging beast with a wide muscular back, heavy shoulders, and strong claws designed to break through compacted granite. It burrows headfirst into solid rock-face with its broad snout acting as a wedge, and its dark coat is permanently streaked with granite dust. Its eyes have grown even smaller as it relies on vibration-sensing through its wide paws to navigate. On the Granite Heights it creates hidden tunnels just wide enough for itself - and precisely that narrow.
stages.note: Groundtusk emerges only at night and seals each tunnel entrance with a plug of earth it mixes with its own saliva - the plugs are waterproof.

stages.name: Terravorn
stages.bio: Terravorn erupts from the ground rather than climbs out of it - a massive, dark, soil-caked behemoth with wide crushing forelimbs, a scarred and heavy snout, and a back that is half-buried by the mountain dirt permanently clinging to its hide. Its tusks are broad and deeply scored. A dark aura clings to it, not evil, but profoundly ancient - the kind of darkness that belongs to deep places where light has never reached. The Granite Heights have recorded this creature's emergence sites for generations: the same three clearings, decade after decade.
stages.note: Terravorn always surfaces at the same three granite clearings, ten years apart - the locals put out a flat stone as a landing pad, and it uses it every time.

stages.name: Snoutlet
stages.bio: Tuskton's first form is a bright-eyed, warm-brown boar piglet with two small but sharp incipient tusks and a trotting gait so bouncy it seems to have springs in its feet. Its snout is perpetually dusty from rooting around in the mortar between Steel Fortress flagstones. It has no sense of personal space and headbutts friends, strangers, and structural columns with equal enthusiasm. The garrison considers it a mascot - until it discovers where the food stores are.
stages.note: Tuskton piglets have been found in seventeen different supply rooms they had no apparent way of entering - no one knows how.

stages.name: Tuskhog
stages.bio: Tuskhog is a scarred, shaggy-maned boar with two thick curved tusks, a bristling ridge of dark fur along its spine, and the kind of expression that suggests it has not been surprised by anything in years. Its hooves ring on cobblestones. It patrols the lower levels of the Steel Fortress as if the patrols are its own idea - which they may be. In battle it dips its head and rams with the full force of its neck, and the garrison has learned that a Tuskhog arriving at a run is more reliable early warning than any bell.
stages.note: Tuskhog always lowers its head three seconds before charging - experienced trainers use those three seconds to redirect it at their problem instead.

stages.name: Ironboar
stages.bio: Ironboar is a fully armoured war-boar with interlocking steel plates covering its flanks, shoulders, and face, two great curved tusks banded in dark iron, and a single prominent horn rising from the centre of its armoured forehead. Its charge shakes the ground fifty metres out. The Steel Fortress has three gates; two of them were reinforced specifically with Ironboar charges in mind. Ironboar holds no grudges - it simply believes the fortress should be exactly as strong as it is, and regularly tests the hypothesis.
stages.note: Ironboar has been recorded charging the same outer wall section every spring for twelve years - the garrison now treats it as an annual structural stress test.

stages.name: Shadowkit
stages.bio: Shadowkit is a sleek, dark-grey kitten with large round ears lined in pink-white, wide violet eyes, and a single golden crescent moon marking on its chest that seems to glow with inner light. Its long tail curls upward at the tip like a question mark. It sits very still and watches - which is more unsettling than anything it actually does. In Ghost Hollow it is found near the quietest pools, staring into the water at something only it can see. When startled, it vanishes and reappears a few steps away without apparent movement.
stages.note: Shadowkit's crescent-chest mark brightens exactly at moonrise and fades at dawn - the brightness can be read like a clock if you know the schedule.

stages.name: Nighthound
stages.bio: Nighthound has grown into a powerful dark lion with a wild, sweeping black mane and yellow-orange glowing eyes. Its body is long and low, built for stalking rather than sprinting. A deep shadow aura ripples from its mane in slow waves, dimming the air around it as if it carries its own private night. In Ghost Hollow it walks the border between the living forest and the hollow's permanent darkness - a threshold guardian that belongs to both worlds and is fully claimed by neither.
stages.note: Nighthound's shadow-aura dims lanterns within two metres - experienced trackers always carry a second light source when they know one is near.

stages.name: Abysswrath
stages.bio: Abysswrath is a colossal dark beast - lion-bodied but massive, with gold-striped flanks, a crown of forward-jutting black spines, and eyes that burn amber-gold with centuries of patient watching. It moves in almost absolute silence despite its size, and the shadow that trails it does not match the light source - it stretches toward Ghost Hollow regardless of where the sun is. The guardians say Abysswrath does not guard the Hollow: it is the Hollow, given will and direction.
stages.note: Abysswrath's shadow always points toward Ghost Hollow's deepest chamber - navigators lost in the woods follow it as a compass.

stages.name: Umbrapup
stages.bio: This Umbrapup is a small, compact wolf pup with fur so dark it absorbs light, bright yellow eyes that pierce the cave gloom, and small rounded ears that track every sound. Wisps of shadow drift from its paws when it walks, leaving a faint ghostly trail. It follows the old patrol routes of the Shadow Caves instinctively, before any trainer ever teaches it to - as if the paths are already written into its bones. The guardians believe Akilla's loyalty passed into these pups when he was lost to Abalont's shadow.
stages.note: Umbrapup pups always run the same patrol loop when left alone - the exact route varies by individual, but none of them ever learned it.

stages.name: Nightfang
stages.bio: Nightfang is a lean, athletic wolf whose body seems to blur at the edges, as if it is slightly out of phase with the solid world. Shadow wisps trail from its flanks and muzzle constantly, and its glowing yellow eyes are the brightest things in any cave it enters. It runs its patrols at a precise trot - the same speed, the same corners, the same pauses. Any creature that falls into step beside it is safe for as long as they keep pace. The Shadow Caves remember every guardian who ever walked them.
stages.note: Nightfang pauses at the exact spot where old patrol logs say Akilla always stopped to check the eastern passage - every single round.

stages.name: Abysswraith
stages.bio: Abysswraith is barely a body at all - a vast dark wolf-shaped wraith with swirling shadow tendrils instead of solid limbs, glowing yellow eyes visible from forty metres in total darkness, and a howl that shakes dust from cave ceilings. It runs its eternal patrol at full speed now, shadow-tentacles streaming behind it, and any shadow it passes through becomes impassable to Abalont's creatures for a full day. The guardians believe Abysswraith is keeping Akilla's place warm, and that it will step aside the moment he returns.
stages.note: Abysswraith's patrol completes in exactly the same duration every time - to the second - regardless of how many obstacles have changed.

stages.name: Crowmber
stages.bio: Crowmber is a round, scruffy black crow chick with orange-red glowing eyes that look too large for its small head. Its stubby wings are just long enough to flutter uselessly, and it compensates by hopping vigorously toward anything interesting. At the Lava Crater it perches on cooling obsidian ledges, watching the lava flows with those bright ember-eyes, counting things only it understands. Its feathers are slightly singed at the tips, which seems to be the natural state rather than the result of any accident.
stages.note: Crowmber chicks always face the volcano when sleeping - no matter which direction their perch points, they reorient during the night.

stages.name: Ravux
stages.bio: Ravux is a full-grown crow with sleek black plumage, wide swept wings edged in ember-orange, and those unnerving orange eyes now sharp and calculating. It sits very upright, turning its head at precise angles to examine things from multiple perspectives before acting. In the Lava Crater it rides thermal columns rising from open lava lakes, gaining altitude effortlessly. When it calls out, the sound carries farther than seems possible for a bird its size - the crater's acoustics amplify its voice into a distant, ringing caw.
stages.note: Ravux can locate a thermal column by tilting its head fifteen degrees precisely and sampling the airflow with its crest feathers - it never circles twice before finding one.

stages.name: Shadowryx
stages.bio: Shadowryx is a large, imposing dark crow with a broad wingspan edged in deep orange-red like slow-burning coal, heavy tail feathers that trail embers when it flies, and eyes that glow with the steady heat of the Lava Crater's core. It moves deliberately and without unnecessary display - it does not need display. Where it lands, the rock warms visibly. It is one of the few creatures that can cross the crater's active flow zone without deviation, reading the lava's movement patterns in the heat shimmer days before they shift.
stages.note: Shadowryx lands on the same three obsidian spires at each sunset in sequence - the spires have been measured to be fractionally warmer than the surrounding rock.

stages.name: Urskling
stages.bio: Urskling is a plump, warm-brown bear cub with a single small steel-blue spike rising from the top of its head like a tiny helmet-crest. Its eyes are wide and warm, and it walks the Amber Desert with its nose low to the sand, sniffing every grain as if searching for something Hunter the watcher lost at sunset. Its paws are large for its body - already built for strength it hasn't grown into yet. It repeats words quietly to itself as it patrols, practicing the way a good guardian always keeps skills sharp.
stages.note: Urskling cubs walk the same patrol route every evening within minutes of the same time - they seem to have absorbed Hunter's schedule through the desert sand itself.

stages.name: Urskalon
stages.bio: Urskalon is a broad-shouldered bear now sporting a full ridge of steel-grey spines running from the back of its skull down its spine. Its thick desert-tan coat is streaked with dust it never fully shakes. It patrols with a long, measured stride, pausing at specific landmarks to sniff the air - the same landmarks Hunter once checked. Other Amber Desert creatures give it a wide berth, not out of fear, but out of something closer to respect. Its strength is quiet, purposeful, and patient in the way that only long practice makes.
stages.note: Urskalon stops at the exact same three desert rocks every patrol - each one, when pressed, is warm from a different underground heat source it has memorized.

stages.name: Urskalith
stages.bio: Urskalith is fully armoured - steel-grey plate fused across shoulders, chest, and flanks, a spiked crown of blade-like dorsal spines, and massive paws that leave craters in hardpacked desert sand. Its face carries decades of dust in every crease, and its eyes hold a patience that has outlasted every storm the Amber Desert has offered. It does not fight unless forced; it simply stands where it stands, and the desert moves around it. The guardians say Urskalith carries Hunter's oath in its bones - strength is for protecting words, never for stealing them.
stages.note: Urskalith's armour plates carry the magnetic alignment of the Amber Desert's bedrock - navigators claim a compass held near it points not north but toward the nearest word that needs protecting.

stages.name: Cubyx
stages.bio: Cubyx is a small, stocky honey-badger with a dark lower body, pale sandy upper face, and tiny bright eyes that convey one emotion: absolute determination. Its short claws are already hardening at the tips. In the Crystal Mines it investigates everything with its nose-first charge style - pointing itself at an interesting rock formation and walking straight into it, then looking indignant when it doesn't move. It eats whatever it finds and finds everything. Researchers note it has no off-switch.
stages.note: Cubyx has been observed attempting to challenge creatures twelve times its own size - in every recorded case, the larger creature simply stepped aside.

stages.name: Urskar
stages.bio: Urskar is a longer, meaner honey-badger with a pale stripe across its broad head, a muscular neck, and thick claws darkened by constant rock-work. It moves through the Crystal Mines in a low, fast trot that never seems to tire. When it decides something needs to move - a boulder, a rival, a trainer who blocked a tunnel - it starts pushing and does not stop until it gets its way. Crystal Mine crews give it priority over all other foot traffic in narrow shafts, a policy established after the third incident.
stages.note: Urskar has never backed away from a confrontation - researchers believe it lacks the neurological pathway to consider retreat as an option.

stages.name: Ironpaw
stages.bio: Ironpaw is a powerfully built armoured badger-bear with thick steel-plate shoulders and haunches, reinforced claws the length of a hand that leave scored tracks in crystal-embedded stone, and a scarred, grizzled snout that has never met an obstacle it respected. It controls the deepest shafts of the Crystal Mines, and the crystal formations there are in better shape than anywhere else - Ironpaw keeps them clear of debris and collapses simply by living there. It is deeply territorial and consistently effective, and the mine crews would never dream of asking it to leave.
stages.note: Ironpaw's claw marks on Crystal Mine walls are used by surveyors to trace old passages - the marks stay sharp for decades in the hardest rock.

stages.name: Cubear
stages.bio: Cubear is a wide, dark-blue bear cub with a stout face, round ears, and a row of short spine-like ridges budding along its back. It walks with a slight waddle that it will lose as it grows. In the Sand Dunes it follows the morning shadows cast by great dunes, resting when the shadow is cool and walking when it warms - a natural navigator for a landscape that shifts nightly. When it finds a name it has never heard carved into dune-drift monuments, it sits in front of it and refuses to leave until it feels it has understood.
stages.note: Cubear cubs sit in front of any carved inscription they encounter for an average of four minutes before moving on - researchers cannot explain what they are doing.

stages.name: Ursolt
stages.bio: Ursolt is a heavy, darkly-coloured bear with well-developed spines along its back and thick, sand-worn paws. Its shoulders are broad and its stride deliberate. It still follows the shadow-paths of the dunes, but now it also makes them - the wide furrow of its passage creates a reliable windbreak other Sand Dunes creatures shelter behind. When it stands upright to survey the horizon, it can see for miles across the flat sea of sand, and it remembers every landmark in three hundred and sixty degrees.
stages.note: Ursolt's rear-track furrow is consistent enough that Sand Dune traders use old Ursolt trails as navigational paths - they stay stable for weeks.

stages.name: Ursovex
stages.bio: Ursovex is immense - a towering dark bear whose back-spines have grown into a dramatic crown of ridges, whose paws leave deep impressions even in packed desert, and whose presence on a dune ridge is visible from the nearest oasis. It does not roar to announce itself; it simply stands where all can see and that is sufficient. The Sand Dunes' most dangerous crossing routes all pass through Ursovex territory - and all of them are safe because of it. Children taking their first long walk in this region are told: if you lose your way, find Ursovex's ridge and you are found.
stages.note: Ursovex has never moved from the same ridge at sunrise in eleven years of observations - it is the most reliable fixed point in the entire Sand Dunes region.

stages.name: Vaulkit
stages.bio: Vaulkit is a small but armoured creature: a stout, rounded body encased in a grey full-plate helmet and chest-piece, with a swirling green runic emblem glowing on its front - a mark of purpose rather than power. Its tiny limbs stick out from beneath the armour at optimistic angles. Despite its size, it carries itself with the bearing of something that has already decided it will not be moved. In the Bug Thicket, it patrols the thorny paths where no other creature bothers to go, checking every root and leaf with methodical care.
stages.note: Vaulkit's rune-glow brightens when it encounters an unlearned word - the glow intensity appears to correlate to how important the word will later become.

stages.name: Vaultusk
stages.bio: Vaultusk has grown into a powerful, low-slung guardian with thick armour plates covering its entire upper body, a broad armoured face-plate, and two heavy curved tusks that glow faintly with the same green rune-light as its chest. Its legs are wide-set and planted, and it rarely runs - preferring to walk steadily at whatever it needs to deal with. In the Bug Thicket it has mapped every unsafe bridge, unstable trunk, and dangerous burrow, and it redirects creatures away from them with a firm shoulder-block, no words needed.
stages.note: Vaultusk's tusks glow stronger when near danger - trainers say a tusk-brightness of three means turn around, four means run.

stages.name: Vaulwarden
stages.bio: Vaulwarden is a massive, battle-worn armoured badger-guardian covered head-to-haunch in heavy plate, with bright green runic glyphs blazing across its chest and bracers, and twin heavy tusks that arc wide and catch light from across the Bug Thicket. Its helm is dented and scratched from centuries of guarding, but the runes beneath the scratches still shine. It is the oldest warden in the Thicket - it does not know how many threats it has turned aside, only that it is still standing and so is the Thicket.
stages.note: Vaulwarden's runes have been identified as an older form of the guardian sigils - scholars believe they predate all known guardian records by several centuries.

stages.name: Veilkit
stages.bio: Veilkit looks like a smooth, grey-purple oval with two wide, glowing lavender eyes and a single bright psychic gem embedded in its belly. Tiny stubby limbs press close to its sides, and the whole body has a pearly sheen as though lit from inside. It sits perfectly still in shafts of light that filter through the Psychic Temple canopy, soaking up the luminous energy of light-trees. It communicates entirely by pulsing its belly gem - one pulse for yes, two for no - before it has yet grown a voice.
stages.note: Veilkit's belly gem pulses exactly once per second; a double-pulse means it has sensed an unfamiliar sound nearby.

stages.name: Veilsect
stages.bio: Veilsect has encased itself in a segmented purple-grey cocoon of chitin, three horizontal bands of ridged armour wrapping its torso. Its head emerges with large compound eyes glowing violet and a pair of small antennae that quiver to pick up stray thoughts. The gem has moved to a deep recess in its chest and pulses with a slow, rhythmic throb. Resting against light-tree trunks in the Psychic Temple, it absorbs the stored warmth stored in the bark and grows its mind quietly in the dark.
stages.note: Press an ear to a light-tree where Veilsect rests and you will hear faint notes humming back - borrowed sounds it is memorising.

stages.name: Veilstyx
stages.bio: Veilstyx hovers among the highest light-trees of the Psychic Temple, patrolling corridors of still, humming air. The Guardians called it the Keeper of Promises - it remembers every voice it has ever stood near, and forgets none of them.
stages.note: Veilstyx can replay any voice it has ever heard in perfect clarity, projecting it as a shimmering note audible only to the person who first spoke.

stages.name: Veilmin
stages.bio: Veilmin appears as a small purple teardrop of pure psychic flame with a single bright eye at its forward point and a flowing fiery tail that streams behind it. No legs, no arms - it drifts on wind currents at the Gale Ridge's base, drawn toward lightning sparks and the smell of ozone. It steers by tilting its teardrop body and can turn in a space no wider than a hand. Young scholars at the Ridge often lose track of it mid-lesson because it silently slips into a drafty corner the moment it grows bored.
stages.note: Veilmin can hover inside a lamp flame without being harmed; it uses candle light to read the shadows of passing sounds on cave walls.

stages.name: Veilwing
stages.bio: Veilwing has grown a proper body - a sleek purple avian form with a rounded head, two broad tapered wings edged with violet flame-feathers, and a long plume tail that crackles with static. Its single bright eye has been joined by a second, giving it full front-facing binocular vision. It rides the rotating updrafts around the Gale Ridge with total ease, folding its wings to plunge and spreading them again to brake hard. When it speaks, the nearby air pressure drops just slightly and loose dust spirals upward.
stages.note: A sudden fall in air pressure during calm weather at the Gale Ridge almost always means a Veilwing has just passed overhead.

stages.name: Veilphantom
stages.bio: The Guardians say it carries the voices of everyone the Ridge has lost in the spaces between its wingbeats.
stages.note: When Veilphantom spreads its crest fully, the wind within a hundred metres changes direction to match where it is looking.

name: Veldfawn

stages.name: Veldfawn
stages.bio: Veldfawn is a small golden-green deer fawn whose body is entirely wrapped in layered leaves and soft mossy fur, with bright amber eyes and a tiny cluster of twig-antlers sprouting from its forehead. Its legs are slender and sure-footed, and a fringe of small leaves runs along its back like a mane. It wanders through the Dark Forest's lighter clearings where thin beams of sunlight pierce the canopy, standing perfectly still in each beam to absorb the rare light. The forest creatures nearby grow calm and slightly brighter in its presence.
stages.note: Veldfawn turns its twig-antlers to face the nearest pinprick of sunlight the way a flower tracks the sky.

stages.name: Veldeer
stages.bio: Veldeer stands tall and proud, its body now a rich dark green wrapped in thick overlapping leaves that form a natural armour along its flanks. Its antlers have grown into full branching tree-like structures with small glowing buds at their tips that shed soft warm light in the darkness of the forest. Its eyes shine golden-amber and it moves without sound through undergrowth, each hoof-step falling as softly as a leaf. Where Veldeer walks in the Dark Forest, bioluminescent fungi spring up in its hoofprints within a day.
stages.note: The glowing buds on Veldeer's antlers shed enough light to read by on moonless nights - forest children have always known this.

stages.name: Sylvanarch
stages.bio: Sylvanarch is a magnificent stag whose great antlers spread wide as a tree canopy, leafed out in full summer green with bright golden light emanating from every tine. Its body is wrapped in deep green layered leaves as dense as armour, and its chest and flanks carry a warm amber glow visible from far off through the trees. When it exhales, small motes of light drift from its breath. The Dark Forest guardians speak of it as the living lantern of the wood - wherever it chooses to rest, the forest is never fully dark again.
stages.note: Sylvanarch sheds one antler-tine each winter solstice; wherever a tine falls, a new song-tree grows by spring.

blurb: Veldfawn lost its herd among the glowing trees. Help Veldfawn find its friends!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Akilla.
facts: Deer can run fast and jump very high.
question: What is a baby deer called?

stages.name: Velkit
stages.bio: Velkit is a small lavender-pink rabbit sitting compactly with its round body, long upright ears, and two bright rosy eyes. Its fur has a soft iridescent sheen and its nose twitches constantly as it reads the light patterns scattered through the Psychic Temple canopy. It sits very still and then vanishes in a flicker, reappearing three body-lengths away with no sound in between. Scholars who study it have never been able to find the moment it actually moves - it simply is one place, then another.
stages.note: Velkit blinks between positions so fast that slow-movement studies have logged it covering two metres in zero measurable time.

stages.name: Velvoid
stages.bio: Velvoid has grown lean and quick, its lavender body now stretched into a sprinting form with long powerful hind legs and ears swept back in constant motion. Its eyes have deepened to a bright magenta and it leaves faint afterimage trails of light when it runs - not glowing tracks on the ground, but ghost-images of itself that linger in the air for half a second. It patrols the outer edges of the Psychic Temple at speed, darting between light-trees and occasionally freezing to stare at something no one else can see.
stages.note: Velvoid's afterimage trails fade in exactly 0.4 seconds - rangers use them as breadcrumbs to find which path it took.

stages.name: Velaxis
stages.bio: In the Psychic Temple it is known as the Gatekeeper of the Still - the creature the Guardians trusted to guard the quiet between one breath and the next.
stages.note: The rings of light Velaxis pulses before a leap have been measured - each ring travels exactly one metre per pulse, spacing out an arrival announcement.

stages.name: Sproutlet
stages.bio: Sproutlet is a round, freshly-hatched chick still wearing the bottom half of its eggshell like a little skirt, its yellow-green down fluffy and bright. Two small leaf-like wing-nubs sprout from its sides and a neat tuft of green feathers tops its head. Its beak is short and bright orange and it opens wide whenever wind passes through - as if it is tasting the Gale Ridge's famous updrafts for the first time. It follows whatever is moving nearest to it and cheeps loudly when left alone.
stages.note: Sproutlet cannot yet fly but bounces nearly twenty centimetres when it flaps hard enough - the eggshell skirt rattles like a tiny drum.

stages.name: Leafawk
stages.bio: Leafawk is a bright green parrot with a long elegant tail feather, a rounded white-crested head, and wide wings that it holds slightly open at all times as if ready to catch the next gust. Its eyes are large and golden and it tilts its head sharply to listen - it repeats back any sound it hears within three seconds, always perfectly pronounced. At the Gale Ridge it is prized by young learners because it refuses to let a mispronounced sound go unchallenged, chirping the correct form until they get it right.
stages.note: Leafawk will repeat a sound back exactly seventeen times before it gives up - trainers have counted.

stages.name: Verdantyx
stages.bio: Verdantyx is a magnificent green griffin with a broad feline body, powerful feathered wings broad enough to block the sun, and a proud crested head with a fierce golden eye. Its plumage is vivid green and gold, and its primary feathers are as wide as ssounds. When it launches from the Gale Ridge's crags, the downblast flattens every blade of grass in a five-metre circle. The guardians treated it as a living storm-warning: when Verdantyx circles three times instead of two, a full tempest is coming within the hour.
stages.note: Verdantyx circles clockwise in fair weather and counter-clockwise when a storm is forming - Gale Ridge keepers stake their safety on this.

stages.name: Verdling
stages.bio: Verdling is a compact little dragonoid covered in dark green scales with golden highlights and a circular golden emblem on its chest like a shield-crest. Its snout is blunt and wide, its eyes bold and alert, and four sturdy legs carry it in a quick waddling trot. Small spines run along its back. Despite living in the Lava Crater's outer edges it is drawn to wind - it scrambles to the highest nearby rock and opens its mouth into the gusts, apparently feeding on hot volcanic updrafts that carry trace mineral dust.
stages.note: Verdling's chest crest heats up noticeably in strong volcanic winds - rangers use this to find hidden vents.

stages.name: Verdaxon
stages.bio: Verdaxon has grown into a powerful quadruped with thickened dark scales trimmed in gold and teal, a broader armoured chest bearing its golden crest, and a heavier spiked back ridge. Its neck is long and muscular and its jaw can open wide enough to swallow a full thermal updraft and hold it. It uses that stored wind energy to sprint at speed across the Lava Crater's stone plateaus, arriving at prey locations before they register any approach. The volcanic ash it constantly breathes has darkened its scales beautifully.
stages.note: Verdaxon holds a thermal breath for up to forty seconds - long enough to silently cross the full width of the crater's central platform.

stages.name: Verdaxarch
stages.bio: Verdaxarch is a towering dragon armoured in overlapping dark plates with gold inlay and dramatic teal-green wing membranes spread wide between spined ribs. Its back carries rows of tall jagged spines and its tail ends in a heavy spiked club. Its eyes burn bright gold-green under a heavy armoured brow. It rules the Lava Crater's rim, perched above the heat columns, and draws the volcanic gales through its body to power devastating breath attacks. The guardians recorded its wingspan as the reason half the Crater's ash clouds blow sideways.
stages.note: Verdaxarch's wing-membrane spines create a whistling tone in strong winds that can be heard from three craters away.

stages.name: Verdlet
stages.bio: Verdlet is a small four-legged dinosaur with bright green scaly skin, a broad rounded head, and a row of yellow spikes running down its back and over its skull. It moves in quick confident bursts, tail held up, and snuffles along the ground of the Dark Forest with its blunt snout, nosing aside leaf litter to find seeds lodged in the soil. The yellow spikes on its head can stand erect when it is startled, making it look twice as large - an effective trick against the forest's shadow-creatures.
stages.note: Verdlet's back spikes stand straight up when it is frightened; they relax flat again only after five full minutes of calm.

stages.name: Verdaur
stages.bio: Verdaur has grown into a proper ceratopsian-like body - squat and heavily built, with a broad armoured back covered in large yellow-green spines and a rounded low-slung head. Its green scales have thickened and its legs are planted wide and strong. It grazes the deep soil of the Dark Forest floor, using its front feet to dig and its heavy head to bulldoze fallen logs aside. Despite its bulk it is surprisingly quiet and the forest's shrieking night-birds do not flee from it - they nest between its back spines.
stages.note: Dark Forest rangers have found up to eleven bird nests wedged between Verdaur's back spines at the same time; it doesn't seem to notice.

stages.name: Verdolith
stages.bio: Verdolith is a massive dinosaur whose broad body has become heavily armoured with rock-like scale plates, its back a fortress of tall yellow-green stone spines that catch and hold the rare shafts of light in the Dark Forest. Its wide low head is set on a thick neck and its legs are like pillars. When it walks, the ground itself vibrates and loose stones rattle. The guardians called it a living mountain - not because of its bulk, but because it has not changed direction in centuries, slowly and certainly wearing its own trail through the forest floor.
stages.note: Verdolith has carved a permanent groove into the Dark Forest floor by taking the same path for so long - plants grow differently in its shadow-trail.

stages.name: Sprouquill
stages.bio: Sprouquill is a rotund white-green chick with a fluffy round body, a short orange beak, and two tiny leaf-tipped wings tucked against its sides. A single bright green leaf-feather sprouts from its crown. It navigates the low tangles of the Bug Thicket by hopping rather than flying, its big eyes blinking rapidly as it monitors the constant insect traffic above. It chirps once whenever it spots something new, which in the Bug Thicket means it chirps approximately every four seconds.
stages.note: Sprouquill's one-chirp-per-new-thing habit makes it an accidental census tool - researchers have mapped the Bug Thicket by tallying its chirp rate.

stages.name: Wingvern
stages.bio: Wingvern is a lean bright parrot with vivid green and gold plumage, broad upswept wings and a dramatic yellow crest that fans forward over its beak when it calls. Its long tail feathers trail behind it as it swoops through the Bug Thicket canopy. It has learned to mimic the clicks and buzzes of the Thicket's larger insects and uses these sounds to navigate through tunnels of foliage too dense for sight. Researchers who have heard it call among the bugs say the Thicket briefly falls silent - even the insects stop to listen.
stages.note: Wingvern can exactly replicate fourteen distinct Bug Thicket insect alarm calls, silencing the whole colony each time it uses one.

stages.name: Sovereign
stages.bio: Sovereign is a vast and magnificent parrot with deep green and golden plumage, a broad heavy beak capable of snapping thick branches, and an ornate spiky crown of golden feathers radiating from its head. Its wings span wide as a child is tall and beat with heavy authority. It perches at the very crown of the tallest trees in the Bug Thicket and the canopy literally sways around it when it calls. The guardians named it Sovereign because even the Thicket's most chaotic creatures go still when it speaks.
stages.note: When Sovereign calls from the treetops, every creature in the Bug Thicket within two hundred metres ceases movement for exactly three seconds.

stages.name: Verdex
stages.bio: Verdex is a small bright green quadruped with a rounded head topped by golden-tipped hornlets, a wide friendly mouth, and a short leaf-shaped tail. Its stubby limbs carry it in a cheerful waddling trot along the Dragon Spire's lower terraces where ferns and mosses still grow among the old stone. Two leaf-sprout appendages flutter near its neck like tiny wings in training. It constantly gnaws on the stone ledges - not to eat them, but because its teeth grow fastest against hard material and it must keep them filed.
stages.note: Verdex's hornlets grow one millimetre per week; keepers can date a photograph of one by measuring the horn length.

stages.name: Folion
stages.bio: Folion stands upright now, a graceful dragon-plant hybrid with flowing leafy appendages at its collar and tail, gold and green scale-plating on its chest, and a longer more angular head crowned by swept-back golden horns. Its body is draped in living vine-like tendrils that it can extend or retract at will, using them to grip rocky ledges on the Dragon Spire. When it stands still long enough, new growth sprouts from its shoulders - it is never the same shape twice from one week to the next.
stages.note: Plant-scholars measuring Folion's vine growth have found it adds roughly three centimetres of new tendril per day in the Dragon Spire's humid air.

stages.name: Phyllarch
stages.bio: Phyllarch is a great dragon whose entire body is part creature, part living tree - massive green and gold wings spread wide, each membrane threaded with leaf-veins that photosynthesize in the Dragon Spire's open air. Its broad body is armoured in overlapping leaf-scale plates and its long neck carries a regal head crowned by large branching gold horns. It breathes a mist of pollen and living spores rather than fire. The guardians knew it as the Archdruid of Dragons - it tends the vine-trees of the Spire the way a gardener tends a prize garden.
stages.note: When Phyllarch exhales fully, the pollen cloud it releases can cause any plant within ten metres to flower regardless of season.

stages.name: Sproutch
stages.bio: Sproutch is an endearingly round little bird, almost perfectly spherical, covered in scruffy olive-green feathers and a messy tuft of brown twigs on its crown. Its large round eyes take up most of its face and its tiny beak pokes out from between two enormous cheeks of fluffy down. It sits on ledges at the Gale Ridge's base and watches the updrafts above it with total fascination - it cannot yet fly but it leans into the wind gusts so hard it sometimes tips over and has to right itself with visible effort.
stages.note: Sproutch has been observed tipping forward in a gust exactly forty-one times in a single day - it never seems to learn to brace itself.

stages.name: Rambrake
stages.bio: Rambrake has shot up into a tall, gangly heron shape with long spindly legs, a narrow body draped in unkempt green plumage, and a wild mane of twigs and trailing feathers that the wind constantly tangles further. Its long sharp beak is hooked at the tip and it stands with a slight forward lean, one leg raised, utterly still in the Gale Ridge's roaring crosswinds for minutes at a time. It is learning balance - each storm season it can stand still in a slightly stronger gust than the last.
stages.note: Researchers have recorded Rambrake standing motionless in winds exceeding eighty kilometres per hour - it has never been blown over.

stages.name: Thornheron
stages.bio: Thornheron is a great and gaunt heron of the Gale Ridge, its body draped in dark green and brown storm-worn plumage, its crown a wild spray of twig-feathers that spike outward in every direction. Its long legs are scarred by lightning strikes it stood through rather than fled. It extends its wide ragged wings against the most violent storms and does not move - it uses the entire tempest as a kind of meditation, processing the raw energy of the Ridge's weather into deep calm. The guardians said nothing at the Ridge grew older or more unshakeable.
stages.note: Thornheron has been documented standing in the same spot through fourteen consecutive major Gale Ridge tempests; the stone beneath its feet is worn smooth by its grip.

stages.name: Chiplit
stages.bio: Chiplit is a small round owl with vivid yellow-green feathers and large, luminous amber eyes that seem to absorb the dim light of the Dark Forest floor with perfect ease. Tufted ear-feathers poke upward and a wave of softer green down covers its belly. Its talons grip a twig and it swivels its head without moving its body, tracking sounds the way a satellite dish follows a signal. It hunts by sound alone on moonless nights and has never missed a target it fixed on - but it refuses to pursue anything it cannot hear perfectly.
stages.note: Chiplit will tilt its head left and right exactly three times before it commits to a strike - watch for the third tilt.

stages.name: Verdowl
stages.bio: Verdowl has grown broader and more angular, its feathers now a complex patterning of deep green and cream with streaked wing markings and a wide flat face designed to funnel sound. Its broad wings give it near-silent flight even in the noisy Dark Forest understory. It has adopted the unusual habit of sitting at the base of song-trees during storms and tilting its face dish into the gusts - apparently the wind carries whisper-fragments of old words from broken branches and Verdowl is cataloguing them.
stages.note: Linguists have confirmed that Verdowl hoots contain fragments matching calls lost from Dark Forest lore over fifty years ago.

stages.name: Zephyrowl
stages.bio: Zephyrowl is a commanding great owl with vast green-gold wings spread wide in flight, a flat broad face of extraordinary sensitivity, and layered feathers that rustle constantly as it adjusts to catch every passing air current. Its amber eyes now glow with a deep inner light and it rarely blinks. It perches above the Dark Forest canopy for weeks at a time, face angled into the prevailing wind, reading it the way scholars read parchment. The guardians said it had heard every voice ever raised by the Dark Forest's trees and was slowly composing them into a single song.
stages.note: Zephyrowl has been observed stationary for twenty-two consecutive days - researchers believe it sleeps with one eye open and both ears active.

stages.name: Verdox
stages.bio: Verdox is a small, bright orange fox kit with large amber eyes, a wide fluffy tail, and two small clusters of green leaves worn around its neck like a scarf. Its fur is vivid and warm even against the Amber Desert's pale sands, making it easy to spot across flat terrain - which it seems unbothered by, trotting openly in daylight rather than hiding. It collects small green things - seeds, leaves, dry grass blades - and tucks them against its chest beneath its leaf-scarf, never discarding them even when they crumble.
stages.note: Verdox kits have been found carrying the same crumbled leaf-fragment for over a year; researchers believe it is a keepsake rather than food.

stages.name: Frondash
stages.bio: Frondash has grown into a lean upright warrior-fox, its body now draped in overlapping leaf armour plates of deep forest green, its limbs quick and powerful. A full mantle of leaves covers its shoulders and back like a cape and its amber eyes have sharpened to a fierce, precise gaze. It patrols the Amber Desert's ancient stone-garden ruins where green things still push through cracked stone, protecting pockets of living plant life from the desert's encroachment. It is the only creature seen digging irrigation channels with its bare paws.
stages.note: Frondash digs channels that always follow the hidden water table exactly - it senses groundwater the way others sense sunlight.

stages.name: Sylvarch
stages.bio: Sylvarch is a powerful, armoured fox-warrior standing nearly upright, its whole body sheathed in layered dark leaf-plates reinforced at the joints, a heavy mantle of leaves spreading from its shoulders like a general's cloak. Its amber eyes blaze with conviction and its wide tail fans behind it like a battle banner. In the Amber Desert it has created an oasis grove from nothing, planting seeds it carried from the Dark Forest and guarding them through every dry season since. It is the living proof that green things survive if someone chooses to protect them.
stages.note: The grove Sylvarch maintains in the Amber Desert contains forty-seven plant species found nowhere else within two hundred kilometres.

stages.name: Verdscale
stages.bio: Verdscale is a small upright green lizard with large round eyes, a wide friendly mouth, and a row of tiny green spines running from its skull to its tail tip. Its scales are bright leaf-green and its belly is a lighter cream. It clings to the cooler rock faces of the Lava Crater's outer edge where mossy tendrils still grow in the cracks, pressing flat to absorb both the warmth from below and what little plant energy the sparse vegetation offers. It communicates by flicking its forked tongue at varying speeds, which the crater's insect population has apparently learned to interpret.
stages.note: Verdscale's tongue-flick rate speeds up to over sixty per minute when it is excited - the insects scatter before any visible cause.

stages.name: Verdrax
stages.bio: Verdrax has grown into a proper Komodo-sized lizard, its green body now broader and more angular with sharper spines and a longer, heavier tail. Its scales have a slight metallic sheen and its eyes track with calm precision. It uses its heavy tail as a lever to move hot boulders aside when searching for the heat-resistant root-bulbs it subsists on in the Lava Crater. Where it digs, small green shoots sometimes appear days later - it has no intention of farming, but its digging consistently improves the soil.
stages.note: A strip of new green growth always appears in Verdrax's foraging path within two days - the volcanic soil it turns over is the richest in the Crater.

stages.name: Verdracus
stages.bio: Verdracus is a massive dragon whose broad body towers over the Lava Crater floor, large green-tipped wings folded against its sides and a sweeping heavy tail trailing behind it. Its scales are deep green and dark gold, armour-thick, and its wide-set eyes glow amber in the heat haze. Where it walks, vine-like root structures emerge from the lava rock behind it as if the stone itself is exhaling plant life. It moves with a total unhurried confidence that speaks of a creature that has never once needed to hurry - because nothing in the Crater challenges it.
stages.note: Scientists measuring Verdracus's territory have found that lava-rock in its path cools ten degrees faster than adjacent rock - its metabolism pulls heat from the stone directly.

stages.name: Sproutkit
stages.bio: Sproutkit is an utterly charming small lynx kitten whose warm tan-and-green fur sprouts little leaf buds at its ears and tail-tip. Two large green leaf-ears fan out from its head in place of ordinary ear-tufts, and its long curling tail ends in a bright green leaf. It prowls the Light Grove on oversized kitten paws, batting at falling leaves with the same intensity it will one day bring to real hunting. Its green ears fold flat when it is concentrating and fan wide when it is happy - a reliable mood indicator that the grove's other creatures have all learned to read.
stages.note: Sproutkit's leaf-ears droop by precisely thirty degrees each hour as it grows sleepy; grove-keepers use this as a nap timer.

stages.name: Verdlynx
stages.bio: Verdlynx has grown into a lean and agile lynx with a full coat of layered leaf-plating over its haunches and shoulders, bright amber-green eyes, and a sweeping leafy tail that trails on the ground as it moves. Its large paws are silent on any surface and it can change direction mid-spring without any apparent deceleration. It patrols the inner corridors of the Light Grove where the song-trees are densest, brushing its flanks against each trunk as it passes - the leaf-plates on its body have been found to carry trace pollen from every tree it has touched.
stages.note: Verdlynx can be tracked by the pollen-stripe it leaves on tree trunks - each grove plant contributes a distinct pollen colour to its coat.

stages.name: Sylvaxian
stages.bio: Sylvaxian is a magnificent great lion-lynx whose entire body is draped and armoured in thick layered leaves of deep forest green and gold, its broad mane a full spray of living leaf-fronds. Its amber eyes carry centuries of patience and its heavy paws leave deep, fertile impressions in the soil that sprout new growth within days. In the Light Grove it is both guardian and gardener - it has been tending the oldest song-trees since before any living guardian can remember, and the trees themselves grow toward it when it passes.
stages.note: The oldest song-tree in the Light Grove leans seventeen degrees toward the spot where Sylvaxian typically sleeps - botanists have been studying this for thirty years.

stages.name: Sproutscale
stages.bio: Sproutscale is a bright green iguana hatchling with a broad flat head crowned by a leafy crest, wide golden eyes, and a compact body carried low on four sturdy legs. Its tail is nearly as long as its body and it holds it curved upward. It is most comfortable in the sun-warmed clearings of Verdant Valley where it basks on flat rocks in the early morning, eyes half-closed, absorbing both warmth and the soft sounds of the valley's singing winds. It tests every rock it finds by tapping it twice - it is searching for one that sounds exactly right, for reasons it cannot explain.
stages.note: Sproutscale has been observed tapping over two hundred rocks in a single morning; it discards each one with the same decisive head-shake.

stages.name: Leafwyrm
stages.bio: Leafwyrm stands taller now, its body broadened and its back ridge of leaf-green spines now sharp and pronounced. Its golden eyes have steadied into a calm, measuring gaze and its broad flat head carries a more developed leafy crest. It patrols the climbing paths of Verdant Valley with a slow deliberate rhythm, testing each traveler it meets by blocking the trail and waiting. It is not hostile - it simply will not move aside until it judges whether the person before it is worth the valley's trust. It has never been wrong.
stages.note: In fourteen recorded encounters, Leafwyrm has moved aside for every trustworthy traveler and blocked every untrustworthy one without any known error.

stages.name: Verdrakian
stages.bio: Verdrakian is a great spiked dragon-lizard whose back is a fortress of tall leaf-green spines and whose heavy body moves with precise, unhurried authority.
