Its leafy crest has grown into a full crown and its golden eyes burn steady and deep. It guards a sun-warmed clearing deep in Verdant Valley that it has held since before Akilla fell - and the grass in that clearing grows greener and taller than anywhere else. Every traveler it has tested and found worthy has left with a leaf-scale from its crest; it grows them back in a week, unbothered.
stages.note: The clearing Verdrakian guards is the only place in all of Verdant Valley where three specific song-trees grow side by side - they have never been found elsewhere.

stages.name: Sproutym
stages.bio: Sproutym is a small, bright green snake with a rounded head, cheerful teal eyes, and two tiny leaf-like hornlets sprouting from its brow. It coils neatly on warm volcanic stones at the Lava Crater's edge, the hornlets trembling slightly in the heat shimmer. Despite living in such an unlikely place for a grass-type, it has claimed a particular cooled lava shelf where a seam of mineral-rich water keeps a thin film of living moss alive - its personal garden, which it defends with surprisingly vigorous hissing for its size.
stages.note: Sproutym's hornlets stand perfectly erect for exactly forty seconds after it drinks - researchers have no explanation for the timing.

stages.name: Windserpent
stages.bio: Windserpent has grown longer and more graceful, its body sinuous and bright green, and small white feathered wings have sprouted near its mid-section, beating gently to keep it aloft in slow gliding spirals over the Crater. Its hornlets have grown longer and more curved and its expression has deepened to something between serenity and hunger. It hunts by dropping silently out of the Crater's updrafts onto prey on the rock face below - the wings make no sound during descent. Even in the Lava Crater, it carries a persistent smell of fresh grass.
stages.note: Windserpent's fresh-grass scent has been confirmed by five independent researchers - no one can identify the source, as no grass grows within its territory.

stages.name: Vinewyrm
stages.bio: Vinewyrm is a huge coiling serpent-dragon with a broad armoured head, two heavy curling horns, and a body thick as a tree trunk that coils in great rings around the Lava Crater's central cone. Its scales are deep green and its underbelly catches the lava-glow in warm amber. It breathes a cloud of spores and mineral mist rather than fire - the spores, landing on the crater rock, bloom into tiny green patches that slowly grow. Over centuries, it has ringed the crater with a thin living wreath of stubborn vegetation.
stages.note: The ring of green growth around the Lava Crater's rim corresponds precisely to where Vinewyrm has coiled at rest over the past thousand years.

stages.name: Leafscale
stages.bio: Leafscale is a compact little lizard-dragon with bright green scales, a short leaf-tipped tail, and stubby legs that carry it in a quick excitable trot through the Bug Thicket undergrowth. A small ridge of leaf-shaped spines runs from its crown to its tail. Its wide eyes track the constant movement of the Thicket's insects and it has developed a hunting technique of absolute stillness followed by a single lunging snap - it catches flying insects out of midair with a success rate that larger, faster predators cannot match.
stages.note: Leafscale has been timed catching an airborne insect in forty-three milliseconds - faster than most predators twice its size.

stages.name: Verdyx
stages.bio: Verdyx is a well-built medium-sized lizard-dragon with broad leaf-thorn spines running down its back and flanks, a heavy armoured head, and a sweeping leaf-edged tail it uses both as a rudder while climbing and a weapon in territory disputes. Its green scales have darkened and it navigates the Bug Thicket by scent and vibration - it holds its head low and its tongue flickers constantly. The Thicket's insect colonies have learned to treat Verdyx's approach as a neutral event, which only encourages it to walk through their trails at full speed.
stages.note: Verdyx walks through the Bug Thicket's most active ant highways without detouring - the ants part, close behind it, and continue as if nothing happened.

stages.name: Phyllodrak
stages.bio: Phyllodrak is a powerful dragon whose broad armoured body is covered in layered leaf-scale plates and flanked by great spiked leaf-wings it can spread to block out the sun above the Bug Thicket canopy. Its back ridge of spines is now enormous - each spine the length of an arm - and its tail is heavy with leaf-armour plating. It rests at the deepest heart of the Thicket where the insect population is richest, motionless for days at a time, before suddenly moving the whole colony on a moment's silent judgment. Nothing in the Thicket challenges it. The largest beetles leave offerings at its resting spots.
stages.note: The beetles that nest nearest to Phyllodrak's resting sites are consistently thirty percent larger than those in other parts of the Thicket - researchers attribute this to soil enrichment.

stages.name: Squeamox
stages.bio: Squeamox is a small, round dark brown mouse with enormous amber eyes that take up most of its face, two oversized front teeth, and stubby powerful forepaws built for digging. Its ears are large and round and it holds its hands pressed together in front of its chest as it sits. It burrows into the Sand Dunes with impressive speed - a Squeamox can vanish into dry sand in less than two seconds flat - and it caches food pellets in small side-chambers off its main tunnel, then systematically forgets which chambers they are in.
stages.note: A single Squeamox tunnel system has been found to contain forty-three separate food caches - none of them ever revisited after the initial digging.

stages.name: Gnawmox
stages.bio: Gnawmox is a lean, battle-scarred sand rat with long whiskers, narrow amber eyes, and a long bare tail trailing behind it. Its brown fur has the texture of worn leather and its forepaws have grown heavy and clawed from years of excavation work. It moves low and fast across the Sand Dunes at night, hugging the shadows between dune crests, and rarely appears in the same place twice. Its gnaw-marks on dune stone have been studied and found to contain patterns - whether language, map, or simple habit, no one can yet say.
stages.note: Gnawmox gnaw-marks on dune stones always face north - researchers have proposed several theories and confirmed none of them.

stages.name: Pestilox
stages.bio: Pestilox is a massive, hunched armadillo-rat with a thick plated back of overlapping earth-brown armour scales, a wide flat head, enormous curved claws, and a long thick tail it swings as a club. Its small amber eyes glow dully in the dark of the deep dunes. It has abandoned the surface almost entirely, operating through a network of tunnels beneath the Sand Dunes so extensive that large sections of dune occasionally collapse into them. The Sand Dunes' few surface-dwellers treat the sudden appearance of a Pestilox as a serious warning that the ground ahead is unsafe.
stages.note: A section of Sand Dune that has partially collapsed overhead is almost certainly sitting above a Pestilox tunnel junction - they always collapse at the intersections first.

stages.name: Vespling
stages.bio: Vespling is a small purple-grey bat with round body, stubby pointed wings, and a single bright violet eye at the centre of its face. It does not land - it hovers at all times, rotating slowly on the spot when stationary. It inhabits the Shadow Caves' upper chambers where thin shafts of moonlight occasionally penetrate, and it chases these light beams the way other creatures chase warmth, circling them until they fade. Its ghost-nature means it passes through cave walls with no effort and often reappears on the other side mid-chirp, startling the creatures it was talking to.
stages.note: Vespling passes through solid rock with a faint pop that can be heard up to three metres away - experienced Shadow Cave spelunkers count the pops to track how many are nearby.

stages.name: Vespral
stages.bio: Vespral is a sleek dark purple bat with large leathery wings, long pointed ears, and wide glowing crimson eyes that catch no light source - they make their own. It flies through the Shadow Caves in absolute silence, wings producing no sound at all, which is physically impossible for its wing-loading - the guardians documented it as its ghost nature suppressing the sound of its own movement. It appears in places ahead of where it was last seen with no intermediate flight time observable.
stages.note: In seventeen timed observations, Vespral crossed a thirty-metre cave chamber in under one second - far beyond any biological flight speed.

stages.name: Vestigon
stages.bio: Vestigon is a vast dark creature with enormous black leathery wings, a heavy angular body trailing tendrils of shadow-smoke, and two blazing red eyes that cast reverse shadows - pools of deeper darkness where light should be. It rules the deepest chambers of the Shadow Caves where no natural light has ever penetrated and no map has ever been completed. The guardians recorded it as the thing that decides which memories the Shadow Caves keep and which ones dissolve - and it has been deciding for longer than the caves themselves have had a name.
stages.note: The pool of deeper darkness cast by Vestigon's eyes grows by one square centimetre per year - Shadow Cave keepers measure this annually with quiet reverence.

stages.name: Vexling
stages.bio: Vexling is a small jet-black ant with a rounded glossy body, two short antennae, and a single glowing violet eye at the centre of its head. Its six legs are disproportionately long for its body size and it moves with a quick, jerky energy - never in a straight line, always at a slight angle to its destination. It inhabits the edges of the Ghost Hollow where the shadows are thickest and the soil is cold. It has no nest of its own - it walks into the nearest occupied nest, eats one thing, and leaves. Every colony in the Hollow has a Vexling file in its threat records.
stages.note: Every ant colony in Ghost Hollow maintains a specific patrol route around the one entrance Vexling prefers - they've never managed to block it effectively.

stages.name: Vexant
stages.bio: Vexant is a powerful dark ant with a spiked elongated body, long jagged mandibles, and narrow violet eyes gleaming from beneath a heavily armoured head. Its thorax is broader and its legs carry it at speed, moving in the same oblique direction as Vexling but now with obvious purpose - it is hunting. It patrols the Ghost Hollow's mid-canopy level, gripping tree bark upside down as easily as right-side up, and drops on targets from above. The hollow's ghost-type residents give it notable distance despite being incorporeal, which suggests Vexant can affect things that have no physical form.
stages.note: Three Ghost Hollow apparition-type sightings have been interrupted by a Vexant arrival - in each case, the apparition did not reappear for days.

stages.name: Vexalord
stages.bio: Vexalord is a dramatic and terrible insect - a great black ant with wide dark wings spreading from its thorax, enormous curved mandibles, and a long blade-like abdomen trailing behind it. Its single violet eye is now large enough to see from some distance and it radiates a low pulse of dark energy that causes nearby shadow-patches to shift unnaturally. It rules the Ghost Hollow as a whole, not through any claim but through the simple fact that everything else moves aside when it passes. The guardians considered it one of the Hollow's oldest problems - and secretly one of its most reliable constants.
stages.note: Shadow-patches within five metres of a resting Vexalord shift in the same direction it is facing - even when no light source changes.

stages.name: Waspling
stages.bio: Waspling is a small, round wasp nymph with a yellow-and-black striped abdomen, big red compound eyes, and two tiny translucent wings that already hum faintly with static charge. Its stubby antennae twitch whenever a machine nearby switches on, and it drifts toward electrical panels in the Steel Fortress like a compass needle finding north. Apprentice engineers learned to watch for Buzzites nesting in open circuit boxes - a tiny shock to the fingers tells them one has arrived. It chittered busily as it explored every new path the guardians showed it.
stages.note: A Waspling can drain a fully charged lantern battery in under two minutes just by resting on it.

stages.name: Vespwing
stages.bio: Vespwing has grown into a sleek, menacing wasp with a vivid yellow-and-black striped thorax, two pairs of buzzing wings that crackle visibly with arcing electricity, and a curved stinger that glows orange at the tip. Its red eyes scan the Steel Fortress catwalks with sharp intelligence. It patrols circuits of the Fortress that no guard bothers to walk, shocking loose bolts back into their sockets and driving off rust-beetles with targeted zaps. Trainers say Vespwing never stings twice in the same spot.
stages.note: Each wing produces a slightly different frequency; the interfering buzz keeps smaller pests at bay for twenty paces in every direction.

stages.name: Apidrone
stages.bio: Apidrone commands the air above the Steel Fortress like a living stormcloud, its broad armored thorax banded in deep gold and black, four powerful wings trailing continuous arcs of electricity, and a reinforced stinger the size of a short sword. Twin orange compound eyes can track a moving target through dense industrial smoke. The Fortress's eldest engineers claim the first Apidrone arrived with the storm that fused the Fortress's original walls - that it and the steel were shaped by the same lightning bolt. Its roar shuts down unshielded machines within thirty paces.
stages.note: The continuous charge field Apidrone generates is strong enough to magnetize iron filings into perfect circular patterns on the workshop floor.

stages.name: Vexfang
stages.bio: Vexfang is a plump, round-bodied baby serpent with smooth lavender-purple scales, bright blue dorsal spines that sit like a tiny mohawk along its neck, and wide curious eyes. Its forked tongue flicks out constantly, tasting the damp cave air of the Shadow Caves for new scents. Despite its small size, the faint shimmer around its blue spines hints at something far more dangerous growing inside. Children who venture into the caves sometimes find Vexlings curled around luminous fungi, keeping warm in their glow.
stages.note: Vexfang's blue spines change shade depending on air humidity - pale in dry air, vivid cerulean near underground springs.

stages.name: Vexserpent
stages.bio: Vexserpent rears up in a tense cobra-coil, its now-sleek blue-dark body banded with faint luminous rings. Its hood has broadened, edged in glowing blue, and its eyes carry a cold calculating intelligence. Purple-tinged venom pools at the tips of its fangs during battle, and it waits with absolute stillness before a strike - trainers call it the most patient creature in the Shadow Caves. It is said the caves themselves hold their breath when Vexserpent lifts its hood.
stages.note: Vexserpent can remain coiled and motionless for up to three days while tracking a single target by scent alone.

stages.name: Vexmaw
stages.bio: Vexmaw fills the mouth of a cave tunnel with its massive dark-armored form. Its scales have deepened to near-black, edged with faint green-purple poison light, and vicious curved fangs frame a jaw wide enough to swallow a boulder whole. Thick coils crowd the cave floor, and every exhale carries a visible purple mist. Abalont's shadow is said to have first taken root in the Shadow Caves because Vexmaw's territory was so feared that no guardian dared enter - the darkness had no opposition. Even now its territory remains silent.
stages.note: The purple mist Vexmaw exhales persists in still cave air for up to six hours and causes other creatures to lose their sense of direction.

stages.name: Vexnip
stages.bio: Vexnip (scorpion line) is a small purple scorpion with a smooth rounded carapace, two tiny pincers, and a thin segmented tail that curves up eagerly over its back. Its legs carry it in quick nervous skitters across the muddy banks of the Poison Marsh. Still young enough to be mostly curious, it probes every mossy rock and hollow log with its pincers. The guardians who first mapped the Poison Marsh noted that Vexlings always nest near the brightest bioluminescent fungi - they are drawn to any light in the dark.
stages.note: Vexnip's tail stinger is not yet venomous - it mostly uses it to tap out a rhythm on hollow logs when content.

stages.name: Vexclaw
stages.bio: Vexclaw has grown into a formidable purple-black scorpion, its carapace now crackling with tendrils of dark energy that cling to its claws like smoke. Its pincers have thickened into crushing weapons and its stinger drips a faint purple venom with each slow sweep. Dark smoke pools around its feet in the Poison Marsh muck. It claims territory fiercely, digging dens under petrified marsh-trees, and only retreats when a stronger shadow falls across it.
stages.note: Vexclaw's dark-energy claws can grip so tightly they leave glowing purple claw-marks in hardwood that persist for weeks.

stages.name: Vexscourge
stages.bio: Vexscourge is an enormous, heavily armored black scorpion wreathed in roiling purple-dark shadow that spills off its carapace like living smoke. Its massive claws crackle with dark energy and its hooked stinger gleams with concentrated poison. Red eyes burn through the shadow-haze. The Poison Marsh grew quiet centuries ago when the first Vexscourge emerged from the deepest pools - local legends say it is part of Abalont's shadow given weight and venom, a guardian-turned-predator. Its territory is a no-go zone even for other apex marsh predators.
stages.note: The shadow-cloud around Vexscourge absorbs nearby light completely; at midnight it becomes nearly invisible even to creatures that see in the dark.

stages.name: Vexcaw
stages.bio: Vexcaw (raven line) is a tiny puff of black feathers with a single vivid purple eye that catches light like an amethyst. Its stubby wings and thread-like tentacle tail-feathers drag behind it as it hops through the Light Grove, strangely drawn to the brightest clearings despite its shadowy nature. It tilts its head at words as if memorizing them, storing everything it hears. The guardians of the Light Grove noticed these little dark birds nesting near the song-trees - opposites resting in the same branches.
stages.note: Vexcaw (raven) mimics the last word it hears before nightfall and whispers it back in the dark hours before dawn.

stages.name: Vexraven
stages.bio: Vexraven spreads broad, ragged black wings edged with deep purple shimmer, its long wispy tentacle-like tail-feathers trailing threads of shadow. Two intense purple eyes carry a sharp, knowing gaze. It nests in the oldest trees of the Light Grove, where the glow of the grove-light throws its shadow into strange shapes on the bark. Those shapes are not random - rangers say Vexraven draws maps in shadow, marking paths only it can follow. It can read mood the way others read weather, and unsettles those with guilty hearts.
stages.note: The shadow-shapes Vexraven casts on walls shift and change for up to ten minutes after it flies away, as if the shadows remember.

stages.name: Vexomancer
stages.bio: Vexomancer is a vast, magnificent raven-form wreathed in flowing shadow-tendrils that billow and twist like ink in water. Its wingspan fills the canopy clearing, and its body radiates dark and psychic energies that cause nearby lanterns to flicker and animals to fall silent. Three concentric rings of purple light orbit its chest. The Light Grove holds it in awe - the oldest texts say Vexomancer arrived the very day Abalont's shadow first touched the Grove's edge, and that its presence has slowed the darkness's spread. It speaks in voices it has collected over centuries.
stages.note: Vexomancer is said to know every voice raised in the Light Grove for the past three hundred years - and chooses only one to say aloud per decade.

stages.name: Vexmite
stages.bio: Vexmite (beetle line) is a squat, round-bodied grub in a smooth purple shell, with a squinting green face peeking from beneath the carapace and two small stubby legs. It has a perpetually sleepy look, blinking slowly at anything new. In the Shadow Caves it rolls down sloped passages to travel, bouncing cheerfully off walls. Despite its easygoing manner, it secretes a faint purple irritant from its shell joints that keeps larger creatures from picking it up. Early-era cave explorers called it the 'grumbling pebble.'
stages.note: Vexmite (beetle) can curl into a near-perfect sphere and roll more than thirty metres on a sloped cave floor without losing speed.

stages.name: Vexshell
stages.bio: Vexshell (beetle line) has shed its grub roundness into a proper upright beetle-form with a segmented purple carapace, six strong legs, and two large curved purple horns sweeping upward from its head like a rhinoceros beetle's crown. Compound purple eyes now scan the Shadow Caves with sharp alertness. The purple sheen on its shell is mildly toxic to the touch, discouraging any who try to handle it without respect. It is territorial about its stretch of cave wall and will charge sideways-on at intruders, leading with one horn.
stages.note: The twin horns of Vexshell can be heard grinding together when it is agitated - a sound that echoes strangely in cave tunnels and carries far further than expected.

stages.name: Vexarch
stages.bio: Vexarch sprawls wide and heavy, a cathedral of dark purple armored segments bristling with blunt spines across its entire dorsal surface. The smooth green undercarriage is now plated and its six thick legs leave deep prints in cave clay. Purple venom seeps from every joint seam, pooling in shallow pits it claims as its den. Explorers mapping the Shadow Caves found they could navigate by avoiding the pools - wherever they led, Vexarch waited at the center. It is both keystone predator and reluctant protector of the cave ecosystem, and nothing crosses its domain without its knowledge.
stages.note: Vexarch secretes enough venom passively over one week to fill a small clay jar - cave herbalists harvest the outer-ring drips (at great personal risk) for antidote research.

stages.name: Vindrelt
stages.bio: Vindrelt is a small, wide-eyed blue-grey leopard cub with dark rosette spots and a bright, hopeful expression that belies the heavy steel chain already looped around its neck like a collar. The chain drags along the ground as it trots, but Vindrelt doesn't seem to notice its weight. It is at home padding quietly through the Ghost Hollow's mist, pausing to sniff headstones and hollow logs. Visiting children sometimes see only the glowing eyes moving in fog before Vindrelt pops out to investigate them with a curious head-tilt.
stages.note: Vindrelt's chain never rusts, no matter how long it drags through damp hollow mud - the links stay mirror-bright.

stages.name: Vindraclaw
stages.bio: Vindraclaw moves low and purposeful through the Ghost Hollow, its deep blue-black body slung close to the ground on powerful legs. The leopard spots have darkened to near-invisible on its coat, and the chain around its neck has grown thick and studded, draped across its chest in overlapping loops. It leaves no sound when it walks - not even the chain clinks. Hollow-keepers say Vindraclaw patrols the border between the living grove and the deepest ghost-mist, allowing neither to spill too far into the other's ground.
stages.note: Vindraclaw can suppress the sound of its chain entirely at will; the only sign it is near is the faint scent of cold iron on the air.

stages.name: Vindramaw
stages.bio: Vindramaw crouches wide and massive, all dark muscle and overlapping steel-plate chains that now cover its shoulders and haunches like battle-armour. The Ghost Hollow's mist parts around it. Its eyes carry centuries of watch-keeping - burning with a cold violet focus that makes even the hollow's ghosts hesitate. It is guardian and judge of the Ghost Hollow both, and its presence is said to keep Abalont's wandering shadows from settling among the hollow's ancient trees. A Vindramaw that approves of a trainer's true heart will lay its chain-draped head in their hands.
stages.note: The steel chains Vindramaw wears are forged from the same ore as the Ghost Hollow's oldest boundary markers, cast when the guardians first sealed the hollow.

stages.name: Vinekit
stages.bio: Vinekit is a small, bright-eyed deer fawn with creamy-gold fur scattered with red-dot markings, a pair of short velvety antlers sprouting green twigs, and two fresh leaf-buds at its rump. Its slim legs are already swift - it races up and down the Gale Ridge's lower slopes, chasing the gusts that rush through the ravines. Wherever Vinekit stops to rest, new shoots push through the cracked stone beneath its hooves. Storm-rangers say the fawn is drawn to the highest points it can reach, always looking up.
stages.note: Vinekit leaves a trail of sprouted seedlings wherever it sleeps overnight; a new path of young trees can mark exactly where it rested.

stages.name: Vinepryx
stages.bio: It carries the memory of every storm the wind has ever driven across the Ridge.
stages.note: The berry clusters in Vinepryx's antlers ripen during storms and fall onto the rocky slopes, seeding new trees in otherwise barren ground.

stages.name: Vinepryxis
stages.bio: Vinepryxis is enormous and majestic, its vast branching antlers so heavy with leaves, vines, and blossoms that they resemble a canopy. Green foliage spills from its mane and flanks, and flowers bloom in its wake on bare stone. When it runs full-stride across the Gale Ridge, the wind it generates can knock a traveler off their feet. Ancient Ridge texts describe it as the reason any trees grow on the rocky summit at all - it arrived before the first storm season and planted the first roots with every step it took. Guardians call it the Ridge's living memory.
stages.note: Vinepryxis's gallop on the upper Ridge creates a wind strong enough to carry seeds from its antler-blossoms all the way to the valley floor far below.

stages.name: Cobralet
stages.bio: Cobralet is a plump round-faced young serpent with smooth purple scales and large, dotted eyes that already hold an unusual depth of focus. It coils contentedly on marsh-lily pads, watching pond-skaters with patient, unblinking intensity. It hasn't yet learned to intimidate but practices spreading a tiny hood that immediately collapses again from its own weight. Explorers who spend time near the Poison Marsh say that Serplets seem to stare into the middle distance as though reading something only they can see - the first sign of their growing psychic sensitivity.
stages.note: Cobralet's eyes track movement up to thirty seconds before it happens - it positions itself to watch a spot where a fly will land before the fly has left its previous perch.

stages.name: Vipyx
stages.bio: Vipyx rears up in a commanding cobra spread, its expanded purple hood edged with faint shimmering lines that ripple like heat-haze above marsh water. Purple-tinged vapor streams from its fanged mouth. Its psychic gaze is now strong enough to cause disorientation in anyone who meets it too long - creatures larger than itself avoid direct eye contact. It has claimed the deepest lily-pool channels of the Poison Marsh as its hunting ground, using psychic pulses to stun prey before it strikes. Guardians who studied it noted it seemed aware of them before they were aware of it.
stages.note: Vipyx's hood shimmer can be seen from sixty metres in fog - marsh travellers have learned to use it as an 'avoid this path' marker.

stages.name: Cobraeth
stages.bio: Cobraeth towers in a full hood-spread that blots out the marsh sky above it, its scales deepened to blue-purple and its hood bearing iridescent psychic markings that pulse like slow heartbeats. The venom it exhales as mist can cloud a traveler's thoughts completely. Its eyes have become luminous, and those who look into them report seeing their own memories replayed with perfect clarity. It is the Poison Marsh's oldest living psychic, and the marsh plants grow in spiral patterns around every place it has rested - as though the land itself tries to read its mind.
stages.note: The spiral growth patterns around Cobraeth's resting spots persist for decades after it has moved on, marked on every old map of the Poison Marsh.

stages.name: Virlet
stages.bio: Virlet is a small, coiled green serpent wound tight as a spring, its scales textured like woven vine-cord and its round yellow eyes wide with alert curiosity. Even at this young age, leaf-like frills edge its back and tiny yellow flower-buds dot its coils. It lives among the cooled lava-flow channels of the crater's rim where hardy grass and creepers push between rocks - a bold little creature threading through the volcanic debris. Virlet wraps itself around anything new it finds, investigating with its whole body rather than just its eyes.
stages.note: Virlet's coils are strong enough to crack a green-wood branch; it wraps saplings at night and releases them at dawn with a slight bow-shape pressed in.

stages.name: Viradon
stages.bio: Viradon twists its vine-armored body into elegant figure-of-eight loops, its scales now deeply knotted like intertwined rope-vines and decorated with leaf-fronds in full green. Its yellow eyes have sharpened with dragon intelligence, and it can uncoil with explosive speed when it chooses. It navigates the lava crater's vegetation-choked side channels with ease, using its body as both anchor and tool - bracing against one rock face to lever another aside. The crater's edge-scrub has grown thicker over the years wherever Viradon has nested, as if nurtured by its presence.
stages.note: Viradon uses its strongest coil-loop as a sling, launching smooth rocks with precision at distances of up to fifteen metres.

stages.name: Viranthus
stages.bio: Viranthus fills the crater floor with its vast interlocking coils, body thick as a storm-felled tree and wrapped so densely in overlapping vine-armor that it resembles a sleeping forest more than a creature. Its broad flat head rests above the loops, watching the crater rim with ancient patience. Green blossoms erupt from its scales each spring regardless of the volcanic heat below. The crater's oldest legend says Viranthus arrived when the lava first cooled and planted the first seeds - that every green thing in this region of the world grew from its body-heat and breath. Its roar shakes ash loose from the crater walls.
stages.note: Viranthus's scales are so intergrown with living vine that botanists cannot tell where the creature ends and the plant begins on its lower coils.

stages.name: Virasklet
stages.bio: Virasklet is a small, upright serpent with bright aquamarine-green scales and a row of vivid sky-blue dorsal spines that flash in the dim Shadow Caves light. Its large round eyes carry a bold, dauntless expression unusual in a creature so young. It sits up alert on its tail-coil, peering at anything that moves. Despite being a cave-dweller, it carries a brightness about it - trainers who found one describe feeling briefly warmed as if in sunlight. Its spines rattle when excited, a sound that rings clearly through the cave tunnels.
stages.note: Virasklet's blue dorsal spines produce a faint bioluminescent glow in total darkness - just enough to read by if you hold it still.

stages.name: Viraxen
stages.bio: Viraxen rears into a wide cobra-spread, its scales now deeper teal mottled with tan, and its open fanged jaw dripping purple-tinged psychic venom. Wisps of violet energy curl from the corners of its mouth. It has shed the brightness of its youth for focused menace, holding perfectly still before each strike. Shadow Cave spelunkers mark its territory by purple-stained rock faces where it has venom-misted a wide arc. Despite the threat it presents, it sleeps in the same hollow each night and knows every mark carved into the cave walls.
stages.note: Viraxen can hold its hood-spread pose for up to four hours without muscle fatigue, waiting for prey to make the first movement.

stages.name: Toxihydra
stages.bio: Toxihydra fills the widest chamber of the Shadow Caves, its scaled bulk thick and armored, its enormous hood spreading to block entire passages. Green-yellow venom clouds drift from its gaping fanged maw and purple-rot energy crackles along its flanks. It has grown beyond serpent into something almost geological - a living feature of the cave system that explorers route around on their maps. It keeps the deepest parts of the Shadow Caves impassable to Abalont's creeping dark, not because it opposes the shadow, but because it tolerates nothing in its territory. Nothing at all.
stages.note: The cave floor beneath Toxihydra's usual resting spot has been dissolved by venom drip into a shallow basin that now holds a permanent pool - cave explorers call it the Toxic Font.

stages.name: Virkling
stages.bio: Virkling is a plump, bright-eyed green leopard cub with vivid lime-and-grass green fur spotted in bold darker green rosettes. Two small curved ears sit wide on its head and its tail curls up in a cheerful hook. It bounds through the Dark Forest with enormous energy, pouncing on fallen leaves and investigating every mushroom ring it finds. Akilla's forest was its home before the shadow fell, and even now Virkling returns to the old guardian-paths, sniffing the moss for traces of the old protectors. It trusts slowly - but once it does, its loyalty is absolute.
stages.note: Virkling follows every new path in the Dark Forest twice - once to test it, once to memorize it - and never uses the same route twice in a row.

stages.name: Viridaunt
stages.bio: Viridaunt moves with quiet, self-assured grace through the Dark Forest, its emerald leopard coat now full and rich with rounded rosettes. It patrols the boundary between the safe inner forest and the shadow-tainted outer fringes, marking trees with claw-rakes at exactly child-head height as a warning to others. It keeps Akilla's old patrol routes alive through pure habit and memory. Children who pass through its territory and speak honestly find it falling into step beside them - a green guardian for the old paths.
stages.note: Viridaunt claws a fresh mark into a guardian-tree every morning at dawn; foresters who study these marks can predict its daily route with near-perfect accuracy.

stages.name: Virantheon
stages.bio: Virantheon stands upright on powerful haunches, broad-shouldered and commanding, its vivid green body bright even in the deepest Dark Forest shadow. Huge rosette-spots glow with forest energy and its heavy tail sweeps slow and deliberate. Where it walks, the shadow retreats. It carries the memory of every guardian word Akilla ever spoke in this forest, and repeats them in a low rumble at the roots of the oldest trees as though feeding them meaning. Children who earn its trust say it places a single large paw on their shoulder, transferring a warmth that lasts for days.
stages.note: The rosettes on Virantheon's coat rearrange slightly over decades - old illustrations show different patterns, and scholars track the changes like a living constellation map.

stages.name: Viroxal
stages.bio: Viroxal is a perfectly round green orb of a creature with a smooth body dotted with neat little green spines and wide friendly eyes that blink slowly from its center. Tiny thorn-nubs ring its equator like a crown. It rolls through the Bug Thicket's leaf litter with remarkable speed for its compact form, nudging against tree roots with soft bumps. Beetles and crawling insects treat it as a landmark - they navigate around it as they would a small rock, which Viroxal seems to enjoy enormously. It grows one new spine every full moon.
stages.note: Viroxal's round body is rigid enough to hold its shape under the weight of a fully grown thorn-beetle standing on top - it doesn't even dent.

stages.name: Viroxian
stages.bio: Viroxian has shed the smooth orb of youth into a fierce-looking cluster of green crystalline spines that radiate outward in all directions. A narrow face with sharp eyes peers from between the longest spines at the front. The Bug Thicket's beetles now give it wider berth - a spine-brush leaves a sting that lasts for hours. It wedges itself into trunk-forks and hollow log openings as territory markers, and anything that blunders through dislodges it into a spinning, spiny defensive roll. It is growing something - the spines nearest its core are beginning to hint at the larger dragon-form to come.
stages.note: Viroxian can control each spine independently; it raises them in precise sequential waves as a threat display - first-time watchers always count the pattern without meaning to.

stages.name: Viroxarch
stages.bio: Viroxarch sprawls low and vast, its entire surface a bristling landscape of massive green crystal-spines that dwarf any individual creature nearby. From above it resembles an island of thorns more than any living thing. Eyes that miss nothing sit deep among the front spines, tracking every insect and creature in its territory with unhurried precision. The Bug Thicket actually thrives under its coverage - the spines catch dew and channel it to the root-soil, and fallen outer spines enrich the ground with minerals. Trainers say it is the thicket's true gardener, not its predator.
stages.note: The outer spines of Viroxarch shed naturally each season; thicket-floor mushroom rings grow in perfect circles exactly where the shed spines landed.

stages.name: Virling
stages.bio: Virling is a small, fluffy cream-white lamb with a round wooly body, large luminous green eyes, and a few vine-tendrils already threading through its fleece like natural decoration. Small green leaves sprout from the top of its head where a fringe flops forward. It grazes the Light Grove's meadow clearings, trailing loose vine-ends that catch on blossoms as it walks. Its psychic sensitivity shows early: it wanders toward trees before the wind picks up, positioning itself in shelter before anyone else has noticed the weather change.
stages.note: Virling's vine-fleece grows in the same direction as the prevailing wind; grove rangers use a sleeping Virling as a compass without disturbing it.

stages.name: Viroak
stages.bio: Viroak has grown into a plump, sturdy sheep with a thick cream fleece swirled through with spiral vine-green patterns that seem to shift and drift if watched from the corner of the eye. Curved vine-horns have grown from its brow in smooth spirals. Its eyes have deepened to a vivid psychic green. It wanders the Light Grove in wide meditative circles, and grove-keepers say it is mapping every song-tree's emotional state - not just their health, but whether they remember being tended. Those that have been forgotten, Viroak lingers beside longest.
stages.note: The spiral patterns in Viroak's fleece subtly match the growth-rings of whatever tree it stood closest to in the past season.

stages.name: Viroakian
stages.bio: Viroakian is a great, heavy-fleeced ram whose spiraling vine-horns have grown vast and elaborate, curling outward and upward in complex double-helix sweeps thick with blossoms. Its fleece cascades to the grove floor in living curtains of vine and leaf, and its eyes carry a permanent distant focus - it is reading threads of thought that no one else can perceive. The Light Grove's oldest trees are known to bloom first in whatever clearing Viroakian has passed through most recently, as though its psychic presence waters them at the roots of their memory.
stages.note: Viroakian has been recorded producing a psychic resonance that causes nearby sleepers to dream about the places they walked that day, settling the memory overnight.

stages.name: Bristlekit
stages.bio: Bristlekit is a tiny brown kitten with huge round eyes, a small tuft of green leaf-sprout sitting neatly between its ears like a mohawk, and a fluffy tail that curls up behind it. It is the most common companion found at the entrance to the Light Grove, greeting every new visitor with an immediate head-butt to the shin. Despite its harmless appearance, Bristlekit's leaf-tuft senses vibrations through the ground, and it will have run to hide in a tree hollow a full minute before any large creature arrives. Guardians say it was the last creature to see Akilla's green light fade.
stages.note: Bristlekit's leaf-tuft doubles in size when it is happy; grove visitors have learned to look for large tufts to find safe clearings.

stages.name: Thornfur
stages.bio: Thornfur has shed its kitten softness into a lean, sharp-eyed feline whose entire pelt now bristles with needle-sharp green thorns in dense clusters. It moves with wary, low-to-the-ground grace through the Light Grove's bramble zones, body perfectly adapted to squeezing through thorn-walls that stop anything larger. Its eyes have sharpened to intense amber focus. Thornfur marks its territory by pressing its flanks against tree bark and leaving neat rows of thorn-impressions - a message that reads clearly to anything with sense: this path is claimed. It continues to visit the grove entrance to supervise new arrivals.
stages.note: Thornfur's thorn density is highest along its shoulders - a precise brush against that patch leaves an itching impression that lingers for three days.

stages.name: Viryx
stages.bio: Viryx is a magnificent, living-forest creature - its body encased in lush leafy foliage so dense it resembles a moving grove more than a feline. Broad leaf-plating covers its shoulders and haunches, and vine-tendrils trail from its mane as it walks. It stands with absolute confidence in the deepest Light Grove clearings, and every green thing nearby grows a little faster in its presence. The oldest grove-keeper accounts describe Viryx emerging from the trees to help trainers find lost paths - not with guidance but by simply walking the right direction and trusting them to follow.
stages.note: The clearing Viryx uses as its permanent resting spot has the densest canopy in the entire Light Grove - trees there have never shed a single leaf in autumn.

stages.name: Viperyx
stages.bio: Viperyx (poison line) is a small, cheerful-looking purple-lilac serpent with a single glowing white horn on its forehead that gives it the air of a tiny, serpentine unicorn. Wide eyes and a broad smiling face make it seem approachable - which is somewhat misleading, as its horn carries a weak numbing charge. It coils in the shallower channels of the Poison Marsh, occasionally rearing up to flash the horn at anything that interests it. New trainers consistently underestimate it. The guardians noted that its horn pulses faster when it hears unfamiliar names, as if trying to record them.
stages.note: Viperyx's horn-glow brightens when it encounters a word it hasn't heard before - marsh guides say the brightness is a reliable measure of how new an experience is.

stages.name: Noxyx
stages.bio: Noxyx rears high in a wide cobra-hood spread, its body now deep blue-purple with banded steel-blue ridges and short back-spines. The single horn has grown prominent and sharp, and a thin venom-mist wisps from its fangs. It holds the deepest lily-channel stretches of the Poison Marsh as territory, and any creature approaching its marker stones receives one warning rattle of back-spines before being driven off. Despite its fierce territory-keeping, Noxyx has been observed using its horn to carefully lift trapped insects from sticky marsh-plants and deposit them on safe lily pads - a quirk that marsh scholars find fascinating.
stages.note: Noxyx uses its horn to draw geometric patterns in the marsh mud each dawn; researchers haven't agreed on whether the patterns are territorial markings or something else entirely.

stages.name: Toxhydra
stages.bio: Toxhydra is massive, its deep blue-grey body coiled into ridged mountains of scale, and its broad hood edged in sharp ice-blue spines that make it look armored even at rest. The single horn has become a great swept ridge of crystalized venom. Poison mists roll continuously from its open jaw. It owns the deepest known chamber of the Poison Marsh, where no other creature dares rest. Ancient accounts describe Toxhydra as the reason the Poison Marsh was never fully claimed by Abalont - not because it opposes the shadow, but because it opposes all intrusion with identical ferocity. The shadow learned not to compete.
stages.note: Toxhydra's shed skin sections have been found up to two kilometres from its territory - researchers believe other creatures carry them as deterrents against predators.

stages.name: Vulpink
stages.bio: Vulpink is a small, vivid orange fox kit with a broad fluffy tail, oversized ears, and a tiny green gem set into its chest that glows faintly in desert shade. Green leaf-ruffles edge its neck like a little collar. Despite living in the amber desert, it is drawn to every scraggly desert shrub and dried herb-plant it can find, sniffing the desiccated leaves with intense interest and sometimes napping atop them. It carries warmth wherever it goes - the herbs it sleeps on smell faintly of cinnamon the morning after. Desert travelers look for the glowing chest-gem as a sign of water nearby.
stages.note: The gem in Vulpink's chest glows brightest above underground water; desert scouts follow young Vulpinks to find hidden oasis springs.

stages.name: Vixbran
stages.bio: Vixbran has grown sleek and quick, its orange-amber coat now decorated with vivid leaf-shaped markings along its flanks and leafy fronds sprouting from its tail tip and ears. The green chest-gem has brightened. It runs the amber desert's inter-dune troughs at full sprint at dawn and dusk, leaving trails of tiny green shoots in the sand behind its paws that blossom briefly before the heat takes them. The Amber Desert's old stories say that wherever Vixbran runs in a full circle, a ring of flowers blooms for exactly one day.
stages.note: Vixbran's pawprints leave soil-nutrient traces that accelerate seed germination - in tested samples, seeds from its trail sprout four times faster than those from untouched sand.

stages.name: Pyrocanth
stages.bio: Pyrocanth stands magnificent on a desert ridge, its body wrapped in living vines and blossoms that trail and glow in the amber sunset. Its tail fans into six broad leaf-fronds that catch the hot wind. The gem in its chest now blazes orange-green, and every step leaves a brief bloom of desert wildflowers that fade within seconds of its passing. In the Amber Desert's oldest legend, Pyrocanth arrived before the first drought and found a way to keep the desert flowering - not by ending the heat, but by carrying the seeds of everything beautiful in its coat and releasing them wherever the land was thirstiest.
stages.note: The scent trail Pyrocanth leaves while running is strong enough to attract migratory beetles that pollinate desert plants - ecologists credit it with maintaining the desert's sparse bloom cycle.

stages.name: Sparkail
stages.bio: Sparkail (eel line) is a small aquatic serpent with a smooth bright-blue body curled in a tight spiral, decorated with soft blue swirl-patterns that pulse faintly with electrical energy. It lives in the Steel Fortress's coolant channels and drainage conduits, tucked into spiral coils against the pipe walls where the current keeps it company. Its psychic sensitivity shows early: it tracks the emotional state of engineers above it through the metal floors, and workers learned that a Sparkail leaving its usual pipe section predicts an equipment fault within the hour.
stages.note: Sparkail's spiral coil orientation mirrors the current direction of whichever pipe it inhabits; reversing the pump flow causes it to spin in confused circles for several minutes.

stages.name: Coilwarp
stages.bio: Coilwarp has grown into a sleek, powerful eel-form with vivid blue-white scales banded in electric-blue circles. Continuous arcs of lightning play between the ridges on its back and its long body coils and uncoils with fluid speed. It has moved out of the coolant pipes into the main power-channel network of the Steel Fortress, traveling at speed through electrical conduits. Control panels briefly light up in random patterns when Coilwarp passes beneath them. Engineers who understand the Fortress's power-grid use Coilwarp's location - tracked by flickering panels - as a diagnostic tool.
stages.note: Coilwarp can travel through a powered electrical conduit at the same speed as the current itself - it has been timed crossing the Fortress's full length in under twelve seconds.

stages.name: Thundervortex
stages.bio: Thundervortex rears from the Fortress's primary power core in a storm of crackling lightning and psychic shimmer, its vast scaled body looped around the central generator like a living engine. Blue spines crown its elevated head and continuous lightning arcs between them. The Fortress's instruments run more smoothly when Thundervortex is near - its psychic field stabilizes the chaotic energy fluctuations that cause equipment failures. Legends in the Fortress say it arrived with the first lightning strike that powered the Fortress's original core, and that it has been the true engine of the building ever since.
stages.note: The psychic field Thundervortex maintains around the Fortress's core increases power output by a measured eighteen percent - Fortress engineers have formally documented this and stopped trying to remove it.

stages.name: Sparkmouse
stages.bio: Sparkmouse (mouse line) is a small, round-eared mammal with tan-brown fur, wide bright eyes, a round belly, and a tiny glowing blue orb floating beside its tail like a personal lantern it never seems to notice. It hops through the Steel Fortress's maintenance catwalks with enormous confidence for its size, investigating every bolt and joint. The blue orb occasionally zaps the metal surfaces near it, leaving faint scorch-marks that workers follow like a trail of evidence to find where Sparkmouse has been. It is impossible not to like - it has the absolute certainty of something that has never been told it shouldn't be wherever it currently is.
stages.note: The floating orb beside Sparkmouse's tail always hovers at the same relative distance regardless of how the creature moves - it has never been dislodged by any force yet attempted.

stages.name: Voltail
stages.bio: Voltail has grown into a stocky, upright draconic form with broad wings folded at its sides, tan-brown scales covering a wide chest, and a face set in permanent serious concentration. Its wings already carry electrical field markings in vivid blue and it stands on strong digitigrade legs. The playful chaos of Sparkmouse has organized into focused power - Voltail patrols assigned sections of the Steel Fortress with the dedication of a guard who takes its role seriously. Junior engineers hand-feed it copper wire, which it accumulates and delivers to forge-workers as apparent gifts.
stages.note: Voltail's wings, even folded, generate enough field to keep the immediate area's instruments running on backup power during a full primary outage.

stages.name: Thunderwing
stages.bio: Thunderwing is an imposing dragon with a heavily muscled frame, vast scaled wings that crackle with persistent lightning along their leading edges, and a broad heavy head set with fierce golden eyes. When it spreads its wings inside the Steel Fortress's main hall, the lights dim and then surge. It has stationed itself near the Fortress's outer gate and treats every creature that passes as personally its responsibility to evaluate - allies receive a short nod, strangers receive the full wing-spread and electric display. It is the Fortress's unofficial gatekeeper and takes no days off.
stages.note: Thunderwing's wing-spread can charge a fully depleted power core in under four minutes - Fortress engineers have documented this and built a failsafe protocol around it.

stages.name: Sparkling
stages.bio: Sparkling is a chubby, wide-faced draconic axolotl with vivid blue scales, small but sturdy limbs, and a yellow mane-crest that crackles with faint static between its spines. Its wide-set round eyes carry a cheerful, unbothered expression. It shuffles through the Steel Fortress's water-cooling channels and drainage troughs, pausing frequently to zap small floating debris with its mane-static and watch it spin. Fortress technicians adore it unconditionally despite its habit of shocking anyone who reaches for it without warning.
stages.note: Sparkling's mane-static recharges fully after a short swim in cold running water - it returns to the coolant channels after every zap like a creature who has found the perfect resource loop.

stages.name: Voltlotl
stages.bio: Voltlotl (axolotl line) has grown into a long-bodied draconic lizard with vivid blue scales, spined back-crest, and powerful four-legged stance. Its mane-crest has matured into full electric spines that arc between tips continuously. It moves fast along the Fortress's wall-rails and overhead struts, scaling them with suction-tipped claws, and has developed a sharp tactical intelligence - it has been observed redirecting power fault-currents away from sensitive equipment by placing itself as a bridge. Engineers credit it with preventing three major Fortress fires.
stages.note: Voltlotl (axolotl line) can climb any metal surface at full running speed - the ceiling included - and has been photographed sleeping upside-down from the Fortress's main archway.

stages.name: Stormlotl
stages.bio: Stormlotl stands at full height as a formidable blue-scaled dragon, four powerful limbs braced wide, electric spines forming a continuous crown along neck and back. Lightning arcs between every spine-tip in a permanent crown of electricity visible across the entire Fortress. Its gaze is sharp and calculating. It controls the Fortress's upper-tier power-routing with apparent intelligence - operators discovered that the most efficient power distribution patterns were not what they had programmed, but what Stormlotl had rerouted. They have since stopped reprogramming and let it run the grid.
stages.note: Stormlotl's spine-crown produces enough ambient charge to power the Fortress's secondary lighting system indefinitely without drawing from the primary grid.

stages.name: Sparrow
stages.bio: Sparrow is a plump blue-grey sparrow-chick with ruffled feathers, a sharp little beak, and a bright yellow lightning-bolt marking on each wing that already crackles with faint static. It perches on Storm Spire outcroppings and leans into the wind with eyes closed, reading it. Its flaps are still short and uncertain but carry a tiny electric buzz each beat. Other fledglings at the Spire keep distance, having been accidentally zapped during roosting. Sparrow doesn't seem to mind the solitude - it prefers the highest ledge it can reach, where the wind is strongest and most interesting.
stages.note: Sparrow's wing-zap at this stage is not strong enough to cause harm but is precisely strong enough to knock a small insect off course in flight - it uses this ability to redirect prey toward its beak.

stages.name: Voltaix
stages.bio: Voltaix is a striking mid-size raptor with purple-blue plumage, a fierce hooked beak, and vivid lightning-bolt markings across its spread wings. Each wingbeat crackles with electric discharge. It hunts the Storm Spire's high thermals, diving at extraordinary speed and releasing electric bursts at the apex of each stoop. Storm-watchers at the Spire track it by the crackling sound before they can see it - it moves faster than the eye expects. It has been observed redirecting lightning strikes away from the Spire's inhabited lower ledges, possibly protecting nesting sites, though researchers disagree on whether this is intentional.
stages.note: Voltaix's dive-speed exceeds the electric pulse it releases - it outruns its own attack by the time the bolt strikes.

stages.name: Thundertalon
stages.bio: Thundertalon commands the Storm Spire's upper atmosphere with vast wings that throw continuous lightning arcs across the cloud-face. Its deep blue-purple plumage is shot through with vivid electric-white markings that flash as it banks. The wingbeats alone drive gusts that rattle the Spire's upper towers. Ancient accounts say the first storm over the Storm Spire was not a weather event - it was Thundertalon's first flight, and the storm followed because the sky couldn't hold the energy it released. It circles the Spire's peak continuously, visible for hundreds of kilometres on a clear day.
stages.note: Thundertalon's full wingspan generates enough lift-wind to ground any small craft flying within two hundred metres of its flight path - the Spire's aerial routes were drawn around it.

stages.name: Voltipede
stages.bio: A thumbnail-sized armored isopod that rolls up like a steel bead when startled. Its overlapping grey plates gleam like polished rivets, and one bright blue eye glows from beneath the front ridge. Voltipede spends its nights threading through the roots of the Dark Forest, tapping each one with its blunt snout to feel the faint electric pulses the old wood carries. The guardians once called it the Forest's Telegraph, for it always seemed to know when something was coming.
stages.note: A Voltipede tapping its snout on roots three times in a row signals a change in the forest's electric pulse.

stages.name: Voltaxon
stages.bio: Voltaxon's shell has erupted into a ridge of sharp silver-white spines along its back, each one capable of holding a static charge for hours after a storm. It moves low and deliberate, pressing its plated belly to the ground and reading vibrations the way a scholar reads text. When threatened, it raises its spines and the air between them crackles with thin blue arcs. Deep in the Dark Forest it claims a patrol route measured in precise paces that it never deviates from.
stages.note: Voltaxon's spine ridge holds enough charge after a rainstorm to light a lantern for ten minutes.

stages.name: Voltaxxus
stages.bio: In the Dark Forest it is both guardian and gatekeeper - those it judges kindly may pass; those it does not feel the static raise every hair on their arms.
stages.note: The gaps between Voltaxxus's armored segments spark continuously - trainers learn to stand back at least two body-lengths.

stages.name: Volteel
stages.bio: A slender blue eel no longer than a child's forearm, Volteel bobs upright in warm shallows with two tiny bright antenna-horns quivering on its snout. Its long ribbon tail fans out like a sail to keep it steady in the tidal drift. In Coral Bay's reef gardens, young Volteel hatch in clusters beneath lightning-struck coral formations and immediately begin hunting the tiny sparks that crackle along broken reef edges - learning to call home by following the electric taste of the water.
stages.note: Volteel navigates entirely by electric taste - it flicks its horns like antennae to sample the charge in the current.

stages.name: Amphydra
stages.bio: Amphydra's scales have darkened to deep blue, and its antenna-horns have lengthened into crackling prongs that fork the water ahead of it. A bright electric aura pulses along the full length of its body, and its large round eyes have turned pitch-black, reading the electromagnetic field of every fish within twenty meters. It no longer hunts along the reef - it hunts by waiting at the reef's edge until prey swims into range, then releases a single short discharge.
stages.note: Amphydra's electric pulse is precisely calibrated - enough to stun a reef fish, never strong enough to shatter coral.

stages.name: Thunderwyrm
stages.bio: Thunderwyrm fills the deepest channels of Coral Bay with its presence - a colossal eel with a fanged dragon's jaw that gapes wide enough to swallow a dinghy whole. Lightning arcs and froths in a continuous wreath around its whole body, and the sea glows pale blue for a hundred meters in every direction when it passes. Ancient sailors charted Coral Bay's reefs by the light it cast, calling it the Wandering Beacon. It speaks in electric pulses that the reef creatures translate into warnings and welcomes.
stages.note: The bioluminescent ring around Coral Bay's deepest trench is not coral - it is the resting glow of a sleeping Thunderwyrm.

stages.name: Sparkemice
stages.bio: Sparkemice is a puff-round blue-white mouse whose fur carries a faint frost pattern that thickens on cold mornings. Its tiny round ears are almost too big for its head, and small blue musical-note sparks drift from its cheeks whenever it hums - which is often. In Frozen Peaks' tide pools it shelters under overhangs just above the waterline, attracted to the chill of sea spray and the static charge left behind by lightning-touched waves. It collects single sounds the way others collect pebbles: one at a time, treasured.
stages.note: Sparkemice hums a two-note tune when content; trainers say each note changes pitch with each new sound it learns.

stages.name: Volteek
stages.bio: Volteek has grown a spiky crown of pale blue fur along its neck and shoulders, and a single bold blue lightning-bolt marking runs from its ear to its flank. Its round shape has become lean and alert, and its eyes carry a sharpness that misses nothing. When it stamps a back foot on a hard surface, a ring of frost spreads outward and tiny sparks leap from the tips of its spiky fur. In Frozen Peaks, Volteek stakes out the highest tide-pool ledge and guards it fiercely, letting no other creature pass without a sound.
stages.note: Volteek's foot-stamp creates a frost ring exactly one body-length in radius - it stamps twice as a warning, three times to charge.

stages.name: Stormion
stages.bio: Stormion is a four-legged predator with the full heavy build of a storm-season wave - broad chest, thick legs, and a mane of crackling blue-white electric fur that stands out like a blizzard halo around its shoulders and neck. Ice crystals form on the ground wherever it walks, and the electric mane sheds sparks continuously with a sound like snapping glass. In Frozen Peaks it patrols the boundary between the warm shallows and the cold deep water, the one living landmark that separates the two - old enough to remember before the boundary was drawn.
stages.note: The temperature drops measurably three steps before Stormion arrives - its electric mane flash-freezes the moisture in the air.

stages.name: Voltidea
stages.bio: Voltidea bobs upright in the warm waters of Coral Bay, its soft body a gentle sky-blue with a luminous orb glowing on its belly like a captured bubble of sunlight. Its crown ridge is smooth and delicate, and its curling tail wraps around coral stems for balance as it drifts. The glowing belly orb brightens and dims in time with Voltidea's heartbeat, acting as a living lantern to attract the tiny plankton it feeds on. The seahorse children of the reef learn to follow its light when the current runs dark.
stages.note: Voltidea's belly orb dims when it is frightened and blazes when it recognizes a familiar voice.

stages.name: Voltimer
stages.bio: Voltimer has grown prominent spined fins along its neck and back that fan open during a threat display, sparking at their tips like a lit fuse. Its color has deepened to rich cobalt, and its belly crest now channels electricity in thin crackling lines that run up to its crown. It no longer drifts - it swims with direction, steering by the electric fields laid down by every other living thing in the Bay. When two Voltimerexchange recognition, they touch crown-to-crown and share a brief shared pulse.
stages.note: Voltimer can identify every creature in a hundred-meter radius by the unique electric signature of its heartbeat.

stages.name: Volthydra
stages.bio: Volthydra is a majestic blue seahorse grown to the size of a warhorse, its crown now a sweeping corona of electric-edged fins and its body armored in overlapping scales that chime against each other in the current. A pair of broad side-fins carry it through the water with unhurried grace, and the electric aura around its body illuminates the deep reef trenches for ten meters in every direction. Ancient Coral Bay lore says Volthydra is the Reef's Memory - it knows every coral formation by name and the name of every creature that ever sheltered there.
stages.note: When Volthydra sheds its outer scale layer once a decade, coral reefs within a mile experience a growth surge from the mineral shower.

stages.name: Sparkitt
stages.bio: Sparkitt is a golden kitten covered in large round amber spots, with round curious eyes and a tail held high and curling at the tip. Tiny yellow sparks fizz from its cheeks whenever it purrs, and a breeze seems to follow its every pounce, scattering leaves in cheerful spirals. In Storm Spire, Sparkitt kittens race between shafts of sunlight as though the light itself is a game to catch. They are drawn to sounds spoken clearly and loudly - to hear a new sound said with confidence makes a Sparkitt bounce on all four paws at once.
stages.note: A Sparkitt bouncing on all four paws simultaneously is celebrating - it just heard a sound it had been waiting all day for.

stages.name: Strikat
stages.bio: Strikat has shed its round kitten spots for sharp gold-and-black tiger stripes, and a crest of pointed golden spines now runs from the crown of its head down to its shoulders. It moves with a stalking crouch and a low, focused gaze that misses nothing in its territory. When it springs into motion the wind bunches around its spine-crest and channels into a gust that bends the light through the spire. Strikat is fiercely loyal once it has bonded - it will not let another creature approach its trainer without a proper introduction.
stages.note: Strikat's spine-crest acts as a wind vane - it always points in the direction danger is coming from before Strikat ever moves.

stages.name: Thunderfang
stages.bio: In Storm Spire the old teaching says: if you can stand still before Thunderfang and hold its gaze without flinching, it will lower its head and let you pass. Every child in the region knows the trick is simply not to run.
stages.note: The instruction for passing Thunderfang is carved into the oldest stone arch at Storm Spire's entrance - the carving has never worn smooth.

stages.name: Voltix
stages.bio: A bright blue fox kit with bold yellow lightning-bolt markings along its sides and a thick fluffy yellow tail, Voltix trots through Storm Spire's shadow-lanes with its head low and its eyes - two vivid amber sparks - scanning constantly. It crackles slightly when excited, small arcs of static popping between its ear-tips. The guardians who once watched over Storm Spire left a lantern for Voltix kits, because they always know the shortest path back to safety but are notoriously bad at waiting for anyone to follow.
stages.note: Voltix always takes the path that has the least shadow between two points - it dislikes being fully in the dark, even its own kind of dark.

stages.name: Voltwolf
stages.bio: Voltwolf's blue deepens at night until its body blends with the spires between trees, with only its glowing yellow lightning-bolt markings remaining visible as drifting yellow shapes. Its mane has thickened and fans out in a stiff ridge along its neck, each hair a separate conductor that channels nearby electrical charge inward. It runs in tight circles around a target before closing in - a spiraling tactic that leaves dazzling afterimage arcs hanging in the dark. In Storm Spire, it is the creature that tests whether a traveler is telling the truth.
stages.note: Voltwolf's circling leaves glowing yellow arcs in the air that persist for almost a minute - navigators in Storm Spire follow these light-trails home.

stages.name: Volthaaron
stages.bio: It is said that Volthaaron remembers every creature that has ever passed through Storm Spire, and it tests new arrivals by waiting to see whether they remember it.
stages.note: The gap between Volthaaron's mane-spines is the only place in Storm Spire where even starlight does not reach.

stages.name: Sparklet
stages.bio: Sparklet is the smallest light in Storm Spire - a snow-white mouse with enormous round ears and a single small blue lightning bolt floating near its face, trailing sparks like a firefly. Its fur is so clean and white it seems to shine in the dark tunnels, reflecting the crystal walls' glow back in every direction. Sparklet makes its home in a narrow crystal vein where the light bends at strange angles, and it knows by the color of each crystal face which tunnels lead to new sounds and which lead only to dead ends.
stages.note: Sparklet's blue lightning bolt changes color whenever it is in a tunnel where no creature has spoken a new sound yet - it glows gold instead.

stages.name: Thundermouse
stages.bio: Thundermouse wears its lightning bolts proudly now - two bright blue bolt-shaped markings across its chest - and its formerly soft fur has grown into a dense fluffy coat that crackles with static when it runs. Its round ears catch the faintest vibrations from deep within Storm Spire, reading the hum of trapped light inside crystal formations the way others read books. When it spots a crystal that holds the light of a sound it has not learned yet, it sits before it for hours, completely still, absorbing.
stages.note: Thundermouse can sit motionless for up to six hours before a glowing crystal - trainers have timed it, awed and slightly jealous.

stages.name: Staticorn
stages.bio: Its white body is thick-set and powerful, and its gaze carries the quiet authority of a creature that has seen every light Storm Spire has ever held. It is the spire's living map, and the Guardians say it knows where every hidden crystal lies.
stages.note: Every crystal in a hundred-meter radius gives a single pulse of light when Staticorn enters a new tunnel section for the first time.

stages.name: Sparksting
stages.bio: A bright golden scorpion small enough to fit in a cupped hand, Sparksting carries a stinger that glows vivid yellow at its tip and hums like a live wire. Its eight legs pick through the leaf litter of Bug Thicket with meticulous precision, and it taps each twig with a foreleg before stepping on it - checking for stability. In Bug Thicket's layered canopy floor, Sparksting is at the very base of the food chain and knows it, staying under leaves and low cover and only raising its glowing stinger when cornered and frightened.
stages.note: Sparksting taps every surface exactly twice before placing weight on it - trainers call this the Sparksting Double-Check.

stages.name: Voltscorp
stages.bio: Voltscorp has deepened to tawny brown with electric arcs sparking between its claw joints, and its tail has curved into a tighter coil at the tip where the charge concentrates. It holds its pincers wide and low, threatening but patient - it will wait an entire hour in perfect stillness for the right moment to strike. In Bug Thicket it claims territory by scorching a ring of thin electric traces into the bark of nearby trees. The other insects respect these borders absolutely.
stages.note: A ring of thin black scorch lines on tree bark at ground level means Voltscorp has claimed everything inside the ring as its territory.

stages.name: Thunderstinger
stages.bio: Thunderstinger is colossal by Bug Thicket's standards - its golden body radiates a continuous electric field that makes every other insect nearby orbit it at a respectful distance. Lightning arcs span the full length of its body from claw-tip to stinger continuously, like a living Jacob's ladder. Its stinger crackles with a condensed charge powerful enough to leave a six-meter circle of scorched earth when released. The ancient texts of Bug Thicket's keepers describe Thunderstinger as the Thicket's Enforcer: the last word spoken before silence falls.
stages.note: A Thunderstinger releasing a full charge stings only once - the recovering pause takes exactly twenty-four hours, and every bug in the Thicket goes quiet.

stages.name: Buzzling
stages.bio: Buzzling is a pudgy green caterpillar with a round friendly face and two tiny antennae that bend toward any sound - especially spoken words. It inches along the storm-struck branches of Storm Spire's lower reaches, leaving a faint trail of tiny electric footprints on bark. When it hears a word it does not know, it stops completely and rocks its whole body side to side, as though the word is a flavor it is tasting for the first time. Buzzling eats electric-charged leaves exclusively, and grows slightly brighter green with each meal.
stages.note: Buzzling's antennae point in the direction of the nearest electrical storm at all times - Storm Spire navigators use them as living compasses.

stages.name: Voltbug
stages.bio: Voltbug has grown thick yellow-and-green banded segments and nubby front legs that grip with surprising strength, and its antennae now crackle with continuous electric sparks. Its round eyes have sharpened into focused amber ovals that track movement precisely. It feeds openly now, climbing to the highest branches of Storm Spire during thunderstorms and absorbing the charge directly from the air. On calm days it is placid and slow; on storm days it is frenetic, racing from branch to branch with crackling speed.
stages.note: Voltbug doubles its movement speed for each additional lightning strike it absorbs during a single storm - on peak storm nights, it is nearly invisible.

stages.name: Stormswarm
stages.bio: Stormswarm emerges from its storm-charged cocoon with broad blue-grey wings that crackle at every vein-line with visible electricity - a living circuit board spread against the sky. Its wingspan casts a flickering shadow that strobes as the electric charge pulses through it, and when it beats its wings the air pressure creates tiny local thunderclaps. In Storm Spire it serves as weather reader and herald - its wing-beat rhythm matches the incoming storm's timing so precisely that the spire's keepers could set a clock by it.
stages.note: The wingbeat rhythm of a Stormswarm matches the exact interval between lightning strikes in any storm it has absorbed for longer than one hour.

stages.name: Sparkub
stages.bio: Sparkub is a round little blue fish that bobs through the dark waterways of Storm Spire with a single golden glowing orb floating above its head like a miniature lighthouse. A thin purple swirl drifts in its wake - barely poisonous at this stage, more like a gentle warning smell - and it blinks its wide eyes at every tunnel junction as if uncertain of its route. It feeds on tiny cave organisms that are themselves bioluminescent, and on full nights the entire cave pool where Sparkub sleeps glows faintly gold.
stages.note: The golden orb above Sparkub's head bobs up when it is curious and droops flat to its head when it is frightened.

stages.name: Voltubby
stages.bio: Voltubby has inflated considerably - its body now bristles with short sharp spines that each carry a small charge of electric-laced venom. Its coloring has shifted to deep purple-blue with a glowing aura of purple haze that hangs around it like a permanent cloud. It navigates Storm Spire' flooded passages by bouncing its electric pulse off the walls like sonar, mapping the tunnels as it moves. When startled, it inflates instantly to twice its resting size and every spine lights up with purple electric sparks.
stages.note: Voltubby can inflate to twice its size in under half a second - cave explorers listen for the sharp pop of its spine-lock as a warning.

stages.name: Thunderspike
stages.bio: Thunderspike is a sphere of dense shadow and crackling electricity - its body has grown into a permanently inflated ball covered in long radiating spines that each end in a bright charged tip. The dark spaces between its spines seem deeper than the cave walls around it, as if the shadow there is not ordinary. It moves through Storm Spire' deepest flooded chambers slowly and deliberately, for nothing else will approach it. The old cave-keepers say Thunderspike does not hunt - it simply waits, and the cave's currents bring everything it needs.
stages.note: The water within a meter of Thunderspike carries a mild electrical charge strong enough to make small fish lose coordination - it never has to chase.

stages.name: Sparkusk
stages.bio: Sparkusk is a dark-furred pup bristling with energy - its fur stands in spiky tufts all over, and bold yellow lightning bolt markings streak its sides and haunches. Its sharp eyes dart between shadows constantly, and it instinctively circles any new object three times before approaching it. In Storm Spire, Sparkusk pups can be found in small clusters at the boundaries between the Hollow's inner dark and the faint light of the surrounding forest, neither fully in nor fully out - curious about both, committed to neither.
stages.note: Sparkusk circles any new object exactly three times before deciding whether to approach or retreat - it has never been observed skipping this ritual.

stages.name: Thunderusk
stages.bio: Thunderusk has grown into a lean and powerful four-legged creature with vivid yellow lightning-bolt body markings that glow faintly even in daylight. Its dark fur has tightened against its frame, and its silhouette moving through the Storm Spire trees is more lightning-shape than animal-shape. It runs without sound until it chooses to - the spire goes perfectly silent for three beats before Thunderusk passes, and loud again three beats after. Old Storm Spire stories say that if you hear that silence, you are about to be tested on something you thought you had forgotten.
stages.note: Storm Spire goes silent for exactly three seconds before Thunderusk passes through any given point on its route.

stages.name: Voltexar
stages.bio: Voltexar's body is a map of lightning - bold yellow bolts cover its dark coat from muzzle to tail in patterns that shift slightly each time it sheds, as if the electricity itself is redrawing its own signature. It stands with a weight and stillness that makes the ground feel different beneath its paws. When it discharges a full bolt it disappears entirely in the flash and reappears three body-lengths ahead - a blink-step that Storm Spire explorers insist must be cheating. The guardians recorded it as the Hollow's Arbiter: the creature that decides who may leave.
stages.note: Voltexar's lightning-bolt markings shift slightly every six months as it sheds - each new pattern is different from any that came before.

stages.name: Boltpup
stages.bio: This Boltpup is grey-and-white with vivid blue eyes that seem to glow with their own cool light, and a single bright blue lightning bolt marking on its side. Its ears are large for its head and rotate toward every unfamiliar sound with clockwork precision. In Storm Spire it is calmer than its darker cousins, spending long stretches sitting very still in the fog, watching. The guardians noted that this Boltpup rarely startles - it has an instinct that tells it the difference between a threat and a test, and always waits to find out which it is.
stages.note: This Boltpup's blue eyes can be seen glowing in thick fog from twenty meters - Storm Spire travelers follow the lights when lost.

stages.name: Boltusk
stages.bio: In Storm Spire it moves along the boundary edge of the fog banks, neither entering fully nor leaving - a guardian of the threshold that takes the measure of everyone who crosses.
