stages.note: Boltusk's howl resonance lingers in the air for seven full seconds - creatures in Storm Spire use it to triangulate directions in zero visibility.

stages.name: Stormtusk
stages.bio: Ancient Storm Spire lore describes it as the Spire's Memory - it remembers every creature that ever entered, and what each of them was carrying when they did.
stages.note: The electric veins beneath Stormtusk's fur pulse once for every creature it has let through - researchers have counted more than ten thousand pulses.

stages.name: Sparkbug
stages.bio: This Sparkbug wears a dark rounded shell and stands out in Storm Spire by the single vivid blue crystal spike that rises from its head like a tiny beacon. The crystal glows faintly and pulses with each step it takes, as though counting. It rolls beetle-style through the dense undergrowth of Storm Spire, following the underground water channels by the faint electrical resonance they carry. Young ones are found near the spire's crystal-veined stones, tapping their crystal horn against the rock to hear it ring - a sound they seem to find deeply satisfying.
stages.note: Sparkbug taps its crystal horn against rocks to test their mineral content - it eats only the rocks that ring in a specific tone.

stages.name: Voltusker
stages.bio: Voltusker has grown into a formidable dark-blue rhinoceros beetle with a thick curved horn that now crackles with active electricity, and heavy plate armor across its back and shoulders. Lightning arcs between its horn and the ground with every few steps, scoring tiny black marks in the soil. When it lowers its head and charges, the horn focuses the electric discharge into a point - and nothing in Storm Spire's undergrowth stays in that line. It defends its stretch of the spire with absolute conviction, and the other bugs give it wide berth.
stages.note: Voltusker leaves a trail of regularly spaced lightning marks in the soil wherever it walks - Storm Spire trackers can identify it at a glance.

stages.name: Voltumoth
stages.bio: Voltumoth has gained broad luminous wings marked with golden lightning patterns on jet-black membranes - a transformation that stuns even those who watched the whole process. Its heavy armored body has become slightly lighter at the thorax to allow flight, but it still carries the full weight of a rhinoceros beetle in its plated limbs and fists. In Storm Spire it is the rarest sight: it flies only at night, and only when the lightning season peaks. Each wingbeat charges the air with the smell of thunderstorms, and the spire's crops grow measurably faster beneath its flight path.
stages.note: The soil in Storm Spire directly beneath Voltumoth's flight path is measurably richer in nitrogen for three days after it passes over.

stages.name: Sparkyx
stages.bio: Sparkyx appears as a hovering purple orb with a faint white eye at its center and two thin filament tendrils trailing beneath it like roots searching for soil. It drifts in the thermal updrafts of Storm Spire, apparently weightless, humming at a frequency just below hearing. The orb is warm to the touch - not from the spire heat but from the dragon-fire compressed at its core, held in check by a thin shell of electric charge. The guardians of Storm Spire called it the Seed - convinced that every Sparkyx contains a whole dragon waiting for the right word to release it.
stages.note: Sparkyx's central white eye never blinks - it tracks everything in 360 degrees simultaneously, rotating the pupil instead of the eye.

stages.name: Coilyx
stages.bio: Coilyx has broken the orb entirely and grown into a compact purple dragon-serpent with a proper head, small spread wings, and a long coiling tail. Its scales carry a metallic sheen of violet and its eyes are bright gold-ringed amber. Small electric sparks drift from its wing-tips whenever it glides. In Storm Spire it prefers the high ledges above the heat plumes, riding thermal columns with a laziness that belies its sharp attention below. It claims its ledge with a single spark from its maw - a mark no other creature disturbs.
stages.note: Coilyx marks its ledge with a single precise spark every dawn - the scorch mark never widens or fades, as if it resets every night.

stages.name: Thunderyx
stages.bio: Thunderyx is a full-grown dragon-serpent of Storm Spire's upper caldera, its massive body covered in overlapping violet-grey scales and its great wings fanning electric storm-clouds when it spreads them. Its wide fanned head-crest and multiple writhing tendrils give it the appearance of a deep-sea predator suspended in volcanic air. It breathes in electric-charged heat and exhales crackling plasma - a breath that is neither fire nor lightning but something between both. The Storm Spire's magma patterns have shifted to match the shape of Thunderyx's flight path over ten thousand years.
stages.note: The curved lava channels that geologists puzzle over in Storm Spire precisely trace Thunderyx's flight path from a thousand years ago.

stages.name: Voxnip
stages.bio: Voxnip's dark purple shell is dusted with tiny star-shaped pale specks, as if a piece of the night sky settled and hardened on its back. It moves sideways through the shallow pools of Poison Marsh with multiple slender legs, and its rounded eyes hold a dim bioluminescent glow that never quite goes out. It communicates not by sound but by brief psychic impressions - the feeling of a word rather than the sound of one. Trainers who spend time with Voxnip begin dreaming in unfamiliar words that they recognize as real when they wake.
stages.note: Trainers who bond with Voxnip report waking up knowing the way through channels they never walked - the crab passes on what it knows through sleep.

stages.name: Voxclaw
stages.bio: Voxclaw has grown pronounced crescent-moon-shaped claws that arc inward like brackets around empty air, and psychic mist curls from their tips in thin spirals. Its shell is wider and darker now, and the star-speck pattern has sharpened into distinct constellation shapes. It walks the waterline of Poison Marsh's deeper pools, and its claws can reach across the boundary between physical and psychic space - it will sometimes pluck a thought directly from the water's surface reflection. The marsh locals say Voxclaw can hear what you were about to say before you decide to say it.
stages.note: Voxclaw's crescent claws can grip objects that do not exist yet - researchers have photographed it holding shapes that formed minutes later.

stages.name: Voxmaelstrom
stages.bio: Voxmaelstrom is a nightmare architecture of claw, shell, and tendrils - its body has become almost entirely covered in radiating spikes and blade-like appendages, and the psychic mist that once curled from its claws now pours from it in torrents. Around it, reality softens: reflections appear in surfaces that are not mirrors, spoken words linger in the air as visible shapes for several seconds. In the deepest reaches of Poison Marsh, Voxmaelstrom keeps a perfectly still pool that no wind touches - there it reads the words that pass through the marsh in the thoughts of every creature that enters.
stages.note: Voices raised within a kilometer of Voxmaelstrom appear briefly as glowing shapes above the still pool it guards - the pool's surface is the marsh's memory.

stages.name: Orbpod
stages.bio: Orbpod is a translucent lavender jellyfish-orb with a single bright blue eye at its center and a handful of tiny trailing tentacles that drift like smoke. It floats through Shadow Caves' air pockets with total silence, navigating by the psychic impressions left on cave surfaces by creatures that passed long ago. When it finds a particularly rich impression - a word spoken with great emotion - it hovers in place and pulses slowly, absorbing. Its translucent body means you can see its single eye from any angle, watching everything without moving.
stages.note: Orbpod never moves faster than drifting speed - but it is never not exactly where it needs to be.

stages.name: Tentavox
stages.bio: Tentavox stands upright on four of its eight arms as legs, with the remaining four held forward and upward as sensory limbs that probe the air and walls of Shadow Caves continuously. Its purple body holds a faint bioluminescent glow, and its large single-eye stare carries an eerie intelligence that makes new visitors uncomfortable. It is in fact gentle - it is simply reading every feeling you carry from the psychic residue in your memories, sorting them by importance before you have finished saying hello. It lives in the lower cave passages where the psychic echo is strongest.
stages.note: Tentavox can sort everything a new person is carrying by emotional weight within thirty seconds of meeting them - it is rarely wrong about which one matters most.

stages.name: Voxelord
stages.bio: Voxelord is a vast purple-dark octopus that moves through Shadow Caves like a slow tide, its eight thick arms spread wide enough to touch both walls of most passages simultaneously. Its central eye is a pure black void that seems to absorb light rather than reflect it, and the psychic field it projects is strong enough to be felt as physical pressure in a room. It does not speak or signal - it simply holds the full history of every voice ever raised in Shadow Caves in its memory, and those who can bear its gaze may access any of them.
stages.note: The psychic pressure of Voxelord's presence can be felt as a subtle headache from a hundred meters away - researchers always know when it is approaching.

stages.name: Voxling
stages.bio: Voxling is a compact green serpent with alert amber eyes and vivid green scales that catch the mineral light of Dragon Spire. It moves in tight S-curves through the spire's lower ledge-cracks, testing every surface with the tip of its tongue before proceeding. A faint trace of toxin coats its scales - not enough to harm, just enough to discourage casual handling. In the ancient records of Dragon Spire's keepers, Voxling is described as the Spire's Reader: a young one placed in a library will have memorized every title on every shelf by morning.
stages.note: Voxling maps every room it enters in under two minutes - it has never been observed retreating through the same path twice.

stages.name: Voxern
stages.bio: Voxern rears up with confidence now, its muscled upper body rising to face-height and its wide-flaring tongue tasting the air with a speed too fast to follow. Its green scales have deepened toward emerald with a dragon's iridescence, and a crest of small dorsal ridges has appeared along its neck - the first hint of the full spire dragon it is becoming. It hunts the mid-levels of Dragon Spire by memory alone, having mapped every tunnel so thoroughly that it does not need its eyes in the dark.
stages.note: Voxern navigates Dragon Spire's entire tunnel network from memory without ever placing a wrong turn - it has memorized approximately 400 distinct route-choices.

stages.name: Hydrovox
stages.bio: Hydrovox is a massive coiled serpentine dragon, its broad heavy body thick as a tree trunk, covered in overlapping emerald-and-gold-edged scales and topped with a full crest of sharp spines from snout to tail-tip. Its enormous jaws drip with concentrated venom that pools in the carved channels at Dragon Spire's base - channels that the spire's ancient architects built specifically to contain it. It is not hostile by nature: Hydrovox tests knowledge. Those who approach with correct words pass; those who approach with wrong ones learn a different lesson.
stages.note: The carved stone channels at Dragon Spire's base exist solely to redirect Hydrovox's venom drip away from the memory-stone archive below it.

stages.name: Voxkin
stages.bio: Voxkin is a plump black raven chick with oversized purple-violet eyes that hold far too much awareness for something so young and round. Its wings are stubby and not yet flight-ready, but it compensates by hopping with great authority across any surface it occupies. In Light Grove it perches on the highest branch it can reach - not to see farther, but to hear farther - and it repeats back everything it hears in a perfect impression of the voice that spoke it. The grove children find this either delightful or deeply unsettling depending on which word was repeated.
stages.note: Voxkin can reproduce any voice it has heard once with perfect pitch accuracy - it never uses its own voice for ordinary speech.

stages.name: Voxraven
stages.bio: Voxraven has grown into a sleek and poised bird with glossy black-purple feathers that absorb light in a way that makes its edges hard to see against any background. It flies in perfect silence - its feathers are shaped to eliminate all wing noise - and it lands precisely and instantly. In Light Grove it serves as the grove's memory keeper: it collects spoken voices by flying over them, and the voices it has collected can sometimes be heard as whispers when Voxraven shakes its feathers. Each feather, say the grove elders, holds one word.
stages.note: When Voxraven shakes its feathers, words can be heard as whispers - the louder the whisper, the more recently the word was spoken in the grove.

stages.name: Voxithan
stages.bio: Voxithan is a towering raven whose wingspan casts a shadow that does not match the angle of the light. From its wings and back trail long dark tendrils - not feathers, but something between shadow and solid matter - that move independently and reach toward things without direction. When Voxithan spreads its full wingspan in Light Grove, every sound goes quiet for a moment, as if the grove is listening. The oldest accounts describe it as the Grove's Archivist: it holds every voice the grove has ever known in the space between its feathers, and releases them back into the world one at a time.
stages.note: The shadow Voxithan casts does not match its body shape - it always casts the shadow of the last word it decided to remember.

stages.name: Voxbat
stages.bio: Voxbat is a perfectly round-headed little bat-dragon whelp, ink-black from snout to wing-tip, with bright wide eyes that catch the lava glow of the crater and reflect it back as two orange points. Its leathery wings are proportionally huge for its body, folding around it like a cloak when it rests. It hangs from the cooler underside of lava-shelf overhangs in Lava Crater, sleeping by day and gliding through the heat plumes by night. It is attracted specifically to words spoken in the dark - as if the absence of light sharpens the sound for it.
stages.note: Voxbat hangs from exactly the same overhang each day to sleep - and each morning the overhang is a fraction warmer from its body heat.

stages.name: Voxwing
stages.bio: Voxwing has grown from round whelp into a proper dark dragon with a muscled body, a spiked back ridge, and green-veined wing membranes that glow faintly when spread. Its eyes have narrowed to slitted amber intelligence, and it now hunts the thermal currents of Lava Crater's mid-zone, riding them for hours with minimal effort. Its dark scales absorb heat and radiate it back as a faint shimmer, making it nearly invisible against the crater's orange glow. When it lands, it grips with all four clawed feet simultaneously - a sound like four locks clicking shut at once.
stages.note: Voxwing's four-footed landing is heard as four distinct clicks - crater explorers freeze when they hear it, knowing it has spotted them first.

stages.name: Voxdrake
stages.bio: Voxdrake is a fully realized dark dragon of Lava Crater - massive black-scaled body, vast wings with green-glowing veins that illuminate the underside of storm clouds, four powerful limbs ending in heavy claws that gouge the crater rim. When it breathes out, the air carries the taste of carbon and deep time. It does not fight for territory - it simply is the territory. The lava flows of Lava Crater follow channels carved by Voxdrake's passage over thousands of years, and the crater's ecology is calibrated entirely around where it chooses to rest.
stages.note: Every major lava channel in Lava Crater was cut by Voxdrake walking the same path repeatedly over the centuries - geology confirms deliberate routing.

stages.name: Voxil
stages.bio: Voxil is a cheerful purple cobra that rears up with a bright grin, its broad hood barely the size of a hand yet flared with evident pride. Its smooth scales carry a slight electric sheen, and it taps its tail against marsh-reeds to produce a faint crackling rhythm that other snakes in the Poison Marsh can read from meters away. It is bold for its size - it approaches strangers first and lets them leave only after it has checked their pockets.
stages.note: Voxil can send a short message through any network of connected marsh-reeds in under four seconds - scholars at the university call it the world's smallest telegraph.

stages.name: Toxvenom
stages.bio: Toxvenom rears taller now, hood wide and head haloed by wisps of purple toxic smoke. Its scales have darkened to deep indigo, and arcing sparks track along its spine when agitated. In the Poison Marsh it has memorized every shortcut in the reed-channels, and it uses the electric current it generates to illuminate the marks carved below the waterline - the ones that only it could ever find. It charges a full second before striking, as if giving fair warning.
stages.note: Toxvenom's pre-strike charge lights up submerged old carvings within three meters - archaeologists follow it at a safe distance during expeditions.

stages.name: Voxiathan
stages.bio: Voxiathan is a thunder-serpent of terrifying scale: its vast purple-black body coils through the deepest poison pools of the marsh, and continuous lightning arcs between the spines along its hood and torso. Its eyes blaze with stored electrical charge, and the marsh water around it glows faintly toxic-purple when it surfaces. The memory-stones at the very bottom of the Poison Marsh - the ones submerged before anyone arrived - vibrate to Voxiathan's electric field and speak themselves in ancient crackling voices.
stages.note: Voxiathan's full electrical discharge, measured once by an extremely unlucky researcher, was enough to power the nearest town for eleven days.

stages.name: Voxlet
stages.bio: Voxlet is a small round-faced purple bat with large round ears, simple leathery wings, and a nose that twitches constantly at air currents too faint for other creatures to detect. It navigates Ghost Hollow by wind-taste alone - it knows the direction of every draft in the hollow, and drafts that carry spoken words are its favorite, carrying a sweet resonance it follows like a scent trail. It hangs in clusters with other Voxlets, and the air between them is always slightly cooler, as if their presence draws warmth from the world and replaces it with quietness.
stages.note: A cluster of Voxlets sharing a roost makes the surrounding air measurably cooler - Ghost Hollow villagers use them as natural air conditioners.

stages.name: Voxian
stages.bio: Voxian has grown into a standing figure - upright on two clawed legs, with long elongated arms that end in wing membranes that fold and flare with expressive precision. Its purple-dark body is lean and angular, and its clawed wing-joints can grip surfaces that give it a disturbing stillness when perched on the side of a tree. It hunts by listening to the voices on the wind from great height, then diving without sound into the source of the voice it chose. In Ghost Hollow it is the voice-finder - it brings back echoes of words that were spoken too quietly to hear the first time.
stages.note: Voxian dives toward any voice it finds interesting - finding one perched behind you in Ghost Hollow means you just said a word it had not heard before.

stages.name: Voxalith
stages.bio: Voxalith is a massive dark dragon-bat hybrid with horns curving back from its broad head, enormous wings mapped with purple-gold vein patterns, and a body armored in overlapping dark scales. When it spreads its wings in Ghost Hollow the air displacement is equivalent to a gale - trees bend, leaves scatter, and any sound in the hollow is carried away instantly. It is the Hollow's wind itself, some say - not a creature that lives in the wind but the embodiment of it, carrying every voice that was ever raised in Ghost Hollow on those vast dark wings.
stages.note: When Voxalith spreads its wings fully, every sound in the surrounding kilometer is erased for three full seconds - the hollow goes absolutely silent.

stages.name: Vulkit
stages.bio: A tiny orange fox with enormous ears and a white-spotted coat, Vulkit trots through the Sand Dunes on dainty paws, its single fluffy tail always wagging. Two small flame-tipped wisps flicker from its ear tips when it hears a brave new voice. It was spotted dancing in the dune embers the night the first guardian was lost, and locals say it guards each buried bone like a precious secret.
stages.note: Vulkit taps its front paw three times before pouncing - a habit no one can explain.

stages.name: Vulcara
stages.bio: Grown sleek and lean, Vulcara bears a vivid green leafy ruff around its neck and three full-flame tails that stream behind it in the desert wind. Its orange coat deepens to ember-red at the shoulders, and sparks trail from every pawstep. It circles the hottest dunes at noon, memorising the memory-stones half-buried in the sand - the ones the dunes would swallow if no one kept watch.
stages.note: Vulcara's three tails burn at different heights, and sand-walkers read them like a fire-signal.

stages.name: Vulkarion
stages.bio: Vulkarion is no longer a fox but a great coiling fire-dragon: thick red-and-orange scales ripple down its serpent body, green flame-edged fins flare along its spine, and four powerful clawed legs grip the ground while blazing wings unfurl overhead. It circles the Sand Dunes at dusk, its roar shaking loose buried memory-stones, reading them aloud into the fire before the dunes reclaim them. Where the dragon breathes, unfamiliar names bloom in the ash.
stages.note: Every scale on Vulkarion holds a word of the old language - together they form the first complete story ever told.

stages.name: Embyx
stages.bio: Embyx stands upright on two strong hind legs, its charcoal-black body ringed with blazing orange heat patterns that glow brightest along its spine. Short, broad-based spines crown its head, and its stubby arms end in sharp amber claws. It hops between the thermal vents of the Amber Desert, soaking up heat with every breath. It stamps its feet when excited and leaves tiny scorch-prints in the sand.
stages.note: Embyx's heat markings pulse brighter each time it hears a word it already knows - like a proud little ember.

stages.name: Ignaur
stages.bio: Taller and armored now, Ignaur wears interlocking plates of black-and-orange scales across its broad torso, and a ridge of sharpened spines rises from head to thick tail. Its eyes glow a fierce amber, and it walks on two powerful legs, arms raised and ready. In the Amber Desert it circles the ancient fire-pillars - heat-cracked columns where the guardian Kael used to hold council by firelight - and drives off anything that disrespects the heat.
stages.note: Ignaur's spine-ridge vibrates at a low rumble when lava flows nearby, long before any instrument can detect it.

stages.name: Vulkyx Inferno
stages.bio: Vulkyx Inferno is a towering winged dragon: vast leathery black wings edged in orange fire fan from its shoulders, a ridge of blade-like spines runs from skull to tail-tip, and its entire body blazes in a pattern of smoldering ember-orange on deep volcanic black. Its four legs are thick as desert pillars, and when it opens its jaws, a torrent of white-hot breath pours out. The Amber Desert ignites with color in its wake - the sands turn glass where it treads.
stages.note: The glass beads left by Vulkyx Inferno's footsteps are collected and strung as protective charms by desert children.

stages.name: Vylkit
stages.bio: Vylkit is an adorable spotted ocelot cub, its cream-and-teal coat dotted with ocean-blue spots, and small blue fin-spines trailing from its ears and shoulders. It pads along Coral Bay's shallows on soft paws, stopping to peer at its own reflection in tide pools with evident fascination. It learned early that staring long enough at still water eventually reveals a face in the ripples - a trick it teaches to any child who sits quietly beside it long enough.
stages.note: Vylkit leaves a faint blue pawprint in the sand that glows for twenty minutes after sunset - bay children follow the prints to find where it has been.

stages.name: Vyleon
stages.bio: Vyleon has grown lean and powerful, its ocelot body painted in flowing blue-black wave-stripe patterns that crackle with built electric charge along the flanks. Fin-crests rise from its spine, and its tail whips with enough static to stun small fish at range. It patrols the bright corals of Coral Bay with the focused intensity of a creature that knows exactly what it is protecting. Visitors feel its presence in the slight tingle of the water before they see it - a fair warning it chooses to give.
stages.note: Vyleon recharges completely during a thirty-second dive - it surfaces glowing brighter every time.

stages.name: Vyltornado
stages.bio: Vyltornado is a magnificent water-lion, its mane a spinning vortex of whipped ocean spray and blue lightning, a twisting tornado-funnel rising from its shoulders as it moves. Its spotted coat has deepened to storm-dark blue-grey, and every step charges the coral beneath with enough electricity to light the whole bay rim. It remembers the day Abalont came to Coral Bay, and it will not be caught off guard again - its funnel-mane spins fastest when it detects a word spoken in ignorance where precision is needed.
stages.note: The radius of Vyltornado's funnel-mane predicts incoming storm intensity to a margin of error of four percent - the harbor authority runs no other system.

stages.name: Vylite
stages.bio: Barely taller than a fist, Vylite is a small purple slime puddle with two stubby arms and a pair of wide, slightly dazed eyes peering upward. A fringe of dark slime drapes around its base like a little skirt, and it leaves a faint violet trail on the cave floor. In the Shadow Caves it clusters with others near glowing fungi, absorbing the faint purple glow into its body until it shimmers. It hisses softly at anyone who shines a light too close.
stages.note: Vylite can flatten itself paper-thin under a rock, then silently reform on the other side - it treats the trick as a greeting.

stages.name: Vyloxus
stages.bio: Growing bolder in the dark, Vyloxus now sprouts four waving tentacles from its central mass - three small stalked eyes blink from its slick purple body, each looking in a different direction. Its underside ripples forward in slow waves and dark drips spiral from every tendril. In the Shadow Caves it stretches across narrow passages, testing the nerve of anyone who speaks to it; a flinch earns a toxic pat, but a brave answer earns a reluctant retreat deeper into the shadows.
stages.note: Vyloxus uses one tentacle to eat, one to sense light, one to splash, and the third for tapping - researchers still argue what the fourth is for.

stages.name: Vyloxidon
stages.bio: Vyloxidon is a dense, heaving mound of interlocked purple-black tentacles, so thick and numerous they seem to breathe with a mind of their own. No visible eyes remain - instead the whole mass pulses with a sickly inner glow whenever something worth hunting comes near. At the heart of the Shadow Caves it is said to sit in the deepest chamber, slowly weaving the lost words of the fallen guardian into its body as a dark archive none can read without its permission.
stages.note: The oldest tentacles on Vyloxidon carry inscriptions that match symbols found on the cave walls - no one knows which came first.

stages.name: Vylmite
stages.bio: A round purple orb of a body with a single large spiral-patterned eye, Vylmite skitters through the Dark Forest floor on four stubby legs. Its shell gleams like polished amethyst, and the spiral in its eye seems to slowly rotate - a trick that makes predators hesitate just long enough. It hides under dark leaves by day and taps a rhythmic signal to its siblings after sundown, counting the words it heard before the forest went quiet.
stages.note: Vylmite's spiral eye rotates once clockwise and once counter for every creature that passes - locals use it as a living tally.

stages.name: Vyloxid
stages.bio: Vyloxid has grown a hard purple carapace decorated with neat rows of dark bumps, and two sharp curved pincers jut from its head. Its green compound eyes glow coldly in the forest dark. Six strong legs grip bark and stone equally well, and it moves with startling speed when cornered. In the Dark Forest it patrols the oldest trees, pressing its pincers into the bark to taste which words were spoken there before the guardian fell silent.
stages.note: Vyloxid can detect which words have been spoken near a tree by pressing its pincers to the roots - it has never been observed getting it wrong.

stages.name: Vyloxarch
stages.bio: Vast and low-slung, Vyloxarch is armored in overlapping purple-black plates that slope like a fortress roof, ringed with sharp thorn-nodes along every edge. Its green eyes shine like lanterns in the deepest dark, and its six legs are thick as tree roots. It no longer hurries - everything eventually comes to Vyloxarch. In the Dark Forest it is the final guardian of the oldest sigils scratched into the stone before Abalont's shadow reached the trees, and it will not let them be erased.
stages.note: The thorn-nodes along Vyloxarch's back each correspond to a mark in the ancient sigil-craft - scholars have been copying them for years.

stages.name: Vynling
stages.bio: Round and green with a stubby tail, Vynling looks more like a cheerful little salamander than a serpent. Its body is a rich leaf-green with bright teal spots, and a glowing purple orb sits at its belly like a swallowed moon. It tumbles through the Bug Thicket's damp undergrowth with clumsy enthusiasm, pausing to press its belly-orb against strange leaves to taste whether they carry useful words. When curious, it freezes completely still and stares.
stages.note: Vynling swallows a tiny glowing spore every day - the spore feeds the belly-orb until the serpent grows large enough to glow on its own.

stages.name: Vynula
stages.bio: Now a proper cobra, Vynula rears up with a wide purple-blue hood flared and two long fangs glistening with iridescent venom. Its blue-teal scales catch the Bug Thicket's filtered light, and its forked tongue tastes the air for any word mispronounced nearby. It does not strike without warning - it sways, hood spread, and waits to see if the intruder is brave enough to hold its gaze and speak clearly before retreating into the roots.
stages.note: A flared Vynula hood shows a faint eye-pattern on the underside - researchers believe it mirrors the psychic link it is trying to open.

stages.name: Vynarch
stages.bio: Vynarch is a coiling sea-dragon of the thicket, its blue-purple body thick and sinuous with a jagged dorsal crest and enormous spined frills fanning at the neck. It undulates in slow loops among the tallest bug-thicket trees, psychic energy crackling from its frills in a pale shimmer. Any creature it locks eyes with feels its entire memory of words reviewed in an instant - a terrifying lesson and a gift at once. It is the thicket's living memory.
stages.note: Vynarch reportedly recited every voice raised in the Bug Thicket during the last century without pausing - it took three days.

stages.name: Vyrule
stages.bio: Vyrule is a compact green snake coiled neatly on itself, its scales a bright leaf-green with a vivid teal eye that glows softly. A glowing green orb sits at the center of its coil like a living seed it is keeping warm. In the cool nights of the Sand Dunes it coils tighter to conserve heat, humming a faint vibration that plants can feel underground. It was here, half-buried in sand, when the first guardian words were spoken.
stages.note: Vyrule's center orb heats up exactly at sunrise every morning - Sand Dune merchants use them as natural alarm clocks.

stages.name: Vyrath
stages.bio: Vyrath rears tall, its green body now decorated with delicate pink flower-blossoms growing directly from its scales - three clusters along its neck and two at the tail. It sways in the warm desert wind like a living vine, and tiny embers drift from its blossoms when it exhales. In the Sand Dunes it is drawn to the rare desert flowers that bloom only once a year, coiling around them all night to keep them from the frost, reading the marks carved in the petals by long-gone hands.
stages.note: The blossoms on Vyrath's neck bloom and drop in exactly seven days - marking a full week of unfamiliar names learned.

stages.name: Vyraxis
stages.bio: This Vyraxis is a great green-scaled dragon-serpent: its long body carries a mane of wind-swept jade scales along the crest, and electric-green lightning crackles between its spines. It moves through the air above the Sand Dunes in wide serpentine loops, its head crowned with a frill of razor leaves. At dawn it calls down from the sky, and the desert responds - every buried seed within earshot pushes one centimeter toward the surface, as if the dunes themselves are trying to answer.
stages.note: Vyraxis's lightning never strikes the earth - it arcs between its own spines in an endless loop, powering its flight without fuel.

stages.name: Vyrlet
stages.bio: Vyrlet is a small, rubbery purple worm that wriggles through the Lava Crater's cooling ash channels, its round head and single large eye giving it an almost cheerful look despite the toxic fumes. Its simple tube body ripples in neat S-curves, and a faint purple sheen marks its skin as mildly venomous even at this tiny stage. Crater researchers leave it alone - it curls up around warm lava-cracks to sleep and always wakes up more talkative than before.
stages.note: Vyrlet uses the same wriggling pattern to greet friends as it does to signal danger - context, it seems, is everything.

stages.name: Vyraxon
stages.bio: Now a proper sea-serpent, Vyraxon's purple body has lengthened and a bright gold-tipped dorsal crest rises from its spine. Its single large eye gleams amber with intelligence, and its tail curls into a tight question-mark as it surveys the Lava Crater's smoke-vents. It can breathe in toxic sulfur and exhale it as a directed cloud - a skill it uses to deter rather than harm, preferring to watch from a safe coil as others learn from the experience.
stages.note: Vyraxon's crest glows brighter at the approach of rain - Lava Crater settlers use it as a thirty-minute weather warning.

stages.name: Vyraxeth
stages.bio: Vyraxeth is a spectacular dragon: a long thick body of deep purple scales fans into a magnificent crest of gold-and-purple spines along the entire dorsal ridge, and elaborate ruffled fins trail behind its head like royal pennants. Its eyes are gold-bright, and its tail swings with the easy confidence of a creature that has never needed to hurry. In the Lava Crater it is the final warden of the deepest forge - the place where the guardian's last lesson was burned into the stone before Abalont's shadow reached the rim.
stages.note: Vyraxeth's spine-fins carry a different poison in each segment - scholars have catalogued eleven distinct toxins, each matching a forgotten lesson.

stages.name: Swaddle
stages.bio: Swaddle is a round bundle of dirty-white wrappings with two bright eyes peering out from the center and a red sash cinched around its middle like a tiny belt. Short leaf-like arms poke from the bandages, and it skitters on hidden legs through the Poison Marsh's reeds. It collects small marsh-bugs inside its wrappings for safekeeping - the bugs tickle, causing the random wriggling that makes it look possessed when it is merely delighted.
stages.note: Each strip of bandage on Swaddle has a tiny word written on the inside - no one knows who wrote them or how they got there.

stages.name: Wrapent
stages.bio: Wrapent has burst free of its tightest bindings and now sports eight writhing tentacle-arms that trail bandage-strips behind them. A single enormous amber eye stares from its wrapped torso, and it carries a small scroll clutched in one tentacle as if taking notes. It patrols the foggy channels of the Poison Marsh, reading the words inscribed on submerged memory-stones and copying them onto its wrappings - afraid that one day the marsh will absorb them forever.
stages.note: The scroll Wrapent clutches can never be unrolled by anyone but Wrapent itself - researchers have tried and the parchment always tears.

stages.name: Mummolith
stages.bio: Mummolith is an imposing column of stacked, locked bandaging from which eight massive tentacle-arms radiate like a crown. Its torso is armored in riveted brass plates bolted over the wrappings, and it holds a massive sealed tome in two of its tentacles - a book that has been filling itself for centuries. A single glowing eye surveys the Poison Marsh from its great height. All lost words of the guardian swallowed by the marsh eventually surface in Mummolith's tome, and it refuses to give them up lightly.
stages.note: Mummolith's tome gains a new page every time a child in the Poison Marsh remembers something they had lost - the book is currently twelve thousand pages long.

stages.name: Frostape
stages.bio: Frostape is a small sky-blue gorilla cub that walks on all fours with curious knuckling steps, its white-fluffed face full of mischief. Soft powder-blue fur covers its round body, and it can hold a perfect handful of snow in each fist for up to an hour before it melts - it uses this trick to chill warm creatures into friendliness. High on the Frozen Peaks it wanders among glaciers, playing games with frozen memory-stones it finds half-buried in the ice.
stages.note: Frostape hides a single pebble under each glacier it visits - it has never revisited the same glacier twice, yet somehow always finds the pebble again.

stages.name: Glacimane
stages.bio: Glacimane stands tall now, a broad-shouldered silverback gorilla whose white fur has grown thick and shaggy as a glacier wall. Ice crystals cling along its mane and knuckles, and its eyes are sharp, pale blue. It beats its chest once - just once - before moving, and the sound carries across the frozen heights like a question. On the Frozen Peaks it tests every traveller: hold your ground and it turns aside; flinch, and it steps closer, patient as the cold.
stages.note: Glacimane presses a single frost-flower into every glacier face it passes - nobody has worked out where a gorilla at altitude finds anything to press.

stages.name: Avalord
stages.bio: Avalord is an ancient glacier-gorilla: its roaring white frame is enormous, ice spines erupting from its shoulders and crown, and its eyes burn with cold wisdom accumulated over centuries. It stands upright, mouth wide open in a bellow that shakes loose small avalanches on distant peaks. Behind that fearsome roar is the warm heart of a guardian - it plays games to see who is brave enough to stay, testing only those it secretly hopes will pass. Each glacier hides a memory of a lost guardian, and Avalord tends them all.
stages.note: When Avalord lets out a full bellow, glaciologists have recorded micro-tremors forty kilometers away - they call it the Avalord signature.

stages.name: Zephchick
stages.bio: Zephchick is a dainty pale-blue dove with soft round wings and a golden halo hovering above its head - not a decoration but a real electric corona that sparks when it hears thunder. It perches on the highest Storm Spire outcroppings, eyes wide, tracking every lightning bolt to map the paths it wants to fly someday. It chirps a quick two-note call before each flight as if asking permission from the sky, and waits for the answering rumble before it dares to lift off.
stages.note: Zephchick's halo pulses once per second in calm weather but triples in speed just before a storm - eleven minutes before the first lightning strike.

stages.name: Zephawk
stages.bio: Zephawk is now a fierce silver-and-white eagle, chest thrust forward, wings spread wide and crackling with blue lightning arcs along each primary feather. Its talons grip the highest Storm Spire crags, and yellow eyes survey the gale with a warrior's attention. It dives at storm-speeds - reaching terminal velocity in four wing-beats - and the lightning it trails marks temporary bright paths through the cloud that other creatures follow for hours after it has gone.
stages.note: The lightning trails Zephawk leaves during a dive form a different ancient sigil every time - no trail has ever repeated.

stages.name: Zephyrian
stages.bio: Zephyrian is a magnificent thunder-eagle: its great white-and-blue body crackles with electric coronae along every wing edge, and its ice-blue eyes carry the calm authority of a creature that has weathered every storm the Spire has produced. It spreads its wings and the air itself charges - hair stands up, lightning finds new paths, and every creature nearby suddenly remembers a word they thought they had forgotten. At the Storm Spire summit it is both sentinel and teacher.
stages.note: Zephyrian has circled the Storm Spire without landing for recorded periods of up to forty-three days - researchers call it the Eternal Loop.

stages.name: Zephkit
stages.bio: Zephkit is a small, fluffy sky-blue husky pup with a spiral swirl pattern on its flank and bright pale eyes full of cheerful recklessness. Its tail curls up and wags constantly, and small static sparks fly off its fur when it shakes dry. At the base of the Storm Spire it races the lower wind-gusts, falling over its own paws, then immediately racing again. When it howls, the sound carries much farther than a pup its size should produce - a fact that delights it.
stages.note: Zephkit howls in a specific direction before every storm, and that direction has never pointed the wrong way in recorded history.

stages.name: Zephound
stages.bio: Zephound is a lean electric wolf, its white-blue coat charged with crackling blue energy, a single spiraled horn rising from its brow that catches and focuses wind into a directed beam. Its howl at full stride has been clocked at three times the audible range for its size, and it leaves a faint ozone trail that lingers for twenty minutes. It races the lightning around the Storm Spire, tracking the paths Jack once walked, howling the guardian's name into every gale it passes through.
stages.note: Zephound's horn acts as a lightning rod exactly once per storm - at the precise moment the storm peaks - and it always survives.

stages.name: Tempestyx
stages.bio: Tempestyx is a glacier-wolf of immense presence: thick icy-blue fur erupts in a mane of frozen crystal spines around its shoulders and haunches, and the air within five meters crackles and swirls in a permanent micro-storm of its making. It howls at the very summit of the Storm Spire where Jack was taken into the gale, and the thunder answers - not as coincidence but as confirmation. Every climber who reaches the top and speaks the right word finds Tempestyx waiting, ready to carry them through the deepest cloud.
stages.note: The eye of every Storm Spire tempest is always positioned directly above wherever Tempestyx is standing - meteorologists have checked eighteen storms.

stages.name: Zephyling
stages.bio: Zephyling is a small white foal with a tousled blue mane and two small feathered wings still too young for real flight - they flutter and carry it a few inches off the ground when it gets excited, no more. Its large eyes are the blue of a clear sky at noon, and it nibbles at light-flowers in the Psychic Temple, each one tasting of a sound it is just beginning to understand. When startled it vanishes behind a puff of psychic shimmer, reappearing three steps away looking surprised by its own trick.
stages.note: Zephyling's wings beat exactly 440 times per minute in calm air - the same frequency as a tuned note - and temple musicians have noticed.

stages.name: Zephyrion
stages.bio: Zephyrion is a graceful white stallion whose broad wings carry it confidently across the Psychic Temple's canopy. Its blue mane streams in a permanent wind of its own making, and a soft psychic glow halos its horn-less brow. It reaches speeds that blur its outline, leaving after-images - children who see it report the ghost of a second Zephyrion running alongside the real one for a moment before fading. It is drawn to places where sounds of courage were once spoken aloud.
stages.note: Zephyrion's after-image always shows the child the thing they most need to see next - no one has explained how the horse knows.

stages.name: Celestiox
stages.bio: Its mane flows in a radiant cascade, and the air around it glimmers with psychic light so pure it feels like stepping into a moment that has gone right for the first time. In the Psychic Temple it visits before each dawn, leaving courage in the soil so that children who walk barefoot there take some of it with them without knowing.
stages.note: The wingbeats of Celestiox are heard three seconds before it arrives - sound, it appears, travels faster in its wake than before it.

stages.name: Zephlet
stages.bio: Zephlet is a round, fluffy ice-blue bird that bounces when it lands rather than walking like a sensible creature. Its tiny wings are oversized for its body and flap furiously to keep it hovering a finger's width off the ground. Two bright eyes peer from a puffy face, and the feathers around its head puff into a crest when wind blows from the sea. On the Frozen Peaks it follows the coastal thermals for hours, practicing each new sound it has learned in tiny half-heard chirps.
stages.note: Zephlet lands on the same pebble every morning at the same time - researchers at Frozen Peaks have named the pebble after it.

stages.name: Zephtalon
stages.bio: Zephtalon has become a proper coastal eagle, its white-and-pale-blue body large and athletic, wings spread wide with ice crystals forming at each primary-feather tip mid-flight. Its eyes are sharp and it rides Frozen Peaks' offshore winds with practiced ease, rarely flapping. It dives at fish - but never takes more than one - and returns the catch to the shore, as if teaching something about sharing to whoever is watching. It circles the peaks three times before landing, always.
stages.note: The ice crystals on Zephtalon's wingtips are a different shape each day - no two flights produce the same pattern.

stages.name: Zephyrial
stages.bio: Zephyrial is a storm-eagle of staggering span, its wing-edges trailing ribbons of glittering ice-mist as it banks over Frozen Peaks. The entire surface of its feathers carry a frozen sheen that refracts light into tiny rainbows below, and the air temperature drops noticeably as it passes overhead. Ancient fishers at the peaks say Zephyrial appears whenever the tide carries a lost guardian's name back to shore, and it circles until someone says it aloud.
stages.note: A Zephyrial sighting always precedes the largest sardine run of the season by exactly two days - Frozen Peaks' fleet watches for it.

stages.name: Zephling
stages.bio: Zephling is a compact grey-blue parrot-like bird with a wedge of purple-gold wing-flash visible when it spreads and fans its feathers in challenge. Its round eyes are bright with the particular alertness of a creature raised in high winds, and it grips any perch with both feet and refuses to let go when gusts hit. On the Steel Fortress battlements it learns the garrison's warning-calls by mimicry - and it has them all correct by the second try.
stages.note: Zephling always repeats a sound back slightly faster than it was made - scholars call this acceleration 'enthusiasm inflation.'

stages.name: Zephsoar
stages.bio: Zephsoar has grown into a fierce raptor with steel-blue and deep purple plumage, a crest of narrow upswept feathers, and bright eyes that track everything. Pale golden feathers catch light along the wing's leading edge. It rides the thermal columns above the Steel Fortress, scanning for weak words - the kind that crumble under pressure - and dives on anything that tries to pass without a good one. Riku the thunder-horse once raced these updrafts, and Zephsoar has not forgotten.
stages.note: Zephsoar adjusts its crest-feathers in response to the question being asked - experienced trainers can read the angle and predict whether a student will pass.

stages.name: Zephyros
stages.bio: Zephyros is a regal and enormous eagle, its blue-purple body lit with a full halo of electric-gold feathers that frame its head and chest like a war-banner. Its wingspan fills the sky over the Steel Fortress when fully spread, and the fortress banners flatten in the downdraft every time it passes. It carries messages no one else can reach - words that need to cross the winds between regions - and it still searches the high skies for the last free guardian, the one Riku was waiting for.
stages.note: Every message Zephyros has ever carried arrives at exactly the right moment - never early, never late, regardless of distance.

stages.name: Zephykit
stages.bio: Zephykit is an adorable small creature that splits the difference between axolotl and tiny dragon: a golden-yellow face framed by blue feathered gill-frills, a plump cream body, and a fluffy fox-like tail that seems slightly too large. It paddles through Coral Bay's shallows, gill-frills fanning in the current, and pauses to lip-read the words that visiting children trace in the sand. When delighted it does a tiny spinning splash that soaks everyone nearby without malice.
stages.note: Zephykit always faces into the current, no matter how you move around it - bay fishers call it the Living Compass.

stages.name: Zephydrake
stages.bio: Zephydrake has grown into a sleek bipedal water-dragon: deep blue scales cover a lean athletic body, swept-back water-fin crests adorn its head and back, and its clawed wings spread wide in a fighter's display when challenged. Its eyes gleam with focused intelligence, and it can launch itself from the water with enough speed to clear a tall fishing boat. In Coral Bay it guards the hand-carved coral formations that Axon made before Abalont arrived, herding curious fish away from the carvings.
stages.note: Zephydrake carves a new notch into the coral each week - researchers have counted forward and backward and found the notches encode a repeating sequence.

stages.name: Zephyrath
stages.bio: Zephyrath is a magnificent tidal dragon, its long golden-and-blue body flowing like a living wave across the surface of Coral Bay. Enormous wing-sails catch both wind and current, and streaming water-tendrils trail from every fin like a royal cloak in motion. Its presence shifts the tide slightly - not enough to flood, but enough to lift every boat in the bay an inch higher in the water, as if it is carrying them home. It is Coral Bay's oldest guardian, and it remembers every voice raised there since the bay first filled.
stages.note: The exact moment Zephyrath surfaces each morning determines the day's tide schedule - the harbor master uses only it, no instruments needed.

stages.name: Zyphule
stages.bio: Zyphule is a lime-green slug with two antenna-stalks topped by round green bulbs, and a vivid purple mantle of slime trailing behind it. Bright green droplets ooze from its back and glow faintly in shadow, marking a trail anyone could follow through Verdant Valley's undergrowth. It moves very slowly, tasting everything it passes with its whole body, and pauses to touch each hand-carved stone in the valley floor with its antenna before moving on.
stages.note: Zyphule's trail glows for exactly ninety minutes before fading - trackers in Verdant Valley use old trails to map where new creatures recently passed.

stages.name: Zyphant
stages.bio: Zyphant has grown a row of green bubble-nodes along its back that it inflates when nervous - each one pops with a faint acid-spray if touched. Its purple underside now carries faint stripes, and it travels faster, leaving twin slime-rails through the Verdant Valley leaf litter. A child who visits it regularly discovers it begins to recognize their footsteps and moves slightly toward them, which no one expected from something this slimy.
stages.note: The bubble-nodes on Zyphant's back pop in a specific sequence when startled - researchers have found the sequence spells 'wait' in old insect-sign.

stages.name: Zyphemoth
stages.bio: Zyphemoth is a great mound of toxic green-and-purple armor, its body studded with dozens of poison-dripping spines that make it look like a living cactus made of acid. Beneath the spines a powerful body moves with surprising purpose, and its two antenna-stalks have grown into sharp sensory horns that can taste the air for words a full kilometer away. In Verdant Valley it is the last guardian of the song-grove's roots - and nothing with bad intent has ever reached those roots while Zyphemoth was present.
stages.note: The spines on Zyphemoth regrow after being shed, and each regrown spine is slightly more potent than the last - it has been growing since the valley's first naming.

stages.name: Thornel
stages.bio: Thornel is a small grey wolf pup whose fur is woven through with living thorned vines, thickest along its back and tail. It moves silently between the roots of Verdant Valley's deepest undergrowth, watching travelers from the dark before deciding whether to growl or simply vanish. Younger creatures of the forest treat it as an unofficial guardian - it snaps at anything that threatens them, then slinks away before it can be thanked.
stages.note: Thornel's vine-fur snags fewer leaves than a bare-furred pup its size - the thorns are angled to slide through brush, not catch on it.

stages.name: Thornfang
stages.bio: Thornfang has grown into a lean, dark-furred wolf whose thorned mane now runs from skull to shoulder like a crown of brambles. It patrols the tangled thickets at the valley's edge, and the vines along its spine thicken visibly whenever it senses a threat to the smaller creatures in its territory. Trainers who earn its trust say it fights fiercely but never presses an advantage against something that has already yielded.
stages.note: Thornfang's mane-thorns curl inward when it rests - the only time the vines relax their outward, defensive angle.

stages.name: Thornmaul
stages.bio: Thornmaul is a massive dark wolf whose entire body is armored in thick, ancient-looking bramble growth, vines thick as rope wrapping its legs and back like living plate. It patrols the oldest, darkest groves of Verdant Valley, and guardians' texts describe it as the reason the valley's deepest undergrowth has never been cleared by anything that wasn't invited. It chooses patient partners who do not pull at its vines or rush it into battle.
stages.note: The oldest bramble growth on Thornmaul's back is older than the wolf itself - passed down, root and all, from its own parent at evolution.

stages.name: Flarewhelp
stages.bio: Flarewhelp is a small orange-scaled dragon whelp with stubby wings still too soft to lift its own weight, and a tiny flame that flickers at the tip of its tail whenever it gets excited. It scrambles over the cooled black rock at the Lava Crater's rim, chasing embers that drift up from the vents below. It is fearless around heat and deeply afraid of loud noises - an odd pairing for a creature born in a crater.
stages.note: Flarewhelp's tail-flame brightens with excitement and dims to almost nothing when it's startled - the opposite of what most trainers expect.

stages.name: Flarewyrm
stages.bio: Flarewyrm has grown a proper set of wings and a crest of hardened, ember-orange horn running down its neck, and its tail-flame has become a steady torch rather than a flicker. It flies low circuits above the Lava Crater's rim, and crater-dwelling traders use its silhouette against the smoke as a rough compass. It is territorial about airspace but shares its warmth freely with anything grounded and cold.
stages.note: Flarewyrm's wing membranes are warm to the touch year-round - crater travelers have been known to warm their hands on a passing shadow.

stages.name: Infernodrake
stages.bio: Infernodrake is an enormous crested dragon whose full wingspan casts a shadow across the entire crater rim, scales glowing faint orange along every ridge as if lit from within. It is the undisputed sovereign of the Lava Crater's high air, and the Abalont texts describe it as the reason the crater's vents have never fully gone cold - its passage overhead is said to stir the deep heat awake again each morning.
stages.note: Infernodrake's roar has been recorded triggering small, harmless ember-showers from vents nearly a kilometer away.

stages.name: Rimepup
stages.bio: Rimepup is a stocky white-furred wolf pup with frost crystals permanently rimed along its paws and jaw, and a habit of headbutting anything that moves - including rocks, and occasionally itself. It tumbles through the Frozen Peaks' lower drifts practicing pounces on nothing in particular, building the strength that will define it later. It is stubborn, warm-hearted, and utterly undeterred by falling down.
stages.note: Rimepup's frost-rimed paws never actually feel cold to the touch - the ice is decorative, not thermal, according to guardian researchers.

stages.name: Frostknuckle
stages.bio: Frostknuckle has become a broad, powerfully built wolf with ice-hardened knuckle-plates along its front paws that it uses to strike stone as easily as flesh. It spars against the Frozen Peaks' ice formations for hours at a stretch, and climbers have learned to follow the sound of its training as a rough trail-marker toward safer ground. It respects strength but reserves genuine warmth for whoever keeps training after they've lost.
stages.note: Frostknuckle's ice-knuckle plates re-form within minutes if chipped in sparring - a self-repairing trait unique to this evolution stage.

stages.name: Glacierbrawler
stages.bio: Glacierbrawler is a massive ice-armored wolf whose entire forequarters are sheathed in glacier-blue plating, capable of cracking exposed stone with a single forepaw strike. It holds the highest, coldest reaches of the Frozen Peaks as its own proving ground, and guardian texts call it the peak's oldest standing challenge - a test that has never once needed to be repeated for anyone who genuinely earned its respect.
stages.note: Glacierbrawler's strikes have been measured cracking stone at a force no other creature of its size in the Peaks can match.

stages.name: Luxling
stages.bio: Luxling is a small golden-scaled dragon hatchling that glows faintly from within, brightest when it's happy and barely visible when it naps. It hatches nestled in the brightest clearings of the Light Grove, and grove-keepers say a Luxling's glow is often the first sign a clearing is truly safe. It is curious about everything and startles easily, dimming to almost nothing at sudden sounds.
stages.note: Luxling's glow syncs faintly with sunrise and sunset even indoors - no light source required, just an internal clock no one has explained.

stages.name: Luxdrake
stages.bio: Luxdrake has grown a crest of golden feather-scales that catch and scatter grove light like stained glass, and its steady glow now lights a small clearing on its own after dusk. It patrols the Light Grove's inner paths at dawn and dusk, the two times guardians say the grove is most vulnerable, and shadows are said to visibly shrink back from its crest-light without it ever needing to act.
stages.note: Luxdrake's crest-scales have been used, dried and pressed, as genuine reading light by grove scholars working past sundown.

stages.name: Luxwyrm
stages.bio: Luxwyrm is a radiant, fully-grown dragon whose entire body glows like captured sunlight, wings casting warm gold light across the whole grove canopy when spread. It is the Light Grove's own guardian in miniature, and the Abalont texts say it was the first creature to prove that light itself could choose to protect something, rather than simply exist. It chooses bonded partners slowly, but never lets one go once chosen.
stages.note: Luxwyrm's full-spread glow has been documented reaching every corner of the Light Grove's central clearing at once, with no dark patches at all.
